We make very little, but this family trip means so much. There are so many things I can say. If its your first time, or even your first time in a long while. Do some research, check out some books. There is more than just rides at the park. Its American history at its finest. How the castmembers collect the trash, to their dealings with the safety of their guests just puts me in awe. Start a pinterest board and collect ideas that you want to do, see, share with your group. We are going with my in Laws who havent been in 35 years, and we have been sharing ride videos, restaurants with them,, to make this adventure amazingly fun for them. if you have questions, I'll do my best to answer...
It truly is the happiest place on earth! This was my first time to Disneyland at age 26! Loved everything about it, and very impressed at how CLEAN it is!! Would go back every year if I could !!

It is Disneyland and the many rides and attractions are always a hit with young children and we had a good time at the park with them. Disappointed the Matterhorn, Pirates of the Caribbean and the Disney train were all out of service at the same time for repair. All ate icons at Disneyland and to have so many out at the same time was a disappointment. We also had a fast pass to Space Mountain and showed up at the designated time and were turn away due to a malfunction of some type. Came back up a couple of hours later. We did enjoy the day but we were very disappointed some much was out of commission.

Third time at Disneyland. This time only for 2 days. We love Disneyland but this time we were left underwhelmed. There were are lot of rides not going. The crowds were ridiculous. It was not holiday times and mid week and ride times were easily over 2 hours in some cases. Even the staff commented on how busy it was. The food was typical to these venues, a bit overpriced, all the same and a bit tasteless. The souvenirs can be expensive but you can get some Disney approved from Walmart for a lot less if you shop around. Staff were great as usual and it's still the happiest place on earth.

This place truly is the best Disney park in the World!!!!!!One thing I would say is when we visited we had to report one of the workers because he shoved my dad out of the way and a little girl because we were all stood in the wrong place trying to watch the fireworks. The way they ferry people through is absolutely diabolical!!! I know people have to stand behind the ropes because of health and safety but there isn't enough room for everyone and when you are told, no sorry this is just for people who have paid extra to stand here, I think to myself what has happened to Disneyland, using the class system to allow people to watch the fireworks, who have spent a lot of money to visit. I am sad because what must Walt Disney think if he could see it now?! Really people? Its a shame because the theming of everything and the food in the restaurants was the best out of both Disney World and Disneyland Paris, so something needs to be done about the rope operation and firework parade operations in both Anaheim parks!!! I say they should limit the number of tickets each day so it doesn't pose a problem! Other than that it is the best Disney park!!!

The timing was excellent due to the amount of people scheduled tp be there. But Disney seems to close down major attractions due to servicing of the equipment. However, the cost is still the same! The big let down was Pirates of the Carribean and the Matterhorn and others were closed. Others were closed or a day or two, which is doable since we wee there for 4 days. Beside there were many shut downs while we were waiting for or on rides. Something isn't totally right with the park. We had no issue at Disney World in Florida.
You must do everything at least once! I hate roller coaster, but even I've done space mountain, thunder mountain, and the Matterhorn at least once. Go in as many shops as possible and just have fun.

No matters how old you are, you instantly get back to childhood when you enter the theme park. It's magical. Everything's is perfectly harmonized and time flies. There are rides for all ages, Indiana Jones, Big Thunder Mountain, Pirates of the Caribbean, Matterhorn Bobsleds,... you name it, we loved them all!

My first visit to this iconic wonder was in 1959. There were a couple times in the 1970s 1980s family era. Then, it was 32 years later. I must admit that visiting Disneyland during December is the best! For one, when you leave    Small    World    that song is not stuck in your brain. During December, though    It   s A Small World    does play repeatedly during your ride, it is intertwined with Christmas songs. In addition, the displays are of Christmas scenes around the world. The ride was delightful and my brain was free. Of course, the theme park is decorated for Christmas, and there is a Christmas themed parade, which is a nice change from the usual. Being    older   , no longer is it comfortable to ride those fast, jarring, roller coaster type rides. Mostly, we hopped onto the    tame    rides     and yes, we did ride the teacups. And, we did make it spin. Though we did hop onto the Indiana Jones ride, which was a bit jarring, though not bad. Mostly, I laughed (almost manically) throughout. It was hilarious and not bad on the bones. SO, if you are    older    you might think about hopping on a ride with Indy. Prices have changed since the last time I visited, though I planned for it. I do not regret paying $105 for the day. We arrived around 9 AM and got into our first line, which was for the shuttle bus. Disney has it well organized. We left the park a bit after 11 PM with a few treasures. All in all, totally worth the price. I will return.

I think we got really lucky with crowds the day we went, a Wednesday. The longest line we waited in was to buy tickets in. (next time I will buy ahead).Parking was efficient, trams loaded a little slow. I felt the park was in great shape, but noticed less interactive cast members than when we visit in Florida. Used the fastpass system, stayed until 8:00 and skipped the parade, which people had lined up for about an hour early. Food was good, loved the bakery treats. Overall just felt less Disney magic since there are no fireworks during the week or parades during the day.

What a magical place, i love Disneyland.  Its so clean and wonderful.  Ok the crowds are a bit annoying but you expect that in Disneyland.  Make sure you go for the single rider options where you can.

Always a fun time to be a kid again. Lines weren't that terrible and fast passes were available for the big rides and Disneyland. The ticket price is through the roof though especially for California Adventure when many rides were closed and there's a lot of pressure on the other rides to manage volume. There should be some discount when multiple rides are closed and you can't get on others for less than a two hour wait.

So we decided that we would have a lovely day at Disneyland on a Tuesday in March and the place was absolutely packed! We are a gay couple in our mid 30s and this place was really more for families and kids that don't mind waiting in long lines for every ride. There were strollers everywhere! We had a much better time at the other park California Adventures.

Booked my stay via a Costco package for October 2016 which included the room, Disneyland California Adventure 3 day hopper tickets, a Disney gift card, free Disney lanyard with pin for each person in my group, and character dining. Check in was smooth and quick. I was upgraded to a room overlooking downtown Disney and California Adventure. And even though we arrived a couple hours before check in time, we were able to get our room right away.The upgraded room allowed us to enjoy the amazing nightly fireworks show in clear view from the comfort of our room to the left at Disneyland and to the right we could see the World of Color show at California Adventure.Beds were very comfortable, room very spacious, and we LOVED the musical headboard! So charming...especially for my son.Hotel very convenient close to the park gates. Right next to the monorail. And if you prefer to walk  which we did  it is about an 8 10 min walk to the gates depending on your pace. Several restaurants and shops nearby (such as two Starbucks on each end of downtown Disney, Rainforest Cafe, and my son's favorite  the LEGO store, to name a few).We also LOVED the pool area which included a monorail water slide. It seemed almost as if my son enjoyed the water slide area more than the parks itself ; ). Several lifeguards as well to ensure everyone's safety. I was impressed with how many lifeguards they had on duty.When we checked out we still had about 3 hours to spare before we needed to head to the airport. The front desk kindly provided a key designated for the pool area and welcome us to hang out and enjoy the pool until we needed to leave. So that was a pleasant surprise. There are showers outside by the pools next to bathrooms which we used to get ready (but only cold water) before departing for airport.Hotel is indeed pricey. I do wish it could be more affordable. However, the Costco package and experience of the hotel definitely made it worthwhile. And I hope to stay at the Disneyland Hotel again in the future.

We expected Disneyland to be busy, but it was really busy! The number of people with prams was just overwhelming!The fast pass process that is used at both parks can be very frustrating when you have been lining up for a ride for an hour, but what feels like hundreds of people get to jump the queue. This is a free service which is relatively easy to get used to, but it can be upsetting for those that have been waiting for an eternity in the line.Not a fan.Other than that, if you can get past the noise and the sheer volume of people (with March being a  quiet  period), it is a wonderful experience, and quite magical. A definite must do.

As a huge fan of all things Disney a trip to SoCal isn't complete without a few days at Disney! It's often crazy busy, but if you love Disney it won't bother you. It is great for all ages with a variety of rides suitable for all. There's a variety of food options, but if you want something fancy you need to book ahead to avoid disappointment. I particularly love the Anaheim Disneyland and walking in Walt Disney's footsteps!!!!

Decided to do 3 days at Disneyland instead of trying to stuff everything into one day and we were very happy with our decision. We were able to take breaks and not feel like we needed to be constantly moving. The only down side to this trip was that quite a few of our favorite rides were closed so that is the reason for the lower review rank. Otherwise still one of the happiest places on earth.

I've been going to Disney for years and it is always a magical experience. Definitely a lot of walking. With the Tower of Terror closed down, California Adventure really isn't worth spending a lot of extra money for. Disneyland is big enough to fill the entire day and more.
For me this is really the happiest place on earth. There is so many rides and fun thigs to doo, cool areas, and great shops!
We went on a Wednesday, so the crowds weren't too bad.  Sadly, quite of few rides were down for repair, but thanks to the FastPass, we were able to ride a few things twice!

Ever since I was a kid, I've always wanted to visit this magical place. SO it was a dream come true to finally have done it as an adult. I loved the rides! I so enjoyed the haunted mansion, hyperspace, indiana jones, the monorail and walking through sleeping beauty's castle!

This is our 3rd time returning with our kids (6 and 4), and 4th for me and my husband. We love Disneyland and all the fun it has to offer. The rides are awesome and we are never disappointed with any of the shows, character meets and parades. The Electric Parade was great and a perfect end to one of our days. We liked it had 2 parade times and were able to catch the earlier 6:45 time with our young, tired kids. The park is super clean and all the staff helpful and friendly. We always set out for certain treats during our visit (not all at once!)   this time was cookies from the Winnie the Pooh gift shop, Dole Whips from the Tiki Juice Bar, the turkey leg from Edelweiss Snacks (2 adults shared 1 and it was plenty!), and popcorn. And for me, Starbucks at the Market House. We had a 5 day Park Hopper and by the end, we had done all that we had wanted, plus some. It rained on our first day but that didn't stop us. Soaked and chilled, we kept on and found the ride lines were non existent. If you are prepared, don't let the rain keep you away! Make sure to use FastPass, Single Rider passes and Rider switch where available to cut back on your line wait times. A couple of our favourite rides were closed for refurbishment this time (Matterhorn and Pirates) but understand this needs to happen, even if it is a tiny bit disappointing for a split second ... until something else shiny catches our attention and we quickly forget! Our trip was awesome, but like any Disney vacation, the crowds and lines can be tiring by the end and we had enough. Until we get home, missed the magic, and start planning our next trip!

This was my first trip to Disney. It was very fun! I do alert anyone going to be ready to run into many many many strollers. Things you can't miss;1. Racers in Cars Land2. Dole Whip at the Tiki Stand 3. Mad Hatter Tea Cups4. Splash Mountain (it's a staple)5. Mickey Mouse soft pretzel *Space mountain was broken 2 different times during our day so we weren't able to ride. There are a lot of shops and places to eat in this park. The parade at the end was very cool and worth staying for. There are no fireworks during the week, only on weekends. Sad day.
Disappointed by the number of rides and shows closed (no matterhorn, fireworks or fantasmic when I went) but still a fun, enjoyable day out. Great for families, couples or solo   like me.
It's Disney.  A great park experience.  We were there off season on a Monday so crowds were at a minimum which made it even better.  Clean and friendly with THE Mouse.  Great fun

What bad things are there to say about Disneyland. This is the third year we have been Annual Pass Holders. We love going to Disneyland. I really don't even know why they need reviews. It is such a magical place. Our daughter is now two and this trip was so much fun to watch her light up with all the characters. Your cast members are truly amazing and give an added enjoyment to the parks. Thank you!!!

Small crowds made it easy that particular day. The only downfall were the messy bathrooms throughout the park. You are better off bringing in your own food and water. Not overly protected with Police but enough to know they are present.

What theme park can give you a clean, wholesome environment and at the same time promote the family. I did not have the opportunity to see this place as a kid, but after moving to southern California, I was able to see for myself the impact this place has on my family. We started by bringing our oldest here when she was not yet 2 and then many times after that with each new sister following in her footsteps. I also had the opportunity to bring my parents here a couple of times who first came in with low expectations (as they do with all theme parks), but left with high enthusiasm for what they called a  chance to reconnect with their inner child . Because of this, they had a blast riding on rides with their grandchildren and meeting characters from the cartoons they grew up with. Now that we live a few states away, we still make it a point to come here now and then and regroup as that kid in all of us. Setting aside all of the expenses that can accrue during your visit, this park offers so much in return. I love that kids under 3 are free and that they can go on the majority of the rides with you. If I have my baby with me, they can sit with me while I enjoy many of the rides like the Pirates of the Caribbean. If needed, the park has a whole Baby Care Center with everything a parent needs whether they nurse, bottle feed, use cloth diapers, or are potty training. They take the stress out of photo taking and offer so many affordable options to get all the photos you didn't have or didn't want to take the time to get. Even though they have great dinning options, they also allow you to bring in your own food and picnic as you wish. The Characters and staff deserve so much of this praise because they set the tone for this whole park with their genuine attitudes and warm hearted friendliness. You have to realize that you are not just paying for rides at this park, you are paying for time to spend exclusively with your loved ones and that it is precious. While other theme parks may be cheaper, they also feel cheaper and the quality of time does not feel the same. You are given so much in one park with shows, good food, parades, fun activities, fireworks, and special events that dollar for dollar, it is money well spent.

As a long time Disney theme park visitor and a HUGE Disney fan, I am saddened to say how disappointed I am to have to rate the park so low. The chaos may be partly to blame for the massive amount of construction and overhaul the park is currently undergoing. It is difficult to understand why decisions to close some bathroom facilities for rehab while not providing additional options were made. Closing down the train that moves people from one side of the park to the other is also a very bad move. People can barely get around most hours of the day and several ride closures complicated things further. There aren't enough places for people to sit and rest and the fast pass system is antiquated and there isn't a system in place to allow people to exchange a pass if a ride breaks during their allotted time. The situation during the parade times is dangerous. There is absolutely no way an emergency situation can be handled. I can't recommend a visit until all construction as been completed.

It has probably been 5 or 6 years since my last visit to Disneyland. My wife and I were season pass holders for several years back then. As ever, the quality of every little thing in the park is amazing. Their attention to detail is so impressive. We got there just after opening, at 10:00 and stayed till just before closing at 8. It was a beautiful day, so the park was a little crowded. Still, never more than a 30 minute wait for any ride, and we did them all. All the open rides, anyway. A little disappointed Pirates and Matterhorn were both closed. Of course that information is available on their website if I had bothered to check.Our trip was with my daughter, son in law, and granddaughters, overall a great day.

My husband and I joke about how Disneyland Park feels more like  home  than our own house. There's joy and unadulterated magic all around you. We went for the first time on our honeymoon in 2014 and we loved it so much that we went back the next year to celebrate my mom's birthday and then went back AGAIN in 2016 with my husband's family! We live thousands of miles away from Anaheim, but Disneyland will always be our  1 vacation spot!

This was our first time visiting. Awesome rides. Great activities. Amazing events and shows. Lots of memories. The park was well maintained. Definitely this is the happiest place on earth. All my kids (12, 7, 3) had very good time and they wanna go back.Know how to use the Disney App, FastPass & Rider Switch before you get there. You will enjoy more!!

We're a couple in our mid 20s, and recently did a road trip down from Vancouver to LA to do the 'typical tourist things', which for us included Disneyland, Universal Studios and Six Flags Magic Mountain. We're very much into adrenaline filled thrill rides so we figured Magic Mountain would be our favourite, but we wanted to do all the others anyway as we'd travelled a long way to be there and had heard good things about them all. As expected our favourite rides were definitely at Magic Mountain, we loved our time at Universal Studios but we wouldn't really rave about Disneyland as it was more about 'the experience' than the rides which didn't interest us as much. There were a few things though that I would have fund helpful to know in advance, so I've written a bit of a summary below   hope it helps someone!DISNEYLAND: We went on a Wednesday during February so we figured it wasn't going to be too busy, but unfortunately it was the week of President's Day and turns out half the schools in California get the whole week off, so it was absolutely packed! (We just went to Disneyland Park, not California Adventure). It took us an hour just to get through the security line, and then the lines for all the decent rides were between 50 90 minutes. No one had told us that the FastPass was free, so we spent a very frustrating day being overtaken by people in the queue that had these Fast Passes, only to be told at the end of the day as we were leaving that it's free for anyone! It's only available for certain rides, but I would 100% recommend using it if you can   will save you loads of waiting time! Our favourite rides were the Hyperspace Mountain, Indiana Jones and Splash Mountain, as unfortunately the Bobsleds and the Grizzly River Run were closed. The park was very clean and the staff were friendly. Loads of families and people pushing strollers around   definitely more of a place for families and children than for a couple like us, but our day would have been dramatically better if we'd known about the FastPass. UNIVERSAL STUDIOS: We loved our day here   it provided a really nice balance between theme park rides as well as 'the movie experience' which we found more interesting than 'the Disney experience'. We are both big fans of Harry Potter so we really loved the wizarding world they had created there We were there on a Thursday and it wasn't too busy at all   the longest queue we waited in was about 25 minutes, so we had plenty of time to do all the rides at least once, and quite a few more than once. Our favourite rides were Revenge of the Mummy, The Simpsons Ride and Harry Potter & the Forbidden Journey. I'd recommend bringing a day pack that isn't too large, as for Revenge of the Mummy you have to check your bags into lockers, and the smaller ones are the only free ones. We downloaded the Universal Studios App which was helpful, and they have free wifi there too which was a bonus for travellers. The Studio Tour was really interesting, and the Special Effects Demonstration and the Animals Demonstration are definitely worth going to. It's not a cheap day, but we had no regrets and would 100% recommend this place to anyone else like us. SIX FLAGS MAGIC MOUNTAIN: We went here on a Saturday as it's only open on weekends during the off season. We arrived super early so we were at the front of the queue when the gates opened, and raced straight to X2 as we heard that was one of the best   unfortunately the ride wasn't operating yet, so despite waiting for about 15 minute we ended up having to leave and go find another ride. The day was plagued with ride closures (this was a comment we'd read on lots of other people's reviews so it's obviously an ongoing issue for them) but the app was super helpful as it gave us approximate wait times and up to date information on which rides had been closed. We absolutely loved all the rides we went on though, and although the closures were frustrating the waits were definitely worth it! Favourite rides for us were the Twisted Colossus, X2, Superman and Goliath, but to be honest we didn't find a single ride we didn't like. We didn't get the FlashPass as we didn't think it was worth another $40 each, however if you're going during the summer I definitely would spend the extra money and get it. All up, we could have happily spent a couple more days here and never got bored, so if you like thrill rides then definitely include a day here in your itinerary! If we got to do our whole trip again we would have skipped the day at Disneyland and done 2 days at Magic Mountain instead.

After 20yrs since my last visit I still found Disneyland to be the most Magical Place on earth...We travelled with my 21yr old son and his girlfriend as well as my 5 year old son...Disney is for any age, as I've explained to friends in Australia Disney rides are not about how fast they can go or the thrill, they take you on a journey & tell you a wonderful story....Nearly all rides allow you to carry personal belongings including backpacks although lockers are available if you need them...If you have a young toddler make sure you take a stroller as there is a lot of walking & exploring to do.. We purchased one from Walmart for $23 which we needed for our three week holiday.. To hire from Disney was $15 per dayWe purchased a Southern California pass which included a 3 day hopper pass to Disney & California Park, one day San Diego SeaWorld & one day Leggoland...We spent one full day at Disney & California Park and then a week later went back & hopped between both parks to all our favourite rides... Friends ask me about the lines & waiting time... I say Fastpass, look it up and make sure you use this as I met other Australians at the park who had no idea what this was & lined up for everything.. There is no cost to Fastpass you will find on your Disney & California Maps the rides that have it & they allow you to get tickets & jump the que every couple of hours... The must see rides in Disney are:It's a Small World   all agesIndiana Jones   Teenagers  California Park  Soarin   5  (Best ride exper. ever)Cars   5 Can't wait to go again

This was our third time visiting Disneyland. Never gets old, We had the magic morning and took advantage to ride space mountain and Indiana Jones. We went during the month of February and we had an awesome time, perfect weather! We love Disneyland and if you do not like to be around people and crowded places this is not the place for you.

Loved it ! Our trip was magical for my daughters 18th birthday .The food is great and reasonably priced. The park is so clean. Lines a little long but with the Disneyland app you know ahead of time what the wait is.

We are annual pass holders we love Disney so much... our children are grown, but this is our favorite Date Night!!!  We have  favoritie  rides, but sometimes we just take advantage of the parade or shows... excited to see the Light parade.

Coming from Florida and Disney World to check out Disneyland.  This park is smaller and easier to get around.  Great food selections and transport to and from parking was great!

Wonderful for everyone. Disneyland is the place for everyone to become kids again and live a like in a dream. This park is nicer than the one in Florida because it is in the middle of the city, in a walking distance to hotels and restaurants.

1st time visitor, and I got a badge to show that, right off the bat! Met a lot of the characters and had SO much fun. The lines are much shorter than Disney World (maybe except for the submarine attraction). You can also hop on the people mover and get a quick view of Downton Disney, the surrounding hotels and the  hidden  parts of the park. The Star Tours are always a blast!

Our 3rd trip here and it was fantastic as always.My husband's first time. He didn't grow up watching Disney and though Disney was a scam just to take our money.I convinced him to join us. I've been to Disney World multiple times and it's always been a great experience. We decided this time we wanted to try Disneyland. I have to say I was very disappointed with the experience. Everyone knows Disney isn't cheap but most people are ok paying because you know you're going to get a great experience, or so we thought. My first complaint would be the number of rides that were closed during our visit. Most people make plans for a trip to Disney months in advance but Disney will often release ride closures on very short notice. We knew about part of the park being closed while they work on Star Wars land and were ok with that. I assumed that meant that the other rides would be open. I was very disappointed to see just in the last couple weeks that in addition to the closures for Star Wars construction the Pirates of the Caribbean and Matterhorn Bobsleds would be closed as well. This was especially aggravating as these were the 2 rides that were different than Disney World that we wanted to experience. In addition to the ride closures we also experienced multiple unexpected temporary ride closures. We were in line 3 times where the ride broke down and they had to shut the rides down temporarily. Even the monorail was broken when we tried to ride that. The crowds were also a problem. We went during what was expected to be one of the slowest weeks of the year for the park and it was still quite crowded. Lines were often long for the attractions. I can't imagine coming here during peak season.Perhaps we were lucky on our previous trips to Disney World but we never experienced these problems before and again when you are paying Disney prices you expect a better quality. In the future we'll be sticking to the Florida parks.

Disneyland California is by far my favourite of the Disney's I have been to. It seems to be much better for teenagers and young adults!   Definitely stay for the parade and fireworks.   Dinner at Cafe Orleans was well worth the price and booking ahead!

Was very excited to visit the disneyland on my trip to LA from australia but its very busy down there even on monday. Paid $97 each for 1 day 1 park.. Went with a baby and its started raining. There is not much proper shelter as everyone is trying to get inside .. and instead of helping people they start selling there overpriced umbrellas and ponchos... the food was very expensive inside and quality is 0... few rides were closed... got stuck on space mountain for 20 mins and had to come through emergency stairs around 8:20pm went there on fast pass and still waited around 30 mins in fastpass line ... no apologize though and handed a pass to skip the line for other ride when its closing in 40 mins and had to watch electric prade at 8:30 as well... had no choice but just to throw that card. Big lines and waiting times are approx 30 60 mins atleast in every ride . Staff is not friendly nor helpful as waited with the baby for 20 mins in star wars lines only to get it know that babies are not allowed on this ride. Didnt you see the people with babies . Even in front of us has a 2 year old girl and they have to get out as well. If people think that staff service in disneyland if great than the have never seen one in other countries. Come down under to gold coast's dreamworld or seaworld or movieworld here and u ll know what a helpfull staff and great service is.

Had a wonderful time here! All the favourites   The Matterhorn, Splash Mountain, Indiana Jones, Big Thunder... all as excellent as ever. Park is just so cool we did every ride at least once! :)We had a 3 day hopper pass and we were very lucky with the weather as it rained and got a bit cold before and after those days.We were also very lucky that the big rides were all open when we were there... bit disappointed at the cheap star wars theme they gave to Space Mountain since I was last year.Magic morning was a major waste of time as so much of the park doesn't open until the normal time anyway, and the parts that are open become MUCH busier with other people having their magic morning.Thought it was crap how Downtown Disney was forced on everyone and we all had to hike through it every day to get to the Disneyland entry. Found the stroller parks to be a major eye sore and obstacle throughout Disneyland   they need a better solution.Lastly... we saw Donald at Disneyland near the main gate then went to California Adventure and saw him there too in a different outfit... and only 5 minutes had past! What are they thinking?! There can't be two Donalds out at once! There can only be ONE Donald!!!

We had a great day   well worth planning and using the fast pass service. BRILLIANT idea   and it doesn't cost! We ran into people after the day who said they didn't use it due to cost, they didn't realise it was FREE! Thanks Disney! FOOD for my son with allergies!!! $63 a day per park. Can't wait to spend son's bday then mine.  It expires May 25.  Check blockout dates.

I admit wholeheartedly that I am a Disney girl! So this review isn't easy to write. And I have taken a few days to think about it. We chose to hit DL on our recent trip to SoCal because the weather was bad in San Diego and it LOOKED good on radar in Anaheim. I am NOT blaming the weather on my day, nor will I blame Weather channel. And granted, it doesn't rain at DL often. BUT!!! They need to step up their rainy day plan. Thunder mountain was closed, and there was no lightening. Autopia closed as we were being placed at a gate to ride. It was merely drizzling!! Buzz light year closed, and it's an indoor ride! Also, more eating areas could be covered, not just for rainy days. On the upside, ponchos were available everywhere we went. Burgers from the place in tomorrowland were much better than expected. As usual, cast members always had a smile to make our rainy, soaked to the bone day, just a little more magical! And it was a perfect day to ride Splash Mountain, even if it was 59 degrees!! LolI will always  go home  to my happy magical place! And maybe, just maybe someone will see my post and take note, even in the smallest of thoughts.

Disneyland really is the happiest place on earth. we spent 2 12 hour days here with our 2 and 4 year olds and had a wonderful time. They cater everything to kids so we were comfortable and happy even in longer lines. We cant wait to go back

Not much I could share here that couldn't be found on a billion other websites. Fast passes are your friends. I would sell my mom for Dole Whip and Indiana Jones is very loud. But the crew members here are always great. I love New Orleans Square, Dole Whip and people watching. Now go enjoy it for yourself.

First came here with my wife 15 years ago. Came here in Jan 2017 with our 2 children (11 and 9 years) and the magic just keeps getting better! Everyone is just so happy walking around. We have traveled to Disney World MANY times, so we decided to change things up and check out Disneyland. The outside of the It's a Small World ride is pretty neat to see! With a working clock, the building comes to life every 15 minutes. So definitely not Florida, but it has its own treasures.
Always love Disneyland! Will return next chance we get. Wish we could come every week, my favorite place to be!

As growing up I Always wanted to go to Disney land but never got that opportunity. I am so happy that I was able to take my child there. I believe every child should go there even it's so good for adults too. Wonderful and magical!!! Unforgettable memories

It was the day after President's Day so we thought the park would be relatively quiet, but boy were we wrong, It looks like people took the day off and took advantage of the cheaper entrance fees (it was around $30 cheaper than the day before) as the park was swarming with people. While this is part of the Disneyland experience it felt like the park wasn't ready for such a large influx of people as security lines were absolutely massive and rides kept on being shut down.Hyper Space Mountain in particular was frustrating as it shut down several ties during the day, At one stage we had been waiting in line for 90min when the ride was shutdown and the cast members asked everyone to vacate. We came back later and managed to get a ride after waiting another 2 hours.We were lucky with the other rides but I heard stories that other people wern't so lucky   and experienced similar issues as we did with Space Mountain,Other than these kinds of issues, the day was amazing and even with the waits the vibe of the park topped us getting too frustrated about it,

Even with a lot of its rides down ( including my absolute favourite) it's still a fun place. Being handicapped it's definitely a place that caters to you but no one tells the other visitors I guess. To the cast members. Hurray. To fellow patrons, a guys in a wheelchair for a reason you dolts!

My family and I spent 4 days at Disneyland and California Adventure and we loved it! There's a reason why they call it the  Happiest Place On Earth ...it was all so magical! I suppose going during the low crowd season in teh rain does have its drawbacks. We love Disneyland, but it has gotten too crowded. We've loved taking our young kids as it's such a family friendly vacation. However, waiting in line after line has made it less fun. We visited disneyland for three days with our two young sons and we had a blast! We bought a three day park hopper package. We ended up only doing one park per day. I have been attending a conference the last 4 years and in the evenings we go to Disneyland and California Adventure. The parks are a lot of fun. I highly recommend getting a Park Hopper pass. It allows you a lot of flexibility at the parks. I highly recommend spending time at the parks.

Disneyland opened the year I was born. Living in San Diego, my parents made sure Disneyland was an annual trek for our family   I remember the days of coupon books, and our station wagon glove box was full of partially used ticket books (all the A & B coupons   LOL!), and admission was around $5. You could go for the day and ride every single good ride multiple times. Once, we went on Space Mountain TEN TIMES! Nowadays, ticket prices are well in excess of $100 and you're lucky if you make it onto 3 rides. In December, we waited in line for Thunder Mountain three times. After an hour of waiting, the ride broke down. This happened twice more. Same happened on Indiana Jones. I finally complained that we had been in the park for more than five hours and had only managed to get onto one  good  ride (Star Wars) and a supervisor gave us a  front of the line  ticket to any premium attraction. After the third breakdown on Thunder Mountain, we decided to just leave the park. We went on a total of three rides. They do have a  Fast Track , but you're only allowed to use that for one attraction at a time. Seriously, Disneyland just needs to limit the number of admissions to ensure guests can at least get on some rides. Very disappointed. Only gave it two stars for the nostalgia of how great the park was when I was a child teenager young adult.

Got tickets online and parking vouchers. Went with 2.5 and 5 year olds. Did 2 days in a row. Did not do too much. Saw Mickey and Minnie, rode it is a small world, roger cars, some rockets and mad tea cups. On Saturday we watched the 8:30 pm electric parade. Lines can be long but move quickly.

Pros: You can get a fast pass on the day rather than having to book it months in advance and being out of luck for them if you aren't a hotel guest. Con: The fast passes were often all gone by noon so be sure to go and get them as soon as you can, and note that you can sometimes hold two at a time so read the entire fast pass card for the instructions.Pro: It wasn't a huge park so hopping to areas of the park that had less time in line wasn't an issue.Con: It is very crowded and there isn't a lot of personal space in lines (the roped sections are made very very narrow to conserve space), or very much seating in random areas.Pro: The price of the ticket was cheaper on the day we went because it was a value season day.Con: It was also Annual pass day so there was a really big crowd to fight at every turn, and being asked constantly about if we were a member got annoying.As always, the staff was fantastic though. Attended Disneyland on Feb 21 2017 and I must say that the operation of their attractions has to be the worst I have ever seen at any amusement park. I am not sure that I will ever be back after having gone through this. Great workout though I guess.

One of the changes to the Park over the past year is they've moved the security check to the entrance to Disney Town (instead of near the ticketing area) and parking lots. What that means is that if you are entering via the parking area there will be long lines as they check your bags and run you through the metal detectors. Unfortunately, their detectors are set more sensitive than the airport and a majority of people have to be manually scanned with wands, which further slows things down. Which comes to our first recommendation:  Stay at a Disney property if you can afford it. The security line coming from the Disneyland hotel was much shorter (only hotel guests). Additionally, you will get the one hour early entrance to the parks. Each day alternates early entrance, one day will be Disneyland, the next will be CA Adventure.  If you are not staying at the Disney property, book through AAA. I believe AAA travel also has a package that will offer the one hour early entrance  Best use of the early entrance is CA Adventure (Cars ride). If you are with older kids and are riding CA Screaming roller coaster, get a FastPass to Cars, but go to CA Screaming first. We were able to ride the roller coaster 3 times with zero wait as most of the early entrance folks went immediately to the Cars ride. We also were able to ride Toy Story in the first hour.  On the Disneyland side, head to Space Mountain if you have the early hour access.  Plan on using FastPass for the main popular rides   again get your passes first thing on entry, as if you wait until noon   the passes may be gone for the day.  Use the iPhone app to book restaurant reservations   the app will book both restaurants within the park, and Disney Town.  Beware of the surge pricing model that Disney is using. Ticket prices will vary based on the time you are traveling. I'm not sure how surge pricing works if you are buying your tickets way in advance. Another reason to check book through AAA (if you're a member)  Several of the rides are under construction, check the web site, or use the App to see which rides are working (or not)  Disney seems to be even more cautious on their rides. CA Screaming was out of service as was Space Mountain for maintenance.  Not sure why the Monorail was not working this trip   we were at the Disneyland hotel, but were unable to take the Monorail into the park during our stay.  Unless you are a local, it's tough to justify the $1,000  for an unrestricted annual pass (even with a single day park hopper costing $157.00 non surge pricing)

This place is much too overcrowded and over priced which took all of the fun out of our visit. First, long lines to get through security. Then long lines to purchase very expensive tickets. Then long lines to use our expensive tickets and enter an overcrowded park. Then long lines for every ride and amusement (many exceeding one hour). Then discovering that my favorite rides we closed. No Pirates of the Caribbean, no Matterhorn, no train, no Tom Sawyer's Island, and no Mark Twain paddle wheeler. Then to have two rides break down after waiting in long lines (Haunted Mansion and Space Mountain.) Then to wait in long lines for overpriced and bland food, and discovering that they had run out of forks and napkins. Then to wait in long lines for a rest room. Then to take a really hard look at many of the worn out buildings, and being turned off by old out of date rides (submarine, Autopia, Small World). Then to find expensive snacks ($4.00 for a chocolate chip cookie? Come on!!!). The Magic is Gone from Disneyland. Walt Disney would be embarrassed and ashamed. It's not the park I knew as a kid in the 60s and 70s. Corporate greed at its very worst. Don't go here. Don't go here. Please do not go here!!!

Many years ago I visited this park and had a great time. No major cues, great normal food and a clean park. Today I returned with my wife. What a change. An extremely expensive entrance fee   110 usd per perspn   and for what? The park was overcrowded from 10.30. Long cues to every attraction (more than one hour   EACH place). Fastpass? Well, you could ask for a fastpass and get a ride many hours later. I tried it twice. First time at 11am   fastpass to 2.45 pm!! Next time at 1.50pm (i was not allowed to as for an earlier pass) this time I got a ride at 11.15 pm!!! Felt so sorry for the many kids ...No decent food was obtainable. The few ordinary restaurants were fully booked the whole day. The rest of  restaurants  were serving junkfood. Filth and garbage was found on the streets everywhere. Greed has overtaken this old gem. Apparently the park lets far too many people in to get a great profit. What a pity   and total loss of a lot of money for the visitors. So sad. Walt Disney must be turning in his grave ...

This is a great park to visit but it has become very crowded. Even on low attendance days it is a hard one to maneuver. I use a scooter (ECV) for mobility. Many times I had to just stop and let people (with their noses in their phones) pass. Don't plan on many rides in a day. Lines on even less popular rides are now 30 minutes or more. The live shows are still best part of the park.

Myself and my family love disneyland but i think we have turned a corner regarding this place. We have visited yearly since our kids have been very young and always love it but the joy gets a little lower each visit. Perceived value is probably the main issue, as prices continue to raise(quickly)so do the crowds. The place is being loved to death. There are only about two hours each day that seem magical anymore, the first and last of the day. On a recent long trip to the l.a. area we took a different tactic and spent limited time at disneyland(where in the past we would have spent the entire time at disney and no where else)and ended up having more, or at least similar, fun experiences at many other spots(knotts, universal, the beach etc.)Our plan moving forward:Do not visit for at least a few years(at least after star wars land opens), to grow the anticipation and preserve the uniqueness of the place in our minds. When planning a visit ,make sure that the planned refurbishments are acceptable(our last trip there were so many things closed that the crowds were far worse on open attractions and some things we thought we would not miss left a void in our visit) and use a crowd calendar(tripadvisor or isitpacked)to ,at least, estimate a good time for lighter crowds. We are no longer going to visit consecutive days(one day on, on off going to the beach or a pool day so everyone is rested and in best mood possible to avoid meltdowns). Everyone has their reason to visit, but be aware that disneyland is not what is has been and if you are expecting a visit to replicate one you had in the past you need to do your homework and learn enough so expectations are not missed.

This is a place with fast rides and meeting characters and both my children loved it. One being 3 the other 6. Expect some lengthy queues. First day we were not sure how the fast lane worked was only because a fellow park goer explained on the 2nd day you use your entry ticket to get a specific time but you might be disappointed as only a certain amount are given out in a day. But definitely a great experience. But food costs are astronomically highly 4 hot dogs fries and coke    60. The best thing the 6yo loved was the parade of light was indeed fantastic. All in all great

Brought our 1.5 year old daughter to her first Disney trip. Spent two days at the park which was a good amount to spend here with such a young child. While there are limited rides that she could go on they were all really a lot of fun for her, it's a small world, Casey jr train, character houses in toon town, Tarzan house, and the jungle cruise all included. The only one that really wasn't appropriate was the Pooh that ride... it was super loud and trippy for some reason. We were surprised by this ride and our daughter didn't like it at all so riders beware. The characters were super accessible and they don't let the lines get too long. The food wasn't terribly expensive and was pretty good for a theme park. Be prepared to wait on lines and do a lot of walking but that goes with the territory. We met the princesses which was a long line but we got to meet three right in a row which was well thought through. The electric light parade was definitely the highlight of our entire road trip around SoCal. On a whim we stayed for it the first night and didn't get a good spot but our daughter was jumping up and down on my shoulders and squealing in excitement so we got a better spot for the second showing and she went bonkers again. So much so that we went back for both showings the next day. As parents we enjoyed it as well, it was amazing. Definitely stay for it, but get there early for a spot. The second showing is less of a crowd.
It's Disneyland, what more can I say? It gets better with each visit. You don't even mind when some rude teenagers butt in front of you.

Having visited Disneyworld in the past, Disneyland park seemed very similar to its Floridian couterpart. The attractions were great, the Space Mountain was revamped to be the  Hyper Space Mountain , plus all the Star Wars themed rides and shows, the always popular Autopia, Tomorrow World, Splash Mountain (which was repeatedly favored by my kids), Big Thunder Mountain and the Matterhorn bobsleds which we couldn't ride much because it was out of service most of the time while we were there.

Do we really need reviews for Disneyland Park ? Just the most awesome place on earth ! It is just amazing how it calms all of us ! The minute I step through the gates and see Main street and the Mickey Mouse (FLOWERS) and the castle I am once again a child of 7 and ready to have some fun. Disneyland is intimate but still amazingly versatile. It is so free of the overkill of most roller coaster parks full of screaming people. Your entertained by simple sights and sounds and smells and laughing children. Disneyland is such a amazing place. Because it is small in comparison to many theme parks, you really feel close to everything in comparison to Disney World and other mega parks ! I love to sit in the center pavilion of the park and just people watch. it is a place you feel secure in a world of crime etc. The rides are amazing and the atmosphere is unprecedented. Love the live music and the overall ambience of the park. Love how the mood changes as the day progresses through music and parades and live shows. It is an art to see how Disney keeps the people entertained no matter what your age is... Never get tired of the park no matter what age I become.

If you have been to Disney in Orlando don't bother going to Disneyland you will be disappointed.Took us 1.5 hrs to park, pass security and buy tickets. There are lineups everywhere, it was not fun. We did not enjoy ourselves.Additionally the staff was not friendly and seemed very unhappy.Getting out of the park was another nightmare altogether.

I hate to admit it but it seems that I enjoyed Disney more than my 5yr old son. The area is so wide and so many options. The one thing that turn us off are the long queues for the rides. My son's favourite was the star wars Jedi training skit. We wish we bought a ticket that would allow us to have a 2nd day or even a 3rd day because 1day at the Disney will never be enough.

Endless lines with no progress or end in sight.  Tons of squandered time.  Get Fast Pass or don't go.  Waiting in line for 1 ride for 2 hours getting 3 minutes of good entertainment isn't my idea of good time.

My parents brought me here right after it opened in 19.....well, 60 years ago! I remember the teacups and Dumbo from that trip, which are still here. Disney is 1st rate with what they do and the park lived up to my memory 60 yrs. later. Loved It's a Small World and Indiana Jones. Very clean, lots of restrooms. A
Disney is just amazing. Definitely prioritize what you really want to see because there is just never enough time to do it all.

I am a So Cal resident and purchased a 3 day pass. It is the cheapest way to see Disneyland without buying an Annual Pass. But if you do want to buy an annual pass you can use the money you spent toward your 3 day pass to your AP. Just use your Magic Morning FIRST and purchase AP before leaving on the 3rd Day. Save your parking ticket for refund if you buy any of the AP's that have parking included. We went on 2 16 with my great nephew who is 2 and we had a handicap person in our party. We rented a motorized scooter from Disneyland. It will cost you 70.00. At the end of the day you get 20.00 back. We had purchased our tickets online, I recommend purchasing everything online in advance to make the most of your time at Disneyland. When we got to the gate you present your ticket, you must prove you're a CA guest. They take your picture and write your name on your ticket. I had no idea that I would be asked for my ID so I had to dig for it and this held up the line, my bad!I heard someone else say that Disney retains pensioners and I believe it to be true. The cast member (was older) and she misspelled my name, crossed it off, wrote over it so much you couldn't make out my name anymore. I was concerned about this for future entry. She told me  here you write it if it bothers you that much  and then added  nothing in life is perfect . I had never been talked to so rudely at Disneyland so I was a bit shocked. With a 3 day pass you get ONE Magic Morning. It is available different days at both parks. Tues, Thurs and Saturday for D'land and the other days at CA. We got into the park at 10am and all of the characters were out on main street. Unfortunately, by the time we got to them they were taking a break. Sadly, my great nephew saw them and wanted to go up to them but couldn't. At Main Street if you're lucky to meet your character jump at the chance. But if you plan accordingly you can also go to the stationed areas where your beloved characters will be. This will help your little ones not be too disappointed. We were at Minnie's house in Toon Town. We had the handicapped person with us and we didn't know what the procedure was. I asked a cast member and she said that one person in your party had to wait in line while the handicapped person waited on the curb. When your party meets the handicapped person on the curb they can then join you in line and the house is handicapped accessible. This seemed odd to us because if a handicapped person went alone with a 2 year old he could not send the 2 year old to get in line alone. It was unclear to me how you prove you're a handicap person if you do not carry the motorized scooter key. We were asked several times to show them something. We showed them the key and we were admitted on the rides.Lastly, during off season there is no fireworks during the week. I am not sure how Disneyland can say there is an OFF season because the parks are always so crowded. Pirates, is down until after May. I am sure it has to do with the 50th anniversary of the ride. It is disappointing to go and not be able to ride. Going into the park they asked me to provide my email address so I could participate in a survey. I did. The survey wants to know how much money you spent at Disneyland and it breaks down your entire day, transportation, ticket, parking, food, souvenirs, etc. I  underestimated . I spent nearly 400.00 just for ONE person. Its expensive folks!

The only reason for me not to give this place a 5 star score is that I will keep that score to DisneyLand Tokyo. Still is the most magical place you could ever found youself in while inside the USA, the sounds and sights and even the smells of popcorn and cotton candy makes of DisneyLand a place to visit at least once in your life if possible with family. In all the park has great rides, on stage shows, parades and fireworks but it suffers a bit from being the original park some areas are a bit confusing sometimes due the layout and expansions. But you can only notice these things if you are a Disney Park aficionado, otherwise this will be perfection.Please, avoid holidays and school vacations at all coast!

A great way to fill a day but the fast track tickets run out really fast so get the ones you want first. The food and drinks are expensive. We took our own water in with us. We saw Spiderman and captain America who were very nice and took the time to talk to everyone and did not rush people away.

Do not go when it's raining, even a light sprinkle causes everything good to get shut down. All the staff we met were great except for the entering security and parking lot attendants. The park is very expensive. I would recommend bringing closed water bottles and snacks for the kids. We bought 3 hot dogs and it was 40$. If you only have a day to do the park California Adventureland is way better to spend he day at.

I am a frequent visitor to the Disney World Resort and a member of the Disney Vacation Club. On my recent visit to the Southern California area I made my way to California Adventure. I arrived at 8:15, went through the entrance and security by 8:40. At rope drop I went directly to the Fastpass location for Radiator Springs Racers (a fabulous ride, similar to Test Track at Epcot) and then for the World of Color. I then went to Soarin' Around the World and waited for 20 minutes. This all went smoothly, though since I am used to getting my Fastpass  reservations in advance from home I now prefer not running around the park when I first arrive. I had the feeling that this park is a little behind the times. I was able to catch the Newsie type Street show, which I thoroughly enjoyed. I would like to have seen more street shows. One of my main reasons for enjoying the Disney Parks is the wonderful music. I felt this was missing from this park. We wanted a moderate priced sit down restaurant ($$) for lunch, but there weren't any in the park. We called for a reservation at Tortilla Jo's at Downtown Disney which was fine, since it is very close and no problem to exit and return to the park. The Live Frozen Show at the Hyperion was spectacular. I recommend you arrive for the show at least 50 minutes in advance. We got there 45 minutes before. My friend and I just missed the line for the Mezzanine, so we sat in the Balcony. We sat in the last row, which was fine for viewing. Our only problem was the walk up 6 flights. We took the escalator on the last flight. If you have any breathing or walking issues be sure to ask to use the elevator. We did that after the show. You have to get a pass from a Cast Member at the theater. The absolute best part of the day was the nighttime show, World of Color. It is truly one of the best water and light shows of all the Disney Parks. Take a peak at it on YouTube. It is spectacular, worth the wait after a long day at the park.

Come on what do you want me to say about Disneyland other than it's the happiest place on earth. Staff is outstanding and always happy with a smile to answer any question and help you out.We come approximately every other year and do a three day hopper and enjoy the privileges of going to both parks at any time we wish. Highly recommend a hopper.

It a took a solid day to complete just this park, started at 10am til about 6pm, the park is open til 8pm with fireworks over the weekend. We bought a 3day pass. We planned a day in each of the two parks and the third day was a catch up or make up day for rides that we were unable to ride due to waiting times. As expected its busy, long, long waiting times. Anywhere between 10 80 mins on our visit. My golden advise is pick the rides that will best suit you or your kids interests and age. Disneyland Park is good for the 2 9yr olds?? Star Wars rides also feature here, best ride was the Star Wars Tour ride  a great simulation ride. Take a fast pass it helps get through the rides. BUT, you can only do this once for the time slot allotted. ie it doesn't work on multiple rides in that theme park. If u have the hopper pass you could fast pass in each park  it will be quite a dash between parks! Food is overpriced. Purchase of Water is a get rich scheme, I paid $4 USD for 750ml water. Coffee was expensive crap. Good that the park employs pensioners, but they are rude and make the 'happiest place on earth, miserable' cos they can't tolerate excited kids,loud music & perhaps the heat. Grumpy, grumpy, grumpy best describes their overall appeal. Ironic, I know. The Indiana Jones ride and Big Mt were worth the wait. Need for more modern, technologically advanced rides to suit the advanced generations. The lanyard with Disney character badges is another scam to make millions in a day! Those very same grumpy pensioners don't have the patience for indecisive kids who are not sure which badge to swap. Overall, we are glad we have ticket the Disneyland experience of our son's bucket list. Enjoy folks!

As everyone knows, Disneyland is a fantastic place to visit. The staff are fantastic, ever single one of them, the park is immaculately clean, the rides are fantastic and the food is lovely with many options. We spent 5 days between Disneyland and California Adventure and every hour was worth it. Just a heads up, binoculars are not allowed in the parks. I am a birdwatcher and wanted to see a few local birds, but was sent back by security as binoculars are a prohibited item   go figure! I have no problem with that in principle, but it would have been nice to have them listed on the prohibited items list that they publish on their website. Then I wouldn't have brought them.

Disneyland is my favorite of all parks visited. With all the different worlds to see, fun rides and just a great atmosphere. Once visited Disney in Hong Kong and noticed a difference of not too many characters walking around. A lot of my old favourites like Donald Duck not to be seen. Thinking it was the time of year their not so busy (if u can say that seemed packed) some of the worlds were closed for maintenance like the paddle steamer etc BUT they have to maintain at sometime for safety. Hate to see what it is like Peak season. Guessing this is why I rated 4 star. But just       Disneyland and I loved February, weather perfect and still had huge line ups at some rides but not as bad as peak

First time visit with our 4 & 8 year old boys. I haven't been here since the mid 70's. Tried to pick off season, disappointed at the massive amount of people (with strollers everywhere) long lines, 60 minute plus wait times, most popular rides were closed for repairs, disappointing and were hoping for a real Disney experience for our kids first time, failed miserably. Food court prices ridiculous, would think with the high cost of admission, you wouldn't need to make a fortune on food also. Restrooms dirty, but the grounds were fairly clean considering the mass amount of people who can't clean up after themselves...Doubt the kids will want to return, they didn't even talk about it much, so sad..

I grew up going to Disney, so I still love going as an adult (without kids). There are lots of fun rides and the whole park is laid out with a lot of thought toe great design.My personal favorite rides are Buzz Lightyear and Space Mountain, with serious nostalgia points for Dumbo and the Tiki Room.

The staff are always so friendly and make you have a great time while there. We came president's day weekend and it was a good time to go. The lines were not as bad as in the summer. We were able to get on space mountain twice and star tours 3 times!
Disneyland is unlike anything you've experienced before! Truly magical and great for people of all ages. My husband and I come to Disneyland at least once a month! Perfect get away.

The park opened at 10am. The park was themed in Halloween in main street area. Goofy and Pluto were in the main street area for pictures. The characters rotate throughout the day. However most of the Mickey Mouse characters are in Toontown all day so you can meet them. Use your fastpass for space mountain as it is one of the rides with the longer lines. However we must of had a good day we didnt wait longer than 30 mins for any ride all day. Matterhorn Bobsled is fun, but had malfunction issues during the day. Splash mountain is another one you may want to use your fast pass for. The parade is daily at 3pm and down the main street. Get there early for a good spot or avoid that area if you dont want to see itor get stuck in the traffic. The food prices are expensive as usual for any theme park. The amount of scooter and strollers is almost dangerous as there are so many they take up the whole walkways.

It's Disneyland! I love it. We go to Disney World Florida every other year or so but since we live on the other side of the country our visits to Disneyland aren't as numerous but they are special. I recommend visiting between October and December so you can experience the Nightmare Before Christmas Haunted Mansion ride layover, it's really fantastic. In November Small World is all decked out for Christmas with the dolls singing Jingle Bells instead of the usually song. There are rides here you won't find in Disneyworld and this park is smaller so you can do it all in 1 or 2 days. We stay for 4 or 5 and see California Adventure Park too and usually an outside area attraction (hollywood, san diego, etc).
Wet. But still the happiest place on earth. Great food and drinks. Loved the old classic rides in Disneyland. Can not wait to goo back

Visited Disneyland with 2 adult women. Got there when it opened and left when it closed. The park was clean, efficiently run and a pleasure to visit. There were a number of ride attractions that were closed but that is to be expected. Plenty of things to do to entertain yourself.

We brought our toddlers here and had a fabulous time! I'm so glad we took the advice of others who encouraged people to go ahead and bring their littles. Even though they are probably too young to remember much of this trip on their own, we will never forget the magical day we had together.

Disneyland Park is by far the best theme park I've ever been to. It has something for everyone and can capture a sense of magic no matter your age, gender or belief. Despite always being packed I love the ticketed fast pass system and over 3 5 days you can just relax and really enjoy the park with everything it has on offer. You really need to spend the time to appreciate everything in the park and not just rush it. You will miss things if you don't really take the time to walk around, check out everything really make note of every little detail.

Having been to Walt Disney World over 20 times, it was a dream to experience Disneyland as well. We went on Monday and were in line 45 minutes before rope drop. We were able to ride several rides before the park got too crowded, so it's worth getting up earlier for. Take advantage of Fastpass to maximize your time spent on rides. As usual for Disney, the park was clean and employees were generally friendly and accommodating. And the queues before the rides were immersive for the story ride. Easily could have spent another day there exploring the park, watching parades shows and riding rides. An 11 on a 1 10 scale!

Disneyland, is, of course wonderful. But you really have to be intrepid to survive the horrific crowds that Disney somehow manages to jam in there. If you want to ride anything, go in the morning. The food has gotten a bit better, but it's also expensive, so be ready for that. Prepare to wait in line for long periods of time, take advantage of the fast pass and single rider systems, and try not to get pissed when it seems like rides are arbitrarily closed. Disneyland is so heavily visited, they don't need to care about your feelings. Also, I do not recommend this park for really young children and babies. They don't understand what it is they are supposed to enjoy, and the lines and weather are an absolute torture to them, if the screaming is anything to judge by.

My friends and I did a 3 day park hopper pass last week when we visited Anaheim. For us, that was more than enough time for us to do everything that we wanted as it seems like this time of the year is a slow time for the parks.Biggest tips are to use the Disneyland apps and to take advantage of the fast passes. Even with it being a slow time of the year, we were able to plan out our rides and check wait times to make sure that we were able to ride multiples times. We took advantage of our park hooper by getting a fast pass in one park and then going to the next park to get another one (you can have one fast pass per park at a time). Such a good trip and I'll definitely be back.

We saw zero characters while we were in Disney on Sunday. Pirates was closed, we waited 75minutes in the Hyperspace Mountain line and then were told that the ride had some sort of an issue and we could either wait if we wanted, or stay knowing that there was no foreseeable time frame of the ride being fixed. We waited for 23 minutes and were told by the crew member that they were back up. Everyone cheered and then 2 minutes later a woman came on the intercom and said the ride was still down. So, we decided to ditch and get food since we had a kid in tow. So about 100 minutes waiting on a ride that the Disney App said 50min. Dunno why Peter Pan's ride has such a ludicrous wait time. Saw a couple celebrities on Dumbo which was cool. Fast Passes were super beneficial for Haunted Mansion. Really what can be said that people don't already know. DON'T go on Peter Pan, get the FP for Hyperspace MTN early. Parade of Lights was ok. The kid loved it. People started getting seating spots 5 hours ahead of time. The staff tried to kick us out of the waiting area while we were looking for seating 2 hours prior to the show saying they were full. We squeezed in behind a couple generous Europeans. 30 minutes before the show AFTER they told everyone to go away and wait for the 10:30 show, they tell everyone to move forward to make more room. Sooooo.......don't listen to the staff. Disney is Disney, everyone knows about the waits. But, we went on 5 rides in a full day even with utilizing the FP system. Not worth the price of entry. Not even close. Disney has their marketing down pat. The park sucks other than to get people's wallets open and to wait ridiculous amounts of time to ride mediocre outdated 1 minute long rides.
It's an amazing place they don't miss any details. If you plan it right you can hit all the rides without huge lines. We have one 2 year old and she loved it.
Every single person deserves a visit to Disney land. Truly magical, wonderful, and delightful. This is for all ages.

Taking the kids to Disneyland for the very first time. I think Disneyland is over rated for the amount we paid for tickets, food, drinks, etc. Its almost too expensive to take the kids to Disneyland. They don't have front of the line passes and at lease 3 4 rides were not working. For the amount of money we paid for tickets, hotel, gas, food, and gifts we could have went on a 5 day cruise trip with everything paid for.

I've loved Disneyland since I was a kid and now I'm taking my children to see it and experience the magic of Disney. This time around seemed like lots of rides had problems but we still had a great time. Grab a turkey leg, a churro and a dole whip if you get the chance they are all amazing.

Seriously, this is Disneyland, of course it's gonna be great. My boyfriend and I visited in the Christmas holidays and it was magical. We also stayed it the hotel and it had amazing benefits like the magic hour! A bit crowded, but amazing!

The original Disney. It's amazing how little has changed since my first visit to the park 25 years ago. It's a small world, splash mountain and space mountain are still the way I remember them from when I was 16. To me, this is what adds to the charm of the park. Some drawbacks are the lines to get on some of the rides. It was a pleasant surprise when we stood in a line with a 25minute wait and we would get through in 10minutes or less, but if you wanted to go to the Star Wars themed exhibits, you would be waiting as much as 85 minutes. The other drawback was the line for the food. I don't really understand why people feel the need to get up to the counter and start talking about their lives. There's three menu items you can choose from, pick whatever you're ordering, pay and step to the side. No need to give the back story as to why your kid loves the clam chowder. Overall, I had a wonderful experience.

Too Crowded, too pricey, and has lost it's charm. Disneyland of the 50's 60's 70's and 80's was a wonderful place to visit. It has lost all charm. If you enjoy standing line line at the DMV you will love this place. Everything has a price tag on it and now all the rides exit to their overpriced gift shops. I'll bet Walt is just rolling over in his grave.
Things have changed since I was last at Disney 33 years ago. I had tons of fun though and had a great time. I totally recommend this for the entire family!

It's been eight years since I last visited Disneyland and it's sister park This past week was great with the exception of Pirates of the Caribbean and the Matterhorn closed for renovations and the Disneyland Railroad closed due to construction. My family went on many of the rides, Haunted Mansion the most ridden ride of our trip. Space Mountain is fantastic in its new Star Wars theme. Once again, glad to have made it out there.
Amazing place.. had a blast from start to finish. Wish restaurants had better choices for vegetarians. Rides were great and took advantage of fast pass option. Love the energy here.
Always a favorite family trip. Make sure to plan for at least three days and have a park hopper pass ( a day in each park plus a third day to go back and get the stuff you missed ! ).

My husband and I spent our first Christmas together. We got there as the park opened and we went right to the Pirates ride then Haunted Mansion then to Splash Mountain and never waited in a line. We spent the morning doing so much and never waited in a line. By 11 the park was packed. We went back to our hotel for a rest and went back later. We were able to get on some rides right away as single riders. We found that to work out great for us. Disney on Christmas is a blast . It did get really crowded but that is to be expected.

Disneyland is one of my favorite places to visit. However, it had been so crowded the last few times that we decided to come during February to see if we could beat the crowds. We were wrong! It was just as crowded as usual and it didn't seem any better than any other time of year. That being said... I still love Disneyland and will continue to go. It is just unrealistic to expect days where it is not packed. It is best to come prepared with a plan and to use the fast passes to get on the rides with longer rides. We found, even though it's not fun to get up early, it is the best option if taking a toddler. It was the only way we were able to get on rides with out waiting at least 30 minutes. The afternoon lines were all 45 minutes or more! I highly recommend going but I would definitely recommend having a plan and getting a multiple day pass so you have lots of time to relax and ride all the rides.

Make sure you call and check to see what is opened, what rides are closed. Will never be able to take my grandkids there again because it is so expensive . And miss'ing pirates of the Caribbean , and the mountain on was a let down.

I've been coming here for over 40 years and notice crowds are now out of control. I suspect it's season pass holders who overfill the place after 5 pm. Many attractions are down: Steamboat, Pirates of the Caribbean, Tom Sawyers Island and more. Lines were crazy long yesterday. Jungle Cruise even 30 min wait! Small World seem to have a breakdown with boats smashing into each other like bumper cars. I was really irritated to find that an older Disney employee had moved my stroller from the front row, to the back row of stroller parking at Small World. It took me 1 2 hour to find said stroller in the dark among Hundreds of strollers!It's still a better than average amusement park, but Disney needs to get their act together and stop selling cheap Annual passes. They are ruining the experience for those that spend a fortune getting there from far distances. Disney World and Orlando area offer more park options. If you are traveling a long distance, I would recommend Orlando area instead of California.
Rides were good as lines were not to long , although it was a pity that many sections of the park were closed for refurbishment.

This visit was 2 adults with no kids, so remember that as you read this. We were in and out in 3 hours and half of that was standing in line for the Nemo Submarine ride. I've been to Disney World hundreds of times, so when you see Cinderella's castle here it just seems sad. If you have kids, I'm sure you would enjoy it because of all the princesses and characters you can visit, and it's a just a good family park. I would probably go back to California Adventures before I came here again.

My family and I were there on 2 9 17, during what Disney considers there  off season . HA! It's like any other theme park across the US, with a lot more adventure. It was lots of fun but you have to wait to enjoy the rides. They offer a Fast Pass but for more $ atop of what you just spent on the entrance ticket. The popular characters also had a long line, only got a picture with goofy, which is my personal favorite. Food is ok.
this park can easily be done in 1 day if you are short on time to allow you to get the whole experience
We had the greatest time ever, got our pictures taken with Chewbacca and darth Vader!! Freindly helpful staff at guest relations
Looking forward to the new Star Wars area. Disneyland is one of my favorite places to visit. In spite of the rate hikes and long lines. But its truly a place to celebrate fun with friends and family.

Oh, well, it's Disneyland! The cast members really make this place fantastic. While there was a lot of people here, the atmosphere was positive and friendly. Oh, and thank you Disney for taking over Star Wars... we saw things we would never have seen if left in Lucas' hands.
Fast Pass not very helpful with long lines at popular attractions.  Just saw that the prices are going up again!

WE went to Disneyland with 70,000 other people. The park was so crowded that we could not enjoy it! Disney has a brilliant idea of making the lines go onto the walking paths. This makes it impossible to get around. Fast pass was full at every ride, so we just had to wait in line. They are trying to navigate crowd control and it is not working! I was very disappointed and I spent a lot of $$ to go. I will not travel to Disneyland for a very long time. One of our family members had a huge panic attack and the only help we got was to walk through the shops. I know that Disney has another way out and to get around. We just needed help getting our family member out without any more issues! I was very disappointed in Disney's lack of help!!

If you can, a 3 Day Ticket to the Disneyland Resort is a must! This allows you to spend two days in Disneyland and one day in California Adventure. Disneyland is best during the offseason, (Mid January Early May excluding spring break) where crowds are low. You can experience most of the park. This does come with a trade off, quite a bit of the park can be under refurbishment construction.
