There are several tools online to help with trip planning and I would suggest Disneyland Crowd Calendar. This can help you find what times are typically busy. Another useful tool is the refurbishment schedule that can be found on touringplans.com. Food can be expensive if you choose to go to a premium dining location. If you are looking for a good dining location for a date, I would suggest the blue bayou. You can expect a $100 bill at the end, but the meal is definitely worth it. The atmosphere is romantic and the food is amazing.

We came here with a group of friends for a weekend and we had a great time together. We were strategic with our Fast Passes so we were able to get on the majority of the rides in one day. The only thing that sucked is 3 of the most popular rides broke down in 1 day while we were standing in line, and we were only comped fast passes once.
The magic is all around you here. Perfect for little ones. Disney isn't cheap, but it's definitely worth it.

Disneyland will forever be one of my most favorite places on earth   from the moment you enter through the turnstiles and walk down Main Street, you are transported to a very special and magical place. Meticulous detail, inspired design and artwork, imaginative and engaging attractions (Peter Pan's Flight is my favorite attraction, along with Indiana Jones & Hyperspace Mountain), great restaurants (Blue Bayou is the best food in the park   make sure to make dining reservations well ahead of your trip), and incredible nighttime parades and fireworks. Disney has continued to build, enhance, polish, expand, and create even more magic (can't wait for the new Star Wars Land!!!), and I look forward to many more magical days spent at  The Happiest Place On Earth .

Disneyland does a fantastic job of entertaining. They are especially great with handicapped and mentally challenged kids and adults. The characters are engaging and their policy for handling people with challenges is great. It is very expensive so plan to spend a fortune, but it is truly an experience unlike anything you will ever experience. It is considered  The Happiest Place on Earth  and it is. It can get very crowded so choose a time outside normal vacations and school holidays. Don't be put off by the weather. Even if it rains it's still enjoyable. I think Walt Disney would be proud of what has become of his vision.

First, when you come here, you need to stay at one of the 3 Disney hotels so you can take advantage of the extra hour that Disney opens this park in the morning for guest that are staying at one of these resorts. As the park is pretty much empty (by Disney standards) during this time, you get free reign to ride as many rides as possible.When my family went we stayed at the Disneyland Hotel which was about a 10 minute walk to the park entrance. When we got there, there looks to be a huge line to get in, but the line is relatively small when you consider how big Disneyland is. When you enter, we went straight for the bigger rides so we avoid longer lines later, Hyper Space Mountain was amazing, then star tours and the Matterhorn. Disneyland just did a makeover to incorporate Star Wars into these attractions and they were amazing!!! About this time is when the park opened to the rest of the crowd so we made out way over to Indian Jones and did Adventure Land and Frontier Land and did the attractions there.As we went at the end of January, there was not a lot of crowds. Well, by Disney standards, the park was only about half capacity. Which meant that the longest line you would have to wait in was about 30 minutes and Fast Passes had return times for about 90 minutes from the time you got them. So we would usually get a Fast Pass, ride the ride and then come back with the Fast Pass to ride again. With that strategy, we got to ride Space Mountain, Indian Jones and the Thunder Mountain Railroad multiple times!!!The day was capped off with the Electrical Light Parade which took me back to my childhood. All in all, it was a great day at the park, the crowds were low, the food was great (love the Churros!!!), the lines short and enjoyed the very pleasant atmosphere...truly one of the happiest places on earth!!! Go and enjoy it!!!

I went to Disneyland today (Feb 13, 2017) and was not only disappointed, but disgusted with Disney management. The park said a couple rides were closed while they built a Star Wars attraction. However, they made no mention that Pirates of the Caribbean and Matterhorn were also closed   who knows why? So for your $97 admission & $20 to park you got fewer rides and long lines   even on a low attendance day. Then there was a 5 car fire in the garage, so they closed it as well as the trams. People (myself included) were in the line waiting for a tram, and we were told trams would be at the far end of Downtown Disney. So we all walked a long distance only to be told  no trams, so walk to the garage    another LONG distance. Upon arrival at the garage Disney stall said  IT WAS CLOSED TO EVERYONE  because of the long ago extinguished fire. So, every had to stand & wait TWO HOURS until the garage re opened. If people had been told about the garage back in the park, they could have done other things while waiting for admittance to the garage, back in either park instead of standing around a lot with no seating and NO bathrooms. Disney's management has atrocious communications skills and are bad at their jobs. Walt would roll over in his grave if he saw how Disneyland's guests were treated.Save your money until you can fly to Orlando and go to DisneyWorld. I'd rather BURN $100 bills, than return to Disneyland in Anaheim.

We went into Disneyland on Friday afternoon. The lines for the rides were short. The park was not very crowded and the perfect day to enjoy the park. The dole whip was so delicious. The beignets were beyond delicious. Most of the employees were very friendly. Angie the worker at the Julep was the rudest person ever. Even after my poor treatment by Angie, I thought I would try it again the following day. The worker I can't remember her name, was also rude. So apparently the workers at Julep are unfriendly, maybe a refresher course in customer service is needed. I loved Disneyland and will be back.

Having come from Disneyworld, it's definitely smaller than Orlando's Magic Kingdom. But still as magical. You can do both parks in 1 day, but would recommend getting a 2 day pass as you can do disneyland in one day, but you need more time for California Adventure.

Great time at the Happiest Place on Earth, despite my wife's B Day falling on an unusually rainy day at the park. The thinner crowds allowed us to enjoy all our favorite rides in record time.We were recognized by the staff throughout the park with our I'm Celebrating buttons, and the B Day Girl appreciated the recognition her Birthday button brought.As SoCal residents, we took advantage of 3 day special ticket, allowing for non consecutive day visits. We'll be back in April and early May.

Visited with my 9 yr old daughter, her first visit here. We maximized times that had minimal crowds (checked several websites) and made liberal uses of Fast Passes. Recommend watching YouTube videos for Disneyland hacks, tips, & recommendations. Our longest wait for a ride was 30 minutes! We got 4 day military special passes for $177 each, best bargain ever! All rides were magical except the sub ride...good effects but smelly & cramped.

Disneyland was the absolute highlight of our Anaheim trip!!!  We LOVED every minute we spent there!!!  It is truly the happiest place on earth, and we experienced it to the MAX!!!!! Thank you Disneyland!!!

Disneyland has just brought back it's light parade, so awesome! Disneyland has also started a new fire work show. The new fire works show has a light show intermingled. The show has various different story lines behind each display. Don't miss the fireworks for sure.

I have been to Disneyland 3 times. I probably won't go back until I have an 8 year old kid (currently childless, so...not for a long time). The park doesn't care about overcrowding and the ridiculous amount of strollers. They want your $100  for the day, and don't care about line wait times, or park capacity. 3 of the main attractions were closed, which was a bummer. It's just too pricey for two people to spend a day waiting in line for 4   5 rides. What's the point? Knotts Berry Farm and Universal Studios are 100x better, and have half the issues (and are more economical).

It was truly magical taking my family to Disneyland. This was where I went with my family as a child. The park has well   maintained parts of the old Disney and has so many expansions, it was incredible. I would definitely recommend bringing your family to Disneyland in California!

My Family and I have been to Disneyland 4 times now, we just returned last week. We had 5 days there. We kept busy everyday.There is so much to do and see and they add new things to keep it interesting. It is a very busy place,some days more busy than others but remember water, walking shoes(You do a lot),camera and just have fun!

While not as expansive and geared toward a long vacation like its Florida sibling, this park still has that charm of its 1950s (though I worry how all the new construction may change that). Still, there's magic here, and it has the best version of both Pirates, and it's a small world. If you can come during the holidays for the special version of Haunted Mansion, all the better.

I am not saying I dislike it but here is my thoughts, it costs too much, its usually too crowded, lines for princesses autographs and any other characters were way long, we basically spent the day waiting for autographs, looking for places to sit, and after fantasmic they pretty much herd you out of the park. It was definitely still fun for the kid, on the bright side it didn't take forever to get the kid fed or something to drink when she was thirsty, and there was a few rides that she was willing to go on so yea mission accomplished for the toddler, but I went alot as a kid and remembered it differently, now I know why you my dad and step mom literally got into a fight there...haha

Prefer a park hopper to California Adventure to a one park per day pass. Harder to find days with low crowds. If you go off season, the crowds are smaller, however, the park hours are also shorter and rides down for refurbishment. I just find it less magical when it is crowded and the lines are so long. Still worth it, though!

Return trip to disney, visited in 2014. I noticed a few changes. Decided to eat different foods this time as ate too much quick service before. Most staff really nice and friendly apart from one that was really snappy called Corina in toy mania.
We bought s 5 day park hopper ticket for Disneyland and California adventure park. It was well worth it.  We spent 10 to 11 hours at the parks each day.

We arrived at Disneyland at 9.30am. What a great day. So glad we didn't go in summer you wouldn't be able to move. Wait lines were good 25 mins max. Unfortunately due to some rain earlier the parade was cancelled moments before it was due to start. The fireworks display went ahead and it was spectacular. Left the park at 10.30 pm shattered. I would recommend getting a shuttle bus to and from your hotel. After a 12 hour day the idea of even a short walk was not appealing.

Disneyland was great. The lines at the rides were not long. For Indiana Jones. Hyper space, and, Star Tours, use fast pass. The mainstreet electrical parade was well worth seeing. Autopia is not the same with support from Honda rather than Chevron. If you are a Star Wars fan, there is a display about the history of star wars. You can meet Darth Vader, chewbaccs, and other Characters. The food is reasonably priced. They will accomodate food allergies.

This was the first time I've been to Disney in such a long time and it was truly fantastic. The weather was so hot but it was still a great day. Would probably recommend a couple of days, we only did one day, but felt we were able to squeeze the main rides in.You can get fast passes for rides but they have time limits and limits on how often you can get them. I would recommend getting the Space Mountain one first   we didn't and it broke down temporarily and then the wait time stayed at over an hour for the rest of the day. Would also recommend doing Splash Mountain early in the day, as the time we got for it, it had to close unexpectedly and when we got to ride it, we got soaked and didn't properly dry for the rest of the day : The Star Wars ride was good   I'm not a big Star Wars fan but it was a good experience. Haunted Mansion   great Buzz Lightyear Astro Blasters   more suited for kids, but it got my competitiveness going.Big Thunder Mountain   fast rollercoaster, loved it and screamed most of the way round!Mad Hatter Tea Party   everyone loves spinning cups Roger Rabbits Car Toon Spin   spinning cars, like a big kidFood   the food was mostly fast food and was very busy at meal times but we didn't find it a problem getting something to eat. The prices were a little expensive but we were on holiday and didn't want to carry things around with us.The night time parades run quite frequently   people start sitting and waiting at least 1 1.5 hours before to get a good spot, so make sure you get there early.Loved the parade, lots of lights, parade floats and great dancers.Transport wise, most people come by car. We were staying near Hollywood so we got an Uber to Disney. It took about an hour and cost about $60 each way. We felt this was reasonable.

Sunny, mid 70's and either a fast pass or lines shorter than 35 minutes. You can't beat that. I will never go to Disneyland during the busy season, it just wouldn't be worth it. There were no crowds, few long lines and the hotels were way cheaper. I can't even imagine enjoying our trip if it was hot, super crowded and super long lines. The kids would have just melted down and been miserable. It was well worth 3 missed days of school.

This was our 2nd trip to Disneyland with out two children. The first trip was 3 years ago when our kids were 7 years old, in July   poor decision. It was super hot and the lines wait times were ridiculous.We decided to do a Disney Do Over. Now that our kids are 10 years old we thought this would be a more reasonable age for them to go and enjoy all that is Disney. We opted to go in February this time thinking it would be far less hot and far less people.The temperature was definitely better although apparently it rains far more than Californians let on. No biggie, we are from Victoria so a little rain is just a regular day for us. The lines were decent without ridiculous line ups like we had experienced when visiting in the summer. Our only gripe was the amount of times rides broke down! Omg. We went on the haunted mansion 5 times and it broke down every single time. Space mountain broke down twice, Alice in wonderland ride was closed for basically 2 days, big thunder mountain broke down, mad hatter tea cups was closed (not scheduled refurbs). Maybe we just had bad luck as it seemed like every time we headed for a ride it was either broken down and closed or broke down while we were on it.Also pirates of the Caribbean was closed the entire 5 days for refurbishments and Matterhorn bobsleds was closed for refurb on day 2 for the remainder of our 5 days.We were aware of this prior to visiting but it still sucked.We were there Friday   Tuesday and Friday night, Saturday and Sunday were extremely busy (summertime busy) but Friday during the day, Monday and Tuesday were amazing with barely any wait times. We had 1 magic morning which we took advantage of (only good for Thursdays, Saturdays and Tuesdays) on the Tuesday (our last day) and were shocked to learn the Magic Morning is only good for rides in Tomorrowland & Fantasyland   Silly us, we thought it was good for the whole park and we tried to head for Indiana Jones ...The park is definitely overpriced in my opinion. Our 5 day park hopper tickets were like $1200 USD which seems pretty out of reach for the average family. Overall visiting Disney in February was great for less people, shorter lines wait times and mild temperatures but not the best for having the  fun  rides all operating and seemed a lot broke down this visit and the ticket cost is the same.

I prefer this place to any other Disneyland as it is the original. The park is not very big and full of rides and attractions. You don't have to walk too far as in the Magic Kingdom in Disney World. The line wasn't too bad as in Tokyo Disneyland. This is my favorite Disneyland of all.
The Disneyland is nice, but the ticket prices are awful nowadays! Place is really crowded so it's better to go early and take the best rides and sites first.
This was my wife's 4th time and she still enjoyed every bit. She said most of the rides were the same but the show Frozen was new and awesome! If I had the chance to see it again I would.

Everything I could dream and more! The park is small compared to Disney World, but so much is packed into the small space. Mickey's Magical Map is a must see! The Matterhorn Bobsleds were a top choice as well!

It is going to be impressive no doubt. I think everyone should at least go once. However, if given a choice I think you should go here before Disney World. If it is the other way around Disneyland seems a lot less impressive.
we had a day at Disneyland and the lineups were short and the weather held.  Most rides we were 25min. on and off.
All life's worries disappear when I go here. I cannot wait to go back later this year for our yearly trip.

Spent over $1500USD for a family of 5 with 3 day pass at Dis Cal land in late January. Crowds were epic, worst I have experienced anywhere in the world making. Each day at least two of their prized blue ribbon rides were closed for maintenance, which upon re opening had lines up to 2 hours long! Fast passes got us onto them all with a 1 hour max wait. Such waits though really are excessive, why can't the park limit maximum crowd number? Why can't families with young kids buy an early entry from 7am like in house guests? Keeping track of young kids in the crowds is most stressful, with park diners offering overpriced poor food that did little to help relax there. Why can't Disney service ALL rides each night to minimise risk of failing during opening hours?? Run a ski resort like this and they would fail miserably.

I love disney! California's park was the first of all so it's nice visiting it. It is way smaller than orlando's. It has 2 parks that can be done in a day choosing the attractions wisely. It's better to stay one night so as to visit it at your own pace.

This is Disney   what else can you say? It has been a long time since I was here, opting to go to Orlando. I remember it being smaller. It is smaller than Orlando but it feels well organized. Were there mid week late January (single day tickets to the park on Tuesdays are cheaper) so the lines were fast. Only ride were I spent more than 15 minutes was at  Finding Nemo , which is a slow ride and not found in Orlando (used to be  20,000 leagues    same submarine concept, but now with the Nemo characters). We decided only to do the Disneyland Park, but if you want to add California Adventure it is literally right in front   for the Orlando regulars it is a weird feeling to have two Disney parks so close by. In my opinion LA Anaheim have much more to offer than Orlando as a city, so if you want to do more things than just parks this is a good option. If you are in an  only parks  kind or trip, then go to Orlando.

Happiest place on earth.  We had a great day.  Fast pass system is great.  You feel like  a special person when you go to the head of the line without needing to pay extra for a  VIP  pass.  Brilliant system!
What can be more magical than a day at Disneyland. We loved A Small, Small World and Pirates of the Carribean .The Day and evening parades were lovely and the fireworks display spectacular.

Had to get park hopper tickets and enjoy Disneyland for my 40th birthday! The lines weren't bad at all and we got to go on everything! Even had lunch at the Blue Bayou, it was a fabulous day! If the fireworks are a must for you, check the schedule first, they didn't have them the day we were there.
Absolutely love a trip to Disney rain or shine!!! My kids and I really enjoy our annual Disneyland trip! No complaints! Just fun!

Wonderful experience for all! First timers from the east coast. We are a family of Disney geeks having been to Disney World many times. Had a great time experiencing both parks. Nice imagining Walt walking around here...
We are from Orlando and used to long theme park lines. Even though the park was busy, we never waited longer than 30 minutes.  It's Disneyland, what else to say?

This was the most wonderful experience. I am now a Disney fan for life. I will return as often As we can. Our kids had so much fun and the are almost 3. They where able to do so much and they where free since they aren't 3 yet. Thanks for making it so fun Disneyland cast. Every one was so friendly and helpful.

Went to park during extra hour before park opens to general public. Lined up well in advance. Went right to Peter Pan ride. Managed to go through half of park, and see all characters photos autographs for 5 year old within about 7 hour trip. Download app as shows where characters are and ride times, in real time. Used fast pass for space mountain and Indiana Jones rides.

This was a work vacation for me with the family.  My husband and kids had a great time and didn't want to go home!  Disney was great as always with rides and all of the LO CAL food options!  Thanks Disney and Anaheim.

This was my first time at Disneyland (having been to Disney World a number of times). Positive experience   all the fun with fewer steps between each! As always at Disney, clean with pleasant people manning the rides and walking the streets. We went at the end of January   GREAT time to go to avoid the horrible crowds and endless lines. It's fun and both kid and handicapped friendly. We spent one day at Disney and one at the California Experience Park   fun, but enough time in each. Definitely worth visiting if you're in the area.

Unfortunately they have continued to disappoint us. Disneyland of 10 years ago is not today. They need to  backtrack . Not let people pay for passes on time, not take little  perks  away like blocking areas from fireworks. Many other items too numerous to list. Still love our Dland! Passholders 24 years

I love Disneyland. They get so many things so right. Lunch at the Blue Bayou was delicious and fun, the Main Street Electrical Parade was terrific and nostalgic, and the Dole Whip was just a good as I remembered it. I was there with my 68 year old mother and my two daughters, ages 8 and 13, and we all loved the princess story time with Belle. With the help of the Disneyland app we met many characters, and with the help of the app and Fastpasses, we never waited longer than 20 minutes for any ride. Even so, the park felt crowded. I think the construction is partially to blame, with the closure of the river and all its attractions, plus high volume rides It's a Small World and the Jungle Cruise were both closed. In our one day, we didn't manage to do everything, but we did all our favorite things.

Three generations can easily have a wonderful time.  Grandparents can get Fast passes for kids future rides if they are partaking of the vigorous rides to save time and allow them to see more.  Meet up for meals.  Don't forget your cell phones!

My sister wanted to go for her birthday and I obliged with only one condition. I would only pay 50 bucks. I said that because I knew finding a ticket for 50 bucks would be next to impossible. Well who would have thought she would actually find the way to get me a ticket for 50 bucks. So I was forced to go. So I'm a big kid and I love kid things, but something about Disney doesn't do it for me. I don't feel the magic as many others do. It had been 14 years since I had gone, and I was a little excited upon arrival. Once in, that's where the excitement sort of took a turn. It's a weekday, and the place is PACKED. Yes, the happiest place on Earth had the entire world there. Here's what is cool: The Fast Pass. Yes get em! If you take several minutes to read the map and map everything out you can get the Fast passes and ride all the rides in one day. We did just that. Well let me give credit to my sister, she did that. I don't have the patience and I get turned around in amusement parks. She had it down packed. The rides are for people who don't like thrills. Sure the wet ride with the big drop and another has a little speed to it. I guess I am the  need for speed  type of person. Here everything is appropriate for all ages who are not thrill seekers. None of the rides should have a height limit. We had dinner at a pretty yummy place. It was a place you could sit down and have a few choices of a meal vs the quick burger hotdog type of food. There was a nice variety of food, and it was tasty too. My disappointments:I was totally bummed out by no captain EO. I knew it was not there anymore, but I was still bummed being there missing it. Yes I just told my age, I know. : ) So here is the ULTIMATE disappointment. I was so excited about seeing the fireworks. Well there were NONE. The show was canceled. I was so sad. If I had paid the full price to get in I probably would have cried tears. I will not be back here anytime soon. Maybe if I had kids, I will take them to enjoy the happiest place on Earth.
Typical Disney, hasn't changes excessively since our first visit over 30 years ago. Still as busy, only much more expensive. If you don't have multi day tickets expect to pay almost $100 at the gate.

Visits to Disneyland are the biggest treat in our annual travel agenda that has included location throughout the US and Europe. Disneyland has been a master at continuous improvement and rather than resting on its laurels the park is continually improved and more value and entertainment added. I hate to leave and as soon as I leave I look forward to the next visit.

Disneyland is a monument to crowd control and grace under pressure. The government should use DL as a training ground for agents and police   these people are never rattled, always pleasant, and in complete control of the situation. The park is always fun, but it felt like there were more mechanical problems than ever. Several rides were going on and off often, we even got turned away in line a few times. But the Matterhorn was open and it was great.The Star Wars overlay was cool, but it changed Space Mountain a little too much for our tastes. And we got to meet Chewbacca!Make sure you save up for this trip, tickets are not cheap and everything else is pretty steep.
Incredible in every way. Loved the parades, loved the rides, most people are really friendly. Definitely worth going by yourself if noone else goes with you.
We had a blast. Firework show was week compared to years past and Electric Street Parade was great for older people but my kids enjoyed previous parades much more

Pretty crumby weather but we tried to make the most of it. Wanted to get to see some characters first so went straight to toontown and it began a heavy down pour. We saw Pluto off to a distance as we huddled at a picnic table under an umbrella. Ponchos in their stores were $10 EACH! When we had enough we tried to make a run for it back to the entrance but the area was flooded and we had a stroller with two youngsters (age 10 months and 2 years) so we circled back to see if there was another way out but nope. Toontown only has one way in out and its under the monorail bridge which is where it was flooded the worst. Had to wait for the rain to ease up so we could get through.Can't complain about the weather but the price of a poncho sucked and the feeling of being trapped wasn't fun either.Going back again and hoping for good weather this time, but bringing them ponchos just in case! Cheers

Attended Disneyland in January with Family of 5. Not   newbies   to Disneyland,last time had a 10 day pass for family so a little bit familiar with whole Disney theme..... we were in early group entering so would have thought Disney Staff would have been Fresh and Happily greeting   Guests  ..... The lady at the gate we entered was more sour than a lemon ! No Good Morning, No welcome to Disneyland ......in fact don't think she spoke at all, she just gestured with her hand what she wanted. After Entering and walked around a bit notice more cast members had similar blank, uninterested faces.With teenagers now, and found 1 day at Disneyland and 1 day at Disney California was more than enough. Just did the main rides and that was that. Could not be bothered with the wait times at the popular rides ie, Hyper Space Mountain..... then it wasn't working anyway later in the day. Did Star Tours once only up to an hour wait....... even Peter Pan was over 40 minutes ??? very surprised at the time of year so many people on a Tuesday?And the Price of Food inside is insanely expensive....when you consider the price of the Park Tickets as well ....really think we've done our dash with Disney.

Disney is SO crowded, it really just takes away from the experience when you can't move around too well. SOOOOO many strollers to dodge (I know because we were using one too) and long waits. Thank goodness for the few Fastpasses we were able to use during our time. Food outrageously expensive, but you know, you get more value at Disney, food wise, than at San Diego Zoo. I WILL say that! And at least Disney really tries to make it taste good unlike the zoo.

My family enjoyed our Disney trip a great deal. I recommend if you're going to go to Disneyland with the family just once, because you live far away or whatever the reason, wait until your kids are at least 7 or 8 years old. That way your kids can enjoy most of the rides and also remember the trip for years to come. There are many rides which younger kids can't go on because of their size. There are lots of rides for the younger ones too, but it's definitely best if they're not too young.
Disapointment from the kids anout missing the parade.  No seating and pushy adults.  Should be able to pre book a spot.  3 days and no parade.

If you are in Anaheim, you're obviously going to Disney. Couple tips:1 Disney allows outside food and drink. Load up those backpacks for the kids and save a ton of cash by bringing in your own food.2 Bring in an extra shirt for each kid... or a trash bag to cover yourself. You'll get soaked on Splash Mountain   it's the name of the ride for goodness sakes. Rather than listen to the kids complain, change their shirts. Otherwise, you'll find yourself dropping $24 on a t shirt while your kid cries   and you'll cry while pulling out that AMEX.3   Go to Autopia right when the park opens. The line for this ride is always long. Why? I have no idea. But trust me. It'll be at least an hour if you wait until later in the day... even on a WEDNESDAY. Ugh.4 Download the app. It tells you wait times. That way, when your kid asks, 'Can we go on Autopia?' you can immediately see the line is an hour long.. and tell them the ride is broken.5 Disneyland doesn't sell alcohol. Sure, that's the way some of us survive amusement parks but Disney hates us. If you want a beer to help you get through this, go to California Adventure. It's less busy and everyone is in a better mood   mainly because we've had a beer to take the edge off.Enjoy Disney!
We love Disneyland! One tip for anyone doing Disneyland don't go Friday to Monday the park is pack!!! And people get a very me first attitude when it's that packed.

I went to Disneyland last weekend with my friends. I bought a ticket for $105 at the ticket office in front of Disneyland. I recommend that you buy a ticket online in advance because it will be cheaper than the ticket office where I bought mine. I entered Disneyland Park around 9:30 a.m. The park opens at 8 a.m. and there were already a lot of people. I recommend you download a Disneyland app which has all of Disneyland   s information, including wait times for attractions and locations of the Disney characters. Disneyland Park is divided into 6 big areas, like Tomorrowland and Fantasyland. First, I went to Tomorrowland and picked up a fastpass ticket for Star Wars Hyperspace Mountain. It was so exciting and speedy, and I really wanted to ride it again but I gave up because of the long line. I went on only 5 rides because they were so crowded and had long lines. At night, there was a parade at 8:30 p.m. and fireworks at 9:25 p.m. They were so beautiful and splendid. I highly recommend going to Disneyland.

This journey was the first journey to LA. I saw UCLA, the Getty Center, Santa monica and other amazing places. The highlight was Disneyland. Disneyland is divided into two places. One is California Adventure Park, and the other is Disneyland park. California Adventure Park consists of rides, and Disneyland park has fairy tale scenes. Where we went was Disneyland park. Although it doesn't have as many rides as California Adventure Park, Disneyland has few rides like Pirates of the Caribbean and Indiana Jones. They were well decorated, not scary. Also, I could take a photo with Disney characters. Before going to Disneyland, here are some tips. First, the food in Disneyland is expensive. You should prepare something to eat. Actually, This is not allowed. Next, you should get the anniversary badge in City Hall which is in Disneyland. It is a badge for Disneyland visitors. It's all free! The last one is the most important. You can see the parade and fireworks every day! They start in the evening, and Many famous characters like Mickey mouse, Minnie mouse, Cinderella and Sleeping Beauty participate in the parade. After it, The fireworks goes for 5 minutes. It was memorable that I can remember it vividly even now. If you visit LA, Don't forget Disneyland. I would highly recommend it.

We came here on a very rainy day. Which is very rare for LA in general. However, that didn't hinder the experience at all. I'd even argue that it made the whole experience better. The lines for everything were significantly shorter. We were able to easily cover the whole park in one day. The service at any of the eating places in the park were better than what you'd find outside. This park caters towards families so there's something enjoyable for all kinds of people.

Love to visit the park but they need to improve their communication! Why have a live information app if you wait to turn kids away AT THE GATE?!Our situation was unusual but it was disappointing: it's not Disneyland's fault we visited during a rainy weekend. We waited until evening when the rain cleared away to head to the park only to be told at the gate it was closing early. I had been watching the app for any info but there'd been no warning. It hadn't occurred to me to check twitter because i assumed the Disneyland app would show an alert but no :( a ticket wasted and a hysterical child to take back to our hotel. So make sure you check ALL their sources of communication!

We just visited on 1 27 17 and experienced the majority of the rides kept breaking down. There were SO many people there during the  off season  and yet with so limited rides that were actually running, the lines were 60  minutes for everything. There were so many strollers everywhere, it was really difficult to get anywhere. I wish Disney would figure our some better crowd control options to help the flow around the park. The park itself was clean and magical. It's frustrating to pay almost $800 for a family of four (2 day pass) to have the majority of rides keep breaking down. Feels like someone's pockets are getting bigger and that money isn't being put back into the park for maintenance and customer satisfaction. I feel like Mr. Disney would be disappointed if he were alive to hear this experience.
Like Disneyland I can only recommend to all ages. Everybody can find what he likes. Very good for one day trip with or without children.

What can I say...it's Disney and they have it figured out. We've been to Disney world before but still really enjoyed Disneyland. Much more manageable with small children. What impresses me about Disney the number of people that visit daily yet the grounds are meticulous, clean and well organized. The water show is a must as well as the fire works.
We'll be back soon! 5 days, and 72 miles walked, 3 pounds lost and I can't wait to get back to the happiest place on earth!
We LOVE Disneyland!  The cleanliess and friendly staff make the park even more enjoyable!  We look forward to visiting the parks again this spring!

I love Disneyland and have wanted to take my kids for a long time. We finally were able to visit from Australia and unfortunately due to new sections and rides being built there were quite a few attractions not available. This would be fine, except Disneyland also choose the winter to perform maintenance on rides, which meant that an additional ride was closed. Add this to the fact that it was raining and this resulted in other rides also closing   as you can imagine our kids were a little disappointed. However   the day was still amazing! The staff are well trained, friendly and enthusiastic. The fast pass system runs well and my two boys thoroughly enjoyed the jedi training which was rescheduled for the following day for us as it is also cancelled in the rain. Disneyland puts on a wonderful day   but I can't imagine visiting on a really busy day as you wouldn't get to see or do very much due to massive overcrowding. Food is generally expensive but this is always the case with fun parks. I highly recommend the gumbo in the New Orleans section of the park.

It's hard to leave a review for Disneyland. I feel like there's so much to say, and yet  It's just so wonderful  seems to be enough.I've been three times (twice with family, once with friends) before this trip with my husband, and each time has been magical. It doesn't matter that I'm grown up now   it's still just as wonderful.For anyone traveling there for the first time, here's what I'd recommend:  Get to the gates one hour to 45 minutes before the park opens. When they start letting people in 30 minutes before official opening time, get in there and as close to your first ride choice as you can.  Hit up Indiana Jones, Matterhorn, Peter Pan, or Hyperspace Mountain first thing. The lines will be long all throughout the day.  Use those Fast Passes! Always have at least one in your possession at all times.  Bring a backpack with snacks. The food and snacks available everywhere are SO tempting. Go ahead and splurge a few times, but you'll spend way too much money if you buy something every time you're hungry.  Don't go for just one day. The chances of you getting on every ride you want to is so slim, and why go on the best rides only once when the second, third, and seventh experiences can be even more fun?  Download and use the DLR Lines app. It gives pretty accurate wait times for all rides, so you don't have to walk across the park to a ride just to find it's got a long wait time.  And last, but definitely not least, do not go at one of the busy times of the year.Anyways, I love Disneyland. Can't wait to go back.
if you're in California you just cannot miss Disneyland... this is the very first Disney Theme park opened in the 40's! Definitely a cult place for every age child.
We LOVE Disneyland.  We love the music,  the friendly cast members and the rides.  No matter what time of year we have traveled to Disneyland we have always had a great time.

We visited with our children the week after Christmas and would never do so again. Don't get me wrong, we love Disneyland, and we ended up having a good time. However, the crowds were enormous, literally making it difficult to move from one side of a walkway to another by the time afternoon came around. We were able to ride plenty of rides utilizing Ridemax and the fastpsss system, but people that did not do any planning were in huge lines (some at 180 minutes), which did not seem worth it to me. The holiday decorations were beautiful and it was cool to see the park transformed for Christmas. I would recommend going any other time if the year though!

Yes it is the happiest place on earth. great for old or young. if you are visiting the west coast don't miss this. Disney world is bigger but 98% the same thing. so whatever one is closer to you is the best for you. Even though the place was built in 1955 everything is kept in new condition. They are always updating and maintaining. Wear your best walking shoes and plan to leave exhausted. Show up early for breakfast with the characters and leave after the fireworks late. your kids wont leave until they are ready to pass out anyway. You won't be able to do everything in two days. and many rides will be good for a 2nd 3rd of 4th time. So plan 3 or 4 days. split those days up with one or two days at California Adventure making a trip to Anaheim at least 3 and as many as 5 days on the parks. Tips:1. Look for deals on the DL website that include hotels and entry tickets. 2. Prepaying for meals is cheaper than paying throughout the days. 3. Make reservations at some eating places days in advance.4. Don't expect to drive home after a day in DL or CA. you are going to be too tired. Stay one more night off property and drive home the next day. 5. Probably do the same coming in on the 1st day. Get an off property room the night before and get up at 6:30 for the early park entry and character breakfast.

Even though we live 60 miles from Disney World , we make the trek to Disneyland because there is special magic in the original. It is always crowded, even off season. The characters seem to be more accessible and cast members more engaged in making them available.

Visited Disneyland solo to celebrate my 50 th. It was a magical, wonderful experience. I surprised myself in that I pretty much did all the rides. I did not feel intimidated or lonely as people chatted in the lines as we waited for the ride. ( I think they were fascinated by my story of travelling from Australia solo leaving my Hubble and kids at home)It is truely the happiest place in the world. I could not wipe the smile from my face all day and throughout the evening. The Christmas de orations and shows were equally amazing. I am so happy I got to experience at the tender age of 50

Disneyland is always the go to spot for any visitors we have in town.   My favorite spots to eat:   Plaza Inn on Main street for the Fried Chicken plate.  Corn Dog Castle at California Adventure for hot link corn dog.

we love to visit this park. it never gets old. the pricing is def. outrages nowadays. sadly, some families cant visit as often due to the pricing. despite that, any day at Disneyland will be enjoyed be people of all ages.this is a full day type of park, perhaps even a multiple day type of visit in order to try and do as much as possible.

Nice to kind of see parade again, and I say kind of because of the enormous crowds. It was like NYC Time Square. Very difficult at times to see. Disney employees did not allow children or anyone to sit or kneel so it was difficult for anyone to see!

Went into Disneyland and there were a few rides , of course the good ones, were down for maintanence. This is the third time I have been to the park where the Matterhorne broke down , again. With so many good rides down, it made the lines longer on the rides that were open. The good was we were able to see the Electric Light Parade..

My husband and I went to Disneyland together for the first time on Sunday. I've been to the park at least 10 times since childhood but this time the magic was gone. It started with 3 of the 4 rides we wanted to go on being closed  Pirates of the Caribbean, Thunder mountain railroad, and Small World. We spent $210 for two of us for one park and were so disappointed. The ticket counter clerk should have mentioned what rides are down as we may not have wasted our time or money. Then the locker took our money without giving us change. What a ripoff! City Hall did give us our  stolen  change without any hassle plus 4 fast passes in an effort to console us but we had to wait 30 minutes to speak to an associate. The fireworks and electric light parade are spectacular! Dinner at the French Cafe was good, especially the French dip. We enjoyed our visit but won't be back for a while due to the crowds and expense. I don't know how families can afford to come here. Parking alone is $18 and lockers start at $7. Disneyland used to be the  happiest place on earth , now it's the most expensive.

Went on the first warm & sunny week end in 3 weeks, so Saturday at Disneyland was really busy. The Disneyland app shows where the lines are short and where Fast Passes are available, which made it easier to plan which ride to choose. It also made it possible to avoid traveling all the way to one part of the park only to learn that a ride wasn't working, as one of my friends learned about the Indiana Jones ride. I only wish the app would tell you where there were tables available outside the restaurants!

Fun for all ages, lots of rides, food options, shopping, entertainment, etc... The recent refurbishing of Star Tours and Space Mountain are awesome. (Star Tours now has multiple adventures) While we were there, there was flooding due to rain and a few of the rides had times they shut down and then reopened. This has never happened so often to me at Disneyland so I think it is just a fluke.

A fantastic land that you can meet every cartoon character you were familiar with since your childhood and you can take pictures with everyone if you'd like to. The attractions here also have a lot of fun and every moment you spent in the main street is memorable.

I have been going to Disneyland about once a year for about 20 years now. After my visit this past weekend, I think it will be a much longer stretch before I go back again. I was expecting heavy crowds, since I made the choice to go over a weekend, but was still overwhelmed when I was in the thick of it all. People with strollers clog up many areas of the park and made it very difficult to get around. Several rides broke down throughout the day, one happened when we were next to get on the ride. Another ride posted a 45 minute wait for standby, but it turned out to be 90 minutes. We waited in line for 60 minutes for a game playing ride, only to have the game not work once our car got inside. Food and drink prices had gone up even more since my last visit. One of the people in my party got sick after eating a salad at the park. The park itself, usually pristine, was a mess. Garbage cans were overflowing in many of the eating areas and bathrooms were unclean. We had lovely interaction with only two employees during our visit, most others seemed just  Blah  about working there. It seemed like the park was understaffed and unprepared for the large crowd. With the increase in ticket prices, I expect Disneyland to continue to operate with excellence and provide exceptional service. They missed the mark by a wide margin on this visit.

Disneyland just seems to get more crowded all the time which is tough with little ones. The wait times seem to be never ending which makes the experience not as much fun. But it is still one of the most magical places on earth they say.

About an hour from Downtown LA, this place is a gem. Its actually a world by itself     a world that one would wish was for real. Whatever your age, one ends up discovering the child within. Unfortunately, we kept only one day for it; one can easily spend couple of days. The place is purest form of entertainment and the Sensational parade is simply out of the world. Don   t miss this parade and find yourself a good viewing spot well in advance as both sides of the road get very crowded during the parade. Bring out the child within you and you wont find a place more enjoyable than this. I am certainly going back whenever I get a chance.
We went January 4 for one day and it was way to busy. I would go for at least 3 days just to Disneyland and would go in the days with less crowds.

I did two days in disneyland over Christmas and loved every minute. Two days was enough to see everything we wanted to do, but if you can try and do three days. Over two parks there are always shows going on, and lines take awhile. Make sure you download the app to help you plan your visit.
I have no words to describe how amazing this place is. My children had so much fun!!! Even my mother thought of this place being the happiest place in the world!
We adults had more fun than our 7 yr old. I rode a roller coaster for the first time in my 71 yrs and it was so much fun.

We haven't been to Anaheim Disney land for a quite while. This place was transformed into more unique, California Disney land. Certainly, California Adventure had a hint of some Disney worlds attraction and Disney sea from Tokyo but twisted to its own unique way. Nicely done!Disney land itself has made a great change. Autopia was a longest and nicest go cart I have ever tried. Nimo's submarine was uniquely introducing the world of sea along with Nimo's adventure. Story telling boat was miniature, fantasy land. Very sadly, some famous  major attractions such as It's a small world, jungle cruise, train etc were refurbished or closed.Weekends were ridiculously crowded including food court  they really should think about  less congesting  strategy. But as always, Disney's dreamy business style, which creates a fun and great time to their customers is beyond stunning.
Had an awesome time.  If you're in Southern California not to be missed.  We could not be happier with our visit.

It was my first time doing Disney with my toddler, and experiencing it from a toddlers point of view. So many rides for the younger ones and the Fast Pass worked great for rides like Buzz Lightyear. I wish they did Fast Pass for Finding Nemo, which was an incredible ride but is a long ride, which means long lines (to be fair, the line was only 30 minutes, but we were spoiled because there were no lines during our trip). The baby care center was a great find and will definitely be taking advantage of that once my next little comes along. Even though I didn't do any of the adult rides, this was my favorite Disney experience yet. The electrical parade at night was cool but wish it were a little longer! We did the VIP experience which I recommend where you get priority viewing. We went end of January and only had to wait about 5 minutes for rides, or they were walk on.

I'll start off by acknowledging that the production quality of Disney is first rate. The cast members were wonderful; warm friendly and very helpful. However, as great as that is, here are the negatives: Overcrowded, even on  off peak days.  Wait to get get your bag checked.  Wait to get your body scanned.  Wait to enter park. Rush to get fast pass. Rush to get in line for ride. Stand in line for one hour, enjoy 5 minute ride. After waiting in long lines, rides break down. (Happened to us 3 times) Dodge constant wave of people and strollers.  Rush to get next fast pass. Wait in line again. Wait in slow line for drinks. Wait in line for food. Search for tables to sit & eat. Hunt for restrooms. Wait in line for restrooms. Oh yeah, lots of waiting and fighting crowds. I get it! If the these things don't bother you, Disneyland can be totally worth it. However, I really don't want to hustle & strategize on vacation. It was too much work & stress to truly enjoy the   magic.

I went here as a kid. And this time I brought my kid. There is to much to write about and so many things you can do and see and miss out due to running out of time or simply missing something cool in a nook and cranny. Splash mountain was good, though it scared my 7 year old. Honestly I only have a couple of complaints because everything else was great. First of all, the lines were crazy long and the place was beyond crowded   even in the early morning and before closing, despite also being school days! A few of the rides seemed last minute rehashes to fit in with newer Disney marketing   such as the submarine ride being  done up  to fit in with Finding Nemo. Also Space Mountain seems to have been transformed into a loosely based Star Wars ride by simply putting some TV screens with SW space ships flying around and some green flashing lights (pretend laser fire), and some loud speakers. Also, the food we had at the Star Wars stand was pretty horrible. Anyway, pretty much everything else was awesome and I wish we went there again the next day instead of the California Adventure place next door.

We love Disneyland and we go all the time. Hands down best experience ever!!!!! Best place to take the family. Rides for everyone and so much to do and see. The Characters are the best! They really take their time with the kids in line to see them. Can't wait to go back.

Whatever age you might be, if you are still young at heart , you will love this place. All kinds of adventures await you and time just flies when you are in the park. Most of the rides are decent and not scary, so the more adventurous among you should try the California Adventure park just next to this.
Always fun. The park is always so well  maintained. There's always something new and yet the 'old friends ' we fondly remember are always there..

Went to Disneyland for a special event and it was great. No long lines for rides. Park was open till 1am for the event. We got to ride so many rides. Kids had a great time. Looking forward to next years event

We did a family trip last fall and everyone had a blast! From my little nephews (ages 5 and 7) to in laws and grandparents   our group had non stop fun and endless entertainment! Take advantage of those Magic Mornings. Get up early and hit the parks when they first open to take advantage of short wait times. We often met back up for breakfast around 9am when the park opened to the general public. Also the Halloween Party is MUST!

Absolutely enjoyed our time at Disneyland. Such a wonderful theme park, very family friendly, rides for adults, and fortunately the day with that we wed the lines were not too long. All of the entertainment in the park was top notch, I cannot wait to take my family back again

It has been 26 years since I've last been to Disneyland. It continues to amaze me and make me feel like a kid again. They have found new ways to cater to all sorts of guest needs including the new downtown area which is a nice addition since my last visit
No more fireworks everyday!!! Sucked big time! They earn so much money not to give its patrons a good show! Electric parade is boring!!!
Our family love the original Disneyland!  We love the history, the character opportunities, the rides and pretty much everything about this Disney Park.  Still as great as ever!  MUST DO!!

We still spent 5 hours at the Park in spite of the rain and benefitted from the inclement weather by not having to wait more than 5 minutes to access rides. The wet didn't dampen the spirits of the Disney characters, we liked Cruella de Ville but the highlight was meeting Moana. We purchased $10 plastic ponchos which now double as a holiday souvenir. Favourite rides were a close call between BIg Thunder Mountain Railroad and the Matterhorn Bobsleds. Do take the time to at least walk through Candy Palace, it's got some creative concoctions!

Let's be honest if you're going on Trip Advisor for a review of Disneyland, there is something wrong with your travel plans. Place is great. 20yrs between visits and the whole family was excited about being there. It's the original and the best.
Expensive and lines, but you already know that. Some amazing rides that you just can't find anywhere else. We are always impressed with the excellent customer service.

One of the most renowned and famous places I've visited as a child, Disneyland has always opened my eyes and encouraged me with all of its fascinating wonderful world theme! Now even in Shanghai there's a Disneyland Park!! Amazing over all. Visited back in Apr 2012.

Disneyland is a great, clean family friendly environment that allows everyone to be a child again. The magic is stil here! Yes, the lines can be long and the food overpriced, but the ability of this park to bring back warm memories is strong. We had the pleasure of seeing the Main Street Electrical Parade which I saw as a young child. Wow, how awesome to experience it again. Even the music was the same as I remember! The Star Wars Launch Bay was an excellent new addition. Our favourites are probably similar to many other visitors: Hyperspace Mountain, Big Thunder Railroad, Pirates of the Caribbean, Matterhorn Bobsleds, Haunted Mansion, Autopia, Splash Mountain and StarTours. Even though It's a Small World, Jungle Cruise and the Disneyland Railroad were closed for refurbishment, there were still most other rides open for everyone to enjoy. Thumbs up for Dole Whips, the monorail and churros! Overall, the staff members are smiling and cheerful. Very positive visit! Thanks, Walt!

We decided to celebrate our 21st wedding anniversary with our kids 8, 11, and 14 at Disneyland. We chose a 3 Day Hopper. Inclement weather: rain, wind, hail, flash floods and lightening impacted our visit. But we made the most of it and the kids still had fun even though it was a soggy mess and the 3rd day Disneyland closed super early because it became so flooded. Water was up to our ankles in some areas of the park. We were prepared though with ponchos and rain suits we braved the monsoon type Storm until they kicked everyone out of the park. We didn't even get to use our hopper to go to California Adventure because weather was so bad. Main Street was flooded, ducks were swimming down Main Street, Frontierland under flooded water. It was crazy an amazing site as wind pushed rain and tree branches and umbrellas sideways die hard parents like us kept going on rides as much as we could with our kidos. Hey when can you get on rides like Star Tours, Hyperspace Mountain, Big Thunder, Indiana Jones, Splash Mountain (already wet anyway), Matterhorn in 5 10 minutes? Though we didn't see Mickey Mouse or Minnie Mouse at all and of course the electric parade that they just brought back and the fireworks show was cancelled, most of the rides kept going at Disneyland. At California Adventure Screaming was only a 5 minute wait... Kids went again and again. We got a bunch of hail that sent everyone in the Park running for shelter, but after that was done everyone went back to the rides. Cars kept opening then closing because the track would get soaked and messed with the audio electrical system. But the wait was anywhere from 10 to 30 minutes. So Friday it rained all day went to both parks. No convenient stands were open, no characters walking around, a soggy mess by the time we went home. Saturday there was a nice break but it was COLD. Still didn't bring a huge crowd. It was the best of the days we were there. Sunday 3rd day was the deluge of flood water and you know it's bad when everyone with smartphones gets a flash flood warning message and Disneyland is announcing over the PA system flash flood warnings and saying they will be closing the park due to inclement weather. As sad as that was we were glad to make our way back to the hotel to remain safe when water is at your ankles anyway. The weather won that day. We felt so bad for the kids because we didn't get a full day out of it nor did we get to visit California Adventures. We were suppose to leave the next day. So on Monday (the day were to leave) of course it was a bit nicer weather with sun peeks, so we went to guest services at Disneyland and said hey what can you guys do for us? We got 3 day hoppers but due to the weather weren't able to use them on day 3 because Disneyland closed the park. So guest services gave us a free 1 day hopper for all of us! awesome! So We Extended our trip one more day and our kids were so happy and kept thanking us for that extra day. We called our hotel that we had just checked out of (Park Vue Inn) and were able to book one more night. So glad we did. Everyone was happy! Thank you Disneyland!

This park is so much stinking fun. This was my first visit to Disneyland in about 35 years. I was raised in Southern California and went to Disneyland numerous times of the time I was eight to about the time I was 25. Went to many grad night at Disneyland. Boy has it changed. But it still has a lot of people on the style Jake things that make Disneyland special. It was wonderful to see the parts for the eyes of my grandchildren

Taking you back to your childhood! Spent an entire day with my husband and 2 year old and we had the best time! The rides are fun and relevant to classic movies we grew up on. Something for every age to enjoy.Enjoyed also the variety of food and sweets. Caramel apple is a must!

There is no shortage of anything in Disneyland, including food, people, rides, attractions, sights, and stimulus. That said, it is also so fun, entertaining, and enjoyable. Plan on spending lots of money in addition to your ticket, because everything is expensive there. Be prepared for line ups at every major attraction, that will only lengthen as the day goes on. We went Monday to Friday with Monday being a rainy cool day. The crowds increased each successive day as the temperature rose. By friday it was packed! Almost impossible to move in some areas like tomorrow land and Adventureland. We left early that day because of the crowds...just too hard to navigate with kids in tow. Overal, though,it was great time everyday. The kids and the adults loved it!

I took my 4 year old son here exactly 30 years after my own first Disneyland experience. It was a truly magical day. I can't believe the 'cast members' can keep up the enthusiasm but they do! My son was a little frightened by a couple of the darker, spooky rides but loved meeting all of his favourite characters. I think the crowds were down as it was a showery winter's day so the lines were pretty short. 30 minutes was the longest wait all day so I didn't even bother using Fastpass. Definitely a day to remember!

I have been to Disneyland many times in my life. The only negative about it is that it has become very expensive. Other than that. What's not to like? From the classic rides like Mr. Toad's Wild ride, Alice In Wonderland, Peter Pan's Flight, Pinocchio, Snow White's Scary Adventures, to the ever popular rides like the Haunted Mansion, Space Mountain, It's a Small World and the Pirates of The Caribbean. Or the newer additions like Cars Land. The characters, the parades, the fireworks, the shows, the monorail, two parks, three hotels and one downtown Disney.Even when I had a trip that wasn't as fun as some of the past ones, I know that maybe the next time it will be as fun as before or even more. I just love the place as it let's you forget about the rest of your life for a couple of days and puts you in a magical state. It is the happiest place on earth according to our household.

We came the last week of January and as I write this review we are still here and it is our last day. This is supposed to be a slower time of year and I cannot imagine coming during peak season. There always so many lineups for rides and although we did use the fast pass you still have to wait in line and you can only use the fast pass so many times. It is really a magical place. You do feel like you're in a different world and I really enjoyed my experience but it's crazy busy. The staff at Disney are fabulous and the rides are great it's just be prepared to wait in the line. But hey it's Disney and really is one of the happiest places on earth.
It's Disneyland same old deal.  Nothing really to write home about.  Taking young children is a chore but it was fun the little ones liked it
went to Disneyland  was a total disappointment  very small compared to Disneyworld in florida  should have went to California adventure Disneyland is for small children  no adult interests

Rides are fine; place is clean but it's a big corporation looking to get the most money from you for the least amount of work. There's no good time to come here. If there are fewer customers, they reduce their staff. Sadly, customers are second class. It would be so bad if the trucks today. I'd understand if it was $30 per person and you had to wait online for 40 minutes, and sometimes two hours. But the they charge so much to get in that there should be better service.

They don't call it the happiest place on earth for nothing! We've only been to Disney World so this was our first visit to this park. There are a lot of great similarities but plenty different than it's Orlando counterpart. We went on a Thursday morning and arrived shortly after the park opened at 10am. We were pleasantly surprised when we drove right in to park and didn't have to fight any long lines getting into the park itself! I would certainly recommend buying your passes early so you don't have to mess with getting them the day of. The lines for the rides were a little long at times so I would take advantage of the  Fast Pass  option, if the ride offers it and especially if you have little ones. This is a great way to get ahead of the long lines and better plan out your day (again, helpful if you have little ones). Since the park is smaller than Disney World it can seem a little crowded all around. Downloading the app on your phone gives you wait times for each ride to help you throughout the day.

The only downside is, of course, the price. But it's Disneyland. People will come no matter what they charge, and they know it. They've updated a few of the rides in Fantasyland, which is cool, and they still have the Star Wars overlay in Tomorrowland (the best is Hyperpace Mountain), so it's still great to visit even though part of the park is closed down to build Star Wars Land.

I have visited Disney for 20 years. great times . great memories. Over the last 5 years the park has become more crowded or less staffed. The rides are not kept up like they used to be or they are used harder . Disney used to be pristine. from rides to hedges to sparking restrooms. This is not the case any longer. It seems that good enough is the new standard. Having major attractions closed for renovations is part of the maintenance. Having 3 of your 6 major rides down seems like i am being ripped off. The food is 3 out of 10. the price is 400% out side in the real world. if you are going to charge me. that rate have the decency to make it taste like someone actually tried it before you tried to sell it. Bottom line is   you will go because you are forced by tradition   you will miss the good old days when there was pride taken in doing an exceptional job and a desire to provide you a magical day. my advice pack a lunch and a few snacks.
I love this place i go several times a year! I can be a kid again with my 7 year old! I will be back again in April!
I could come back here again and again. Buying a park hopper pass is worth the investment. The park, the staff, and the atmosphere is just what's needed to help melt your cares away.

Disneyland is a place of fantasy and enjoyment. Always a fun experience. Everyone is so pleasant and they are so accommadating for the Handicapped. If you come to California, Disneyland is a must to visit!!!

As a family that loves Disney World in Orlando, we have been several times in the last 10 years, I was excited to visit Disneyland on our recent trip to Anaheim. I had been told that it was not as great as the Magic Kingdom and to not get too excited, but it was a bucket list thing for me so we went. Truth be told, it is not as grand as the park in Orlando, but it was still fantastic. I never should have doubted Disney. Main Street is a bit shorter and the castle is pathetic compared to Cinderella   s castle in Orlando, but aside from that, it was great. One of the things I love most about Disney parks is the atmosphere and their attention to detail. Both were spot on in Disneyland. When we were deep in the park, there was no way to tell the difference between land vs. world. The New Orleans area is beautiful and is an aspect of Disneyland that is not in the Magic Kingdom. With a few exceptions the rides were also a lot of fun. We really enjoyed the Matterhorn and the Indiana Jones ride. The one real let down was the Finding Nemo Submarine Voyage. The sub moves around a pool that contains nothing worth seeing. There are no living creatures of any kind in the water. It was nothing but fake starfish affixed to fake rocks next to fake plants. There was even a fake scuba diver. I was glad there was not a long wait for this ride because it was a complete waste of our time. Also, there seemed to be quite a few ride breakdowns while we were there. Autopia was broken down all day so we didn   t even get to ride it. Indiana Jones broke down twice as did the Pinocchio ride. We also got stuck for several minutes in the Haunted Mansion. That isn   t even including the rides that were closed for refurbishment. I need to give a special shout out to the staff at Disneyland. The day we were there it was pouring down rain for most of the morning. The employees were cold, wet and had to be miserable, but they never let it show. Each one greeted us with a smile and could not have been more friendly and pleasant. That is a big part of the Disney Magic that brings us back every time. For anyone who loves Disney World, do not be nervous about visiting Disneyland. It is not as grand and magical, but still loads of fun and well worth the time and money.
Amazing place, even in the rain! Unfortunately several attractions were not operational which was a little disappointing but there was still loads of things to do and see. Staff are great!

Just moved my daughter to Long Beach for an internship and told her that I couldn't be so close to Disneyland and not make a visit, even if it was only for a couple of hours. I am so glad that we did. Spent an entire afternoon and evening in the park. Though it was relatively crowded, we still enjoyed ourselves very much. It was my goal to see where Walt's vision started and I finally made it. I look forward to returning the next time I am in Southern California to visit my daughter.
No matter,meow many times you have been before, Disneyland is a great place to go.  I have been many times with all sorts of people and every day is great!

We enjoyed the park on Saturday the 21st of January 2017 it was still as much fun as if it was a spring day. We have yet to ever visit this time of year but found it simply amazing if you allow yourself to immerse yourself into the full experience.

The food options are limited and we crave fresh options but mostly everything is fried or laden with sugar. Whilst the fast passes are a great idea and we utilised them they're not exactly fair on others. Just too manic for my liking and this is my 2nd visit.

So much to see, so little time and something for everyone. We spent 10 hours here we were celebrating my daughters 21st birthday. Seeing Disney with a teenager and a adult child so different and a lot more relaxing for us. We stayed ten ours prepared for when the weather started to get cooler. Whilst in LA we took a trip to Disneyland Park. We went in November on a Monday to the park. We drove down from North Hollywood and it took us around an hour. It was a straight road down and the park was well signed as was the parking facilities and very easy to get to. Parking cost $17 for the day. Once you have parked they have constant shuttle busses on that take you to the park entrance. We were parked in the Toy Story car park so the busses were Toy Story busses. If you want to use public transport really read up on it as we looked and it was going to take a couple of hours on public transport with changes. It's all well on the way down but if you stay at the park all day and leave at the end after the fireworks the journey back may take a while and if you have children could be tired and done in by this time. Once we got to the park we just paid at the kiosk for day tickets. There are 2 parks that you can visit Disneyland Park (to the right) or California Adventure Park (to the left) as I wanted to visit the original Walt Disney park. It cost $95 on the day to get in. As it was our first visit we got given first visit Disney badges to wear. This park isn't full of fast paced rides but is more aimed at younger kids I think and has a lot of the original older rides. But it was amazing to wander around the park and take in all the sights. Thankfully being November it wasn't as busy as it would have been in the height of the season but even still queues for rides were long. Some rides broke down whilst we were waiting and were closed and re opened later. You will be given a guide when you enter telling you about events and shows that are on in the park. The Frontier Land show in the food place was fun and the food was lovely for a lunch stop. Later on was the parade. If you want to have a good spot for the parade I suggest going and getting a spot early. People were starting to queue and take front row spaces from 40 minutes before it and it fills up very quickly and you may be pushed right to the back of the crowd. And Disneyland are funny about where is acceptable to stand and you may be moved on. Everyone was friendly though, staff were helpful and friendly but also in general I found Californians lovely people who love to chat to anyone. If you are looking for photos with characters then look at your time schedule they don't simply walk around but are situated in areas where you must go and queue to get your photo with them. We stayed right until the end for the fireworks which were amazing! We stayed near the back though so we were closer to the exit for when we were leaving as the park is closed after this. There is a large shopping street as you go in with everything Disney you could imagine but the price is quite high so expect to pay over the odds for things. But things are on sale before release of new films. Moana was just about to premiered when I was there but the toys were available to buy before it. After the fireworks we got out the park in good time and went for the Toy Story busses we didn't wait long and we were on one and straight back to the car park and soon on our way back to Hollywood. Overall it was a brilliant day in the park and would highly recommend it. I'm going back in 2018 and will visit the California Adventure park which I believe has all the fast paced rides but you just can't do both parks in one day.

We went on the weekend and the rates are a bit higher. We had such a lovely day riding the rides and meeting the characters. While it was expensive when you factor in tickets, parking and food it's well worth it and so much to do at the park.A must see in Anaheim.

For a first time visit to Disney in LA, I can say it was a super magical for our child, he definitely enjoyed every moment we spend in the park. We arrived noon time and as you can imagine, we couldn't do much as it was cold by 4 PM onwards. Will definitely come back again to complete all the attractions so we have to pay again. From an entry perspective and pricing and as I can see feedback from other travelers about the prices, I agree with them, it is a bit high pricing for families with kids visiting the resort for a day or two.

We visited Disneyland on December 23, it was a drizzly and overcast day. What a great time to visit. Crowds were light, lines were short with minimum wait times. Just remember... whatever time of the year you visit Disneyland to bring 1 thing. Patience, plenty of patience. Eat off schedule, eat lunch early or late and the same with dinner. This will help alleviate some of the long wait times to eat.

The park was quite busy, but as usual a wonderful place to visit and enjoy the rides and entertainment.  The fast pass was very useful and Magic Morning was wonderful.  Food much too expensive in the park.

My husband and I have been to Disneyland probably 7 or 8 times since we've been together and each time has been amazing. Truly a magical experience for people of all ages. Our most recent trip was with our two year old, my husband's parents, his sister, and his 80 year old grandmother. Everyone had a fabulous time and we are already talking about when we can plan our next trip!

We have been coming to Disneyland forever! Lineups and people seem to grow. Take plenty you will need it.

I have held a season pass to Disneyland for at least the past 10 years. My poor experience on Martin Luther King Day coupled with bad service experiences my past few visits convince me that Disney really has made a decision to under staff its park to the detriment of guests. First, the lines for bag check are simply unacceptably long. These long, long lines to enter the park area are new. In year's past, I never waited more than a few minutes to get through a bag check. Now, it is a 10   30 minute ordeal every time. Monday's line was 30 minutes. Then, I waited in a ticket line for another 30 minutes to purchase a ticket for a child who I took with me to the park. The park itself seemed overwhelmed. The staffing was simply not up to the crowd level. Splash Mountain broke down while we were at the front of the line    no information provided about how long it would be out of service and no Fastpass to come back later for folks who had already waited more than 40 minutes to get to the front of the line. I understand lines, but the park was much better at servicing large crowds in the past. I love the park, but it really does seem like they have decided to drive people away by providing far less service to customers than in the past.
Been coming to Disneyland since 1967 been on everything, Love the cleanliness, it's amazing friendly worker's and staff. Always a great time. Thank you

I have to say I was amazed by the amount of people when we went and my sister in law said it wasn't a busy day. Having said that the waits weren't too bad for the rides either. We enjoyed our day here.  More quaint and less touristy than Orlando. All the employees were friendly and we never had long lines.

Yes the lines are long and the admission isn't cheap but it is 100% WORTH IT. Disneyland couldn't have been more fun. I would go everyday if I could. I absolutely love it.

We enjoyed our visit, even though we have been to this theme park 4 times over the years. Some things are looking a bit dated and could do with a refresh, but it's always a fun day out. Expect big crowds regardless of the time of year. Make sure you take advantage of the fast pass facility, as it helps with the lines. The food is never the greatest, and is expensive.

I love Disneyland it's got something for the whole family! I think the best time to go is March I've been 3 times at this time of year and it's not busy! It's prices are fair for what you get. I can't wait to go back!

I went during Christmas period, So the mood was brilliant. Nice decorations and cool weather gave me the most awesome experience. Though it will be crowded, its open till 12 am so it gives you alot of time to visit the rides.

Disneyland is definitely fun for the whole family. It was busier than usual this visit.
