What is not to love at Disneyland? Something to do for all ages. Kept pristine   so clean. Can be long wait lines but all well worth it. Such a magical place. Attractions are run very well, food from meals, fast food, snacks, treats are all wonderful everywhere.

I have had an annual pass for the past 13 years now, and there has never been a dull moment in Disneyland. The place dear to many a child growing up in the 70's, I finally got there! And it was everything I had hoped. The wait for rides were minimal and not a bother at all. The food was uninspiring but I wasn't there to eat. Managed to meet Goofy, Chewbacca and Daisy so was happy with that. My only complaint would the the overly officious staff who kept moving us along even when we weren't in the way of foot traffic or blocking any views. They made it very difficult to enjoy the spectacle and in my opinion caused more hassle than was warranted. And also when it was time to leave were herding everyone down Main St at a very fast pace. We had to duck into a shop to avoid the crush (once again unnecessary). Overall a great day only ruined by the staff with light sticks policing the crowd at night.
Disneyland Park is just a wonderful attraction in the heart of Orange County!  Perfect for the kid in all of us!  There's just so much to see and do, so plan on spending at least a full day!

While I truly love Disneyland and all things Disney I did not renew my annual pass. Very sad to say that but it's become so over crowded that the wait time for some rides has reached two to three hours! My last visit saw the park reach capacity and they actually stopped letting people in at a certain point. You could barely move with so many people there!They still maintain the level of cleanliness and customer service it's just too crowded to pay the prices and not get to enjoy yourself. I hope they do something about this so things will be different going forward.

Disneyland is an absolute must if you visit LA. The new features at Universal Studios Hollywood are very appealing, and if you have time, visit both. But for a very, very full day of riding rides and experiencing a fully themed park, don't miss the chance to visit Disneyland for the day. THANK goodness they still use the old paper Fastpass system too   you can really maximize your visit without the hassle of having to plan 6 months ahead for your trip. I've heard they may change that, but for our trip, the old paper system was firmly in place, and we were able to max out our rides without crazy waits. Yes, you criss cross the park a bit and walk more, but it's a great way to ride everything, on a crowded day, without waiting in lines like at Knott's Berry Farm. Whether this is your first time or if you go daily   you'll find something to love at Disneyland.

I had broken my ankle and was in a boot, couldn't really stand for long periods of time. Was able to go to exit of rides and either get on the ride or be given a time to return. They offered me a wheel chair as well. Very accommodating.
Love going in the middle of the week. Low crowds and great weather! Sundays seem like the busiest when I'm in town.

seems to me that whenever I go to  get away to my happy place  it ends up being stressful.Things have changed so much since I was a kid going there, the lines are atrocious and the people seem to think that when they are walking that they are driving on the Fwy. Let's star with it only get a four because my wife loves Disneyland and it was her birthday. I would give it a two or three. We were able to get some photos with some Disney and Star Wars characters which was nice. Now for the bad. Can this place get anymore expensive. It starts with the admission, $460 for to adult two day park hoppers, come on really. Then the overpriced food from every cart, stand and restaurant is just insane. It just seems you can't walk 10 feet without them trying to get in your pocket. Our second day was sunny. Guess what? Everybody was there, or at least it felt that way. It was unbearably overcrowded, and the lines were all at least 45 minutes some were 2 3 hours. I always wonder what the occupancy of the park is, or do they just pack them in. It doesn't really make you feel like your in the happiest place on earth, or very magical.

Amazing place for adults as well as kids. Food was expensive, but I expected that. Queuing times were long, but the app from Disneyland let us know waiting times, so we could plan our rides efficiently. The Paint the light parade was amazing and what I saw of the fireworks display, it looked wonderful. All in all, it was a dream come true, even for a 53 year old, but there were some areas that could be improved.I can't wait for my next visit, now I've been once.

We apparently picked the worst time to visit. :( it rained everyday we were there and they had just closed two rides to take down Christmas decorations: the haunted mansion and the jungle cruise. I was really bummed because we had wanted to see the haunted mansion all dressed up. We still had loads of fun and they can't control the weather. Didn't realize they don't have an evening firework show except a few nights a week. Overall takeaway is I wish I would have planned better. We have been to Disney world over 10 times and there was really no comparison to it in my opinion. I didn't like how there was no meal plan or fast passes link that we have grown accustomed to at Disney world.
I loved the shopping. Just too many people. Prices were surprisingly good. Why is inside Disneyland always good weather?

We (7 of us, 3 generations) had two days at Disneyland earlier this month. One day was sunny and warm, and the other was very rainy  but we loved every minute of it.One complaint: Apparently Autopia closes when it rains. But they don't tell you that's a possibility. We waited over a half hour in line, watching the clouds roll in and the drizzle turn to a downpour. Then an attendant abruptly stated that  the ride is closing, please exit to your left.  Pretty hard to explain to a 5 year old boy patiently waiting to drive his own car....And a bit of advice: Disneyland is ALWAYS crowded. We checked a website that presumably could predict attendance levels. On a day they projected crowd level to be  Ghost Town,  it was just as busy as the sunny weekend day we had spent there. Plan on crowds. Go early. Use Fast Pass.Yes, Disneyland is expensive. Plan in advance. It's worth it.

Way overprice.  That wasn't a problem as it was all worth it.  The rides were extraordinary and the lines weren't that bad.  I recommend this place if you are looking for a day of fun or a fantastic trip.

I'll keep this short. Disneyland is awesome. My tips are get there early, like before the gates open. Prior to going download the Disneyland app and have a look at which rides have the longest wait times. That way, when you get there at opening time, make a rush to those rides with the longest waits, as we found there was not as many people first thing in the morning. Also try and get fast passes where possible. We found by getting there first thing in the morning within a couple of hours we had done all the rides with the larger wait times. We then had the luxury of cruising around doing all the smaller rides in the afternoon.

I wouldn't recommend going to Disneyland unless you enjoy long line ups and crowded people. This place did not offer that true Disney experience in comparison to Disney World. I don't think I would ever go back, it had some decent rides, but i spent most of my day waiting in line ups. It felt less like Disney, but more like a amusement park just trying to take your money.

I was there with my family on 27 December 2016 and this place was crowded with thousands of visitors. It took atleast one and a half hours to get to any ride. Queues were very long. People were getting impatient while waiting for so long. The place where I got my tickets from Discount Tickets and Tours in Anaheim and they never mentioned anything about `Fast Pass'. I would recommend to everybody visiting Disneyland Park, to buy `Fast Pass'. It could cost more but atleast you don't have to wait in long queues. The queues for `Fast Pass' is not very long. It generally takes 10 15 minutes to get to the ride. If you don't buy `Fast Pass', then you cannot enjoy the rides and cannot finish visiting the whole park. Other option is to buy a pass for 2 3 days rather than one day.

We spent 2 days at the park. Me, husband and 5 year son. The first day we went to the  original  Disneyland side. The second day we went to the newer side (Cars land). Disneyland is SO busy! Crowds. Line ups. Expensive. Yes we had fun. But waiting 1.5 hours in line for a 10 minute ride is not fun. We tried to take advantage of the Fast passes (you HAVE to use these to actually get on any rides!!!). Still... your best bet is to plan midweek during low season to come here. And come early. And plan the order of rides to go on. We liked the original Disneyland side much better than the new one. If we come back we would just do the original side. More rides and options. And   sigh  since our son is only 5, I see more Disneyland trips in our future....

We went to Disney after the holidays and it was packed! Lines were average of 30 60 min wait for rides. Don't get a photopass because photographers are hard to find. Bring strollers or rent them... also download their app to help you.We survived it but dead tired with kids who were 2 and 4 yrs old. Because of the crowd it was not as magical as I thought. I want to go back there on off peak season.

I can't say enough good things about Disneyland. I apologize to those of you reading this as you likely won't get much out of it. The one piece of advice I have is to map out a plan of attack for your visit and use your early day attendance wisely. Regarding planning your day, don't go back and forth between areas because you will spend more time walking and waiting in line than actually having a Disney experience. Spend a little more money and get reserved seating for the parades. The minor interaction with the characters during the parade and the reserved seating area leads to memorable experiences and excitement for the youngest children and the young at heart.

Have just spent the day at Disneyland. Having only one day we decided to go to the original park and we weren't disappointed. The weather was miserable so we bought ponchos the night before for $2.99 (they are $10 inside) and we wore them for most of the day. Here are my tips for a great day;Get there early just incase. We were told that it opened at 10am but at 9.15 the gates were open and the rides were going. At 10am people arrived and it was suddenly busy. Maybe Disney felt sorry for us arriving in the pouring rain! We waited on average 15 mins for each ride so aim for a day when the weather is not perfect as this may deter some people.Head straight to Hyperspace Mountain and then grab your first Fastpass. Try to get your rides done in the morning.Take some snacks so you only have to buy lunch, food is pretty average.You can ride on the rides with your backpack. Water bottles can be refilled around the park.Most people are helpful, friendly and there to have a great day. Everyone was patient, particularly in the bad weather. Staff were fine but I have read that other reviews say they are rude. We didnt encounter this at all. Queues moved well and were organised. Enjoy!

Whats can i say but its disney. The place is Amazing compared to what we have available back home in australia. You will not see much or enjoy to much if only going for one day. We went two days and still missed alot.A must for anyone of any age

While on a road trip my family decided to take a spontaneous trip Disneyland just a few days before Christmas. None of us had ever been before and we were so excited. Disney definitely did not disappoint. It was decorated beautifully for Christmas. Even though lines were long, they seemed to move quickly. The longest line we waited in by far was to see Mickey at his house and we waited there for close to an hour. The characters were awesome, it was so cute seeing my 4 year old interact with the princesses, Tinkerbell, Minnie. Especially Moana, she was great! My daughter love love loved It's a Small World. She was really looking forward to the Alice in Wonderland ride & the teacups, but they were both closed due to rain which was disappointing. I loved the Indiana Jones ride and Peter Pan's Flight and my husband is a huge Star Wars nerd and wanted to spend all his time in Tomorrowland. Shopping for souvenirs was fun, but I guess I was expecting more variety. I thought this would for sure be the place to find souvenirs with the lesser Disney characters like Hercules etc. but I didn't really see many outside the more popular movies. We were excited to try the food because we had heard how amazing it was. It was good, but it didn't blow my mind or anything. The churros were awesome though. The parade we watched that night was spectacular!We absolutely can't wait for next time!

It's a great park for your younger set and less mobile members of your family. I went with my active teen and we both enjoyed the park even with the crowds. It is clean, well managed and consistent. The lines were reasonable at the beginning of the day and after 8pm but were quite busy at the middle section.We were surprised by a number of mechanical malfunctions during the day when rides were shut down. this included Pirates of the Caribbean, Buzz Lightyear and Space Mountain. While everything went well, at the end, we both thought that it may be our last time for a while. The rides and park are clearly aimed at younger kids and perhaps we would be better suited for California Adventure Land or a straight amusement park without the characters.It rained on us so we bought plastic ponchos for $10 inside the park on Main Street.

Everything in this place is awesome. But I liked the Disneyland Park better than CA Adventure. It's always nice to spend your day in any of these 2 parks. Although, it's now very expensive to visit both places, esp for a family of 4. It all adds up. But they always say,  gotta pay to play .Don't miss these parks whenever you're in SoCal.
First visit for granddaughters 6 and 3.  Wonderful time! As usual food is a little pricey but didn't have any trouble finding something they would eat!

Even in the rain we had a great time. 4 day park hopper pass worked well to maximise our time. Make use of early morning entry by staying at a Disney hotel. Fast passes really help to cut down on wait times. The Disney app is useful for checking times and fast pass availability.
Disney is the best there is, food is EXpensive, always fun, go on a week day when it rains a little the crowd is smaller!
Disneyland Los Angeles is amazing place. I had been in Hong Kong, Paris. This is 3rd Disneyland. All the thing was perfect. I plan to stay longer in next time. (More than 1 day)
Not a very well run place, staff rude, due to the amount of people, boycott and go straight to Florida, that's a Disney you dreamed of, and great staff and very helpful,

We loved every minute from opening to closing. Use fast passes wisely and keep track of time as you can get another fast pass every 2 hrs. Got a good spot for the electric parade. Such a magical place. Thank you Walt Disney.

Fantastic trip with my grandchildren, first time at Disney's California adventure and it was phenomenal the light show was amazing at 9:00 PM, day two Was at Disneyland and we thoroughly enjoyed all the new additions and had a blast

Wow, first time going to Disneyland and I was not disappointed. Arrived very early at around 9am and stayed until 10pm. Managed to go on 90% of the major rides and had the greatest day of my life. The fast passes are a god send and can save you massive amounts of time. I never had to wait in line longer than 30 mins. The firework show at the end of the night was like nothing i have ever seen before! simply a wonderland

Had an amazing day here. We went in March and didn't have too much of a problem with lines. It's so good that the park stays open till midnight! Really helped us take it all in. Was a bit disappointed as there wasn't as many characters as we'd expected walking around.
What can I say that as not been said its Disney except that I enjoyed Disney Florida a bit more but really who's complaining

I loved every minute of our visit to Disneyland. We only bought tickets for one park and chose Disneyland over the Adventure Park because of the Star Wars area. I'm glad we did because we could see the Adventure Park from our hotel window and it didn't look as good. We were there from 10:00 (queue to get in was quite big) until about 18:00 as we had a train to catch so we didn't get to see the fireworks from inside the park and we somehow managed to completely miss the parade which was a shame. We fast tracked on all the rides that we could, and that worked a treat, we hardly ever had to queue to anything   but there still wasn't enough time to cram it all in! We never even made it into Toontown, and barely scratched the surface of Fantasyland. The only ride we queued for any length of time for was Indiana Jones because I think it must have broken down. That was only niggle over service too, they didn't tell anyone what was going on and people didn't know whether backtrack or wait. Other than that, service was excellent, everywhere. The restaurants were all very busy, and we couldn't eat at Blue Bayou because we hadn't reserved, but the jambalaya in French Market Restaurant was surprisingly nice, and not as expensive as you might expect. The halloween theme was fab, especially the Disney villain banners and the decorations on the Haunted Mansion. LOVED IT. Top tips:go for at least two days; pre book lunch if you want to eat anywhere specific; use fast track on the rides, even if it means crossing the length of the park each time.
great place to get well over 10,000 steps   actually more like 20,000.  can get a little crowded at peak times, but off season times are ok

We thoroughly enjoyed our time at Disneyland in every way. Having looked forward to seeing it from when we were children it was surprisingly still enjoyable as an adult. The queues for the rides can be painful but they are a fact of theme park life from our experience. In any case they weren't too bad and we got to see everything we wanted to

We really like Disney...but, during our visit (Jan 4, 5, 6) the major rides shut down every day...Space Mountain, Matterhorn, Indiana Jones, Thunder Mountain and others...so, how is it that we pay a premium to go to Disneyland to receive bad service...My advice is to avoid Disney until they figure out how to maintain their rides.
Loved it, loved it. So much to see and do. Did 2 days and still not enough time. I will be back. Disneyland makes you feel like a kid.

Have been to Disneyland a couple times before. I really enjoy the amusement park including the neighbouring California Adventure Park. I recommend using the single lines whenever possible to avoid very lengthy waits in the lines. Your party will possibly be split up, but it is well worth it to cut down the wait time by approximately an hour, on average. The park was extremely busy, and so it was sometimes quite difficult getting around, however the staff did quite well controlling the direction and flow of foot traffic. We wanted to eat at the Cafe Orleans for lunch, however were turned away because we didn't have reservations. I found this weird and frustrating. Who makes reservations at an amusement park restaurant? The rides and attractions at the park are wonderful, although I find the price of admission quite expensive, especially the park hopper pass. California Adventure Park was a bit of a let down due to the closure of the Twilight Zone Tower of Terror. Had I known this I would have skipped the park hopper pass. I was also disappointed that no wifi was available within the park. Most other amusement parks in the area offer wifi and I found it surprising that there was none in Disneyland. This park is geared more towards families with younger children, however I still really enjoyed my time.

What more can be said of Disneyland that hasn't already been said? Long lines for short rides, expensive unhealthy food and pricey toys that are everywhere and unavoidable. All negatives easily overlooked because of the incredible quality of the entertainment at Disneyland. A must do for every family, requires you bite the bullet and shell out for a good time that the whole family will remember forever.
Pack your patience and great walking shows, longs can be long and lots and lots of people. But past that it's  Disney : fun, creative, historical and magical

I really love Disneyland but going there during Christmas time it is a massive number of people. Best to go early in the morning. Leave at noon and come back at 4pm. I took a break the new Candlewood Suites just down the street. Great outdoor heated pool.

I LOVE Disneyland. It should be on everyone's bucket list. I'm often asked questions by coworkers going to America, and I tell them all do not miss this   they all tell me  thank you for convincing me to go, it was the best day   that's from 21 year old females to 65 year old men. It is the ultimate theme park. The detail in their rides is phenomenal. Does it have the biggest rides? No. The lines are long but if you go early and hit the main attractions first you will be happy. To make the most of the place I recommend  The Unofficial Guide to Disneyland    it's a book or a weblink that gives you an order to do the park, and if you follow their touring plans, you don't wait more than 20 minutes in a queue. I've done it so many times and it's the way to go. Also go on a weekday if you can.

Disneyland Park gets so crowded,this makes is nerve racking when you have little ones but we still enjoyed our time. There were 13 adults and 2 little ones and we enjoyed the rides. We are honored to say that we are so glad you have the baby exchange it truly helps so that we could all have the same amount of fun. Granted we could have gone without the little ones. But we didn't and it was still wonderful. So for you haters don't complain it was great. You just have to have patience and a loving family with you. Thank youThe questions below are not good questions because they all have different answers depending on age and health.

Had a fabulous first time trip to Disneyland with my son between Christmas and New Year.The park is everything you would expect of Disney and I have to be honest I preferred the overall experience to Disneyworld.This in no way deflects from how tremendous Disneyworld is but this is so much more compact and doable in a 3 day trip.
We love visiting Disneyland.  Hyperspace mountain, Big Thunder Mountain, and the Yeti roller coasters are our favorites.  Peter Pan always has a crazy long line.  Dumbo is a classic!

This is the ultimate theme park. People will complain about the crowds (never go the last week of the year, horrendous crowds!), and the price (it's a lot). But you get so much out of it if you do it right. The best way to get your money's worth is to go at opening and stay all day. Plan your fast passes right and enjoy everything. Be a kid again! Download the Official Disneyland app (the one disney made) and it will give you all the current information on wait times, character appearances, and fast pass times. And if you have multiple days, you don't need a park hopper. Just enjoy all Disneyland and California Adventure have to offer...separately. Also, if you are lucky to go for Christmas or Halloween (totally recommended!) pay the extra money to go to the after hours parties. I think Disneyland does a Halloween party every year and Disney World does a Christmas party. They cost more money and you have to book the tickets in advance because they sell out. But they really are worth it. I love this place.

Well you got to love Disneyland everything about it was wonderful except the fast food ,not great But let's face it That's the last thing your there for ,we spend 2 days in Disneyland and had a ball at night the place lights up and is so beautiful. You always have a smile on your face the happiest place on earth. It is a must do and Christmas time is a special time We stayed in Anaheim at the Hotel indigo close and doesn't break the budget short walk to Disneyland and walk the other way to lots of restaurants We booked ticket thur Viator and went to the ticket office and had a issue getting the tickets sorted. But star were great and we had it fixed and off we went  IT IS A MUST DO

This was not my first visit to Disneyland but it was my first visit at Christmas and it was simply magical!No matter what your age is this is an amazing place to visit. The crowds were a little more at this time of year making wait times longer, but everyone was in a festive mood and the time passed quickly enough.I highly recommend the use of fast passes where available to keep the wait times to a minimum. Don't miss the Mickey's Magical Map show or Frozen the musical. And of course the fireworks and parades are a must.I have visited Walt Disney World but I prefer Disneyland, you can almost feel Walt's presence in the park. Also some of the actual attractions are longer than in WDW, giving you more time to enjoy the magic.Everyone is friendly and there is a definite magic in the air! This is my favourite holiday destination and I hope once you visit, it will become yours too!

Very nice Christmas celebration in the park, very pretty decorations, lovely christmass parades, and such a great environment for the whole family. We've been there several times in the spring and summer but never for Christmas, Loved it.

Firstly, to be rejected at your entrance due to an extending go pro stick that I had in my possession was very disappointing!!! We waited in long lines to get bag searched only to be told once we had got to the front that gopro sticks were not allowed!! ABSOLUTELY NO SIGNS TO GIVE PEOPLE ADVANCED NOTICE!!! It does not make for a good day having travelled half way across the world to fulfill a childhood dream.Secondly, your lines are ridiculous!! People pay a good amount of money to come here and are barely able to get on rides due to the lines! Yes you have fast track options, but seriously, the amount of money given for entrance for approximately 6 rides people can get in within a day? Doesn't add up !! You are making money off people's childhood dreams to attend a famous park yet not really giving them an experience that they deserve for the money they pay, there seriously needs to be discussion around the amount of people that should enter on any given day, this would ensure all round fairness.Pretty disappointed in this park and the lack of attention it gives to ensuring guests times here are a pleasurable experience.

I have been coming to Disneyland for 30 years and now I get to share it with my children. Everything about the park is calculated to create a magical experience. From Star Wars, to Pixar, to Marvel, to Princesses, everyone can find something they love at Disneyland.

Don't get me wrong, I love Disneyland, what I did not love was the capacity crowd the first week of Jan 2017. It was miserable, we could not move, literally shoulder to shoulder with by all estimates between 75,000 and 80,000 people. I feel sorry for all the employees of Disneyland. Even with that unbelievable crowd, every employee I came across was kind and helpful. My list of unacceptable things: Bathrooms: filthy, so disgusting, just too many people, not enough bathrooms. Rides: unable to ride 3 4 of what we wanted to, as the lines were more than 1 hour and sometimes almost 2 hours long. Thank goodness for fast passes, I will never go during a holiday season again. Love the Grand Californian, this was not my first time there, staff was great, room was clean, Storyteller restaurant food however was sub par. Disney has had food issues for a while. They need to step up with better food. Hey Disney, I would pay more for better food. We ate off property. No Disney magic this time. I need a vacation from my vacation.

OMG! I so wish I had been to Disneyland much earlier in my life. We absolutely loved everything about it! We are now addicted and want to go to all the Disney parks! DO NOT let peak time of year put you off because ALL the rides are in operation and the staff are so very organised that they have the whole place running super smoothly. We will go to the other parks at the peak times now because who wants to go when some of the major rides are closed for maintenance? That would really suck!

We are return clients and love the park. It's clean and organised and staff give the optimum customer service. We did visit during the busiest time of the year but we arrived early and took advantage of fast pass and planned our rides so that our wait time was bearable. The longest was Tower of Terror (2 hours) last day of operation before closing permanently so we endured the pain. One of the elevators was out of service which made the wait twice as long. Overall we had a wonderful experience and noticed that the food quality and variety is definitely improving. Thanks Disney but still room for improvement in that area. There is a Starbucks in Main Street but you have to ask or check map as there is no signage.

Are you kidding me?! That is what the sign said on Wednesday, January 4, 2017. It was CRAZY CROWDED! Don't get me wrong, I LOVE Disneyland but this was insane! When I lived in Southern California, I had an annual pass. We would go on off days to avoid the crowds. We came down on off days and rainy days, hoping that it would keep the crowds low. I guess everyone had the same idea! This year our kids had a weird Holiday schedule. So I thought it would be fun to make a quick trip to Disneyland. It was so crowded that it made it hard to have fun. We got in right as it opened and got our first fast pass and then went to ride Indiana Jones. After waiting for 20 minutes in line, they closed the ride. They should offer return tickets for those that had waited in line. It was so crowded that there were horrible lines to use the rest rooms and then you had to wait in line to wash your hands! I've never been to Disneyland where the bathrooms were so poorly maintained. They were dirty! I've never seen this before at this park. Stalls had no toilet paper and there were no paper towels. I even informed a a cast member of the problem and they shrugged their shoulders at me. I'd have to say the most annoying part of this visit was the LINE CUTTING! When did this become acceptable? Everyone was doing it. Old people, young people, little kids, and parents were all cutting in line. You get in line and wait like everyone else has had to do. You should not be able to play, eat, use the restroom, whatever and then when your party is at the front, you push your way up to them!!! NO! NO! NO! Also, people walking in the crowded park texting or using their smart phones and not paying attention to where they are walking. I lost count of how many times I got slammed into by people not paying attention. Play your games, text, read your email or what ever while in line, not while walking. I could go on but you understand. I Love Disneyland and will continue to visit but I think that they need to rethink some of their policies.

After Holiday Christmas gift for the love bugs. Disneyland with a 6 & 2 year is magically within itself. The maps were detailed enough to easily navigate the park. The signage helped with getting around as well. The day started off a little brisk and ended up comfortable by midday. By night fall it was freezing! However we did stay through Holiday parade & watched the fireworks from our hotel. In the park we spent most of our time in Mickey's Toontown, which was most appropriate for the children's age range. We saw a couple of the show's and the favorite was Beauty and The Beast. We did not run across many characters but the kids were happy enough to see them in the parade.Having been to Disney World several time and Disneyland only twice, I do think Disney world is much bigger; has a lot more attractions & entertainment but Disneyland is a lot more manageable and doable in a day, especially with younger children.Overall, the day at Disneyland was a good day!

We love Disney, and the Magic Kingdom is extra magical during the Christmas season. The decorations, the music, the merchandise, the shows are all extra special. Be ready for big, long waits, though, a lot of moving around the park to find the stuff to do that has shorter waits.

Park was at capacity by 11:00 AM. Too many people to be enjoyable. Paid over 100 dollars admission and rode two rides. It was a 30 minute wait just to get a fast pass for Star Tours. I know this is not typical and should not reflect on Disney, just the wrong time of year to go

We are a family of four, my husband and my two girls aged 11 and 15, Last year we went to Disney World for Christmas and this year we decided to come here for Christmas. I knew that Christmas Day would be too busy so I made sure we avoided that date, and visited a few days before and a few after. I made sure I booked our dining on line months in advance. That was when I realised that Disneyland Park is very much the poorer relative to Disney World. No magic bands , no photo pass to buy, no fast passes to book............ and not being able to do those things makes your experiences not as magic as they could be. The Fast passes for rides we wanted ran out before we got into the park, you cannot plan your route around the park as you need to visit the Fast Pass booths by the rides that you want to go on. It's so silly !We visited on December 22nd and it was raining, lots and lots and lots   that said we are British and theme parks in the rain are our thing and we were able to do most rides in the pouring rain.The next time we visited was December 28th and it was a very different experience. The queue for security was insane, there is no exact queue to join so you join a mass of people and it gradually filters to a line. I bought the tickets on line so we had them in hand, but the first time you use them they take you r picture so each time you go to the park you scan the ticket and they see your picture. This is great system, but taking your picture holds up the line, there after its fine.The queues that day were insane, at times you could not move and I was glad we had endured the rain and done most of the rides then. I love Disney but even most rides are poor versions of Disney World.

Pretty and clean but not as much to do and see as Disneyworld. I would highly recommend getting the Disneyland AP for your phone to check wait times, view restaurant and restroom locations. Fast passes a must for the busy rides.

A bit expensive, but that's what happens when you go to a place this great. The only complaint is the amount of people. The number of season ticket holders really made it crowded, and forget about lining upfor the parade, people were doing that 2 hours before the event. Really great rides and characters throughout the park. One of a kind experience, just wish there were less people.

Coming from Australia we were very excited but the crowds were incredible. I get it was school holidays but I was shocked. The amount of prams (strollers) and mobility scooters mixed with foot traffic meant everyone was walking at a snails pace, bumper to bumper. The line ups for the rides were at least an hour long each with some up to 4 hrs long. The park itself was beautiful but you couldn't just simply enjoy it. Lining up for 2 hrs just to get a family photo with Mickey Mouse was sad.

The lines just to get through security were over 45 minutes long. Then you have to stand in line again to buy tickets if not pre purchased. Then stand in line again to enter the park. I do not recommend coming here anytime around the year end holidays. The crowds are just too big.

Disneyland is the happiness place on still. We planned our trip based on the Disney occupancy calendar which was definitely not how busy the park was. Oh well we still had a tremendous amount of fun and will be back for another week of fun in a couple of years.

I love taking my children to Disneyland. We live in California and it is by far my most favorite place to visit. We go when the weather is perfect and in the middle of the workweek. I'm moving from California soon and I will miss most Disneyland.

We liked this park better than California Adventure. You can do it in a day but if you have more days, this is the park to visit.Rides were good and wait was actually quicker than the wait board said. Thunder Mountain such a blast! We were lucky enough to be there on New Year's Eve (both with the rain that had finally stopped and being in California at the time!) And the fireworks were incredible!The park stayed open til 2am which was great as you could still ride and enjoy the vibe at the start of the New Year.
What can you say about a place that has it all! Fun, food, characters! We go as often as possible! Great themed lands, great themed food and lots of things to do.

This is our second visit to Disneyland and maybe our last! We knew it was going to be busy on the holidays but what we dealt with was ridiculous! Last time we came during the summer holidays and it was 5 star all the way this time not so much! Using our park hopper tickets on one of our days was useless for a while as Disneyland was full so we couldn't go from park to park! The Fastpass system was useless by lunchtime as they were all taken! I feel sorry for the people who were there for a once in a lifetime trip! Walking from place to place was also a nightmare! Disney needs to catch up with the rest of the world and design a Fastpass you can pay for so first timers and people from far away can pay the extra money and get around the park! We felt that this time we did not get value for money and left with sore backs, sore legs and a bitter taste in our mouths! Please Disney think about your park capacity and ways to cater for people during busy times! Oh and if you want to get into the Frozen show good luck! Congratulations to Disney in the profits you have made in the last two days!

As always a visit to the magic kingdom is wonderful. We have been a number of times and it never fails to deliver. We particularly liked star tours ride and would recommend this to anyone. The pirates of the Caribbean is still a favourite even after all this time. Well worth the money to go but be warned queues are very long at this time of year so choose when you go carefully.

We were here for 2 days early Dec 2016 with my 4 and 6 year old. We thoroughly enjoyed ourselves. The park was clean, the wait times weren't that bad, maybe 30mins for the rides we wanted. Others, like splash mountain was no line and so we went in 5 times in a row.I was a bit disappointed with the photo pass photographers as we wanted some magic shots but they were so rushed they only took one photo. At the Princess meet and great the photographers battery was flat so couldn't take our photo and couldn't tell us how long till a replacement so we missed some of those photos. Considering how much we paid for the photopass I wanted to get more for the price.The kids had fun and I can't wait to go back again!

It is first theme park of the world and it is simply great. Hundreds of visitors come for fun. Rides are plenty but u can manage only around 7 in a day. Even fast pass can take more than that. Got to plan your rides, lunch & dinner to maximise. Nighttime with lights brings the fantasy world. We got to see fireworks too and it was beautiful. Must visit place.
We new Christmas was going to busy, and it was. Fast Passes are the way to go. Book dining 2 months ahead online, even did this for lunch on the 26th

What can one say .... I've always marvelled at the amazing level of customer service and marketing and branding at Disney but let's face it it's much more fun than that. Highly recommend that you get vip fast passes and planning your day in advance. All of the shows are pretty amazing as is the fire works at the end of the day. Food is all good too. Had great service all day. I highly recommend dropping the 11.75 for the amazing huge and tasty turkey legs. One other tip...we got the park package which included all park passes our room at the Disney resort and all meals snacks and drinks for the entire week....all of that and your room key are loaded onto a convenient wrist strap ....no need to carry alot of cash and all the paying is done before you arrive. But so convenient...oh and your fast passes go on there too!

Amazing place to visit, especially for first timers. There is so much to do with rides and attractions catering for all ages. The parade down main street was incredible to watch, as was the nightly fireworks over fantasy land. If you dont mind the crowds and sometimes waiting in line for up to an hour for some rides, there will be no need to fast pass. The socal city pass makes it more affordable as it gives you a three day pass hopper pass for disneyland, california adventure park, legoland and sea world.

JUST FOUND OUT YESTERDAY you're going to ruin Disneyland for a temporary craze? I would have signed that petition months ago if I had known you were going to destroy the back lot and some other attractions to put in Star Wars Land? That doesn't fit with the theme of that part of the park. Hey executives, that was really stupid!

.....is absolutely beautiful but remember the crowds of . Try to stay at the Disneyland properties so that you get the extra magic hour and get in early to ride . We e rode and rode rides for a the first part of the day and then when it became crowded we would take a break at the hotel. Then come back later. Use the Fast Passes to ride super crowded rides so you can go ride other people things while you wait for your time to ride. The staff at he park are fine. I've gone to the park for 30 years and they ebb and flow on their staff and courteous behavior .We had a few rude moments. When using a fast pass at Indiana Jones, the girl barked  it's not your time  My husband looked at our passes and then she looked again  oh, my bad   she said and moved us on. Very odd for Disney. At Peter Pan we were there a few people back from the first to ride it for the day and I heard th girl bark at the little family at the front  your going to have to wait  I thought for most people they don't come here often, it's there first ride of the day o their trip with their little children and they are being barked at. not to mention how much they pay for the pleasure . So just preparing you. Mostly it's ok ( not like it use to be but ok) We will be back as always .

I went to this magic place more that 100 times in my life, I made marriage proposal to my wife in this place in front of the castle, now I have a little girl (3 years old) and she love it, My favority time to visit Disney is Christmas, all the employees are nice and very polite, Now with my baby I see another way this park but Always my favorites shows are Fireworks and all the parades.Be careful using your fast past this can give you a lot of help but need to be smart to used, look very carefull the return times to the games.Start tours, Indiana Jones, Pirates, Haunted house, space mountain are some of the best rides of the park.

It's Disneyland the happiest place on earth, what else can I say, for this quote hits me true by heart esp when I am visiting it as me not as mommy me. Food: Ok, yes it could be really expensive but there are ways to be economical by not eating at sit restaurants like the Blue Bayou but more value meal like Turkey legs that is actually could be good for two people.Wait Times: Yes it can be long, but utilizing the Fast Passes is a good wait to help with that issue. Or if is plausible to your schedule come on a weekday (middle of the week) like Tuesday thru Thursday
the ticket here is also fastpasses for the popular rides that offer them!! and do the character dining, we did mimmie dining for breakfast good service and food!

Prepurchase your ticket(s) will save you much time queuing up. If on a one day ticket, even if a park hopper I strongly suggest purchasing  skip the line  ticket(s) as wait times on popular rides can exceed 1 hour which is a waste of your time. Those persons with  skip the line  tickets simply walked in their own line bypassing everyone else lining up. Will pre purchase  skip the line  tickets next time especially if you are a tourist and have a short time to experience Disneyland in Los Angeles.

Had a great time , kids loved it.Went early and did rides before the crowds and hour long lines. Very $$$ place to purchase eats. Bring it in if that's doable for you.Kids are older and so am I but still had fun. You just gotta roll with it.Very popular place.This stop can be done twice in a day so as not to miss the evening shows, lights, fireworks etc.Disney has perfected the fine art of hearding people. They are professionals at it , and polite too.Bring $$$ & have fun.

Our family visited in November, and we found that the queues were short with hardly any waiting time at all. There were no queues at the front gate, which surprised us, and we went straight in. It was everything we expected, and more. We arrived late morning, and stayed into the night to see the fireworks and the castle light up. Absolutely fantastic. Most importantly the kids had a wonderful time. Plenty of different foods and snacks are available, with places to sit and eat. We all enjoyed the rides and meeting the various characters who were walking about   and they were available for free photos (to take yourself). By visiting in November, we saw the whole Park in one day, and managed to go on some of the rides twice, because of no waiting time. For anyone who has difficulty walking about, there are mobility scooters available for $60 per day, down near the front entrance. The people who rent the scooters will find that there are areas for parking them, outside the rides, so there's no problem with missing out on any rides they want to go on. We went there by local bus from out hotel, and it was easy to find the bus home, in the designated bus area just outside the Park. All in all, Disneyland does its best to make sure everyone has a happy and fun day. I'd definitely suggest staying into the night, if you can, because the whole place is lit up and looks fantastic, plus you see the fireworks and the wonderful castle light show   which had everyone in the crowd gasping because it was so beautiful. By arriving in the late morning, we probably missed some of the early morning queues too, and we still managed to see everything and to get on every ride we wished to go on. And there was still time for souvenir shopping in the night before we left for home. Thanks Disneyland for a great experience!
Spent the first day of 2017 here. Yes, there's a lot of people but, still a lot to offer. No boredness at all. This is what we call, good for the young and old.

We made our first trip to Disneyland in November. Having been to WDW many, many times, it was strange how familiar, yet, different the park seemed compared to Magic Kingdom. I absolutely had a blast on my visit, but the things at Disneyland are not up to par with Disney World. To me Disneyland seems kind of rundown and second rate compared to all of the parks at Disney World and California Adventure for that matter. That being said, the nostalgic feel of the park, and the family atmosphere were wonderful. The guests who visit DL seem to be a family, and I loved that. Being in the original park that Walt built was very special to our group, because we are what you might call,  Disney People,  and as you know if you are a Disney Person, Walt's vision has made an impact on our lives. Being at this park just feels different than the others in that way.The rides and attractions here are great. DL's Space Mountain is light years better than Magic Kingdom. The Matterhorn was a once in a lifetime experience that I would not care to repeat, but I will do anything once! Nemo's submarine was also an interesting ride, if not claustrophobic ride. Our other favorite DL ride was Indiana Jones. Oh my, was that a fun one! We were also able to ride Haunted Mansion Holiday, which is very cool, especially for Nightmare Before Christmas fans. I am not a huge fan of the movie, but the overlay is phenomenal. The food here is fantastic. We ate at Jolly Holiday twice, and at the Market in New Orleans Square. Both were really delicious and not outrageously priced. All in all, I can't wait to go back one of these days and experience it again. I would like to take a little more time next trip, but being our first trip to Cali, we had other things to see as well! I feel like I only skimmed the surface of what Disneyland has to offer in my four days spent in both parks.

It was my youngest first trip to DL and she enjoyed it. It was super crowded, long long lines, and everything was over priced. Definitely make use of your fast passes. My older one is 13 and he didn't enjoy the rides as much as she did as the park had mainly slower attractions, California Adventure would be better suited for the older kids.
Words can't describe this place. It's a magical kingdom where the time stands still. Last 90 minutes of the day which includes the parade and fireworks is indescribable     a must visit

We visited on 25th December, Christmas day. Not that we didn't expect crowd, but the park was overflowing with visitors. Almost no place to stand. And they dont seem to be equipped to handle the crowds. Toilets are a struggle to find (unlike Universal Studios), there are queues for the toilets when you find one. The park maps are filled with tooooo much information for anyone to follow and get the bearings right in the 1st hour. Then they have this Fast Pass system which makes you run around the entire park a few hundred times. We walked almost 7 miles within the park on 1 single day, trying to get done with most rides. Eventually we did manage to do all the rides which needed the fast pass, but you gotta be on your toes from 9 am to 9 pm to be able to achieve that.The rides are superb. None of them to be missed. The Parades are something the kids and adults enjoy to watch.Overall it was a bad experience for the amount of crowd in the park. I would STRONGLY recommend a visitor to choose a working weekday (if possible) to visit the parkAnd to Disney to restrict the crowds to a manageable number. I understand its business for you and should be maximized, but not at the cost of such inconvenience for people with families looking to have a good time
Again, never disappointed.   Be careful of when you travel as peak times will mean long long lines for all attractions.

I have been visiting Disneyland for over 45 years and it has always been a place I have loved to visit. We as a family have visited the park in the last 20 years probably 8 times. We try to go every 2   3 years and it has become a family tradition and something we look forward to. Over time it has become less magical and unfortunately I find myself while we are there questioning what we are doing and whether it is worth it. We just went last week and it might be our last. This was the first time we had gone at Christmas time and we knew that it would be super crowded, but I had no concept of how crowded it would and could be. We always expect crowds and are normally good at managing them and accomplishing what we need to in order to have a good experience. These crowds were unmanageable. We literally couldn't move at times. My favorite area is over by Adventureland and New Orleans Square. There were so many people and the lines for the three major rides over there were so long that they were spilling out into the walkways and made it impossible to move. You literally couldn't walk normally, you just kind of shuffled your feet as you were pressed by bodies and tried to stay with your family. Many times the mass of people would stop and not be able to move and you would have to find another route. We found ourselves going through restaurants and over chairs to get through and heaven forbid if you needed to change directions and part the red sea. Besides the rides my favorite thing about Disneyland is the atmosphere and soaking in all the wonderful details, buildings, decorations, etc. When you are in a sea of people, getting hit in the shins with strollers and getting run over by motorized scooters, the last thing you are enjoying is the atmosphere. There is nowhere to just sit down and take a break, catch your breath and look around. The areas over by New Orleans Square that you can normally sit and enjoy yourself are filled with the overflowing lines of Pirates and The Haunted Mansion. It is exhausting and it gets to the point that all you want to do is leave, but you don't want to because of all the money you spent. You shouldn't feel physically violated after a day at Disneyland. It has lost the charm for me and isn't worth it any more. Obviously it is popular and people want to go there, but there needs to be a limit where it doesn't ruin the experience for the visitors that are there. The rides are cool, but there is a line that you cross when the ride isn't enjoyable any more because of how long you had to wait. The wait time for the Radiator Springs Racers ride was 240 minutes. Yes the ride is cool, but it is 4 minutes long and no ride is worth waiting 4 hours. You could watch 2 movies. I just don't know if it is worth it any more which is sad because I love Disneyland. The return is not worth the cost and hassle. Disney is letting their fans down for the almighty dollar. They need to limit the crowds so that those that are in the park can have an enjoyable time. It gets worse every time I go and it is out of control at this point. It took over an hour each day just to park and get in the park. If we ever go again we will look for a less busy time than Christmas, but from what I read that may not exist. Disney needs to build a new park in Texas or somewhere else or limit their crowds and put their customers' enjoyment first.

We came here 2 years ago. It's a special place to visit and the Christmas atmosphere is beautiful with music throughput the parks. The 2 shows we saw in Fantasy Land were excellent. We missed the Frozen musical in the California park, it was called canceled after standing in line for an hour.The fast pass is great, if it's used at times that work for you.Some of the area is being upgraded, so check on line for more information. There is an app for your phone to give you information on wait times.
have been there 3 times with our little ones. never disappointed. look forward to go back there again!

Any Disney Trip is enhanced with advanced planning. (I think) We've visited on a whim and also with planning. Planning is always best. Does it cost more to stay at the park? You bet, but it's well worth the price. Convenient locations, early entries, perk after perk really makes a difference. This time we didn't stay at the park. Yuk. But, the magic is still great.
We went on the Monday after New Years Day and it was incredibly crowded. The park is beautiful and very well done. Still worth the waits.

First time visiting Disneyland and it was a blast. Similar to Magic Kingdom at Disney World but smaller. Spent the whole day there from opening to closing at Midnight. Hit all the rides we wanted to and used the Fast Pass as much as we could. Place was packed, so some longer waits for rides, but we were fine with it since we were doing the whole day. Seemed a lot busier than its Florida counterpart, probably because it was smaller. Food was expensive, but what can you do. Parades were great, especially the night time one. Fireworks started, but had to be cut short due to wind. Liked that there was still some old rides like Nemo'sSubmarine which have been removed from Florida. Star Wars additions are awesome. Had a great time!

You cannot have a bad time at Disneyland! The park was decorated beautifully with all the lovely Christmas decor. During Christmas they have fireworks every night and several parades during the day. Always something exciting going on. And the Disney staff do all they can to ensure order during the busy Christmas season. Politely asking people to move along if they have stopped in a through walk way etc. The food and drink are ridiculously over priced but everybody knows that so it should not shock you. My only complaint are the strollers. Oh my goodness the strollers!! I don't understand why people think it's a good idea to push a stroller around that is the size of a small car? Or why they feel the need to stop abruptly in the middle of a walkway. They are a hazard in my opinion. I would like to see double strollers banned from Disneyland during peak times. Disneyland is a magical place though and Disneyland at Christmas does not disappoint!

The staff at Disneyland I found were quite rude. Orlando Disney staff way more friendly and helpful. 5 times getting a bus shuttle the bus driver drove off as we were standing there and the bus was half empty. Told us  I have to go. Oh well you guys can get the next one . The very rude cast member onNew Years arguing with my husband and yelling at him as we were all following instructions to move to designated area for fire works and cast member following behind us telling us to move faster and get out of area at the time. Very disappointed. I know they have a job to do and organization is important but the rude body language and verbal inappropriateness was not appropriate. Next time will go to Disney world in Florida. Have been to Disney Paris as well and was good. Overall the park itself is nice. Food is very overpriced and unhealthy. For a park catering to families with children they should offer more healthy food and snacks instead of fast food. Would not visit this park again. Haven't been here for 25 years ( I was 14 last time) and I know why.

We have been here twice now and would come again. It doesn't matter how old you are you can be silly and childlike and just enjoy the amazing rides and soak up the atmosphere. It does pay to get there early to miss the lengthy queues. I really think it could be 'The happiest place on earth''.
No matter when you go, it is always the Happiest Place on Earth and we have a blast!  Although not kept as  clean  as it was when Walt was alive, it is still clean and promises a great day for all!

Was my wife and daughters first time in California and we had a really nice time in Disneyland. The rides were fun and the staff was great....despite it being a rainy New Years Eve day. I was very impressed with how clean they keep all of the venues throughout the day. Food and souvenirs were a bit expensive but the food was decent for a theme park. All in all we had a really nice time and will definitely go back for another visit (with hopefully better weather)!!

Wow! I was deathly afraid to come on NY Eve coz of the comments made on the forum. They said come as it opens and don't leave & plan to come back later or you may not get in. But I think the weather kept the crowd in check.We got there a little later than I planned to (about 11). We were turned away around to park elsewhere coz the parking garage was full. The parking lot was across from the Marriott where we stayed so we just parked back at our hotel and Ubered it to the park. It was $6 for 4 people and shorter walk. The grueling wait was thru security, lines were crazy! But once thru it, we got thru pretty fast since we already had our tix. We got our fast pass immediately for Star Tours then got in line for Indiana Jones. As soon as we got in line, the wait time went from 75 to 100 min. Yeah, groans all around but it was actually only 75. Once you got in the structure it went by pretty fast.It started raining so we headed over to the Haunted Mansion. But we couldn't yet get our next fast pass coz we still had FPs for Star Tours so we ate lunch at Harbour Gallery. Then we were able to get FPs for HM, walked around a little bit till it was time for HM. The attraction was redecorated for Christmas, it was fun to see the decors. Got out in time for Star Tours. The 'ship' we were put on for Star Tours didn't work. After a few tries they finally got us out of there and moved to a different one. The story line was updated so it now includes BB8, otherwise the ride's the same as it was.Because it was NY Eve, I had the sense to reserve for dinner which was a good thing. Most, if not all restaurants were reservations only. The ones that allowed walk ins had just as long of a line as the rides. We ate at Carnation Cafe right on Main Street so we got to see some shorter parades including Mickey and the gang.Paint the Night show was cancelled coz it rained. They had talked about the fireworks possibly being cancelled too coz it was windy but thankfully that wasn't the case at all. They had three diff New Year's countdown events, the biggest one of course was in front of the Castle. We opted to stay by the River coz it was less crowded. They also handed out hats and noise makers. Now, here's my thing...I wanted to do the VIP tour but because I waited too long to book, it was already sold out so I asked to be on the waiting list. They did call me because of a last min cancellation so I was ecstatic.The price for that day? $550 hour with a min of 6 hours! This didn't even include being able to get seats for the shows coz they were booked, and NO food. Basically I'd have spent another $3000  just to get to the front of the line on rides I didn't care to ride on anyway. In contrast, we did the VIP tour as Universal Studios for four people at $1500 which included a buffet dinner. Guess it really depends on your preference.Overall it was a good visit for New Year's. Probably won't do this park anymore; with older kids it isn't as much fun to do.

This was our first trip to Disneyland and I'd heard it was small compared to Orlando, but it seemed large to me. We had three days to cover both parks and it was just enough. There's something special about knowing this is the original park and even though some attractions are a bit old now, they're all very well maintained and I thought Disneyland was as good as Disney World's Magic Kingdom.

Disney just does it right.  The parks were packed for the new year celebrations but it is still the happiest place on earth.  Use fast pass, keep moving and your sure to have a great time( I know I did)

My son (almost 9) and I visited on the first Sunday of October   we got there before the gate opened so we were ready to go right off the bat. We went to Star Tours first thing to get a fast pass but the line wasn't very long so my son went ahead and rode. We met some nice people in line and they allowed him to ride with their kids, that way I didn't have to worry about him while he was riding. I stayed with him until he boarded then they allowed me to walk through and wait on the other side. I was afraid he might get scared but he didn't. We then went to get him signed up for Jedi Training   he got one of the last spots available later in the day. We then went to get a fast pass for Splash Mountain but ended up just going on the ride as the long was really short   we both loved it. We took ponchos so we weren't worried about being wet first thing in the morning. After that we got a fast pass for Big Thunder Mountain then went to Jungle Cruise, which we both loved. Our guide was so funny, I know it is a script, but she was fabulous. That was a pretty long line but we got it over with early. We did Autopia twice   first time together the second time he drove his own car and he did much better. It's a Small World did not disappoint   line wasn't outrageous and moved pretty quickly   it has been years since I went to Disneyworld, so I was excited to go on this ride again. We also loved the teacup ride and did it probably about 6 times   he didn't think he would enjoy it, but loved it especially when we really got it spinning pretty fast. That line was short so we got through it pretty quick. He spent some time in the kiddie land area then we rode the Gadget Go Coaster. Big Thunder Mountain we did fairly early in the morning and I loved it more than I thought   I was a little nervous about it due to back issues, but it wasn't a problem at all. I would have gone again, but he wasn't up for it. He was a little pale when we got off and kept saying he was going to throw up while on it. After he sat down for a couple of minutes he was fine and ready to go. Don't miss the apple freeze with boysenberry   that is possibly one of the best drinks I have ever had and my son agreed. We split a corn dog and fries   got water to drink  which is free   so that was a pretty cheap lunch. We also had a churro, pretzel and pineapple whip   only spent around $30 on food for the day and were well satisfied because we were so busy! The Jedi Training show was so good   even if my child wouldn't have been participating. I had no idea what to expect   I thought they were just going to be showing them some moves, boy was I surprised. He got to  fight  Darth Vader   the photographer got better photos than I did, so I was pleased with that. The photo pass is pretty cool   however we only saw 1 photographer   however we had the Jedi training photos, the ones at the castle and then our ride photo. I made a mistake by not downloading the photos when I purchased them   I didn't know they didn't stay on there until you were ready to download. Fortunately when I called, I got a sweet girl who found my photos and made them available for me to download. Don't miss the light in the window at the fire station on main street near the entrance. That light now stays on all the time   when Walt Disney was alive   that light was on whenever he was at the park. Very nice tribute. All in all we had a great time   were there longer than we thought we would be which was completely fine and would go back again if we had the chance.

This was the first time I've ever been Disneyland & there are several things I wish I had known before we arrived. Our first morning was rough! We got there & stood in line to get our bags checked (security check point) then went to the line to go in (nobody told us we had to trade in our paper tickets for real ones) so I got sent to stand in that line just to find out I needed my Drivers License which I left at the hotel because I didn't realize I would need it (thinking I had the  tickets ). We walked back to the hotel just to get it then had to stand in all 3 lines again with toddlers. Once we FINALLY got inside everyone was tired & annoyed. After about an hour & only one ride we gave up & went to take a nap. The Disney characters are only out for about 15 20 minutes at a time. So if you see them get in line quick. Go as soon as the doors open if you want to ride anything! Our second day we got there early & rode lots of rides! The light parade & fireworks are magical. (If there is any wind they won't do the fireworks) The princesses rarely come out but we finally found them in the back, there is a house where you can stand in line to get pics with like 4 of them. This trip was a mess. But we had fun & next time we'll be better prepared! Definitely take food & drinks with you! They check your bags but never said anything about our water bottles & snacks. We've never ate at the park the prices are insane. We'll go again someday. :)

We love Disneyland and California Adventure, but Tomorrowland has become Star Wars overload. I'm certain that it will change once Star Wars Land is completed, but to what is the question. Everything there, with the exception of Space Mountain (now called Hyperspace Mountain with a Star Wars theme) is dated. Doing something with that big building next to Autopia would be a big step. The Star Wars displays housed there were cheesy. What that area will become in the next few years is anyone's guess. Hope that there will be cool attractions to help alleviate the crowds.
Except for the queues, which are inevitable, this was so much fun! Everything about it   from the rides, to the people, to the weather   was great.

Our son graduated marine boot camp so we decided to celebrate!!!Our Disney planner asked for feedback on our trip... this is what I sent her:Downtown Disney was great!! We wanted to eat at Rainforest Cafe...but it was a steady 3 hour wait through the day....crazy huh?I learned that I should have studied my park maps better!! I should've known them inside and out. I should've made plans on which shows and itemized my day better. I should've learned more about fastpasses and gone to those rides first and itemized my day. I just didn't fathom how busy it was going to run. We couldn't see an inch of pavement on Saturday ...so we couldn't see the beauty of the park...but when the lights came on...it was gorgeous. I utilized the team members A LOT!!! Some things Disney could consider in my little ole opinion...hahahaha1. Limit guests...cut off their ticket sales and only allow so many annual passes in per day?? Somehow limit their numbers so that people can thoroughly experience the magic. (There was estimated to be 50K guests in the park the first day we were there and it was miserable!!! We only rode a few rides the entire day!!)2. Color code their walk paths to help people know where they are. 3. Better signage for bathrooms. 4. And somehow better identify where fastpass booths are. We only saw ONE!!5. Better identify entrance and exits on rides. I'm telling you...we couldn't find them half of the time. 6. Better lighting of the walkways at night. 7. Better signage of where strollers are. And which way is what. For instance we left the park on one end just to get out to realize that we were on the wrong parking lot. Had to go back in and back thru security. We got a 3 day pass for 5 people. My husband and teenager stayed for a total of 5 hours and couldn't stand the crowds and left. Sad bc it's supposed to a magical family adventure and it wasn't like that for us on the first day which was a Saturday. On Sunday we went to California Adventure and it was sooooo much better!! That's why I give my rating a 3. Our DL experience was a 1.Our CA experience was a 5.So I meet in the middle with a 3.
Can never get enough of this place.   Spent grand daughters 2 nd birthday here.   She loved it.  As always overpriced and long lines but worth the trip.

Who doesn't??? Dianeyland equals magic! It is not a cheap place to visit but ir is worth every dollar when you see your kids' faces!! Love Disneyland! Anaheim is good for the first visit as it is not as huge as Orlando's. You can bring food with you in a backpack or in your stroller. It is a good choice to save few dollars since food inside the park is a bit expensive.Enjoy!!

We have been coming to Disneyland for the last few years and have always had a great time! It's always been a dream to go during Christmas! The decorations were great and the rides and parades didn't disappoint! The only downfall is that there was too many people there and I mean too many!!!!! And lots of them sick and coughing all over the place needless to say my kids came home with the flu! Ugh... also it was very hard to find places to sit to eat and lines were long for everything, even the bathroom!!!! I would like to know if there are better times of year to go because this was ridiculous?!?
Our family had a great trip to Disneyland again! We love going to the park and having a great time, especially around the holidays. Great atmosphere during the holiday season.

Big Disney World fanatic and wasn't sure what to expect at the smaller Disneyland and Cali Adventure. But it was very pretty with lush landscaping as well as being very walkable. Love that the two parks are across from each other and one can go back and forth with a hopper pass. I certainly felt  in the Disney bubble  here. Downtown Disney I find is better than Disney Springs in Florida. It's prettier and more quaint. I didn't find the cast members quite as friendly as the ones at WDW. There was once when one was downright rude because my card stripe wasn't working when she was swiping it. I was shocked as this NEVER happens at WDW. Another great Disney experience; can't wait to return.
What must I say? A youth dream came true. It is a suitable experience for young and old. A must when you are in California.

It's a smaller park than Florida and it's not really as Christmassy as you would think. Was really busy but died down after 4 and the wait times were only like 10 30mins instead of 60 mins. The lines a fluent . Would recommend single rider if that's possible with your group. You can fast pass but they are only available at certain times. You can get more than one at a time aswell but I think you have to wait an hour or so. The fireworks were okay but nothing compared to Florida. The light parade was amazing! A must see! Was quaint but busy park. Downtown Disney wasn't much to see, city walk was better. Has the lego shop and a big Disney store and lots of food places. If theres a choice between Florida or California,definitely Florida.

I wanted to give a shout out to the Disney Park Operators that made our visit with a motorized wheelchair individual worth the trip. Our son in law is confined to a motorized wheelchair and cannot transfer easily out of the chair. There are a few rides that are accessible to a wheel chair bound person. Our experience was a great one with these rides (both in Disney and California Adventure). The operators were excited and very efficient at the transfers of the chair and even allowed the rider to go twice on a number of occasions since there were few rides and getting back in line could be an issue. The people doing these transfers were professional and seemed genuinely happy to help us with the rides.Thank you to everyone who helped make the 3 days special and we will go back again due to our experience, just not during Christmas week.

We are Disneyland fans and go often. I would say in all our years of going to Disneyland, this time was the most crowded. We pretty much just go for the Christmas ambiance. WE  risked  our lives and went there in the highh season ( the week after Christmas).Although the place was totally full, we had a great time . I had planned my retirement for late this year and thought my wife and I would take the adult children back to Disneyland that we had last seen when the kids were in grade school. We included the significant others on this trip so there were 6 total. We all stayed at the Tropicana Inn (Good Neighbor Hotel) across the street from the parks, and it is very close to the crosswalk to Disneyland. Very comfortable place, quiet, and a very friendly staff.First of all, as hoped, Disneyland hasn't really changed much in the intervening years. It does change, but those are small incremental changes, and nothing really caught us off guard. It was so pleasant to walk down Main Street and see all the places we remembered from 15 years ago. And our girls knew right where they were once they got into the park, and remembered much more than they thought they would. We had been here twice with the kids when they were small, and I had been there when I was stationed in San Diego in the early 70's. It was like visiting an old friend who never ages. But it was fun to ride on the newer Monorail cars, and I'm looking forward to the new Star Wars Land.California Adventure had just opened (less than a year old) when we last visited, and that's where we saw the most change. The whole park is different from what we remembered, and I would say the changes are welcome. When we first visited, it looked new, there weren't many people in the park, and there really wasn't a lot to do either   Soarin', Screaming California, Bug's Life, Muppet's Movie, and a few others. Now, it really is a full day park, lots to do, and lots to eat, and that includes alcohol, which floored me (still no alcohol in Disneyland). Very popular with the 20 somethings in our group for sure.If there's a complaint, and there is, it was the crowds. I thought I had picked dates that would ensure that the crowds would be manageable (second week in December, according to several crowd trackers), but something worked against us on that score. We walked into Disneyland on Friday afternoon, and could walk down Main Street without too much trouble. But getting around in the parks was slow due to the crowds. We anticipated being able to ride most of our favorites the first half day. But the Disneyland app for our phones showed 45 and 60 minute wait times for most rides. Disbelieving this bit of relatively new technology, we first made our way through lots of people, strollers and scooters to the Indiana Jones ride, and was in line for about 45 minutes (about what the app said). On the way out we checked what the Fast Pass return time was, and it was mid evening (4 6 hours later). We found that to be the case all week   the worst was for the Radiator Springs Racers, the  E ticket  ride in the new Cars Land. We found that if you got into the park when it opened and made your way to the Fast Pass Station by 8:30 or so, you're return time was probably noon. By late morning, the return time would be late in the evening (just before closing), and then by early afternoon, they'd shut down the Fast Pass station. It was just so crowded.We didn't realize it was the weekend for the annual Christmas Choir in front of the Train Station at the end of Main Street. We had a reservation for dinner at the Carnation Cafe for 6 pm, and it was all we could do to make it down Main Street to get to the Cafe in time. The kids changed their strategies to get to the rides after the first day, but my wife and I, not all that interested in doing forced marches to get Fast Passes, decided just to put up with the lines for rides. We made it to all the rides we wanted to go on, but it would have been almost impossible to do everything in the three days we were there. And we did a few rides once that we would have liked to do a second or third time (Big Thunder Mountain, Star Tours, the Racers) but it took too long to wait in line. We did spend some time just walking through to parks and enjoying them, which was part of the reason we went, and shopping for Christmas gifts.Despite the crowds, everyone had a great time. You have to admit that while you may be in a line for over an hour, the lines do move. Its not like you're spending all that time just standing. And thanks to the great theming for most rides, you feel like you're part of the experience even when you're a half hour away from the ride.All in all, Disneyland doesn't disappoint. We're all glad we did the parks at Christmas time, because it really is very festive, all the lights, the Christmas music playing, the Jingle Cruise, the Haunted Mansion. Its amazing to me that the park looks just like it did so many years ago, and that California Adventure looks so much grown up and gives you so much stuff to do. We loved it, and I hope to be able to do it again sometime.
