Waited 40 years to go to Disneyland and finally my dream came true. This place is truely the happiest place on earth. For me anywhere. I'm like a little 10 year old again and love it.The details, patience, effort & passion put into this place is absolutely first class. Thank you Disney.

Just returned from Disney and it gets worse every time I go. I think the Disney company has lost sight of what the park was supposed to be: Fun. There is a sign at the end of Mainstreet USA that indicates the wait time for the  major  attractions. By shortly after lunch: space mountain: 120 min, pirates: 90 min, indiana jones: 100 min, etc... how is this fun? The shortest of these rides was a wait time of 70 min. We talked to a park official and he indicated 88000 for the day we attended. We rushed through the gates at 8am and ran straight to Indiana Jones and were told the ride is down come back later. We then ran to Space Mountain, lined up, got on the ride, our car started to move, lights came on, announcement: ride is malfunctioning and you are being evacuated; ride broken come back later. Back to Indiana Jones: still broken. As they day went on we got on some of the rides. The crowd grew. As the parade was about to start we were accosted by rude staff as we attempted to walk to Fantasyland and were told we need to be moving in a counter clockwise direction to walk there which amounted to around the whole park which didn't make any sense since we were about 50 yards from the castle? Way too full. If there is over an hour wait on EVERY major ride there is a problem. Not enough attractions? Too many people? Bad crowd control? Not pleasurable at all. Is this what Walt wanted?And I won't even start on $8.10 for a sandwich!

There are reviews floating around that Disney sucks and is not worth the trip but honestly its just not the case. I went with my brother in November 2010 and we fell in love with it... truly, madly, deeply in love with it. The whole of Disney (including the Hotels, parks, and shopping) was fantastic and the Cast Members always with a smile on their face will ensure your trip is the best in can be. We left disney with tears in our eyes and smiles on our faces because we will never, ever forget our experiences at Disneyland.However don't be mislead, it would be foolish not to book restraunt tables in advance at the start of the day due to the amount of people, it also makes sense if you prepare to spend money and wait in line (Only a truly 'Foolish' person would think that they could spend a little money or skip lines, seriously its a once in a lifetime oppotunity for most travellers and we only live once). the longest wait for us was the Toy Story Ride where we waited for an 1 1 2 but who cares once your interacting with others and your own family.So in all seriousness Disney is a fantastic experience for all ages if you prepare well in advance for a fantastic time.

We've been to both Disneyworld and Disneyland at Christmas and Disneyworld is definately easier to navigate. The crowds were unbelievable at Disneyland. They don't have as many fast pass opportunities nor do they have many single rider lines. So the lines are incredibly long. I missed having a separate theater for Fantasmic (although the Disneyland show was better) and World of Color would have been nicer to see if I actually could have seen the whole thing. We had fast passes for it and got there close to the earliest time to line up (almost an hour before it started) and we still were so far behind people we couldn't see the whole thing. The Aladdin show is a must see.

This review probably won't even reach the web. I swear the bad reviews are filtered by the rat himself. It makes no sense to me that sooo many people give this place good reviews. We were at Disneyland on 12 27 and 12 28 2010. Turns out so were 80,000 fellow suckers. I cannot fathom why so many people would subject themselves to waiting in line for $80 per person per day. We waited an hour to park, a half hour to board the shuttle buses to drop us in line to wait another 1 2 hour to get into the park, only to be herded down main street to enter one of many excruciatingly long ride lines. One of which exceeded 2 hours for the 2:42 min. duration Space Mountain ride unbelieveable. (First time we tried to ride Space Mt. we waited for 1 2 hr only to be told by Space Commander Tom that the ride was down and  check back later in the day to see if it was up and running.  This happened to us on the Indiana Jones ride as well, but thankfully we had just shuffled into line when that news was dropped on us.)We got a great deal with plane flight, hotel and rental car, but I kept thinking of the foreign suckers that shelled out probably twice what I did to enter the rat trap. Tokyo $1,600, France $800...Hopefully they got deals like we did, but can you imagine hauling 4 people halfway across the globe to basically wait in line at the  Happiest place on Earth?  (It's like political talking points If you float it out there, many will actually believe it without looking into it guilty.)On the second day we were considering leaving at noon to take the kids to the beach (my idea), but I was voted down. I would have loved to see the kids be able to run in the sand instead of stand in line ride on my worn out shoulders again. I have read another review of a guy that  enjoyed spending time in line with the family chit chatting.  (Hey Scandanavian Donald from Newport, I'll flip the bill for your whole family to return to Disney if you can send me a video of your family just  chit chatting  in line for 2:15 hrs.)I know there are ways to beat the crowds (fast passes you're only allowed one per family at a time and they sell out by around 10am), but I shouldn't have to work the system when I'm paying $80 for a ticket. Disney owes its customers to alleviate the crowds by limiting the number of people through the gate or putting all that revenue to work and create a thinktank to streamline the process.Bottom line Ask your friends about their experiences. We sprung it on the kids on Christmas morning so I didn't spread it around with fear that the cat would get out. On my return two co workers said,  You should have asked me, I would have told you it was going to suck.  And suck it did.

After visiting this theme park multiple times, I am a true Disneyland fan. Our entire family loves each visit! The staff is excellent, the rides are amazing, and the experience is one of a kind. We keep going back because of the  magic  we feel there. Even heavy crowds, rain, and long lines don't put a damper on things. This is the perfect family vacation destination.

It was my second time in Disneyland. First time I was celebrating my engagement and now that my parents came we went again.This time it was raining a lot but it did not prevent us from having loads of fun. Actually, the rain made it different and somewhat memorable.Plus, park wasn't too crowded which made easy to go to the busy attractions quite easy in fact. My mum, who is on her 50's, even cried after the ride in the old replica cars from the main street to the castle. My dad, late 50's, laughed as I can't remember in long time. My brother (26) loved it. We had only 2 days, one for each park and it was enough to see everything we wanted and even repeat some. The money should not be, at all, a concern. After your visit, you will definitely say it was a well spent money. That's because they keep the parks perfect. Landscape and details. A to Z, all is very well done and if we, adults, loved it, I can only wonder how a children will feel like. Extremely recommended!

What can I say.DISNEYLAND you never get tired of going. They keep updating the park. It continues to be clean and family orientated.We went there with our five year old granddaughter. We enjoyed seeing the park through her young eyes. We went on rides that we had never gone on before. Even those kiddie rides are a lot of fun.You have to go

Disneyland, What can be said that has not already been said it is fantastic. The atmosphere is electric, the rides and shows are mind blowing, the people who work at Disney are awesome. If you really want to spoil yourself and the family go to Disneyland. From the moment you enter the gates to the moment you walk out you are made to feel like family, I kid you not! They have a system that if you purchase food at Disney you get a voucher ,20% off, for shopping at certain Disney stores. Then when you do shop you get another voucher for 30% off food at certain Disney locations great savings if you plan to do some shopping and eat out a couple of time we saved about $110...... It rained for the last 2 days of our trip but who cares its Disney sure some of the rides were closed for obvious safety reasons but the atmosphere never left it is great......

We went to Disneyland Dec 5th 9th with our two daughters, ages 5 and 10. On the whole we had a great time at both parks and were so glad that we went at a  slow  time of the year. A couple of disappointments, though: We purchased the  World of Color  picnic and  preferred viewing    what a joke. We were corralled onto a walkway like cattle, with no clear way to eat our picnic dinners   we finally just sat on the ground. When the show started 45 minutes later, we adults could only see the top half (and we're both over 5'9 ), the kids couldn't see at all... we ended up carrying them on our shoulders the whole time which was not pleasant. I'd hate to imagine what regular viewing was like. They loved the show, though. Another disappointment was the Princess Fantasy Faire. Our youngest is very into princesses, this was to be the highlight of her trip. We waited 40 minutes only to find that there were only two princesses in attendance, one of which was quite clearly over it and didn't even crack a smile or talk to our girls. There were none of the other activities (story reading, crafts) that I had been led to expect. We wanted to warn the people waiting in line   they should have a sign out front with the number of princesses to expect.Other than this, we had a great time. Some of the famous Disney customer service seems to be missing   about half of the employees were great while the rest were just average. The characters on the whole were very good with our kids. We will be back for sure!

I couldn't help but compare my 3 day December trip to Disneyland and CA Adventure to my 2 day March trip to Epcot and Magic Kingdom. First, I will say that my husband and I had a blast last week at Disneyland and CA Adventure. We just turn in to kids and exhausted ourselves spending all day at the parks. Some reviewers commented on the Cast members behavior, and I thought to myself before we arrived  how could the employees be anything but awesome? . Our Florida experience in March was so amazing   every single Cast member made us feel like we were family   seriously. But Disneyland really was different. We would walk onto rides and the Cast members would completely ignore us, like not even acknowlege we were there. And I heard two Matterhorn operators complaining about a teenage girl who had lost her camera, saying they wouldn't help her   I was honestly surprised by the lack of friendliness. My husband and I have concluded that it has to be due to the  local  feel of Disneyland vs. Disneyworld. Disneyworld truly feels like a vacation destination, and Disneyland feels like the locals probably visit the park all the time   there were alot of lone teenagers milling around.OK, enough complaining, but it had to be said. We really didn't let that get to us, because we had an amazing time. If you get there when the park opens, you have a good shot at getting on all of your selected rides with little to no wait. Utilize fastpass so you only have to wait for rides that don't have it. We went Thursday, Friday, and Saturday. Thur and Fri were not too busy. Rode the rides until 11 am on Saturday, then it was just too crazy, so we shopped and walked around. CA Adventure is nice, but it will be better when Carsland and Little Mermaid are done. Bugs Life was awesome, and we loved World of Color, but what a hassle! Wait for fastpass, wait in crowd for show...that wasn't fun. Haunted Mansion decorated for holidays was so fun that I am inspired to watch Nightmare before Christmas now (I have never seen it!) We stayed at the HI Express maingate and easily walked all three days to the park and back. I think you'd be wasting time if you took a shuttle from that hotel. I hope this helps anyone as you plan for your trip   get a park hopper, it will the magic morning. We got to be the first riders on Toad's Wild Ride, much to our delight. Stay at a hotel you can walk from, and make at least one of your visiting days a weekday. You'll love it.

Disneyland allowed their handmade candy canes to be featured on a national program but has done nothing to meet the increase in demand. They will tell you that you have an equal chance to get these items but unless you do a magic morning or can be there at park opening on a weekday you don't stand a chance & they allow guests to get in line knowing that they have already reached the quantity to be distributed. They also will not do anything to make amends for you missing out.

This was our 4th trip to Disneyland and it was different this time as we had our teenage son with us and this was his trip, Spent 9 days in the parks and was awesome the only thing I was not happy with is that their merchandise is just too expensive.

I took my 1 yr old daughter to Disneyland to see the holiday lights Dec. 4. We got to the park at 5pm so we didn't spend the whole day. It turned out that Disneyland also had the Candlelight Processional going that night so it was very crowded so I left and went to California Adventure. I was glad that I made dinner reservations for 5:50pm at Storytellers Cafe so by the time that we got into Disneyland it was less crowed by Main St. There where cast members that were directing traffic on Main St but I went directly to the back of the Park where Fantasyland is. My daughter loved Disneyland. We rode 3 rides. Pinoccio, Storybook and Peterpan. Storybook did not hold her attention as much as the other 2 rides. It was very crowded but we still had short wait times on the rides (20 min max). We hung out at the Carousel for a bit so she could hear the music and see the lights on the castle, which was a big hit with her. I wanted to shop there but the shops were way too crowded. I couldn't fit into some shops with her stroller. I opted to shop instead at the Disney store in Downtown Disney. We left the park close to 9pm so we heard the Candlelight Processional and they sounded wonderful. I think next year I will plan better and go for the Candlelight Processional. Overall I got some great pictures and I have some great memories of my daughters first Mickey's Christmas.

We took our 2.5 year old daughter two weeks ago and it was so great. Disneyland is magical if you let yourself believe. Every detail is tended is to meticulously. The whole park is as clean as a whistle. We saw the new show 'World of Color' at California Adventure, which is the other half of the Disneyland Resort. The show is beautiful, but not very comfortable to wait for and watch. We went the day it was decorated for Christmas, and it was awesome. If you have the chance to go during the holiday season, GO.

We had a brilliant time at Disneyland   all the corny things you hear about it being the happiest place on earth really ARE true. It's a truly wonderful place to spend lots of quality time together as a family having fun. HOWEVER, the main reason I want to write this review is to warn visitors about the PhotoPass system used at Disneyland. Upon our return to Australia I spent hours & hours over many weeks creating an absolutely beautiful photobook on the PhotoPass website. When I went to order it, the system froze and  lost  my photobook. I have contacted PhotoPass by phone & email numerous times but they have done absolutely nothing to assist me   the silence has been deafening. I have also written to Disneyland's head office and customer relations departments, and received zero response   extremely disappointing & frustrating, especially after the excellent customer service we received from staff whilst at the park. All I can say is, DO NOT USE PHOTOPASS OR THE PHOTOPASS WEBSITE   unless you want your holiday memories lost forever :(

I have been the biggest fan of Disneyland my whole life, as it was always truly a magical experience even as an adult. I was so excited weeks before to My last trip, On November 22, 2010, It was such a let down. The park obviously has cut back on services. You never in the past would have seen garbage cans overflowing. We went to the lockers and the machines wouldn't take the money or print the receipt and we could not find an attendant. Though it was cold outside the locker room was so stuffy, no air flow. First thing in the morning the bathrooms already smelled like port a potties and the sinks only have cold water in the cold of November. Apparently Disney wont pay for warm water. The worst was Cinderellas castle. The sewer smell was so overwhelming that we couldn't stand to shop in the shop and left. Nasty horrible smell. There were kids climbing tall walls by space mountain that says law suit all over it when they fall over, again no attendants. Of course the non attentive parents could care less, I just hate to see kids hurt or Disney sued. We always get shirts and other souvenirs, yet just to try and buy something was a 45 minute wait, only two registers in the store we were in. For the big bucks spent to go to the happiest place on earth, it seems now Disney has fallen into the bottom line and no longer cares about customer service. I'm sad. And lastly, we spent lots of time on main street and I never saw one Disney character except in the parade. 45  years of magic for me erased. Very very sad. Hotel, gas, food, souvenirs, in a recession, not worth it anymore. it felt like a cattle drive. It really breaks my heart that one of the places that dreams are made of is no longer that. I do want to say something positive, The shuttle bus service is great! We never had to wait coming or going and the drivers are very nice. A Big Thumbs up for them! When you wish apon a star has always been my favorite song.

Came for the Christmas season here at Disneyland. What a great time. Beautiful holiday lights and decorations. Several key rides are completely re themed. What a fun time of year to be at Disneyland. Only thing I have noticed over the years is that the staff keeps getting more apathetic and less interested in helping guests than chatting among themselves or trying to do as little as possible. It sure is nice to find those upbeat, enthusiastic cast members when you come across them.

We LOVE Disneyland and went a couple months ago to celebrate my son's 1 year birthday! We had so much fun!! Luckily we got the tickets free for doing community service through their Give a Day, Get a Day program and we found some cheap parking near the park so we didn't have to pay that much to have a wonderful day with Mickey and Minnie! :) My son (who at the time was 12 months old) absolutely loved it and just had a blast! My step son who is 9 years old and has been there MANY times had a lot of fun too! We didn't buy any food there (just packed snacks) and we were able to do the whole trip for under $20! (Parking cost about $10 and we got a couple small souvenirs!) I don't think we could ever do it for that cheap again but we really enjoyed ourselves and stayed there all day but not too late! I would recommend that anyone who is coming to San Diego (it's about an hour two hour drive from San Diego to Disneyland) takes the trip up there at least for one day! It's a fun and memorable place and there are tons of picture ops too!!! :)
We went as a family of 24, all I can say do not go Nov 12 13 as its Memorial Day and the crowds triple and it is suppose to be the same Christmas Day.  The days before were great.

I live in Southern California and bought a premium annual pass to go any day of the year. My pass expired in August and I am not renewing it. Not only is it very expensive, but it's also extremely crowded   even in this so called economic recession. Don't even try to go on a weekend or holiday, unless you enjoy bumping elbows with thousands of people crowding the streets. If you have kids, I would recommend taking them to Sea World over Disneyland. At least it's educational. Disneyland is a tourist trap.

This place is just amazing. Everyone says it's the happiest Place on Earth, but you don't believe it until you experience it. When you walk through the gates you feel like a kid again. I recommend it!

But SO WORTH IT!!How can you not love Disneyland? The vision of Walt Disney is alive for everyone who enters! It is a magical place where parents and kids can have fun together!! You get to enter into a make believe place and just relax and be a kid again! There is no better way to make some fabulous family memories (and take phenomenal family photos!) than at Disneyland! hope that if you are considering making the trip that you GO FOR IT!!!

Disneyland in Anaheim is a great place to take young children on a vacation! We took our two children ages 2 and 5 in November for a quick weekend getaway. The kids had a great time and we were surprised at how many rides they were able to go on without worrying about height restricitons. The availability of characters for autographs and pictures really made it a fun and happy experience for our whole family.

My family and I had an amazing time during our 3 day stay at the parks. The only thing I would do different next time is skip the Halloween Party. Basically you are paying $60.00 for a small bag of candy. Not even good candy. It was a huge disappointment! I am glad to see that there are other reviewers on this site who felt the same way. It is definately not worth the extra money. Otherwise, we had a great time at the parks and cannot wait to get back!

Im 23, but there is no place like Disneyland. I now liv far away but recently was able to go visit family and take trip to the happiest place on earth. I am always pleased with the treatment I recieve from every single cast member. I know how hard they work to make DL a place everyone wants to be and will always remember. I suggest taking all kids to visit at least once and let them experience the magic!

Visiting Disneyland in the off season is the best bang for your well spent buck. The park can get very crowded during Halloween and Christmas as well as summer. Take advantage of the fast passes if you plan on riding lots of rides. You might end up going back and forth across the park, but it is good walking. Eat either before or after the 12:00 hour for less crowds at the restaurants. Stay for the fireworks show... it is well worth your time. Fantasmic is another great show, but you will want to arrive early for better seating.Utilize the train for travel around the park. Pin trading is a great way to get into your trip if you have younger children with you... the cast members trade pin for pin and there are great deals for pins on ebay.

I have to say that Disneyland is one of the most accommodating places for those that have handicaps that I have ever been too. We went to the park in September with my father who is handicapped and they allowed all of us in our party not to have to wait in lines. They also were more than accommodating with seating for their amazing show the World of Color. We were all able to stay together and watch it in the handicap seating area. I was very grateful that we could all be together and enjoy the magic of Disneyland.

Disneyland is the. place. to be.! We just got back from a week long trip to Anaheim, Ca. We were able to go to Disneyland during the Halloween Time season. It was decorated perfectly for the season. Little Mickey shaped planters in fall colors hanging from the street lamps, all of the villians out and about, the haunted mansion set up as the nightmare before christmas. It was a wonderful time to be there! The weather was beautiful and all of the different shows were wonderful!! We got to spend three days at the park, hopping between Disneyland and California adventure. It was a treat, and the perfect amount of time to spend in such a wonderful place.Make sure you bring snacks, water,(of course you can also purchase theirs) camera, comfy walking shoes. And if you have little ones...strollers are a must have!!I was a little bit dissapointed with the number of characters they had out and about. We didn't get to see very many. Other than that, it was a wonderful time of year to be there and experience and participate in the magic.

We were so impressed with the amount of characters this trip. My kids loved to get their pictures taken with them and also get their autographs. They were each so fun and made my kids feel like they were there just for them. Their interaction with the guests was wonderful. It really made this trip magical and brought the characters to life.

My family and I visited the Disneyland theme park in Anaheim, CA for the first time ever on our recent trip to California. We went for one day, a Saturday, near the end of October and really had a wonderful time. My kids are 7 and 10, and there was plenty to do ride etc. throughout the day. It was a great experience overall, but I wish I had known how expensive all the food and souveneirs were, because i would have planned to save more money for our trip. Also, the lines were outrageous! I absolutely wish we had 2 days to spend there instead of just one because there were many things we would have loved to do, but ran out of time: even using the FastPass ride coupons they have! In the end, I can't complain though because the kids had a blast, and so did my husband and I!
this is for sure the happiest place on earth, my family and I had a great time together , and definitely recommend

Love disneyland! It's a great place for the family to go and spend time together. However, you will want to spend a couple of days to be able to see and do everything without feeling rushed! We used to go every year when I was little and now I will start to take my little girl so she can create wonderful memories there like I did when I was a child.

My husband and I took a trip to Anaheim, California with our 2 daughters to visit the famous, Disneyland and Disney's California Adventure parks. These 2 parks are very impressive with the shows, parades, and firework shows they put on for their guests each and everyday. The price for tickets for each park it rediculously high however I felt with the treatment we received from all the employees there, was great and we got our monies worth with the memories we made there. It is a great place to take a family to enjoy the day or days, take advantage of the shows they put on and remember to bring your camera!!

We love going to Disneyland. We go as often as we are able. We live over 10 hours drive away but the drive is well worth it! The people are friendly and helpful and we love the fast pass distribution system they use. My daughters are old enough now to appreciate the Disney princesses and other characters they have seen in the movies. I also appreciate the fact that they let you take food in the park  my family has food allergies so this makes it nice for us to be able to eat. They also have food in the park that accommodates for allergies, gluten intolerance, etc.  you just have to ask for a hand out with listings at the city hall as you enter the park. My only concern was some areas of the park were hard to navigate through with my double stroller, especially during a parade or other night time show (World of Color). But over all it is always a fun and great experience for my entire family!

Disneyland just does it right. Their attention to detail is incredible! We loved seeing the fun Halloween decorations that were creative and not too spooky. The Haunted Mansion and Space Mountain had Holiday changes in them that were so fun to see. This is an all day event that makes you want to come back for more.

My kids were 3 and 5 when we took them the 2nd time to disneyland. They keep asking us when they will get to go again. We said when they are tall enough to ride all the rides. At least there are a lot of kids rides to keep them entertained.
We have a great time every time we visit Disneyland. I would visit during the week to avoid the really really long lines.

Great place, great hotel at California Adventure. It is nice on the boardwalk, easy to get to especially if you have little ones that need a nap. A little more on the spendier side but well worth it for location.

Ticket prices are a little high but Disney has put in so much attention to little details. The food is not badly priced and toys and gift are fairly reasonable compared to admission price. It's definitely worth going and I would suggest not getting a hopper ticket if you're only there for one day. One park is plenty for just one day, although the hopper pass is a way better deal if you can stay for more than one day.

We recently took my almost 3 year old son to Disneyland for spring break. At first we thought that he'd be too young to enjoy himself, but boy were we WRONG!Before going, he knew most of the main characters by face from reading books. He was not shy at all when seeing the large life size versions in person. In fact he would RUN to the front of the line to try and say  Hi.  We spent most of our time in the age appropriate areas ... so ToonTown and FantasyLand. However, he enjoyed the Buzz Light Year ride and the Nemo Submarine ride in Tomorrow Land ... The Winnie the Pooh ride in Critter Country and oddly Pirates of the Caribbean.Of course the lines were a bit of an issue, especially for a 3 year old ... but that was to be expected. The indoor ones with slight entertainment in them such as the Buzz Light Year one was much better for him then say standing in line for the Nemo Submarine. And of course food is a bit expensive, but that I also expected as well.Overall he absolutely loved the place. In the evening the fireworks were a big hit.

Disneyland is great because it appeals to young and old alike. It is a family attraction that brings families closer together. My favorite attraction involves the Disney princesses. Every female child wants to grow up and become a princess. I also love the interactive Buzz Lightyear Astro Blasters ride. And the finding Nemo Submarine is also a treat! Fireworks are also a great way to end the night!

disneyland is one of the best places to go to, especially for kids. this rides are for all ages, however if your a thrill seeker this park might not be for you. i really like the peter pan ride the and indiana jones but for children there is dumbo rides the sombreros etc of the best part of the park is the parade
It was our families 1st trip to Disneyland and we were amazed by all the wonderful things, areas, and people there.  This place gave our family the most wonderful memories for a lifetime.

We have visited Disneyland several times over the last year and my girls (3 and 1) are really starting to LOVE Disneyland   seeing the parades has become our favorite pastime. How ironic since in the 25 years I have live in Socal I have not seen a Disney Parade. Definately recommend it for all ages taking them at age 1 then 2   it was amazing to see the different responses. Love Love Love Disneyland!

I took my 3 1 2 year old to Disneyland about a week before Christmas. This was the worse idea ever!!! It was soooo packed we could move dowm main street. We stayed for 4 day and 5 nights thinking that it would be long enough to see do everything...it wasn't. I knew that it was going to be busy, but never imagened that it could get that packed. They actually had to turn people away because they were at their limit at the park. Thankfully, we were already going to California Adventures that day. That being said, it was kinda cool seeing all of the Christmas decorations up. The best thing was that the Haunted Manson was changed to Nightmare Before Christmas. Overall, I think this time of the year would be bast for older children who can easily walk through a LARGE LARGE crowd.

We enjoyed the entire day in this park and also de California Adventure Park, just in front of it.We loved it, because all the attractions are perfect, in every single detail! Not only fun, but all the decoration is amazing, and the Fast Pass makes it easier to enjoy all the attractions :)Hope you also like it, we want to come back next year!

our two year had the best time at the character breakfasts, each of the characters spent a lot of time with my family we had so much fun we had to go back six months later not expecting a similar experience but I am pleased to report that we had just as nice a time 6 months later.

I live in Orange County where Disneyland is located and I love the place. The food is wonderful just about anywhere! At Thunder Ranch BBQ they have an all you can eat BBQ Buffet for about $25, which is well worth it because you can spend about $25 dollars on just walk around food which is good, but not as good as the ranch! Plus you'll get much more full at the ranch. I must say that you need to come to Disneyland with money. Not only to pay admission, but for food and souvenirs!Make sure you take pictures with the big letters outside the park! Downtown disney isn't apart of the park, but is an awesome place to explore. The rides are surely fun, but honestly you don't need to go on all of them. So many people go and make a schedule of what to do, and these people are usually tired out of their minds by the end of the day! Go to relax and have fun, not to rush everywhere to try and ride every ride they have. Any light shows they have... go watch! It's well worth it and an amazing experience.Having a turkey leg is a must for me every time! They have carts all around the park. I also try and eat clam chowder in New Orleans, its very good.

Altough our first family trip to a Disney resort we were a little bit unsure if we shouldn't pay a little bit more and go to Orlando but everything was perfect and we had a perfect week and of course enjoyed much more by our 9 years old son.We started with easy rides ending with Matterhorn of Space mountain.Also we were impressed by how organized the park it is and altough sometimes we had to stay long time in lines everything was wonderfull.

This was the first time to Disneyland for myself, my husband, our granddaughter (21) and her aunt (23). We were so disappointed that there was no lighted parade, but a group of about 5 or 6 floats with Disney characters, stilt walkers, etc that rolled to a stop near the Castle, played some songs, did some dancing and moved on to disband. Sad there were no fireworks either. Guess if you go in late September you miss those things, which we were all looking forward to. They had the castle blocked off and allowed no one in (around 5 pm) because they were going to be shooting a commercial. Now I had wanted to go inside the castle but was not allowed. The lines were long   seems Australia had school holidays they were all in Disneyland. The Fast Pass tickets didn't work at Pirsates, our granddaughter ended up tryin hers and ours. None worked so I found someone who said they wre having problems with them and just go to the Fast Pass line and they would get in. Silly.The very best part of the day happened while we were standing outside Space Mountain. We were all wearing our first time buttons they gave us, plus the granddaughter had he celebrating 21st birthday button on her lanyard. A Disney rep came up to us as we stood there and said Happy Birthday       . How are you enjoying Disneyland  She was surprised he called her by name then realized it was on her button. I told him we were a bit disappointed that we planned the trip for when school was out thi8nking the lines would be shorter and about the fast pass business, etc. Said the girls wanted to do space mountain again but were so tired of the long lines. This lovely gentlemasn said  Hmm, 21st birthday, first time to Disneyland and bored? I thiunk I can do something about thast . I waited   wondering if he really did work for Disney   and lo and behold they were back in 15 minutes. He took them inside the building up the stairs to the front of the line. What a great birthday gift! Love you Disneyland.We did a lot of shoppibg for gifts for the family back home. But were out the gates by 7 pm  0 can you beleive that? But they closed at 8 anyway.

This place is amazing. The scenery is absolutely beautiful. A great place to take your family or your loved one. The characters are very friendly and photogenic. The experience will change your life. The rides are fun, the food is yummy. The turkey leg is to die for. You HAVE to bring a camera, and water. Long walking is required. This is an all day event!

We took our son 4 to Mickey's Halloween Party! it was a great because I was given a trick or treat bag too, scored at least 4 lbs of candy and got to ride the rides with little to no lines and the Halloween fireworks show was spectacular and so speical ! It was amazing! The entire park was decorated for Halloween from the light posts to the treats and rides. The Haunted Mansion looks so cool. for sure will come back next year ! the best place for Treats Truck !

It truly is the happiest plce on earth. We love going to Disneyland an we always have a great time. The one thing that we don't love are the food prices inside the park. The best advice that I can give you is plan you day so that you can take a short break from your fun, leave the park and enjoy your breakfast, lunch and or dinner at Downtown Disney. It is only a short walk from both parks, the food is great and it won't cost you a weeks salary to feed your family.

It's always nice to say you have been to Disneyland but we went on a weekend that they were celebrating Halloween and it was packed!! There were people everywhere and you had to queue for everything. I knew some queuing would be involved but this seemed over the top. I had to queue to wash my hands after using the bathroom. My advice to avoid the queues would be go early in the morning as it was a lot less crowded then.Also it's well worth using their fastpass system, where you can book time slots for different rides and then you get to skip the line. We did this for 3 rides and it was nice to walk past all the people. Some of the rides were looking a bit tired and in need of a do up, but hey, it's Disneyland and they are still raking in the money.Car parking was great and well organised and a free bus took you right to the entrance. You do have to pay for parking but only USD$15.00 which I thought wasn't too bad considering it's Disneyland.
Fun park with endless enjoyment and activities. we went there for our family vacation and were very pleased with our trip

We went to Disney at the beginning of January and it was awesome. Our kids were 6,4 and 18 months. Our little guy struggled a bit being stuck in a stroller but our older girls had a blast. They LOVED the Bibbidi bobbidi boutique. It is a MUST if you have young girls. I am sure it was the highlight of their trip. They loved being treated as princesses and having their pictures taken. We brought our own costumes (which saves you a bundle) and then bought the photo package from Photopass. So we still got all of the adorable portraits, without spending hundreds of dollars! The princess lunch was fun   but don't expect to spend much time with the princesses. The whole thing seems pretty rushed   we probably wouldn't do it again. Although it was fun for the girls since they were all dressed up from the boutique! We loved dinner at Goofy's kitchen. It seemed like we spent alot more time with the characters. The ride lines still seemed a bit long to me but we were more into the parades, shows, etc. The girls got to dance in the parades, dance in a show with Mary Poppins, do the warm up for a Mickey Mouse Clubhouse show, etc. They had so much fun. And the Aladdin show is a must see.We thought the food was good, and really not all that expensive considering it was Disney. Although my 18 month old did become addicted to churros!!All in all, Disney was better than I expected   by far!

Disneyland is a great place to enjoy Halloween with your kids. There are special treats like Mickey Mouse Halloween cookies and Mickey pumpkin candy apples, and decorations galore. You can also enjoy Disney's Happiest Haunts Tour and ride attractions such as Space Mountain, Tower of Terror, and Haunted Mansion Halloween style. I found a link that has discounted tickets at http:  tickets.101things.com 4670 attraction tickets a18.html

Loved visiting the home of Mickey and friends!! We were able to do so much more than we expected by making use of the fast pass . . . be sure to get the most popular rides first and you don't have to go at the designated time . . . just after the designated time! We had the park hopper and it was worth going back and forth to the two parks. If you do this, definitely get the pass when the California Adventure opens (ask where the line up is) to see World of Color   it is spectacular!!

I've always been a big fan of Disneyland. I always feel safe bringing my two year old son here, even when it's just the two of us for a fun day out. One thing that is amazing is how people are very respectful of this being a family oriented place. There's lots of rides and attractions to keep my son entertained, unlike some theme parks where children under 3 are often left out. Fantasyland is especially great for younger children. The lines for some of the rides are long, so if you can get a Fast Pass, definitely take advantage of that. For quick bites, there are lots of stands for snacks and drinks, as well as lots of walk up windows for more substantial food like burgers, fries, corndogs, etc. You also have some choices for sit down dining if you'd like to get away from the noise and crowd for a little while.Another thing I greatly appreciate are the numbers of clean restrooms available so there's never one too far from wherever you might be in the park and the lines are never too long a wait. You'll understand how great that is when you have little kids with you! If you have babies, the baby care stations are such thoughtful conveniences.The only negatives I can think of are the long lines (but like I said, take advantage of Fast Passes where available) and the cost of the food is kind of high (like all theme parks). Also, you have to take a tram or bus from their parking lots which can delay you usually from about 15 to 30 minutes depending on the crowd. But all in all, Disneyland is such a wonderful experience. We usually go there at least once every 1 2 months.

One detail that caught my eye at disneyland  My daughter had lost one of her trader pins, and with her disappointment asked if we could go to lost and found. Wanting to be the mom that looked like I had tried all things said yes (though I knew this was such a slim chance). The guest helper asked her the description  tried to find one similar  let her chose several and then GAVE her them all. My daughther was tickled, gave the gal a hug, and was so thrilled to have the gifts  the disappointment totally gone. What an event, a gift!
Go on a weekday especially if it is overcast. The lines are much shorter and it is more fun. If you plan to go without kids you can get on a lot of rides towards the evening.

The World of Color nighttime water spectacular weaves water, color, fire and light into a kaleidoscope of fantasy and imagination. More than 1,000 jets of water form incredible shapes in time to the music as Disney characters come to life on a shimmering veil of mist. it was very nice and my son are very enjoy !
Disneyland Park in Los Angeles exceeded my expectation where everyone were telling me that it doesn't worth the visit. But what I saw is completely different.

The most amazing place ever. I love everything Disney so knew i would love this place. We went as a couple without children so this place is just as much fun for adults, it makes you feel like a kid again you forget everything else that is going on and just have fun.I am not sure on the price to get in as we had the southern Californian city pass so had 3 days for Disneyland and California adventure. I felt this was a good amount of time, as we went in September so it was not as busy as I think it can get the queues we that large. The longest wait was for the Indian Jones ride approx 40 mins and this was only on one occasion, this was my favourite ride. We did not get to go on space mountain as it had broke down. The haunted mansion was closed as it was being decorated for Halloween. Get the maps as you will need them as you will get lost, make sure you put walking shoes on as it is spread out. When they take your photos with the characters they give you a little card which you can take with you and give to others for more photos to be stored. Try to get as many photos as possible on the one card as to print off just one picture it is about $20 or you can get a disc for about $60 with all the pictures on whether 10 or 100, only found this out on the last day gutted. The card works in both Disney land and California adventure. The photographers will take photos using your camera to.If you want to watch the world of colour you need to get there very early a get in the queue straight away as you will be disappointed.Do go and watch the parades so much fun for adults as well as kids. We arrived in Anaheim on the evening of a firework display so watched that from our hotel, this was the last night during the week for it but I can imagine watching in the park would be breath taking.All the staff are so helpful and so nice, I did not find any of the staff fake which I was told by others they appeared genuine which I really like. As I have said on other reviews places like this are expensive for food so either bring your own or you can go out of the park to eat. If you do eat in the parks go to California adventure to the place where they make the sour dough the caf   there serves soup in big sour dough rolls, it was this nicest soup every and you then got to eat the bowl.I can not recommend this place enough I am already planning my next visit.
Friendly characters, fun stores and great rides for all ages! Disneyland was the best experience that my family and I have ever had. We will be back again and again!

We had the best vacation ever! I have two kids, a 5yrs old and a 3yrs old. They spent the entire day from 10 am to midnight and could not get enough. We had a great time as a family and would recommend this place to anyone and everyone with kids (or kids at heart!).

Our first experience of Disneyland was so positive and wonderful that we ponied up the extra money for a yearly pass! The park is absolutely immaculate, and full of beautiful flowers, shops and attractions. Every cast member (employee) was incredibly helpful, and always gave us a very happy response. It sounds like a cliche, however, it really is the happiest place on earth. We feel like we are on vacation every time we go there, which is about 2 times per month. I'm sad every time we leave, as the music and the atmosphere always keeps a constant smile on my face. Our children love it too, but we would still go if we didn't have kids! The rides, attractions, characters, and shows continue to impress us with each visit. Everything is always changing for the season, and the shows continue to amaze us!

World of color is amazing! There's no water show like it, and it just brings you back to some of disney classic movies and even some of the newer movies disney has made. Fireworks show is always great... they change the show about every month so you're not stuck watching the same firework sequence every time you visit. Beautiful and always coordinated just right to the perfect disney songs. The holiday firework show is my favorite so far. I definetely recommend getting the (socal if you live in southern california) season pass. If you get a pass and don't like staying at the park the entire day (it get's tiring), there's 3 hour free parking at downtown disney. Rides wise, I like California Adventure better (tower of terror, midway mania, and california screamin'). But Disneyland is definitely more classic with the fireworks show, indiana jones, and space mountain. Either park you choose to go to you, you're bound to have a great time.
awesome experience!!  we had a great at disneyland!! would def reccomend it to all of our friends!!
I got the annual pass to Disneyland and we love spending our free time there. I am waiting for Costco to bring back their annual pass so I can renew mine.

We just recently went to Disneyland park and we had the time of our lives!! Everything is so clean, perfect and detailed and the service surpasses all the rest. It does cost an arm and a leg to get in, but I see why now and would really like to return to the park again someday. Only con was the food was also expensive and not very good at all.

We took our preschool aged son to Disneyland and he absolutely enjoyed his experience there. We stayed for the entire day, and it was worthwhile because our child enjoyed many rides there. We were worried initally that he may be too young.

Once again, Disneyland delivered all of the magic and glory that it is famous for. I recently traveled there with my younger brother and sister, and was amazed and impressed by the kindness, joyfulness, helpfulness, and professionalism shown by the entire Disneyland staff. I have been to Disneyland over a dozen times, and it never fails to exceed all my expectations.

We planned and organised our own trip to Disneyland Park   an attraction not very common to Swedes. The reason for this being the equivalents in Paris and Florida. But we wanted to go to the original park, were it all began. We had a splendid time for a whole week in the park. Eventhough it was very crowded everything worked quite smoothly and with a friendly atmosphere. We stayed inside the park in Disneys four star hotel. Well worth the stay on its own. The only negative thing was the the costs of the flight tickets. They were 75 % of the total cost for the vacation!

It's one of those places I felt the need to visit just once in my lifetime. I did feel disappointed however. The price to get in for our family of 4 (for a 2 day hopper pass) was nearly $600. I did not feel the place justified such a high entry fee especially since there were still so many things you had to pay for once inside.Kids (8 & 10) were over it by the first day. We had to force them to come back for day 2 and we ended up leaving after just 4hrs, due to everyone being tired of walking and waiting in long queues. I heard other kids complaining to their parents and wanting to go back to their hotels.For a place that is supposed to be the happiest place on earth, there sure were a lot of miserable looking parents and kids walking around.The food available for purchase inside is another story   I wouldn't feed that kind of food to my dog! So unhealthy and disgusting. Don't eat at Pizza Port   ended up throwing it away.

It's true! This really is one of the greatest places in the world! There's something for everyone here, good food, shows, rides, shopping, people watching...you name it. The level of quality and attention to detail by Disney is unmatched. I've been going for 30 years and I still notice something new every time I go. It's the one place were we can be kids again: relive happy memories and make new ones every day. There really is something  magical  about it!

All the rides are for 5 10 years old children. And I was expecting something more, I have seen so many better amusement parks. I would recommend Disneyland only for children under the age of 10. I hope we had not gone there, because it took the whole day, but I had no idea... :

we went there in summer and the park is open until midnight and at 9.30 they have fireworks over the castle to music and a story,it makes you feel emotional,space mountain,indiana jones ride and the haunted mansion are a must to do

Loved Disneyland, but I would suggest to the Disney management that it's probably time to shutter Toon Town much like they are doing at Disney World. When it first opened years ago, in the wake of Who Framed Roger Rabbit, it was an interesting novelty and an interesting idea. But now, the trolley doesn't work anymore and serves no purpose. The houses are looking worn and in disrepair. The playgrounds are dangerous with various unsupervised larger children bullying the little ones. Mickey's meet and greet has always been an agonizing bottleneck. The area usually shutters early. Roger Rabbit has always had maintenance headaches. Like California adventure, it has the feeling of being half done...a shadow of what was suppose to be the Hollywood land. Current Disney management has done much to mitigate the harm done to the park during the Pressler era. It's good to have the submarines back, to see the Tiki room preserved, and to have back a great level of service. I would suggest it's time to look at Toon Town as well, much like they are doing at the Magic Kingdom.

Last time we were at Disneyland was five years ago. In between those five years, we've always gone to Orlando and visited the Disney parks there. After all these years, I still prefer the one in Anaheim for the main reason being you can experience the full Disney magic in one whole day. Disney World was just way too big for my wife and I, and with our stay in Southern California short, Disneyland was a perfect way to spend one full day. Unlike five years ago, we really made the most of our experience at DL to soak it all in. Riding the Matterhorn and the Indiana Jones rides are just a couple of examples of great experiences you won't find in DW.

We have not been at a Disney theme park in about 5 years, and we decided it was time to visit. My husband, daughter age 20 and son age 21 went for a three day pass and stayed at the Disneyland Hotel. This is our 5th trip to Disneyland, and we expect that some rides will be closed due to maintenance refurbishment, but we were really surprised at the amount of rides that were down due to technical problems. Space Mountain was closed down for an entire day. California Adventure is undergoing a major renovation   half the park is under construction and new attractions are coming in 2012. The World of Color is amazing and well worth the wait to see. Be aware that there are no seats for this show   you will be standing for the entire show. We still enjoyed ourselves and were able to ride everything we wanted with a minimal wait thanks to the fastpass system. Be careful of food prices   it is really expensive to eat inside the park.

Having now been to Disneyworld's Magic Kingdom last year, and then at the original Disneyland just a few days ago, I say unreservedly that it is hand's down the best theme park ever. I am a true fan of Disneyland, haing been dozens of times in my life and it is always a pleasure. I have been to two Legoland's, Knott's, Magic Mountain, Universal, Epcot, even Playland Park in Rye, NY. Nothing is better than good old Disneyland. They strive to constantly maintain the magic and entertainment value. The rides are fun and enthralling, the atmosphere is great. LOVE IT!!!

I would live here if they would let me! Disneyland is truly a place to go to relax, refresh and to feel ultra special! Our little girl was born with multiple medical and developmental issues. Every time we go to Disneyland we are treated like royalty. She gets to be part of what every girl her age gets to experience. We all laugh together, enjoy the attractions, the food and the Cast Members are the tops when it comes to guest services. Their only goal is to make sure that every guest has an amazing time and memories to take with them forever.If you have never been, the time is now! Save up, do whatever it takes but make sure that at least once in your life you experience this wonderful destination on the West Coast!

horrible experince with my three year old daughter. It was so crowded there were even lines to get into gift shops. I did not bother trying to make my daughter wait 2 hours in line for the peter pan ride.disney obviously pays the fire department to look the other way in terms of overcrowding. Walt is turning in his grave seeing his guests treated like this: squeezing the life out of them for every penney to maximize profit.they pay their employees so badly that only overweight desperate grandmas in need of income will work there. they dont even look at you and smile. they are too buzy being depressed.

As part of our trip into L.A., we drove down to Anaheim, CA to the Disneyland Resort. We stayed at the Anaheim Desert Inn and Suites. Our first day in Disneyland began at the Disneyland Park. Being early in the morning, we quickly got on line for Matterhorn Bobsleds in Fantasyland. The line went pretty quickly. The attraction uses the same track layout that Space Mountain uses in Walt Disney World (which I personally find kind of jerky). Next, we got on line for Space Mountain which broke down, forcing us to leave for another ride. We rode Finding Nemo Submarine Voyage next which we both liked. It was then time for Buzz Lightyear's Astro Blasters where you aim for the Z's and defeat Zurg. We would come back to Tomorrowland later in the day to ride Space Mountain, but first we ventured on over to Adventureland and rode the Jungle Cruise. The Indiana Jones Adventure had just broke down too, so bypassing that we went to New Orleans Square and had a quick bite (a turkey leg; kind of a Disney park tradition). We rode front seat on Pirates of the Caribbean and then rode The Haunted Mansion. I got FASTPASS for Splash Mountain while my wife stood on line for Big Thunder Mountain Railroad in Frontierland. We rode Big Thunder and then decided to get on the just arriving Mark Twain Riverboat. We neglected to ride this in Disney World, so we chose to ride it here. It's a very relaxing boat ride along the  Mississippi River . It was time we rode Space Mountain and we found it much smoother than Magic Kingdom's. We headed back to Adventureland and after another break down, we finally got on Indiana Jones Adventure. We had dinner inside the park at the Blue Bayou Restaurant. It's a very relaxing place where you can have a nice meal and watch those riding Pirates of the Caribbean go along in a dusk, southern themed room. After dinner, it was time to ride Splash Mountain in Critter Country. We rode  it's a small world  (a truly great ride) and the Storybook Land Canal Boats. We caught some of the Fireworks show Magical and then headed back to our hotel (directly across the street from the resort). Before you leave the park though, take a look at the Disneyland Fire Dept. and the window above it. The light through the window represents Walt's presence in his original park. The next morning we got up and had breakfast at the Downtown Disney District. We grabbed a bite at the Compass Books Cafe. Since Disneyland Park opens before California Adventure, we headed back in to Fantasyland to ride Peter Pan's Flight, Mr. Toad's Wild Ride and Roger Rabbit's Car Toon Spin in Mickey's Toontown. After that, we went to California Adventure and got the two biggest things in the park covered. My wife got on line for Soarin'(Over California) and I got on line for FASTPASS for World of Color. We rode Soarin' Over California and then since my wife didn't want to get wet that day, I rode Grizzly River Run in the Golden State area. Honestly though, if you are comparing it to Kali River Rapids at Disney's Animal Kingdom Park in Florida, you really don't get that wet on this one. We took a picture with Mickey Mouse, while on the way to Paradise Pier. I rode California Screamin' three times in hardly no time at all utilizing Single Rider. Look for an attendant to hand you a Single Rider pass for the ride and off you go. We rode Silly Symphony Swings and the Golden Zephyr. We FASTPASS'd Soarin' Over California, so we could ride it a second time. After that, we had Mickey Mouse pretzels and went back to Paradise Pier. We got on line for the fairly new Toy Story Mania! (in all honesty, it's worth the wait). After it broke down, I finally got to ride Maliboomer. We went back to our hotel to rest for a while. When we arrived back at the park we went to the Hollywood Pictures Backlot to ride Monsters, Inc. Mikey & Sulley to the Rescue and Twilight Zone Tower of Terror. The Tower of Terror in California Adventure drops you many more times than its Floridian counterpart. It was time for the insanely long line for World of Color FASTPASS to pay off. And did it ever, we've seen every Disney nighttime show there is, but World of Color just blew them out of the water. 1,000 jets of it dance and project many of your favorite Disney characters while your favorite Disney songs from your favorite Disney movies play making this Disney's best yet. After the incredible show, we had an ice cream (not having dinner that night) and went back to our hotel.

The prices here are unbelievable. $76 each to get into California Disney. Most of the rides have a 45 minute wait or longer. In 12 hours, we probably went on 7 rides; over $10 a ride. Probably spent over half our visit in a line. Spent about $30 on lunch for a meal that I could have picked up at any fast food joint for a third of the price.$3 for a bottle of water? Really? Not going back.  Happiest place on Earth?  Highly doubtful. Probably got one of the highest profit margins though. Walt Disney had a great idea. I doubt that corporate Dsney has the same vision.

We visited Disneyland today, my wife, myself and my 3 year old son attended.I don't know where the park managers get the idea that they can safely pack the number of people in to the park that they do and have any degree of safety.The management obviously has not a care for their patrons' fun or enjoyment either. The wait for anything was at minimum an hour to ninety minutes with SO many more people than the park was ever designed to deal with..The place was obviously designed for maybe 20% of the number of people who they actually let in.It seems that the only thing the park wants is money, nothing else.The Parking was exceptionally expensive, the tickets were exceptionally expensive, and what did we get for it? There were no employees on the grounds, except ones selling things or palpably miserable overworked minimum wage teenagers running the rides.We left in disgust after 2 and a half hours of misery, nothing could salvage ANY part of the experience. It was literally the worst time I have ever had at a park like this, and there was nothing special going on, IT'S ALWAYS this bad!Save your money and your time, go elsewhere, Universal City Walk is much much nicer, less crowded, cost less and was more modern. They could not pay me to go back here.

I'm 50 now and finally got to go to Disney Land. I've been to Disney World about 6 times, but the thrill wasn't the same. I've wanted to go to Disney Land since I was a kid, before there was a Disney World. I loved the park. It has a few attractions that the Magic Kingdom doesn't, so that was nice. The park seems a little smaller and compact than the Magic Kingdom, which is also nice. Cinderella's castle is much smaller, which goes to show the differences between the year the parks were created. When this park was built, Cinderella's Castle would have been considered grand. My grandson (8) had a wonderful time. If you're in the Anaheim area, make plans to visit this park. You don't have to have kids or grandkids to enjoy this attraction.

I've been going to Disneyland since I could remember, not being able to sleep at night when i was kid since i was too excited for the Disney day to come. My husband and I have had an annual pass of some kind since we first met. We got engaged there (@ New Orleans Square), and got married across the street (@ the Sheraton Anaheim). And we continue to carry that tradition with our now 1 year old son (who has gone to Disneyland since he was 4 5 months old). To sum it up, it's our happy place. : ) After working long hours in nightshift along with all the other stresses of life, Disneyland has always been a welcome environment of childhood fantasy, innocence, and pure fun.Our last trip on Aug. 2010 led us to a whole new adventure though...I was in line for a Dole whip (best refreshment you can get at Disneyland by the way), near the always crowded entrance of Adventureland. I took off my wedding ring in order to apply sunblock lotion to my son and I, & in the process of trying to put my ring back on, the worst possible thing happened... my ring slipped off my fingers & rolled away... underneath a plank... in one of the busiest places in Disneyland! Needless to say, I got very flustered, very fast. As my husband went to find someone that could help us (fortunately, you can see the ring from the top of the plank, but you just couldn't fit a finger in there to pull it out), i continued waiting in line, dumbfounded, feeling like a world class idiot, all the way until i ordered my Dole whip (which didn't sound as great anymore to have after the fiasco). So as i was waiting there with my son in the triple digit CA heat, and our Dole whip melting in the process, I was becoming very frantic in my head. Thankfully, my husband came back with someone who worked at one of the nearby stores, who said that they couldn't do much until maybe 10:30 pm when maintenance could try to get it out. But he did suggest to check with City Hall to see if they could do anything about it sooner. So we headed down Main Street (as i was in tears) to City Hall, where we spoke with Christy (don't know if i remember her name correctly, since i was bawling at this point). After speaking with someone on the phone, she told us to head back there and wait for 2 maintenance workers in all blue, who would assist us any way they could. So we headed back, continued to wait in the heat, as we were trying to find the ring again among the planks. Not too long after, 2 maintenance workers came with the names of Alex & John. They thankfully had flashlights to help us find the exact location of my small gold ring with diamonds on it, & worked steadfastly in their attempt to get it out. They had brought a metal rod that they bent to make a hook, which helped to get the ring from the dirt. But the problem was that the metal hook couldn't fit back through the slits in order to be taken safely out. So as John got a wire he could strip, Alex stayed back (very nice guy) and reassured me that they would get my wedding band out somehow, no matter what it took. He told me they had to disassemble an Indiana Jones ride vehicle in order to find something before, and that John had to get into scuba gear to fish something out from the water. Now that's what i call first class Disney cast members, and Disney first class service!!! : D I just loved how i was constantly reassured, since i already felt so lost and small during this whole thing. Thanks Alex! : ) So after John returned with some wires, he was stripping it to get a small metal piece that can help my ring come out. Alex then took a wire piece, wiggled and maneuvered around underneath the plank, and before i knew it, out pops my ring, safely in between the wire strip! Hooray!!! : D Alex even wiped it off for me (there was dirt on it of course) before returning it to me. I was ecstatic to have my wedding band back! : ) It has my husband's name & our wedding date engraved on it, as well as 5 small diamonds as a setting, that made it irreplaceable. And thanks to the help of 2 of the most awesome cast members ever: Alex and John, my happy place in Disneyland stayed intact. I was soo happy when they rescued my ring, that i hugged them! : ) Thanks soo much Alex and John once again!Come to Disneyland everyone! World class Disneyland cast members like Alex and John make this truly the happiest place on earth. : D

Disneyland is still best of the breed but it is an expensive place. The entry price is quite expensive. We didn't buy tickets in advance and discovered that they had 'blocked out' the discount for locals and didn't offer discount for AAA membership at the park. Also we discovered that you have to pay extra to get into the adjacent and smaller Disney California Adventure which is right by the Disneyland entrance. A big disappointment is the additional costs. For example parking is $15 per day. Food and refreshments are very expensive (e.g. $18 for 2 hot dogs and two small cokes). The quality of meals on site sometimes leaves a lot to be desired   the $14 chicken lunch was like bad dorm food. Kids still love Disney. The staff are mostly very helpful and very friendly.

I took my 14yr old son to Disneyland and we had two full days there. Disney itself was pretty average as there aren't many adrenaline type rides there to make it exciting. Space Mountain was by far the best but with queues being 75mins long rides were scare. This ride broke down for nearly a full day and the Indiana Jones ride was a 2 1 2 hr wait even though the sign said 1 hr. It also broke down when we were right at the front of the queue after waiting 2hrs! Use the fast passes, definitely helps with the waiting times. Best time to go is 8am in the morning, worst time after 3pm. The park was parked which became very stressful and with many people from different cultures , with an emphasis on one in particular, having no personal space boundaries, it was pretty stressful.California Adventure Land was by far the best. Great shows, much more relaxed atmosphere and great night parties in the Hollywood area of the park. Awesome.

We travel here at least a couple times each year, and stay for a week each time. There is so much to do and see that we never get bored. The Cast Members are always helpful and go out of their way to make your experience enjoyable. The food menus are changing to healthier and tastier choices, and I personally don't think the prices are unreasonable at all. There is enough of a variety of rides to please everyone, and plenty of places to rest when you need to sit for a few moments. My favorite place to vacation.

Went to Disneyland and CA Adventure and of cours ethe place was packed but there are new iPhone apps that let you know how long the wait time is at all the rides in the park which really helped in mapping out our day. It relies on visitors to enter the wait times but the app that I downloaded was right on everytime.

Too many people have already written great reviews, so I won't go over what they've already said. I found the following to be the most helpful:Use Fastpass! (and use it again!)If you have an iphone, get MouseWait (free app) ! Take your own snacksWear sunscreen (kind of obvious)Mornings are less crowdedI was told there are daily thefts of a few double strollers (or people upgrading) but don't lock your stroller to Disney property. Just run a cable bike lock through the wheels and to itself   NOT to a fence, etc.

I was privately a bit worried about doing Disneyland for 2 days at the end of our 2 week US trip. I   m not keen on theme parks and we were dreading the queues for the rides and crowds trying to get food. Then we saw a recommendation for a book called the    Unofficial Guide to Disneyland   , which has incredible detail about every aspect of the park, and includes various length    touring plans    which you can use   adapt for your own party. Having read the book, we then started to think that we would have to plan it like a military operation for our time there to be a success. So we arrived with trepidation, armed with a plan, plenty of water and 2 very excited children... and had the most amazing and brilliant two days! I was incredibly impressed with the attention to detail everywhere in the park, the friendly helpful cast members, the smiles, the colours, the parades, the fireworks, the rides, the characters   everything! Getting there early makes a huge difference     we used Fastpasses wherever we could and went on the most popular rides before 10.30am. Note that you don   t have to go back during the hour printed on the Fastpass   you just have to make sure you are there after the start time. In fact we were allowed to get on one ride 10 minutes before our Fastpasses started. The longest we waited was 35 minutes for Buzz Lightyear   apart from that one we only waited 15 minutes at most. We also used the    child swap    when our daughter was too nervous to ride which worked really well.Food was OK and not as expensive as I had thought it would be     much better value than SeaWorld in San Diego     we ate in the caf   in Tomorrowland as the queues seemed not too long and there were pastas, pizzas and salads which the pleased the adults and the kids. We had fabulous ice creams on Main Street     there was a big queue but it seemed to move at a good pace so we didn   t wait too long. We got a spot in the shade about 30 minutes before the afternoon parade     arrive any later and you   ll be searching for a shady spot. Quite by chance we were sitting at the point where they stop and dance   the dancers encouraged all the children to come out and dance with them too. I did some autograph hunting with my daughter and was very surprised that we managed 21 autographs in 2 days! We didn   t do the princesses (seemed to involve a very long wait), but concentrated first on Toontown where we saw Mickey & Minnie in their houses, and Pluto. I asked a cast member where we could see Donald (my favourite) and she pointed us towards Town Square (at the entrance), adding that he might be there around 10am. So off we went     and he appeared on schedule, along with 15 other characters, one after the other. We spent about half an hour hopping from one queue to another, having a great time! The rides are varied and fun, beautifully made, and loading and unloading is in the whole extremely well organised, ensuring that they get as many people through as possible. I loved the Tiki Room     a very unusual and quirky show with animatronic birds with various different accents     and Pirates of the Caribbean was very impressive. All in all it is a totally magical place. I was a bit wary about the whole Disney experience, thinking it would be sickly sweet and over the top, but it is just fantastic!

Just finished a 4 day vacation at Disneyland, and the one thing I would like to comment on is how efficient they are at moving huge amounts of people through that park. From the drive up the highway to the parking, the trams, security check, and finally the admission gate, you practically never stop moving. There are crowds that at times are hard to navigate, and you do have to wait for rides,but you never feel 'stuck'.We didn't even utilize fastpass or ridemax, and never felt we waited too long for any rides. Granted, all the rides we went on were geared for our daughters' ages(3 and6). Our wait times ranged from 5 40 minutes.I would like to disagree with some other reviewers about California Adventure. The park was certainly less crowded than DL and our daughters got more facetime with characters. There were also plenty of kids' rides and attractions. We went for half a day, but probably could have stayed longer.Let me leave you with a helpful hint about Disneyland. I don't think security cares at all about what kind of food you bring in. We kept pushing the envelope, and by our fourth day we literally had about 10 hot dogs in our bag. I showed it to security, smiled and said,  we're ready to eat! . She just smiled and told us to have a good day! The park has some good food, and you can even find some relatively good deals, but why spend money on food needlessly?Also, for iPhone users, there's a free app called mousewait that tells you how long each ride is running. It also has menus for each restaurant, so you can contrast and compare. We found it to be pretty helpful(especially for free).Yeah, there's no way around it, it's going to be expensive, but we don't regret it. Our kids loved it, and can't stop talking about it!

Disneyland is one place we all know. Most of us have been there. Many of us several times in fact. The one thing that we all have done is shown up with a camera and gotten home to look at our photos and realized that our photos look nothing like what we saw. There are many super rides and attractions here at Disneyland. Plan your trip in the fall or early spring to avoid crowds.

First, this is the only review I have ever written  I have noticed that Disneyland has felt less and less personal the past few times we have gone (we are southern Cal. residents). It seems that what was once a well oiled machine, has become very robotic and cold (not to mention $$$$$). Number one: Beware of the guy at the nearby Marriott (an employee of Disney) who sells the tickets to Disneyland. We had three families all staying there to avoid morning traffic as we were to meet an entire kindergarten class the next morning. We all bought our tickets at different times, however when we met up for dinner, we had all been sold three day tickets, and we were all baffled at how masterful the guy was at talking us up before we knew it. Had it only happened to one of us, you could say it was just one of us being gullible, but all three of us? Number two: Part of the scam was that we (each) asked if it was reasonable to go to the California Adventure for the light show (since we had a night to fill). Without any mention of anything extra needed, we were sold these three day things so we could view the show. He told us the time of the show, but neglected to tell us that a fast pass is required (and those are gone by mid morning usually)  So, we all have our $$$ 3Day passes, and keep our 10 very young children up late by going to a very loud restaurant on Disney Way (all restaurants had long waits). Then, we go into the Disney Adventure to see the light show, and we just keep getting ushered down a street by  cast members  with flashlights...We think we are being ushered to the show, but after tremendous amounts of walking with now very tired children, we figure out (by asking one of the wavers on) that we can't see the show without a Fast Pass (we did not know what that was). Even though there was PLENTY of room behind a rope surrounding the edges of the street, we were not allowed to either go inside the rope to watch or even stop where we were standing. I don't know if you can imagine, but three Moms and ten tiny children at 9:30PM walking endlessly, and being told they cannot stand for a moment. One Mom stood for a minute with her child to get a glimpse, and security was called. When we promised not to stand, the followed us from behind a little, making sure we kept moving. Needless to say, we were all furious that were sold 3 Day passes only to miss the whole reason we bough them  A pure scam. Number three: Disney Customer Relations: After all this, I at least wanted my money back for the night we just walked and were not allowed to do anything in the Park. The customer service was the worst I have ever encountered. Instead of acting sympathetic, they were cynical and argumentative.
