The person I spoke with loved to talk, and would give long explanations for why they actually did nothing wrong. After two separate conversation, and then asking for a supervisor, I again found the same defensive and unhelpful, unaccommodating attitude. It was as though they had memorized scripts. It was a very big disappointment to us all.

I cry every time we have to leave this place, so much love and magic is in the Disneyland Resort. It's one of those places you'd never get bored in...it's spectacular. It's one of the only places I feel like a kid again..and I think everyone should come here once.

Never in a million years did I think I would like Disneyland more than Disney World. After 5 spectacular trips to Disney World in the last 9 years, I had significant doubts about my decision to travel to Disneyland. I was convinced that nothing could trump my love for the Magic Kingdom; but, boy was I wrong!We had purchased the special deal that afforded us 5 days in the park for the price of 3; however, we only had 4 full days and 5 nights to spend. So, our first view of the park occurred around 7:00 PM in the evening (with closing time being at midnight). When we arrived, I was not the least bit impressed by the Entrance Plaza, nor was I enthused with the Train Station. And, when we walked down Main Street, the only thing I could concentrate on was the wimpy castle. I was completely underwhelmed and almost in tears. I tried not to show my disappointment, but I sincerely wished that I could click my heals and be transported to Orlando.That first evening, we had 7:30 PM reservations for The Blue Bayou. To get there, we navigated our way through Adventureland, and made our way to New Orleans Square. I must admit that through the entire walk, I must have been in a stupor, as I don't remember much of it. All I recall is checking in at the restaurant, turning around, and being awakened by the allure of the unique shops, the lively jazz music, the stunning architecture, and the positive energy of the area. At that moment, I took a deep breath, and allowed the Disney magic to consume me. When our name was called to enter into The Blue Bayou, we were immediately transported to a different time and a different place. It was quite dark (as it is perpetually twilight in this restaurant) as we walked along the terrace to our table beside the river, where the pace was slower, the air was richer, and the atmosphere was one of intrigue and mystery. As we looked up, my daughter and I found that we could not see the ceiling...it was if there was no end to the  sky . It was simply divine to watch boat after boat gently float by as they began their journey toward The Pirates of the Caribbean. To be honest, I can't remember what we ate; all I remember is that it was good and it was also expensive. Yet, we felt so special and so lucky and so smart at having made the decision to start our Disneyland experience at this magical place.At the conclusion of our meal, most people were in position around the lagoon to watch Fantasmic, so we were able to  hop right on  to the Pirates of Caribbean. That also turned out to be a wise decision, as each day thereafter, this ride always had ridiculously long lines (except for during Fantasmic). As we got into the boat, we were tickled to see The Blue Bayou from a different perspective, and smiled and waved at our waiter as we floated by. Needless to say, we found it a bit peculiar to begin in the bayou, yet somehow end up in the treacherous waters of The Pirates of Caribbean; nevertheless, none of that mattered, as Disney has a way of seamlessly making all things work out. By the way...the ride itself was very similar (if not the same) to that in Orlando.The rest of that first evening we spent walking around and making plans for the next day. As we slowly strolled about, we took in all the scenery and marveled at the details. This is one of those elements that makes it so strikingly different from The Magic Kingdom (I make this comparison, as Disneyland is most like the Magic Kingdom in Orlando). When I told my husband this, he asked me to explain; but, I really couldn't. It's just that every square millimeter is magical; everything is perfectly placed; meticulous attention is given to every single aspect of the land. That's why I was so glad that we opted to take the first evening just to look...to notice all those details and to make sure they weren't overlooked...to see everything as they are meant to be seen. It's so easy to get lost in the hectic shuffle as you rush from ride to ride. If you have time, I strongly recommend that you stop and look...really look. You'll be glad that you did! During the next four days, we spent three in Disneyland. We arrived 45 minutes before park opening, and were shocked to see that there were already so many people waiting in line. This didn't end up being a factor, as once the park gates opened, we quickly headed in the opposite direction than most of the crowd. For the first time in our Disney experience, we honed in on one area of the park, as a way to save our legs and to maximize our time on the rides. The first full day we focused on Adventureland, New Orleans Square, and Critter Country. We were the first to arrive at The Haunted Mansion, and rode it two times. In between times, I rushed over to Indiana Jones and got a Fastpass. We then rode Splash Mountain twice before lines ever really formed, and got another Fastpass for later in the morning. After that, we rode Winnie the Pooh, enjoyed its shop and some delicious chocolate, then went to the Pirate's Lair on Tom Sawyer's Island. After a little more than an hour on the Island, I obtained a Fastpass for Thundermountain Railroad, and we went to ride Indiana Jones and Splash Mountain, at which time we were then able to ride Thundermountain. While my family ordered our meal at Critter Country (which had a lovely view of the lagoon and the island) I headed over to get another Fastpass for Indiana Jones. With that being said, we really worked the Fastpass system, and rarely waited more than 10 minutes for any ride. This side of the park has more opportunities for such a system, as we soon found out the following day, when we toured Tomorrowland.What were our favorite rides? Indiana Jones, the Haunted Mansion (although it's different on the outside, it's very similar on the inside), Splash Mountain, Space Mountain, It's a Small World, and Buzz Lightyear. Truthfully, however, we enjoyed each and every ride and were able to do almost everything at least twice. Naturally, not to be missed is Fantasmic! But, be sure to get there early, or you will struggle to find a spot to see, as the cast members will not allow you stop in any of the walkways just to sneak a peek! Moreover, we were awestruck by the fireworks spectacular, and were almost brought to tears. Any spot is a good spot to see the fireworks; but, if you are lucky enough to be behind the castle, you will have an up close and personal experience with Tinkerbell as she careens down the cable from the Matterhorn Bobsleds to the castle. Our only real disappointment was Peter Pan's Flight, as it was so much more dated and less magical than the one in Magic Kingdom. On the other hand, we were pleasantly surprised by Fantasyland at Disneyland, with so many more delightful ride options, such as Alice in Wonderland (so cute) and Mr. Toad's Wild Ride. We were equally surprised by our fondness for the castle, especially since we were so disappointed upon first sight. It is actually quite splendid, and you can actually walk through a portion of it, during which time you can    participate    in the story of Sleeping Beauty. Perhaps even more surprising was Toontown. It definitely is not one of my favorite spots at Magic Kingdom, but it is a real kid pleaser at Disneyland. We really could have spent hours upon hours here! We were also surprised by how chilly it gets in Anaheim right around 6:30 PM. As a matter of fact, we wore sweat shirts, and many of the cast members had on long winter coats! So, keep that in mind as you make plans to visit Anaheim.In many past Tripadvisor posts, I have read how irritated some people are with the commercialism of Disney (i.e. all the shops). I must say that I rather enjoyed each and every one of them, as they are all different thematically, and truly offer quality merchandise. You always have the option to say  no  and to avoid the shops altogether, but we found them to be a nice option when the crowds are large and our feet are tired. Plus, we like to have mementos from our trip, and do our best to make wise purchases. Our favorite shops were in Adventureland and of course, on Main Street. In regard to restaurants, we highly recommend The Blue Bayou and the Carnation Cafe (on Main Street). We were lucky enough to have a table reserved a half hour before the parade was slated to begin, and were able to enjoy the parade while eating our yummy supper. Along with that, you absolutely must get reservations for The Plaza Inn character breakfast. We snagged the very first seat at opening, and were greeted by a plethora of characters. Chip and Dale were especially playful, as they constantly teased my daughter and played with her long hair. Naturally, we loved the characters from Winnie the Pooh; Eeyore was especially sweet, as he lumbered around our table for most of the time. At one point, the characters began dancing, and Hook took our daughter by the hand, and invited her to dance. It truly was a highlight of our trip. And, yes, the food was great too!I don   t' know about you, but when I'm on vacation, I crave fresh fruit! You will find plenty of it in the park. That leads me to our favorite treat at the Tiki Juice Bar in Adventureland...Dole Whip soft serve. Believe it or not, this is the one and only thing we waited in line for while at Disneyland (and it   s a long line!). After this epic depiction of our Disneyland experience, I just want to reiterate how joyful this place is. While you do spend a lot of hard earned money, it was worth every penny to us. We were there at opening, and stayed until closing. We strategically planned everything, from the areas of the park we worked, to the times where we rested our feet; yet, we also felt free to just throw our plans aside, and just enjoy the splendor of this magical place. Although we still love Disney World, and will likely visit again in the near future, we much prefer Disneyland to the Magic Kingdom. So, do not miss a chance to go to Disneyland...it is just what the kid inside each of us craves! Enjoy!
Disneyland IS NOT Disney World.. It is the original and maximizes the Disney experience in its (comparatively) small space.
The rides were great but the crowds were ridiculous! I waited for 60 minutes for some rides. The food on offer is not the healthiest. Otherwise it was great fun.

I honestly believe this is the best theme park in the world. I think it has the perfect combination of big exciting rides and a heart warming atmosphere. I have also visited Orlandos and Paris' Disenylands and I believe Anahiems is the best park. My only negative would be that you need to spend a few days there to see everything, however it is obviously better to have alot of attractions instead of too few.

Disneyland is just as we remember. It is very crowded in summer. Do use the Fastpass whenever available. Go to the park when it opens, leave for a break in the afternoon, and come back after dinner and stay as late as you can stand. Early morning & late evening are much less crowded.
Great fun   everything Disney should be. Definitely worth taking advantage of the fastpass during the busier months to avoid spending long queues for rides.
There are some unique rides here that arent at Disneyworld, but you can easily visit both parks in one day.  If you're used to Disneyworld you won't be impressed, but it was fun for a day.

Disney was as we expected. Crowded and very overpriced. Use Fastpass whenever possible. Don't eat in the park. The food is awful and overpriced. We found Tortilla Joe's Taqueria in Downtown Disney. They have huge burritos that we shared for two people. My kids loved the placeand it was better and cheaper than eating in the park.

Disneyland is the best place to be with your children, I stayed at the Sheraton and while the fireworks are fabulous at the park, they are great at the hotel,and no crowd, afterward take your kid to the park and enjoy everything without the lines and crowds.It's Disneyland, too bad it is so overpriced. 300 hundred bucks for two days, I'm talking admission though to both parks.Anyway It was great and Preston and I hope every parent and child enjoy the main street USA.

I am from Australia and have visited Disneyland 4 times and love it. If your thinking of traveling over to LA from Australia to visit remember the first few days will be a blur because of jet lag and the time differences . Stay at a hotel close by to Disney and stay at least a week before you move on. We based ourselves at the DIsneyland Grand Californian Hotel and hired a car to see LA. DIsneyland And California Park are both wonderful. Both parks have great rides and lots of things to do for Adults as well as kids. If you have children seeing the excitement on their faces when they see the characters or watch a parade is soooo worth the trip itself. And for those Australians wondering weather to head to DIsneyworld in Florida or Disneyland in California I ve been to both and in my opinion Disneyland and California Adventure Park is better then Disneyworld. Disneyland is less busier (still busy but less then Disneyworld) and Disneyland seems to have only all the good rides and Forgets the boring rides. At Disneyland the two parks are so close to each other which is great. But in Disneyworld the parks are far apart and you must use buses or boats or monrail to go from park to park. Disneyworlds good but Disneylands better.

If you've been to Disneyworld in FL... you're in for a surprise. This park can be done in 1 day. Small, but cute    still the same great rides. LOVE the FastPass option on the bigger rides. California Adventure right next door w in walking distance. Parking was in a covered garage, so not hot tushys for the ride home.

We had a great day split between the two parks, morning at California Adventure, and afternoon into evening at Disneyland. The rides, and attractions are fantastic, and it is a great way for the family to spend a couple of days. Keeps getting better.. as well as more expensive

This was an aazing place.It was clean   we noticed that there was no dirt, grime or paint work needed anywhere except on one bin.The staff were amazingly friendly and the attractions were amazing. Customer service everywhere in the park was fantastic.Everything was amazing.

We surprised the kids (8,13 & 15) with a trip to Disneyland and we were not dissapointed. Disneyland is a place where everyone can feel young at heart. We spent 3 full days at the park including California Adventure Park and still didn't see it all but loved every minute of it. We were lucky as it was a quiet time especially in the mornings and we had the RideMax (software) plan in our hand and never had to wait for a ride!! This a great tool to purchase for just $15 and saved us so much time and stress. I loved the Minnie and Friends Character Breakfast so much I nearly didn't eat! We were all like little kids when the characters came to our table and posed for photos, autographs and made the children laugh. Great way to get those Character Photos. My 9 year old had a Bibbidy Bobbity Boutique experience that was just amazing and so worth it (can be expensive depending on your choice) but it was so wonderful to see her behave like a 9 year old and go along with all the magic and fantasy they dish up at the boutique. Get there early and do the popular rides and if you are staying close by, go back for a break in the afternoon and come back for the evening. Don't miss the Fireworks, they are the best I've ever seen and really sum up the whole disneyland experience (It's crazy busy, so if you can get there early for the fireworks to get a good spot). If you can't find a place to sit for lunch, venture out to downtown Disney which is full of great places to eat. Some rides you do get very wet so cover your camera or wear a poncho but don't be scared enjoy it. See the parade, watch the shows, try and do it all, there is so much to see and do.

I just got back from a long weeked getaway to Disneyland with my two teenage daughters and it was so very Magical. We had been to DisneyWorld twice before, but wanted to come to DisneyLand, and we are all still wishing we didn't have to leave. Everything single thing about Disneyland is pure enjoyment, at any age. I am in my forties, and I still get excited when I see a cast member or character, infact, I think I shed a few tears when I met Tinkerbell for the first time on this visit. The details of each ride and the effort of all the staff who work there to ensure that you have a magical experience is undescribable. Our only disappointent was that a few of the rides were down, but that is to be expected. The thrill of being there and just experiencing each moment makes up for it. We are already planning our trip for next year.

After going to Disney World in Orlando a few times and having not been to Disneyland in Anaheim for many years, I was really worried. Would Disneyland live up to the way I had grown to love Disney World?Simple answer. Yes. I consider myself a commando when it comes to Disney (e.g., getting there super early, planning itineraries, working fastpasses to perfection, etc.) But it never ceases to amaze me how, while I'm focused on making sure my family is having the greatest day ever at my own expense if necessary, Disney is able to take you away and really let you enjoy being alive for a while.People smile. People are helpful. Guests seem more courteous. Everything just seems a little brighter. Walk into Toontown and look at those buildings...if it doesn't put a smile on your face, you've got issues. Vacations can be more work than going to work. Get on Small World and then tell me that.Disney is different. My children love it. My wife loves it. If I'd never been there, that would be enough. But I love it, too. And why not.....it's the Magic of Disney.

I had the best time in Disneyland this month. I went with my partner and a friend. We are all 25The most amazing thing about this place is you can tell all they think about is the experience of the guest. They will never put you on a ride next to someone you dont know and they always seat families together on rides. The whole day you could really tell people cared about you having a great time. We even got badges that said 1st visit and many people had ones that said just married or just engaged or things like that its the most amazing place!The best tips I can give you are definitely take advantage of fast passes. The most popular rides let you go up and get a ticket and it tells you to come back within a time frame. Say you go at 10am it may tell you to come back between 11.30 and 12.30. It basically lets you to the front of the line when you come back. Rides such as space mountain have long lines nomally 40minutes! When you compare that to the 5 10min wait you will have with a fast pass there isnt any reason not to do it. Then you can ride the rides without fast passes before you come back. You can get one fast pass per hour basically.We bought a 5 day pass because it was the same price of a 3 day at the time of booking. We got a magic morning included which means we got to go in an hour before the general public. Well worth it!!! Go straight to the rides like Nemo Submarine and Peter Pan(great for kids!) or any of the others that dont have fast passes which attract lines quickly. Food isnt ridiculously expensive inside I was surprised. A hot dog is about $5 a turkey sandwhich is about $8 ish I think. Also Check your maps for the mickey hand in a red box. It shows you where to find they disney characters. Usually in main street between 9 and 5. California park   go to the Toy Story ride FIRST THING!!! There is no fast pass and the line is ALWAYS 40 minutes at least. We went at 10am and we went in 3 times in a row and didnt wait more than 5 minutes. But the rest of the day there was super long lines. Do not miss the Disney Animation in the Hollywood Backlot. Itson the right on the way down the street towards Aladdin (also very worth seeing!!!) There is an animation class and it teaches you how to draw the characters faces it was really cool. Also the show with the turtle is awesome for kidsI could go on and on and on about it but its really best to explore but remember the sunscreen!! And there are plenty of water fountains around so bring your own bottle. One thing for parents   if you dont need a stroller leave it at home. There are hundreds and hundreds of strollers competing for space with walking people. It looked like a lot of hassle for the parents who had them (most cant avoid bringing them because of the age of their kids ) but its something to think about. Have fun!!!

Finally broke down to bring our daughter, who is 4 1 2 , to Disneyland. We wanted to wait until she was old enough to really enjoy and remember things. I   m glad that we did because she had a great time and just watching her so happy made us happy. Even my husband who is not the biggest fan of Disney enjoyed seeing her face light up.I think some of our planning also helped make it an enjoyable trip. First, went during the week . In fact, the weather was very iffy that day and in the middle of the day when the temperatures dipped, you could definitely tell that folks were leaving. Also we chose one of the    slow    times between Spring Break and Memorial Day. Many rides had very short waits or no wait at all. Five minute wait for Pirates     unbelievable! We also bought our tickets through AAA and got some perks     free parking, etc. Also because we ended up buying a park hopper, we went to California Adventure, which I   m glad we did (separate review on that).We also let our little one call the shots. She was a trooper and never got cranky or tired. If she had, we would have left in a heartbeat, taken a rest and then returned later at night.Because of the short lines we were able to go on many rides multiple times. We made it to most of the really popular rides, but skipped the bigger ones like Space Mountain because we just weren   t sure if my daughter was ready for it. Got to the see the Celebrate parade     it was fine, nothing exciting, but if your kid is into all the characters then it   s a good opportunity to see all of them.We only ate one meal in the park and that was lunch. Ate at Caf   Orleans, as opposed to the more expensive Blue Bayou. Only had about a five minute wait. The food wasn   t the best I   ve ever had, but it   s certainly wasn   t the worst. Had the Monte Cristo sandwich, which of course contains what has to be a few thousand calories.I always laugh when I read how expensive people think Disneyland is. Every resort, theme park and tourist destination is expensive. Yes, the parking was $14, but go to any major city and try to park anywhere and $14 is a bargain. Food is expensive too so get over it. We brought bottled water and some snacks in with us so that we would only have to eat one main meal.All in all, we had a very good time. Lines were shorter than we thought, people were more polite than we thought and the park was in good shape, but it will be a few years before we return. If you   re not gung ho on Disney than once every few years is more than enough.

Really enjoyed our day here   kids are 8 and 13, so at the top end of the age bracket this park appeals to. We've been to Orlando and thought this park measured up pretty well. Space Mountain and Big Thunder Mountain Railroad are still favourites, but Pirates of the Caribbean was better than Orlando and Indiana Jones was really great fun   we rode 3 times on our first day then went back using our hopper pass on day 2 to go on again. I don't agree with the review criticising the food. In our experience in Orlando 6 years ago was poor in terms of healthiness and quality (fries nuggets burgers soda), but here we had turkey salad wholegrain sandwiches (no mayo) from the bakery on main street, and all had fruit from a stall near the Tiki Room (also one on Main Street) which sold a big, fresh variety   we had bananas, grapes, mango slices, pineapple and apple. Not perfect, but big strides made in this respect, plus water bottles can be refilled throughout the park.

Did Breakfast in the Park with the characters at 8:50am at the Plaza Inn  get there at least 30 minutes before. Crowds of people are gathered at the end of Main Street to be the first in the park. We learned that the hard way  the reservationist through Disney Dine's 1 800 number told us to get there 10 minutes early. It was easy for my 5 year old son and I to walk through the crowds waiting to get in  however, we left my poor husband and 2 year old daughter in the dust because he couldn't maneuver through the crowds with our Maclaren Volo stroller. Note to self: get to Breakfast in the Park (Plaza Inn) 30 minutes before actual reservation. They have photo takers to take your picture right at the Plaza Inn entrance behind a sign that reads,  Breakfast in the Park with Minnie & Friends,  which is about $32. I cringed at the price but then I was glad we did it because it was the only picture we had as a family at Disneyland. Breakfast was not a self serve buffet  the people serve you, which was not a big deal since you just tell them what you want. We also opted for the $15 pirate treasure chest for my son's 5 year old birthday, which was a little chocolate cake. Pretty good cake, but save your money as he only ate two bites because of all the buffet food. Awesome cinnamon french toast, good bacon & eggs. All the characters came to each table  no one was left out. Each child also gets a balloon, which I ended up tying to my stroller (making it very easy to pick out in the throngs of strollers!!!). With a full belly we did not need any snacks  just shared a bottle of water. We also decided to pack light  only diapers & wipes in the stroller. I saw a ton of people carting around their big backpacks  they looked like they were going to hike the Matterhorn! The best entertainment was watching these backpack people trying the fit their packs with them on the rides  too squishy for me. With only diapers & wipes in my stroller I did not worry about anything being stolen from my stroller. My husband wore cargo shorts and put his wallet, camera, sanitizer, and chapstick in the pockets  much simpler than a cumbersome backpack. After a few rides  only about5 10 minute lines as we went on a Monday in between CA and AZ spring breaks. We had reservations at the Blue Bayou (again, 1 800 DINE), great Monte Christo sandwich, excellent salmon, great kid's mac & cheese, which my son gobbled up. After that we went back to our hotel for a little two hour nap and then back to the park for a late dinner (cafefteria style in Fantasyland) and ice cream while watching the fireworks. My husband and I decided that the only thing we would change when we go back for my daughter's 5th birthday is to get to the park 30 minutes prior to our reservation. Traveling light was THE BEST!!! Eating sit down meals in the restaurants for two meals warded off the little snacks that can nickel & dime you till you are broke.

Visited a few parks in So Cal over the past years and hands down D.L. is the best. From the cleanliness to the attention to detail, even the way they load the rides, all top notch. Well done Disney we had a great time. The best fireworks choreography I have ever seen.

Disneyland is a must for any family. It was built by Walt Disney for families to come and enjoy. We are Australain and have been 3 times and plan to go back in 2013 when the work is complete in California Adventureland. We saved like crazy and this time on a budget had the most amazing 8 days again over Christmas. We stayed off site at the Howard Johnson (we previously stayed at the Grand California). If money is not an issue, stay at the Grand on the concierge level and you will have the time of your life. Magical especially for little ones and the closest of all the hotels. Food and drink are available at most times of the day, with a concierge to help you learn your way around. If you cannot afford this, don't let it put you off, just opt to stay somewhere like the Ho Jo. We saved probably $4500AUS  night and got to see another side of Disney but just as lovely because we made use of dining at different places. We had breakfast at Mimis each day (coupons online). Dinner venues varied from Mimis to Millies(vouchers online too) which were near Ho Jo and lovely no complaints, huge servings, fast service etc. .Also dined at McCormick and Scmicks at happy hour(bar) with best food ever at unbelievable prices if ordered at bar with a drink. We went back to the Grand California on our wedding anniversary as had booking at Napa Rose but our booking had been overlooked and although dressed up and eager to at long last try this restaurant out, we forewent the opportunity after waiting 20minutes (and handed a menu with a 4 course menu and no children's menus at $80 person). It was unfortunate but we went to the beautiful bar in the Grand and had cocktails and the kids had tinkerbell pink lemonade and we ordered small appetisers which came to our table and it was sufficient and the atmosphere lovely. American meals are huge and appetisers were enough for us. Some venues within Disney which we ate at were the Bengal Bar B Q opposite Jungle ride in Adventure land, Garlic fries in outside Restaurant at right of Pirates of Carribean, Soup in roll listening to Billy Hill and Hillbillies show in saloon at Frontierland (brilliant) and hamburgers at hamburger place next door to Soarin over California in Cal. Adventureland. Amazing treats were had at the Pineapple Whip stand outside the Tiki Room in Adventureland and the Tiggertail or cashew pretzel in chocolate shop just near photo place of splash mountain.But to the Parks which are the drawing cards. Go on the train first to get your bearings. Download the activity sheet for the actual day before you go and list the shows etc. Don't miss Fantazmic, the nightly fireworks, the parade, Billy hill and the Hillbillies and Aladdin (CAP). We initially paced ourselves with a land a day and enjoyed everything but the kids (8,11,13 on first trip) had been told about Space Mountain, Splash Mountain, Thunder Mountain, Indianna Jones and Buss Lightyear. I suggest you find these on the map and use your entrance pass to Fast pass them, ie. get to one of these attractions, you put your entrance card into the Fast Pass machine and another card pops out like a parking ticket and tells you what time you can come back for this ride. That way you do not have to queue. You can get another Fast Pass on the time at the bottom of this ticket, so if you plan it well you can get about 4 5 fast passes in a day and this is great for these rides which the kids love to go on everyday we were there. Photos are also wonderful to get done professionally and then at the end of your trip just purchase the entire CD to bring home. We are not early risers so the magic morning did not entice us but we did stay till late most nights and after the fireworks you can get on many of the Fantasyland rides like Peter Pan quite quickly especially if you watch the fireworks from in there. If you are tired there is a lovely spot to sit away from the crowds a little and that is to the left in front of the castle where bands play. There are toilets there too.Enter the spirit of Disney. Buy the kids a Disney hat at the Mad Hatter store near Alices teacup ride and buy them a lanyard and a starter pack of pins and let them trade with cast members. It is where they can spend their pocket money and come home with a couple of small souveniers which they will treasure. Our kids traded for their particular favourite character and they still treasure them. They started with 4 and now have 12 each! We have had some of our most wonderful family times here so enjoy the experience, savour the amazing way Disney has developed this park from intricate features as you wait in line to the parades, the music, Tinkerbelle flying through the air before the fireworks and then the snow falling after. Just so special with memories talked about for years after.

I was upset that not one person all day asked my daughter who was seven about her volunteering experience. She was wearing the button proudly, but after awhile she wanted to take it off because she said not one person asked her about it. I asked her to keep it on to show the other people that she was a volunteer. I was very disappointed in Disneyland, I expected more.

This park has a few attractions that are unique, but much of them can be found in Orlando and Orlando has much more. Sleeping Beauty's castle walk thru was nice. Tinkerbell's meet and greet was horrible. The wait was insane to spend seconds with 2  fairies . Toontown was very cute. The Nemo sub ride had an insane wait, no passes, and the ride was kind of lame. Small World is huge there and beautiful on the outside. Don't leave your camera in a pouch on ride, you'll never see it again.

It was our first time at Disneyland and we were not disappointed. The rides and attention to detail are better then imagined. The lines were long and it was busy. It take patience to spend multiple days at Disneyland, but that is to be expected. Do Magic mornings atleast once and it's an easy way to ride ateast 4 rides quickly before the general public gets in. See the parades atleast once..... they are FABULOLUS!!! They make anyone in a good mood. It's so fun. We did a character lunch that way we didn't have to wait in long lines for autographs. Best money I ever spent. Mickeytown is fun for kids 8 and under and the lines seem to go by quickly. Teacups and Carousel is fun to do with no hassle. Bibbi Bobbiddi Boutique (sp) is the BEST for young children. My daughter LOVED being made over by the fairy god mothers and it's quick and painless. The big rides and water rides are exactly what you expect. You could go for a week and never see everything. Get park hopper tickets and plan what rides you can't miss in advance. We had a great time and look forward to going back in the future. Perhaps an Easter tradition.

Went to Disneyland with the kids at Easter time and it was so crowded you couldn't see 2 feet in front of you. The wait to get any food in the park was as long as half an hour at the little snack stands and several hours at any of the sit down restaurants. The lines at the attractions were generally 75 minutes or so, and even when we got fast passes first thing in the morning, we couldn't do the ride til 9:30 at night. Some of the rides, like space mountain, were completely out of fast passes. We waited in line for HOURS and then when we finally got on the ride, it was...nothing. A roller coaster in complete darkness. Long lines at the Matterhorn for a sad little roller coaster with really hard seats that trundled past a shopworn  abominable snowman  and some plastic  ice crystals . Totally out of date and crummy. At California Adventure, we thought we'd get to ride the big roller coaster, but it was shut down for the day, no refunds. Same with the big ferris wheel. Not much else to do there for kids older than 9 except for the Tower of Terror (truly terrifying, a good ride if you like that kind of thing) and the Drop Zone ride, same thing as Tower of Terror only outdoors. On teh other hadn, Universal Studios was not crowded, fun, hip, and completely entertaining, with great shows, amazing stunts and fun rides.

Don   t waste your time or money at Disneyland. Both parks are over crowed and small compared to Disneyworld. Cinderella   s castle looks like the size of a doghouse compared to the one in Florida. Airfare, $250 and hotel costs, $100 is about the same for LA or Orlando. You may pay $50 more for a Disneyworld park hopper pass but your park options, less congestion and larger parks is well worth the trip to Orlando. Disneyland has held up well but is showing signs of its age and is not designed for today   s volume of people since it was built in 1955.

The food inside the park was such a disappointment. Fried, gross, only two choices for salad dressings. All the places are cafeteria style, no relaxation, we tried a different place every day for four days and never found one single place we would go back to. If you like county fair food for your whole trip you won't be disappointed.

We went to Disneyland for 5 days from December 29th to January 2nd, and it was sooo crowded. We went to see the park all decorated for the holidays, and that was really nice but it was so crowded. There were times when it was almost impossible to get around people, especially around New Orleans Square.We have been there during spring break before, summer, and this was by far the most crowded I have ever seen it. I guess not only are people there for New Year's eve, but there is also the whole crowd from the Rose Bowl going there.The last day (January 2nd) was definitely the worst because it wasn't a black out date for season ticket holders so attendance was wall to wall people.

Disney still has it.  All workers friendly helpful.  Park was spotless!!  It was crowed but the  Fast Pass   worked very well, look for the signs, swipe your ticket and you come back within a certain hour.. Saved a lot of time.

Visited Disneyland and California Adventure with kids over Spring Break.Arrived at 9am (park opens at 8am) on a Tuesday. Place was packed by 11am. Weather was perfect and had a really good time. Was at California Adventure the day previous and did not have a real fun experience. 3rd visit to Disneyland over the last 10 years, so understand where all the park layout, and made good use of the Fast Pass system.. Really enjoyed, Space Mountain, Splash Mountain, Indiana Jones, Thunder Mountain Railroad, Haunted Mansion, Pirates of the Carribean, and kids really liked Autotopia (3x). Never waited longer than 10minutes (Fast Pass really helped). Heard lots of complaining about long lines at Splash Mountain and Space Mountain.Lines were great until 10:30am, also during the afternoon parade, and after 5:30pm. Left the park at 6:15pm. Parking is insane at $14.00 day. I was tempted to park at one of the adjacent hotels close, but noticed all the cars, had a pass in the window, and did not want to return and find my car towed. Next time will ask if can park for $10.00, the hotel parking area was pretty empty. Can take food in the park. Bags are checked on entry, but failry relaxed about food and drink.

March, 2010My friend and I just returned from three days at Disneyland California Adventure, and I wanted to share some thoughts and suggestions as you look at your vacation options.We had a great time, but I can see where a Disneyland vacation is not for everyone. Even during an    off season    visit (mid March, Thursday     Saturday), you still have to deal with crowds. It is mass market experience. If you   re ideal vacation is quiet relaxation, exquisite service, and gorgeous scenery, then this may not be the trip for you.The first thing to consider is do you actually like Disney stories and rides? You   ll be immersed for a couple of days in everything Disney, so if you don   t actually like the Disney    product,    then this is not a choice for you. Understanding that a lot of people move through Disneyland each day, if you come prepared then you will have a lot better time. We picked up the latest copy of the    Unofficial Guide to Disneyland,    which has    Touring Plans    included. These will show which attractions to see in which order, to minimize the time waiting in line. If you want to avoid the worst of the crowds, and do many of the rides, then you must follow the Guide   s advice, and arrive at least    hour before park opening. This will mean a relatively early start each day, which some people really don   t want to do on their vacation. Also recommended is that you take advantage of the    Magic Hour,    if your ticket allows you to, and you are there on a day when this occurs. The    Magic Hour    is a time when selected ticket holders (3 Day Park Hoppers for instance) can enter the park one hour prior to the rest of the visitors. This is the time to do some of the more popular rides. This means an even early start to your day.A trip to Disneyland involves a lot of walking (usually three to six miles), and exposure to the weather. You can always take breaks, and the restaurants and rides are generally air conditioned, but during the summer the heat of southern California can take it   s toll. Even during mild weather, walking three to six miles on hard surfaces can be arduous.Costs     A Disney vacation is not cheap. You can save money by staying in a hotel off of the property, and by limiting the number of meals which you eat in the parks, but still be prepared to make an investment in the experience. For instance, lunch in a sit down restaurant for two adults (no alcohol) cost us $58 (Caf   Orleans). Before suggesting Disneyland as a destination to your family, you might want to do some research on what the costs will be.Currently, there is a special running on a 3 Day Park Hopper pass. This allows entrance to both Disneyland and Disney   s California Adventure. In order to fully enjoy both parks, I would recommend three days; two days in Disneyland and one day in California Adventure. You could    do    Disneyland in one day, but it would be a very rushed and exhausting day. Going to Disneyland can be a fun experience, if you prepare in advance. Definitely getting the    Unofficial Guide    will help you to understand how to avoid the worst of the crowds, and give you ideas to make for a much more enjoyable trip.
I cannot express how much I love this place.  I have so much fun on the rides, watching the parades, some of the great food, there really is something here for everyone of every age.

We once again visited Disneyland last week during spring break. With the help of the unofficial guide book we got there twice before it opened. On the first day we rushed to the Nemo submarines and were the first ones on (other guests were heading for Space Mountain) which means this is the best time to do the ride. On almost every day I got a chance to do Big Thunder Mountain or Space Mountain with very short waits. I did not go on the wet rides or rides with scary effects (such as Splash Mountain, Indiana Jones or anything similar). We did the early entry on Thursday and got in at 8:00 AM. The only rides that were closed were all the Rivers of America transports.At Disney's California Adventure there were narrow routes to all the rides because of construction for new rides. Every time we would try and do Toy Story Mania, there was almost always a 40 45 minute wait and we just had to wait. Try doing this ride at park opening.

When my fiance and I decided on a trip to Disneyland it was because I had never been and he couldn't believe it! We went in February 2009 for a week arriving just before the President's day weekend. Since it was a long weekend, we were lucky enough to see the fireworks show that had been limited that year to save money. Disneyland was everything I imagined as a child and just as exciting as an adult! We used the Unofficial Guide to Disneyland and followed their itinerary. These people know what they are talking about! We maximized our time in the park and minimized our time in line! I loved the rides especially Indiana Jones, Find Nemo and Peter Pan's Flight, but the lines are notoriously long for these rides, this of course, is the downside of Disney. I brought a small purse   we don't have any children to worry about   and in it I had my credit card, some money, my Disney pass, camera and some lip chap. That was all we needed and it wasn't bulky or annoying to hang on to. I recommend comfortable shoes, you will be one your feet all day. If you have time, definitely check out Fantasmic and the Fireworks. Conversely it's a great time to ride rides because a majority of the park is watching the shows. It really is fun for all ages.

This is a place for the little set as there's just not much for teens. The teens in our party took off for Knott's Berry Farm while we did Disney with the 6 & 7 year olds. Be for warned that a lot of the rides are cars going into dark places with super loud music and lit up characters. My high functioning autistic son couldn't take this. The simple rides around mainstreet were the answer for stress relief...horse pulled trolley, old fire truck and double decker bus. Super yummy corn dog vendor just off mainsreet.

This was my first time here and can't belive how much fun we had. I have been to LA a few times but this week we some time for fun and we went to Disneyland. My husband and I meet Mickey, how cool is that! I felt like a kid again.

We visited Disney from 2 15 through 2 17 and had a great time. This was our first visit to Disneyland (or Disneyworld for that matter). What made the trip most enjoyable for our family of 7 was a small $15 investment in a program called  RideMax .The biggest trouble our family of 7 encounters, with kids between 5 and 15, is that we show up someplace, look at each other, and say  ok   what do we want to do? . RideMax mapped out a schedule for us, taking full advantage of the Disney  fast pass  system. We never had more than a 5 10 minute wait the whole day, even for the most popular ride.My only wish is that the RideMax software would integrate both Disney and California Adventure into the same schedule. Even though the program doesn't do it automatically, there are some tips on the RideMax website for how to do it manually.I also liked the  tips and tricks  section of the software, as well as the  ratings  of the attractions at Disney and California Adventure. It was nice being able to sort the attractions by their rating, and then focus on those attractions first.Some of the tips   such as which lines to use   also dramatically cut down on our time.Considering that bottled water at Disney is $3, and a  cheap  lunch for our 7 was $80 each day, the $15 we spent on a 90 day RideMax license was the best money we spent.As far as Disney itself, we really liked Space Mountain and the Big Mountain Thunder Roller Coaster. Our favorites at California Adventure were the Toy Story Mid Way, Hollywood Tower of Terror, and the Soaring over California ride.

Disneyland used to be the  happiest place on earth'. That was when it was all about the guests. Now cast members are short, sometimes downright rude to guests and not at all knowledgable about their jobs. It would be nice also if there were a couple of days a year that Disneyland would only be open for adults, so that there aren't a hoard of strollers everywhere. Be aware that if you want to eat at places like the Blue Bayou, you had better make a reservation there before you go. We went and had no idea about this new development, and the hostess at the Blue Bayou acted like we should have been psychic. Disneyland has also been lax about making sure that their most popular rides and up and running during peak season. One summer it was the Monorail that was down, the next summer it was the Monorail and the Haunted Mansion.

Decided to surprise the kids, 2 and 4 year old, and go to Disneyland for Christmas.Wait time for average rides was 40 minutes, average wait time for popular rides was 90  minutes. You could barely move in the park. Wife and I were extremely frustrated and disappointed. On the pro side, they do make an effort to provide healthy food. Plenty of options for fresh fruits and vegetables at the park, which was a very nice surprise.Bottom line, if you are the type person that likes the Disney experience try to go during the low season, otherwise your enjoyment will be diluted.
Loved every minute of it allow at least 3 days in Disney and and 2 days in California.  Fantastic

We had a wonderful time at Disneyland. Our kids are 4 yrs & 16mths and both had fun. We went in early and had breakfast at Carnation Cafe on Main Street USA. Breakfast turned out great! We visited Disneyland Anaheim for 3 days from December 31st, 2009. The best piece of advice I can give you is to PLAN your trip in advance. We read lots of reviews and forums on trip adviser and about.com (go.california.about.com) it made our time at Disneyland flow beautifully. Following the advice from submitters, firstly we purchased the RIDEMAX program and then we set about constructing 3 scenarios for each day at half hour intervals between them. This allowed for holds up on entry or ride malfunctions throughout the day etc. We also purchased the Hopper Park 3 day ticket online whilst still in Australia. This was very easy to do and it saved a lot of time on the first day at the turnstiles as we entered the park. Our first day happened to be a Magic Morning day, so with ease we handed over our home printed ticket and within a minute, it was exchanged for a Disneyland ticket and we were on our way.Our first port of call was to the lockers where we placed our backpacks containing snacks and jumpers for the night. The lockers cost $7.00. I would advice taking $5 and 2 X $1 notes with you for this. $1 coins are not accepted and many people found that their credit cards would not work. We headed firstly to Finding Nemo and we were being submerged less than 10 minutes later. We then next headed to the Pirates of Caribbean and found a short line here too. By the time our RIDEMAX schedule was due to start, coinciding with the park officially opening, we had done several of the notorious big line queue rides.We followed our RIDEMAX schedule exactly and despite being at the park on one of the busiest days of the year, we did not wait for more than 10 minutes on any ride! By lunch time, we were very savvy with the whole FASTPASS system and could negotiate our way around the park with ease. This was great for us as by 1.30pm, the park had shut the main gates as it was filled to capacity. Yes, there were 65,000  people and it was busy, but we thoroughly enjoyed ourselves and would not complain about the number of people there. After all, it was New Year   s Eve and we felt the crowd added to the atmosphere.Once again, following the advice from trip advisers, we had phoned Disney Dining and had book our evening meal. We did this from Australia and it was well worth the international call as we were guaranteed a table and despite the crowd, we were seated on time. We ate at Caf   Orleans and thoroughly enjoyed our meal.Yes, New Year   s Eve was a busy, crowded day but our RIDEMAX schedule made the day flow perfectly. After the fireworks at midnight, the crowd rapidly depleted and although it was a little cool, we rugged up with jumpers and coats from our lockers and we revisited all of our favourite rides again until to 2am with little or no queue lines!New Year   s Day was far better crowd wise as considerable fewer people visited. On this day we popped over to California Adventure Park. This Park is quite small and my only advice is to avoid the Grizzly River Run if you don   t like getting saturated!On January 2nd, Disneyland seemed to be only half filled with people and I think this had a direct bearing on the number of characters out and about. They were everywhere and we thoroughly enjoyed our photographs and cuddles with them all!I would not criticize the cost of entry as each and every day we were there from opening time to the closing time. For roughly $65 a day, we rode ride after ride, we were entertained with fantastic shows and fireworks. Not to mention also that the park was still decorated with a Christmas theme which was just beautiful. It even    snowed    on us several times! We did not find it necessary to take bottled water as throughout the park we found numerous drinking fountains.We thoroughly enjoyed our three days at Disneyland and seriously had tears in our eyes as we sadly bid farewell to the happiest place on earth! Thank you Walt Disney. X.

Disneyland California is a fantastic dream where perfection is continually perfected   almost. Whether you are 6 or 66, you can't help but love Disneyland California! We went with our 8 year old son just before Christmas 2009 and had a fantastic time. If you only need to remember ONE THING, it is FASTPASS: figure out how it works (below) and use it, always. OK, another suggestion: buy  The Unofficial Guide to Disneyland .Back to my impressions:Pro's1. The Rides: Many of them are amazing. BEST: Thunder Mountain (we rode it a dozen times), Pirates of the Caribbean, the Haunted Mansion (with a Christmas theme!), Splash Mountain (soaking wet), Autopia, Buzz Lightyear, Star Tours, the Matterhorn Bobsleds, Indiana Jones, Jedi Academy (awesome for Star Wars fans like our son). GOOD: It's a Small World, Jungle Cruise, Honey I Shrunk the Audience, Tom Sawyer's Island. FORGETTABLE: Space Mountain (freaky, too thrilling!), Nemo Submarines (complete waste of time). Disney takes everything to the extreme of perfection in the rides. Can you believe that the Indiana Jones ride cost $250 million to design and install? Compare this to Legoland (see my separate review   don't waste any time there!).2. Fastpass: If you go to Disneyland and don't use Fastpass, you are wasting your time! It is free! Many high traffic rides use this system that cuts down wait times to nothing. It works as follows. You go to the really high traffic rides (the best ones) and get a Fastpass, then you go to another high traffic ride and use the normal line (short early in the day), or just do something else. Once you finish that, you come back to the ride where you got the Fastpass and hop to the very front of the line. If you are good, you get another Fastpass just before that. In this way, we did all the rides we wanted to over 4 HALF days and NEVER waited in line   we glided to the front of line ups that were sometimes 2 hours long, shaking our heads at how people can sit in line for 2 hours when the FREE Fastpass system is staring them in the face??!!3. The Cleanliness: I swear they hire engineers to figure out exactly where to place trash bins, how to keep things perfect and tidy. Took 1 hr from the freeway exit to the parking garage. Signs to the garage are poor. Verbal directions from Disneyland were difficult to follow   and we had a GPS! Seems to be set up best for people to stay in Disney resort hotels. Bring water bottles that can be filled at infrequently placed water fountains. Bring healthy snacks or pay $2 for an apple.Indiana Jones and Space Mountain  broke  so we never got to go on them. We waited 85 min for Nemo's submarine. Use the FastPass system.  Cast members  weren't friendly. Long, long lines to purchase food. DIsney characters were few and far between  only saw the evil queen in snow white in 12 hours (but she snarled perfectly) Parade a blast!

The 3 main issues regarding Disneyland have always been:1) Its too busy the waits are too long 2) Its looking a little shabby 3) Its overpricedHaving been to Disney Anaheim 3 times in the past 20 years I can tell you that as at September 2009 you can strike off number 2 above   it was looking refreshed and fun, smiles and fresh paint all round.OK but yes, in the high season and on weekends, you will wait ages for the good rides and generally feel the crush even just walking around. Plan your trip during the Californian school term, and make the most of early openings   we had 3 or 4 rides under our belts on each of Splash Mountain and Thunder Mountain railroad when others were still eating breakfast. That frees you to pace yourself for the rest of the day   especially if you have smaller kids. Dragging toddlers round at a fast pace in the LA heat will put your mood (and holiday) in critical condition. Plan what you want to see and become familiar with the maps   if you' do have kids, take 3 days and just chill. Nothing wrong with a dip in your hotel pool mid afternoon and returning again later, somewhat energised. A G&T or soothing Vodka could also help here.Lastly, cost. Yes, its expensive   $184 for an online advance purchase, 3 day park hopper. So if you're visiting from overseas or interstate, take a breath, shell out the wad of cash, and take another deep breath   then just enjoy yourself. Bringing your own water and snacks, and avoiding the crappy souveniers will keep the costs down somewhat.Then just have fun.

We had visited Disneyland 12 years ago and had an absolute ball it was just fantastic   coming back a second time I was a bit weary it would not live up to the expectations. We visited Disneyland resort for 3 days in October 2009. We did 3 day park hopper passes, which for us was just the right amount of time. My wife, I, and our 9 and 3 year old daughters (actually almost 10 and almost 4) were here for the first time, and were completely satisfied with this trip. It's been about a month since we've been back, so some of this review will focus on reflection from the kids now that we are home.First of all, we had absolutely perfect weather during our stay. It was around 70 and overcast each day, so that allowed us to push harder walking around than we would have been able to do in the summer if it was 95   or so. Had it been hot, we certainly would not have had as good of a time and would have worn out much more quickly. As it was, I wore a pedometer and was clicking off on the order of 20,000 to 25,000 steps a day. That is a lot for me! We were very tired after each day for sure.Some tips for the park:* I highly recommend the  Unofficial Guide to Disneyland  book, and read it thoroughly before going. In fact, having both parents read it is even better to make sure you are up on everything you need to know for this place. This book has suggested plans for the order to do the rides, and they worked out very well for us (we rarely had to wait more than 15 minutes for anything, even the popular rides).* If you can, stay within walking distance of the park so you can avoid having to drive in, and this allows timing your arrival more closely (get there early so you are near the front of the admittance lines). We tried to arrive at the admission gates around 20 30 minutes before opening.* You get a magic morning pass if you purchase the multi day park hopper passes, which allows you to arrive an hour before the general public passes. This was awesome, and allowed us to get on the most popular rides right away and avoided lines. I believe the Disney hotels allow magic mornings each day, but those hotels are also quite expensive. We stayed at the Camelot and highly recommend it, especially the family suites. Very short walk to the park.* Get acquainted with the fastpass system and use it liberally. This is fantastic, and allows 10 20 minutes lines instead of hour  lines.* You can bring in food, water and snacks in your backpack. They do a security check before you enter the park, but no one ever complained that we brought in food. The security check itself is a joke though, as they seem to just be profiling since they really didn't look hard inside our bags.* We made a point to arrive early, go for a few hours, then come back to the hotel midday for a rest, then go back later in the day for more. This avoided the busiest mid day crowds and allowed for some rest mid day.* We did use a stroller for our almost 4 year old and are glad we did. Otherwise she would have worn out much faster. They charged $15 a day for their strollers if I remember correctly, but they were very nice ones.* Make sure you verify the opening times for Disneyland and DCA, since they are not the same for both parks each day, and they can vary by day of the week as well.* Favorite rides is subjective, but we really enjoyed the Big Thunder Mountain railroad (a smaller scale roller coaster), and the Indiana Jones adventure ride. Those were our families favorites. The only one I was disappointed with was Nemo. Just not my thing (longest wait we had, and the loading for it was quite inefficient).* Admission prices are expensive (our hotel did have discount multi pass tickets though), food is expensive, the gift shops are expensive, everything is expensive. Just get used to the fact that you will be spending a lot of money here. That said, we would do it again since the smiles per dollar factor was quite high for my daughters, so it was worth it. * I highly recommend having your kids get familiar with the Disney movies if they aren't already, even the older ones. This helps the fun factor if they are familiar with all of the characters. * Plan, plan, plan! Figure out what rides you want to do beforehand. Checkout videos of the rides on youtube to get a flavor of them. Again, the Unofficial Guide to Disneyland was very helpful.Both daughters, and especially our 3 year old, keep saying  when can we go back to Disneyland , so they were both very happy with this trip. We did these 3 days as part of a larger trip to LA, and this was one of the funnest trips we've taken as a family so far.I can't comment on how things have changed here over the years since this was out first trip here, but as the park stands in October 2009, we were very pleased with how happy our daughters were. So for that, I give 5 stars!Check out some of my pictures to get a flavor of the place. If you do visit Disneyland, I hope you have a great time! Thanks for reading.

Here are my tips and guidelines for those who are interested in going to Disneyland:1) If possible, go there during weekend. Its just for the fireworks. Its because fireworks is a confirmed event during weekend but not a  must  during weekday. Of course, the drawback is you need to have a longer queue during weekend since the crowd will be more compared to weekday.2) Arrive there early in the morning. This is to prevent the long queue for all the ride.3) Once you enter the entrance, you will seeing a lot of scene mascot that will attract you. My advice is dont stop and take the picture first. Instead, go directly to MIckey's ToonTown as they will be long queue at the later time (especially photo with Mickey). 4) For camera ppl, its better that you DONT bring your tripod. Ask other ppl helping you take the pic instead. Its because there are so many visitors and its very hard for you to set your tripod and take the pic freely. Of course, if you not mind bringing the tripod ard, you can bring it as well
Just returned from a trip to Disneyland today.  The Haunted Mansion is decorated for the holidays in a Nightmare Before Christmas Theme.  It is a must see!

This truely is the happiest place on earth. It is clean and fun and everyone is so friendly and helpful. All the events, shows and parades are incredibly well organised. The only problem with Disneyland Resort is that it puts the other theme parks in the area to shame.

My husband and I have been to Disneyland many times, and it is a wonderful experience every time. This year Disney is having a  Year of Celebrations  theme. On the lamp posts that line Mainstreet USA are birthday hats hanging upside down and filled with flowers. Also on Mainstreet there is an enourmous birthday invitation and Mickey Mouse shaped ballons. Every Disneyland parade we have seen at Disneyland has been wonderful. They are always full of entertainment and energy by the Disney characters and all of the entertainment crew. If you are wanting to get a picture with the Disney characters, I would recommend you be at Tunetown when the gates open. The last time we were there, Tunetown opened an hour after the park opened. It is located next to  It's a Small World . In Tunetown you can visit Mickey's house and Minney's house. They are both in their own houses posing for pictures with you. You will also find Pluto and Goofy posing for pictures with guests. Tiger and Pooh pose for pictures in another area of the park. It is a lot of fun for children to purchase autograph books and then try to acquire an autograph from each Disney character they see in Disneyland. The entire Disneyland staff is so friendly! A day at Disneyland is always a wonderful day!

I went to Disneyland in 2003, 04, and 05 after a gap of like 15 years. Then EuroDisney in 2007. This visit was in OCT of 2009. Much of the ambiance was gone as the moat was drained around the castle and the entire pool was drained in California Adventures while they are working there. The trains were closed as well, which was sad. The parades in both parks were the lamest in years. The fireworks were all halloween and used mostly left over effects from the great show of 2005. Very skipable.The parks have been maintained to the high standards of 2005. Our visit in 2003 was marked by overflowing trashcans and the like. The staff was doing good things and made the visit pleasant.Some rides were closed for the off season maintenance. The new Nemo ride was open and I was very dissapointed given the number of years that area sat vacant. If you are over 10 it isn't worth the line. They should have left the 20,000 League ride alone. The new Toy Story ride in CA was great however. Sadly there is no fast pass for that ride and lines get long, but it is worth it.Another complaint is the total waste of time security check prior to entering the park entrance area. These checks create lines and congestion and my 10 year old daughter can check a bag better than the people working there. This is just a  check the block  station to free the park from liability. Do the checks right or stop wasting our time.It is still Disneyland but it isn't scheduled to shake off the construction and be totally ready until 2011. For the kind of serious money this place demands I had high higher expectations.

They were great with helping my son who has autism. We were able to get a special pass to go to the quick pass line so we didn't have to wait in those long lines and crowds of people.

Loved d land and had a wonderful time w  our daughter for her 10th birthday. Staff was amazingly nice, courteous and so very helpful. They even made suggestions that would save us $$. It was our first visit and we got lost a few times, and had a blast! Truly a Wonderful place to visit for ALL! : )

The resort has not changed much since my last review. Cast members were a little more animated this time. Of note:1) It was very crowded the weekend of October 16th. My wife and I honeymooned at Disneyland and had a lot of fun it is said to be a geat time for families with kids but also a lot of fun for just two!
My family loves going here.  There is fun for all ages and so many different things to do that you can go for several days and not be sick of it.

We've been here in the month of October before and there wasnt as many crowds, this time around it was so busy the lines for rides was crazy, trying to get out of frontier land in the evening was a joke, we left the park earlier than expected our first night there, on sunday we woke up early to get into the park an hour early but there was a chalk walk that we were not informed about it was not posted in the park either we got to the park at 7:30am and were told to come back until 10am but they might open up at 9am depending on the walkers

I went recently to Disneyland for the first time in my life and it was fantastic. The only negitive word about it is that it is too big and you need more that 2 days to see both disneyland and disney california park

my four year old loves coming here and he is tall enough for most of the rides now so we like to come at least once a year.

I love this magical place! I danced here with my competition group and never forgot the magic of the backstage lot. My favorite ride is Space Mountain. I just returned from Disneyland, and it was awesome! the rides were so fun and my daughters eyes twinkled with excitement! Our favorite rides were Pirates and Small World (classics!). It was magical to watch her face light up with all of the amazing things there. The food was pretty good (although pricey). The cast members were friendly. The park was clean. We loved Disneyland but the crowds of people were really hard to deal with on a Friday night as both fireworks and the laser show were held. I am still a little cynical about  The Happiest Place on Earth , but all in all Disneyland does have lots of interesting stuff to do for all ages. It wasn't just roller coasters and princesses as I had feared. And, yes, my kids had a blast!

Disneyland is a 9 out of 10. Magic Kingdom is still great. Californian adventure keeps getting better. 2010 World of color water fountains with fire and 8 HD projectors. The entire size of the lagoon and taller than the ferris wheel. I will be about 8 times the size of Fantasmic. 2012 Cars land with new rides. Look to go for these additions.

Disneyland is a great place to take very young children, even babies, but beware of the typical peak times (weekends, long holidays, summers). The best time to go is in October during the week when the park is relatively deserted compared to their busy season. Disneyland is extremely baby toddler friendly as amusement parts go. There is a baby feeding and changing center on Main Street next to Tomorrowland. They even have little kid sized toilets close to the ground for toddlers there. There are plenty of rides for the little ones, and surprisingly, even for babies (think Its a Small World, Jungle Cruise, Dumbo the Flying Elephant, Disneyland Train, Pooh's Adventure, etc). For nap time, there's a small park in Toon Town that is great for the little ones to sleep in their carts when the park is less crowded. Another quiet area is a big public space between the Castle and Adventureland, lots of tables and shade and never anybody there. Toddlers who are between 35 40  have even more ride options. Braver toddlers can ride the Toontown roller coaster and even the Matterhorn. Davey Crockett's island is always a lot of fun, the kids can run around an  undeveloped  island with winding trails, caves, and lots of things to explore. And after a long day with the kids, parents can unwind at any of the fine dining options at Downtown Disney, like Catal. Fine dining and young children? Yes, only at Disneyland.

I knew that there would be masses of people at Disneyland as there always are, but who knew so many would be there on a Sunday night. We had gone there just to ride two rides. The new ghostly Space Mountain and the Haunted Mansion. Both lines were incredibly long so I'll have to wait until I can make time during the weekday to go. Despite all the long lines and missing out on the reason for going we still had an awesome time as always. We rode Buzz Lightyear which is in my opinion the best ride at Disneyland, because what ride will give you a FREE picture of yourself and your score! I never pass up FREE at Disneyland. We hopped on the train to go around the parade crowd and headed toward Small World. When we got there the parade was just starting so we decided to just get on the ride. We waited about 10 seconds and we were on the boat. After that the crowds actually started to get larger so we headed home. Still a great trip and I can't wait to go back again.

We had fun after the we got used to the lines, but honestly they don't make it easy. There was very little explanation of what to do, where to go, how to get started. You have to line up to get past the bag check. Then you line up to get to the ticket window. Then the ticketing process is the LONGEST of any attraction I've EVER been to. What is up with that? Then you line up to get in to the park, and then you line up to take a picture, buy a drink, go on a ride.... and so on and so on. We were there at the end of September and supposedly the park wasn't that busy. I can't imagine being there when it was busy. You'd have to wait all day to get on one ride. The thing I disliked the most was the lack of explanation. If you didn't pick up a map at the beginning you wouldn't ever even find a bathroom. There were a slew of people walking around with 1st time badges. It was our 1st time, but we don't know where we were supposed to go to get the badges or whether they made any difference. We had to watch people walking by us in line to figure out that there was a thing called a  fast pass  and then I spent 15 minutes trying to find a fast pass machine with little or no guidance from the park attendant that I spoke to. Once you figure it out you realize that you probably should've saved it for Splash Mountain though... We knew that there would be a parade and that we should reserve a space early, but had no real understanding of the process. It turned out we picked one of the worst spots. We were right at the curb, but only a few meters away from the end of the first section. This meant that we could half see everything without actually being part of it, then when it did move down, we were right at the very end and barely got to see any characters. The fireworks were somewhat the same. Awesome, but I would've preferred if I didn't have to look through a tree to see the narrator (Halloween show). We were there in plenty of time to stand anywhere, but simply chose the wrong spot. Who knew? It seems to me that it's all designed to require you to come back to do it right. I don't know if I like that. We didn't have the opportunity to come back for the fireworks again. Oddly, I found California Adventure easier. Atleast there are plenty of signs to help you get around although still very little guidance about the best place to stand for performances and plenty of line ups (but much less busy than Disney land). Loved that California Screaming Roller Coaster!

Disneyland and California Adventures was an amazing decision for a family vacation. We stayed at a family members house on Balboa Island so we had a short drive the morning of Disneyland. We bought park hopper tickets which was a great decision. Fantasmic was an amazing show and definitely a must see! Soaring over California and Space Mountain were great rides. We will definitely go back next year!

Moderate crowds; more that expected. Prices have gone up 30% since we visited four years ago. Our favourite ride was closed. Why don't post this information on the web somewhere.Parked by downtown and had to walk the gauntlet of the downtown area before getting in. Will avoid next time. Came back on the monorail and missed most of it.Eat at the cafe orleans. had to wait about 45 minutes. Reservation system very inefficient. Many people taken to their table who arrived after us.Space Mountain and Haunted house have been updated since we were there last   much better.

Made a memorable trip to Disneyland with my daughter & mother in law. Ended up being a girls only trip and we had a great time. My daugher was 5, so big scary rides were out, but Dinner with the Princesses at Ariel's grotto was a hit! The close up interaction with the Princesses was the highlight of her trip!

Loved Disneyland. We ate at Goofy's Kitchen and that was one of the big highlights. My grandchildren loved the characters and the food was really good too. The rides at Disneyland are great for small children. We especially liked the teacups and it's a small world. The whole trip was a sucess. I think everyone should visit Disneyland at least once a year. It will keep you young.

Save $$$, by staying at a nearby hotel that is on the Anaheim Resort Trolley Route. Only $6 R T p.p. Drops you right at park! Also, for adults, the Segway tour of California Adventure (Disney's adjacent park,) A fun experience if you have more than one day to spend here!

Though Halloween can be scary for little ones, Disneyland has done their best to make it little one friendly! Near  It's a Small World,  they have a special area set up for you to visit  scary  Disney characters. This is a fun, but not frightening way, to get your little kiddos in the Halloween spirit!

cast members and guests alike were courteous and respectful. the fireworks show was appropriately modified for the seasonal holiday theme and lines are relatively short and manageable. we had toddlers that for the most part didn't ride anything beyond the capacity of mr toad's level of thrill though.
Always great to go to Disneyland.  We went in July.  Weather was beautiful.  Long lines, but worth the wait.  Would go every year.
Its the most beautiful place i have ever been.Really had lots of fun in the rides.

I love this place, once you go through disneyland doors, your fun begins. No matter how many times you have been there before it's always a different experience, employees are nice , rides are fun, except the ride lines but it's expected from any amusement park, you can always get a fast pass. I enjoy going with family and recomending it to friends there no need to travel too far if you live in the area since this resort has everything you need for a perfect vacation.

we didnt see as much disney characters as we would have like walking the streets of disneyland. unless you bring your own food and drinks or eat at the better restaurants, most of the burger places were awful and high priced..they were doing reconstruction on the main area of cali adventures so it was not worth the price of admission for this section.
We went on 9 28 09 and were satisfied with the place. It's in a great location, but the accommodations should be much classier for the price.

Disneyland continues to out perform any so called competitors in the amusement park field. There is a slight hiccup with the new Celebration parade right now due to crowd control being very uncontrolled. However, since it's a new parade being presented in an entirely new way, we'll give them a break to work the kinks out.Staff is always impeccable in their friendliness and warmth. After going into Woody's Roundup hoping to decorate pumpkin cookies (as in previous years of Halloween activities) we were disappointed to learn the cookies were no longer being provided. A very sweet cast member proceeded to give my son an awesome Davy Jones tattoo and my niece, who was less than interested in a tattoo, received an exclusive cast member release Tinkerbell pin!We also had our first interaction with first aid this visit. My son fell into the Dumbo ride and skinned his knee very badly on the no slip flooring that covers all the rides. The ride operator immediately attended to him and then we made a quick visit to the first aid office where he was cleaned, bandaged, and given an adorable Nurse Minnie sticker by the most personable nurse I've ever met. This saved the day, as a 3 year old with an injury can easily swing to the dramatics.As always, Disneyland goes above and beyond in accomodating every visitor to their parks and making sure that the visit goes past great and into magical territory!

We just love Disneyland! One way that we make our trip more enjoyable is to go on the Disney website and create our own map of the park. You can plot only the rides you want to ride and eliminate the ones you don't. Then you get a personalized map and list of your activities for the day. This has really helped us to get to all the rides our kids want to ride without having to look at the giant map provided by the park at the entrance booth.
