Make sure you leave enough time to enjoy all rides.

I decided to walk back rather than take the tram. It isn't as bad as it seems as long as the weather is nice and you can handle a small walk with a stroller. Took about 10 minutes which was shorter than the possible wait in line.

We had a fantastic trip to Disneyland! The weather was warm, the lines were short and everyone around us was having a great time. We took our first trip on the new Finding Nemo Submarine ride and visited our old favorites: Pirates of the Caribbean, Big Thunder Mountain, Peter Pan, Mr. Toad's Wild Ride, the Tree House and the Jungle Cruise. We saved our Small World for the heat of the afternoon. It was wonderful to ride through the magical lands in ultra air conditioned comfort! We made ourselves wait until dark to visit our number one favorite attraction: The Enchanted Tiki Room. It was even more mysterious and fun then ever.We always try to visit something new (to us) each visit. This time we went to the Penny Arcade. It was great fun! We watched hand cranked one cent movies, had our fortunes told by Esmerelda and enjoyed watching and listening to the band machine.We ate a delicious lunch at the River Belle Terrace. It was so good (for Disney food) that we went back for dinner. We also had some terrific skewers from the Bengal Bar B Que.

My family went to Disneyland in June before the local schools were out of session. That seemed to be the best time to go, because the parks were not crowded at all! We were able to get in line for a popular attraction ride and only have a 15 minute wait compared to a 60  minute wait.The weather was perfect. Shorts and tshirts with the slight chance of cooler weather in the evenings. Most of the week we didn't even need a jacket.I highly recommend going to Disneyland on a off peak time so you can really enjoy what the parks have to offer. We did!

Had a great trip to Disneyland this year! Stayed at the Annabella Hotel and enjoyed it. Would stay there again. Rooms we renovated probably a while back and need more updates. Great location I thought.

I had a sense of nostalgia and came back to DL for a visit on Mon 28 Sep 09... It was so, so amazingly crowded, thousands of strollers and almost impossible to actually take any rides, although I did use the Fastpass for Indiana Jones & the Haunted Mansion with the cool holiday overlay... I first came here in 1979, then again through the end of the 80's and the early 90's, and there was a time when Disneyland had off peak times, when ride lines were sometimes short. I suppose those times are over. Nothing wrong with that of course. In terms of the Disney magic, I didn't sense much in the faces of cast members who looked hot, bothered, and quite obviously frazzled by dealing with the massive crowds. One cast member on the Disneyland Railway was quite rude to a whole bunch of people with small children waiting for a train. I've never quite seen anything like it before. But there you are... I hope you find the magic you're looking for   I'm just sharing my personal experience!

Friday night at 7 pm, unbelievably crowded in  Downtown Disney . I was a single person visiting. the moral of this story is don't go to this resort if you're single. I first went to a Cajun Restaurant, Ralph Brennans. I was told there was only room for at the bar, although I saw several vacant tables. The hostess didn't have to courtesy to look to see that the bar was already completely full.The House of Blues restaurant was completely closed for a special event. Every other restaurant had at least a 45 minute wait, up to 1.5 hours. At this point it was 8pm.. I was ravenous. I returned to the Napa Rose restaurant, inside the Resort. Again, empty tables all around, but I was told I would have to eat at the packed bar. There were two chairs and I would be smashed together with strangers, but I was starving. 15 minutes passes, a waiter didn't even make eye contact me. I was furious. I went to the hostess and asked if there was ROOM SERVICE at the resort, and they said yes. I lodged a stern complaint with the manager of the Restaurant. First, it was obvious I was being denied a table because I was a single, and the restaurants didn't want to lose out on more revenue. Second, the resort is HORRIBLY unprepared for this volume of guests for dinner. The manager was nice enough to comp my room service dinner, but heck whats the point of going to Disneyland to eat by yourself in your room?If you're going on a busy weekend, be prepared for a LONG wait for dinner, rude service people and huge crowds. My first night on a group tour, I was so bummed I didn't go to the first night event. I would actually like to check out early. Disneyland is not for singles, and the group that invited me made it appear we would be accomodated for.

My family has gone to Walt Disney World in Florida the past four years for vacation. This year we wanted to do a mixture of things for vacation (not just theme parks), so we decided Southern California would be the best bet for us as we could spend time at the beach, go to Hollywood and Beverly Hills, take a Dolphin Whale cruise, and of course go to Disneyland and California Adventure!I had been to Disneyland before, but it was my wife and daughter's first trip to California. When we started to plan our trip, we initially looked at the Disney Hotels since we are used to the resorts at WDW. We quickly learned that there are quite a few differences between the WDW Resort and the DL Resort with hotel price being one of them (we ended up staying at the Ayers Inn on Chapman (see my review). In addition, guests do not enjoy the same benefits at the DL Resort Hotels that they do at the WDW Resort. For example, there is no Magical Express     guests have to pay for their transportation to and from the airport. Along with that, at WDW Resorts guests are able to check their bags and get their boarding passes at their resorts, but that service is not available at DL Resort Hotels. Also, there are no  Magic Hours  like the ones at WDW. Now, DL (not DCA) does have  Magic Mornings  on Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday, and Sunday mornings where magic morning ticket holders can get in the park an hour early (7am instead of 8am), but the Magic Mornings are not only available to the guests staying at the DL Hotels. Any guest purchasing a 3 day (or more) Park Hopper Ticket is given one  Magic Morning  to use during their stay. We bought a 3 day Park Hopper Bonus Ticket which gave us one MM. We used the MM, and we were glad we did as it was the only way we were able to go on some of the rides since the lines were very short. One more difference we saw between WDW and DL was the dining. Those who have gone to WDW know that you need to call for dining reservations on the day when your trip is 90 days away because dining (and the dining plan) is so popular. This is not the case at DL. After we had decided we weren't going to do character meals this time, my wife and I changed our minds 2 weeks before our trip and decided to see if we could get reservations at Goofy's Kitchen at the Disneyland Hotel (see my review) for the first night we would be in town as it would be a great surprise for our daughter. I called less than 2 weeks before the date we wanted, and there was a lot of times available for reservations. In fact, we were able to pick the exact time we wanted and to top that, we walked up to Ariel's Grotto and asked if there was any availability for that day (it was already 4:20pm). When we aksed at the front desk of the restaurant, we were surprised that we could have our pick of times, so we made a reservation and were seated 30 minutes later (see my review). There are other differences between the resorts hotels, but those are the ones that quickly come to mind.As far as the Disneyland Park goes, I remember seeing hearing reading that the grand opening in 1955 didn't go so well. It was very crowded, they ran out of food, the lines were very long, and to top it off, it was really hot that day. I also remember that sometime after that Walt Disney himself believed that he could do better, and that is when he started buying up swampland in central Florida. Besides having that in my head, all of the reviews from this site saying that the park is small came to my mind when I was at DL. Now don't get me wrong, we had a great time at DL, but I finally understood what drove Walt to build in Florida and I finally understood what people meant when they referred to DL as being  small.  Here is what I saw when the  lightbulb  came on: 1) sidewalk walking areas around the park did not seem as wide as they are at WDW (making it tighter to walk around the park), 2) many of the DL rides are close together which adds to the congestion since it is common to have entry exit areas of separate rides near each other causing a large number of people to congregate in areas and make it difficult for others to navigate through around the area, and 3) There seems to be less counter service restaurants at DL than at the WDW parks. Don't get me wrong, we had a great time at DL! Rides like Alice in Wonderland, the Matterhorn, and the Indiana Jones Ride are only at DL (not at any of the WDW parks). All 3 of these rides were great! In addition, we liked how guests load and unload outside for many of the rides (in Florida most rides are inside and guests wait in line inside too). Now, even though many rides are at both locations (WDW and DL), there are differences between them. This includes Pirates of the Caribbean, Peter Pan Ride, Buzz Light Year, Space Mountain, and more.... One last difference I want to share is related to Fantasmic. At Hollywood Studios in Orlando, there is a nice outdoor theatre with plenty of bench and handicap seating. However, in Callifornia people have to sit on the asphalt walking paths or stand. While it isn't the best set up, it was a slightly different show than Hollywood Studios and we liked it! My  Disney's California Adventure  review is listed separately under that park name. Between DL and DCA, it took us 3 days to get through what we wanted to see and do. We had fun, enjoyed our time at DL, and were glad that we went! The bottom line is that we like WDW in Florida better than Disneyland, but I can't say that I would  never come back to DL.  In fact, once  Carsland ,  the Little Mermaid ride , and the  World of Color  open at DL and DCA, we might have to take a return trip to Southern California.

I can understand that southern california is a crowded place, however, I think the themeparks should consider limiting how many people enter their themeparks, for the sake of enjoyment. All the lines were very long, so we didn't get to see as much as we wantedWith that aside, I do have to say we did enjoy our time at Disneyland. The staff there are friendly, and the park is very clean. You can almost imagine what it was like when the park was opened, as many of the attractions are still the same, giving you that 'remember when' feeling of what themeparks were like before hype and 'thrill' rides took over. Its a great place to take a family, but be prepared, as the prices are much higher than they use to be. And come early to beat the crowd and catch a few extra rides before the lines get long.

I have to say that it is NOT true that you cannot bring water food into park. We bring in our own water every single time and there are tons of water fountains that you can refill your bottle throughout the day. I have not spent a cent on water on any of our trips. Use the lockers for a small cooler and bring your own sandwiches as well. As to long lines, they are to be expected. Try to get the most popular rides done by 10 a.m. and you should be fine. If you are adventurous do Splash Mountain in the evening, 10 15 min waits. And, of course, use Fast Pass for Indy, Splash and Space Mountain, as well as Soarin' in DCA (by the way, I love DCA, it has been very unfairly maligned in my opinion). I highly recommend the Animation Academy, I can barely draw a straight line and came out of there with a very respectable drawing of Mickey. The crowds this summer were a bit crazy so, if you can, go in September October, the weather is awesome and the crowds are reasonable. Disneyland is a must do experience if at all possible. I went for the first time at the age of 40 and I am hooked. It is truly a magical experience and I highly recommend it. Just do your homework and you will have a smashing good time.

Let me start by saying that I have been to Disneyland before and loved it, but this time it was just way to crowded. I was with small children and I can honestly say I didn't feel safe. I couldn't even get my stroller through the crowds, and I was too afraid to let my little one out of the stroller    because he could get lost in two seconds with all the people swarming.I'll be back, but not in the summer and not on a weekend.

We had the 3 day pass which include magic morning. Unfortunately we had to be there on the last week of August where lots and lots of day camps kids were also in Disneyland.We came in early in the morning, as soon as the park opened, because by 10am the queue started to get on the long side. Between 8 and 10 you should be able to get 5 6 (most popular) rides done. We would go back to our hotel, because we had 100 degrees temperature when we were there, at around 11am to have lunch and afternoon siesta. We would go back to the park around 4pm 'til 7pm where we would have dinner at the many places outside the park also to have bit of rest at the hotel. By around 8.30pm we would be in the park again just in time for the fireworks or fantasmic. We generally left the park around 1 2 hr after it closed.When we were there they only allowed FastPass from Friday to Sunday only. A number of popular rides don't have FastPasss, like Toy Story. My son manage to get on California Screamin' three times on one night because he rode it around 1 2hr before closing time. He basically ran to the entrance again after finishing one ride, and because there was no queue he was able to get on again immediately.For shows etc. we tried to arrive on the last minute because it was most likely you'd be able to get in since the crowd wasn't that big, and you didn't have to stand in the queue for 30 mins!!They searched your bags, but I'm not sure whether you're allowed to bring food in. Water bottles are fine.

Do yourself a favour   don't go in the busy period (if you can)! Don't get me wrong   it is a great place with exciting attractions and shows. But when you have to wait in a line for an hour, the power drops down just when you started to watch a 3D show and most of the attractions do not work for an hour and a half because of that, and all people flood the street till you can barely move, positive and negative emotions are at par.On the back of the entry pass it says that:  Parks, attractions or entertainment may change operating hours, close due to refurbishing, capacity, weather or special events; and may otherwise change or be discontinued without notice and without liability.  And it is nonrefundable. So you pay $12 parking and the $72 one day entry and get no liability of any kind. The Fast pass is no good   you can get only one, and the time you save on one attraction, you wait on another one because of people with fast passes entering all the time.Disney should try to improve this   by an online reservation system or something else. Although I doubt if they want to do that   that will mean fewer admitted people and fewer money. Why do that since people keep coming anyway?

My fiance and I went to DL on August 18th as part of our California road trip. I had been there a few times before as a child and teenager but it was his first. We're in our late 20s early 30s and we had a BLAST! It's not just for kids! Here's what made our trip enjoyable:1. Buy or borrow the  Unofficial Guide to Disneyland.  It's a life saver. Used the 1 day plan and followed most of what the guide recommended. The book doesn't change much from year to year so a slightly out of date one should be fine. I had the 2007.2. We stayed on the beach at Newport so we drove in but I know several of the hotels in the area offer shuttles. Parking is $12.3. Show up at opening or before and eat breakfast before you get there. Don't waste valuable time eating breakfast or grabbing coffee once you arrive.4. Wear comfortable clothing and shoes. Bring a small backpack (that you'll want to carry for the whole day) with a water bottle, a few snacks and sweatshirt or jacket. Even in August, you'll be chilly at night. Having the food and water meant that we didn't have to stop what we were doing to grab a snack from one of the vendors. I know several people post that they bring coolers of food and store them in lockers. I thought that would be too much work for a party of 2. I guess if you have a family of 4, that would make more sense.5. Ride the most popular rides within the first 2 hours of getting to Disney. I know it sounds crazy but we rode Space Mountain, Matterhorn Bobsleds, Big Thunder, Splash Mountain within the first 90 minutes. Pirates of the Caribbean loads people very quickly and was at a constant wait time of 30 min. each time we checked back so don't waste time in the morning doing this one. 6. Use fastpass if the waits are over 30 minutes. This will save you lots of time! You may need to wait a little while even if you have the fastpass. For example, we had a 20 30 min. wait for Indiana Jones. I would recommend that you ride this one earlier in the day than we did (which was just about 2pm). The later in the day you get your fastpass, the later the return time will be. For example, if you go to a ride at 2pm, the standby wait time may be 50 minutes and the posted fastpast return time may be 5pm   6pm. However, if you arrive at the ride at 10:30am, the wait may be 30 minutes and the fastpast return time will be at 11:30 12:30. Basically, fastpass machines are at a select number of rides and you enter your ticket into the machine and it spits out a return ticket and time. You cannot get another fastpass until the return time passes. Using the above example, at 11:31, you would be able to get another fastpass for another ride (regardless of if you've used your first one). You do not need to pay attention to the return time. In this example, you can ride anytime after 11:31am.7. Save the attractions you can  rest  on until later in the day when you need a little sit down. These include the Mark Twain boat, Jungle Cruise, Golden Horseshoe Stage, Tiki room, Disney railroad, Honey I shrunk the Audience, etc.8. A lot of postings have been made about food at DL. We ate at the French market cafe and had a delicious salad and jambalaya for about $12 each. There were lots of veggies, flavor, chicken and sausage in my jambalaya and it was GOOD! If you want burgers, pizza, healthy stuff   there is lots to choose from. I found there to be lots of places to eat in the shade or inside. Golden Horseshoe has a food counter and there are lots of tables and air conditioning inside!9. Do not let crying children, slow walkers, arguing families, or anyone else get in the way of your fun!10. Get the showtime schedule when you arrive. We only looked at it during our lunch break and found out that the Mark Twain ride ended at 5:45 and the Golden Horseshoe ended early (I think 5 or so). We were also able to plan our wait for  it's a small world  during the afternoon parade. 11. Finally, have a plan of action for the day. We followed the guide from the  Unofficial guide  but don't waste time wandering around aimlessly. You'll grow snappy with each other if the lines are long or if you disagree on the next ride. Hope this helps and hope you have a great, memorable trip to DL!

Disneyland is very busy during the summer months but can still be enjoyed and line waiting can be minimized with a strategy.*Toon Town for young children should be done first thing in the morning, in order to avoid the rush and crowds. We arrived at 9:30 a.m. on a Saturday and were able to do the rides with no wait and met Minnie and Mickey with a short 5 minute wait each.Right after that we went to Princess Fantasy Faire where we waited for about an hour to meet 3 princesses (which princesses it will be varies).*In Disneyland we obtained Fast Passes where ever possible to avoid the long lines for the popular rides. *California Adventure has a neat feature that is not well advertised: it allows single riders the chance to move to the front of the line to fill any empty seats (groups of three). That worked very well for us as someone was always staying back with our toddler.*The crowds were much denser at Disneyland than at California Adventure where wait times for rides and attractions are much, much shorter. *The parade at California Adventure is based on Disney Pixar movies (The Incredibles, Monster's Inc., Finding Nemo, Toy Story etc.) a definite must for families with young children. We ate all of our 6 meals in Disneyland and were not disappointed with one meal or food item. There is an excellent variety of foods to choose from for all types of palates and Disney has a wide selection for those who are looking for healthier options. Each meal was ~ $30 for 2 adults and one child.Just outside of Disneyland and California Adventure is Downtown Disney: a really great shopping attraction that offers a wide assortment of stores, restaurants, and live entertainment. There are several Disney stores as well as other neat stores that are not Disney themed. This is a must see visit, if you have the time.

We visited Disneyland on Aug. 10 and it was PACKED. Our best strategy was to arrive shortly after the park opened and do some of the Tomorrowland rides right away. We were able to do the Buzz Lightyear ride twice in about 15 minutes, had a very short wait for Autopia (which should be updated with a Cars theme   would be a natural fit) and had about a 30 minute wait for Nemo. The lines got pretty long after that for just about everyything. By about 1:00 p.m. everyone was getting tired and crabby so we went back to the hotel for a short rest and returned to the park about 3:30. That worked out well. We ended up not going on everything we wanted, but we made sure we took in the attractions the kids would enjoy. Highlights of the day were the Buzz Lightyear ride, Pirates of the Caribbean (not to be missed!), the Jungle Cruise (the guide was hilarious), the Tea cups and the Dumbo ride (I've been to Disneyland 3 times now and DisneyWorld 6 and have never done this ride.) Before we went I purchased Ridemax, but didn't use it once we were in the park. I would subscribe to it again though because if nothing else, it was fun to use it to prepare for the trip. I knew going in August would be hot and crowded, so I was prepared for that. However, if we ever go back, I would definately pick a time when we know there won't be quite as many people.

What can i say but this was everything and more than we thoughtMy wife and i in our 20's spent 2 full days and nights here and would go back tomorrow in a heartbeat.Did alot of reasearch and had Fastpass down pat which makes such a difference.

Disneyland is a spectacular theme park. The rides are top notch and the grounds are lovely. Whether you will have a good time, however, is entirely dependent upon the time of year that you visit. We just returned from a couple days at the park in August 2009. It was so crowded that it was not even enjoyable. Walking anywhere was like being stuck in a can of sardines. Everywhere you looked there was a mass sea of humanity, with plenty of pushing and shoving going on. It would easily take 30 minutes just to get across the park because there were so many people there. The wait times for most rides were from 1 2 hours.The FastPass system works great, but only a handful of rides offer Fastpass, and for those that do, you will frequently find yourself getting a ticket to come back in 5 7 hours in order to ride. We were not able to get Fastpasses for some rides because they were all gone before noon.We arrived at the park at opening time, and it was great for about 45 minutes. We had to wait no more than 10 minutes for a ride and could easily walk around the park. However, by 9 or 9:30, the wait times climbed up to 30 to 45 minutes per ride and by 10:30, you could expect to wait an hour or more.If you want to truly enjoy Disney, come when it is not so crowded. If you must come during the summer, be prepared for a long day of waiting. Plan out everything you want to do and stay on top of your Fastpasses.

It was so much fun! Went with boyfriend, and as two adults, we were able to race through the park and see everything. We downloaded and used the Ridemax software, which got us way ahead of schedule and we were able to get way ahead of schedule and see most of the park in one day! As anyone knows, Disneyland is a magical experience. I do have to say, though, that the staff was less friendly than I remember. While we never had any direct negative interactions, I witnessed  cast members  being almost surly with guests on several differnent occasions. This was disappointing, but we still had a great time! I recommend a few things: 1.) Share food when you can   if you split a sandwhich or pretzel, it cuts your costs in half. I was suprised that we actually stayed within our food budget using this method. 2.) Invest in the Ridemax software. I was skeptical, but it was only $14.95 month and it seemed to save us a huge amount of time. I will get it again the next time I go. 3.) Careful of the water. As out of towners, we both got a little ill after a few days of refilling our waterbottles in the park. I have since talked to friends who experienced the same thing. In all fairness, it is probably just not being used to the water in So. CA rather than Disneyland itself. 4.) Learn the fast pass system. The Ridemax software helped us with this. (No, I'm not affiliated with them or anything; I was just way impressed!) 5.) It's ok to take breaks! Looking back, one of my favorite parts of the prark was just fooling around on Tom Sawyer Island and sitting and watching the boats go by, rather than rushing to get in line for another ride. 6.) If you are going to be there for more than two days, be sure to take care of your feet! I am a regular walker, and even alternating two comfy pairs of tennis shoes, my feet were really sore by the third day, and they just got worse. I wouldn't try this in sandals! 7.) Don't take anything too seriously. We saw quite a few heated arguments about what ride to do next or where to eat or where to stand, etc, instead of people just enjoying whatever they were doing. Just have fun!

Disneyland is where I've been, where I am, and where I'll always be. The cast members are courteous and friendly, and the atmosphere is unbeatable. One thing I must say, though the food prices are OUTRAGEOUS! Be prepared to pay $4 $5 for a water, or bring your own. The security will not take it. The best time to go is mid September, the weekend after Labor Day weekend. The weather is perfect, no lines, it's a dream come true. I live 7 hours away from Disneyland, and once bought an Annual Pass! It's that worth it. Go you won't regret it.

This is my third lifetime visit. This was definitely the worst trip. Compared to what this place could be and what it is, it gets a 2 circles out of five and probably deserves 1.As other reviews have stated, there seems to be a problem with ride breakdowns. Out of three and a half days, the Indiana Jones ride broke down twice, the Matterhorn twice, the dumbo ride once and we talked to others that commented about other rides breaking down. The fact is, if these rides are maintained properly these things are not going to happen this often, if at all. I sense there must be budget cutbacks to maintenance staff. This is absolutely unacceptable. If you do a search you will find that one individual lost his life in 2003 on the Big Thunder roller coaster due to Disney's admitted fault in not maintaining the equipment properly. Do a search you will find more instances.This is not why I down grade Disney so much though. I down grade them because they have marketed the      out of Mickey. In my opinion, there should be more attractions and rides than stores selling the same crap all over Disney. Every where you turn they want to nickel and dime you for hats, food, more hats, shirts, clothes, etc. The rides and entertainment are secondary here to them selling you products and food.The place is hot and shade can be scarce. They need to get off their butts and install misting fans, misting nozzles and more shade throughout the park. Universal studios, although a complete rip off, does a great job with this aspectThere was no magic for me this time and I doubt that I really want to come back.The crowds of people were over whelming much of the time and this included weekday entry. The strollers get in the way. They are every where. You get tired of people running into you, cutting you off, stopping in front of you, etc. There were so many rude people that just made a home in the walkway where ever they felt like it. The fastpass machines actually closed about 6 pm one day, 6 hours before park closing timeI did not find any of the food enjoyable. The funnel cake sucked. The beef at the Mexican place in Frontier land was horrendous. The 20 cent bottles of water that they charge $3 for was bunk. The ice cream was good, but that really isn't food.Disney is relying way too much on the mouse and many outdated rides. The one star wars ride is from the early 80's and was pretty lame.I was disappointed that they actually allowed smoking in the park. The designated smoking areas are right next to the regular areas with no barriers in between. Again, I suspect this is an attempt to squeeze as many pennies as possible from all demographics.The bathrooms could definitely use some work. Everyone I used smelled bad and could have used some air flow. They were not particularly dirty just smelly. No reason for that.The good things are that the park was kept pretty clean and the young kids have a good time in Toon Town and other kid rides. It isn't magic though, it's marketing.

We absolutely loved Disneyland. Although we've visited previously we can never get enough of Disneyland. Everyone we came into contact with, characters, ride staff, shop staff (or cast members as they're called) and visitors were friendly and happy. Disneyland is unlike any other theme park we've visited because it's always clean and every inch of the park has something to look at, even while waiting in line for rides.Can't wait to go back.

Even though any critical review on this site gets a  not useful  mark from the fans, I have to share a comment on the frequent breakdowns in Disneyland. We went on July 28th, 2009 and entered a  short  line at Splash Mountain which had just recovered from a breakdown. After 70 minutes we had reached the boarding station and ride broke down again. Another 20 minutes later just standing still, our small children could not bear anymore and we decided to leave. I argued for a while with a cast member that we should be given fastpasses, but it was stay in line for an indefinite amount of time or loose your spot. I cannot believe they treat people that way. Because the waiting time on any attraction averaged 45 minutes and we went through 3 more breakdowns at other rides, we managed to do only 10 attractions in a whole day, even making the best use of fastpasses. The bad treatment at Splash Mountain made our day at Disney less then memorable.
great for kids, very memorable. everyone loved it, but bring good shoes!

It only took me and my husband 50 and 54 years to get to Disneyland (from Australia) but it was well and truly worth the wait! It was all we could ever have imagined and more! We went in July so it was very hot and school holidays, but hey, there are plenty of rides to get wet on and when you're so pumped who notices the heat? We had a 3 day Park Hopper Pass plus Magic Morning pass and stayed right opposite at the Tropicana Inn which meant we were at Disneyland in no time and could easily go back to the hotel for a rest (not that we did that much) and return to the park barely losing any time at all. Queues are to be expected but they move quite quickly. Early morning and late at night are the best times to ride those really popular rides to beat those crowds. We didn't really think it was expensive (hey, we came all the way from Sydney, Australia) ... just consider how many rides you can go on and the free shows and just soaking up the atmosphere and taking it all in is worth admission alone! California Adventure Park is great and has the more 'serious' theme park rides ... l'm not usually one for rollercoasters but I was there and I just had to try 'California Screamin' and it was unreal! The nightly fireworks show and Disney electrical parade were AMAZING!!! Too many great rides to have a favourite, but we'll always remember our first ... Big Thunder Mountain Railroad! Everything about our trip to Disneyland was great, it's so very clean, friendly, magical and really is the happiest place on earth! We won't leave it for another 50 years to come back that's for sure!!!!

The best advice I received was to get there early. Cannot stress this enough. We had virtually no wait for any of the popular attractions when we went early. The fast pass is also very helpful. One day, it was 2:00 pm and we still wanted to ride the Grizzly RIver Run in CA. The fast pass return time was between 4:30   5:30 pm. This was perfect   we had reservations at the Rainforest Cafe at 5:30, so we went back to the hotel, cooled off in the pool, returned at about 4:45, rode the ride and went to dinner (WET). MY TWO FAVORITE RIDES at DL were Indiana Jones (SERIOUSLY, you CANNOT miss this!) and Splash mountain. We also did Pirates of the Carib, Star Tours and the Haunted Mansion (all very good). Did not do Small World (I had seen this many years ago, plus my 9 yr old son was not interested). If you have small kids, they'll love it. Would not do Autopia again. You ride around on these little cars but it is SO hard to press the gas pedal, I had to hold my leg down with my hand (and you cannot let up because someone will rear end you). A child would never be able to hold that gas pedal down the whole time. At CALIFORNIA ADVENTURE, you MUST do Soarin Over California. This ride is incredible and is like you are actually hand gliding! (I don't do coasters   this ride is different.) The Grizzly River Run was also awesome. Very nice to get that wet on a hot, hot day! Although the water in Paradise Pier was drained because they're building a new attraction, we went there because my husband wanted to ride the Maliboomer, the Twilight Zone Tower of Terror and California Screamin. He loved all three!  I WISH SOMEONE HAD TOLD US  NOTE: If you are staying at a hotel on Harbour Blvd near DL, use the 43 bus to go get your supplies (milk, snacks, liquor   for a cocktail after a loooong day at the Park). If you are on the side of the Camelot inn (or Best Western), take the 43 to Lincoln Ave. and get off. Turn right (east) and a block down, there is a CVS Pharmacy (liquor was A THIRD of what we paid at a liquor store close to DL) and there's also a VON's grocery. When you're done, go back to Harbour Blvd, cross the street, and catch the 43 coming back. The bus costs $1.50 per person each way. NOTES: Rainforest Cafe was a great (but noisy) place to eat. Awesome coladas and coconut shrimp! Take the 43 bus (in either direction) to a Carls Jr instead of eating at McDonalds. Their burgers are so much better!

My sister and I travellered for a 12 day vacation to see Disney, Vegas and LA Hollywood. Since we're all the way from New Zealand, it really will only be a once off for us (sadly). I did a lot of planning before we left because I wanted to get the most from our 2 day park hopper pass, since we had to cover both parks, it was even more important we didn't waste time.This is not endorsed by Disney, but I have to recommend those who are under tight time constraints, invest US$14.99 in RIDEMAX!!! Just google it, it's an amazing program that has been formulated to give you the least waiting time possible given the rides you want to do. I cannot recommend it enough, it saved us hours. We arrived both mornings at 7.30am to try get in first, while everyone else raced to do line up for Nemo, Splash Mountain etc... we ran to get fast passes in one hr gaps (maximum you are allowed is 1 per hour) and riding the less popular rides first. We would come back at the fast pass allocated time and have no wait while others had to wait about an hour. Sure there is a lot of running around, but you can take pictures and see virtually the whole park at the same time. Ridemax prints you out a schedule that is planned to the minute, if you follow it, I guarantee you the estimated ride wait times is accurate. On the 2nd morning, we went to Mickey's Toon Town to take pictures with all the characters   no lines, all the main characters were there. Everyone else is busy waiting in lines, then do character pictures in the afternoon. We managed to do DIsneyland in 1.5 days (the other .5 in DIsney Cali), and had a awesome time. We were there on 4th and 5th of July, the crowds were shocking and the days were so hot   we had to go back to our hotel to rest(5 mins away   tip: stay within walking distance!!).We absolutely LOVED the Fantasmic show   so much we went both nights just to record it the second night. GO EARLY!!! Even going 30 mins before the show didn't help   all the standing places were taken. We managed to squeeze in before they turned people away, told them to come back at the later shows (10.30pm or 11.30pm on Saturday). The prices of food and drink at Disney were of course, off the charts... very expensive to eat there, but I suppose it is to be expected. We brought in Subway sandwiches with us in our bag to eat, but buying no food drink is pretty hard! Disney will always be one of those must do attractions, we're so happy to have done this memorable trip!

Maybe from reading some of the reviews of Disneyland my expectations were lowered, but my experiences greatly exceeded my expectations.The complaint I've heard quite a bit is how Disneyland is expensive. My first remark to that would be, compared to what? I've been to many Theme Parks on the East Coast over the past few years, and Disneyland was not more expensive than any other major theme park. I was pleasantly surprised that the stores and restaurants in the local neighborhood were not any more expensive that the ones in my local neighborhood. I've been to many resort areas where the local establishments really jack up the prices. Actually, in that regard, I think Disneyland, and the area around it, is more like a  real  neighborhood that anywhere around the Orlando Area. I just feel like all of central Florida is one big tourist trap.I've heard a lot about the price of meals at Disneyland, and I was a bit concerned about that. Again, I can honestly say I was pleasantly surprised. My wife, myself, and our two teen age daughters, ate breakfast at the Carnation Cafe, we had waffles, sausages, fruit, coffee, and juice, all had similar meals, and the price was less that $40. Heck, that's not any more than for the same meal at IHOP. And sitting at an outdoor cafe was sure better than any atmosphere at IHOP! We ate another meal at the Test Pilots Grill, all getting a gourmet burger platter, and again, for the 4 of us, the meal was about $40.00. To compare that to a typical eating out dinner for four, such as our recent visit to a gourmet burger chain, the quality of the food, and the price, was no different that the food I had at Disneyland.As far as California Adventure, there has been many negative reviews of it. And I admit, I fell into the trap of expecting California Adventure to be just like any other amusement park, only with a Disney logo on it. Well, that's wrong. For example, Grizzly River Run a first glance looked to me like just another spinning rapid river ride. As I looked closer at the ride, I saw a typical amusement park ride, that went higher, went faster, and had more detail and depth to it that similar rides at other amusement parks. Yes, it appeared that Disney took a typical amusement park ride, and cranked it up a notch. I enjoyed California Adventure, as did our family. Not it's not anything like Disneyland, just like Epcot is not anything like the Magic Kingdom in Florida. And no, California Adventure is not just like Epcot, but what's so wrong about that?We live on the East Coast, but we have been to Disneyland 3 time in the past 5 years. When we say we are going to Disneyland, folks around here ask, Florida? And I say, no, the real one in California. I absolutely love it. When I am there I digress about 40 years in age. I can't wait to go back!

Disneyland has become a money mongral. You get searched on your way in and are not allowed to bring in food or drinks. Then they charge you $3.00 for a Dasani water (the kind you pay a dollar for in the store. Plan on spending at least $10.00 per meal per person if you eat in the park, and losing at least an hour going to your car or out of the park each time you eat. Lines were at least an hour for the good rides so all in all you pay $75 to get in and get to ride maybe 6 rides if you utlize the fast passes.Money Money Money  and souvaniers...Please do yourself a favor and go to Wal Mart for the clothing.Basically, you are paying for the  privilage  of seeing a  must see before you die  place. I will never go there again. Also, too see the whole park, you need more than 3 days.

We took our kids to Disneyland and California Adventure this summer. The boys (7 & 9) have asked to go there ever since they were little, thanks to the advertising on videos. We finally got the chance to take them and they had a great time! The rides were great, the shows were great, and the staff was always friendly and helpful. It really is a magical place!Probably my biggest criticism would be the crowds! We went July 13, 14, & 15, 2009, and there was no end to the lines! The best advice I can give is to be there early! DL opens at 8 and CA opens at 10   be there then and you will have the chance to ride the most popular rides without much waiting. Later in the day, you'll spend plenty of time waiting   even with the fastpass.One morning we used the magic morning option that came with our parkhopper tickets and arrived at 7 am   it was early, yes, but well worth it! We rode space mountain 3 times and the matterhorn once before the park even opened! Food and drinks here are expensive, so be prepared. We ate a big breakfast every day (we went to IHOP across the road one day and discovered it was REALLY high there, too   7.99 for the kids' breakfasts; go to the Coco's on Harbor & Chapman   it's MUCH more reasonable!), then brought waters and snacks (crackers & candy bars) to tide us over until the late afternoon. By then, the crowds were usually so bad that we left, ate an early supper, and rested until evening. By the way, evening crowds are horrific. I am surprised that one person even mentioned that they close the park when it's full to capacity   it sure didn't seem like it at night!!! You couldn't hardly move in the place! And stake out your place for the night shows early   at least an hour before. We didn't , and had trouble finding a place to watch   even though we showed up for Fantasmic 40 minutes early. People are rude, also, and will come and stand in front of you even though you have been waiting for a long time and they just walked up . . . be prepared; I was really ticked off by the number of people who pushed me and my kids around, trying to get in front of us for a better spot. However, I can't blame Disneyland for the decline of manners in America!!Souvenirs are really neat, though a little overpriced as well. I bought two t shirts   one for each of my kids. One is a youth sized shirt, and one a small adult size. I spent $47!! The t shirts are just regular shirts; not long sleeved, not embroidered, etc. I was also going to buy my kids a set of mouse ears for them to have as souvenirs   but they were $15 , so I passed. My kids, who had saved their own money, even shopped discriminately and mentioned how expensive the toys were. And trust me, my kids aren't great at saving money, so I was really surprised that they noticed how expensive things were. However, I took plenty of pics and plan on scrapbooking our trip, so that will make the best souvenir of all!As for the rides, our favorites at Disneyland were Space Mountain, Splash Mountain, the Haunted Mansion and Indiana Jones. The boys weren't impressed by It's a Small World, but we felt they HAD to ride it, just because. They also really liked Pirates of the Caribbean. They also enjoyed the Honey, I Shrunk the Kids show and the Innovations (Innoventions?) attraction at Disneyland.At California Adventure, California Screamin' was the favorite. It's quite a unique roller coaster ride that takes off in seconds   and never slows down until you stop. It has great dips and even a loop, but you really don't have time to anticipate what comes next and get nervous   it's over and done before you can think about it. My kids both enjoyed this, and the 7 year old was tall enough to ride it.The water ride here   I can't remember the exact name   was also a favorite. We got wet, but not soaked. My nine year old enjoyed the Tower of Terror, but it was a little much for the 7 year old   he cried after it was over, and he's my little dare devil, so be warned that it might be a little much for young children. There is a nice little section of rides just for young ones in CA, and the shows here are fantastic! We saw the It's a Bugs Life show (I can't remember the exact name again) as well as the Muppets in 3 D (twice), and Talking with Crush. There is also an Animator's Workshop in the building where the Crush show is   they teach you how to draw a cartoon character   very neat! My youngest and I have bad eyes and cannot usually see 3 D attractions   these are VERY well done, and we could see the special effects without any problems! All of these will be great for your kids!Finally, I can't go without mentioning the acapella group that sings in front of the theater on the Hollywood side of CA. I can't remember there name   the something Daddy os??? I'm not sure, but they are a wonderful quartet and sing some great oldies like  Under the Boardwalk  and  In the Still of the Night  and many others. I could have listened to them all day; they were really good. If you enjoy oldies, make sure to look for them!Despite the crowds and expense, my kids said this was their best vacation ever. My 7 year old even cried today when we left because he wanted to go back again and again . . . however, since we are from Oklahoma, that may have been his only visit! However, if it ever works out, we will consider taking him back, if only for the magic . . .
one of the most overblown  family  destinations I've had the displeasure to visit.  Be prepared to stand in long lines, the hot sun in summer and pay thru the nose for everything except bathroom use.

We visited Disneyland on July 5th (a Sunday). We expected huge crowds, but the park was practically empty, especially in the first few hours of the day. I was hoping to try out the Fastpass feature, but the lines were almost nonexistant so I never bothered. Because of the short lines, we were actually able to do everything we wanted to do at both parks! We visited Downtown Disney on the Saturday night for dinner, fireworks, and to get some of our shopping in which saved time on our big day. We stayed at the Candy Cane Inn which is right by California Adventure park, so the walk over was easy. Also it was my son's birthday, so he got in free (we registered online beforehand, brought his passport, and paid the difference to make his ticket a parkhopper one). Only complaint: pricey food and drinks, but this is to be expected. We actually left the park for lunch and drove to In N Out burger a few miles down the road (best burgers ever!) :)

I traveled to the USA from New Zealand in November last year, myself and two children, 13yrs, 12yrs. We stayed at the Howard Johnson (See review) We arrived at Disneyland on November the 19th, a Wednesday. Firstly I must say ,we had what no one really has   NO CROWDS!!! And you know why? Because they were all waiting for the Christmas Displays to open on the Friday. We followed the plans in the Ultimate Guide to Disneyland book, they really do work. We were early and I had studied the maps. We could ride Space Mountain as many times as we liked, the most we waited on any ride was 10mins. We even said to each other, what was everyone talking about? Disneyland isn't that busy!! We used our park hopper ticket again on the Friday   we then knew what everyone was talking about!!But because we had been on everything twice!! we just picked the ones we wanted. Also, we split up for two hours and met back, the older kids didn't want to ride  It's a small world!  We also found using SINGLE RIDER passes to be fantastic too! Most of the time we used these even though we were together, 4 5 times we were on the same ride together anyway! Just not sitting next to each other. I would do this again if I'm so blessed to be back. I felt very safe and did not worry about the kids. Coming from new zealand, we found the food to be very resonable, Knotts Berry farm was a joke, $8 for a milkshake???!!! At Disney they have water fountains for you to use. I loved Disneyland.

We just got back from our first trip to Disneyland with our 10 years old daughter. I purchase RIDEMAX and made plans(print) for 3 days at both parks just in case. Well, we saved a day! You'll have to hurry in the morning, have a big break in the afternoon for other things to see(parades...). The only thing that did not work was when it's time to get your Fastpass(A MUST)...it just seemed that it was NEVER the right timing. We never waited longer than planed on the schedule. The first morning the 2 first rides were not running so we went back on the third day with the other print out for that day. So if you're going for more than one day, make and print few plans ahead and bring them with you.Also, if you get there early enough, for Disney California, stick to the gate in the middle and you will have a chance to open the gates with the staff!!!! We did it the two days we went! : )PLEASE, have has many pictures taken of you in both parks and use the photopass for all the days you'll go. On your last day, go to the Kodak store(on the corner in Disneyland park) and view your pictures. The sell it $15 each or THE CD WITH ALLLLL THE PICTURE FOR $60!!!! We had 48 but next time, we'll have more as it cost the same!Buy on line as much as possible before(entrance, Grotto Ariel lunch amazing, Goofy'S kitchen...)You'll save a lot.Have a great time!

The recent  5 day pass for the price of 3  brought too many people to the parks! It appears the rides cannot handle the volume of guests during a promotion especially in Summer, it's busiest season. Within 24 hours there were 12 rides that we attempted to get on, that broke down resulting in a 45 minute to an hour longer wait time or the ride closed and we had to leave. It was so crowded that there was no room to walk. Our last evening, after a trip to Laguna Beach (which was beautiful) we rushed back to Disneyland and we never made it on any rides ( the  E ticket  rides that we wanted to go on) due to  technical difficulties . However, the next morning (Sunday) we used our Magic Morning (early admission) to Disneyland and went on 5 (Mountain) rides in one hour which made up for the night before. Thankful for that Sunday morning   the day we were going home   to be able to leave happy. Overall, I would say this was a very expensive trip to be somewhat disappointed at the Happiest Place on Earth. I still recommend Disneyland but not during Summer when there is a promotion. We usually have an excellent time at Disneyland and have never experienced any ride breaking before. This was a strange trip this year.
enjoy so much here so much nicer than paris disney. nice to see park and places. so expensive need to bring price down or peopel from europe better price.

Typically we need 3 days to experience the Disneyland Resort; a day at each park and one to jump around to things we   ve missed    We needed all 5 days this time the park was so crowded. We thought Friday and Saturday were bad but they were nothing compared to Monday and Tuesdays hoard of people. Don   t avoid the park on weekends in hopes of a quiet time during the week. Not during the summer anyway. Southern California resident passes are not good on the weekends so they come during the week. If you have to go on a busy day, expect a wait and plan for it. You will have to wait at the bag check and at the gate. Get in the park early and if you need to leave get a hand stamp. It will get you back in if they close the gates due to full capacity. If you plan to visit both parks go to Disneyland first when it opens then leave to go to California Adventure when it opens at ten (don   t forget that hand stamp.) Once you   re in you can hop back and forth all day but expect to wait in line each time. Use the fast pass feature on any rides that have it even if you decide to go ahead and wait in line. You can always return later and ride again. If it   s very busy get a ticket that tells you to return later then while you   re waiting explore another part of the park, stand in line for a ride that doesn   t offer fast pass or eat a meal. Food is expensive in the park but we found that Denny   s and IHOP were more expensive than normal too. Choose food vendors that offer larger portions. Linger where other customers come out with their trays and ask questions. Restaurants in New Orleans square are good. Make reservations for Blue Bayou (inside Pirates) early they fill up very fast; you may not be able to get in your first day! Very pricy dinner but worth the experience at least once (I recommend the cr  me Brule for dessert it comes with a sugar treasure chest.) Stage Door and Golden Horseshoe are not great unless you really like overpriced chicken strips. Avoid Bengal Barbeque! It smells awesome but is extremely overpriced! Almost $4 for one skewer of meat (three bite size pieces of beef or four pieces of chicken.) Their jalapeno cheese pretzel was a good snack though. In DCA corndogs can be found at the farmers market behind the fruit stand and PT fleas gift shop. They are the best! So are the bread bowls at the bakery. We found that at the vendors that offer bread bowls you can also get a cup of soup without the bowl. Saves the waste if you   re cutting down on carbs or if you plan to share with a partner. We split a salad in a bread bowl (larger than the soup bowl) and bought just a cup of soup plain to dip the bread in when we were done with the salad. Very filling and less expensive! Taste Pilots Grill, the burger place next to Soarin    has cut cost by flattening the burgers paper thin but still has good fries and onion rings. Ice cream at both parks was reasonable compared to Cold Stone outside. Sunday scoops in the train at the entrance to DCA were bigger than at Gibson Girl in Disneyland. Bring portable hand wipes  they fit right in your pockets and are helpful for removing bird poop from tables and chairs. Bring hand sanitizer! You have been standing in lines touching handrails and lap bars that millions of people have touched, climbed over, stood on    Plan your wardrobe accordingly  Don   t wear white pants! Many rides require you to step on the seats to enter and exit. I wore pants with button down pockets thinking my stuff would be secure but ended up ripping off buttons when they got caught trying to leave rides quickly. Cast Members are doing their best to hurry things along    if you are slightly overweight be prepared to move quickly in and out of rides. Also if you want to enjoy parades, fireworks and shows with    good    seats bring a blanket or a beach towel and show up at least an hour or so early. Yes, that   s right at least an hour. We waited three hours for fantasmic. A blanket or beach towel helps hold your valuable realistate. Send a member of your party to bring back food while you wait and have a pick nick or better yet pack a backpack. We saw someone using a fold up grass yoga mat that worked wonderful and packed easily. DO NOT show up a half hour before a show and stand in front of others who have been waiting for hours. DO NOT show up after a show has already started and put your child on your shoulders in front of others seated in the handicapped section either. Pixar Parade is awesome but beware of your camera all floats spray water! Light Parade is my very favorite. Fantasmic can be scary for very little ones but you can see the fireworks from the first showing just not the castle. The best seats for the fireworks are in the street in front of the castle but keep in mind they make you stand before they start. Talk to the people around you  be friendly and you might find out ahead of time who is planning to put their kids on their shoulders and you can ask to stand infront of them if you are short like me. Celebration parade and Highschool musical were both lame dont wast your time waiting for them! Have a good time! Be Patient. Respect other peoples space in line. Dont step on the back of their shoes; we'll all get on the ride eventually. Be kind to the Cast Members; they are doing their jobs to the best of their ability. If you are nice they will do all they can to help you.

Let me first say that I am a huge Disney fan and have been to the Land and the World many , many times. That said, my family and I just returned from a trip to So Cal and were disappointed in the changes that I noticed in the parks. First of all, I haven't been to Disneyland since 2003 but this trip I saw TRASH thrown down in attractions and cups left on benches and gum on the pillars. I have never in all the years I have been going to Disney seen anything like this before. I think it is probably a combination of things that has caused this. One, there were way to many people under the age of 20 without adults to influence their behavior and two, I think Disneyland is vastly under staffed. I was given a photopass card upon check in at the Grand Californian but over a 5 day visit found no photograghers in the parks. Disappointing to say the least.Finally, for my birthday we ate at the Napa Rose. The food sounded fantastic but was mediocre at best and VERY expensive. The food is better and cheaper and any number of restuarants in the World. I will not be returning to Disneyland any time soon.

My wife and I made Disneyland a must do on our world trip. The trip of a lifetime. Maybe my expectations were to high, but the lines are huge you line up for security checks then you line up to buy your tickets (pretty expensive) then you line up to enter the park. then you spend the rest of the day lining up. Tomorrowland really does need some paint and maintenance, the monorail track showing signs of corrosion and concrete cancer on the supports. As the header says a life time of waiting and it continued for our visit to disney land.

My husband & I went to DL last month for a week   last time I was there was 6 years ago. We just loved DL & DCA so much! I finally got to try the Monte Cristo sandwich that the people were raving about....it was super yummy but it was definitely rich so hubby had to help me finish it. The corn dogs were so good too, it had to be the best corn dog I've ever had. The pineapple whip float was so refreshing and wasn't too bad for $5. Yes, the food was expensive in the park so we only got the food we wanted to try and dined outside of DL...it definitely saved us $.Pirates of the Caribbean had Jack Sparrow incorporated in it...it was cool but man, he looked so real it was pretty freaky! The Haunted Mansion got some updates too with the Bride. Indiana Jones   you gotta remember to get on the left line when it forks. We got on the right line twice and the big boulder finale was missing and I was completely puzzled. We got on the left line and there it was...the big boulder and the drop. Yes! It just didn't feel right without it. We had such a blast!! We can't wait to go back to the Happiest Place On Earth! : )

We tried to enjoy our two days at Disneyland, but everything kept breaking down. We waited forever to get on Splash Mountain, and when we finally got on the log, the ride broke down after a couple minutes and we were told we would have to get off and climb down. Then the Indiana Jones ride broke down, the Peter Pan ride was under construction, there was an hour wait to meet Tinker Bell, and even just buying a snack on the street took twenty minutes. This was only day one. For myself, and my two kids, it was a $600 weekend, and it was definately not worth the time or the money. I requested getting some of our money refunded due to all the mechanical problems, but they said no and gave us an extra fast pass. The soaring California ride at California Adventure was beautiful!

Still a great time for kids. It was fun, May was a good time to go. Most of the families there had kids that werent in school yet and that made for some super short lines on the bigger rides in the morning up until about two in the afternoon. Next time we will go during the off season again for sure and during the middle of the week again. Nothing much has changed since my parents took me when i was younger. I took us about 2 1 4 days to see everything (not including California Adventure) with the two of us, a 15 year old, 10 year old and our 10 month old daughter. Feeding and changing the baby as we enjoyed the park wasn't as bad as i thought it was gonna be. In the morning we could usually ride two rides and then walk to the next ride before the fetus needed something which wasnt bad at all. What we did worked out pretty good if you have a young one, the first day we stayed away from the kids ride and tryed to hit all the big rides (baby went on most of them) and then the 2nd day we tryed to stay on the rides that the baby would enjoy such as the Flying Dumbo and what not. By the third morning all we had left to ride was Its a Small World and Mr. Toads Wild Ride and that worked out great to hit in the early moring also because there quite popular when theres mostly little kids in the park. After that we headed to the California Adventure Park. The catch there is i guess we didnt need a park jumper pass exept for the last day??? If ya had older kids i could see getting one if you had dinner reservations at one of the other parks.Use the Photo Pass people, made for some great pictures once we got home. It's expencive thats for sure but well worth it. A good tip, if you buy yourself some of those hybrid sneaker sandles flipflops they make now... wear them everyday and try to walk as much as you can in them. I got the worst blisters on the sides of my feet i'd ever had. Limping around in pain wasnt much fun. Come prepared for some heavy walking. Our best things, Indiana Jones, Splash Mountain, Jedi Training Academy was cool to watch, Meet The Princesses was fun for my younger daughters.Have fun guys. Maybe you'll get a good laugh at all the  Pin Junkies  like i did.

Took my school group here May 19 and thoroughly enjoyed it all. Rides were great, lines were short, eating was as expensive as you would think (about $15 each meal per person.) It seemed there were not as many workers as in year's past but it could be early season yet. There were management people supervising here and there so I guess they are called on to help monitor workers and be there to observe. Guest services were helpful and cheerful about it when I had to get some help. Rides closed down a couple times, one time for a 4.0 earthquake which they were not allowed to talk about being the reason they closed the rides for an hour to inspect (I'm not complaining, please inspect!) But there was plenty to do while we waited. Disney is a great place to visit. Get the map, plan your visit so you don't walk your self to death, take advantage of the shows and parades, and you will have a very fun day.

Its hard not to love Disney! My kids ( 8,7,6) just loved it! Disney has done a great job rennovating and updating! For example,  Nemo  is far better than  Twenty thousand Leagues Under the Sea  and the new  Toy Story  rides were among the favorites of my son. The parking garage is great   only one stop for all the lots   great idea!The prices were fair for a theme park. We spent a lot   just because we wanted to. Personalized, embroidered mouse ears were $15   not bad, Disney!We went during off season so the lines were very maneagable! The only parade was Dance Party USA which was like watching my grandmother drink booze in a corset. Instead of a graceful Cinderella, I see Goofy grinding with Minnie Mouse   sad but perhaps a sad reflection of our culture. If you have small kids, I will join with others in saying most of your fun will be found in Tomorrowland and Fantasyland. The only big rides in Adventureland and Frontierland were Indiana Jones and Pirates of the Carribean. Indiana Jones and Pirates did terrify my kids. I took them out of tradition, but would actually skip these in retrospect.I recommend staying at the Disney Hotel because the extra hour multiplies your time, allows you take a great break in the middle of the day, and pro longs the great experience. You will also find that you save money in other areas.

Well, whoever has stepped foot in the Happiest Place on Earth will surely agree with me   it's a very magical, fun, awesome place   even for adults like me! ;) Theme parks are great and Disneyland, although much smaller than what I've imagined, is a place for the young and the young at heart. Loved the Indiana Jones ride and this is coming from a 'not so fond of rides' person! ;)If you have small younglings   get them to participate in the Jedi Academy   it's very cool! ;) And, for food   well, we feasted on Churros   our favourite! :)

We got to the park at about 10:30 and we rode all the rides that we wanted to go on with time to spare for watching the evening parade. The longest time we had to wait for the rides was about 30 to 45 minutes. Will definately choose to go at this time of the year again to avoid all the long lines in the summer. The only downside is not being able to find the Disneyland parking garage easily on the GPS. Had to go drive around the entire park it seems to locate the entrance to the garage.

We visited here in April May in 2009. The weather was freakily hot for April   107 in Disney one day. We visited Disneyland three times before but in August 2006   and there is definately a difference. The fireworks and parades are not as regular in April as August (which I guess we should have expected). We were at Disney for 2 weeks and I think the fireworks were only displayed 3 times. Although we did get to catch them on the last night and they were well worth the wait   as with all Disney Fireworks.The parade was not up to standards that we have become used to at Disney, however, Calafornia Adventure Parade was well up to the normal standard, which did put the Disneyland Parade in the shade!The park was also very busy considering the spring breaks had finished. I would say busier than when we visited in August 2006.I want to recommend the Baby Centre to anyone visiting that has a baby. Not necessarily well known part of the park, or well used. But the centre was amazing. Air conditioned. A kitchen to warm up bottles   food. High chairs for feeding. A comfy seating area for bottle feeding. A seperate nursing section. An amazing baby changing area. I could not recommend the Centre enough   well staffed too   with very friendly people.Another brilliant disney holiday! Disneyland rarely disappoints!

I recently took my 3 daughters (aged 7, 8 and 11) to Disneyland, when their dancing group was invited to perform both at Disneyland and California Adventures. We found Disneyland to be fantastic, we park hopped between Disneyland and California Adventures, but we definitely spent more time in Disneyland. Overall we spent 8 days in the parks and we could have spent more time.We went on almost all the rides, enjoyed the shows and parades and had time to stop and enjoy the atmosphere while having a snack.I agree with the previous posters, it is definitely worth doing your homework. There are great guidebooks out there and some terrific websites. We used fast pass to our advantage (read Dark beer's fast pass guide on trip advisor) and didn't wait any longer than 10  15 minutes for a ride ( we were there in peak Spring Break time). It is definitely worth being in line before the park opens as you can get a lot done in the early hours of park opening before those who have slept in get there! If you are able to get Magic Morning entry with your ticket or by staying at one of the Disneyland hotels, that gets you in one hour early on selected days and is also worth doing.By spending some time researching you can work out which attractions you really want to see. Disneyland is more than rides the shows and parades are also fantastic. The fireworks are fantastic too. My daughter was able to battle Darth Maul in The Jedi Training Academy which was a highlight for her as an avid Star Wars fan!We did not find the food overly expensive (although it was definitely not cheap) There were lots of options for kids that included veggie sticks or fruit, often I would have a kids meal too as it was big enough for me. We also ate often from the fruit carts scattered around the park. It was great to have a pineapple spear or fruit salad especially when it was hot.We had a wonderful vacation and while we visited other places Disneyland was the highlight. It truly is the happiest place on earth  take your time and enjoy it, be a kid again!!!!

I live in California and have been vacationing Disneyland since I was a baby in a stroller, now I am 36 yrs old and its still as magical as when I was a child. My daughter is following in my footsteps and her first visit was when she was only 3 months old. We go once a year if we can manage it.I read these bad reviews and can not believe people. Yes Disneyland is expensive, its DISNEY, people. But well worth every cent. When you think that this is supposed to be a vacation, it isnt a every day type of thing, you have to account for expenses. Disneyland is not cheap, but who would expect it to be. Its ridiculous that people say its a rip off, I would have to disagree, though their food could be cheaper, their souvenirs are supposed to bring you magical memories to last a lifetime. I think the people who call it a rip off are people who didnt do their homework or ask questions about expense before their trip. You have to be aware of your expenses, if you arent, then it can lead to a diappointing vacation, with the knowledge ahead of time, you can go on your vacation worry free if you only do your homework. I am that way myself. I am always checking into things and making myself aware. Prices do change so I am always keeping up on that. Dont judge Disneyland, for you travelers not being finanically prepared for costs. You can go to certain Disneyland sites and get info for restaurants in the Disneyland Resort and get copies of the menus and get prices on food. They have all that available online for guests customers. Nothing is a surprise, they arent ripping anyone off. Like I said this is Disney, not a carnival or state fair, or rinky dink amusement park. This park has brought enjoyment to millions of people for over 50 years. Not everyone enjoys DL, but to me and my family, and my mother who was there on opening day over 50 years ago, it is truly a wonderful experience. Going back every year is like going for the first time, and it brings out the kid in all of us and lets us forget about whatever stress, or unhappiness, may be in our lives. It lets us enjoy ourselves without any worry.I truly hope all of you who had a bad experience will give it another shot. It is a truly great place for anyone, families with kids, or even with out kids. There is something there for everyone at every age. Just be thorough and get all your cost and expenses figured out before hand so there is no need to have to juggle your finances.

If you are travelling to California to visit Disneyland from a long way off (Aust, NZ, UK etc ) you are investing thousands of $$$$, so you should do a little research online to get the most out of your trip, which may be a  once in a lifetime  visit.Several disgruntled posters here complain about expensive food at Disneyland, long queues for rides, and even the Fast Pass system! While there is some truth to these complaints, there are several excellent Disney websites (not run by the Disney Corp) where you can get plenty of tips to avoid these problems. We just visited from NZ, bought a 6 day Park Hopper pass for not much more than a 3 day pass   it worked out about $65 NZ a day for each of our family of four to visit Disneyland   which is pretty good value for the level of entertainment we enjoyed.We took our own lunches and snacks most days   saved $$$   and ate dinner outside the parkWe learnt how to use the Fastpass system, which will save you ever having to wait in giant queues   if you learn how to use it PROPERLY   most visitors don't seem to bother.To give you an idea: we visited during Spring Break, one of the busiest times of the year, and only ever waited longer than 20 minutes ONCE in 6 days. We averaged about 20 rides a day.In addition to rides, we saw a couple of great parades, fantastic fireworks every night and a Broadway worthy stage show ( Aladdin ) twice.We literally had a magic time   three weeks on and our kids are still talking and writing stories about their trip everyday   well worth the expense IMHO   but please, please, please, do your homework   you'll enjoy your trip so much better. For starters check out the forums on disboards.com, miceage.com, mouseplanet.com   and even the tips here on the Disneyland page

Disneyland.... 2 Adults 3 kids(15,13,11).... pay for 5 Adults...At around $1200 Australian dollars for 3 days. Value for money not there, even with California Land(half open, waste!!). My wife and I were here 21 years ago... not much has changed.... Food was REALLY expensive... better off leaving the park and returning later. Considering that the place is full nearly all year round, the food is so over priced. Disney must be struggling these days.... Not only they slug you $150 $175 US (3 days) then expect you to spend around $30US a day to drink & feed yourself...I call it a RIP OFF!! kids enjoyed it... But went hungry until we got out of the theme park... and ate just over the road at a third of the price.

Our family had fun here! My best advice would be to purchase a copy of The Unofficial Guide to Disneyland and follow its plan(s) on what to see and ride. The book is very accurate and trustworthy, we saved a lot of headache trying to figure out what to see and do.

Disneyland was an absolutely magical experience. It has been 15 years since I have been there and it was not only magical for my 5 year old princess but for me as well. The cast members (staff) are all incredibly helpful....they have made a few changes but all for the best. They have photo passes now that captured so many amazing parts of our vacation as well as fast passes to make line ups a thing of the past for the most part. Food was reasonable inside the park unlike other amusement parks (legoland was unbelievable). I have been back for 36 hours and I am already starting to plan my next trip down. Best part, I have a head start because Disneyland cost a lot less than I had expected!

We arrived at Disneyland on April 9. We stayed at the Grand Californian which is pretty pricey, however we have stayed there several times in the past so we knew that part. What we did not know was that Disney has now offered their annual pass for the locals more affordable. You can pay for it over a 12 month period of time. The place was packed out miserably. The sewer system at both parks had issues so you were constantly smelling sewer. Their were 80 minutes wait for the popular rides. The Resort was filthy and the service bad. We have been to Disneyland about 6 different times and will not go back. Disneyland has made changes that are not acceptable.

Our high school band traveled to Disneyland in California to attend a workshop with Disney personnel. They also performed on one of the stages in Disney. Although the chaperones were not able to go backstage with the group for the workshop, we were able to go to help them for their performance. It was a very well run program and the kids really enjoyed the experience. Not only will they remember this experience, they were able to be behind the scenes at Disney which is also an experience to remember. Thanks Disney for providing this experience for kids...and the adults who accompany them.

The longest line we waited in was 30 minutes for the monorial (which had technical difficulties). Almost every line we were in was less than 15 minutes. We used the FastPasses, avoided peak times at certain locations and had a wonderful time! Only negative was getting stuck at parade time and having to go through Adventureland instead of Fantasyland, which was blocked off for the fireworks.

Fast pass appears to be a tool to minimize your wait time for some popular rides. It isn't.You can on ly have one fast pass outstanding at a time, and you uusally have to wait 40 minutes or so to be able to use it. So you really cannot use it to increase the number of rides you can enjoy.The only thing fast pass accomplishes is that it allows you to avoid standing in the line and to instead, waner in the park while you're waiting. This is a huge benefit    for Disnay. People do not spend money while standing in line for an hour. But those who wander in the park with nothing to do for an hour will almost invariably spend money, at the very least for high priced snacks.this isn't to say you shouldn't use fast pass. Just do so with your eyes open and recognizing what it's really about: a tool to switch your wait time to a situation likely to induce you to spend more.

This park was very expensive for a few big rides. i do not reccomend you come, but you if you do you should ride the california screamin. The Embassy suites was a great hotel down the street that i recomend you stay at if you are from out of town.

I just visited Disney with my sister and her 2 daughters, 5 and 7. We had a wonderful time. It is amazing that Disneyland still has it after all these years. The kids AND the grownups were dazzled.Get there early as possible and get to the rides you want the most in the morning. The crowds got heaviest after noon. Long waits go with the territory so don't go if you can't handle waiting for an hour or more for the most popular rides. Get FAST PASSES when you can...the system is a bit confusing at first but you'll figure it out. Look for the wait times for the rides posted on the signs to decide if you want to get the FAST PASS.
