It did rain in the mornings while we were there, but by noon it cleared up. And the rain scares the SoCal residents away so the wait in lines are non existent.On Friday morning there was a wait of 3 hours for Nemo. We came back at around 7 PM during the Parade of Dreams and the CM said the wait for Nemo was a 1 2 hour. We got in line and an hour and a half later we made it to the front. We were disappointed that the CM had lied to us about the wait time (they weren't even close and she was specifically advertising to everyone it was ONLY a 1 2 hour; a lot of us in line were discussing how off she was) but despite that it was still shorter than 3 hours.Besides Nemo the longest wait we had was a 1 2 hour at Indy. We walked on Pirates, Haunted, Splash, Star Tours, Tower of Terror, Monsters Inc, Muppets, Tiki, Tough to be a Bug, Pooh... and had about a 20 min wait at Screamin, Soarin, Thunder, Mr. Toads, and Storybookland. We used fast passes on Space and Roger Rabbits and walked right even though they had a 40 min stand by wait.In Feb 2006 we had visited as well about a one week apart difference from this year's visit. We noticed that Tiki and Small World had several problems with not functioning birds and dolls. Small World was closed (to fix the boats since they are supposedly having a problem with the population being heavier than before) but when we sat through Tiki all of the birds, tikis, flowers were functioning perfectly.The crowds were so wonderful, I couldn't complain. Although it seemed for no reason they closed Tom Sawyers Island, even though only in the mornings was a drizzle. They also randomly closed the Tea Cups, Alice, Thunder because of the rain but reopened later in the evening on Fri.We ended up walking from our hotel on Disney Way to the park. It saved us $12 a day (that's $36 for 3 days) and was very close to the walk from the tram to your car in the Mickey & Friends parking structure (especially if you parked way in the back). We also saved money by eating one meal in the park (lunch since its cheapest) and then just munching on a churro   popcorn   cotton candy until dinner. (Have breakfast out of the park, as well as dinner  will save you loads of cash) Although churros   popcorn   cotton candy is about $3 each. Soda runs from anywhere from $2.69 (for a cup) or $2.75 (for a bottle).We really did have a magical time, and Nemo was cute. If I really had to wait 3 hours to see it then I don't know how I would feel about it. The loading unloading time for that ride is ridiculous. We also got to do the new  Pirates  since it reopened with Capt. Jack Sparrow and Barbosa. We enjoyed the Davy Jones smoke screen but was kind of annoyed at how much they mentioned Capt. Jack throughout the ride. It was a bit overkill and I missed the original. Although the last shot of Capt. Jack with the treasure was fitting and better than those two pirates pushing the treasure up the lift.Some more tips for you travelers:  If you are going to eat at Blue Bayou (inside Pirates of the Caribbean) make reservations a couple of weeks before you visit the park through Disney Dining. Also if you are on a budget make reservations before 3:50 PM as their lunch prices are 1 2 of their dinner prices. Lunch prices range from $21 35. If you want waterside seating ask when you check in, it could be anywhere from 15 45 mins extra to sit by the water. The restaurant has wonderful atmosphere, good food, and excellent service.  Another great place to get more bang for your buck is Rancho Del Zocalo located in Frontierland. They have huge portions that you can split with someone. Also good food.  If you are on a budget for Disney souvenirs you can get some pressed pennys from 50 cents to $1 in the Crystal Arcade on Main Street. You can also go to the Disney Outlet store located on Harbor past the 91 where they still carry current items inside Disneyland for normal (instead of exuberant prices)  During the parade   fireworks do rides that have abnormally long lines like Nemo. You'll only have to wait 1 4 to 1 2 the time when something isn't going on.Anyways I  3 Disneyland and had another wonderful time. Hopefully next time I'll finally be able to see the fireworks (they were canceled due to winds) and eat Plaza Inn's Character Breakfast!

This place is MAGIC and will always bring the kid out of you!. I'm glad my family had a good time! Everyone knows what to do at amusement parks so I will tell you the good and bad about disney.Pro: buy your tickets online or at your hotel map out your day for efficiency ALWAYS do fast track for families with small kids, get the switch pass (fast pass for families) eat ice cream, dole whips, corn dog, popcorn, bacon cheeseburger go to mattahorn, Pirate and nemo rides early.  bring your own drinks, strollers and appropriate clothing for the weather.Cons buying your tickets at the park...you'll be sorry waiting in those lines. security check points are small and time consuming, need more staff. souvenirs and food are overpriced adults falling in line for town town and fantasy land rides (these rides are meant for little kids, not ages 18 30.although its the happiest place on earth, you'll see crying kids not getting what they want, pissed off parents yelling at each other or their kids, people upset with each other due to crowding and long lines. LOL! we're all human!

I've been to Disneyland probably more than anyone I know. I'm 21 and I've been at least over 100 times. I've seen this place change many times. I love it. Here are some tips:1. Go in off season. Basically anytime schools are in session. Also weekdays are much better than weekends. People worry that rides will be closed, but usually it's only 1 2 rides. There are usually only 5 minute waits. 2. Fast Pass is good. People underestimate the power of the fast pass, but it really can save you time. Get Fast pass to the major rides like Indiana Jones and then while you wait go on another ride or eat. 3. Everything is expensive at Disneyland. If you are on a budget you can go outside of Disneyland and eat. Research the area and you'll find that just 2 3 blocks away there are affordable food. 3.a. Bring your own water and snacks. Drinking fountains are sparse and you will get thirsty in line. I always bring 10 bottles. 4. Backpack, Backpack, Backpack. Not a fanny pack, backpack. Where are you going to put 10 bottles of water?5. Shows are an opportunity to get on the rides. There are going to be hundreds of people lining up to watch the shows, which means hundreds of people are out of line. 6. Get your tickets online. You can just walk up to the gate with your printout. If you plan things right you can get on every single ride in one day.

We just returned from a vacation at Disneyland. My son is 3 1 2 years old and thought the whole place was magical. Every one of the staff members at the park was very polite and helpful. It truly did seem like the happiest place on earth! All the characters were super friendly and interactive to the children and seemed to seek them out to give extra attention. I definitely recommend the  Breakfast with Minnie  at the Plaza Inn. It was a little expensive but definitely worth it. It is a buffet breakfast and during your time there the characters come to your table and interact with the kids. There were about 10 characters there the entire time. I think with a younger child who still thinks the characters are real it is great. Maybe not as fun with older kids. We also ate at the Blue Lagoon inside the Pirates of the Caribbean ride. It was ok. I thought it would have been more interesting... but still a nice experience. On Tom Sawyers Pirate Island, definitely ask the boat driver when the next time Jack Sparrow will be appearing is. We just missed him and my son was so insistent on seeing him that we had to wait another 45 minutes to see him again. We did not do any of the coasters and mostly stuck to the kid stuff due to my son   s age. The roller coaster in Toon Town was great though... just right for a toddler preschooler. Definitely take the time to go through Mickey Mouse's house. The only let in 6 pp at a time into see Mickey so you have nice one on one with him with out 50 other kids around. We also went to California Adventure. Not that great to be honest. The Magic of Disneyland definitely does not carry over. The staff is not as attentive or happy. The rides were not as clean. And something was definitely missing in the ambiance. It seemed plain and bland in comparison. At Disneyland every detail was looked into. The decor was very consistent and detailed. There were employees everywhere to help and characters to interact with. We ended up leaving the California Adventure after 1 hour to go back to Disneyland. I also recommend the parade. My son loved it! Several of the characters came up to him and shook his hand of patted him on the head during the parade which made him feel special! There was also a sword in the stone ceremony which we happened to wander upon that was pretty cool. The Jedi training camp looked neat too but my son was too young to participate. All in all it was a magical experience for my son who was the perfect age for his first trip. I think next time we will come back when he is a bit older and I am sure his experience will be all together different!

We recently returned from our family trip to Disneyland. While Disney does a good job of creating a fantasy vacation, they definitely know what it means to have a monopoly. We stayed in the Grand Californian and found it impossible to have even a simple snack without spending at least $10 per person. I was shocked when a small individual serving size orange juice bottle was over $4 !! A breakfast sandwich in nearby downtown Disney (most likely with every vendor owned by Disney) was $9. Yes, that's right $9!! What you would pay $2 for in the outside world was more than 4x's the price.Here is the problem. You get to the park, your family is having fun enjoying the rides and then someone mentions they are hungry. You have to feed them, no choice, and Disney knows it. Our small family of 3 averaged more than $100 daily just to have simple meals and drinks while in the park.Then someone wants a sweatshirt, or a toy, or a souvenier of some type. You can't say no! This is a once in a lifetime experience, so you sucumb and allow Disney to violate you again and again and again. All the while, you are trying to justify paying 4 to 5 x's what anything should in reality cost by telling yourself you are at the happiest place on earth and making memories.Heed this warning. If you go to Disneyland or Disney World or anything Disney. Pack a back pack with food each day before you go. Have everyone agree you won't eat more than 1 meal in the park while you are there. Have everyone agree you won't purchase more than one souvenier and that the price of that item will not exceed x $'s.While the Grand Californian is a beautiful hotel, it is there to rob you of your hard earned cash just like the rest of the Disney regime. If you have a spouse who wants to stay in this hotel, insist that it be for only a single night and then stay at a nearby non Disney hotel for a fraction of the cost.Frankly, I would have really enjoyed the 4 days we spent in the theme parks if I didn't have to work for the next 2 months just to pay for the experience. Don't be another Disney victim. Let common sense prevail and you will make great memories and be able to look proudly at your bank account when it is all over.

We recently returned froma trip to Disneyland. It was our first overseas trip as a family and I did plenty of research before going. I was very concerned about our two year old who is very timid in new situations. I read the Frommers Guide to Disneyland which was excellent and planned exactly the attractions we wanted to see and in which order. Although we didn't stick to it completely it was great to have the plan their when it got to the end of the day. Our two year old was terrified the first day of Disneyland. Luckily it was a shorter day as the park closed at 8.00pm. He only went on two rides which was the carousel and the Casey Jnr train. He cried the whole time on the carousel, but was only slightly terrified on the train. We decided not to push and just let him sit and soak up the surrounds while the other kids went on the ride. We kept our distance from the characters with him and talked to him about what as happeneing around him. The second day we had a Princess breakfast in Ariels Gotto. WE had to go before the park opened, which was great for him to experience it without the crowds. He was much more relaxed the second day and actually got out of the stroller in the Bug's Land area and played around. He became willing to look at the characters from a distance and even went on a ride without screaming (just one mind you). We came home around 1 and went back around 3.30 for the fireworks and got back after midnight. After having come home you would think that the two year old loved the whole trip. he talks about it all the time and says he wants to go back when he sees the video and photos. I am really glad we didn't push him because he go so much out of it even if it didn't seem like much to us at the time. That would be my advice to anyone, let the kids guide you in what their experience is. Whilst it costs heaps of money they will get alot more out of it at their own pace. We loved it and would visit again anytime!

First of all, Disneyland was wonderful. The people were great. That said, DO NOT USE EXPEDIA TO PURCHASE PARK TICKETS. I had invited my entire family to a reunion at Disneyland and purchased a package thru Disney Travel which included hotel and park tickets. This was a 3 day trip and a couple of family members could not make the 3 days we were there but at the last minute were able to come 1 day before us and were to join us for 2 days but leave early . I purchased online park tickets for them through Expedia, two 2 day park hoppers. I coud not find anyplace during the purchase to enter any name other than mine, but since I was purchasing two tickets, I thought that was the way it had to be: obviously Expedia does not think 1 person will be using both tickets, so the name must not matter. I printed the tickets and gave them to my nephew to use.He and his girlfriend arrived at Disneyland but when they got to the gate, the person at the booth said they had no record of the tickets and sent him to customer service, who also could not find a record of the tickets.. My nephew had them call me directly. They said were still unable to locate a record of the tickets, going from the booth to customer service and then waiting while they explained the situation and then called me took aver an hour, added to the time they had to stand in line. I told Disney to just charge my credit card for another set of tickets and that I would work it out with Expedia but the people at Disney said they would honor the tickets, but asked that I bring a copy of my purchase information when I came the next day. They also kindly gave my nephew a coupld of Fast Passes to make up for the inconvienience. The next day I stood in line with my newphew and took the paperwork to the booth, where they once again searched and told me there was absolutely no record of the ticket I purchased from Expedia on file, but that again, they would honor it since obviously I had purchased it: I had all of the paperwork with me. Once again they gave us a couple Fast Passes and appologies. They were great. Here's when the problem comes up, I contact Expedia when I get home: they say the entire probelm was that MY NAME WAS ON BOTH TICKETS SO ONLY I COULD USE BOTH TICKETS. And yes, that's what it says on the fine print in back. They insist that that was the only problem with the tickets and refused to even address the issue that no one at Disneyland could even locate a record of the tickets. Together the kids and I lost 4 hours of time standing in extra lines trying to get the problem resolved, I asked for a partial refund, Expedia offered me a discount on a future trip. NO THANKS. I will not be using them again. So this is just a caution   Disneyland was great, Expedia may ruin your dream vacation.

When visiting the  happiest place on earth  on Christmas day like we did, prepare to get there before the park opens (especially if you haven't purchased your tickets in advance), be ready to wait in long lines all day and deal with the huge crowds. For first time visitors like ourselves, it was really helpful to do a little research to find out the park's layout and decide which rides to go to. I picked up  The Unofficial Guide to Disneyland 2008  from Borders to prepare for the trip. I found the book quite helpful because it reviewed each ride and offered different plans depending on how many days you plan to stay & whether or not you're traveling with or without kids. Our party (7 adults, 1 teen)decided to do the clockwise rotation starting with Adventureland and ending with Tomorrowland. I highly recommend the following rides: Indiana Jones Adventure (great 1st ride; gets your blood pumping), Big Thunder Mountain Railroad (pretty tame coaster, but still lots of fun), Matterhorn Bobsleds (love this ride! try to ride it at night), Buzz Lightyear Astro Blasters (you get a free picture showing your score that you can send to your email), and ofcourse, Space Mountain (a truly thrill filled ride.) One of the newer rides, Finding Nemo Submarine Voyage, was a major let down. It wasn't worth the 1.5 hour (the longest line at the park) wait at all, unless you want to take a break & have a quick nap because that's what a couple of us ended up doing. It was quite boring... we pretty much just watched scenes from the movie. If you see a long line, skip this ride! Pirates of the Carribean and Haunted Mansion was okay, but is mainly for little kids. Autopia is another one that you can skip. Do it if you have little ones who want to experience what it's like to drive a car, smell gasoline fumes & be stuck in traffic. If you're up for wise cracking humor and a laid back, relaxing ride, check out the Jungle Cruise. There are a lot of eating places inside the park. Our group snacked on churros & McD's french fries earlier in the day. For lunch, we ate at Hungry Bear Restaurant in Critter Country. They serve burgers, chicken & salads. The burgers & salads were reasonably priced and quite tasty. We finally left the park at around 11 pm... extremely exhausted, with aching feet, but with huge smiles on our faces nonetheless. The castle and main street is breathtakingly beautiful during this time of the year. Unfortunately, the fireworks show was canceled due to the weather (it was clear, but windy). Don't forget to stop and grab some souvenirs. There were a bunch of good deals especially with it being Christmas & all. I'm glad we spent Christmas day at Disney... It was very crowded, but it's worth experiencing once. Just be patient, keep a good sense of humor, and wear comfortable shoes. For our next visit, we plan to stay longer and visit during the slow season.

Before I start my review, I must admit that I was aware that Disney would be crowded around Christmas but never did I imagine sold out crowds with 2 hour waits for rides, fast passes sold out by noon, and herds of some of the rudest people I have ever been around.....and a MERRRRRRRY CHRISTMAS TO YOU TOO!Ok, so my family and I have been to Disney several times but never during the Christmas season. We decided to surprise our kids with a trip to Disneyland and left Christmas morning. We stayed for 5 days and 4 of the 5 days were sold out. We averaged 4 rides a day. UGH. My kids begged to just go back to the hotel and swim. I couldnt blame them. Disney is magical and it is the best theme park anywhere. I will never be able to take that away HOWEVER, if you go, DO NOT go during this time of year. It was a waste of 656. for park hoppers. Every single day, fast passes were sold out by noon. We preferred to stay late as we seemed to get more bang for our buck between 10 and midnight so, it really stunk that we couldnt get fast passes later in the day when we arrived.The parades were fantastic as usual but we didnt get to see many characters, and I dont blame them for not wanting to come out to the rude mobs of parents pushing their kids in front of others to get their pictures taken with them.All in all, I would NOT recommend that people go to Disneyland during Christmas. It is simply not a good value.Wait until mid Jan or early February to go if you want to ride a lot of rides and not have your heals ran over by strollers. True, you do give up warm weather, but I would take no lines over hot sunshine anyday.Still love Disneyland, DO NOT LOVE DISNEYLAND DURING CHRISTMAS. It would be nice if Disney could somehow figure out a way to control crowds. BUT then they wouldnt be making as much money, which is what it really is all about for the Disney corp.

Having been born, raised, and lived in Southern California for most of my life, Disneyland was an institution visited regularly. This year, my daughter is approaching her 7th birthday, so we decided to take her to Disneyland for a Christmas gift. Once the decision for the gift was made, we had to decide on the day. December 26th!!! We were told by many that the park would not be as crowded as a few days past Christmas. They were DEAD wrong!!!We arrived at the park @ 10am only an hour and a half past it's opening time. The main parking lot was already full and we were directed to overflow parking. This provided us with a half mile brisk morning walk before we could even get to the ticket booths and purchase tickets. After plopping down $500 to get the family in to the park, we were promptly greeted with a crowd size of such magnitude I couldn't believe it. I have never seen so many people in one place at one time. Many of the people that (cough, cough) inadvertenetly bumped in to us were SoCal locals. One nice lady attempted to run my mother in law down with her stoller and when asked to be more careful, politely responded with  F*** you!  And a Merry Chistmas to you too! The most polite people we found were the ones who didn't even live near the park. We met a nice Seattle family, who like us, we quite astonished at the attitudes of those around us.So, we spent a total of 6.5 hours in the park. The little ones were so tired of standing in lines that they got to ride on 3 rides each. The big kids (myself included, wink wink) were able to make it on to 5 rides. Is it worth what we spent? I say NO! In fact, my wife and I agree on one thing, if we never see Disneyland again, neither of us will shed one tiny tear.Maybe Disney ought to take some business advice from some much smaller businesses like Snow Summit and the likes. Sell only enough tickets to make money and still allow your guests a great day! Until that day, this family will never set foot back in the  Happiest Place on Earth  and boy is that a subjective statement.

We just got back from 2 days at the Disneyland Resort. We had a great time (our best Disneyland trip ever) because of two things:1) We went the week before Christmas (Dec 17th & 18) and the parks were almost empty. The only ride we waited longer then 15 minutes for was the Finding Nemo submarine ride (which was new), otherwise we almost walked right on to every ride. 2) Bob Sehlinger's book  The Unofficial Guide to Disneyland . Even though I had been to Disneyland a half dozen times before (but not since DCA had opened) this book gave me a  plan of attack  months before our visit. The touring plans in the back are awesome. If you follow Bob's advice you'll save yourself time waiting in lines and bypass unnecessary rides or attractions (unless you really want to see them). I was able to pick up a copy of the book at my local library, so check there before you buy it.

We spent a day at Disneyland at the beginning of December. It was raining, so the crowds weren't too big.When we arrived at 8am for park opening, we went straight to the Finding Nemo Submarines, as I'd heard about the long lines. We got there about 5 minutes after the park opened, and we had to wait almost an hour to get on. The ride itself is fun and cute, but nothing spectacular. The parts of the ride featuring Nemo and company are clearly on videoscreens, and it sort of ruins the illusion of the ride. I enjoyed it, but I wouldn't wait for hours to go on this ride.We then went on the Buzz Lightyear ride. We walked right onto this ride, as there was no lineup. It was quite fun, and the fact that you get to use lasers and shoot targets makes it more fun than your average dark ride. We walked over to New Orleans Square next. What a beautiful area to walk through, especially at Christmastime. It's so nice there. We went on Pirates of the Caribbean, which is always a classic. They've changed it a bit since I've last been, adding Jack Sparrow and a few elements from the movie. The only downside about the ride is that it is so dark, pictures don't turn out.We went to the Indiana Jones Ride, which I'd done previously at Disneyland Tokyo. It was exactly the same, but its a pretty fun ride. Even though there was no wait to get on the ride, you have to walk forever through the queue to get to the ride. It probably takes 7 8 minutes just to get from the entrance to the ride.We then went to the Enchanted Tiki Hut. Having been to Disney in Florida, Tokyo, and California previous to this visit, I'd never been to the Tiki Hut. So I was determined to finally go. We grabbed a Dole Whip(best stuff on earth, IMO), and went in. What a crazy show. Singing birds, singing flowers, singing Tiki Poles. I really am not sure if I enjoyed it or not, but considering it's one of the oldest attractions, I suppose I was amused.We went to the Haunted Mansion to do their holiday version of the ride, featuring the Nightmare before Christmas. I must say, I didn't enjoy this nearly as much as the normal ride. I found the theming to be forced, and it didn't really fit in. I'd much rather go when the normal ride is operating. We went to Critter Country and went on the Pooh ride. It was a bit anti climatic, but children would really enjoy it.We then went over and did It's a Small World. Do they ever do it up for Christmas! I don't think I've ever seen that many lights in one place before. It's a sight to behold, even if you don't go on the ride.Once we got in the boat, we needed to sit crosslegged, as it had been raining and they hadn't cleared the water out of the boats. The ride itself is cute. They change it for Christmas, and parts of the ride use Christmas songs instead. I must say I find it rather ironic that all the children of the world (representing their cultures) come together to sing Christian Holiday songs. It's cute, but ironic.After this, we went and staked out a good spot to watch the fireworks. We got a spot to stand halfway between the castle and the Walt Mickey statue. It was amazing. We had such a good view. It's amazing how many people push and shove to try and steal your spot, even though we waited for a while and they showed up later. I was also shocked to see how many people thought it was acceptable to use umbrellas during the fireworks, blocking the view of people behind them. Anyways, the fireworks were stunning, as always. Really well done. Unfortunately they couldn't do Tinkerbell or the snowfall due to the rain, but it was still a brilliant fireworks show.After the fireworks we headed to the back of the castle and went on Snow Whites Scary Adventures, which was rather dull. The same can be said for Peter Pans Flight. Both of those rides are meant for little kids. We were pretty tired by 11pm, and decided to call it a day, having been on all the major rides by this time. We did have a really good day, and went on some great rides. I would recommend taking 2 days to visit Disneyland (3 if you go to California Adventure as well), in order to pace yourself and enjoy your time. We did one long 15 hour day, and if the crowds were so small (due to the rain), we wouldn't have been able to fit in nearly as much as we did.

My family went there on 22 & 29 Nov 2007, this is our first time visiting a Disneyland and we had a wonderful fun time there! As 22 Nov 2007 was the Thanksgiving Day, so the park was filled with people and yet it didn't spoil our mood for fun, also we just landed on that day morning after 18 hours flight!We bought the 2 Day Park Hopper Tickets and and we think it is worth the money! If it is a off peck season, 2 days should be ok, otherwise 3 days will be good! Highly recommended to everyone!

Lovely. Gorgeous decorations and lights. The fireworks show not to be beat. We worked really hard to get near the  snow  and it turned out to be bubbles. Was neat, but not my six yr old said  It's just bubbles!  They played Christmas music throughout the show and it really was magical. Now we loved the Nightmare before Christmas theme at the Haunted Mansion, but we go often enough that it was a treat for something different.Didn't make it on a Small World for holiday, so can't review that, sorry. Tips for Disneyland that worked for us:*Bring a change of clothes and warm clothes! Especially in winter months where it can be warm day cold night. Rent a locker on main street. Worth every penny. Bring a cheap rain slicker for Grizzly Run Splash mountain in cold months!!!!They sell for $10 there, $1 at home!*Eat in Downtown Disney for lunch or dinner. Have a cocktail, and relax, get waited on. It won't cost you much more, and compared to my experience in the park the food service is better.*Use single rider passes!!!! If you can and you don't mind riding alone. My husband got to ride the coaster at CA Adventure over and over again. Loved it. He was a happy man.*Mickey's house ~ we had no idea, but if you meander through there, you see some neat stuff. Then you get to take pictures with Mickey! We did it late evening with no wait. *Learn everything you can about Fastpass. Use it!*Get a photo pass when you arrive. Take pictures when you are still fresh and then whenever you see the photograpers. Buy expensive, but worth it, pictures on line when you get home.

We had two full days in Disneyland with our 5 year old and could have spent a week there. So much to see and do. Visiting during the day is a different experience to night.Particular favourites include Rocky Mountain Railroad; Blue Bayou Restaurant in New Orleans Square (make sure you reserve a table earlier in the day!); Toontown; Tom Sawyer Island and Fantasyland. Lots of characters around for photos.The new Nemo ride is over rated and we waited an hour in the line up.Tips: get there early to enjoy the day with little ones   you can hire a stroller but they cost. Head to the back of the lot ie Toontown and Fantasyland and get the small rides over and done with.We noticed that Sunday was a popular day however the fireworks are on Sunday evening. The Tuesday we also visited was quiet compared to the Sunday. Also we went in Autumn out of school holidays. The most we waited for a ride was the hour for Nemo but most rides were 10 15 mins.Lots of fun and with a small child, the original and the best theme park when compared to California Adventure.

This is first trip vacation we had that required an airplane transportation since my son was born on April 2003, it also the fist time for him. We spent 2 days ( 11 09 11 10) at Disneyland and the California adventure. The waiting time was not bad for most rides before noon time. Fortunately, my son is over 42  tall, otherwise, he would not have been able to even get on some of the good rides. The worst waiting time were the  Finding nemo   and   Matterhorn Bobsleds  , and both rides do not acepted the  Fastpass  method. Remember, a stroller is a must if your child is under five years old. At the end of the day, those little legs just give up. My overall experience in the park was excellent, I had more fun than my kid. The only negative I found is that was not enough cartoon characters through out the park. We need to pay $24 per adult and $12 for child per child for  breakfast with Minnie   ( besure to make reservevation ahead of time ) at the Plaza Inn for photo opt. Even then, no Mickey was to be found.

We were here with our two kids   ages 5 & 8 and 6 adults of varying ages. We just got home   EXHAUSTED, but what a terrific time. Disney does everything to such an amazing level, that it is hard to even write down what was so great. The Great: Fantasmic, Space Mountain, Indiana Jones, the Characters, Fireworks, the parade, the customer serviceThe Good: the new parking structure is terrific and the trams run like clockwork, the photopasses, the 3 D shows, the Princess Fantasy Faire, Big Thunder Mountain RailroadThe so so (are okay, but could live without waiting in line for): Nemo   the lines were ridiculous and we waited for the kids sake, but it wasn't worth an hour and a half in line, they need a fast pass for it. Food   too expensive for families to eat here and only one designated picnicking area. Characters walking off with a line up of kids waiting and no notice   this got really irritating. My kids loved meeting the characters, but Mickey, Donald, Ariel and Tigger all disappeared without a trace and never returned. They should post signs with times or something. The bad: There wasn't really anything bad. The line ups while we were there were good. We rarely used the fast passes because we didn't have to. My husband and I were disappointed with the Nightmare before Christmas theme in the haunted mansion   we prefer the original version and as we aren't big fans of the movie, didn't really love it. The kids had a terrific time, the adults had a terrific time and the weather was reasonable. It was great.

What can I say 2007 is Disney's year of Dreams and thats just what it is Magical. As a 35 year old just walking through the gates onto Main Street made me feel like a kid all over againThere is no getting away from it you will get tired but if you visit on a weekend please please please do try and stay in the park for the fireworks thay are sensational and well worth waiting for, keep an eye open for tinkerbell flying through the sky.As we are from London my Husband and I have visited Disneyland Paris........... No comparision. Anaheim wins hands down.

If you are planning a visit to Disneyland and can travel in October I would recommend it. My wife and 2 kids were there the last week of October and it was great. We never waited longer than 20 minutes for any ride. All 4 of us had never been to Disneyland and didn't know what to expect. I thought overall it was great! The Tower of Terror in Disney's California Adventure was the best ride with Soaring over California a close second. In Disneyland we really liked the Indinana Jones ride and the Matterhorn Bobsleds. The only ride we didn't ride was the Nemo submarine, because that line was long all day and night. One cavet to the off season is the parks have limited hours and they only have fireworks on the weekends. But if you can live with that then I felt it was the perfect time to go.

Our trip to Disneyland Resort was awesome! We took our family with kids ages 4, 8, and 10, my mother and my sister and her husband. We stayed in the Disneyland Hotel which turned out to be very convenient and the closest of all the 3 Disney Hotels. The room was nice and clean but we wish there were some sort of complimentary breakfast offered. We flew in to LAX airport which I think was a small mistake given the extra travel time and hassle of 3 kids in such a large airport. Next time I'll book to John Wayne. We were there a total of 7 days in the parks and I think it was a bit too long. 3 5 would have been plenty, but we managed to see and try nearly every attraction Disneyland Resort had to offer! California Adventure side was tougher with the 4 year old since most the rides have a 40  height requirement. We were really impressed with the food everywhere EXCEPT the Blue Bayou restaraunt which is inside the pirates attraction. It was way over priced for the quality of food and service we experienced, plus the kids found the selections too wierd for their typical kid tastes. I highly recommend getting a food plan, we had the 5 day plan and it was enough for all 7 days. It was really nice to have the special character meals and Goofy's Kitchen was fantastic.Overall we absolutely loved it and were all so sad to say goodbye.

Had a better than expected time with my 2.5 year old girl, infant son, wife and my parents.My daughter loved the Princess Faire   attended the events almost daily, wearing her Snow White dress. My intention was to go for 5th birthday when she'll be able to remember more but it turned out to be a perfect age   she really was excited to see the princesses! Other highlights for her (and us):The daily Sylvania parade   watched the afternoon show which was just fine. The evening show was too late for the little ones.Fantasyland   she loved the outside rides mostly   teacup ride, Dumbo, Casey Jr train, and carousel especially.PhotoPass   for $60 you get a CD of unlimited photos taken by photographers stationed at the main landmarks (eg, Cinderella Castle, with various characters).Bug's Land in California Adventures   about the only place for a toddler   only spent 1 hour here but would spend more time next trip if I had known more about it.. Tame but fun and cute rides for young ones, similar to Fantasy LandNegatives:Food is mediocre   ate at French Cafe, and twice at Plaza Inn.Food was so so at the French Cafe. First time we went to Plaza Inn the fried chicken was very good. Second time we went it tasted slightly strange   like some chemical in the oil that shouldn't be there. The dinner buffet at Storyteller Cafe was decent but also not worth a special trip if you are staying off park.Ariel's Grotto Princess Breakfast   table visits by the princesses were very brief (maybe 1 2 minutes each); Arielle and Belle were very nice but the people playing Snow White and Cinderella were superficially friendly only   not as nice as the ones at the Princess Faire. Food was bad too. My advice   save your money and wait in line to meet them for free at the Princess Faire.Mixed Opinions:Staying off resort   we stayed at the Marriott Suites Garden Grove, a very nice place and much less expensive than the resort hotels. However we had to rely on the ART shuttle which was often very crowded especially in the evening. It was quite miserable luuging a stroller, while standing with a crying infant shoulder to shoulder after a long day at the park in this bus. I definitely recommend staying walking distance away at one of the hotels on Harbor Blvd or stay at a hotel with its own private shuttle.Disneyland Express   pick up at the airport was flawless however we scheduled a pick up back to the airport but it did not come   we waited for over 1 2 hour and ended up hiring a limo to bring us to John Wayne airport for $45. Ended up losing our pre paid fare which was non refundable. If traveling with at least 4 adults, I would definitely hire a minivan taxi next time   fare is cheaper anyways and they don't require infant or toddler seats, which I did not realize.Hope this helps!

Before leaving we were nervous about how our 2 year old and 4 year old would go at Disneyland. But to our surprise they loved it, the long hot days and continuous lines also did not seem to bother them as they knew another ride was at the front. Our 4 year old is tall for her age and was allowed to ride Splash Mountain, the Rapids and California Soarin (at California Adventure Land). She had a ball. We were impressed with the amount of fruit available within the park and would not hesitate in taking young kids to the park again. There was so much for them to do that they forgot about being cranky even when arrived at 10:00am an left at 10:00pm. What a place   dreams do come true.

And welcome we always felt indeed. Every cast member we encountered was so happy and helpful that you just felt you had stepped into another world of magic and wonderment and utter happiness. My husband is not what you'd call a softie of any sort and you could not get the goofy smile off his face the entire trip. This was our 2nd trip to Disneyland in 2 yrs. and this time we took our 4 yr. old with us as he was finally big enough to do the rides and understand the whole concept. I cannot say enough about how great it was to see his face when we saw a character or when Mickey hugged him... PRICELESS! At that age they still think Mickey IS mickey, not just some guy in a suit. Anyways, we knew cramming everything into a few days with a 4 yr. old would just be maddness, so we booked off 11 days over Oct. 3   13 and got a 6 day park hopper pass that included 2 early entry days. Originally we had planned to do 5 day hoppers, but realized that upon our early arrival into Anaheim, the kids would be going mad with anticipation (and us too) to get into the park. Lucky for us we bought our tickets through GetAwayTodayVacations.com and it was easy enough to upgrade our tickets to a 6 day at only $10 extra per person!! That said, we arrived at the park at 3 p.m. the first day and it was nice and quiet with little or no lines at all   sweet. Our son could not get enough of Pirates of the Caribbean and is just as much a fantatic as I am now. We used our first early entry the next day (Thur.) arriving in the park 1 hr. (9 a.m.) earlier than regular park guests. Now early entry has it's good and bad points as we were to find out. The bad was that only Fantasyland and Tommorrowland are open, so even though there are fewer people in the park, they are all crammed into 2 lands, making the lines just as long as any other day. Now the good (or great) thing about early entry was that this is the time that ALL the characters are out and about on mainstreet signing autographs and doing pictures with the kiddies. It was a great time and we got some hilarious video footage of our little guy screaming at the top of his lungs  HI GOOFY !!! Over and over again. For our 2nd early entry day we opted out of the rides and just spent time seeing the characters again or getting the ones we had missed. We were only in the park on the Sat. during Gay Days, but it was extremely busy, almost unbearable, thus we spent alot of time seeing the shows and shopping in Downtown Disney etc. and saved the rides for a weekday. Our last trip to Disneyland was 2005 during the same weekend and we never noticed any large groups for Gay Days at that time, we hardly noticed that the event was even going on. Must be more popular now and I think we'd avoid the first week in October in the future. On that Sat. evening the fireworks were cancelled and the park was so crowed that you almost couldn't walk, felt a little dangerous and I think that's the real reason they were cancelled. Cast Members began dispersing the crowds in different directions but ultimately towards the main gate exits. The park wasn't closing, but they were definitely encouraging people to leave without saying so. We ended up leaving being unable to stand the stampede like crowd and headed for our hotel across the street. Laying in bed around 10:30, we could hear the fireworks going off. I guess once the park thinned out, they were back on. Owell. On our last night in the park (Fri. Oct. 12), I had booked VIP tickets to Fantasmic! and that was absolutely one of the highlights of our trip. Tickets weren't cheap, being $60 for adults and $50 for children, but you receive roped off front row riverside seating and a special box of treats for each person which contained chocolate dipped strawberries, mickey rice crispy treats and other various items, plus any drink you wished for. The VIP cast member was very courteous and was constantly at our service, it was a wonderful experience. I would definitely do that again. All in all, we were happy to have the 6 day pass as we split the days up and did other things in between like Universal, Seaworld, the San Diego Zoo and a day at Venice Beach. I don't think we would have changed a thing and it was nice that at the end the kids and adults had all had enough and were looking forward to home instead of 'wishing we had just 1 more day'. It was a magical and adventurous vacation and we all can't wait to go back. Our 1 and only disappointment would have to be that Indiana Jones was closed during our entire stay for what they said was a scheduled refurbishment.... but funny enough that refurbishment was never mentioned in the Disney website in advance, and I checked it religiously beforehand. As other reviewers stated, the Finding Nemo Submarine Ride ALWAYS had at least a 90 min. line and I just couldn't force myself to wait it out, so we missed it this trip   owell.Everyone should see Disneyland at least twice in their lifetime, once as a child and then as an adult seeing it through your child's eyes. Nothing could have been more special or memorable.

3 day park hopper. We got started around 5pm on Saturday night..We stayed in the Disneyland hotel, so we strolled through Downtown Disney to reach the park entrance. You could also pick up the monorail back at the beginning of downtown disney, which deposits you directly inside of the park..If you choose the monorail route, from the hotel, it's about a 5 minute walk.. If you walk through Downtown DIsney in it's entirety(which is awesome in itself), it's about 20 minutes..Regardless how you enter the parks, they will stop and search your bags and carryied items before you can enter. This did not seem to slow down the line at all however. We were there during the Gay Days of Anaheim (try explaining that one to the kids), so it was extra busy, but surprisingly no painfully long lines. average of around 40 mins, with the longest being about an hour and 10 mins for splash mountain.. As the night wore on however, the lines were shorter and shorter.. One disappointment was the Nemo Submarine ride.. THAT line was always at around 2 hours, no matter what time we went back to check on it.. so we had to pass on that ride altogether.. Oh well, maybe next time. 'It's a Small World', is a wonderful ride. don't miss this one. It takes you through these incredibly intricately designed sets that represent all the countries in the world.. WIth music and decor to match each nation.. It's a sight to see.Most all the rides here (peter pan, alice and wonderland, etc.. etc.. ) are all sit down 'tram' type rides.. They wheel you through these VERY elaborate, and very clever sets. Like the Peter pan one, you are 'flying' high above the city streets below, and encounter all sorts of visual treats and sounds along the way.These were all great rides, if you have younger kids in tow. Splash Mountain was awesome.. Also the Matterhorn Bobsled ride was a BLAST.. seriously was yelling out loud during that one. Of course the standard things, like a merry go round, the Haunted house (which was awesomely done up in a Nightmare Before Christmas theme.)   and Space Mountain, which is a one of a kind unique roller coaster.Food was easy to find throughout the park, with plenty of places to stop and eat, weather you want a sit down restaurant, or a quick grab and go popcorn, ice cream, or turkey legs (weird) at one of the many stands.Plenty of disney shops sprinkled all over the place too.. So you'll never miss a chance to get those mouse ears, or that snow globe, or just aout anything else you can think of (even saw them selling camcorder tapes   genius!)The Disney train is a great escape   you can just hop on at one station, and ride it through the whole park, and depart at another station, which would dump you into a different section of the park. It encircles the very outer edge of the park. Nice if you like to rest the feet for a bit.. It's also a ride in itself as it takes you through some really really neat sets and special areas that you can only see through this train ride. I do have to say that all of these attractions were very very well put together. very thoughtful, and detailed, and just flat out clever and inspiring. Everything really did 'wow' you. Take a look at the phots, to see the detail i am talking about. Really very impressive.there was stuff for EVERYONE.. from the littlest ones, a ride though Pooh Corner, to the toddlers, with the Buzz Lightyear shoot em up laser ride, to just about anything else for any age 'kid' you can think of.Do NOT miss getting yourself a prime time seat for the parade down main street. This happens every day. check the times, when you go. they literally rope of massive sections of the park, and it seems like all time stands still, to make way for this parade. the parade was AWESOME. all the characters. Little Mermaid, Lion King, Alice, Peter Pan, all the princesses.. the whole gang. they each had their own massively themed 'float;, which was VERY neat to see. The detail was just amazing. Street dancers, music, the whole lot of it.. it was the highlight of our day. It goes for about a half hour, and finishes off with the Mickey, Minnie and Donald Duck float. Don't miss it. Also, the fireworks. AWESOME show ! they were canceled the first night we were there due to 'higher than expected winds'....... blah..... but they were a go on the second night, and man were they a sight. LOUD, and long. they had some actually shooting horizontally OFF of the top of Matterhorn mountain (where the bobsled ride is).. Don't miss this show, if you can help it. (i think it's only Friday through Sunday, but verify once you are there). We got stuck up at the Space mountain section of the park, when the show started.. but not a problem.. Sat right down on the ground and had a great view. man were they loud though, and our 3 year old didn't have that great a time.. i had to actually move indoors after a while because he was getting scared.The park is HUGE. don't expect to cram it all in on one day. You can't, and will just feel frustrated. However, i could see where one would have just about enough, after 3 or maybe 4 full days there. Bathrooms were plentiful and suprisingly clean, large and nice. Really !Angry : did not see ONE, repeat, not ONE Disney character wandering the streets. If we didn't stop to watch the parade, we would have not even known Mickey, or Pluto or any of them existed. I felt bad for all these kids lugging around these big autographs books waiting for a photo opp, and a signature. Hey, i know, it's a BIG park, maybe we just werent in the right place at the right time.. but seriously, we did not see one character the entire day.Another negative: was the complete absolute lack of signage. Anywhere. If you did not have your park map with you, there was no way you'd know where to go.. Make sure you pick up 2, maybe THREE copies of the map when you enter the park, as within short order the one you keep having to repeatedly unfold and examine will wear very quickly! Why not simple posts with arrows pointing in different directions, with the 'main' area attractions on the arrows ? at least SOME general idea.. i couldnt believe it. but maybe thats by design.. maybe you are just supposed to 'lose' yourself in the wonder and magic of disneyland.. hey, you know what ? that works too.

Disneyland was everything we hoped for plus more. All kids dream of going to Disneyland & it should be every parent's dream to take their kids there. It's hard to know who loved it more the kids or the big kids (parents)...!!! We stayed at Ho Jo's & intended to go back to the hotel for a rest during the afternoon before heading back but the rest never happened   we were having way too much fun to rest.We got 3 day hopper passes & used them to the max. We just loved everything about Disneyland   the parade of dreams is excellent, the fireworks are sensational well worth staying till 9.30 for and the rides and attractions are second to none.The Downtown Disney district is lots of fun as well   great shops and places to eat.If you can, take your kids to Disneyland. It is a great family place and creates memories that will last forever.

We have a 17 month and a 3 year old. We got off a cruise and since we are down here we decided to do Disneyland. We had a good time but some of the theme rides are very scary for toddlers. We went on Snow White and the Seven Dwarf and most of the story they showed the witch. The scary music didn't help to. We decide to go to Toontown and went on the Roger Rabbit ride. This one also showed alot of the weasel and had scary music. California side was better for the kids with the shows and outdoor rides. My son 3 loved the water ride and bugs amusement park. I would suggest going to Disneyland when the kids are older 8 and up. My son is now scared to sleep by himself. Just a warnning to all parents thinking of taking there toddler.

We have visited Disneyland twice in the last year. The first time we went for 6 days and it wasn't till the 6th day did we start to feel bored. Our kids however would still be there if they had had their own way. It is an experience and one that every kid should have. The staff were great, helpful and very friendly. The Princesses were amazing. They and I mean all of them Belle, Cinderella the works were all very approachable and welcoming to our two daughters ages 3 and 5. Alice as in wonderland was fantastic. The young lady playing Alice one day was even so kind to stop and talk to our girls on their own. WQe had waited a short time to speak to her and did but it was near the end of her alloted meet and greet time she left in a hurry. Later that day however there she was and she spent a good 10 minutes just talking and later walking us over to the Teacups ride. We had such a good time that we decided to return again. Our kids love the place and so do Mom and Dad. A must do....By the way we went during the 3rd week of September and the crowds weren't bad at all. Not like I remembered from my visit as a kid during a summer one year.

I was able to stay two nights at the Hilton Anaheim and after getting the Park Hopper Ticket i went to California Adventure and the Disneyland Resort.Major Note: At California Adventure, if you are a single rider, utilize the single rider lines Available at:Hollywood Terror HotelSoarin over CaliforniaCalifornia Scremin'MaliboomerYou basically get to the front of line and wait only momentarily versus waiting for 40 mins for a specific ride, make sure to get single rider ticket from employee at front of each ride.At Disneyland Resort there is only one ride with a single rider line. That is Splash Mountain, you basically go to the single rider line via the exit and walk all the way down until you get to the boarding area.Food is quite expensive versus eating across the street on Harbor Blvd.Expect this, a 3 day Park Hopper TIcket was at $164 (but i purchased the ticket at Hilton Anaheim) At the park the price would be $179. So, check with your hotel to ensure they sell the tickets because you get a price break at the hotel versus at the park.Transportation was good, the Anaheim Resort Transit operates different routes depending on what hotel you stay at.Hilton Anaheim happens to be Route E. You arrive in the big loading bus area. Very well marked so you can't miss where your bus boards at, runs every 15 mins.Be sure to get the 1,2 or 3 day transit pass as well which enables you unlimited rides versus $3.00 one way on the bus.All in all, was a great time and experience.Oh yeah other tips:Fireworks start at 9:25 p.m. each night.The California Adventure Park opens at 9am and closes at 9pm.Disneyland opens at 9am and closes at midnight right now.(With 3 day or more park hopper ticket you can get in at 7am to DIsneyland)

We had 3 day park hopper tickets   and put them to good use! Our stay was during the last week of July and we were expecting the park to be heaving with huge queues. We were pleasantly surprised!We arrived at the park at about 7.15 on Monday morning to use some of the early entry our hopper tickets offered. We headed over to Tomorrowland to go on Space Mountain but it wasn't running yet (there seemed to be quite a lot of technical problems with the ride while we were there   one time we were on the ride and instead of turning right at the beginning by the control room, we turned left into a behind the scenes area. We all had to get out, go back to the loading area and wait for them to re set it. We did get to ride a few times over our trip though) so we headed over to Fantasyland while it was quiet as they're the kind of rides which are nice to see, but you don't want to queue a long time for them! (Being a family group of 4 with the youngest aged 21!) We got on a few rides before regular opening which was a good bonus. We expected the queues to steadily build after opening, but we never really encountered any queues more than about 30 minutes throughout the whole 3 days. We put this down to 2 factors: a) good planning and use of fastpasses (more on that in a minute!) and b) Finding Nemo. Everyone seemed to be queueing for Nemo, leaving other major attractions with much reduced waiting times. We had decided that we weren't going to bother queueing for half the day for one attraction when we could experience so much more by avoiding it! We got on loads! This was as well as taking a few hours out in the afternoon to return to our hotel for a swim and a break before heading back for dinner and the evening refreshed. I would really recommend this, as by around 3 the park is really busy and you'll be getting increasingly hot and bothered and so won't really enjoy the rest of the day   plus it's a nice rest for your feet!!We really enjoyed this year being the 'Year of a Million Dreams'   especially as we got lucky every day! On the first day we came across Dream Cast Members giving out limited edition million dreams Mickey Ears, and on the second and third days we got Dream Fastpasses! These were great as not only could we use our fastpasses when a queue was huge, but unlike regular fastpasses it meant that we didn't have to zig zag back and forward to get the fastpass and then go back and use it. These really made our day!We enjoyed Fantasmic again, although some people keep trying to push you of the way which is really annoying!I love Disneyland and am such a big kid! It's just a shame it's so far away!

Our family of nine enjoyed Disneyland this week! One of the best parts of the vacation for me was that I could bring my 7 pound Pallion. He stayed at Disneyland Kennel Club. The cost is $20 a day which is from 7:30 am until 12:30 am. You should bring your dogs favorite toy(s) & blanket. I also brought his food dish and his food, but they have food & food dishes on site. You will need to come in from time to time to take your dog out for a potty break (they do not do this for you). The area for the break is pretty big, but it is not grassy. I was very happy to be able to bring my dog to Disneyland! Check online or directly on what shot paperwork they need from your vet.As stated before wear comfortable shoes, use LOTS of sunscreen, stay hydrated. I used a hip pack, it worked great. The large store in downtown Disney sells very nice hip packs for $16.00. They are large and have 3 zippered comparments. I bought one for our next visit.

okay i went to disneyland in los angeles and i have to say it really sucked the lines were very long the staff were really rude and they only have 2 thrill rides which are California screamin and space mountain which are very ordinary for thrill rides aside from that i would say it is a good place for little young girls since it doesnt have much for others,anyway if you are thinking of going to a thrillpark in Los Angeles go to Knotts berry farm or six flags they are heaps better

July, 2007Disneyland was absolutely wonderful. You truly need at least 2 days to get through the entire park. We walked through the park the first day and then next day decided what we wanted to do. Go early in the A.M or late in the evening to ride popular attractions or you may have to wait 1hour or longer. I encourage anyone to get the fast pass then go back to ride with your time on our ticket. This helps with you not having to stand in line and missing most of the other attractions. I also suggest that you go for breakfast in the morning with the disney characters. My son is 20 and he thought that it was not going to be fun due to his age. There were ALL AGES present and we had a great time and took many pictures with the characters. Definitely will return again!!!

Visited Disneyland and Calif. Adventure July 19 22 07Stayed at Disney Hotel. Inside hotel is very average, nothing really magical but the resort grounds are extremely beautiful! Large sliding window was nice. Bonita tower is peaceful with the sound of waterfalls! It is quite a walk through downtown Disney to Disneyland, hard at the end of the day. The monterail is also a bit of a walk but it's the 1 2 hour wait in line that got me! Not as convenient as I thought. kids had a hard time with all the walking and waiting. Hotel is geared around making money! Everything costs money! Disappointed in that, felt like they were piliging guests for every penny. The obiance was wonderful and I liked the fact that you were in the resort the whole time and away from streets and daily life. It felt like we were away!

We've been to both CA Adventure (less crowded, clean, adult friendly & comfortable) and Disneyland (obnoxiously crowded and less magic). One visit, we just went to CA Adventure. There is not that much to see here and you could see everything in 1 2 day, if you go on a quiet day (Mon   Wed) with no crowds and really enjoy yourself. They now have an electric parade (which was not there when we visited last) so it appears that they are trying to do more things for this park and it does have a great look and feel to it. It's beautiful and picturesque.Then there is Disneyland. Unfortunately, we went on a very hot day and didn't get into the park until after 10:30am. Big mistake! Be there by 9:00am and get on the rides you want to see ASAP! Go for the sub ride because after 10   the lines get too long and it's not worth all that. We did not see this ride because of that.Bring water and a hat, we were dehydrated in no time and had a sun headache. Lack of poor planning on our part. The sun hit us hard within 2 hours (1:00pm) we were dehydrated and cranky. So we left. The lines get even LONGER after noon.Stay close to the park and leave between 1:00 4:00pm to refresh and eat. Felt that the food was overpriced for what you get but even the restaurants directly outside the park are overpriced, so be careful. We ended up spending $40 in an IHOP so be careful.Don't visit on holiday weeks. If you do   get there early, leave the crowds and heat around 1. Return around 5ish when the sun is going down, things cools off and people get off lines to eat dinner or leave. Go on rides during the parade (only if you've seen the parade, it's really fantastic!)We found all of CA to be very nice but Disneyland was a misrepresentation. It appears a lot of the LA crowd does not like tourists and can be quite rude. CA, to us, tends to be one of the friendliest states to visit but only if you avoid the LA area ;o) ha sorry, folks but the fact remains   most are obnoxious drivers and they drive their strollers, like they're cars ;o) The crowd control in Disney could be improved greatly and make a nice Disney experience. Unfortunately, they need to keep this LITTLE park  less accessible  for the safety of all paying customers.On a nice note   We truly enjoyed their parade and their fireworks display. This made it worth the cost. We would return, but only on a less crowded week. Put a limit on entrance on busy weeks for safety and comfort reasons. Disney, listen up for safety reasons! There is no need for greed   when it comes to a safe, family vaca.

Ok, so there are a lot of ways to spend money at Disneyland. We can't argue that point, but we are so impressed at their customer service. They have employee's who take pictures at various venues in the park, but they are also happy to take group photos with personal cameras (some places won't do that). The employees are almost always friendly. They are having their year of a million dreams and in a 4 day period, we had 2 people get fast passes to all fast pass rides and the whole group got  year of a million dreams  mouse ears. When my husband went to buy 2 disposible cameras for the kids, the Disney clerk went to an adjacent store in Disneyland to get a 2 pack that only the other store sold because it was quite a bit less expensive per camera (this was completely spontaneous, we did not ask for a less expensive option). There were so many examples of good customer service that I can't even name them all here. I don't mind paying extra when I feel a little pampered, and Disney certainly does that! It is a very busy place during the travel season, but there is so much going on (parades, shows, rides, food, etc.) that you can almost always find something fun to do. We got 4 day passes and almost wish we would have gotten 5 day passes.

My Husband and I decided to spend the weekend in Disneyland the June 29th 2007 one. We went on Pirates right away and we enjoyed the few additions to the right that adds Davey Jones, Jack, and Barbossa. We also noticed new additions to the Haunted House and it was so nice to see it be not the Nightmare before Christmas. With food we got lucky and got a last minute reservation at Blue Bayou where we got to keep the menu as a souvenir and the service was excellent along with the food. Hands down Blue Bayou is the best eatery there. Everyone was efficent and friendly and of course we will be back again!

This is where the wife and I decided to spend our Honeymoon. We bought a 2 Day Park Hopper pass and went on a Thursday and Saturday.We were in Disneyland and did all of Tomorrowland (excluding Nemo b c it was too long of a wait) and the Matterhorn within 3 hours. Went over to CA Adventure, finished it, and went back to Disneyland and finished Adventureland. So for our seceond day we just wandered around and had the rest of the park fininshed within ~5 hours (on a Sat). Went to see the line for Nemo during the parade, and it was still a 2 hour wait. Passed on that.The park is always clean, and yes the food is expensive, but so is every other theme park in CA. The cast were very helpful and ever made us feel unwelcome. They helped us find all the pressed penny machines when I couldn't see them.The longest waits (other then Nemo) were for Splash Mountain, Indiana Jones, Space Mountain, and the Matterhorn. All extending to 1 hour each, but if you fast pass it, there's no problem at all.I love the rides, and will continue to do so. Some of them are simple, but nostalgic. It funny seeing the little kids look at a grown man get excited to go on Mr. Toads Wild Ride, Alice in Wonderland, or Pinnochio. However, when you are a kid at heart, this is the perfect place to be.

RIDE SPOLIERS:My family and I visited DLR on June 24 and 25 2007, specifically to get a couple last days in before our annual passes expire (can't afford the ~$1000 to renew) and to catch Finding Nemo. While the first day we saw lines of over three hours (which was unacceptable to all of us) we  lucked out  and waited for 90 minutes starting at 9:30pm that first night. Let me just say that while I felt the ride was technically interesting, the storyline was weak, not heartwarming in any way like the movie (when Nemo was found it seemed like no big deal to ol' dad), and it left us parents and our normally sappy kids (13, 10 and 6) like they'd been ripped off. My inclination was to tell everyone in line on the second day to pass on it... but how do you do that without breaking some hearts? They wouldn't have gotten out of line anyway AND I'd be a total Scrooge (no Disney pun intended). So what I'll do is just say that I don't think the ride's worth more than a fifteen minute wait if you're a local, or an hour wait if you're a tourist from out of town, IMHO.

In my lifetime I have been to the Disneyland Resort 2 times. The first time I went it was like a dream, everything worked out perfectly! We stayted in The Fairfield Inn the first time we went. Our expectations were surpassed from the cleanliness of the room to the kindness and knowledgable aspects of the staff. Our second trip was not as pleasant. We stayed in the Tropicana Inn which had a nice pool but the beaver looking staff or the quite large woman who arranged our trip stole our second free day pass to Universal Studios. The room had a unusual smell and the pool an unusual taste. There were many homeless people lining the streets outside the hotels and Disneyland's front enterance asking tourists for money. This was about our 10th visit over many years. The happiest place on earth is still a marvel. The rides and attractions functioned well (which wasn't always the case in the past). However, the employees no longer seemed to as happy to see us and give us that  Happiest place on earth  feeliing. We were at Anaheim from May 15 19, we bought the 3 day hopper pass and I'm not embarrassed to say we don't have any kids. It was just my b f and I acting like kids. Its not long before your trying on the goofy hat or the mouse ears and its the one place you can wear them without ridicule. Everybody, regardless of big or small had their kid mindset on. I was concerned that in the land of kids there would be tempers lost all over the park but it must be the fairy dust they sprinkle on you when you arrive because it really is a pretty happy place.My only suggestion to others booking and staying around Anaheim is to check to see what ART transport route your hotel is on because we were on route J and even though it said the bus came every 20 minutes, on each trip we waited somewhere between 35 to 45 minutes. I have been to Disneyland 10 12 times in my lifetime and I have had a blast each and everytime. My family and I have visited Disneyland 3 times in the past few years with the latest visit being August 2006. Each time it just gets more wonderful. But we were disappointed in the Princess area near ToonTown. Perhaps we expected the wrong thing but it sounded to us like the Princesses were just walking around the area, but instead there was a line (longer than others) to meet one Princess and get your picture taken with her. My husband and I don't have children, but we thought we would still at least have fun. That can't be farther from the truth. I have visited Disneyland nearly 15 times over the course of my life and have never had a complaint until now. We have been to Disney World five times, and love it. Since we were in CA on Spring Break, decided to try Disneyland. We were very disappointed for a number of reasons. The park is not kept up like Disney World  peeling paint and lack of manicured landscaping, as well as at least 5 closed attractions. Our family of 5 just returned from a much anticpated and planned trip to DisneyLand. We stayed at a hotel across the street (and down 2 blocks) and even though the convenience of walking instead of waiting for a shuttle was nice, I have to admit walking back after 12 14 hours on our feet became a bit much. First tip   wear comfortable shoes!!! That said, here are a few other pointers that saved some time, money, and added some extra fun.If you stay in a hotel around the park and do not have your own car, you should know that there are no grocery type stores outside of convenience stores that are almost as overpriced as the park itself. Buying water in the park is a last resort at over $2.50 for a 20oz bottle. Even at the convenience stores bottled water can be pricey (at $2 per bottle) but we brought a couple of small drinkable bottles and a gallon jug (at $1.69 at the convenience Market on the corner). We packed the gallon jug in the locker and refilled it throughout the day. We tried filling the bottles with the drinking fountains, but we were unable to tolerate the taste. You can also pre buy and pack the individual water flavor cystals, they mask the taste of the water in a pinch. Food in the park is pricey (figure $8 10 per adult per meal for counter service) and generally portions are small. We pre bought crackers and snack packs and packed them into a back pack. This was a lifesaver when feeding 3 boys!! They search bags before entering, but aren't concerned about small snacks. We packed them in their own suitcase and had an empty suitcase at the end of our stay for souveniers!The lockers on the outside are on the left hand side of Disney main entrance. $7 for small (fits about 1 backpack) and $10 for large (we fit 2 backpacks and gallon jug in it). They are a good value and you can use them all day. We kept snacks, water, and warmer clothes for nighttime. Well worth not having to walk back to the hotel!Pin Trading! This is something I had read nothing about prior to going to Disney and was a highlight of our trip! Our 8 and 13 year old had as much fun with it as they did on the rides! Disney lanyards are worn by many tourists to hold hopper passes, fastpass tickets, photocards, etc. Disney Pins (with characters etc.) can be bought to place onto lanyards at many of the stores in Disney, California, and Downtown Disney. A fun twist to purchasing the pins is to trade them! Many Cast Members (Disney staff members) also wear lanyards with pins on them and must trade their pins if you ask them (they seem to enjoy it too)! We bought packs of 4 pins ($22 for 4 is a good deal since most are $6.95 and up) and let the boys trade at will! Our boys had a blast looking for cast members with pins, trading them, and learning about the different kinds of pins. Many of the pins that the cast members wear are exclusive and cannot be bought in stores. It was alot of fun and the boys came home with stories to go with their souveniers.Fast Passes this is a great way to save some time, but there are rules and helpful hints for using them. Once you get one, you have to wait 2 hours before you can get another one. We ended up just waiting if the line was less than 30 40 minutes and using the fast passes for longer lines). Also, if you are going during a busy time of year (we went during Spring Break) many of the attractions go through their available fast passes early in the day. For example, one day we went to get one for Space Mountain at 9:30am and our time to return was 3:30pm, by 10:30am the return was 6:20pm! Also, not all of the busy rides have fast passes. Matterhorn, Pirates of the Caribbean, and Haunted Mansion, don't have fast pass and can get really long lines. Best to hit them first thing in the morning (before 9:30am) and you will get through the lines pretty quick.Pictures   There are professional photographers on site all of the time. You will see them throughout both parks. They will take pictures of your family, with the characters, posed with a backdrop, etc. When you get the first picture, they give you a little card. Whenever you get more pictures you just hand the card to the photographer and all the pictures are registered to that card. The card can hold up to 200 300 photos I was told. You can look at them and purchase at Disney or look at them online when you get home. We didn't take advantage of this since we learned about it on the last day, but thought it was a nice service.The bottom line is  expect to spend alot of $, stand in long lines for long periods of time, and collapse into your hotel bed at the end of the night utterly overstimulated and exhausted, but with a huge smile on your face and the  it's a small world after all  tune running endlessly through your head. Hope this helps..... a little preparation makes a huge difference!

We traveled from Indiana to go to Disney.The park is much smaller than Florida. The lines are unbearable. No kidding   we waited 90 mins then got out of line at Space Mountain.The food is extreemly expensive and the workers could care less.The park is so over crowed that literally had people bumping into us all day long.The ride lines are unbelievable. Attaractions are simply awefullGet ready to spend $600 $700 for a family of four for two days (without hotel).Disney is a once in a lifetime visit. What a blast! Make sure to go to the busiest rides first thing when you arrive in the am so the wait isnt long. Bring water and snacks with you, things inside the park are spendy. Buy souvenirs at the end of the day, otherwise you will have to carry, sometimes heavy bags around. Make sure to get a schedule of parades and shows either at the gate or your motel. Everyone seems willing! Make sure to take a few breaks during the day, especially with little children.

There are certain places that you must visit whilst you occupy your time on the mortal coil...and Disneyland should be on everyone's list. I first visited in '92, revisited in '95 and '97 and after a decade's break, conquered again in 06. California Adventure was open this time so I had something else to view.Whether you are 5 or 55, if you cannot have an enjoyable day out at Disneyland, you are extremely hard to please. Regardless of your preconceived ideas about Disney (either good or bad), go with an open mind, a good night's rest beforehand and a solid pair of walking shoes.Take a minimum of 2 days to do justice to both parks and you must purchase a 2 day hopper pass, so you can enter and exit both parks on the same day. California Adventure is the newest park and one that you can fairly comfortably do in half a day. Much quieter than it's older brother, the waiting times are much smaller on the attractions and rides and much less frenetic. You should do the rollercoaster at Paradise Pier, the Ferris wheel at the same location is pretty good and the white water rapids are tremendous but it would be considered a crime if you don't do  Soarin Over California . An absolutely outstanding ride even for someone like myself who has a phobia about heights.A good array of souvenir shops and food outlets are scattered throughout the park ensuring a pleasant few hours.But the real highlight is Disneyland itself. I won't go on about each attraction....people have written entire books on that...but for what it's worth, the must do list should include Space Mountain, The Matterhorn (if it's open), Submarine Lagoon (if it's open), Splash Mountain, Big Thunder Mountain (if it's open), Indiana Jones and Pirates of the Caribbean. (As you may have gathered a few of the rides that I have enjoyed before were closed during my most recent visit!!!).The shopping is superb, and the food is acceptable. Punters who criticise the standard of the food should accept that you don't go to Disneyland for a culinary experience. Similarly don't whinge about the clothing souvenirs being expensive. Guess what? It's Disneyland not a factory outlet. Accept it for what it is and you'll have a terrific time.....everytime!!!

After going to Disneyworld several time in the last 15 years, Disneyland was a little bit of a let down. My family and I just spent 4 days at Disneyland and DCA. We had never been to DCA before, so it was new experience. I have to say that the park is somewhat disappointing compared to Disneyland.
