The only thing I enjoyed was the Dole Whips.What's with the wait time at some of the food service areas. I waited 20   minutes to get a coffee at the bakery near the front of DCA. My wife waited over 30 minutes to get McDonalds food at Burger Invasion in DCA (the only affordable option at DLR). There was only 1 person working the cash registers at lunch time!!!!!! Disneyland ParkOne of the few places in the world where everyone must visit at least once in their life time. And yet whether you   re 5 years old or 50 years old, you can be sure that there is something for everyone. From thrill seeking rollercoaster   s (your choice of indoors, outdoors, or both!) to peaceful steamboats cruising the lake, Disneyland, despite its age, keeps bringing people of all ages, from all around the world back year after year after year. The larger and older of the 2 parks in Anaheim, the Disneyland Park is not showing any signs of deterioration with rides very regularly refurbished and the kept grounds meticulously spotless by the ever cheerful staff to make it the happiest place in the universe. Lookout for the new Finding Nemo submarine ride, opening in the 1st half of 2007; another sign that Disney is keeping up with the times.Specific rides that are a must see are Indiana Jones (an adventure in a desert truck through dark caves), Space Mountain (the fast paced, futuristic indoor rollercoaster) and Pirates of the Caribbean (a journey through a pirates life including the battle scenes to the drunk scenes). Note that these rides are not for the faint hearted     look for the warnings at the front of each ride.For a comprehensive tour around the Disneyland park, take a trip from Main Street on the Disneyland Railroad train, with regular stops on the way as you steam roll around the entire circumference of the park. Also, take a fun and leisurely cruise down a lake filled with exotic animals on the Jungle Cruise where you may see more than 1 kind of elephant along the way.A trip to Disneyland is not complete without watching the world famous street parade along main street. Once staff begin to rope off the pedestrian area, take a seat in a prime position along the roadside for an energetic Disney themed parade with all of the classic characters. During the festive season, Santa even makes a visit.At 9:30pm every night of the year (weather permitting), Disney treats guests to a fireworks extravaganza, which can be seen and heard from all around Anaheim. A shooting star initiates a colourful array as Mickey   s face lights up the sky. If staying in a hotel, the best view is arguably in a room at the Hilton Anaheim, with a front row seat of the action from the comfort of your own room.Disneyland is infamous of long lines which can be particularly tedious in the hot summer months or cold winter months. To minimise this waiting time, come to Disneyland during a weekday, some time during the school term. With Disneyland Bonus Hopper passes (3 days or longer), 1 of those days allows the ticket holder entry to the park 1 hour before the general public. This is particularly handy if you already know which rides you want to jump on first, to avoid the long lines. Note however that not all of the park and rides are open during the early entry hour; notable most of the western side of the park. In addition to this, Disney has introduced a new system called a FastPass, where guests have the ability on selected rides to swipe their entry passes and receive a reservation card. So all they have to do is come back at the time printed on the card and go right to the front of the queue. Excellent if you   re about to go for lunch so you can come back and jump straight onto the ride.Disneyland is not a cheap last minute attraction, where some people from Australia plan to see Disneyland first, while the rest of the USA is second in importance. Being a one of a kind, Disney rarely offers discounted tickets to distributors, so the most chance of scoring cheaper tickets is through Disney direct. They currently have adults at kid   s prices if you visit in the 1st half of this year, where a 3 day bonus hopper pass is currently $US129 per adult (far cheaper than what a Sydney travel agent can offer). If you buy the tickets only 31 days before your visit, you   ll also save on the international courier needed to send tickets to Australia (you   ll be able to pick them up there   Will Call). Note that a 1 day pass will not enable entry into both parks on the same day. Ideally to visit both parks comprehensively, depending on the number of people in the park, a 3 day bonus hopper pass is ideal (one park each day, the 3rd day split between the 2). Disney   s California Adventure ParkJust a few years old, Disney   s California Adventure Park was built to resemble a mini California of fun. While smaller than its larger, older brother, DCA is for the thrill seekers, with the famous California Screamin    rollercoaster at Paradise Pier. Disney   s attempt at recreating California has not come without critics, but if in doubt, take a flying tour at Soarin    over California where you realistically take off around California   s most famous areas. This is one of the most popular rides with waiting times of over 1 hour, so do it first!Paradise Pier is a great place to grab an ice cream, as you really do feel like you   re on a carnival filled pier facing the ocean, while you watch the California Screamin    rollercoaster zoom around the circumference of huge Mickey   s face. Another unseemingly blood rushing ride is the Sun Wheel, and while guests can take the traditional ferris wheel ride, most take the swinging carriage side which freely swings toward the centre and outward of the giant wheel, of course with no seat belt restraints.It   s tough to be a bug! (A Bug   s Life) is also a must see 4D show which includes the sense of touch. This cheeky, hilarious yet slightly educational film will impress young and old.Disneyland is infamous of long lines which can be particularly tedious in the hot summer months or cold winter months. To minimise this waiting time, come to Disneyland during a weekday, some time during the school term. With Disneyland Bonus Hopper passes (3 days or longer), 1 of those days allows the ticket holder entry to the park 1 hour before the general public. This is particularly handy if you already know which rides you want to jump on first, to avoid the long lines. Note however that not all of the park and rides are open during the early entry hour; notable most of the western side of the park. In addition to this, Disney has introduced a new system called a FastPass, where guests have the ability on selected rides to swipe their entry passes and receive a reservation card. So all they have to do is come back at the time printed on the card and go right to the front of the queue. Excellent if you   re about to go for lunch so you can come back and jump straight onto the ride.While Disneyland Park has its world famous Disney character themed street parade, California Adventure Park has a more interactive parade aimed at the pre teen kids, with characters such as Buzz light year and the blue giant from Monsters Inc. Once staff begin to rope off the pedestrian area, take a seat in a prime position along the roadside in the Sunshine Plaza area for an energetic Dance themed parade.Disneyland is not a cheap last minute attraction, where some people from Australia plan to see Disneyland first, while the rest of the USA is second in importance. Being a one of a kind, Disney rarely offers discounted tickets to distributors, so the most chance of scoring cheaper tickets is through Disney direct. They currently have adults at kid   s prices if you visit in the 1st half of this year, where a 3 day bonus hopper pass is currently $US129 per adult (far cheaper than what a Sydney travel agent can offer). If you buy the tickets only 31 days before your visit, you   ll also save on the international courier needed to send tickets to Australia (you   ll be able to pick them up there   Will Call). Note that a 1 day pass will not enable entry into both parks on the same day. Ideally to visit both parks comprehensively, depending on the number of people in the park, a 3 day bonus hopper pass is ideal (one park each day, the 3rd day split between the 2).

It's now been just over 12 months since my husband and I travelled to the US for our 25th wedding anniversary. Part of our trip was spent in Anaheim and of course Disneyland. Ordinarily I'm not a theme park kind of girl so I was sceptical of a 3 day pass thinking how on earth could we fill in all that time at a theme park! Was I wrong !! We are both in our mid forties but we had the best time imaginable. To an Australian the whole Disneyland experience is like actually living all those old tv episodes we watched as a kid   the castle, small world, the older style rides. Then you move on to the new rides   each one bigger and better than the last and all with so much detail. Shows like Aladdin in California Land and even the street entertainment were just wonderful and waiting in line (which we didn't do all that often) was an opportunity to people watch. It was just so much fun! We were also incredibly lucky because we didn't encounter any crowd problems at all   we were there in the first week of december 2005 and had perfect weather, mild and sunny. Being the Christmas season and the 50th birthday celebrations only added to the whole feeling in the park   lots of things had been themed for the holidays and it was incredibly beautiful and festive. No one celebrates Christmas quite like they do in America and Disney is no exception! The staff at both of the Disney parks were always helpful and the grounds were wonderfully kept and extremely neat and clean. Even though we could have used the fast pass system we had no need for it (except maybe on the Saturday when the park did fill up due to the special Christmes carol parade with Dick Van Dyke) and I also can't recall any problems with rides being closed for maintenence either. Even the food was pretty good and not too expensive considering you're in a theme park! There are also lots of spots to buy souvenirs throughout the park but somehow it doesn't feel like too many! We had a terrific time and would love to travel back some day perhaps with granchildren to see their faces when those spectacular fireworks light up the sky after a wonderful day at Disneyland!!!! Don't think Disneyland is just for the kids, if you have the opportunity to visit even once you won't regret it.

We're not a very pop culture family, but I grew up with Disneyland, and when our first child turned 3 we knew we had to go see it. 11 years later, we're still going back, usually annually (we live 7 hours away by car).The key to the Disney experience is going with the Disney program. If you let go of your cynicism, embrace serendipity and wear comfortable shoes, you'll have a blast. I won't go over all the highlights, anyone can find those   but some things that really are worth doing:GO ON AN OFF DAY. I can't stress this enough. We always arrive Thursday and max out on popular rides at DL, have a blast on Friday at the less popular rides at DL and take in the shows at night, and then spend Saturday at DCA (way fewer crowds). Figure out the best schedule for you, but to ensure you have fun, spend one not busy day at DL. You won't regret taking the day off from work school!Take your teenagers on the kiddie rides (It's a Bug's Life   13yo girl   priceless photos). Preteen boy on Dumbo   same.Ride Tower of Terror with a newbie. After the first drop, tell 'em,  see, that wasn't so bad!  Heeeeeee hee hee.Save a spot by the water for Fantasmic. Bring a blanket and a book, have a member of your party bring you a snack, and chat with the people around you. You'll meet some interesting people and have a spot so spectacular for the show, you won't believe it. When they light the water on fire   WOW.Watch some of the little side shows. The garbage can guys, the cowboys in Frontierland, etc. Very entertaining, very clever.Go to Mickey's House last thing before you head out, and have your photo taken with him   staff will take a photo with your camera, you don't have to buy the Disney photo.Get to know a ride that photographs you (CA Screamin' is our favorite) and plan a goofy face for your holiday Christmastcards.Try something you think you won't like. We avoided Space Mountain for years...just didn't think we'd like it. Now it's our first stop.Hydrate. You're allowed to bring bottled water into the parks, and you should. Buy some, too. Everyone will be much happier well watered, and there are bathrooms everywhere.Take breaks. One of the best reasons to do multi day trips to the parks is that it allows you to slow down. My spouse and I discovered Downtown Disney on the last trip, and let the teen and preteen head out on their own with cell phones in hand and strict instructions on what to do if they got lost. They soldiered on, ride after ride, and Pops and I did a little Christmas shopping, had a latte, sat by some soothing fountains. Tom Sawyer's Island is another great spot for parents to rest while younger kids run around, and there's usually a band playing at New Orleans Square. Or take the train around the park to sit for a while   lots of fun!Loosen up your purse strings. You can save money by eating kids' meals and buying no souvenirs at the park, yeah, but...c'mon. Just have fun. If it bugs you to give so much cash to Walt's estate, buy some Disney stock.Favorite less popular attractions:The Enchanted Tiki RoomPetting Zoo at Big Thunder RanchMinnie's House at Toon TownHoney I Shrunk the AudienceInnoventionsThe Movie Theatre on Main St.The Mr. Lincoln ExhibitThe Train (take it all the way around   hokey fun!)Davy Crockett canoes (oh, yeah!)At DCA:The California Story (With Whoopi Goldberg)The showsThe music in the plazaHave a great time   hope to see you there!

We had 5 days at Disneyland and California Adventure with our two children   a girl aged 4 and a boy aged 6. My husband and I had visited the park in 1992 for one day. Our kids absolutely adored Disneyland and we did too. 5 days was just enough time to fully experience both Parks. Our daughter loved the characters   to her they were real. We recommend the Princess Lunch at California Adventure   the food was good, it was well organised and there were 6 beautiful princesses to meet   each one spent quite a lot of time with our kids. Our son at 6 was tall enough for every ride and he went on them all. He loved Buzz Lightyear and Indiana Jones the best. We used fast passes for the more popular rides and found that the queues for all the other rides moved really quickly. The longest wait we had was for the Peter Pan ride   20 mins. Our daughter loved the simpler rides e.g. pooh bear. Disneyland is unique in that it has the fast thrill rides for the older population and the more relaxed but equally as special rides for younger children. Having said that, every ride and attraction was special, expertly presented and enjoyable. Even in late Sept we would recommend timing your visit to Disneyland to fall on a weekday s. We spent Wed, Thur and Friday at Disneyland and then moved on to California Adventure for most of Sat and Sun, only returning to Disneyland for specific rides or the fireworks. It was almost twice as crowded on the Saturday. CA copes well with weekend crowds, we experienced minimal queues and used fast passes when there was a significant line. The food at both parks was pretty average and pricey, but who cares, the atmosphere and every thing else more than makes up for it. We appreciated the early access to the Park, Toon Town and the other little extras provided for booking with Disney Travel. Toon Town in particular gave us wonderful access to the characters with minimal queues. My husband and I will never forget our kids' true delight and happiness during their time at Disneyland and CA. As adults we were hooked as well. It's worth the long flight from Australia   it truly is the Magic Kingdom.

Just returned from Anaheim 5 days ago, a family of 4  2 boys aged 10 and 7. I did some studying of the reviews on tripadvisor and formed my own ideas. Things need to be maintained (not fixed ONCE they're broken), and crowds are going to be there if you go during vacations. If certain rides are important to you, then plan to go when they're still open, otherwise just accept it. If you can't stand the crowds, then go in off peak time. We had a superb time in later September. Nice weather, hardly any waiting, and happy people enjoying themselves. The Monorail wasn't open, nor Haunted Mansion or Matterhorn. Okay, disappointing, (the monorail is one of those things I remember from Disneyland on TV when I was a kid, so had been hoping to ride it) but plenty of other things to do, and it didn't spoil anything. When the Dreams Really Do Come True fireworks began, I felt a bit tear y, thinking that yes, I really was at Disneyland! It was a magic feeling. We got on Pirates each day we went (3), and plenty of other rides we did more than once. In the 3 days we only used Fastpass 4 times between both parks, plus one just as a souvenir! When we saw the chains for the queues when it's really busy it made us cringe at the thought. For us, it was the holiday of a lifetime  we're not prepared to fly 15 hours each way again real soon  and nothing stopped us from enjoying it. Stop whining, people, and enjoy the happiest place you can be!!

We spent three days in Disneyland during July 17 24, 2006. This was our first trip to Disneyland so I thought I would share some of our thoughts and experiences. We have three daughters Becky (just turned 6), Meggie (almost 9) and Anne (10). Anne is fearless, Meggie is more timid than her two sisters are and Becky is scared of monsters but not rides so we had a range of ages and temperaments to deal with. We bought a 3 day hopper ticket on line and ended up going on Tuesday, Thursday and Sunday. We used the early pass on Thursday. First, some general comments:1. We stayed at the Howard Johnson across the street. We were on the seventh floor, which is nice for its high ceilings. It also provides a great view of the fireworks if you are on the Disney side of the hotel. The hotel is right next to Interstate 5. I didn   t really hear it on our side but my wife did. One potential disadvantage of the seventh floor is there are large skylights, which light up the room early, making sleeping in more difficult. Wasn   t a problem for us. The air conditioning was rather loud but it keeps the room cool during 95F days. The pool is medium sized and good if you have kids that like to swim and play in the water. They also have a salt water pool that seemed a little quieter. 2. I didn   t realize that the early pass (which allows entrance at 7 AM instead of the usual 8 AM) was really only useful to get into Fantasyland since most of the other sections of the park don   t open until 8 AM. There went the idea of three Indiana Jones rides before eight. 3. I also didn   t realize that California Adventure opens at 10 AM so keep that in mind when planning your itinerary. 4. Fast passes are necessary during the summer. By carefully collecting fast passes, we never waited more than 10 minutes for any ride. You can collect several fast passes in the morning and then use them later in the afternoon because the ending time on the tickets doesn   t matter. For example, if you get a fast pass at 8:00 for Indiana Jones, it may be    good    to ride between 8:40 9:40. You can then get another fast pass at 8:41 for example Splash mountain that will be good between 10:30 11:30. At 10:31 you can get another fast pass for something else etc. You can save all these passes until you come back in the early evening and jump to the head of long lines on these rides. In addition, you can collect fast passes at California Adventure independently of the Disneyland passes since the systems are not connected. 5. If you go to Disneyland from 8 10 and then go to California Adventure when it opens at 10 AM, you can miss the worst of the crowd for 4 hours.6. We also went to Universal Studios. Bad traffic jams all the way. They don   t allow food in. $50 for an individual fast pass. We didn   t really feel like we got the same value as Disneyland although the Terminator and Shrek 3Ds were fun. We were there on a hot day so it may have influenced our perceptions.Specific comments about individual rides or shows:Disneyland1. Space mountain (Tomorrowland)We went directly to Space Mountain the first day. Big mistake for us. Our 8 year old was terrified. I also didn   t like the ride because it is entirely in the dark. I like to see what   s coming up next. We probably should have started a little slower and worked our way up to Space Mountain. We may have had an entirely different experience.2. Autopia (Tomorrowland)Fun for all the kids but not a favorite. They didn   t want to do it again. May be more fun for boys?3.  Honey, I Shrunk the Audience  (Tomorrowland)All of us enjoyed this 3D movie. Becky took off her glasses when it got too scary.4. Star Tours (Tomorrowland)All the kids but especially Becky and Meggie, fans of Star Wars, liked this ride through space. 5. Buzz Lightyear Astro Blasters (Tomorrowland)Ride around and shoot targets. Fun for all of us, especially Becky. Not scary at all.6. Enchanted Tiki Room (Adventureland)Fun for all of us. Very glad we saw this vintage show. Nice air conditioned room, nice break from the hot sun. 7. Indiana Jones Adventure (Adventureland)One of my favorite rides. Becky was scared but we still went on this twice. Fast pass strongly recommended. 8. Tarzan's Treehouse (Adventureland)Nice walkthrough up a treehouse. Becky wanted to go again.9. Big Thunder Mountain Railroad (Frontierland)Made the mistake of telling my kids about the numerous accidents and death on this ride so they refused to ride it.10. Haunted Mansion (New Orleans Square)A little dated but enjoyable for all of us. Becky absolutely insisted that we go a second time.11. Pirates of the Caribbean (New Orleans Square)Huge lines for this revamped ride. Really just a boat ride past moving displays. The detail is remarkable but we all thought it was overrated. Fortunately, we got there early and only waited 10 minutes. Would have been bummed if we waited 60 minutes for this.12. The Many Adventures of Winnie the Pooh (Critter Country)Great detail and a nice rest from the busier rides. Didn   t have any wait during the firework show.13. Splash Mountain (Critter Country)Meggie was almost hysterical on this ride because she was so afraid of the big water slide at the end. I was more scared of the second water slide in the dark. Nevertheless, we ended up going on this ride three times. Was voted in the top three rides by every one of us. Great details, good music and exciting ride, what more could you ask for. Too bad pirates of the Caribbean wasn   t more like this. A fast pass is very helpful for this ride (If you want to cut 60 minutes off your wait). In addition, you will get wet, especially if you sit in front.14. FantasylandAll rides here are good for the little ones. Nice details in the rides. The kids especially liked Mr. Toad's Wild Ride, Peter Pan's Flight, and Alice in Wonderland. Meggie went on several of these rides 2 3 times.15. Matterhorn Bobsleds (Fantasyland)Fun rollercoaster type ride that is not too scary. We all went on this at least five times. Meggie   s favorite. Short lines the first hour or two. 16. Gadget's Go Coaster (Toontown)This rollercoaster was too mild for all of us. Might be good for younger kids.17. Mickey's House and Meet MickeyHave to get Mickey   s signature. We were lucky to wait only 15 minutes but the lines can be very long.18. Roger Rabbit's Car Toon Spin (Toontown)OK ride but had higher expectations. The waiting line length is very deceiving so use fast passes if possible. None of the kids was interested to ride it a second time even though we had fast passes. 19. ToontownToontown is a great place for taking photos of the kids because there are many colorful props spread throughout, especially near Roger Rabbit's Car Toon Spin.20. FireworksGreat show this summer but be careful where you stand as the view can be blocked by trees of the castle. Slightly on the left as you face the castle is good.21. Fantasmic! (New Orleans Square  Frontierland)Great show but you must get there very early if you want to sit down. California Adventure1. Disney Animation (Hollywood Pictures Backlot)Disney animators show you how to draw some of your favorite cartoon characters. This was a lot of fun and Meggie went three times and wanted to go more times. 2. Jim Henson's Muppet*Vision 3D (Hollywood Pictures Backlot)Great 3D for the little ones. We all enjoyed this 3D show, which was not scary at all. 3. The Twilight Zone Tower of Terror (Hollywood Pictures Backlot)We hesitated to go on this ride because of all the screams we heard coming from the hotel. Anne ended up going 10 times because this was one of her favorite rides. Becky (6 years old) also went 5 times. I went twice, which was enough for me. Definitely a rush if you are afraid of heights like me. Great atmosphere. Meggie refused to try it and I think she would have found this attraction too scary. This is a Fast pass ride but we didn   t need one in the early evening while Aladdin was showing. 4. Aladdin: A Musical Spectacular (Hollywood Pictures Backlot)Excellent live musical of Aladdin. We all really enjoyed this show and it was one of my favorites. If you don   t get in line too earl, you can get in the Mezzanine waiting line. We ended up in the second row of the balcony excellent viewing fro here. Highly recommended.5. Soarin' Over California (Condor Flats)Fun for everyone and not scary. Great feeling of flying. However, once was enough for everyone.6. It's Tough To Be a Bug! (A bug   s Land)Fun 3D show. Was a little scary for Becky in some places (I noticed she took off her glasses in some parts). Recommended. All the other rides in A Bug   s Land were too tame for our kids. They would likely be just right for 2 4 year olds. 7. Grizzly River Run (The Grizzly Peak Recreational Area)Fun ride down some rapids. We went several times. You will get wet. Not scary. The fast pass machine here doesn   t seem to be connected to the others in California Adventure so you can get a fast pass here while having another. 8. California Screamin' (Paradise Pier)Great roller coaster. Anne went at least 15 times. Becky was just tall enough and she loved it. She went 6 or 7 times, a couple more times than I did. Meggie even went one time. We liked sitting in the front since we are wimps. If you ask nicely, the attendants will likely let you sit where you want. Just say Please. 9. Jumpin' Jellyfish (Paradise Pier). A frogger type ride. Was too mild for everyone. Might be good for younger kids.10. King Triton's Carousel (Paradise Pier)Typical merry go round but Meggie liked it. 11. Maliboomer (Paradise Pier)Good ride, but one of the few rides Becky couldn   t go on due to the height restriction. Was almost too intense for us and we ended up only going once, except for Anne, who went twice. Meggie also went on this. She almost got off before it started but was OK once it was going. I told her to look up instead of down and that seemed to help.12. Mulholland Madness (Paradise Pier)Good intermediate level rollercoaster. Meggie must have road this at least twenty times. Just the right level of thrill for her. You can ride without much of a wait if you enter the single rider line.13. Orange Stinger (Paradise Pier)Fun ride that is a swing that goes around and around. The kids went on this repeatedly because there was no line. Becky liked it a lot.14. Disney's Electrical Parade (California Adventure)We all enjoyed this classic lightshow. The kids thought they would be bored but it was a hit, especially with Becky. Overall, we had a great time. Three days was enough to see all we wanted to see but at a sometimes frantic pace. A 4 day pass would be nice if your kids want to collect autographs or take a more leisurely approach. Having one day on, one day off was great in that it allowed us to sleep, swim and generally recharge before hitting it hard the next day. Hope these comments are helpful!

I've been to Disneyland 7 times. Last year my best friend and I went there for the 50th anniversary. There are things to do for all ages. I recommend the Blue Bayou restaurant, located inside Pirates of the Carribean. Last year, we went for lunch and got a table right beside the water. Definatly a highlight!! Another recommendation is having dessert on the Disney Gallery balcony during the nightly preformance of Fantasmic!. You need to call EARLY because it sells out fast. It's a little pricey but worth it! The desserts are incredible and its so relaxing to sit there and enjoy the show.Even though we were there on one of the busiest days (July 14th: the actual 50th anniversary day) we found crowds weren't unbearable and the lines went by quickly. On that note, GET FAST PASSES. Saves plenty of time!! Defiantly recommend it to all ages!

I chose to fly my family of 5 from South Australia to California for a two week trip of a lifetime. I went to Disneyland when I was 8 in 1976 and I believed all children (and adults) should have that experience. It truly is magical. Our holiday was in the first two weeks of December 2005 and the weather was perfect, everyday, beautiful sunshine but cool nights. Arriving at the Howard Johnson Hotel (seperate review) in the afternoon we chose to dine in Downtown Disney before dedicating the next full day in the US to Disneyland. We loved the Rainforest Cafe but the whole atmosphere in Downtown was great, with beautiful lighting decorations for Christmas. We had 5 day hopper passes for the Disney Parks (which included California Adventure). Disneyland is just a fantastic place, it really was an experience for our whole family. We all had our favourite attractions   Space Mountain, Indiana Jones, Pirates of the Caribbean, Buzz Lightyear, Haunted Mansion to name a few. The park was spotlessly clean, the staff were polite and helpful, and the attention to detail just amazed me and the characters were great. We loved the 50th Anniversary firework display, brilliant! and the Fast Pass option really helped. There were a couple of issues though which have stopped me from giving the park a five star rating, which is no fault of anyone   1. There were just too many baby strollers which really got in way and 2. When it got crowded, it really did get beyond a usual busy crowd, it became a headache. Luckily when it did we just 'hopped' over to Cal. Advent Park next door and although I thought that was excellent too, it wasn't nearly as crowded. This holiday is something we, or our kids will not forget, with plenty of photos and video they can relive it over and over. And yes we are planning another trip there already.

Our family went to Disneyland for the first time from Aug 16 Aug 22. I wanted to compare Disneyland with Disney World where we have been five times. The big difference was the weather low 80's in the day and high 60's in the evening and no rain. It made the walk thru the parks and waiting on line a pleasant experience. Also, we stayed at the Disneyland Hotel where it was a two minute walk to the monorail which takes you directly into the park, you do not have to wait at the main entrance to get in. Unfortunately the monorail is being refurbished until mid December. Both Magic Kingdom (Disneyland) and California Adventure are not very large and the attractions are close to each other although the down size to this is that it gets very crowded in the afternoon and their is very little room to move especially in Frontier and Adventure lands. Both POTC and Splash Mountain are longer and better rides in Disneyland than their counterpart in Florida. Space Mountain is not as fast in Disneyland which was fine by me but my daughters were a little disappointed that it was not as trilling as in Florida. The one attraction that you must see as it is only in Disneyland is Indiana Jones Ride it is unbelievable. At California Adventure Soaring is the best as is California Screaming and the Grizzly Rapids ride is way better than Kali Raft ride in Animal Kingdom. I must warn you that if you want to eat at one of the table service restraunts call at least 30 days in advance. What Disneyland lacks in quantity as California Adventure is no more than a one day park it shines in quality. I would love to go back but living in Northern NJ makes the trip a long one. Even though we will visit Disney World many more times I sure hope to get to the original one more time in the near future. Trust me you will not be dissappointed. Thank you Walt your vision it was years ahead of what anyone could imagine.

Between our family members we have been to four of the Disney sites around the world and it is apparent that the Anaheim site is in need of some maintenance. We just took a trip to Anaheim and spent a day at the park. During the course of the day a lot of the rides broke down and it kind of ruined it for us. Thunder Mountain broke down twice for a couple of hours each time, Pirates of the Caribbean broke down and Indian Jones broke down just as we got to the front of the 45 minutes cue. there were a lot of unhappy people in the park.My wife complained to customer services who, to their credit, offered us complimentary tickets for both Disneyland and Disney California (next door) another day. We took them and returned the next evening. However when we got to the Disney California thrill park the California Screaming rollercoaster had broken earlier that day and was still out of order, as were a couple of the other rides.Stay as close as you can to the park to avoid having to use the local busses. Some great  family room  deals can be obtained by looking for hotels offering  Suites  like La Quinta and others across from the park. Downtown Disney is great and has several nice places to eat in the evening which are family friendly. In general the Anaheim Disney parks and Downtown are no match these days for their Florida counterparts.

For this, our 3rd visit with our kids (now 8 and 10), we used the RideMax software we've seen mentioned. What a difference it made in our visit!! No wasted time (or frayed nerves) trying to decide what to do next, only to find that by the time you arrived at the consensus ride there was a 2 hour wait...With a little advance planning, the RideMax plan was amazing. My wife and I looked at ourselves about mid morning, looked at our  plan , and were simply stunned to see we were right on schedule   and without any compulsiveness over maintaining it, either! As the day progressed, we had to make minor adjustments (Haunted House was closed for a short spell, etc.), but used the plan and tips as closely as we could.Keys to success, we think:1. Plan ahead; choose the rides attractions you want to hit and use the software to create a plan2. Don't fudge on the plan   if it says be at the gate at 7:17, be at the gate at 7:17! Don't know how they do it, but their predictions of wait times were simply UNCANNY.3. The tip about the unwritten rule allowing guests to use FastPass after the end time was correct   no CM ever questioned us when we arrived after the FastPass time window.In just one day, we saw everything we had set out to see and even had plenty of  free  time. Bear in mind we've been here 3 times, so for families making a vacation of it, you really need a lot more time.

No one does it like Disney! My teenagers loved this Park, especially the new Space Mountain and the Bobsleds. Queues moved quickly, single rider was available and even when rides broke down they were back in action in no time. I was a bit worried about the new Pirates ride as I was very fond of the old one, but I had no worries. The ride is great and just wait till you see Jack Sparrow. The firework show was the best I have ever seen and is worth the admission price on its own! Everything is spotless and the staff were efficient and well trained. Defintely go, no matter what your age.

Read Disneyland Travel Books before you go: Disneyland Resort PassPorter by the Marx is fantastic for planning, Birnbaum's Disneyland Resort has great pictures, & Disneyland with Kids by Fodor has great tips. We went with our 7 year old and did a 4 day Park Hopper 8 7 to 8 10. My plan worked out which was we split the DLR park in half. Day one we did Fantasyland, Toontown, and Tomorrowland. Day two we did California Adventure. Day three we did the 2nd half of Disneyland   New Orleans Square, Critter Country, Adventureland, and Frontierland. Next tip...beat the heat. If you go in at 8:00 you can do a lot of rides for 2 hours before everyone else starts showing up. We always left park around 1:30 or 2:00 and went back to the HoJo Hotel for a swim and relaxation. We came back in the evening when it was cooler and less crowded. Day 4 was  favorites day  and we did both DLR and California Adventure. In 4 days we were also able to see the Fireworks   a MUST SEE. Go the 1st nite as sometimes they are canceled due to winds so keep going until you see it. We also saw Fantasmic   a MUST SEE and the Electric Parade at California Adv   which we also enjoyed. One thing we didn't anticipate was Days 2 4 we ended up getting a stroller for our son as he has asthma and it really is a lot of walking, so even though he is 7 years old   he couldn't walk that much. The service and food at DLR was very good   much better than expected. It truely is one of the happiest places on earth. A favorite activity of our son's was getting character signatures so we had to fit a lot of characters into our schedule. Characters are at Toontown, at beginning of main street, and for Poo Characters   go to Critter Country. We did character breakfast at Goofy's kitchen and that was fun for us adults too! P.S. Wear good walking shoes   forget the sandals or flip flops   you'll regret it if you don't. Last tip   make reservations ahead. We got right into restaurants with reservations, while I heard others complaining they couldn't get in or had long waits. Not all make reservations but check the guide books. It was one of the smartest things we did   especially with a hungry child!

It was our first time visiting this park in several trips to the LA area. After reading other reviews I was a little hesitant to put up the money to go. After arriving we found the park spotless and the rides were fun for my teenaged daughters as well as myself. Do arrive early and have a game plan. We arrived at 8:00 am and rode all of the  big  rides early. The pirates of the caribean had a 10 minute wait when we got there (no fast passes) when we were ready to leave around 3pm the wait was 3hrs. Get fast passes when ever you can and plan smaller rides around them they are a life saver! We rode acouple of rides with them and I was never able to figure out why people were standing in the long lines and watching us move to the front of the lines like VIP's. The food was good and priced about where I expected it to be. Again I say arrive early and get a park map and plan your rides you should have a ball just as we did!

I live about 3 hours away from Disneyland and I try to go as much as I can. Go figure that I'm just NOW buying the Annual Pass. LOL. That's okay because as a Southern California resident and military brat, I have the discount privileges. Anyways, it's Disneyland. It's going to be crowded. It's not something you just discovered, it's something everyone wants a piece of. Yes it's going to be crowded during the summer, yes it's going to be crowded on the weekend, yes it's going to be crowded in the afternoon when locals stop by. Of all the researching people do, I think this is the FIRST thing that you need to understand. Yes, it is overpriced but so is every other amusement park. It's not like Disney came up with that on their own, in fact my niece has an amusepark simulation game that TELLS the person playing that that is how you success. It's about seeing your children happy not about counting every penny. The point is to enjoy yourself and relax, not complain because it doesn't have the luxuries of home (no crowds, A C, cheap food, etc) because if that's the case...stay home. There are little ways to save if you try. Buy tickets when they are discounted (online, special packages, etc), you CAN bring water and snacks into the park (I have done so) they are just asking you not to bring a cooler of food (which BTW I've seen people leave them in their car and return to their car for lunch dinner...good way to save without totally leaving the park), and get your souvenirs at a Disney store (or online) before going to the park (cheaper and the kids get to carry it around the park).Tip: Since Disneyland is  mainly  for children, if you have young children, hit up Fantasyland first. This is the place that gets packed before noon. If you are with older people, start the opposite side of the park (Tomorrowland).Point is, stop complaining because it's not going to make it any better. If you accept it, then you'll give yourself time to get over it and HAVE FUN.

We were at Disneyland on July 9th, 10th and 11th 2006 and it was truly an amazing experience! Yes the flight was long and exhausting from Australia but everywhere we went we were made to feel welcome! Yes the crowds were thick, the lines long and the food and drink expensive but it was worth it! There is so much to see and do 3 days weren't enough, even from early morning to late evening. Disneyland is a place that everyone can enjoy and from what we saw, it really is  the happiest place on earth . We stayed in a hotel across the road from the entrance which was very convenient. If we had our time over again , we'd probably go at a different time of year when it's less crowded and not quite as hot, but overall we have no regrets. We highly recommend Disneyland, especially the Pirates of the Carribean ride. It was awesome, we went on three times ! The Blue Bayou restaurant, situated inside the ride, was great too   what an atmosphere! Expensive, but very nice!Our four year old loved the Buzz Lightyear ride, and it was cool that you could email the photos from the ride home   a nice souvenir which didn't cost anything! We took our stroller with us on the flight, which was an excellent idea   we didn't have to worry about hiring one and we always had it with us. This was vey handy. I was impressed by the security too   while on a ride you could leave the stroller with no worries about it being stolen. The employees were all extremely courteous and helpful. It was a wonderful holiday!!

This was my first trip to Disneyland having flown from Austraila, a long trip for a 10 year old. But still, i was not dissapointed. We had a 3 day park hopper ticket and to make to most of it we arrived at 8 o'clock on most days. thankfully there were no lines to the rides at that time. At about midday the park is crowded and hot. Luckily our hotel was situated close to Disneyland so we could escape the midday heat. the Fast Pass system was most useful for the more popular rides. Some rides not to be missed are: The big thunder mountain, Mullholland Maddness & Star tours. In California Adventure you must not miss Aladin the musical or California Soaring!!! If you are going to see Aladin then don't wait in the long line just turn up at the show time   there are loads of seats. I reccomend Disneyland to people of all ages.

I too did a lot of research before we went to Disneyland and California Adventure. I was travelling with a 4 yr old, 2 month old, and an easily annoyed husband I wanted our visit to go smoothly. I purchased Ridemax software. I was great! It really help us to cut down on wait times and helped us plan an efficent plan of attack. The first day we visited Disneyland was the first day Pirates of the Carribean reopened. The place was packed, but we still got to go on all the rides we had planned to go on. I don't feel like we missed out on anything. The line for Pirates was 5 hours long so we never made it on that, but that is okay.The fireworks are really special, but you need to claim a seat very early. Do not sit on the benches around the Walt and Mickey statue. Right before the show started that area got very crowded and people who were sitting on the benches could not see a thing. Some tips I learned  go early keep a sense of humor the outdoor food area near the Buzz Lightyear ride has air conditioning vents mounted in the ceiling, so even though you are outside you can still get some cool air. ignore the time ending on fastpasses. The CM don't care what time they end, but they are to the minute to the time they start. We were 3 minutes early for our fast pass window and they made us wait the 3 minutes. consider using Ridemax it was worth it for us.

Arrived at Disneyland on June 30th and stayed till the 5th of July. Lines were fairly long for mornig entrance, but moved quickly once the park opened. Tempetures were warmer than forcast, though only in the mid 90's. We saved a lot on water by bringing our own in the morning, then saving the bottles for refills. If you don't like LA water(I don't) we used the single servings of lemonade and tea to dress up the water. By proper use of fast passes and going to popular rides durin parades & shows, are wait were kept under 1 2 an hour. The park was clean and neat every day. Cast members were upbeat evenwhen short staffed. we had a great disney experiance. The key to a great Disney trip is to book early, stay 4 5days (so you don't have to rush) and do your homeworkon how thw park works with the time of year and attractions. Love Disneyland!!!!!!!!

I read these recent reviews, and thought I should share my latest experience at Disneyland. We go at least once a year, and this year will be two. We just returned in May and will go again in August. NEVER buy tickets at the gate. They cost more here. Buy them online or from the Disney Store. Also, you can buy a package from AAA which will save money. You CAN get free ice water, but you have to go to vendors who sell soda from a fountain, not just any vendor. Also, there is a fountain by the Rancho Del Zocalo resteraunt in Adventureland that has a water fountain with cups by it. The searches at the gate are the result of 9 11, and did not exist prior to this. I am thankful for them. I brought my own snacks in a backpack, and I have always done this. We bring our own water, beef jerkey, nuts, pretzels, etc. If you want to pack a lunch for a day trip, there is a picnic area outside of the park (I have used this in the past when I lived in Southern California). We have always brought outside food with us and have NEVER had a problem. They are looking for weapons, not food.Check the Disney website prior to your visit. It is updated all the time, and you will be able to see which rides are down, and check shows and schedules. As far as escaping the heat (this is Southern California), try a cooler show like the Tiki Room or Main Street Cinema). If you don't like the heat or crowds, don't go in the summer. We had a great time, as always. The 50th is ending, so we wanted to go again. Also, Space Mountain has opened again after a long closure. I was sooooo excited to share my old favorite with my children. We were not disappointed!

About 200$ first thing then 5 waters at 3 dollars each for 15$ and a toy for 15$ for my three year old. About 230$. There were about a zillion people there when I went. so 200x 20,000 people (or more) 40,000,000$And moldy water in splash mountain, sticking and old rides in need of work, no shade, and tons of walking and lines and crowds.This is not the happiest place on earth, the 240$ plus the hotel with high tax for 2 nights 250$ 500$ in 2 days. Whoa.Hope this helps

So I read everything I could about Disney and didn't see this come up. So I'll let you all in on a secret that no one at Disney will tell you unless you really press. EARLY ENTRY IS ONLY ON MONDAYS, TUESDAYS AND SATURDAYS. They don't tell you that online when you purchase your tickets. They don't tell you that when you go to pick up your tickets at the will call booth ( now your tickets are good for one early entry day . What's missing    and those days are Mondays, Tues... ). They don't tell you that when you show up early on WEDNESDAY ( oh no mam', we don't have early entry on Wednesdays ). They only tell you that when you show up on FRIDAY early AGAIN!!!!!! And don't even bother complaining. THey have your money and they don't care at that point. They also don't tell you that the fireworks show is only on the weekends. But most nights they cancel it anyway due to  high altitude winds . But we did get to catch the fireworks on the way out of the park. They probably hadn't heard of the  high altitude wind  problem at Angel stadium where fire works were going on there ( p.s.   if you here the  pre recorded announcement  that the show will be delayed for 5 minutes because of the  high altitude winds , you might as well start heading out and beat the crowds now. The next  pre recorded announcement  tells you they are cancelled. There is a reason it's a  pre recorded announcement . LA doesn't suffer from a huge high altitude wind problem. It's a scam. It's the only way they can afford to set them off every weekend (well at least one night per weekend). Here's some other tips:Autotopia   use FASTPASS. Don't go to the first ramp. They usually only have one side of cars running. Go to the far ramp, they have 2 lines of cars going and even if they don't (like when they first open the ride), it will be the first one to get the other side going.Monsters Inc ride   don't bother waiting in a big line for this stinker.Alladin show   this is a really great live show. but it only runs Thursday to Monday. So Tues Thurs is no show. Check your brochures the first day and make sure you know when your shows are. They're not everyday.Best way to ride Tomorrowland ridesAs soon as the park opens, bank to the right and follow the crowds of running people to Space Mountain. Don't go on the ride. Grab a FASTPASS instead. Head over to the Matterhorn. There is no fastpass to this ride and the lines are all the way around the mountain within a few hours. You can practically walk on at this point. Then head over to Autotopia. It's still early so don't need a fastpass (nor can you get one because you can only have one per hour, and your Space Mountain time hasn't come up yet). After Autotopia head over to Buzz Lightyear ride. Grab a FASTPASS for this ride (by this time your timeslot is ready for Space Mountain so you can pick up your next fastpass). Head across to Space Mountain (remember you can ride ANYTIME after your fastpass window has passed, even at the end of the day, but I would do it now). Exit Space mountain and move on over to Star Tours. After Star Tours head directly across and use your FASTPASS for Buzz Lightyear. You've just done the best of Tomorrowland and morning isn't even over. If you wait until Mid morning or afternoon, you could never do all those rides in that timeframe. We never did hit Honey I shrunk the audience or the innovations of tomorrow. So I'm not sure if we missed anything good? Now head over to Frontierland to the River Belle Terrace for for a late breakfast enjoy Mouse pancakes. (ps   You can email your picture home when you exit Buzz Lightyear.) Single RiderEven if the attraction doesn't have an official  single rider  line, you can usually walk in the exit and get on really fast by sitting with another single. FASTPASSThe fastpass is usually faster than if you ran into the park and were one of the first groups to go through. The fastpass line gets to move ahead of people who are waiting in line in certain parts of the lineup. People really give you the evil eye as you go in front of them like you're some kind of VIP. Do the fastpass!! It's free easy. I even gave some away that we weren't going to use to some poor fools who didn't know about it. CharactersIf you see characters on the street with big lines, don't bother waiting. They have to go on breaks. You probably won't even get very far in line before they take off. And it's not like the  handler  will tell you,  don't bother because you'll never make it to the front by the time we take off . Can't tell you how many times this happened.

I've been taking my daughter to Disneyland and the other parks since she was 1 I take her at least twice a year and would go more if we could but living in Olympia Washington and with school and work thats not possible.All the workers at Disneyland and California Adventure are just awesome, never have had a problem with them, there funny and very helpful.the rides are great, splash mountain, thunder mountain railroad, indianana jones, haunted mansion, piarates of the carribian, soarin over california, california screamin, etc all loads of fun, if you go first thing when they open the lines aren't bad, also short lines when fantacmic is showing and the fireworks.also don't forget the shows, you have to see Aladin super show, snow white great show. there are neat shops all over the two parks, and food good there also. my daughter is now 9 and still loves disney, were taking our 2nd trip this year July 22 only for 7 days but its great being a kid all that time I;m 56 and will go as long as I'm able to.see you all there.

Disney World has all of the Disney magic. There are a few things you want to make sure of before you go. Buy the book Unofficial Guide to Walt Disney World by Bob Sehlinger. Make sure you are familiar with the maps and ride information before you go. All the parks that we went had very detailed maps with ride information as well. DW was a little hard to figure out and not very descriptive for attraction information. This is probably not a problem for most but if you have motion sickness or any light sensitivity of any kind   make sure you verify the ride information. My husband has problems with both of these and he is always checking the information before he gets in line   after 2 attractions with no warning of motions or lights   he decided not to try anything else. So for him it was a little boring. There is usually something that a person with this kind of problem can do but in our case he just waited for us because he did not want to be sick for the rest of the day. At one ride we even asked the attendant and were assured no problem only to find out the ride actually turned the whole time   lucky for us it only turned a half turn each time then would stop and then turn again so he only came out with a headache. If you have older children and you want the Disney experience make sure you do at least the 2 day ticket so that you can go to Disney California Adventure too. At DCA the rides are geared for the older ones not so much Disney stuff though. The Disney experience will come from DW. Also make sure you stop at City Hall to find out the schedule for the character appearances. They have scheduled appearances in certain locations. Otherwise you might miss them all.

This was my first visit to Disneyland since I was 7 years old. I was very excited to check it out. I have been to WDW many times and I love it!! I knew Disneyland was going to be smaller and  less then  WDW, but what I didn't expect was the attitude from the Disney cast members towards WDW. They seemed very bitter and vindictive when I made mention of WDW. Nor was I expecting the products to be such trash! I was planning on doing some Christmas shopping, but I didn't even buy anything for myself. The products were so poorly made and they had such high prices. The 50th celebration t shirts all had a bad print, it looked like it started to print, but then moved so that there was a shadow. The kids clothes were falling apart on the hanger and outrageously priced. I was so very disappointed I can't even begin to tell you. California Adventure was great, but even they had poor products for sale. I did love both parks, but I was extremely disappointed in the quality of items available for purchase. The highlight of the trip was using the Ridemax schedule. Ridemax saved the day with a plan to see the parks and all of the rides in the most leisurely manner. I highly recommend using Ridemax if you are planning a trip to any Disney Park. I will be returning to WDW next year and I know I will be using it again, it really works!!

This was my first time to Disneyland and I enjoyed it. However, I don't think I'll be transformed into one of those Disney freaks who HAVE to go at least once a year. The  kiddie  rides were all fun. Space Mountain was one of my favorite  grown up  rides. Star Tours is alright, but I won't be knocking anyone over to ride it again. Indiana Jones is another ride that you shoudn't waste your time standing in line for. The Haunted Mansion is my official favorite ride. The effects are so cool and the air conditioning was a welcomed retreat from the hot weather. If you have little ones like 6 and under, they will thoroughly enjoy Autopia. My niece and nephews got stuck on Splash Mountain and were given useless passes to any ride they wanted in the park. Ummm . . . duh . . . they could already go to any ride they wanted   we already paid to get in!The thing I enjoyed the most about my visit to Disneyland was the fireworks display. It was so awesome! It was probably even better than usual because they are still celebrating the 50th anniversary. I thoroughly enjoyed it.Two things that irked me about Disneyland were the crowds and the prices. Our first day there was unbearably crowded. But, the cast members tried their best to deal with the crowds. As for the prices, charging $149 for three day park hopper passes isn't enough, you get nickle and dimed for EVERYTHING. I guess paying for one pass doesn't seem bad, but I paid for myself, my husband, and our 17 year old nephew. That's 3 adult passes to the whopping tune of $447! OUCH!I'm happy that I experienced Disneyland. I'm just not going to kill myself trying to get there anytime soon.

I've been to Disneyland countless of time as a kid and will always remember the magic feeling of going each time. This was my first chance to take my family as a parent and I noticed a few changes that were not for the better. The most obvious was the cast members. When I was a kid, I remember thinking   How are these people so happy?  Now, it seems like the older staff still has that magic, but the younger staff give the impression that it's just another job for them.Another downgrade from years past is the parade. It used to be a major deal, but now it's a short 10 minute show that is not worth the wait.Overall, Disneyland is still a great vacation spot for families, but it's hard to say how much longer that it'll be the happiest place on earth.

We just got back from a few days in Disneyland. Despite the ever increasing commercialization, it's still the best theme park around. I'm sure most people know the basics of the park, so rather than go on about that, I'll just mention what we considered the highlights:  Splash Mountain. Awesome ride. Definitely worth going on. Fantastic drop at the end, and some great theming. It's a bit like an updated It's a Small World, with a big water drop at the end.  The Billy's @ the Golden Horseshoe. Go see the Billys! They perform at the Golden Horsehoe in Frontierland, 3 4 times daily with a great music show. Really worth seeing. The Sunday night fireworks are amazing. Really worth being there to see them. No skimping from Disney on this one. It's a good show.  Parade of Dreams. You have to see this at least once while you are there. But be warned, it gets incredibly crowded so find a spot to sit down somewhere on main st early in the evening.  Celebrating 50 years of Disney. There's a 20 minute film with Steve Martin in on, showing on Main street, which goes through a history of the park. Very interesting and worth seeing.  Space Mountain. This one's a no brainer.A lot of people have mentioned the money grabbing aspect of disneyland, such as the countless stores all selling t shirts, mugs, etc., but I personally don't think it's any worse than most other places. When we went (Sun   Tuesday) in mid May, the crowds were pretty low, and the maximum wait for rides was about 20 minutes. Use the Fastpass system when you need to, and go on rides like Splash Mountain early in the day.We still love Disneyland, even though it's getting expensive, and we'll definitely be back again soon.

Disneyland is a fantastic place, well laid out, lovely gardens, clean facilities and the staff are very helpful and friendly. However, coming from Australia (where it is still an icon) we assumed that we would be able to access Disneyland from any location in LA   either by bus, train or coaches running on a regular basis to Disneyland   wrong! We were staying in a hotel in Beverly Hills (a long way from Disneyland) and we had booked our tickets directly with Disneyland, for entry into Disneyland over the internet and were to collect them at the gate. On arriving in LA we enquired what was the best way to get out to Disneyland and most people said  drive yourself . As we were not going to hire a car we had to make arrangements as we soon found out that there is no public transport system which gets you there! We eventually ended up purchasing part of a tour package, but had to get ourselves downtown by taxi (US$16) and then it cost us US$25 each for return coach trip. As we only had one day available for Disneyland we were hoping to make it a full day evening....but the tour did not leave Downtown until about 10   arriving at Disneyland about 11 and then said they would collect us at 7pm.........this was very disappointing as the fireworks are on at about 9pm. Apparently this company (Starline) only collects later in summertime and we were there in Spring. Suggest other tour operators be investigated for comparison. At Disneyland we recommend  Fast Pass  which some of the more popular rides have   this is a machine at the rides which gives you a time when you should come back and  go to the top of the queue    it was brillant.Loved Disneyland and wish to go back and see all the bits we missed   definitely need at least 2 days.

As a native Californian, I'm ashamed to admit that I haven't been to Disneyland in 16 years. This was my first trip back with my husband and 2 children, ages 2 and 4. We also traveled with my neice, age 11 and my parents, who probably don't want me to disclose thier ages. The trip was awesome. I can't believe how much has changed. I think Disney did a great job with the expansion of Cal Adven and Downtown Disney. It took some creative planning, but they pulled it off in the usual fine Disney fashion.Okay, okay, back to Disneyland. We were there from May 7 11, 2006. We purchase the 3 day hopper passes. On a positive note, there were very few lines or wait times because school hasn't let out yet, but that also means the parks have shorter operating hours. It was very difficult to squeeze everything into these three days. I would definitely return during the off season, but perhaps extend our park hoppers by a day or two. Also because we didn't go to the park on a Saturday or Sunday, we missed the big fireworks and parade. Thankfully my daughter has no clue what she missed and I wasn't about to tell her. Also on a bit of a sour note, the characters were not readily available for meet & greets or getting autographs. Everytime we'd get in line to see Jasmine or Ariel, we'd wait about 10 minutes, then they would scurry away with their attendents, and it was made abundantly clear that they were not available. We were able to see Pluto, Goofy, & Minnie. Ironically, the only time we saw Mickey was in the parade. I wish, for my 4 year old daughters sake that she could've met more princesses.Okay, I'm done gripping. Our trip was magical. The food at the parks was good, expensive, but good. There was adequate room for strollers and hardly any wait times for the rides. We took advantage of our early entry vouchers which was well worth it. Cal Adven was great too. My neice and husband loved the rides there and the little ones loved Bug land!All and all our visit was magical. I'm already planning another visit for next year.

We had our 4th trip to this great place April 20th to the 26th....... as always, it was wonderful ! Our family of 5 stayed at the Marriott Fairfield Inn, right across the street from Disneyland. The weather was great, sunny, but not too warm, and I was so happy to see the lines for the rides were so short ! We were able to walk onto the rides in under 5 minutes ! It was the best ! Only one ride was down while we were there... Pirates of the Caribbean, due to the update it is undergoing. We will catch that next time. This is the second trip we have taken during the 50th celebration, and we were happy to see all the decorations up, still looking great. The parades were fun..... the kids enjoyed the Block Party Bash, and the fireworks show  Remember , still amazes me. The soundtrack to this is incredible.... we now listen to it in the car!! DCA was fun.... we love the Tower of Terror, and It's Tough To Be A Bug ! still makes me jump out of my seat ! Those of you who have seen this show, know what I mean by that ! All the CM's were helpful, kind and funny.... Jungle Cruise guy was the best !! We had a wonderful time this year, and we plan on going back in October, right after our move to Las Vegas this summer. Annual Passes, HERE WE COME !!!! Get to Disneyland before the end of the 50th.... it is a priceless family memory waiting to happen !!

There were my husband, our two sons, my husband's parents and myself on our adventure to Disneyland this April. We stayed at the Holiday Inn Hotel & Suites, which was fabulous. We had a 2 bedroom suite overlooking the pool & hot tub and it was marvelous. We bought groceries to eat breakfast in our room and save a few bucks. The restaurant had wonderful food and the kids eat free with paying adults. We could still watch all the fireworks over Disneyland but without being trampled by the crowds. They were amazing by the way! We had a nice walk to the tram beside the Mickey & Friends. We learned to take the Monorail into Disneyland from Downtown Disney to avoid the huge crowds at Disneyland opening. The food was very good at Disneyland and I would completely and utterly recommend the character breakfast at Goofy's Kitchen. The food was wonderful and every 30 minutes or so, there would be something fun for the kids to do with Chef Goofy. I would go there again with or without my kids, it was that good! We enjoyed the fruit stands in Disneyland as a healthy alternative to some of the fried food that were being offered, not that fried food is bad but at least there was an alternative. We learned that using a locker, which is multiple entry, is the best place to keep your overloaded backpack while you enjoy the rides. We kept our jackets for the evening packed in there, as well as our snacks.

Family of 2 adults and 2 teenage children visited Disneyland for 5 days during April spring break 2006. It was our 1st visit and 5 days was not long enough to see and experience all that we wanted to in Disneyland and California Adventure park and that was after entering the park at 9:00 am and leaving after 1:00am each day!We stayed at the Howard Johnson Anaheim just a relaxing 10 min (max) stroll from the park entrance. The staff here were courteous and genuinely friendly and helpful. Although they don't do meals here, there is a small shop in the foyer for snacks, drinks, souvenirs etc. We ate most of our meals at MiMi's restaurant next door to the hotel. There is a McDonalds and other eateries as you walk to Disneyland.Being spring break we expected crowds. However, they were not as bad as anticipated with an average wait of 40 mins and 60 mins for Space Mountain. Unless you make queueing your mission in life, I strongly recommend making use of the Fastpass system for those rides where it is available. Disneyland has a mixture of rides, displays and shows whereas California Adventure park is more ride focussed. If you get to the park early or stay late you will find that the waiting times for rides are greatly reduced. Note that Disneyland is open until about 1:00am ( last rides at midnight) whereas California Adventure park closes at 10:00pm. Check the Disneyland web site for up to date opening and closing times.We had three character meals: a Goofy Breakfast and Dinner (buffets) and an Ariel's Grotto dinner (multi choice set menu). We found Ariel's Grotto is probably best suited to younger children but we all had a ball at the Goofy meals. It seemed to be more relaxed and 'Goofy' at the Goofy meals and the characters were more interactive with all the guests and stayed longer at each table. If anybody in your party is celebrating a birthday (any age), let the staff know and Goofy and the staff will visit the table and sing Happy Birthday to the great delight or embarrassment of the birthday dude. Snack meals throughout the park are expensive and I did not find them value for money.If rides are not your thing, be prepared for a lot of walking. There are electric carts and strollers for hire if you need them. Bags are searched at the main entrance although I was never sure what they were looking for. I reckon that we probably needed another 4 days to see and do everything we wanted. But that will have to wait for our next visit!

Our trip was from March 26 to April 1with 4 adults and 2 children. This was our first visit to Disneyland   all the adults in the party have been to Disney World before. We had a ball we took advantage of our early entries to the different parts of the park and the fast pass tickets to rides. The longest wait was maybe 30 minutes, but it never really felt that long. As far as any of the cast members being rude or not being happy we did not encounter any of that. We had a lot of cast members who were very helpful to us. My friends had said we would enjoy Disneyland better because there would be less walking between rides which I think was a benefit for both the grandparents and the young children in our party. The weather during our week was not the greatest, it seem to rain most of the time at night around dinner time. So we worked around the rain, no big deal. I would recommend character dinning its was great for the kids and US   we did the Lilo and Stitch breakfast. We only did a 3 day hopper pass because we also wanted to visit other parts of California. We are already planning on next year's trip back but doing Disneyland the whole time we're there. We stayed at the Anaheim Fairfield Inn   about a 10 minute walk from the entrance   it was also great.

This was the first time I've visited Disneyland in 13 years and not a whole lot has changed. Disneyland was excellent, however Disney California was not as great as I had expected. I found Disney California more dedicated to rides   activites for children. If you plan to get a single park pass definately stick with the original Disneyland. There is much more to do   see! Overall its still the happiest place on earth!

Visited Disneyland in April 2006. Good rides but it's to crowded. Using the fastpass shortens the lines but it can be hard to find the fastpass machines. This place is more for the younger kids, teenagers demands more thrilling rides. I presume it's a very nice place in the evening. Saw the fireworks from nearby California Adventure and it looked really good.

Disneyland is a first class entertainment complex! I am sixteen years old and found Disneyland to be the most amazing (And fun) place in the world. The 50th Aniversary really made Disneyland Park beautiful, the castle especially was so amazing. Here's some tips you need to know before you go....1. Disneyland is VERY busy, so if crowds bother you will have to face the music at DIsneyland. I myself didn't mind the crowds, as I was too distracted by the wonders of the park. 2.Ride Pirates of the Carribbean and The Haunted Mansion during the  Fantasmic  show, as there will be hardly any wait at all. Pirates of the Carribbean is a MUST SEE!!!!!!!3.Make sure you check out the  Fantasmic  show yourself. It is the best show I have ever seen, with so many amazing speical effects.3.Ride the Fantsyland rides even if you think you are too old for them. They are slow I admit, but so cool with the effects in them. Be prepared to wait ages for Peter Pan's filght, but do take the time to ride it as it is one of the best Fantasyland rides.4.Ride all the rides, even if they look scary. Disneyland is about scary fun, not maing you feel like you're going to be sick!5.Splash Mountain is very fun, but you WILL GET WET!!!!!!!!! The big drop at the end isn't scary, it is very fun. Ride Splash Mountain during the day and then at night, because at night it is a whole lot funner!6.Live in the moment, don't complain about lines and what not, just have fun!Most impotanlty, rememember how lucky you are to be at Disneyland, and enjoy it to the max!

Stay out of Toon Town at all costs! My husband took both my children (3 and 5 years old) into Mickey's house for a meet and greet. There was no line or sign outside posting a wait time however he waited inside Mickey's house for over an hour in a dark narrow hall way filled with tired children and parents. There were no cast members around and the Exits were not clearly marked. He ended up moving some props to find an Exit and lead a small exodus to freedom. All the while I sat in Mickey's garage with 8 other abandoned spouses making desperate cell phone calls to our missing families. The streets were lined 3 deep with abandoned Disneyland rental strollers. The entire place smelled of boiled hot dogs. I loved the rest of Disneyland and feel very strongly that the  Imagineers  who created Toon Town should be shamed into becoming grounds clean up workers.

We just spent 6 days in Anaheim, taking our four year old son to Disneyland. We had been many times as a couple and wanted to share the experience with him before we got too old to enjoy it! (We are both in our 40's). I have to say I enjoyed it as much this time as I did 20 years ago when I first went   and possibly more as I got to see it through my sons eyes. There were many more people there than ever before, yet we never waited longer than 30 minutes for any ride and fast tracked a couple of the more popular rides. What a great invention fast track is! The park was spectacularly clean (as always) and I loved the face lift the Castle had and many of the rides. Was disappointed that Pirates was closed for renovations, but we will just have to save up to make the return trip from Australia again in the near future. The  new  rides for me were great   Winnie the Pooh, Buzz Lightyear, Honey I Shrunk the Audience. I missed out on Star Tours (another I will add to the list) and of course the Nemo submarines will not be ready until June.There were plenty of food places although I would have liked to see a bit more variety than the burger fries (and variations thereof) combination. Yes there were fresh fruit stands around the park which was nice, but a menu that was a little less fat laden would have been nice too. The serves of anything you buy though are MASSIVE so sometimes you could even buy one serve and share. The peanut butter and jelly sandwich I bought for my son was amazing with a half inch thick of peanut butter spread! It was a bit too much for a 4 year old. The parade was wonderful and the fireworks spectacular and I saw for the first time the Fantasm light show! That was awesome!For those with little children be warned that some of the rides for the littlies are quite scary. Snow White is one and Toads Wild Ride is another. Perhaps start off on the less confronting rides (Peter Pan, Storybook land). Toon Town was fabulous. I just have to say how wonderful I think the staff at Disneyland are. On day 4 of our 5 day visit I went into the City Hall to find out when Donald Duck was going to be appearing (as he is our son's favourite). One of the girls offered to check his schedule while another asked our son what his name was and then said  I think I have something here for you . Within minutes she appeared with a personally signed photgraph of Donald Duck! The look on my son's face was priceless. Of course for the rest of the day we were asked how Donald knew he would be there! One thing that made me laugh was the fact that Disney characters have been given the ability to sign autographs (something that was not around last time I went). While this is quite  cute  and clearly a merchandising boom, it makes the lining up for photo opportunities a little harder. For some characters you probably could do with a fast pass! The only thing my son didn't like were the  automatic toilets . Obviously a great invention to stop the spread of germs, it can be quite traumatic for a young child when the toilet flushes in the middle of..... well you understand. Not sure how they can get around this.

Just returned from our Spring Break Disney vacation and had a fabulous time. It had been almost 4 years since our last time there and we were very excited to go. Yes, the lines were longer than expected, but we took the time to chit chat with others. Met people from all over. Didn't wait more than 30 minutes for anything  never used a fast pass and averaged 12 rides a day. The stand by wait times aren't accurate. Was told it would be 65 minutes for Splash Mountain and were only in line for 20. To avoid the crush into the park in the morning, board the train at Main Street. Thought this might be our last Disney vacation since the kids are getting older (10 and 13), but they and my husband are already planning for next year. Never met a single rude employee in the three days we were there. And never had a long wait for food in DL or DD. Yes, it's pricey, but expected. Only disappointments were the Matterhorn breaking down  we did get to ride it once  and the Monsters Inc. ride. After the nearly 30 minute wait, not that great. And we love the  kiddie  rides, they bring back memories of when I went with my family as a child. Have asked the family if they would like to go to DW in Florida, but they'd rather come back to California. Don't miss: Soarin', California Screamin', Indie Jones, and Splash Mountain at night!

I took my two kids (ages 6 and 11) to Disneyland March 19, 20 and 21. We stayed in the Grand Californian, had a terrific view of the park and a hotel exclusive entrance to DCA which was sweet.We rode everything line free until about 11am each day and then the lines were unbearable. Thank goodness for Fastpass! Some rides were hopeless from the getgo, Peter Pan being one of them. Who could have guessed Roger Rabbit would be impossible to ride? Monsters Inc. was broken for several hours and they closed the Fastpass for it. We suspected even with Fastpass, we weren't going to get on it so we didn't return there.We unexpectedly found Pocahantas in Frontierland. What a treasure!I seldom see reviews about park food. If the princesses hadn't saved the day, I would say Ariel's Grotto was the worst. For one, it's  rock concert  loud and noisy. The selections are limited and it's at a fixed price.
