For $20 ($15 if you're a child), you pick an appetizer, an entree and a dessert. Onion soup, burger, peach tart and then the gratuity is tacked on for you.Our favorite was the Granville, which is a steakhouse in the Disneyland Hotel. It's elegant, it's calming, and you pay the equivalent of Outback prices so you feel a little burned, but in a relaxed kind of way. : )

Visited Disneyland yesterday, March 22 right in the heart of Spring Break for much of the Western U.S. We arrived a bit later than we wanted (1 hour after opening) and took a big gulp when we saw the enormous crowds. Much to our surprise, though, the longest we had to wait was 30 minutes, and 20 minutes was the average for the rides (and we did all the big ones). Disneyland cast members keep things moving in a tactfully urgent way (i.e.  get your butt moving onto off this ride so others can enjoy it....but have a great day! ). Fasttrak Splash Mountain early in the day for a twilight ride   you'll run past the 60 minute line @ 6:00pm and have a beautiful view of the park and setting sun. Other tips   bring in lots of bottled water and don't worry about a decent sized backback. None of the rides go upside down so with a little care you won't have any problems riding every ride with your bag.Many people skip the parade to enjoy the short lines, but I wouldn't. It's really spectacular and feels like it adds value to the sticker shocking ticket prices. Ditto for the 50th anniversary Fireworks show   best I have EVER seen, anywhere, anytime.Disneyland's awesome   I'm a 20 something who went with my 20 something wife and another 20 something couple. we had more fun than most of the kids there.

We stayed in Anaheim for 9 nights Feb. 27   Mar. 8. We had 5 day Hopper tickets for the Disneyland Parks. These were a great option for our 1st visit so that we could take our time and not be overwhelmed. Lines were not a problem ... about 20min for the most popular rides. We found it amazing how clean the Parks are! Food is a bit expensive but every fair, amusement park, etc is that way. We took our own bottled water to dodge the $2.50 $3.00 per drink.The weather was good   about 67F or 17C and sunny most days. Any rain we did get diminished crowds even further but did not affect our experience.I think the key is to take the kids out of school and allow extra time to enjoy a leisure vacation.The other days we took 2 trips to San Diego and 1 to Knott's Berry to add some variety to our holiday.

Great place to visit the first week of March!! Had a very pleasant weekday experience there. Hardly any lines and no need for fastpass. Only regret is that we saved a day for the weekend in order to see the entertainment only offered then. CROWDS on the weekends!! Next time I would get four day passes rather than 3 days and then would save the fourth day for the weekend and only enter the park in the evening and just do the entertainment offerings such as parade, fireworks, and Fantasmic. Relax and just settle in early for good seats. The entertainment is definately worth that fourth day!!!

My Boyfriend and i just resently went to Disneyland in CA, and it was the most fun we have ever had. We went in the middle of feb. and it was perfect. I will say though it did rain a little in the mornings but that only made it better because there were short lines for all the rides for the first 4 hours that the park was open. We got to see all the shows with great seats including Fantasmic, the firework show and the Parade od Dreams. The firework show was truly magical. We also had great seats for the Block party bash and Aladin play in California adventure. The lines were not long for all 3 days that we were there, and we only had to fastpass one ride, Tower of Terror, which we prob. didn't even need to. The prices have seemed to go up since last year, but it is the 50th anaversary. I recommend a Disney vacation esp. if you have little ones ages 5 and up. It was a wonderful time, and well worth the money.

We visit DL once a year and we always take the time to research when to go and then pencil out an intinerary to get the most of our trip. I do not agree with previous reviews saying DL has lost its magic. To the contrary, it has never been more sparkly or enchanting! They have gone all out for the anniversary and the new fireworks are amazing and worth the price of your vacation. We have never come across a rude or unhappy CM in our years of coming. What we DO see are visitors that have entitlement issues which makes it difficult for everyone and perhaps frustrates the CMs. The key to enjoying DL is to go in with the right attitude and expect lines closures. The previous reviewers that visited the end of February should have checked the Anaheim Convention Calendar which would have told them there was a cheerleading convention , same time every year. There are certain times of the year to avoid, like the spring dental convention, October Fall break for Utah, July, 2 weeks around Easter etc etc. We have figured these out by visiting boards like www.laughingplace.com and we also check Disneyland.com to check ride show closures and schudules. Also riderefurbs.com. You can still have fun when its busy. Be there right at opening, utilize Early Entry, learn the Fastpass system (there are a few rides that will let you have 2 at one time, you do not have to use it before the return time but do have have to use it the same day) Eat lunch before 11:30, eat dinner before 5:30   call Disney Dining 60 days in advance (on their website) for preferred seating, there are a few other restaurants as well that accept them (website). In the afternoon when the parks are busy swim at your hotel or visit Downtown Disney. These are just a few things you can do, if you stress easily, to make your vacation more smooth. But just lighten up people   its the Happiest Place on Earth, come and celebrate with 60,000 of your closest friends   LOL!

I spent four and a half days in Anaheim in late February, three of them at the Disneyland resort. My sister has already rated the Parks based on this late February 2006 trip but I thought I would add my thoughts to this.A great many reviewers found disappointment at Disneyland due to the large crowds, unpleasant individuals, rude Cast Members, etc. While some may wish to suggest we've all made this up, that isn't the case. No sour grapes here, friends, just the facts: Disneyland is, indeed, too crowded and it absolutely makes for an unpleasant time.Only silly clowns can paint smiles on their faces and pretend the ridiculously long lines are fun, or that being bumped, pushed, or mowed down by rude adults armed with monster sized strollers is part of the Disney magic.I've seen the Park more crowded than it was on our visits February 20 23    but it still wasn't great. There are certain traditions I could do without, such as the Main Street crush prior to park opening, of which I have included pictures. That isn't part of the Disney magic, is it?You definitely have to have a strategy mapped out before entering the Parks, and you cannot deviate from it or your day is a loss. Even then, your plans may not hold if a ride is shut down, etc.But maybe that's the problem. Maybe you shouldn't have to have a strategy to enjoy Disneyland. I don't know what the answer to the problem is for the Disney folks    I'm not sure they are too worried about it as long as people parade through the gates willing to put up with it. It's not :sour grapes  to be displeased with it    if anything, it's foolish to pretend it's wonderful when it's not. The cost of tickets, hotels, etc. is too great these days not to get the most from your money and enjoy a pleasant, high quality experience.For what it's worth, I was at the park late August 2005 for three days and it wasn't nearly as crowded as it was in late February. How do you explain that one?

We visited Disneyland on February 24 & 25 as my son had a vacation and we thought the parks wouldn't be too crowded. Unfortunately, that was not the case. The last time we visited Disneyland was prior to 9 11 so we expected some entrance issues with new security but found that the security lines were extremely long as were the lines to get into the park. And if you wanted to  hop  parks, the lines were long no matter what time we decided to see the other park. What's the point of the hand stamp if there isn't a special entrance to move people through quickly? Aside from Saturday morning from 8:00   10:30 which was lovely because it wasn't crowded, everything had a line. It was clear that Disneyland wasn't prepared for the crowds. At California Adventure it took almost an hour to get lunch at the burger place by Soarin' over California. We also had problems with trying to eat dinner at the River Belle Terrace. After waiting 20 minutes (the line hadn't moved at all), we decided to just grab something at the Bengal Barbeque. Not exactly what we had in mind for dinner, but by then, we were all so tired, hungry and frustrated with the lines that we just wanted something easy. Unfortunately because everything was so crowded it did tend to bring out the worst in people. We found that many were extremely rude and would bump into us (or run us over with a stroller or mechanized wheel chair). FastPass did work most of the time (although we had to do Splash Mountain on a different day because it wasn't running during our FastPass time) but not all rides offer this option. The Monster's Inc. ride at California Adventure had an hour long wait for a less than 4 minute ride. Definitely not worth the wait!! So the worst were the people. The best were still some of the rides like Soarin' Over California, Grizzly River Run (Fast Pass both of these), the new and improved Space Mountain (definitely worth a ride) and the Talk with Crush (California Adventure) was really well done and very cute. All in all, it'll be quite a while before we would even consider returning to Disneyland. Disney has always been a bit money grubbing but it was abundantly clear that once you bought your ticket, they could care less about your experience.

We visited Disneyland during the 50th Anniversary Celebration and for me it was very disappointing. We visited on February 20 22. We purchased the 3 day parker hoppers so we could visit Disneyland and California Adventure. This was the first visit for my girls who at 7 and 4 were very excited about visiting Disney. We took out 7 year old out of school for a few days and thought February would be a good time to visit and we might just avoid the huge crowds that converge on Disney during the summer months. Well, we were wrong. It seems that there isn't a really good time to visit and avoid the huge crowds. Our first day was a Monday and it was a holiday so we expected them to be crowded since school was out. The following Tuesday and Wednesday were not any better. Seems a lot of other people had the same idea. The only times we were able to ride any of the rides were first thing in the morning. By noon it was impossible to get on any ride without having to wait well over 45 minutes to an hour. Certain rides did have the Fast Pass which did work well but that is only used for certain rides and even then is not always used. There is a line for everything at Disneyland and California Adventure. You wait in a line to have your bags checked before you even enter the park. On the third day the line was really long. Once you enter the park you have to wait in a line to show them your ticket. Once inside the park the lines really start. You wait in a large, crowded group line at Main Street for the actual rides to open. Then when they open there is a mad dash my grown ups with small children and strollers to get to the rides. If your not careful you could be run over. On our visit we knew at least 2 rides would be closed. On the first day we got in line for the Matterhorn only for them to close it as we were walking up because of some problem. We finally got to ride it on the 3rd day but heard later that same day that it was closed again. Spash Mountain was not running the first 2 days, finally at the end of our 3rd day we saw it was running. We eventually were able to ride some of the rides that we wanted to ride. It is just very frustrating and almost like work instead of fun to go on the rides. Even trying to ride the kiddy rides was difficult. We waited for at least 30 40 minutes to ride the tea cups, which my little girls enjoyed very much. I just wondered if the 4 grown men in line ahead of us enjoyed it too. Grown ups waiting in lines for rides that are for small children, I just did not understand. The worst part was probably the very rude people. People who would crowd in front of you so they could get a better view of a parade or a character. They would push their kids right in front of other kids who had been standing in a line to see one of the characters. We stood in a line for about 25 30 minutes for my girls to get a picture and autograph from Cinderella and Sleeping Beauty. They did get there picture and autograph but I had to point out to this one man where the line started. Had I not done that my girls would have missed out since the princesses had to leave after seeing my girls. People started lining up along the street at 6:00 for the parade that started at 7:15. We sat a table near Main Street about 30 45 mins and started out with a pretty good view of where the parade would pass by. Just as the parade was getting ready to start, people tried to crowd us out of where we had been sitting. Trying to push their children in front of us, pulling the chairs away from where we had been sitting and even standing on the table. And then these same people were overheard complaining because their children could not see the parade. There were way to many people, the food was overpriced, the Cast Members were not very friendly and we hardly ever saw any of them smile. From my memory of visiting when I was a child it sure seemed to be a lot nicer place to visit. For the price that we paid we came away very disappointed it what we got for our money. It seems the only thing that is important at Disneyland is money. It seems that no one cares about it anymore. Trash in the water, bathrooms smelled and paper and trash in the streets. I'm glad that my girls got to visit Disneyland but it will be a long while before we ever return again. It was just not a very good experience for us. Think twice about spending your money on Disney.

As Disneyland Annual Passholder's, we try to visit Disneyland once every month or every other month.All our experiences with Disneyland PRIOR to the 50th Anniversary were good. Since the 50th Anniversary began, Disneyland has been anything but the  Happiest Place On Earth . According to my husband, it was the  Most Miserable Place On Earth .On 12 10 05, I called DelivEARS to inquire about a shopping pass for 12 11 05. I was informed that I would be able to get a shopping pass for that day.On 12 11 05, my mom and I left Bakersfield for the 3 hour drive down to Anaheim to shop at Disneyland.After a very long 3 hour drive and $70. in fuel, we were told that due to filming in Disneyland no shopping passes were being issued that day. I made a verbal and written complaint to Disneyland, but Disneyland did not compensate me for the lost time or money.Then when renewing an annual pass on line, the Disneyland web site was experiencing technical difficulties and we did not get our early renewal discount of $20. I wrote an e mail addressing the web site error and asked for my discount but received no reply. I had to write a written letter accusing Disneyland of FALSE ADVERTISEMENT before I was offered my $20. discount   BUT   I had to wait in a line at Guest Services to get my $20. refund, and no other compensation was offered. As annual passholder's, we receive special mailings and offers from Disneyland. My 7 year old daughter was sent an elaborate mailer advertising the opening of the new Monstres' Inc., ride at Disney's California Adventure. The mailer gave instructions to print coloring and activity pages from the computer. Since we all like Monsters' Inc., we planed a trip to Disneyland 1 20 06   1 22 06, so we could experience the new attraction. I always check the Disneyland web site for attraction closurers, weather forecast, etc. According to the web site everything would be open except Goofy's Bounce House, The Haunted Mansion, and the Redwood Creek Challange trail. After a week of my children coloring Monsters' Inc., coloring pages, watching the movie, etc. they were very excited to ride the new ride.As we went to ride the new Monsters' Inc., ride, it was CLOSED due to some celebrity that we had never heard of being there for a media event. Obviously, this was a planned event   WHY THEN DID THE DISNEYLAND WEB SITE NOT LIST THE RIDE IN THE CLOSED ATTRACTION SECTION???Once again I made a verbal complaint, and once again Disneyland did not care. It is my opinion that Disneyland does not care about the customer   just the customer's money. Once Disneyland has your money, Disneyland does not care if you're a satisfied customer   all Disneyland cares about is having your money.Since the 50 th Anniversary, I have notice long lines, over crowding, poor service and rude cast members. Disneyland is so focused on promoting the 50th Anniversary to make as much money as possible that Disneyland does not care about customer satisfaction. Please think twice before visiting the Disneyland 50th Anniversary.

We went to Disneyland in California in the summer and we loved it. It's very fun for all ages. Our daughter loved to see all Disney characters and the beautiful shows as well as the colorful parades. For first timers, we recommend to go to Disneyland rather than Disneyworld in Florida because it's smaller and less overwhelming. The weather is also nice, not as hot as in Florida in the summer. Hotel is very reasonable and available within a walking distance to the Disneyland. We did rent a car, but you can probably survive without renting a car. To sum it up, it was a fun trip for our family.

A wonderful celebration   the fireworks and parade were great!  Hard to imagine how it will be topped after the party is over.  The hidden golden mickey's were also great fun to find.  highly recommended

Well, glad we waited 'til after the holidays to catch the 50th Anniversary version of the Disneyland we had all grown up with as native Angelenos...there were no problems with mobs until the fireworks and the exodus out of Main Street that follows, so we did some last minute shopping between 10 and 11 pm while the crowds eased up. For a Saturday it was not overcrowded at all, it just gets cramped in narrow areas like Adventure Land with strollers lined up like an RV Park. We actually got there on the late side just after 12 noon   but we had picked up our tickets first at the local Vons Market. First smart move.Had lunch right away outside the park in Downtown Disney to save a little $$$, there were no lines yet at any of the nice restaurants but we picked a Cajun fast serve spot  my po'boy sandwich was not real cheap but very generous portion with fries enough to split if you had to. They checked into our bags through the exit out of DD into the main gate area   you can find lockers outside and inside park, very small lockers at that for $6   so bring the bare minimum (leave kids home if possible)... it's a drag to schlep a lot of stuff around. But don't forget sweatshirts  coats for evening even though the sun is shining and it won't kill you to pack extra pair of shoes in case your feet hurt. The parking garage is the size of a small city. Go immediately to get your fast pass validated at the most popular ride you can't bear to miss  like Space Mountain, Indiana Jones,Pirates. After you are assigned your first time slot, you will know what to do and see around that area with shorter wait times or go to another part of the park to return a little later. Fast pass gives you 1 hour window to show up for ride, be there at the start time for almost no wait at all. At dinner time we jumped on the Monorail to the Disneyland Hotel to find a bar for drinks and appetizers   walking through Downtown Disney to the hotel we heard a great street musician and noticed long line at Rainforest Cafe. We passed knowing we had to be back on the monorail by 8:30 before it shut down for the fireworks. Wow, no crowd at the wine cellar by the pool area restaurant   shared a bottle of Pinot Grigio, filled up on complimentary fresh cheeses, fruit and crackers along with buying a couple of  o.k.  appetizers and it was a nice, mellow place to relax for awhile. This was definitely the way to go without strollers, backbacks and a mad rush to hit every attraction. BEEN THERE, DONE THAT. But, the best was yet to come   we headed back to find a spot in front of the castle as recommended by a Disney employee, staked out a whole bench before the area got roped off and took turns going to get hot drinks and something sweet the hour before the show began. Find your spot on the curb early ! It was worth every penny of admission   incredible sound system, re creations in special effects, music and narration of the most famous attractions rides; shooting flames, lasers, flying Tinkerbell larger than life and more bang for your buck than I have ever seen. Oh yeah, so the parades were off that week due to some construction and the Haunted Mansion closed to convert back from Xmas decor   you can just check the Disney website to find out the schedules ( and weather )so you won't be disappointed. Don't buy the first t shirt you see, look around the different shops, kept hearing about Showcase in Main Street for anniversary items and the staff we approached were very helpful looking for other sizes. If you want to go into Disneyland already wearing something in character check out cute tops in stores like Walmart( Tink, Hook, Mickey, Grumpy) or buy those cool glow in the dark necklaces (someplace else cheap) for night time fun. I could have gone on until midnight but the other broads pooped out. Can't wait to see the other park for free... but I'm not going back on Small World until I have grandkids ...

This definitely ain't Disney World, but still good. California Adventure was OK, but I didn't feel the Disney touch there at all (except for a few rides imported from other Disney parks).DisneyLand was good, but not as well organized as WDW. Lines were long for everything. A number of Fast Pass distribution points were broken and not available. The Fast Passes for Space Mountain were out by 2pm! And we weren't going to wait 90 minutes in the standby line. So we didn't get to that at all.Do NOT try to do both parks in one day   it's just too much. We were so tired at the end of the day. Plus you just can't do it all. So allocate at least two days, or if you only have one day skip California Adventure entirely.I was surprised how much I enjoyed the Matterhorn. Being a 1955 Original I expected it to be lame   it was exciting! Splash Mountain was great, of course. And definitely take in the history of DisneyLand movie at the Museum at the beginning of Main Street. It was very informative and funny too (Steve Martin hosts it).Anyway   with some simple planning (don't go at peak times, when school is out) you will enjoy DisneyLand. There is plenty of Disney Magic here for everyone.

I had previous wonderful experiences there, but there were soooo many people that you could hardly move, could not enjoy anything wonderful there. Disneyland is probably only after the all important buck, instead of enjoyment for their Customers. Numerous rides broke and when they reopened there was only one or two employees to control the Kaos for the line. We even had the Fast Pass equipment break. My family and I may never go back and that is a shame!
This Pic was taken at LA and Disney, It was a bright sunny day and we were hoping to get a good pic and what a terrific pic it is

This is most definately The Happiest Place on Earth. My family had the best time. We visited in October 2005, which we thought would be a slow time. Apparently, while we were there, the year round schools were on a 2 week break so it was pretty busy. We used the Fast Pass quite a bit. Unfortunately, we didn't get to see everything we wanted to, but that means now we have to go back. I'm so excited. This is the most awesome place.

My family and I went to Disneyland in Sep05 stayed at the Howard Johnson Hotel Anaheim was in building 2. Very clean rooms and staff very helpful..Pool and spa was great we sat in the spa at night and was able to see the fireworks from disneyland....Great hotel and would come back again...Loved It Thanks HOJH.Then from there went to Las Vegas stayed at the Luxor we had a room on the 15th floor in the Tower room had a great view of the strip it was so lovely at night to look at from our room. Huge hotel it was awsome if we ever get another chance to go back we will stay again.

Disneyland was awesome! But make time for California Adventure!  First the Good: Definitely stay (if you can't afford to stay on the park) at a hotel near the park. We were at the Anaheim Plaza Hotel. It was nice to just walk two lights down to Disneyland.  FastPass is the way to go. We couldn't get onto Space Mountain till day 2 of our trip. But we used the FastPass for Indiana Jones, and Buzz Lightyear. It was wonderful to just walk to the front of the line and go inside. Must Sees: Indiana Jones, Space Mountain, Buzz Lightyear, any Disney Character you can. I was 4yrs old when I first took a picture with Gepetto. And at the ripe old age of 25, I was giggly again. If you must collect autographs be prepared to stand in line. Check out the parades. It was cool to see what little we did. Ride the Monorail too! California Adventure: A breath of fresh air. We just came back from Disneyland the week after Xmas and right before New Year's. Disneyland was so crowded that C.A. was practically empty. We got great pictures of the different characters. It was soooo fun. Ride the Tower of Terror. Make sure your stomach is empty and you went to the bathroom prior to riding. California Screaming is such a well planned roller coaster. It was great.  Walk the Hollywood backlots. We got to see Turtle Talk with Crush, Muppets 3D, and sneak preview the Monsters Inc ride. Oh and I took pics with FroZone. Now the bad...If you want to go during the Holidays be prepared for the crush. The crowd had to have jumped at least 3K every day. Get there early. I'm talking around 7am. We got there at 7:45 and the lines were 200 deep. Beware of people stopping in the street. It's dangerous but just watch your step. If you plan to eat lunch at downtown disney defintely go there around 11am. When the eateries open. It helps so much. MOST IMPORTANTLY: Adults leave the grown up self behind. Kids, be yourselves! And have fun. My husband sure did. It is truly a magical place! Hope this review helps!

Having travelled to Disneyland Parks across the world, it is clear to any traveller that the Anaheim park is the the best. Well maintained, clean and well operated, Dineyland is truly the ultimate tourist attraction which provides fun for people of all ages. A trip to Disneyland is a trip into imagination, relive your childhood fantasies and enjoy a total escapist experience.Los Angeles, as a city, is lacking in many areas. It has little history and no casual commercial districts where tourists can relax. For this reason, toursits flock to the Disneyland complex in Anaheim. A holiday in Disneyland is much more enjoyable than a holiday in central L.A, especially for families.The Disneyland Park is a good size, with many fantastic attractions. The best rides fill up fast and the lines can be quite long, but if you are a patient person, you will do fine. The new California Adventure park was a pleasant surprise. With the exception of the closed  California Screaming  ride, the attractions were great fun without the long lines of the main park.Top Five Attractions (for both parks)1. Indiana Jones Adventure2. Pirates of the Caribbean3. The Haunted Mansion4. The Tower of Terror5. Soarin' Over CaliforniaFor nostalgia fans, you can see the original Haunted Mansion and Pirates of the Caribbean attractions, still in great shape and still as much fun as in the 60's when they were built. The best ride (in my opinion) is the high tech Indiana Jones Adventure, perfect for fans of the movies and anyone who wants to experience the most realistic ride on the planet!My Top Tips1. Wait in line for Indiana Jones, it never takes longer than 30 minutes no matter what the sign says!2. Instead of eating meals in the parks, cross the road to IHOP, have a $7 two course dinner and re enter the park.3. Unless you ABSOLUTELY MUST see the Fantasia show, avoid it. It gets ridiculously busy!4. During the fireworks shows, try and stay on the  Adventureland  side of the park. It is impossible to leave  Discoveryland  during or just after the show.5. The parade attracts the crowds, once you have seen it once, go on the popular rides during parade time.6. Stay in the park until closing time. Some rides take on a new life at night (Tower of Terror, Haunted Mansion).Let yourself go in Disneyland and you will never forget it!

Wewere in this magical place for the first time for both my husband and I and our two boys, ages 10 and 12. We stayed at the Park Place Inn and Suites. Very nice rooms, very clean and quiet. Nice large rooms too. We were just outside the pool so the boys could swim while we relaxed!! Loved downtown Disney and very, very impressed with how clean everything was. All the workers were extremely helpful. We used our fast passes for a few rides but the rides were not busy at all until the Friday. We were there Dec 6,7,9. Fantasmic was well worth the 2 hour wait to hold out spot to watch it. Pirates of the Caribbean was our favorite ride next to Splash Mountain. I would go again but next time leave more time for shopping. The fireworks were like nothing we have ever seen. None of the rides made any of us nautious. Just completely mezmerized by the whole place. Yes, food is expensive   you have to eat at the Rainforest Cafe, very unique setting. Boys enjoyed playing games in ESPN Zone. Very professional music played in Downtown Disney each night, very relaxing and enjoyable to listen too. Our hotel had 2 very nice gift shops with items much cheaper than in the parks. Would highly recommend this hotel. Stayed at the ocean park inn in San Diego. Had ocean front view, very nice. Extremely enjoyed our 2 week holiday, very sad to have to come back home.

Wow, as a single 33yr old guy I wasn't sure I wanted to bother going to Disneyland, but since I was staying across the street for 2 nights I figured I should since I'd never been. Turns out this was the highlight of my whirlwind 6 day  5 night SoCal trip. I spent most of one day at Disneyland at a cost of $56. This isn't bad considering the rides and most everything is free once inside. Had a few bites of good food Bengal BBQ skewer, Dole Pineapple Whirl, and Tortilla Jo's, of course this is an extra cost.You can experience the whole park in one complete day. Keep in mind they have the adjacent Disney's California Adventure where you could spend another day. I missed going on a couple rides due to having to leave for a while in the middle of the day   open 10 8 at the time I was there. Granted it is somewhat cheesy and fake, but it is  make believe  afterall. Great for the young kids and the young kids inside us adults.

Disney Land & California adventure is truly a magical experience. The resort is a spectacular combination of Walt Disney's vision of family fun and adventure. The rides are fun for all ages. There is so much to see, hear and do. The shows are fun to watch with family and friends. It's truly magical to see Mickey and Minnie walking hand in hand walking thru the park. I really loved the firework shows at night; it made me feel like a kid again. I hope you enjoy this park as much as I did. Make sure you wish upon a star, while you are there.

We, total of 8, including 4 kids, had a visit from Nov. 19 25. I couldn't of asked for a better time. Beats Florida 100%. Contrary to other reviews the park is not old. Restrooms were very clean and always well supplied. We had our 2 year old and the diaper changing area was always available and always had diaper pads, a great convenience. I was amazed that the park had healthy snacks for a change and at resonable prices. You can pick up bags of grapes, there are buckets full of fruits, trays with celery and carrots sticks throughout the two parks. Totally contrary to the many McDonalds fry stands in Florida. You can also bring in your own snacks. Location was great. Access to the two parks and Downtown Disney all from one point. Not across freeways or parking lots. Just steps away from each other. We covered both parks and Downtown Disney within three days, which gave us plenty of time to do other activities in CA. Very realistic and not as overwhelming as Disney World. Contrary to other reviews crowds were not so bad. What else would you expect at the greatest place on earth? Main street has most of the crowds, as you get futher into the park the crowds dwindle down. We got Speedpass on 2 to 3 rides the entire time, the remainder had waiting times (15 25 minutes) that were average. Everyone was extremely polite. We will definitley be back really soon.

My wife, 2 children and I spent 1 magical week in late September at Disneyland.For my wife and i it was our third visit for our children their first.....and i assure you not their last.We have theme parks in Australia yet i advised my kids in advance Disneyland is like no other place.My children through watching DVD's, the internet and reading up on Disneyland thought they were prepared.Well you should have seen their faces during our visit.Even though my wife and i had been twice before it still captures us and takes us to another world.I enjoy it all.It's not just for kids,it's for adults who posses a young heart.As an added bonus to see my children's reaction at the turn of every corner,or yet at another performance,attraction or shop was priceless.What made it even better was the new  extension  ....California adventure,though it doesnt have the same feel as the original it will in time create its own and no doubt will further grow.I cannot recommend it highly enough.This trip will be remembered by wife and i for the rest of our lives and i know that when my children grow up it will form part of their fond childhood memories.For now we have hours of recording,photos and memorabilia though we have made an agreement that we will come back as soon as possible...all of us.

My grown daughter and I were at Disneyland September 27th through September 30th. We had planned on heading home early on the 30th until we found out that the Haunted Mansion would be closed and wasn   t scheduled to re open until the 30th. So, we changed our plans to leave late the afternoon of the 30th with plans to ride the Haunted Mansion as many times as we could before we had to leave. Well, half way through the first (and only) ride, we looked at each other and said,    This      !   . They had done the ENTIRE ride (inside and out) in A Nightmare Before Christmas theme. We had our hearts set on the beloved old standard. Instead, it was barely recognizable. What a disappointment. Other than that, Disneyland was as wonderful as we   d remembered. We rode the Indiana Jones Adventure for the first time. Loved it! Ended up riding it at least 8 times.

We have been to DL twice in the past year. Once the 2nd week of January, and again at the end of August (both times for each child's birthday). Visits were like night and day as far as crowds were concerned. In Jan. the park was practically empty   it was great! However, it rained too, so alot of the attractions were closed. But we didn't care because we had a a blast on what was available and with each other. Then in Aug., naturally, it was extremely busy. And the ONLY thing that made it  bad  were the lousy attitudes of the other guests there. What horrible manners people had! We saw a woman get knocked down and trampled after the fireworks because people were more concerned with getting to the Fantasmic show that being kind to their fellow human being. The park, however, was fine. Sure, we had to miss some rides because of lines; but we spent most of our time at shows and just walking around enjoying the park itself. As for food prices   yep, it's pricey. I would think anyone planning a trip to ANY amusement park could expect that. But where else in California can you eat in the French Quarter or on a quaint Main Street? We CHOOSE to spend the money to eat in the park because it's just part of the experience. And there are water fountains everywhere that don't charge for water. We used them the whole time we were there and saved money on buying drinks. To plan a Disney trip is to know what your budget limitations are and stay within them. We are very fortunate that we didn't have to worry about finances, but if you are someone who does   hit the Disneyland website. It will give you an idea of prices in all the restaurants inside the park. The prices outside aren't any better   for my money I'd stay at the location and enjoy yourself!California Adventure is a really nice park. It's not flashy like DL, but it has it's good points. Namely that it isn't quite as busy!! We love walking the  boardwalk  and listening to the great California themed music (Mamas & Papas, Beach Boys, etc....). My husband and kids love this park almost as much as DL   and they can't get enough of Soarin', Grizzly Rapids, and Tower. I just hope by the time we head back California Screamin' is open (we've missed it both times).The secret to a fun and stress free DL trip is planning, planning, planning. Decided how much you are willing to spend on hotels, food, etc...and stick with it. Remember, some of the properties that surround DL are dumps   check out the reviews to find a good hotel near the park. And yes, location is worth the money!In the meantime, we're counting our days till we can go back. Can't wait to see that parade and fireworks again...

This was my 7th trip to Disneyland and did not dissapoint! When you live as far away as New Zealand Disneyland is a dream that only a few ever realise. I am amazed by some of the complaints by reviewers who perhaps don't know how lucky or privelaged they are to have had such an opportunity in life   perhaps in the United States people have become complacent about having such places at their doorstep and don't understand what it is to dream! When waiting in line   don't get grumpy  watch people, talk to people and enjoy the excitement on the faces of children and adults around you!   smile and the whole world smiles with you! The magic is there   it's up to you to find it. Every time I heard the recording of Walt saying  To all who come to this happy place   welcome  I got chills down my spine   this place was his dream and he made it happen.The 50th celebrations are absolutely outstanding and I was able to have one of my past trip photos included in one of the collages. This place sparkles like it was only built yesterday and no matter what rides they build (how fast or tall they are) in other parks no place will ever compare.I am doing a Western USA bus tour next August and will spend 3 nights at the Disneyland Hotel at the end   I'm excited already. My advice to all who go   don't sweat the small stuff or look for things to complain about   just enjoy!

My family just got back from a trip to the    Happiest Place on the Earth   . Believe me this was the best vacation we had in along time. We had 2 kids with us this time my 7 year old son and my 12 year old daughter. The lines to the rides were not long only a few mins and the best was Indian Jones and Space Mountain, this was on Wed and Thurs. but on Friday and Sat. it was so busy and the key is go to Disneyland during the midweek and not on weekends. And try to go off peak if you can. Prices for food are so high and they get you by that because you walk 2 miles from the front gate to Denny   s across the street. That is very hard with the little ones and you waist time. (But to save money, do this!!) We ate breakfast in the room by bringing cereal and bowls on the trip. Let me say this again    food prices are very very high in the park   . Some days we ate in the park and some days we ate around the area. In California Adventure Try Turtle talk for the little ones and also Californian Soaring they we love this!! Bugs Life was great too. Turtle talk was so funny; my 7 year old was talking about this for the rest of the trip. We were walking around and getting autographs from all the characters, just seeing the smiles on the little kids just made the trip worth while.

No wonder there is so much hype about Disneyland   its amazing. The park itself is so well done, no expense has been spared! There are many shops and things to see, once I got there I understood why people get 5 day passes! My advice is to go on a weekday, we went on a Wednesday and it was pretty quiet. The most we waited for a ride was 20 minutes (which is great). I recommend getting fast passes for popular rides or you'll spend alot of time waiting   even with fast passes we waited 15 minutes on some rides. Also make sure you pack water as food and drinks are very overpriced. You can do it in one day provided you go on a quiet day and keep moving. We got there at about 10am and left about 9.30pm and we saw everything and went on all the rides.Fantastic day, Great Experience...

I lived 20 minutes away from Disneyland until 1991, when I moved to Northern California. This is my fourth trip since I moved. Two occasions were for Christmas, and the other  non holiday  visit was in 1992. This is the first time I have spent multiple days in the park, and it was well worth it.My first visit to Disneyland was at the age of 5, in 1970. Let's say it's changed a lot. As much as I miss some of the old nostalgic items in the park, what they have done in recent years, and especially for the 50th anniversary, are wonderful. I wish I could have stayed more than 3 days. The park is very crowded on the weekends. No offense to the little ones or their parents, but getting clipped on the heels or having your feet run over by huge strollers gets old very quickly. We were there Sept. 2 4, and very thankful we had Friday in Disneyland. We spent some time in California Adventure, but since California Screamin' is closed, we didn't spend too much time there. Our goal was Disneyland, and we were able to do all the rides that we love, those we haven't tried since we were kids, and those we have never been on at all.The fireworks show is worth camping out for. If you can secure a spot in front of the castle, even 2 3 hours before hand, you will not be disappointed. It is the best vantage point for this presentation. Not to give anything away, but the castle in very much a part of the fireworks. Space Mountain is open again, and still a great ride. Astro Blasters, which has been open in Florida for a few years now, is fun for all ages. I have been to the resort in Florida, and you really can't compare the two. I am partial to Disneyland, and other than the castle, didn't really warm up to the Magic Kingdom in Orlando. We loved MGM and Epcot, and the Orlando experience as a whole, but since I grew up with Disneyland, it will always be my first love.If you haven't been to this park, it is well worth going during their 50th anniversary. Some of the items on display, such as the artwork and scale models, are an absolute treat. The photo collages are very cool.For those who haven't been in years   it's an E Ticket all the way. And for those that are really into it, the hunt for hidden Mickey's is quite fun. I found quite a few new ones, in addition to the 50th emblems.Just go   make the most of it. If you hate crowds, don't go on the weekend. And have a Monte Cristo and Mint Julep at the Blue Bayou   call ahead for a reservation. It bumps up the experience an extra notch.

Disneyland is a very exciting and magical place. Inside the park is history, and you can see the dream of Walt throughout the day. There is planty of shopping inside the park, but it's best to do it in the morning to beat the herds of people at night. Take a break in the afternoon when it is most crowded. I reccomend going back to the hotel for an hour or two to nap & change shoes. (Bring band Aids for blisters!) This way you beat the crowds, and can come back rejouvenated. We stayed at Disney's Paradise Pier Hotel, which was perfect. Great service, food, staff, value, etc. Only about 5 minute walk to Disneyland gates. Get to the parks as early in the AM as possible. Use the fastpass system. Check with your travel clubs (AAA) for special promotions including unlimited use of fastpass. If you can stand to carry a bag all day, pack waters from home, or juices. Also dried fruits or fruit snacks. Nuts, protein bars, trail mix. Any snck to keep the family going, without having to break the bank on a $3.00 12 oz. soda. If you want to try eating at a nice restaurant during your stay, it ios best to do it mid afternoon(after the luch crowd has settled, but early enough to miss the dinner crowd.) This also saves you big bucks. You get the same meal, at a luch time price. Also check out proportions EVERYWHERE before you buy. Disneyland is in America, and here we EAT BIG! So share a burger with your kid. You don't need any  large size , they are already huge. Be sure to watch some of the parades and shows. These give you a time to rest your feet, and a quite time for kids. Also very fun! Most Disneyland rides are not very scary, so don't expect huge thrills. But don't get me wrong, they are still very fun. If you venture over to california Adventure, be prepared for much shorter lines, and way less people. (Disneyland lines are long!) DCA is great, and be sure to chack out every nook & crannie. There is tons of stuff to do here, too. Downtown Disney is basically an outdoor mall. Be prepared to spend money! There are fun activites here also, for grown ups and kids. Average daily spending, with food & souveniers(not including entrance fee, parking or hotel) is about $100 a day per person. Some must sees at Disneyland are: Blue Bayou restaurant, Fantasmic show, It's a Bug's Life Show, Soarin over California Attraction, the monorail, Buzz Lightyear astro blasters, and The Emporium on Main Street. Have fun & bring at least two pairs of comfy shoes.

I would like to clarify that DisneyLand is older than  Disney World . The Florida attractions are much faster, Much NEWER, and actually replicas of what is located in Calif. Disneyland is the original, don't be confused. It's annoying to read bad things about the happiest place on earth. I went there as a child and learned patience (standing in line for Small World), how to deal with dissapointment....when I wasn't tall enough to get on a ride. Disneyland isn't about cramming as much information and rides into a day to make you feel like you got your $$ worth. It's about spending time with your kids and self, having a great time eating expensive churros(you know you spend more money in Vegas) thinking about all of the possibilities of the imagination. Stop Complaining people. lots of folks don't have that luxury. It is the happiest place on earth and some people are just miserable.

Okay so going in the middle of summer on a weekend wasn't the best choice. (Just happened to work out that way) Good God I have never seen so many people in my life. and boy are they Grumpy! We barely had time for 2 days to see do everything we wanted to. We got to ride a total of about 10 rides in the whole 2 days, due to standing in line, and making our way through the huge crowds. I bet this place would be the bomb in the off season. Fast pass is a great way to do some of the major rides, but a good portion of them don't accept them. Go when the park first opens. you'll be able to enjoy more rides in the first 2 hours then you will the entire rest of the day. Seriously. Then get fast passes for the other rides for later in the day. The rides we did get to go on were great   and the 4d movies were incredible! We had the most fun with those, and the  underground  rides than anything. (Pirates of the Carribean, Haunted Mansion and Indiana Jones) Space mountain was a blast, and scared me efficiantly. First time ever I've been on any ride that people were actually cheering when it ended. FUN! I was a little dissapointed that there weren't more rides for the littler kids   no more than any other theme park IMO. Being with 2 kids within different age preferences, we spent alot of time waiting at rides while one or the other went on with a parent. We'd stay with the 5 year old while one of us would ride something scary with the 13 year old, then switch again so both of us could see the ride. Same deal with the little rides   the 13 year old didn't want to be caught dead on the Dumbo ride. that sucked up alot of our time. If you have children of different age groups, bring a helper grandparent or wait until they're bigger to enjoy all of the park. (that is if you want to see all of the rides, as well) The Fireworks were the most amazing I've ever seen. what a show they put on. Kudos to Disneyland for that. There was so much to do and so much to see, it was unreal. We wanted to do more see more but by the 2nd night we were so tired, we didn't care what we missed!  Be advised do NOT buy drinks or food in this place. Between 4 people, for 2 days, we dropped nearly $600 in food and water drinks and one hat each for the family. Bring water with you and eat somewhere else. Be careful that the stores and restraunts immediately surrounding Disneyland are overpriced as well. California Adventure was very fun for the little one. he loved the bugs life themed area, and we rode that silly Caterpillar train like 5 times. There was also some great areas there with lots of water spraying around, and we took advantage of that   since we were all so hot. The lines there were nearly non exsistant, and the crowds much more mellow. I didn't even have to stand in line for the restroom. Again, we didn't have time to see the whole park there, as we only had a 2 day hopper and spent the first day and a half in Disneyland, and the other four hours in Cal. Adv. We missed alot there, too. Very nice feature is that if rent a stroller at Disneyland, and leave for a while   if you keep your receipt   you can get another Stroller at no cost. Works for California Adventure, too. If you rent at Disneyland and go to Cal Adv. you can get one at no cost.

If you fly into LA from overseas probably the first signal for a happy holiday on arrival at LAX airport is when one of the Customs Officers reads on your form that you are heading to Anaheim and in return they will look up, smile and say,    Headin    to Disneyland? You are going to have a great time   . There really isn   t much else in Anaheim to head there for! Our 16 year old daughter was performing with her troupe from the Young Talent School in Australia, at Disneyland and California Adventure Park as part of Disney   s 50th Anniversary and California Adventure Park opening. To make the most of our stay we purchased 5 day passes and were most thankful for the Fastpass facility on the busy rides that had long, long, long queues. We used our Fastpasses to the best of our advantage. You need to work out which rides you really want to go on and set a plan into motion. Being the beginning of the school holidays (June 2005) the parks were packed to the seams and there was no time to dilly dally if we were to get on the rides we wished to enjoy. In Disneyland we all loved the Pirates of the Caribbean and the Peter Pan ride. We were told that the Indiana Jones ride should not be missed but we never got around to trying that one. Every time we looked, the wait time was over 90 minutes! In California Adventure Park make sure you give Soarin' Over California a shot     it   s unlike any ride we have ever been on and it is probably as close to free flying like a bird that you may ever have. This ride is suitable for the young right through to the very old, although I think toddlers and younger may not be allowed on this one as there is a height restriction. Also bear in mind that C.A.P. opens later and closes earlier than the Disneyland Park. The evening parade there is fabulous though and there is time to get from one park to the other if you are fleet of foot and well prepared. The biggest disappointment for us at both parks was the lack of good food. We worked out it was best to eat a huge breakfast, and there are a couple of good restaurants near to the park entrances (not Downtown Disney), buy fruit from the stalls in Disney for a snack during the day and then escape for a good meal in the evening. We did eat at the Blue Bayou in New Orleans Square, which Disneyland classes as    Fine Dining        I think it is just the best that they have to offer. It had a nice atmosphere about it though with the ride Pirates of the Caribbean running alongside the dining area. It is advisable to book in advance if you do wish to eat here as the chances are you will be turned away and asked to try again later.If we had had our choice we would have booked to stay at one of the Disneyland resort hotels     so much handier     but we had someone else   s child in tow with us and had to choose a less expensive form of accommodation. We settled on The Sheraton Anaheim which had just one downside and that was that it was just too far to walk to and from Disneyland. They ran a good shuttle service though, the staff was all very happy and helpful and the buffet breakfast was good enough to keep us going until lunchtime. The room we had was sufficient for the four of us and in the evening the front of the hotel was a fabulous place to watch Disneyland   s fireworks.If you need a rest from the theme parks take a walk to Downtown Disney and check out the shopping. The biggest pull for us was the Build a Bear shop     and we brought back a much loved, newly built teddy. There are a lot more than just bears to choose from too. You choose an unstuffed toy, give it a name, add a heart, give it a voice, make a promise to love and cherish your newly adopted toy forever, stuff it with love and stuffing, give it a hug followed by a    fluff up   , choose an entire wardrobe for it, fill in the adoption papers and that   s it     your own    Build a Bear   . Ours is called    Brandy   ,

August 4, 2005Hello I am a single mom (widow). I have one son, (married with an 8 year old son of his own) and two teenage girls. My children wanted to go to Magic Mountain, but I suggested Disneyland. Since I wasn't sure if my grandson could go on most of the rides at the other theme park. And I used to love Disneyland. Big mistake on my part. Let me start with admission prices,  way overpriced  I paid $438.00 for 7 adults and 1 child. My daughters took 2 friends. Over $250.00 on just snacks, bottled waters, and dinner.And that does not include the money that my son and his wife spent. I couln't even afford to get my kids a souvenir this year. But that is not the worst of it. We spent most of our day waiting in line. There should be some kind of limit on how many people are allowed into the park. I know the Disney Corp. really doesn't care. All they are concerned about is raking in the money. They do not care how miserable people are spending most of their day waiting in lines, for snacks attractions, rides, food, and even the restroom. Well I was very disappointed this year. It will be a long time if ever before we go back to Disneyland. It just keeps getting worse every year. More expensive, too many people. I am sorry but it was not the happiest place on earth for myself and my children.

I have always been a fan of the Disney Organization. We go to Disney World a lot because we live on the East Coast and it is much closer. This time we decided to give Disneyland a try. Disneyland has two parks in one. the Magic Kingdom (an older version of the one in Disney World) and California Adventure. We were not impressed with the California Adventure. It is just like any ordinary park. Nothing special or magical about it. Disneyland is okay but nothing like Disney World. The stores used to be spectacular, but now they are just cheesy souvenir shops. The new  Tower of Terror  ride doesn't even compare to the one in Disney World. I think old things are sometimes better than the tacky things we construct nowadays. I don't mean to put down the park. It had it's good things too, like Soarin' the new ride in California Adventure and Autopia. I would not steer clear of Disneyland if you are in the area, but keep in mind it has some flaws.

This is not about what Disneyland is for everybody. That is a fact.We knew about the off school seasson we were visitng it, sorry there were no other time for us, even more, We knew about some loose time and delays in the operation of some attraction, but it couldn be worst.More than 10 hours in the park and could only visiting some minor attractions and three big ones, Haunted mansion, Tiki room and It's a small world, the rest even with the fast lane, were out of order, with the amusemnt park full!!!!!!; I mean it is understandable with a few attractions but all big ones!!!!!!!.I kept the fastlane tickets to show what I am saying.Wrote to Disneyland's contact....Nobody cares....The parade saved this nigthmere called visit.Before go, please find advise on the attractions's behavior

We have recently returned from a trip to Disneyland. We stayed for 6 nights at the Candy Cane Inn and had great time. The hotel was clean, the grounds were pretty, and the shuttle was wonderful! The air conditioner worked quietly. The continental breakfast was ample. We never got around to using the pool. The rooms did only have two chairs with the table. We had a standard room. Since it was just the two of us, we used the other bed for our luggage and misc. The shuttle drivers were a real plus! We were happy to be within walking distance, but have a shuttle to fall back on when our feet hurt...Since they have added California Adventure and Downtown Disney, it takes more walking than it used to! Use the fast pass system. We had great meals at the Jazz Kitchen for lunch and at Blue Bayou, also for lunch.

Our family (3 adults and 1 teenager) just returned from Southern California. We did the Disneyland, Universal Studios, Sea World, and Beach trek, and we all agree that Disneyland is tops. I am 47 years old and still love Disneyland and enjoy it as much as the kids! Disney has outdone themselves. The Dreams Come True fireworks spectacular is incredible, the best fireworks show I have ever seen. Don't be fooled, it is much more than just shooting off fireworks, it is a performance you will not want to miss, in fact, be sure to see it twice (I think it was better the second time). The best spot is in front of the trees in the circle at the end of Main Street in front of the castle if you can get there. If not, get a spot in the middle of main street as close to the circle at the end of main street as you can get. Fantasmic has been enhanced and is even bettter if you can imagine that! Don't miss the Alladin musical in Disney California, it is incredible. The Electric Parade was really cool. The special 50th Aniversery Parade was incredible (the best parade I have ever seen) and the Block Party bash was a lot of fun. Disney sure knows how to put on an increble show, party, parade, etc. Plan your shows and parades carefully, it gets very crowded and it is not easy to move from one to the other if they are relatively close together. If you want a really good place to sit or stand for any of the parades, arrive 45 minutes to one hour before they start, or you will be scrambling to find a good spot. Our family really enjoyed all the 3D * 4D shows as well as the Golden Dreams show which is really inspirational and some reaaly cool special effects is awesome. We manged to do most of it in 3 days (both parks). I wish we would have had 4 days (upgrading from a City Pass 3 day hopper or a discounted 3 day park hopper pass to a 4 day will cost you $50 per ticket, be warned). I highly recommend Birnbaum's 2005 Disneyland Resort Guide. It cost me $15 but was worth every penny. I have been to Disneyland before, but Birnbaum's guide is an invaluable resource that helped us plan our stay and went with us to the park everyday.

I think I love Disneyland more now (as a grown up) than I did when I was a kid!!! However, it's always more fun watching my 4 year old son and anyone else who's visiting for the first time. It is truly awesome, esp now with the 50th anniversary going on. MUST SEE: 50th anniversary Fireworks show   there's nothing like it. I know it's a pain to stake out and wait 'til the end of the evening, but believe me   it's quite the show! Also, the character dining experiences are superb! The best is to start the day with a character breakfast at the Plaza Inn or Goofy's Kitchen. It's a buffet and a bit pricey, but most definitely worth the premium to have some quiet time with the characters. (Once you get in the park, expect to wait in line for any photo opps with any of the characters   even the ones you don't recognize!) Oh, and if the budget allows it    stay at one of the 3 Disney hotels at least for your first night. There's something about being inside those Disney walls that makes it feel like you're possibly in another country (maybe it's like an instant exchange rate where you're losing dollars), but all the Disney touches make the hotel stay wonderful.

We just got back recently from Disneyland and we had an awesome time. We were ther May 23 28th a little bit more busy that we thought but with the 50th goin on they say every time of year will be busy. We stayed at the California Grand and with this being our first trip there I would never stay anywhere else it was awesome and close to everything!!! We also love California adventure and not near the crowds. We have two boys 11 & 6 and it was just the most memorable vacation we have ever had we can't wait to go back. Feel free to ask questions and I will try to answer.Must see shows Bugs life, Muppet's and Alladin to name a few Wonderful Time!!

Having just returned from Disneyland, I encourage anyone and everyone to visit the original Disney. Disney World is nice, but NOTHING compares to the real thing. The Walt Disney Company has perfected the 50th Anniversary Celebration Homecoming, without overdoing it. Fantasmic is a must see. Eat dinner at the Blue Bayou (and ask for a table near the water, you can have a lot of fun with the people riding the Pirates of the Caribbean! Make sure you have reservations at least a day in advance to get the time you want!). While you are waiting for your reservations, be sure to check out the Disney Gallery above Pirates.Unfortunately, Space Mountain is closed until July, however, there is more than enough to occupy your time while that ride is being renovated!Finally, I urge everyone to buy a park hopper pass and, if you don't want to see the cool  Parade of Dreams,  you can  hop  over to Disney's California Adventure and ride  Soarin' over California!  It's not nearly so busy at that time! :)Visit Disney and you will truly believe that it IS  the Happiest Place on Earth!

We visited Disneyland again May31st thru June 6th. Our last visit was in January and things are looking much better. The Jungle Cruise, Haunted Mansion, and Pirates have new scenes and special effects that really add to the experience. The new fireworks show is definately worth seeing. The new Buzz Lightyear ride is fun but the attraction itself looks kind of cheap and probably would have been better suited in Toontown. Uniformed security people now seem to be everywhere in the park. I'm sure this is to make guests feel safe but they dont seem to be very friendly or helpful. I dont think so much visible security fits in with  The Happiest Place on Earth  theme. Still the park is on the comeback trail from just a few years ago and is still the most family friendly park in California.

Just a note to say how much we enjoyed Disneyland this May. We took our two children and my mother and father, and met up with friends there as well. My three year old has autsim and we were very worried that Disneyland would be too much for him, that the characters might frighten him, etc ,etc. No way! The thought of seeing his eyes light up when we walked through the gates and saw Goofy standing there brings tears to my eyes even as I write this! He kept looking at us all like  Am I the only one here seeing a 7 foot Goofy standing here?  It was a magical time for us all.For those of you with special needs children, please note that you can go to Town Hall on Main street and request a Special Assistance Pass. These passes are given out on a case by case basis and it allowed our son to wait in a quiet area rather than in the regular line. It is NOT intended to be a  go to the head of the line  pass, though we often did get on the rides quicker. All but one of the castmembers were very polite and understanding about our use of the pass, and I suspect the young man that wasn't so nice couldn't see anything obviously wrong with our son, so he assumed maybe we were pulling a fast one (apparently people used to really abuse the use of these passes). We used this pass at both Disneyland and California Adventure, and for people who really need it, it was invaluable. Feel free to email me if haveany questions about it.There is also a rule at disney that if you have a small child that can't ride a ride, but another that wants to, you can have a child ride a ride with one parent, then get a pass to ride the same ride with the other parent without having to wait in line again. We used this only once or twice but it was nice. Also, I HIGHLY recommend doing the character meal at the Goofy cafe in the Disneyland hotel. It is pricey ($12 for kids 3 and up, $25 for adults), but it is not to be missed, esp. if you are looking to have lots of one on one time with the characters! The food was pretty good (buffet style), the characters come right up to your table to sign autographs and take pictures, and they do impromptu dancing (like the YMCA and the macarena) with the kids involvement. My son freaked out a little bit when Snow White's evil stepmother came around, but when she saw that he was frightened of her, she would make a point to avoid even walking by our table. It was totally awesome!Finally, if you are taking small children I suggest you stay close enough that you can go back to your room during the afternoon and take a nap. That way, you can go back for the fireworks and evening activites refreshed. It sure worked for us!Travel during the off season if you can (we went in May and that worked out great), and go during the week to avoid crowds. And above all enjoy the time with your loved ones!

We were at Disneyland May 3, (4th was closed), 5, & 6 of 2005. On the third we walked onto all ride with less than 5 min wait if any wait at all: we did all of disneyland that day. The 5th was crazy, grand opening for the 50th anniversary. People waited 4 hours staking out a spot to see the parade and rides were 40min to 2 hours long of a wait. We showed up 15 min before the parade and found a great spot (dont waste 4 hours). California adventures was not very busy (15 20 waits) so we spent the day there. The 6th we went shopping and walked around; too busy for the rides. It was a great time. They do check bags when coming into the park and food is expensive there also. I would advise going during the week when kids are in school and not during the holidays. Also go on all the rides, even ones that look too scary, its well worth it. Remember its all safe so have fun.

My sister and I first visited Disneyland in mid May 2003. Exactly 2 years ago to the date.We had always dreamed of going there when we were kids but in our thirties we got to go and it was 50 times better than we could ever dream.We reckon that you need 5 days to see everything including California adventure park. We were not disapointed one bit, but loved every minute of it as it was better than we had ever dreamed and the best part is IT'S NOT JUST FOR THE YOUNG IT'S FOR EVERYONE.My sister and I are taking my daughter there this coming September so she can not only have her 11th birthday there but experiance a chance of a lifetime.

I just returned to New Zealand after my husband and 2 boys (5 and 7) visited Disneyland from 25 28 April 2005. We had the most wonderful time there as a family and even though it cost us several thousand dollars to get there it was one of the best family times we have had together. We got a 3 day hopper ticket. There were lots of people but the park handled it well. I had bought in advance the guide book   The unofficial Guide to Disneyland 2005  by Bob Sehlinger. This guide rates all the rides by a star system so you can go directly to the best rides. There are touring plans but we didn't stick to them. We only had to wait 10 15 minutes at the most and used the fast pass system as much as possible.The only disappointments were that the park was only open until 7pm at nights and several of the attractions were under repair. We did however get to see the new fireworks display from our room at the Fairfield Inn, as they seem to be practising letting them off for the 50th anniversary celebrations.I still think Disneyland is great, I went there 30 years ago and it has lost none of it's magic. We are already planning our next visit there!

I'm 25 years old and this July I'll be taking my eleventh trip to Disneyland. I can honestly say it's the BEST place to go for fun. Although I have to say I don't suggest going there over the Christmas holiday. I did just this past year in 2004. It's the most crowded time of the year. I had gone the previous summer and it wasn't nearly as crowded that time. The majority of the visitors during the holiday season are sick and coughing in everyones face. I'd have to say the best time to go is the summer on a week day. If you go during the least crowded time of the year, usually in October, that's when the Matterhorn is shut down for refurbishment. What's a trip to Disneyland without a ride on the Matterhorn? I have so many special memories of Disneyland and look forward to the many more that will come. :)

The wait was over and we left Canada for our looong anticpated trip to Disneyland. Did much research on prices, and land is cheaper than world! biggest tip: take morning flights, get in afternoon , have good supper and rest before going to the parK. We loved everything! My kids are 12 and 14 and both had a blast. First major trip for my husband and he is talking about when we can return! We went end of Feb, and had no problems with line ups. We only did 2 days at park and soooo disappointed! Should have gone 3 4 days, just because there is so much to see and do. leave one day just for buying the souveniers. Tip: downtown Disney is opened much later, and can buy anything that you may have seen earlier inside the parks. save your searching till later, go on rides and shows! We also took water and granola bars, no problem at gate search, shared lunch burgers and drinks and ate supper off park to save more money. We stayed at the Carousel Inn, just 5 min walk to main gate(good hotel). Disappointed with some attractions that were closed, but Alladin and Soarin over California more than made up for it. Off season: good for no line ups, but bad for small stores not open, especially by California screamin, paradise pier. Grizzley rapids area reminded us of our home area (smell of the pine trees) which was pretty cool. Also, Digital camera is the way to go. if you like pictures get the biggest memory card and go wild. Tons on  kodak  moments! Absolutly loved rollarcoasters, 4 d shows (honey I shrunk the kids, bug's life) and Alladin! The Characters and staff were very friendly and helpful any time. We want to back in Dec next time, just to see what the christmas decor will be then. Also! WEAR COMFORTABLE SHOES! got blisters with all the walking we did! We also took in Universal Studios, great and SeaWorld was cool too. A little disappointed with the zoo, we love the Calgary zoo....overall. wonderful trip, can't wait till we can come back.

We were at Disneyland on Friday 4 8 and at California Adventure on Saturday 4 9. We got in at 10:30 and there was about a 5 minute wait to go thru the bag inspection tables and another 5 to go thru the turnstiles. A friend of ours already bought us the SoCal 2fer tickets and so we didn't have to line up for tickets. By the way, we are not from SoCal but our friend was. Apparently they only check IDs when they sell the tix but not at the turnstiles because we got in without anyone checking to see if anyone in our group was from SoCal. By the time we got in, the park was teeming with people already. I had planned to go to the Winnie the Pooh ride first thing, but a character sighting derailed that plan. Because of our late entry and judging from my son's reaction to the park so far (it was our first time at the park) I realized I had to ditch my well researched plan (I researched many internet sites and more than a couple of guide books for this trip) and just  go with the flow.  Next stop was the Dumbo ride. We waited for almost 45 minutes to get on, but it's a good first ride for preschoolers. Dumbo was a familiar character and the ride is really easy to take and gave my son a sense of control (since he could make Dumbo fly higher or lower) over the situation. After that my son warmed up more to the idea of getting on the rides than meeting characters. So we did a couple in succession   Pinocchio's ride (not worth waiting in line for), Gadget's roller coaster (exciting enough ride for preschoolers but not too scary for protective moms). Then we watched the Snow White show which was a good break from all the walking and standing in line. Before we went on the rides we got a FastPass for Buzz Lightyear's Astro Blasters. And so by the time we finished the 2 rides and the show, it was close to our FastPass time. We squeezed in a quick lunch at that eating area in Tomorrowland and was pleasantly surprised with a Buzz Lightyear appearance. I think he's there most times of the day for about half hour appearances and then he takes a break and comes back again later. The Astro Blasters ride was a blast. It was the best ride according to my son (who's 4). At the end of the ride, I got to email a picture of us and our scores to my home email account. It's a great souvenir. We went back to our hotel (HoJo across the street   will post another review for the hotel by itself) for an afternoon nap. We went back to Disneyland around 7pm via the ART (cost us $3 roundtrip) and this time we needed to wear light jackets as the air was getting quite chilly. We went on the Pirates of the Caribbean ride and the lines were moving quickly because people were flocking to the waters' edge to save their seats for Fantasmic (yes, it was 2 hours away but the roped off areas were filling in fast). My son realized he needed to use the bathroom just as we were about to get on the boats and the cast member was kind enough to let us use the bathroom and come back thru the exit and not wait in line again. The ride was too scary for my son (he doesn't like spooky noises and the ride starts off with that) although he wasn't bothered by the 2 sudden drops in the ride. When you exit from the ride, you enter a replica of New Orleans' French Quarter which was neat for someone who's been at the real place. As we exited from that land, Fantasmic was just starting and we managed to squeeze into a spot near Tarzan's treehouse where I made my son stand on the fence giving him a good view of the show. Tarzan's treehouse itself was blocked off. He called it the Magic Mickey show because the lights, sound, and holographic effects were just awesome. He wanted one last ride and I made him choose between Winnie the Pooh or Buzz Lightyear. He chose Buzz and patiently waited for almost an hour in line just to get in. By this time it's already close to 10pm and the lines are still that long. So if you can get FASTPASSES to this ride, do so. By the time we exited, there was hardly anyone along Main Street most people were staking out their places for the 2nd Fantasmic show. By the way, I was surprised to see that Disneyland is dark at night. I didn't get to appreciate the buildings and other sights because apart from the streetlights and the lights from the shops and entrances to the rides, there was not much illumination. However, there were still a few characters milling about and we got some photo ops with Pluto and Chip n Dale. The next day, another late start for California Adventure. This time you could tell that the locals were out in full force. So much more people than Friday, more kids and teens and less  tourist y  people looking at maps and looking like they were lost. I made a beeline for the Soarin' over California FASTPASS station. We were there around 10:45 and our FASTPASS time was already for 1:35. In between we caught mostly shows in the Hollywood area. Muppets 3D was fun for my hubby and I because we recognized the characters from when we were growing up watching the Muppet Show. It was fun for my son to experience the 3D effects. After that we caught the Aladdin show which was awesome! They even had Aladdin riding an elephant around the Orchestra section. If you sit on the Orchestra, you see the  parade  up close and you're closer to the stage. If you stay on the Mezzanine, you get to see Aladdin and Jasmine and then later the Genie closer as they soar in their magic carpet ride. Along the way to these shows, we saw the lion from Jojo's Circus and also Mr. & Mrs. Incredible; a Disney princess was there too but my son wasn't interested. There wasn't any signs indicating they were going to be at a certain place, it was all by chance. We had lunch at the Burger station served by McDonalds at Paradise Pier. The meals were about $2 more expensive than they were at regular McD's outside of Disney. Then my hubby and son rode the Zephyr which was on again after an earlier period of time when it was closed down. There was no reason posted why it was closed earlier. This ride lasted maybe a minute, if at all. Not worth a long wait. We walked to Bug's Land where they rode Heimlich's chew chew train which amused my son. Again, a very quick ride. But maybe worth the wait for it's cuteness factor. Bug's Land by itself is a  cute place  so definitely worth a visit for preschoolers. We also got on the bumper cars shaped like one of the characters in the story. By then it was past the time for our Soarin' FASTPASS. But apparently, as long as you come after your designated time, you can still get on the FASTPASS line. So even though our time was set for 1:35   2:35, at 4pm they still let us on the FASTPASS line. There was also a singles line that seemed to go as fast as the FASTPASS line. That was another awesome ride.
