Although I'm afraid of heights and get queasy pretty easily, the special effects of the ride was enough to distract me from my queasiness and I actually enjoyed it. My son liked it so much he wanted to get on again. But at this time, the standy line was going to take over an hour before they could get on the ride, so no way was I going to stand that long. We had another event to go that night and so that was the end of our Disney visit. Although I didn't follow my detailed plans, I still ended up enjoying the trip. Everyone else was right in saying that one day is not enough to experience ALL of Disneyland or DCA, but if you're willing to skip some attractions and be spontaneous about what you can do, the visit will still be fun and memorable.

We took a family vacation to Disneyland in March of this year and what a great time we had. We have three boys ages 14, 12 and 10 and we also met up with family and close friends. We had an excellent holiday, noone wanted to come home. We did the 3 day hopper passes Disneyland was excellent the staff were very friendly and very helpful. We did the week before spring break and we basically walked onto every ride in the park I think the longest we waited in line was 15 minutes, certain times of the day were busy and the fast passes were great. I would certainly recommend bringing in your own food as it is very expensive, we had lunch one day and it came to $80.00 and it was awful very greasy, the churros were great though!! Universal Studio's was really good the charter bus picked us up at our hotel and took us there, the driver was great, very helpful and talked the whole hour's drive there about what was good to see and what shows we should see and everything he recommended was worth seeing and they then pick us up at the end of the day and take up back to the hotel. it was $125.00 cdn for us a family of 5 round trip, but a taxi ride was $140.00us only one way. It is well worth the shuttle service. We also did Medevil Times dinner it was good expcept the shuttle service again picked you up and took you there, but we found it was too early, we took in the 7pm show and we were there at 5:30 a lot of hanging around not much to do while you were waiting the show was good and so was the food, they really get the audience participation in the show. We had really good weather sunshine the whole week, sweater's are definitely needed at night but that's okay, California Adventure was good as well the favourites there were Grizzly River Run you get soaked though I think we did this one 6 times, Soaring over California is a must see, and also the Screamer was a favourite with the teens!!A good time was had by all.

If you're planning a trip to Disneyland, definitely plan to stay for at LEAST two days, if not three. You will NOT be able to do everything you would like to do in one day, or even two! There are too many conflicting Show schedules, too many predictably long lines queus for rides, and there are too many characters that you'll bump into for you to even try to plan around. There are over 100 characters in the park at any given time anyhow, so if that's what you're going for, get a Times Guide. It'll tell you when what characters will be out and where, in a general sense (which is all they can guarantee anyway, as thing happen and schedules change without notice). I don't recommend going JUST to hunt down characters, as they are so highly advertised, their lines fill up very quickly and people get turned away a LOT. Autograph books are a fun little quirk, but the characters really slow down when that's all people want. They turn into autograph machines instead of being in character and making fun experiences for the  Guests,  which is what they are there for. The books are meant to be an ice breaker, a reason to approach them, something to start a conversation with, not a mission in life that cannot be thwarted! Most of the tension in Disneyland comes from Guests getting too caught up in that part of it, and they end up fighting with eachother and being childish, while the REAL kids could care less whether or not the character can write it's name (unless the parents have pushed it so much that the kids think that's the reason they have to meet them, which you'll see a lot of). If you're just coming for one day, pick about four rides you really want to go on, and pick one or two shows you really want to see, and work around that. And you can always go meet Mickey in his Toon Town house if you need a character fix, he's there the entire time Toon Town is open, without fail. Relax and enjoy Disneyland! Oh, and kindness is rewarded WAY more often than being a jerk, so be nice to people and you're more likely get special treatment. (People who complain and are mean to Cast Members OR other Guests generally get shafted on things, and it's a waste of the mean people's time and the Cast Members who have to deal with them.)

We just got back from a week in Anaheim, during the Canadian Spring break and it was a nightmare. I knew it would be, and we were prepared, we had 5 day park hopper passes, but it was still overwhelming. If you are on limited time, and you have small kids, try and get a character breakfast in. We took our daughter to the Princess Breakfast, expensive, but she got to meet all Princess' and the breakfast was awesome, they do not rush you out. My nephews went to the Goofy breakfast and were happy with it as well, good way to see all the Characters at once. Toon Town was fun for younger kids, and we found a hot dog place that had a good kids meal which included a lunchkit to take home. The food in DCA, at the wharf was a good value as well. We didn't eat many meals in the park, and were happy with it when we did. Pop was a big rip off though, $2.75 for a small bottle, bring your own. Line ups at rides were awful, sometimes up to 2 hours long, I have no idea who would wait that long for a ride, but obviously lots of people did. We went back one night at 9:00 and walked onto every single ride, that was a riot. The Fast Pass is great, works really well.

We just returned home from a wonderful trip March 7 16 2005. We decided to come down before Spring Break to beat the crowds and we were very thankful....The weekdays were wonderful with hardly any waits on any of the major rides. When we returned on March 15th it was really crowded as Spring Break had started already for many. It is definetly worth going in the off season. So much more enjoyable and more fun for the kids. Who wants to spend hours in line for a few rides? If we go again we will be packing our food. It was really expensive. We bought three small pre packaged fruit smoothies and it came to $13.50..yikes! We had never eaten at the Blue Bayou so we reserved a spot for dinner. The food was really good but the cheapest meal was $22.95. The portions were huge for my Mom and I. We should have shared a meal. It cost over $100.00 which is pretty pricey for a theme park. The restaurant....I believe it was the Plaza Pavillion where you used to be able to get a wonderful roast beef meal has really gone down hill food wise. I had the roast but I don't know what the meat was....it was awful and expensive and I don't recommend eating there. Disneyland is starting to look better and better. Two years ago it was looking really run down but this trip it was starting to look like it used to along time ago. I hope the new management keeps it up. We had a wonderful time, much more enjoyable though when the park isn't so packed with people. Thunder Mountain was our favorite ride, especially at night.

Disney land was great , if you want no waiting go during the week in the off season . We went feb 8 10 2005 , no more than 5 mins wait and never needed a fast pass. Bring food and drink in back packs as the park food is extremely expensive.

Our family visits Disneyland every year, our most recent visit being the last week of january. This is a very good time to go. Very few crouds , no need to use fastpass, and you can get on all the rides with hardly any wait. We always take our own bottled water and snacks with us and have never been hassled about it. If you look around, most of the other guests are doing the same. It just costs to much to buy in the park. This visit, we really noticed the price hike of merchandise. The same cup that I bought my 3 year old last year for 4.00 was 7.00 this year. I didn't see too many people with shopping bags and the stores were not crouded at all. I think Disney is outpricing themselves and maybe if they lowered the prices a bit, they would sell more. The ride height requirements need to be changed. Tower of Terror and Thunder Mountain Railroad is kind of wild for a 40 inch child height requirement where as Grizzly River run is more easy going and the height requirement is 42 in. And what is up with the Matterhorn? When you ride it, it is like riding on a jackhammer. It was never that rough before. We really enjoy both parks, but it would be really great if the monorail, or some kind of people moving system, would be routed through DCA with a stop there to make park hopping easier. From our experience, food in the park is good, but pricey. Most of the surrounding eateries outside the park are not to cheap either and average or below for food quality. Disneyland is fun for all, but not when it is crowded. You must plan ahead and go in the off season and bring plenty of your own snacks and drinks.

I agree with Canberra, Australia and the the last reviewer. It's all in understanding the crowd patterns and adjusting your expectations or your plans accordingly. DO YOUR RESEARCH BEFORE GOING, ESPECIALLY IF YOU DON'T HAVE AN UNLIMITED SUPPLY OF MONEY OR CANNOT HANDLE LARGE CROWDS.We carefully picked the timeframe   Dec 12 to 17 and were blessed with good weather, small crowds (we did some rides again, and again, and again until we were tired of them with no more than 5 minute wait times). The park opened at 10am and closed at 6:00 8:00 but we had plenty of time to do everything and have the kids in bed by 10:00. I was actually glad the timings didn't extend till midnight!! The Christmas decorations were amazing.The shows were fabulous, and our 6 year old's eyes lit up each time we entered the parks. We liked the California Adventure park A LOT and spent about half our time there. Interestingly, very few people mention it.We had 5 day park hopper passes (bought using our airmiles) and stayed at the HoJo   a short 7 minute walk away. The HoJo was amazing   2Q, big room, extra sink, very clean, great staff, good looking pool area and hot tub (which we didn't use) for USD 66 a night. Tip   Sun to Thurs night rates are lowest. We carried lots of snacks, drinks, water etc. which really helped. You can get cups of ice from any vendor if necessary.A few final tips comments:  Lots of walking.   Start early, end late. Have a strategy to pace yourselves.  Eat two meals outside (or keep them small) and enjoy one meal in the park. Yes, it's expensive, but it is something to look forward to when everyone needs a break.  Use FASTPASS. It blew me away that people would line up for 30 minutes while my kids and I walked past them to do rides a couple of times over using FastPasses.  Take 5 days to enjoy the parks if you can. I can't imagine what people do in 1 2 days, especially in the summer. At that pace it becomes a chore rather than something to enjoy and absorb.  Kids should be at least 6 7 to fully appreciate the ambience and keep pace with the rest of the family. We saw mothers with babies and frustrated parents with tired tots. The kids would probably have been happier in a local playground!All in all, a great experience. The Disney magic lives on!

I have been visiting Disneyland annualy for 35 years. In the last 10, every year another great attraction is abandoned. First it was the skyway, then it was the peoplemover, the motorboat cruise, the submarine voyage, mission to mars, the penny arcade, the keel boats, the main street electrical parade, and now sleeping beauty's castle walk thru will not be reopening for the 50th anniversary. To be fair, there are a few things the disney management have added. $50 a person per day for less attractions than before. Plenty of cash generating retail and restaurant spaces that use to be attractions. Multiple rides closed for months and sometimes years for refurbishment. Shorter operating hours for people who like seeing less for full price. The only good thing about Disneyland is enjoying the remaining original attractions that Walt built. I wonder what attraction will disappear in 2005?

It's Christmas time... and you thought there would be no crowds?! LOL!Christmas Day and the 26th Disneyland was declared 'full' by 3:00 pm both days. My family and I had 'Hopper Passes' and had a GREAT time in both Disneyland and California Adventure. My sons 9,11,13 and mom of 81, knew the crowds would be thick. Don't forget, both Rose Bowl Teams were in the park too. Did I mention the BIG rain storm?Well we stayed at the Candycane Inn. Very nice, clean hotel. You can walk to the Park. We ordered dinner from an Italian place that delivered to our hotel. Their prices were very reasonable.We knew going at this time of year there would be large crowds. But you deal with it, go to the park early, get your Fast Passes. Leave the parks about 4 pm. Then head back about 8:00 pm. It was open until Midnight. I must admit, we skipped the parades. Space Mountain was closed. But what fun to ride the Matterhorn in the pouring rain!! Had a wonderful time by all!Thanks, Northern California

I'm very sorry to read the review below from the person who visited Disneyland just before Christmas and had a bad time   I can only imagine how disappointing that was.We visited in early December and had the best holiday of our lives. Crowds were non existent and we walked straight on to most attractions and never queued for more than 20 minutes.This made all the difference   I can see how how huge crowds and queues would wreck the holiday. But for us it was a magical place   great atmosphere, wonderful staf, and superb rides.We had a choice of doing Disneyland at the start of our holiday, or at the end, just before Christmas. But a little research told me the later option was the busiest week of the year and to be avoided at all costs. If you have the flexibility, plan your trip for the slow times (September to mid December, and mid January to March   avoiding holiday weekends like Thanksgiving and MLK) , try to go weekdays rather than weekends and you will have the best holiday ever.

Visited Disneyland and California Adventure between December 18 and December 22, 2004. Food in parks is typical amusement park fare. Could use more variety and healthier choices. The rides are banal but for children below ten it is more than adequate. Could have definitely used more Fast Pass. Overall, Disney is cleaner than other parks and personnel are more attentive and appear to be better trained than the typical ride operators. Lines can be frustrating and daunting.

We were visited the Disneyland Resort on Dec 20th to Dec 22th and here are our observation:The park is overcrowded with people and even with the best effort from the staff, is was a dissaster. The average wait for all the rides ranging from 30 min to 2 hours, yes, two hours for a five minutes ride. Somebody will suggest fast pass, but face this, a certain ride can only accomodate a certain amount of park goers per hour, it does not stretching the time or reduce the number of people waiting in turn so it a zero sum game.There is only one bathroom facility per cluster of attraction, says Toon Town, somebody just try to squeeze more rides into same amount of space without giving additional bathrooms or rest areas.The train ride around the park is fine during daylight but at night is totally dark around you with very few lighting, it's very scary for little children to say the least.There is very few signs or kiosk for direction to go from one area of the park to another. The staff at the entrance does not giving out the map or giving instructions to where a particular attraction is.Half way throught the park openning hours, there are trashes everywhere, don't blame the staff for not keeping up, I have seen them tried to sweep the trashes while hordes of people streaming around and kicking the trashes around. The real problem is overcrowded condition. I'm supprised that the fire department is not cited this park for safety condition.The saving grace for the trip is not the park itself but the people of Anaheim (hotel maid, grocery clerk, laudromat owner) who're showing their friendliness and hospitality. We will be back but will patron different local attractions instead.The magic is gone, only the quest for money remains at Disneyland.

We were in Disneyland for the week of Nov14 21.I took my 13 year old daughter and my husband,itwas their first time to disneyland,and I hadn't been there in 20 years.I don't care who you are,walking into the main gates and seeing the castle we all grew up watching on t.v every sunday night,was an amazing experiance.I believe that going at the low time is the best time to be there.The lines during the week are so short,I think the longest we waited was 10 min for the more popular rides.The fireworks are some of the best we had ever seen,and the fact it snowed in disenyland was a very nice touch.The best part of the experiance was to watch my oh so cool 13 year old being a little kid again.She was in awe of it all.Her favorite was the tower of terror.She said she loved everything about the park.The different disney charecters were easily accesible for pictures,and were so kind to have you take as many pictures as you liked.Even my husband said he would have no trouble going back again.The food in the park was very expensive,but what do you really expect.It is just like every other attraction place so don't be surprised.the rides, the shows,the people were all so amazing.It was a little disappointing that some of the rides were closed,but that just gives you more reason to go back one day.I'm glad I spent the money and time to share the wonderful experiance of Disneyland with my family,and I would definatley go back to the happiest place on earth.

It'd been over 25 years since I'd been to Disneyland, so my expectations were a little different. I didn't expect rides to be  under repair ,  will reopen May '05 ... And having read all about going on an off season time, I figured mid November would be fine, I didn't think that Veteran's day was that big of a deal  but now I know  we actually hit the crowds on Veteran's Day Wednesday, and what do think, it turns out most of California's kids had a long weekend off... meaning crowded!It was a shame that some of the bigger rides weren't on line... and some favs like the Tiki Room were under repair...I was amazed at how some of the rides have been redone to reflect current popular themes... the Swiss Family Robinson tree house is now  Tarzan based... the Monsato shrinking microscope ride has been updated to the  Star Tours  experience... I recognized some of the older rides basic structures... with new dressings...Food in the park was pricey  and uggg not very good. How can you mess up a cheese burger? Yipes.The bigger restaurants in  down town Disney  a strip of land between Disneyland and the new California Adventure Park... were ok  we ate at the Rain Forest Cafe a couple of times... fun having a little show with dinner...Interestingly, CA was almost empty  but Disneyland proper was packed packed packed! The fireworks show was cancelled three minutes in... and left the gathered crowd of what seemed to be 6 thousand of my new best friends (jammed onto mainstreet)a little shall we say bummed... I felt like a sardine ready for canning... one of those times when you're not deciding which way to walk... you're just following the flow and hoping for the best.The lines were fairly long, we we're in line at the Peter Pan ride as it broke down twice... back in the early 70's I can't recall rides breaking down... or being put under repair for months at a time... I guess Disneyland is really showing it's age.But I'd say the  magic  was still there... you just have to  imagine  a little harder.: )

My son and I spent the week of Oct. 25 31 at Disneyland & California Adventure. Even though I took him out of school, I wanted our first time to Disneyland to be special, not fighting the crowds, waiting in line, the heat, ect. The first day we went was on Tuesday and we got right on the rides, into attractions, got a table to eat, everthing. It was really nice. There is alot to see & do, but being with an eleven year old, we were able to see & do everything in three days and then do it all over again. If we ever go again, we would definately go Mon thru Thurs. It was packed Friday thru Sunday and the only way you could get on the popular rides was with the Fast Pass tickets, unless you wanted to wait in line for an hour. The people that worked there were very nice & helpful. I am not going to complain about the food & drink prices, because that is what you are going to pay when you go to the movies. There were some rides that were down, but if you haven't done them, you won't miss them. Overall we had a great experience and would do it all over again.

I will agree that Disneyworld is the happiest place on earth. Disneyland is definately the unhappiest place on earth after fighting crowds for only a few hours. Disneyland is in dire need of customer service and reconstruction to accomodate the crowds. Each theme park in Disneyworld seems to cater to specific age groups. My son being three years old doesn't need rides that rip his teeth out of his mouth. The MGM Theme Park in Disneyworld catered to smaller rides, puppet shows and low key entertainment. The park has much more room to walk around and lots of stands to buy small items like hot dogs, pretzels, popcorn, ect. Disneyland you will find only snacks that do not contain any other item but sugar...candybars, ice cream bars, soda pop, slushes, etc. If you want real food in Disneyland expect to stand in line at the only 1 or 2 walk up grills, and expect it to be spendy for a sandwich and soda. Oh, there are other restaurants that you can sit down and enjoy a lunch, but for a family of four it will really get spendy. The nice people at Disneyworld never hassle you about your backpacks with one or two bottles of water and a few snacks for your toddler. At Disneyland it is worse that going through airport security. They will confiscate anything edible they can dig out of your bags. My advise....save up the money for flight tickets and spend your money at Disneyworld. It is worth it to visit Mickey and Friends in Florida. You will have a really good time and be treated like royalty.

It was Disney but I knew I was in the Anaheim area. This was my first time in Disneyland after visiting WDW, 3 times early in the 90's. The 'Land' is right in the middle of a city and it shows. The 'World' is located miles away from the city and off the freeway in Florida and there is nothing to indicate that there is anything else around you. (From the Califonia Adventure theme park I could see the Coast hotel.) The 'World' immerses you into the Disney experience whereas the 'Land' gives you a taste of it. It even has its own transportation system. At the time I went, WDW did not advertise itself on billboards just the directional signs off the freeway. Our Disneyland package had the 5 day hopper and it took that long to get acquainted with the  feeling.  For our first anniversary, my wife and I had a good time but I had an overwhelming need to show her the 'World.' Other notable things 3 rides broke down while I was there   the young staff did not really know how to manage the crowds; they were energetic but inexperienced at crowd control   finally the people seemed to push and shove as if they were at any amusement park (which it is) but they lacked a restfulness felt at a RESORT which puts you into another 'WORLD.' There is a difference and it depends on what you want to experience.

We took our 3 year old, he had such a fun time and so did we, but knowing it made him so happy... it was so much more enjoyable! We focused on taking him on all the rides, meeting the Disney Characters and buying him the neat Disney toys...the prices are high, but so worth it! The lines were long, but went by pretty quickly...September is really the best time to go, not as crowded as in the summer and the weather is perfect! California Adventure was great for the shows such as Disney's Playhouse and Bugs Life 3 D show and of course the Electric Parade, a classic!!

July 15 20, 2004 Disney's magic is alive and well. This summer I spent five days and nights at Disneyland and Disney's California Adventure. The weather was pleasent. The park was pristine! The new healthy food choices were welcomed by me. I thought that the entertainment was excellent. Disney offers a great value for vacation dollar spent. Their attention to detail is always noticeable and appreciated by me. I loved being at the original park for its 49th anniversery! I usually vacation at Disney World, but the climate is so comfortable in California compared to Florida. I think DCA is an awesome addition to Walt's dream and I look forward to seeing future growth and attractions. Disney, you have done it again! Kudos!

I went to Disneyland last month, and it was my first time at the Anaheim. I have previously been to the Paris twice.We stayed at the Coast Anaheim (not recommended at all) which was a good 20 minutes away. We were there from the 25th to the 28th of July. We arrived at the park at about 8.30am, and it's better arriving at this time as there are hardly any queues for rides (there was a 5 minute wait at the Indiana Jones ride!). It usually gets busier at about 10am, but then you can get a fastpass ticket. However, when we were there no fastpasses for Pirates of the Caribbean or the Haunted Mansion, although we went on these first and hardly queued.I was very disappointed to find out that the Thunder Mountain was broken for a few days, and this was my favourite ride at Disneyland. Space Mountain was also not working, and won't be until 2005. The Matterhorn Bobsleds also broke down while we were queueing and the Haunted Mansion broke down when we were on it! (I'm not sure if this is a part of the ride as it happened at the Paris once out of about 4 times I went on it. It's also a different theme than the one in Paris, so if you've been there and were hoping that you'd understand what the jilted bride was saying during the introduction, you'll be disappointed!) Unless you like being bored, don't do Star Tours.The Matterhorn Bobsleds were great, as was Indiana Jones. In the California park, the river rapids ride is a must! Also tried California Screamin' (didn't like it! If you love rollercoasters though, you'll love it!)Another must is the Electrical Light Parade!I thought the place would be very congested and busy, but it wasn't as bad as I thought.I think that everyone should have at least one experience of Disneyland!

Everytime we go to the Magic Kingdom it's a new and different adventure.This time we utilized the Fast Pass sytem for several rides...It really worked!Especially for the awesome thrill ride Indiana Jones the line was tremendously long and we just fast passed by everyone and waited no more than five minutes to enjoy the thrill!I only wish that more rides had fast pass!

Loved Disneyland! My family had a great time seeing old favorites in Disneyland and exploring the California Adventure side. Downtown Disney was a great break inbetween the parks. Great restaurants and great service. My favorite area was the Hollywood side. Saw the Aladdin show twice. The Hollywood Tower was the best new ride. The Golden Dreams show in the Bay Area was very moving. Only rides down were Alice in Wonderland and Space Mountain. Met all of the Disney princesses and saw characters all day long.

My family and I went to Disneyland for the first time ever. That includes my parents, sister, brother, sister in law, husband and our four kids. All 11 of us had the best time ever. My parents got the biggest thrills watching their grandkids see their favorite characters in person. I was expecting the worse when it came to meeting Disney characters let alone getting a picture taken with them. But the park has the best set up. As soon as the characters came out, a cast member would form a line and everyone would get a turn. It was such a great experience. We are definitely making plans to go again next year. Also I wanted to mention that Fastpass is the best! I don't know how we would have done without it.

My family and I went to Disneyland in February 2004. It was a real magical experience. We loved it, although we kinda felt a bit 'ripped off', as 3 major rides were closed, Space Mountain, Indiana Jones and Thundermountain railroad, also there were NO FIREWORKS which was really disappointing. It was very busy, they said even busier than at Christmas, so for it being so busy I don't know why they didn't have fireworks. In CA the Electrical Parade only ran on Saturdays, when we were there it rained on Saturday so the parade was cancelled (another rip off). You spend so much time planning and saving for a family holiday and when these things happen it is disappointing.

we spent four days at disneyland and california adventure park...we liked  the excitement of being at disneyland  the nostalgia of being back ( we are late 20s )  the indiana jones ride  fastpass  electrical light parade ( fantasmic was so so )  downtown disney  soaring over california  the big roller coasterwe didnt like  the staff looked depressed and underpaid  the lack of vegetarian options  pirates breaking down twice on us mid ride  haunted house closed for half day for maintenence, then breaking down on us mid ride  most of tomorrowland being closed or out dated  three fantasy land rides being closed for service including peter pan :(would i recommend going? sure, why not. but it sure isnt as magical as it once was... or maybe im just getting older!

We went to Disneyland from 04 27 05 01 04. Great time to go!!! Disneyland was fun!!! I enjoyed it as much as my children (ages 2, 4 and 7). However, my 2 year old had alot of trouble with many rides (she thought they were scary) and it is my opinion that she was too young to enjoy. I felt like a kid again with my older two. Disneyland is made for kids!! We attended Fantasmic, the Main Street Parade, Storytime for Princesses, had autograph books to be autographed by every character we saw (and we saw many) and made every attempt to ride every ride Disneyland had! I'm 30yrs old and have been going to Disneyland since I can remember. It truly does bring out your inner child. I'm alway's so pleased with the growth of the park and the staffing. I've been to a hand full of theme parks in the past and none of them can hold a candle to Disneyland. This will be at least the 20th time that I'll be visiting and am so excited! My family and I will be staying at the HOJO for the first time and am looking forward to trying a different hotel. I recommend Disneyland to all both children and adults alike!

Disneyland is great and fun, but they continue to raise the prices of all there stuff in the park  here are a couple examples:  1) parking tickets have gone from 6 bucks to 9  2) sodas 2.25 2.75  This is the only drawback to this park

the sad fact of life is that most reviews seem to for get the less mobile among us. Most amusement parks are saddly lacking in the ease of use. Queing lines are too tight, sharp turns that force the guest to preform many back and forth motions just to continue through the line, along with the grumbling of guests behind you that voice discontent with the slowness of the guest in front of them. And then the ussual rentals of wheelchairs that force a guest to rely on the goodwill of one of the party willing to push the guest through the park hoping that you do not run over some one. BUT disney is different they have accually made it quite simple for the guest to move through the park by making electrict cart advailable fo rent. the lines in the newer attractions are wide enough even for these to move through them with little impedment, and if the lines are to tight for the cart they have a special entrance for use by the guest and five members of his her party. (it also give a sort of back stage feel because you go into the ride difrently than the normal guest) some rides like small world even have special ride vehicles so that guests that are confined to their chair dont even have to get out they just ride right up onto the ride. one word of caution though is to get to the park early to rent the carts because the rent out fairly quickly. going to disneyland is a joy anytime of the year, Christmas is by far my favorite time of the year its a totaly differant park and worth a look. No one could understand why I would travel twice the distance to California to go to Disney rather than just go to the Orlando resort. New Englanders will tell you that Disneyland pales next to Disneyworld. Well, they are wrong! These people probably went twenty years ago when Florida first opened. So....if you are on your multiple trip to Disneyworld northeasterners, try Disneyland, you'll love it!

We returned on April 13, 2004, from our holiday. I was surprised by the one review where the lady was there for the California Spring Break. Our family of 4 did the popular rides (ie: Pirates, Indiana, Big Thunder, and the Matterhorn) at least 5 times each in a span of 4 days. Disneyland is always a great vacation and does bring a little child like magic. The key to a great vacation is timing though. Most negative reviews complain about the lines. Disneyland is a nightmare if you go during any peak time as you spend most of your time waiting in hour long lines and being jostled by crowds. Avoid: weekends, any holidays, June August, mid March through mid April (spring break), and the month of Dec. Reportedly the best time to go to avoid crowds in the first week or so of November. We have had great success going the first week of March and in October   but ALWAYS go on a weekday. It will make your day 10x more enjoyable because the crowds vanish. If you must go during peak times make careful use of the Fast Pass option (see Disney website for details). During high capacity days, Fast Passes for high demand rides like Thunder Mountain and Splash Mountain go fast and tickets run out by early afternoon. Get yours early in the day.Lately Disneyland has had some ride closure problems. e.g., Space Mountain will be closed until 2005. Be sure and check their website for ride closure scheduled maintanence so you know your favorite rides will be up and running when you go.Rides are still great, employees much more pleasant than at other theme parks, and they seem to have worked on improving some of the food within the park. Your best dining options though are in Downtown Disney. The independent restaurants have much better food for a comparable price and is usually worth the 15 minute walk out of the parks.Disney California overall has so so rides and is not particularly little kid friendly. Kids at 42' (4 ish) can ride most of the coasters thrill rides in Disneyland but their choices in Disney Calif. are limited and pretty mundane. It does have some excellent shows though including a Broadway version of Alladin. The Muppet show is excellent too and be sure not to miss the 10 minute Bug's Life show in the kiddie ride area. It is wild hilarious for adults and kids alike (Creepy crawly bug phobes should not attend). Disney's fastest coaster is there too and is worth a ride. Once the Tower of Terror opens in May there will be more thrill ride options.Just pick a low crowd time and allow a few days and you're sure to have a great time at Disneyland.

For spring break our family took our vacation at Disneyland and California Adventures. We had a fantastic trip! The one major disapointment was that Space Mountian was closed. Other than that all of the parks major attractions were open. In previous years the Matterhorn Bobsled ride was closed. I was glad to see that it was operating this year. The park was pretty crowded for the holiday week. A good portion of the rides had lines that were over an hour long. We were able to use our fast passes on some of the attractions, but did spend a lot of time in line. If you are the kind of person who doesn't like waiting in long lines, I would recomend you don't plan your trip over the holiday break. The best time to go to to Disney is in late August when the school year is about to start. The lines are short and the parks are not crowded. I have been to Disneyland and Disney World and have always had a great time. On May 5th California Adventures is opening the Hollywood Tower of Terror and that will make a good reason to go back. Disneyland and California Adventures are a must do for everybody!

To list a few:  Indiana Jones   we obtained a fastpass and when we returned the ride was closed. The next day, once again the ride was closed and finally on our third try we managed to get on. (It was a good ride, for your information and worth the wait).  Matterhorn   we were told by other people that they spent 75 minutes in the lineup only to be turned away when they got to the entrance as the ride was shutdown for maintenance after problems. People were led off the ride. This occured on at least 2 3 occasions. We gave up and didn't bother going on it. Pirates of the Caribbean   We went on this ride after about a 30 minute wait and got stuck on it at the part where the town is all singing  Yo ho, yo ho, a pirate's life for me!  for at least 30 minutes. This is not a pleasant experience and actually people were getting kind of panicky.  Haunted Mansion   We had a temporary stall when we were on this ride, but only for about 5 minutes. If you are going, check out the restaurant by Soaring over California   the  all dressed fries  (not sure of the name, but they have fries, chili, sour cream, cheese, onions, etc and are fabulous and a good bargain!) The rides are more exciting for older children teenagers and the Aladdin show is awesome. Also, Who Wants to be a Millionaire, a Bug's life, and many others. Very worthwhile.

(seemed like we were the only family at seaworld) have a wonderful time, we will be back!

Our family of five went to DL March 9 13. We booked through Alaska Airlines. What a great vacation! The vouchers for your hotel, car, park passes, etc are great. There is NO NEED for a rental car. Save your $$ and the headaches and take the shuttle! We stayed at the Marriott Fairfield on Harbor Blvd. It was totally within walking distance, even for our four year old. We have three boys (9,7,4) and they LOVED Disneyland & DCA. The lines were all fairly short, but we did see an increase in people as the week progressed (we started our time there on a Tuesday). We didn't even use Fastpasses (except once) until Thursday. We hit everything we wanted to and saw a lot of characters. Toontown is a great place to see the BIG CHEESE and also other characters. Even with young kids, we did not feel we missed anything by not doing a  character meal.  Instead we had lunch at the Blue Bayou. That was a TREAT! Go for the lunch  (save $$) and make your reserv. before you leave home. Send someone to get fastpasses after you order, then after you eat, you can hop on the Pirates ride! The park hopper ticket is the way to go. We went to DL on Tues afternoon evening, then back on Wednesday, Thursday was DCA and then Friday we hopped back and forth to hit everything we'd missed or wanted to do again. Saturday we hit Downtown Disney. I would not waste too much time shopping for DL souvenirs. Most everything you can get at your local Disney store. Don't miss rides are the Pirates, Matterhorn, Star Tours, Jungle Cruise, Splash Mtn, and Big Thunder Mtn. Over at DCA don't miss Soarin' over CA, CA Screamin', Grizzy Mtn. or Bug's Land. Overall we thought DL was not as polished as usual with updates needed here and there, (bathrooms in the castle needs work and we did see some trash and messes) but DCA was in better shape. This was a great time of year to go. Low crowds (before spring break) and good weather that was not too hot. Customer service was at the typical HIGH Disney standard while in both parks. They did search our bags at the entrance, but they never took any of our food from us, as I had been warned. The suggestion to rent a stroller (it holds up to a 75 pound kid) was a great one. For $7 day you get a place for a tired kid (ours took turns) and a place for your stuff. They have updated to nice  jogging  type strollers that are very easy to maneuver. You can  hop  back and forth between the parks with your stroller too and that was nice. We can't wait to go again! It was the family vacation of a lifetime.

I went this past weekend, which also happened to be both Valentine's Day and President's Day weekend. I figured because it was February, it still shouldn't be that crowded, right? Boy was I wrong! Word to the wise: avoid any time that is even remotely near a holiday. Waits for some rides were 2  hours long, and so many attractions were closed that there were too many people crammed into too little space   too few rides. I think the SoCal resident  2fer special  comprised much of the crowds, though, and I know that special expires in March. More advice: (1) Check the calendar online at disneyland website so you can be prepared for what attractions will be closed for renovations. There will possibly be other things closed (e.g., monorail or Disney RR stations), but this will at least give you some idea so you're not too disappointed. (2) Take advantage of as many FastPasses as you can and obtain them as soon as you come in the park. (When you obtain one at 11 a.m. on a crowded day, the FastPass return times may already be as late as 7 8 p.m.) Also, you must hold onto your original entry ticket to get the FastPasses! (3) You can get stamped for re entry into the park, so you might take a breather from the crowds by doing a meal at Downtown Disney or near the Disneyland Hotel. Both have excellent options. You should make a reservation, though. Overall, Disneyland is as charming as I expected, even if it was somewhat run down (it's been around since the 50's, so what do you expect?). And, the much needed renovations should have it looking much spiffier for their 50th anniversary in 2005!

Disnyeland has to be the BEST place to take a family for a wonderful vacation or just a day of fun! It is safe, clean & takes you back to a simpler time. I have visited Disneyland at least 50 times & never tire of it or the magic it gives to everyone. When you step onto Main Street you see what Walt saw evertime he was there. Look up over the Fire House & that was Walt's apartment for when he stayed at the park. There is a light on in the window which meant that Walt was in the park, when he was alive. That light is left on all the time now to remind the cast members & visitors that Walt will always be with us & is always  in the park . To best enjoy the park go at off peak times. Summer & holidays are notoriously busy & the lines for all the rides will be long. Waiting an hour to ride Dumbo does not make anyone happy! If you must go at these times of year get an early start on the day. The park will usually open at least 20 30 minutes early on the busy days. You can get in early to also shop along Main Street before they  drop the rope  to enter the  Lands . If you are staying at one of the Disney hotels (I highly recommend the Grand Californian if you can afford it) your purchases can be sent to your room at no charge, a great deal so that you don't have to carry bags around all day.  1 rule, have some sort of a plan. This will save time deciding which ride to go to next. It is best to try to ride the  big rides  as early in the day as possible. Indiana Jones, Space Mountain, Splash Mountain are all rides that can be a very long wait later in the day. One of the best ideas Disney has come up with is the Fast Pass. Use this to avoid some of the lines later in the day. First thing in the morning ride 1 or 2 of your favortite rides then go to get a Fast Pass for another ride to ride later. You can only have 1 Fast Pass at a time. Once you have hit the time for your current Fast Pass you can get another one. For example, if you have a Fast Pass for Indiana Jones at 11:30   12:30 you can go get another Fast Pass for another ride (or the same one) at 11:30, before you even ride the ride. The machines only know you have one up to the beginning time, after that they don't recognize you have one. Another tip, you can ride that ride any time after the beginning time, so if your Pass says come back between 11:30   12:30 you can ride anytime the rest of the day after 11:30. You are not limited to just the one hour it states. The parades are geat entertainment but getting a good spot for viewing takes someone staking out a place at least 45 minutes to an hour (some people will go even earlier) before the parade starts. One of their best shows is Fantasmic. If you want to splurge, book a seat on the Disney Gallery balcony ahead of time (call Guest Relations before you even get to Disney, up to 30 days in advance). The current price is $40 which includes a dessert buffet, a drink & your most perfect seat to watch the show. Pricey but you don't have to stake out a place 1 2 hours in advance. For young kids Fantasyland will be there first stop. Dumbo & Peter Pan are the rides that usually are the longest wait during the day. Ride those first if possible. One underrated ride is the Storybook Land Canal Boats. This is a very serene ride to see the miniature towns of the characters made famous by Disney. The details in the miniature villages are wonderful. It is especially fun at night. Another fun land for the little ones is Toontown. The rides are all (except for Roger Rabbit) scaled for the smaller visitors. There are lots of fun things to do in this land such as blow things up (at least it sounds like you are blowing things up!) & breaking out of jail. The Roger Rabbit ride is great fun for the whole family. One great place for kids to burn off steam & adults to find a shady place to rest is Tom Sawyer Island. Mom & Dad find a bench to relax on while the kids explore the caves & climb the rocks. A great place to get rid of any extra energy after standing in long lines. Teenagers will enjoy the big roller coaster rides like Splash Mountain (yes, you will get wet), Space Mountain, Big Thunder Mountain Railroad, Star Tours & Indiana Jones. They may even enjoy the corny Jungle Cruise ride with all it's great jokes by the  captians  of the boats. Mad Tea Party in Fantasyland is also a favortite of teens just to see who can get their teacup to spin the fastest. Adults who have grown up with Disney all their lives will enjoy everything it has to offer. A good way to learn more & find out some behind the scenes facts is to take the  Walk in Walt's Footsteps  tour. Interesting & full of fun facts. Look for all the things that make Disneyland special. The care & attention that is given to the smallest details are what make this a very magical place indeed!

After multiple visits to the original Disneyland in the states, we were so excited to make a trip to her sister park outside of Paris. The park itself is stunning, with gorgeous details and a castle that took our breath away (we kept pausing to admire it as we walked by!). We also loved the dragon in the dungeons  that's a must see for sure.The parks were clean and not too crowded, but they definitely lacked the personality and  Disney magic  of the American park. Cast members were subdued and not very interactive, the parade (Pirates and Princesses) wasn't up to par with the ones we've seen stateside, and the dining options were few and *very* crowded.The secondary park, Walt Disney Studios, was difficult to navigate and really didn't have much we were interested in seeing. We rode Tower of Terror and the Ratatouille ride and went back to Disneyland proper.All in all, it was nice to have had the chance to visit, but neither of us really wants to go back.
Why they selling fastpass tickets without have buy before the entrance tickets???  Any answer ???  Shame on you!!!   We came here from Greece until the entrance!!!  Avoid this place!!!

We have had a fab 2days here, totally action packed with lots to do and see.Expect to do a lot of walking each day, we done over 23000 steps each day and are aching all over.The parade at half 5 is awesome so is the firework display each night.The rides are.fun and majority of the staff are good especially  Benjamin  on the big thunder ride.The ride broke down after over two hours of queuing and we got told to leave, not allowed to wait.I complained to one guy who said we shouldnt of left, I told him we were told too along with all the others waiting, he said he didn't believe me as we wouldnt be told to leave. I went and spoke to Benjamin who was great in dealing with the situation.In general had a fantastic time and a great hotel Cheyenne

We weren   t intending on going to Disneyland Paris as we had traveled to Disney World in Orlando a few years prior & knew how crowded it would be. But after finding Paris to be highly over rated & dirty & not wanting to drag our young girls through the hordes of people around the Effiel Tour & on and off the boats on the Seine we decided it would nice to get out of the city for the day.It turned out to be brilliant. The girls had a ball. And it was no where near a busy as Disney World.The only thing I recommend is   GET TO YOUR BUS EARLY ON DEPARTURE We were there with plenty of time, however we witnessed a couple of families get left behind & this would be the fast thing you would want after spending a full day at a theme park!

This was my first trip to Disneyland Paris and it was absolutely fantastic! The staff were extremely helpful! The park was but this was to be expected with the time I visited. I would highly recommend this park! The character parade and end of day show are literally incredible!!

We went to Disneyland Paris during the Easter break with family members who had come over from the States. As we had all experience Disneyland in Anaheim and Disneyworld in Orlando, perhaps our expectations were just too high. First off, the moving sidewalks from the parking lot to the park entrance were broken. Not a great first impression. Furthermore, there was a lot of gardening work ongoing when we arrived. Isn't Disney supposed to be magic, with everything looking in top shape and perfect? The security line moved, but was the first bottleneck. The second major bottleneck was to actually enter the park. As we had bought tickets online, we thought we would be able to enter the park fairly easily. However, there was pretty much mass chaos at the ticket check point, with many people jumping the queue and others just standing around. We eventually made it through and made our way to Fantasyland.We managed to ride a few rides, but when it came time to get on the Teacups, they had closed the ride. Not for the day, but for about 45 minutes to disperse the line. This caused many people just to loiter around the entrance, waiting for the ride to open again. Not great. We did manage to eat lunch  early  enough that we didn't have to wait a long time. However, the food that we got was not what we ordered. None of us had the wherewithal to go back and try to fix the order. so we just ate what we got. When it came time for ice cream, it took about 45 minutes just to get to the front of the line, and then another 10 minutes to process the order. This was because the staff at the counter were poorly trained, and only one person knew how to use the register, and others seemed like trainees. There were plenty of other foodcarts around the park that were empty. Not enough staff at the park to operate these. There were also plenty of rides (like Autopia and Dumbo) that were closed for renovation. Disneyland Paris does not carry the iconic felt mouse ears. We definitely won't be going back, and I can't recommend Disneyland Paris to anyone who is looking for a true Disney experience.

Trust me, you don't want to miss this. Your inner child will be forever grateful. The park is just magical and huge. There is so much to do and even more to see. You have a lot of rides, beautiful shops, cafes, everything you could want and more. From my trip to Paris, this has definitely been my favorite part. We went on a Monday, so we didn't have to wait in lines for too long, so if you can I recommend visiting on a working day.

As season pass holders to Disneyland in California, we love and know Disney well. But we definitely underestimated how huge this park is. You need a few dedicated days to do it right, and check the holiday schedule in Europe before going to make sure you don   t overlap with everyone else going too. That being said, we are definitely planning to come back again and spend more time. It   s beautiful and clean and a fabulous Disney experience!

we have traveled during December. the day was a bit rainy, so it was less crowded. and we went dining before the big lines.the sad thing was that some attractions were closed   either renovation of weather, thus some lines were too long.overall, it was great.we went there by train, very efficient

Lovely day at Disney Great experience lots to see my son he is 6 years old had enjoyed himself and had a lot of fun just should be more organised at the entrance not enough of customer service to help and give you enough information

First time at Disneyland Paris and had the most magical time. Loved that there were bigger rides for thrill seekers. However, there was no monitoring of people cutting the line which added to the wait time. Its a shame this park carry the name Disney... We had the privilege of visiting Disneyland Paris in August 2014. We've had the opportunity to visit all of the Disney parks in the US, as well as in Tokyo, so when we were in Paris with our kids, it was a must see. So much fun... and easy to do in one day.

I visited Disney in Florida so i knew what to expect   characters meet and greets, overpriced merchandise and treats every corner. Since it was Easter and we are on holiday we decided to take our 8 year old for the day. I figured with it being Easter maybe they would have an egg hunt or some fun Easter things   WRONG. It was business as usual. We arrived at 10 am and 30 minutes later she rode the carousal. We waited 90 minutes for a roller coaster, 45 minutes to get sandwiches for lunch, 60 minutes for another ride. It was crowded, disorganized (don't bother shelling out more money for fastpass) and even my 8 year old said it didn't have the enthusiasm of Florida. I would like to say the workers were very kind but the guests were aggressive. As a parent i would expect better behavior   after all it is a family theme park. 7 hours   3 rides. Not worth the price.

This was just a gorgeous day for us and our 9yr old. We stayed in the centre of Paris and took the RER train (red A line) return tickets for the 3 of us was 38euros. It is the last stop on the line and you exit from the station in front of the entrance. You just can   t stop smiling once you enter   felt like being on a film set. We arrived when it opened 10am and headed straight for the ride we didn   t want to miss out on. There was still a queue but moved quickly. Like other reviews have said you have to queue, minimum 60mins or more for each ride so prioritise the ones you want to do. We didn   t do Walt Disney Studios as we didn   t think we   d have time and we were right. The parade at 5.30 is not to be missed but get your place at the front at least 30mins early as it gets very busy. The ending (10pm) is spectacular, a wow factor. Take lots of snacks, a pack lunch, there are water fountains available. Just be aware some restaurants close by 5.30 6pm. It was a fab day even though it involved a lot of queuing for rides, meet and greets, food, toilets etc. We plan to return soon!

It was amazing excellent exciting family tour in which we find our children excited happy enjoying from entering Disney land till leaving it all we enjoyed are the smiles and joy on our children   s faces

I know Disneyland is a money machine but hadn   t realised how much service and enjoyment had been sacrificed to achieve this aim. We visited with our 2 grandchildren and entered the park just after the gates opened. Even then it was manic, probably too many people for the park to cope with.The story was Q,Q and Q. The worst was Peter Pan, the board outside said a 100 minute wait but this became an actual 127 minutes! The reason for this is Fast Pass. As a day visitor you are a third class customer. The pecking order starts with those who are on special deals in the resort hotels, then comes those who have paid even more money for Fast Pass. These people are able to queue jump leaving you to watch as they go to the front of the line. The Q situation extended to the catering facilities, even a coffee took 42 minutes. The guy was morose, monosyllabic and unhelpful. There were a number of these    solo    food stations around the site and all seemed to have the same issues. Having visited Disney in California a few years back and loved the experience, Paris was an awful, poor value experience and will not be repeated.

Amazing and magical place to go for kids and adults. Lots of fun with chances to see characters throughout the park and lots of rides for all ages. The shops have lots to attract kids and to buy things you can   t get elsewhere.

My advice is to get there early, we arrived at 10am and didn   t get into the park until 11.45am. It cost    30 to park the car and we were so far back it was a long walk, you then have to queue at security and the entrance so by the time I got in I felt stressed. However another    45 later we leave the first shop with mickey ears and a Star Wars hat. The park was packed, far too busy and the queues were horrendous it didn   t help that a lot was closed for refurbishment.That being said the look on my daughters face when she saw the princesses on parade was priceless. She was on my husbands shoulders so he missed it as we the crowds to see the parade were bordering on dangerous. We didn   t feel we scratched the surface as the queues were so bad so I don   t feel the cost was worth it. Saying that we   d go again but try and find a quieter time, my tip take lots of money, drinks and food. It even took 30 minutes to buy an ice cream and a coffee.

A fantastic way to spend one day (if you are wanting a quick Disney fix) or a week (if you are an avid Disney fan). This is one of two parks within the Disneyland Paris hub and most definitely is the best of the two. The park was clean, the staff were mostly friendly and it was well laid out. The theming was fantastic everywhere but I thought it was particularly good in Frontierland (I believe better than the other Disney parks). Another distinctive characteristic of this park is the extensive amount of hidden gems that you can find scattered throughout. Whether that be the Dragon under the castle, the underground caves in Adventureland or the hidden above ground walk as you enter Frontierland they are must visit places throughout the park (particularly when it is busy). You also cannot miss the extensive attractions on offer, most notably the Rock n Roller Coaster, Hyperspace Mountain, Tower or Terror amongst many more. The only draw back...no one smokes in the designated smoking zones. It is unfortunate this isn   t more heavily enforced.

This is definitely a must do, it   s a lot bigger than you imagine so comfy shoes are a must, there is so much to do and see, really enjoyed the Parade where all the characters came to life, the Aerosmith ride was just fantastic. Que times are something that need to be looked at as waiting 2 hours with children isn   t ideal this was for a train type ride, A lot of the staff also do not understand English well, I qued in line for an ice cream to eat whilst watching the parade, I qued up for an hour and when it was my turn I realised the reason it took so long was because the staff couldn   t understand what British customers were requesting very well.I would definitely return but would go during term time when it   s not so busy to avoid long ques .

This was very disappointing on this visit, three times in last four years. A number of the attraction s being closed and queues being very large for some of the rides. There appeared to be. A shortage of staff in many of the catering operations which caused more chaos. In all this was the most disappointing visit we have had as a family and would give us cause for concern re visiting again next yeah.

Having visited the Disney parks in both FL and CA in the states I have certain expectations of the Disney brand and parks and this park fell extremely short. From the initial unorganized entrance to the park to the lack of cast members available, it was a let down. Lots of areas in the park were under renovation while we were there, and there was nothing to make up for it. We were there the Monday before Easter and the crowds were terrible. And let   s add to the fact that visitors to this park will cut you in line and skip through the lines and not blink an eye, super annoying. They do this for all lines. The very few cast members we encountered were unfriendly, unhelpful, and did not have any    Disney    magic. We love Disney and have been visiting the parks annually for the past 11 years. We would never go back to this park.

Disneyland paris is beautiful and clean. It's smaller than florida but manageable to do in a day. The fireworks display at the end of the night was so nice. I just Love Disneyland ParkBeen there several times with my wife and kids(Now 10 & 13 and still loves it)Sure there are some negatives  the prices   everything is expensive  be preparerad to pay    100 for lunch for a family of four, souvenirs costs  the cues to the attractions   sometimes over 2 hrs  remember to collect fastpasses as foten as you are eligeble

I visited Disneyland Paris with my 2 nieces and my sister in law during the Easter school holidays   although I expected long queues for the rides waiting 1 hour and 20minutes for a hotdog was unacceptable. Don't get my wrong, my family have been to Disneyland Paris twice in as many years, my kids love it and the atmosphere is unique. I think its going a bit far to call it magical though. I wont comment on queues for rides, as you expect this in any theme park anywhere and if it really bothers you there are ways to speed it up of course if you want to pay more. I think what is really lacking though in 2019 is organisation and updating the offering. For a start, nobody should have to queue for an hour to buy a hotdog, the restauarnt areas are hopelessly disorganised and innefficient. The systems just dont work and add so much time. I had about 8 people in front of me on two days to buy 'fast food' and it took an hour. Its also expensive and very limited in choice. Basically if you dont eat junk food, there is not much for you here. There is also nowhere you can charge a phone, not a single charge point in the whole park. And when it takes an hour and a half to queue for a ride, phones etc and quite useful for keeping the kids amused. As there is nothing else going on. It seems so easy to make some improvements that would make the experince so much better and the amount of money being made could surely justify putting a bit back in! Also some rides just seem perpetually closed. Which is annoying when you are returning. The theme parks in UK are a lot more efficient, but I guess they dont have those famous ears to let them get away with it. I call it QUEUEURODISNEY now but will no doubt be back.

First time to Disneyland Paris. Really enjoyed it.Went with an open mind as my only other Disney experience is a number of visits to Walt Disney World in Florida, that is on a completely different scale and if you go to Disneyland Paris expecting the same, you will be disappointed... It is completely different.First of all my gripe, the fast pass system is rubbish. Doesn't work, means alot of back and forward and wasted time. They need to sort it out.That wasy only issue. The park is clean, familiar with other parks... The layout and amenities, rides and eateries.Had a Caseys Corner, loved that. Beignet, loved that too. Family had a great time.I would recommend a visit, we stayed close by at Dream Castle Hotel and the transport links etc were fantastic.There was one incident that I will be contacting Disney about, wasn't caused by them... But the company I purchased the tickets from in the UK... Feel a situation could have been handled better by them. I haven't marked down on that but felt the way it was handled... Wasnt Disney style.

We went to Disneyland in JanuraryWasnt as magical as i remember.firstly we were all stuck in an area till it opened very crammed, we had fast track tickets but noone told us we had to collect then before they ran out so every ride we queued for between 60 to 90 minutes even the small rides and every character we saw you had to queue for unlike previoulsy when i visited characters walked around greeting guests .On a plus side the parade and light show were superb and it was lovely and clean

We decided to take our 6 year old for a long weekend. I must say we are very disappointed with the experience in general. Whilst I appreciate it was school holidays and the crowds were huge, I cannot see the value in paying so much for passes when actually you are likely not even to make it to 10 attractions over 2 days because of the queues. Some of the attractions were closed for renovation and others just look very tired and dated. The staff are poorly trained and for both days we were sent on a goose chase for our tickets because we had some vouchers. On day one we queued for over an hour!. We had downloaded the passes to our phones and one would expect that just like your plane ticket this should work at the barrier but no it didn   t! Leading us to queue at three different queues as none of the staff was trained enough to to know what to do. On the first day after what felt like endless hours queuing we were given tickets for    both days   , except this was not the case so the same drama the second day, another 70 minutes of queuing. This put us on a back foot for both days meaning we only had limited time and endless queues to endure before we could visit any attraction. The place is also VERY EXPENSIVE for the most basic things i.e. food I paid    37 or so for a meal of fries, a small bottle of water and a fish burger, 1 small portion of fries and 4 chicken nuggets. On day two we decided to leave the park and eat at one of the restaurants by he entrance. It was much more reasonable, it was proper food and peaceful. Merchandise is also cheap and tacky but EXPENSIVE!. We also stayed in a vacation club and not at Disney. This was a great choice away from all tack at Disney.The marvel attractions were ok but they had technical glitches and the queues horrendous. The parade was so busy the little 6 year old could hardly see anything. I know people were queuing since 4 pm for the 5.30 pm parade (what a waste of a day). Same with the fireworks we turned up at 9 ish to find a good patch but taller selfish people just walked in and stood in front of us again he couldn   t see much. I must add that not once did we see Mickey or Minnie except on the float or if we were prepared to queue for ages or book some silly breakfast (more money) with the characters. Why couldn   t they just have a few of these characters meeting and greeting children?. Their app is not very good and doesn   t give much info nor is it interactive enough. Information in general is sketchy unless you sit there planning for weeks. I think if you are a regular or know how to play the game you   d be ok. This is not a destination of once in a life time for a 6 yr old. There is no room for spontaneity. In general I felt we could have holidayed in Africa and seen real lions or the Caribbean and enjoyed the beaches for a better experience for the amount of money we paid. This was just a very tacky, dirty and over priced experience for very little return. I feel the place is so commercial (money, money, money)that the spirit of the magic is lost!

This was my second time back, being younger the first time it was obviously more amazing than the second! But the second was just as amazing!!! It   s a great day out holiday, we did fast track for a lot of the rides so we didn   t have to que long this was available for free on loads of the rides! We didn   t see many characters around the park and the parade didn   t happen either because of the rain definitely take your own food and drink! It   s expensive and actually trying to get in a restaurant to sit down is a whole other mission and you waste half your day! But an AMAZING experience can   t wait to go back!!

Loved it, great for all ages. Would recommend staying for the illuminations at 10pm, they last about 15 20 mins and are amazing. Would also suggest watching the parade but get there early to get to the front so you can see. Lots of queues, try to get on rides when the queue is smallish, food and drinks are expensive. Bring snacks and water bottles to refill in the taps, was a great day!

This was our first trip to Disney with our 6 year old daughter. It is fair to stay she loved it. I have been to Orlando but it was a few years ago and I also loved the park. I would say do some research first in terms of how to make the best of it   fast passes, meal packages etc.We had a fantastic time and loved the rides, meeting the characters, the parade and the fireworks (so much more than just fireworks!). The cast members were always friendly. The park was very clean and well kept. I would recommend downloading the app because it gives you the queue times without having to go to the ride. It definitely helped us plan a bit better. We went to both DLP and Disney Studios. I think Studio's is aimed at slightly older kids and because its smaller it feel busier but we LOVED the ratatouille ride! Probably our favorite of all! Dont miss the fireworks   they are AMAZING. We saw illuminations when we visited.Things that could be improved? Meals and food are eye wateringly expensive! If you are staying at Disney itself consider a meal plan and book some meals before you go (queues are wild). As a vegetarian I lived off pizza, pasta and chips for 5 days which was less than ideal (and i now have a waistline to prove it :D). Disney please could you add some Veggie meals to the menus? :) We are back home with many fabulous memories, tighter jeans and a lot lighter wallets! But we will definitely come again!

A very disappointing experience.Went with my husband , grandchildren and daughter and her husband for three days.Long queues everywhere, some over an hour for rides which last 5 minutes. We went on 3 rides a day ! Poor signage and lack of information on site. Queues to meet Disney characters , plus charges for photos. All in all there is no Magic, just a money making concern.

First time we came was a part of our honeymoon trip around Europe 16 years ago. The food was plastic but we enjoyed ourselves laughing about it. The rides were typical though. Now it   s updated with more modern rides for adults but it doesn   t have the same feel as Anaheim, which is still our favourite Disneyland.
It could be really nice, but I couldn't stand the que, too large, wait sometimes more than one hour for 5 minutes fun. I am too old for this...

This was our first Disneyland experience and wow, what an amazing place! The park is immaculate, and the staff are friendly and constantly happy to help! We were concerned that we had seen so many complaints about rude people pushing their way to the front of the parades etc, but we only experienced this twice in our visit and it didn   t ruin our experience. The character meet and greets are brilliant, and worth the queues! Make the most of extra park hours if you stay in a Disney hotel, as queues for rides do get rather long! We went with the rule that if the queues were longer than 30 mins, we didn   t queue and we managed to do all the rides we wanted to using extra park hours and going on rides during parade and illumination times (once you   ve seen them once, you don   t need to see them again, they are the same every day!)We will return to this lovely park in the future.....starting saving the pennies now!!

Disneyland Park, Paris is a wonderful, magical place which makes me forget any stress and completely relax to enjoy a family holiday. We have visited many times but this was the first time we have taken my sister, nephew and niece with us. It was fantastic to share our favourite rides, experiences and the magical atmosphere with them and see it through their eyes.

Wow...nobody quite does it like Disney!Our first family trip (2 adults a 6 year old and a 13 year old).We downloaded the app which is extremely helpful as it gives you the waiting times for all the rides. We bought personalised t shirts and Mickey ears before we left..Disney is VERY EXPENSIVE so be prepared to spend a lot of money on most thingsWe booked breakfast with the Disney characters which was wonderfulThe main strret parade at 5.30 gets super busy so book your pavement slot early (just sit down around 4.45). The fireworks at 10pm are magnificent, we probably should have got there at 9pm for a better viewing place but after 3 full days its exhausting!..we did end up hiring a buggy for our 6 year old as she was so tired by 9pm...its 25 Euros but well worth it should the need ariseOverall...fabulous magical colourful...nobody does it better then Disney

Managed to find an out of season deal combining accommodation, entry and full board in both the Disney Park and the Studio Park which was very good value considering how much it all would have cost had it been in season and booked `straight`. The visit at the end of March saw some of the attractions and facilities closed for refurbishment and reopening in time for the impending summer season but it did not diminuish the great experience we had with our 3 1 2 yr old granddaughter who is into all the characters. The adults were scared witless by some of the rides and she enjoyed the more gentler ones like the teacups and the various train rides available in both Parks. So glad that meals were included in the price (accommodation was in the Davy Crockett Ranch about 10 mins drive from Disney so a self drive visit was essential) but thank good ness we were not buying food each day as it would have been eye watering. Parking at 45 Euros each day was also included in our 4 day pass so day visitors be warned ! Cannot fault the staff   they were there to give everyone a great time and they performed that task perfectly. The evening firework display and son et lumiere was stunning but beware of the self centred visitors who push you out of the way to get the best view and then climb the lamp posts so everyone behind them is obstructed. The parade of characters each tea time is also excellent as you get to see the characters you may otherwise miss in this vast complex. We would recommend the Ratatouille visit in the Studios Park despite the wait to get in and the Hollywood Hotel ride that scared and thrilled in equal proportion. Eating recommendation   Billy Bobs for really tasty food and great staff. Overall?   well worth what we paid and a great experience. Downside?   the cost had we not booked an out of season package deal. Did we miss out with the refurbishment?   perhaps, but still worth it. Would we ever go at the height of the summer season?   Never !!

Visited Dismal land Paris in April 2019 and what a truly disappointing experience that was! Previously visited other Disney parks in the United States and the gulf between the two couldn't be more obvious. We stayed at the Newport Bay Club hotel for 5 nights and had 4 and a half days at the Disney Parks. We thoroughly enjoyed our time at Disney. We had been to Disney in Florida twice before when the children were younger and I was concerned if they would still enjoy the Disney experience now that they are 11 and nearly 13. I need not have worried as there was still plenty for them to enjoy and we actually managed to do a lot more now they are older. As we were staying at a Disney hotel, we had the extra magic time when we could access the rides from 8.30 (around and hour before the park opens to everybody else). It seems early but this was essential to get on the bigger rides without waiting for over an hour. We got the Disney app which showed live waiting times for rides and allowed us to plan our day. We generally got to the parks early and did as many rides as we could before the waiting times went up, then just picked the rides with the shorter waiting times during the day. We then found that going back to the parks later in the day meant being able to get on rides with less waiting time. Disney studios closes at 8pm but Disneyland Park is open until 10pm, so we used to go there after our evening meal and managed to do some of the rides that have longer wait times during the day such as Star Wars Hyperspace Mountain, Buzz Lightyear Blast and Big Thunder Mountain Railroad. This also worked well to then see the illuminations which were at 10pm (we saw twice during our stay). It is easy to move between the Studios pro and Disney Park if you want to see shows or do rides in both. The Hollywood Tower of Terror was usually quite easy to get on if you keep and eye on the app for wait times and the Aerosmith Rollercoaster. If you want to ride the Crush Coaster (I would recommend!) or the Ratatouille ride, you do need to get there early or use a fast pass (we didn   t have this). You need to get the LineBerty app to meet some characters at the Toon Studio (Mickey, woody and Buzz). This queues for you and tells you when your slot is ready. Also if you have a MasterCard you can go to guest services at Studios or City Hall at Disney Park by 8.30 at the latest and book a reserved seat for the Mickey and the Magician show and the Marvel show. Overall, we had a great time but one big negative was the amount of people smoking around the parks. Smoking is only allowed in designated areas but nobody follows this and it goes unchallenged by park staff. We felt that we were constantly dodging smokers on the parks, through the village and up to the hotel. Unfortunately when we watched the illuminations on our last night, we were plagued by smokers (around 3 people smoking around us) and we couldn   t get away from it. I probably breathed in more second hand smoke over the 5 days at Disney than I have in the last 10 15 years in the UK. I do think this is something that Disney need to sort out, it is not acceptable especially in a place so aimed at children. They either need to challenge people smoking and enforce the designated areas or ban it on the parks altogether, which would be preferable. It was the one thing that put a downer on our trip unfortunately.
