The only things that appeared to be functioning were where money could be taken. Shops and restaurants. These places became almost claustrphobically overpopulated. Snow ploughs were attempting to clear parade routes but were only succeeding in making pedestrian areas even more treacherous. By lunchtime we had enjoyed only 4 hot chocolates each and one ride for with our grand children so we gave up and retried the Disney park. Things were a little better but only for the mainly indoor attractions. Again there were lengthy delays as staff were not letting queues from getting too large by limiting those being let into the undercover walkways. It was impractical to queue outside of marshalling areas because of the large crowds wandering aimlessly. A slight easing of the weather enabled two of the parades to operate but the main wish of our grandkids to see princesses was not achieved. In the end we booked an expensive character dinner just to enable them to meet Mickey, Minnie and some of the animal characters. Instead of any magic we saw confusion and raw commercialism at its worst . Our 8th visit in 9 years was a total disaster and will never pay for a winter visit again.

Well I was really looking forward to this trip over the Christmas period, as were my family. I have 2 small children 5 and 3. It was absolutely freezing which obviously is not Disney's fault but it was snowing when we arrived which was quite magical but the snow settled on ice and previous snow which basically created a lethal surface with which to walk on!We made it through the crowds and survived Christmas eve and Christmas Day, even through the ludicrous queues to get on the shuttle bus from the hotel parks hotel, the french have no idea how to queue!Anyway we were going to the Buffalo Bill Wild West Show on Christmas Day and on entering the show I promptly slipped on a wet floor. They had made no effort to clean or sweep the floor which was like an ice rink. The pathways up to the entrance were not cleared of ice snow..I expected more from Disney.Anyway to cut a long story short I ended up in a french hospital for 7 hours on Christmas night on my own as my husband had to watch my children. In fairness the staff were very pleasant at Disney but I think they knew they were very wrong in not cleaning putting something down to make floor less slippery.It ruined my holiday but I think the children still enjoyed themselves...favourites were Buzz Lightyear ride, Peter pan ride and Live animated Stitch.Glad I looked on here before we went for tips..Don't catch shuttle from hotel to parks..walk along canal river at back of Disney..brings you out at Disney Village and much less hastle!Take rolls batches cheese and ham from buffet breakfast to eat throughout the day.we actually took a suitcase of our own food drink which was a life saver.Rainforest cafe was great to eat...everywhere is expensive but you get an experience with this too!

If staying at a Disney hotel make good use of your extra hours & your fast pass it will help avoid the long queues. Not all rides use fast pass so go to the nemo ride 1st to avoid at least an hour wait, similair with the toy story rides. If you want lunch the shop by the train station sell drinks sandwiches & fresh rolls much cheaper than the parks & you can take them in with you.Remember to take a mac in case it rains they are around 8 euros (child size) for a thin rain poncho in the disney shops.Have fun!

Went to Disneyland Paris for New Year and wa expecting alot as I have been to Disney in Orlando 3 times which is amazing and due to go back there in Febuary. In Disney Orlando when you walk in it feels magical, clean, colouful with uplifting disney music and different chracters everywhere. Here it was un magical, dirty, only a handful of characters and the music was dismal and not very loud. Staff looked like they didn't want to be there and didn't speak english very well so didn't understand what I was saying ( like another review said i'd expect that in any other part of france but not in Disney!). The american staff really get in character when you get on the rides, here they all lack any kind of enthusiasm and you can forget about going the extra mile. The rides are nothing compared to disney orlando, the food is awful and lacks variety and everything is seriously ripp off. Most of everything is in French so when watching a show it means nothing to you or they have one chracter who is french and one is english but again you can't follow the story. Overall I seriously think the place needs closing down as it really doesn't do justice to Dineyland. I think maybe if you haven't been fortunate enough to go to disney america then you would maybe think its good but NEVER magical! Its about as good as any theme park in england so why bother to go all that way and spend all that extra money when you can go to camelot at home. I;m not saying the theme parks in england are not fun, just not anywhere near the magic that is disney orlando. The build up to new year was a total let down too. There was some euro trash old music, no real band and no countdown to new yaer just some un inspiring fireworks. Please please save up for orlando not this place its really not worth it unless you already live in france. Between the two parks disney paris, the studios is better than the kingdom.

We visited the park first week of december and it was generally lovely. Magical atmosphere and the actual park immaculate. Parades fab, character meet and greets brilliant at hotel (pretty busy at park although my niece queued for the princesses and totally worth it). Main street great with little shops everywhere. Prices ok if you expect it! Most staff polite but obviously not american friendly! It snowed while we were there which was beautiful. the train which went around the whole place was great, as was meeting santa. little old fashioned bus which runs down main street a must. It started to snow while we were on it and goofy came on with us. Sequioa lodge in general was nice, but corridor STANK and i mean STANK, also room old and musty. Bed very comfy though! I have a few wee tips we would know for next time....  PLEASE TAKE THE EXPRESS SPEED TRAIN FOR TRANSFER FROM AIRPORT TO DISNEY. So quick and straightforward, and you just walk across road to shuttle buses to get to your hotel. IF YOU ARRIVE AT AIRPORT LATE AT NIGHT DUE TO A DELAY AND ARE QUEUEING FOR A TAXI, BE AWARE THAT YOUNG KIDS GET PRIORITY IF GOING TO DISNEY. We were able to jump at least a 2hour queue. DO NOT BUY VOUCHERS FOR FOOD BEFORE GOING. AND BE PREPARED FOR PRETTY AWFUL FOOD! The vouchers are a bit of a rip off, menu very limited and meals cheaper than value of vouchers in a lot of places. Gorgeous little pastry shops along main street do yummy snacks and coffee (something that is seriously lacking in disney, no stands, no snacks). Continental breakfast not pleasant so skip it and have brekkie in park. also mcdonalds prob best food believe it or not , annetts diner also good for atmosphere and ok food. Cafe mickey and lucky nugget good for characters but food dire. starbucks nice for a break. save your money on half board vouchers and do a mixture of the things i have mentioned, it will be nicer and the same price if not cheaper. also consider your hotel, buffet at sequioa lodge better than any food in parks. try and eat at odd times, ie brekkie after early 2 hours and then tea sort of late afternoon , this works really well if you dont have the vouchers and to avoid crowds. We just had a quick coffee juice at hotel in morn. PLEASE MAKE USE OF EXTRA 2 HOURS IN MORNING AT PARK PARTICULARLY IF YOU HAVE YOUNG KIDS. No queues at fantasyland rides at all, ie peter pan, carousel, its a small world, teacups, the little fast train behind its a small world. The queues later in day just not worth it! do the wee rides early, go for a coffee and then plan rest of day. also just spend time wandering soaking up atmosphere, there were so many people on a mission and it is supposed to be a holiday!  TRY AND AVOID WEEKENDS. Know this is difficult but the crowd situation at term time is dramatically reduced through week. MAKE PARADES A PRIORITY. MEET N GREETS FOR WEE BOYS AT WALT DISNEY STUDIOS. BUZZ ETC.  IF YOU REALLY DONT LIKE THE COLD DO NOT GO IN WINTER, THE STANDING AROUND FROZEN GETS TO A LOT OF PEOPLE, WE FOUND IT MAGICAL IN WINTER BUT BE PREPARED! LOT OF PEOPLE TALK ABOUT THE SHOPPING CENTRE VAL D'EUROPE   BIT OF A WASTE OF TIME FOR US. We packed drinks and some wee snacks and brought them with us. val d'europe is a vast shopping mall full of designer stores and an enormous supermarket, It is more useful to bring some stuff rather than waste an afternoon there. (unless you want to shop till you drop, but kids do not like it here!) there is also a little shop in train station at disney.If you go prepared eurodisney is brilliant if not it can be a chore rather than a break! we much prefer florida but for a cheaper option paris is fine!

Our visit to the Euro Disney was not as expected.It were too many people in the park. The wait for the attractions were 1 to 2 hours. Fast pass is simply unfair. Long distances make it quite impossible to calculate the time ... The children of 7 and 11 was DISAPPOINTED and day 2 we went around and just looked at the queues in the Walt Disney Studio. Finally we went back to the hotel. It was not what we had paid lot of money for.It was very disappointing. There should be something done to improve conditions for visitors! Regards 4 disappointed people from Norway on a visit to Euro Disney

Walking through those gates was like re entering my childhood!! it was great!We had never been before and got a 2day pass which we got from disney store in manchester.it was great there are of rides and shows happening through out the day. the food and drinks can be expensive but other than that its so much fun the detail that has gone into the park in unreal its magically.Also look out for the stunt shows there worth going to see.If going to Paris it would be seriously wrong not to go to disney no matter what age.

We went to Disney on Christmas day. I let my guard down considering it was Disney and I was pick pocketed in one of the stores on Main Street. I reported it and the staff was very helpful and I did get it back a few hours later (it was dumped in a bathroom) minus the cash I was carrying. If you are used to Disney in California of Flordia you will be disappointed. When we went many of the rides were not open and no one could explain why or if they would open later. We got there at 9:30 and we had to walk around for an hour to find a ride that was open. It is also cold which you don't experience in the states. On the day we went the whole park was icy they did not take care to cover with salt or sand to prevent falls and we saw many people fall as a result. Paris is beautiful and we loved everything about it. We wish we did not waste a day at Disney we would have been better off enjoying the city for another day. We experienced good customer service everywhere we went and all the Parisians (except the pick pocketers) were wonderful. Overall we had a great time in Paris.

We went with our son, daughter in law and 3 year old grandson for his birthday... here goes:Hotel was great, Newport Bay loved it don't listen to the bad reviews we loved it!Near the park as well, we stayed 3 nights with 2 full days in the park I would have liked another day to see Paris:)We loved it, it was snowing which made it magical (I was sceptical as well:)) first day was in the disney park and our second day was in Studios, they are mainly shows inside which was great for our second day but they are close and if necessary you could do this in half a dayNot as expensive as everyone said it was which was a pleasant surprise but not cheap either!a small bottle of fizzy drink was 2.5 euros everywhere the best deal was a massive drink for 8.50 euros with a refills free if you have bigger children, we took juice in a cup for him and bought more, You have to expect to pay a bit more.Tip on shopping every shop gives you the same price for things and if you buy something you can pick it up in the village disney shop at the end of the day so you don't have to carry it round. If you stay in the park hotels they will deliver it to your roomWe ate at the village outside the park as there is plenty of variety and because of the little one (stayed out all day then) we went to eat after the park closed, no queues! If you eat later be prepared to wait (not good in the snow but the park was quieter) we ate in Planet Hollywood and the rainforest cafe (this was brill moving animals and thunder , lightening and rain!!) worth every penny to see their faces and we loved it as well ha ha. The park is easy to walk around as it's not too big for little legs (thats only me not the little fella!)I would go back and stay in the Newport Bay, we did stay in the Admiral floor and were in the main block with a lovely view of the lake. If you stay on this floor you can get room service which was great, 10 euros delivery charge and for as many people as you like, we had 2 rooms but all had breakfast together with no queues what more could you ask for.Great stay and a magical place!!

Was there on Christmas Day 2010. Nice and quiet, most queues less than 10 minutes, but cold. With some planning (The Brits guide is excellent) you can get round both parks in a single long day (Park Hopper tickets) and see and do pretty much everything. We always drive, P&O often give you a free Disney ticket and at the moment Tesco Clubcard vouchers offer deals on the other ones we need. Big change since we were last there 3 years ago is the French smoking ban, hardly anyone smokes in trhe park any more. We have been to all the Disney Parks, many people tell you to go to Florida instead but where this one scores is it is so much cheaper if you plan and drive, less hassle as no flying, and, if you have young girls the Princess   Castle thing is much better in the French version.

Visited here just before christmas as agroup with a small child and whilst some rides were closed for safety due to adverse weather conditions (it snowed every day during our stay and many airport were closed due to snow and fog) there was plenty to do indoors so no time was wasted and the staff worked extemely hard clearing pathways and stages in order to get the shows and parades back on schedule. Although shows and parades were cancelled, again due to the weather, I cannot complain about this as a float not being able to stop on the slushy ice that coated main street and hurtling into the crowd would definatly have ruined my holiday!The Staff were more than welcoming and thankfully they were patient enough to be able to speak enough English (and universal hand gestures) for it not to matter that I dont understand any French at all. The charcters meet and greet were organised well with lines being formed and monitored by the Disneyland staff and people in the main waiting their turn, which was a welcome relief from earlier visits to the park which were more hap hazard free for alls were small children were often pushed out the way by older teenagers and occasionally even adults.The food within the park was fantastic you can tell this Theme park is in France and not England just from the overall quality and high standard of food options available to guests.Overall I would recommend this destination it is a great place to just be a child again. There is plenty to do even in the most adverse weather and the quality of attention to detail both in the scenery and the staff cannot be complained about in my opinion.

We went to Disneyland Paris while we were stuck in Paris because of the snow in the UK. As with Disney attractions generally (and everyone will know) they are not cheap so one expects something a little bit special. Our only comparison is Disneyland Tokyo. Unfortunately Paris Disneyland fails to deliver. The performances were lacklustre and weak there was a lack of ad hoc encounters with Disney stars that we normally see at Tokyo Disney. Also there were technical problems meaning that rides broke down during the ride and worse the main show had to be cut short leaving our daughter very disappointed. We were there at Christmas time and though there was some Chistmas feel and themes we honestly expected much more.Quite a few of the staff could not speak English and while I think this is fine, perfectly natural and to be expected with other attractions in France or any non native English speaking country I don't really expect this for 'Euro' Disney   an attraction that is I thought supposed to be for everyone and is owned by an American company. (I guess employing staff who are multi lingual costs them more.)

Well i'll start with saying i have visited dlp on numerous occasions, each time a pleasure! Allthough some reviews are negative, the thing is with disneyland you need to plan ahead. Avoid weekends school holidays & families will have a fantastic time for sure! It also is somewhat a pricey break, but in saying that you get what you pay for. People complain on price of alcoholic drinks ect, but disney isnt about going there to drink. What it is, is a family orientated break to relive childhood dreams....Anyway lets start, our last family trip was end of septemebr 2010 on a mon thurs visit, we stayed in Disneys Sequioa lodge, in a montana lake side view room. The hotel was lovely, rooms clean, spacious and the view absoloutly breathtaking! Hotel staff were happy to help too. We arrived to disney direct via eurostar, wich we find very easy. Disney even take your luggage so you can go straight to the parks!There was myself my 2 year old son, my mother, father, brothers, friend, her child, and my grandmother. The weather was good, ques were short on majority of the rides. I think the longest que was for Crush's coaster in Walt disney studios park wich totalled around 45 minuites. But other than that no other rides were more than say 15 minuites, and alot were walk straight on.Rides that cannot be missed:*Pirates of the carribean (classic)*Space mountain (not for young children)*Small world (for the little ones)*Big thunder monutain (for adults & older kids)*Star tours (clever!)*Phantom manour (may scare some little 1s)In studios park:*Rock n roller coaster (amazing, not for young)*Cinemagique (great show for family)*Animagique (kids will love!)*Terror tower (wow!)*Stich live (funny & my sons favourite!)Make sure you dont miss the parades too! And get a spot around 20min before it starts so the kids get a good view! Eating out:With dinner we always find going to City Hall in Disneyland park helpful, we reserve the reatraunts before hand to avoid que and any dissapoinment as it does get busy. We have found the best places to eat are certainely in Disney Village. 1  Cafe Mickey, excellent service, plus there are characters there in the evening & what better way to end the day than a character dinner before bed? You can get a set meal, wich i dont think in price compasrrison is much different from the other places. Kids will love it here, plus its a photo opportuntity without the hassle you can get in the park.2  Planet hollywood, we usually eat here too dont think you can reserve here so just get there for a good time e.g just before the park gates shut. Again the kids will enjoy there is alot too look at in here, and some nice food too.3 Mc donalds, same as the UK basically if your wanting a quick meal for a bit less expense then hers fine, althogh we found this extremely busy to que up and we made sure we reserved dinner at cafe mickey againFood in the parks is basic, we usually have snacks during the day, maybe a hotdog from Caseys, or in the Studio park you can get a kids meal for around 6euros wich is enough for any adult lunch! (burger,fries,drink & ice cream) I must say with every visit to Disneyland paris the magic is still very much alive :) my son absoloutly loves it, he has disabilities but i have to admit disney staff are fantastic & make it easy for families with disabled children adults to enjoy also. We are of again january 24th 2011 and cannot wait too see hes magical smiles again!

My family and I travelled to Paris for the first time this June and decided to go to Disneyland. The rides there are great and there are all different rides for different ages. Im not much of a thrill seeker so if your not one either, don't worry there are plenty of other rides to go on. But expect to wait at least an hour to go on the busy rides. We waited two hours to go on one ride because it broke down. You also can use the fastpass which is when you put your ticket in the machines in front of the ride and it will tell you a time to come back and you will get straight on the ride. Only the busy rides have it but sometimes the fastpass machines aren't on. The food there is not the best though. Pretty much junk food burgers, chips etc. Otherwise Disneyland is a place to remember

I'm a big fan and have been about 6 times now. Now was the first time I stayed on the premise and it is well worth it. A few tips:Definitely try to go on  slow  days. Last Saturday, even though it was during Christmas shopping, was absolutely packed and long lines for even the most basic rides.If staying at Disney, there is storage at the train station, so you don't have to spend an hour going back and forth in case you are arriving or leaving via the train station.The bus ride from the airport is quite expensive: 18 euros as far as I recall.If you are sleeping on the premise, make use ot the extra hours for hotel guests. You can power ride some of the more popular rides. But do account for a good half hour for breakfast and 20 minutes to get to the gates if you are at one of the outer hotels.Disney is a business: don't get all excited because everything is more expensive then outside of the Disney park. They have cheap places, mid price places and expensive places. Get over it. The park is really nice and does not look it's age.Same thing for the souvenirs. Again, Disney is a business. They have souvenirs from 2 euros and up. Get what you like and enjoy your day.We found the staff   characters quite nice and pleasant. If they sometimes have a bad day or a slip up, be nice to them. Think how you would react having to deal with thousands of overexcited children and adults.

Took our one and a half year old to Disneyland for the first time.We enjoyed it but don't go unless you have a bit of spare money as things are a bit overpriced. I knew things would be before I went and took this into consideration. There are alot of french people who dont like the english but there are also people who appear quite friendly too.Out little boy was in the big disney store in Disney Village we had stayed out later than usual as usually in bed earlier, we have a baby who has sleeping difficulties due to an underlying disorder that he has. My husband was holding him on one of the low displays as he got his camera out and baby lurched to the side and fell flat on his face!! Queue dirty looks from all. The actual Disney store staff were very kind and referred us to the First Aid department to get us checked out. One of the medical staff was fine but there was a lady sat on the chair who didn't even lift a finger to help,I was directing questions!! It was so obvious she didn't give a toss and it really offended me! So basically don't bother with the first aid department if u hurt yourself. Oh and they also gave me a lecture about having a baby out so late (it was 10.30) but thats not really their business anyway!! Could of done a better job from a one day first aid course to be honest!Anyway all said and done if you are a chatty person who likes to smile alot with the locals then don't go to Disneyland. Even the staff at the Playhouse Disney in Studios were like the gastapo!! Just give attitude back is my advice!!

Took a 5 day   4 night December Christmas break with wife & daughters (9 and 6). Eurostar from Ashford was a breeze. Disney Express service gets your bags from the train to the hotel so you go straight to the park (& vice versa when you depart). Train is hot & crowded, very poor aircon, so take drinks. We used Hotel Cheyenne. Basic but clean and warm & staff very helpful. Ask for extra pillows straight away otherwise they run out. No tea or coffee facilities in room but kettle hire etc at Reception. Breakfast's a right bun fight if you get the times wrong. We ate everyday at 8.15. By 8.45 they were queuing (or not if your French) out the door. Good continental breakfast & masses of it. Been before so took freezer bags & made rolls at breakfast for lunchtime (otherwise paying 8 Euros for a 6 inch hotdog) Both parks are great. We got 9 inches of snow on the 2nd day so it was really magical. Quite a few things got closed for safety & following days staff had difficulty getting in so some attractions stayed closed. It was bitterly cold throughout so take thermals & layers. Staff worked really hard to open what they could maiking sure indoor shows ran so visitors could get in out of the cold with kids. French don't (sorry, can't) queue so getting to see characters & keeping your place at some of the shows was a matter of determination and bony elbows   a rucksack on the back and lots of turning around seemed to work !! All the rides were great. Age doesn't matter, its Disney, we're all kids !! Suprised you can get onto the Tower of Terror at a height of 1.02m but you need to be 1.40 for Indiana Jones rollercoaster ? PS TofT is mental, my 6yr old was having kittens laughing and screaming at the same time ! We booked 3  events  before we went. 1. Wild West Show. Great entertainment and a meal included. Would highly recommend this as kids had a ball shouting and whooping. 2. Princess character meal at Auberge de Cendrillion. Posh menu, average cooking, cafe level of service   and it wasn't that busy ! Kids meal total trash   dry burger, manky sloppy veg and what was meant to be mash potato (but wasn't ?) you could fit in an egg cup. Only a few characters too. Would NOT recommed this. You can get far better value for money elsewhere. Like .. 3. Character lunch at Golden Nugget. All you can eat buffet. Plenty for kids, pasts, chips, nuggets, chicken, salad. Really tasty selection for adults   Mexican, fish etc     just great. Loads of characters, really friendly staff. Excellent value and kids loved it. (PS Wife says loads of great deserts too !!). Friend with us did Buzz and Woody lunch in Frontierland that was justa s good. Bus transfers between hotel and park take about 100 people and are every 12 minutes. Other than A de C can't say a bad word about the holiday. You can pay more and get a posh hotel but by the time we got back in the evening all the kids wanted to do was crash out. Room TV only has Disney Channel and 24hr news in English but does have scart sockets etc for portable DVD use (need batteries as mains socket a way away). Park prices are typical disney. In Euros expect to pay Coffee 2.5, hotdog 8, small popcorn 5, beer 6, 75cl coke 4. In a  character venue  meal 18 26, beer 6 9 a pint, OJ 4. No free water for kids only 1L bottles.

I booked this taxi service to collect us from the airport and bring us back three days later. They were great. There was a guy waiting when we came through arrivals with my name on a placard and brought us straight to our hotel. The same guy collected us from the front door of our hotel and brought us back to the airport (He was three minutes late). I had read the other reviews that were posted about them the night before we left and was dreading the thoughts of them not turning up. I rang them a couple of times while over in Paris and after a couple of attempts I always got through. I felt that I should post a review to say that booking these made our trip a lot easier and was well worth it.

Went to Disneyland Park today. Was generally a good day but ended very badly after an unfortunate incident with a staff member named Nathalie at the Storybook Store. Whilst waiting in line, a fellow customer attempted to push in line and get served first. When it was our turn and Nathalie called the next customer, we approached the counter with our items only to be refused service and told that she would not serve us until after she had served the pushy woman who had arrived to the queue after us. As this was completely unjust, we promptly dropped our items and left. There was absolutely no basis for refusing to serve us next, as was our correct place in line. The only difference was that we (being Australian) were speaking English and the other customer spoke French. I can honestly not suggest any other reason why she would discriminate between the other customer and myself other than on the basis of culture. She made us feel humiliated in front of all the other customers. The LA Disneyland is much better, cheaper and friendlier.

Please don't go on busy weekends if you don't like to wait in long long lines. Check out prices on entrance tickets before you go. If you want to visit the parks more than two days and are not staying in a disney hotel or buying a complete package it is cheaper to buy a year pass (free parking too, if you own a camper you can even stay overnight for free on the parking).

Went at the end of November with Wife and 2 kids on a Mon Fri B&B deal staying in the Disneyland Hotel.We flew to Paris CDG and got the TGV (not recommended with young Children, it's a good 15 min walk to station from the gate and you have to haul all your luggage about) get the bus at 66 euro.The Hotel was in the Park so couldn't have been handier to the attractions, no queues worthy of note which was an experience for me on it's own and the kids loved seeing all their favourite Disney characters.On the negative side the room, rated as 4 star was rubbish, no tea coffee, no iron board, pillows must have been filled with onions they were so hard, only 1 English language T.V Channel (Disney) other than News (kids got very bored), Can of Fanta in the Mini Bar 4.40 euro! 500ml bottle out of hotel shop 2.50 euros.Food in the Parks is grim to say the least, hotel food is prohibitively expensive and well below what I have experienced from Disney in the U.S, staff in general don't come accross as being particularly 'Disney' friendly or helpful.We ended up eating at Planet Hollywood in Disney Village at around 90 euros a night.My advise is wait till you can go to Disney in L.A or Florida and experience the real Disney, Disneyland Paris just isn't worth the euro shafting you get here.

My 9 year old son and I just returned from a day where we had fun, but found the service and attention to detail very lacking compared with Orlando and Anaheim (I have come to find out that this has been a problem since day one of when it was EuroDisney). The usually impeccable and bend over backward service at the City Hall information desk was virtually nonexistent. Not only did the cast member not know the answer to our question (was there a place we could buy fruit), but seemed very disinterested in helping us. There also were many places where the physical upkeep of the park was less than what we have come to expect from Disney parks. Many restaurants and shops closed before the park's closing time (which was not even late in the evening    only 7:00). Lastly, there were many ride interruptions and times when rides were completely down    including Pirates of the Caribbean being (somewhat suspiciously) down for about the last hour the park was open.Again, we had a good time but you would need to go in with less than usual Disney park expectations.

I just visited DLP 4 days 3 nights Nov 13 16     Children age 8 & 5 yrs. Contrary to some very negative reviews     we seem to have enjoyed the park and find the deal worth the money.Some tips for the Budget Traveler : ( Previous reviews helped me a lot to plan my trip)As mentioned by some travelers     disagree that Disney is trying to fleece. Food is allowed into the parks. Val D Europe a shopping mall is located nearby(8 mins ride). There is ligne(line)   50 shuttling from Disney bus stop     have to get down at hotel Elyssees stop     walk a bit forward and look to the left u will find one entrance of the mall. Forward into the mall you will not miss Auchan supermarket on the left where you get everything     water, breads, ham, Vine etc. Walk further down the mall straight you find the food court where you get all foods at reasonable rates.Only note line 50 timings are a bit not regular     but if you time the travel to and back you will waste very little time. Below are the current timings of the line 50 from Disney stop     8.53,9.30,10.00,11.40,14.40,15.10,15.52,17.02,18.05,18.35,19.05,19.36,20.05,20.30,20.55,21.20 the line is free if you are staying in a Disney group hotel     just keep the hotel identity card.There is McDonalds in Disney village     opposite the parks where you can grab a quick burger at regular rates and be back in the park.The restaurants in the Park and Village are highly priced but I saw them all fully occupied. The Disney merchandise are heavily priced and the Disney stores in Val D Europe and Champs Elysee sell at the same rate     so might as well buy from the parks. However I saw some Disney merchandise on sale in Auchan     Val D Europe at regular rates.Opinion on RidesRides in Disney Studios were worth it     1) Crush   s Coaster as the 5 yr old could do it we did it 5 times though the ride stopped in between due to malfunction(scary @) 2) Stitch live     did 2 times Children enjoyed and we appreciated the technology 3) Twilight Zone     did 2 times 3rd time the ride broke down 4) Car Show     don   t miss it, 5) Armageddon     OK, 6) Toy Story Area     avoid it     the Parachute ride is very slow ie the Q is very small but it takes very long time to reach the ride and the ride seemed to be boring.Rides in Disney Park : Most rides were outdated     the few new ones seem to be good 1) Buzz light year     did it 3 times was entertaining for the 5 yr old and all 2) Space Mountain     both my Children below height level min 1.50m? but heard it is the best ride in the park 3) Star tours     try it once     but feel it is an 80   s ride. 4) Peter Pan and Pirates of Carribbean     it could not entertain even a 5 yr old. Hope Disney realizes we are in the Digital 4 D era and they should not be using hydraulic operated puppets any more. 5) BigThunder Mountain     normal roller coaster ride with a themeHope Disney would go for Digital 3D Visual effects etc. in our lifetime. The parades and shows were fabulous(made my day!)     if possible try not to miss the parades and shows     refer to program timings sheet at the entrance to the parks     if in doubt check with information staff     they are trained to answer you     even if some are hesitant.The characters were so real and seemed to have just jumped out of the movies. They performed so well that I think my children will remain their loyal subjects for life.Saw the Buffalo Bill Wild West Show     see it only if you interested in the history of the show(I read it was a 100 year old show). It cost me around $ 300   for a front seat(net of 20% discount on pre booking), but noticed that as there were no sufficient crowd everybody was seated in front rows. The second row seats cost only around $220   (for family with 2 children)and have the same dinner menu as the rest. Even back rowsgive a good view plus less exposure to the saw dust kicked up by the horses and cattle(your dresses smell cattle & horse once you are out). So I suggest take the 2nd rows only as it is worth the money including the dinner     unlimited beer and excellent meat( 2 big ribs and big leg of chicken     I could not finish it) served in traditional cast iron tawa. Plus there is a small entertainment before the show and Mickey Minnie  Goofywere there and provided ample photo opportunity     report 1 hr before the show.( ) ves1) The park was well kept and clean2) Staff were very friendly     after reading some reviews expected the staff to be rude especially to Asians.However obviously they have been trained to be polite.3) The Qs seemed to be reasonable     though on Sat & Sun it was a bit more. 40 mins for one time forCrush   s coaster was the max we experienced.4) The Parades and shows were fabulous     obviously lot of hard work has gone into it.( ) ves1) The rides in Disney Park seem to be outdated (as compared to Disney Studios). Hope Disney comes up with new technology.2) Disney Merchandise heavily priced3) Some characters were a bit discriminatory     Mr Incredible declined my daughter an autograph while he obliged for all the white children(Is he racist : ?!     one less character she is subject to). But others made up for it     Goofy, Mickey, Minney, the Chipmunks. My son could   nt get to Ratoutile     he was in a hurry.However Buzz lightyear(his favorite) obliged him     I ended up buying much Buzz LY merchandise.

I had an incredible time at Disneyland Paris but the entire parked seemed incredibly understaffed to the point where things that were supposed to be open by 10 were still closed at 10.30 and staff dressed for the Peter Pan rides were working in the Small World queues.Hopefully they were just inbetween the Summer staff finishing and replacing the necessary roles. If this isn't the case then I'm very disappointed.

This was the worst day of our 2 week trip to France. My 11 year old daughter & I queued for one hour to buy tickets (which were very expensive), we queued another hour to go on the Buzz Lightyear ride, queued 30 minutes for the Stitch show, queued 1 hour for the Pirates of the Carribean ride, queued another hour to buy lunch. It was horrible, I think I even cried! After a few more queues we watched the street parade and left. We spent more time in queues than actually enjoying ourselves. I have been to other Disney parks and expected to queue but this was a nightmare.Meals, souvenirs and junk food items are expensive and there are not enough chairs around the park to just sit down and enjoy the atmosphere. You couldn't pay me to go back to this park!

Went to Disneyland Paris with my nearly six year old Daughter on 13.10.11. Flew with BA no probs there. Had hoped to travel from CDG by TGV to Marne la vallee but due to the various strike actions we had to return to the terminal to catch to Disneyland Bus. Was   60e return for the journey which took 1.5 hours due to a crash on the motorway. We stayed at the Magis Circus Hotel, which was great. Staff courteous, spoke numerous languages and went out of their way to ensure your trip was enjoyable. Shuttle bendy buses were fab, around every ten minutes or so until late, drops you just across from the Disney gates. Had a great time there, French schools were not off and so this was a good time to go as little or no waiting for attractions so managed to get round all the rides we had planned to. Result! Very much geared up for family fun, not like the UK theme parks. The only downside was that one the last day I was suffering from a bad headache and as I don't normally suffer from them, had not headache tablets with me. Had to endure a 10 minute taxi ride to the Marne la valle shopping Centre, then a three mile hike to the nearby shopping centre to the rear of this to find a chemist (right at the back). My advice is be prepared for nothing but Mickey&Co while you're there, especially if you are travelling with little ones. If you need something for them, it's certainly a trek. Apart from that, will definately be back. Can't wait!!! Thank you :)
