I have just returned from a three day visit to DLP. It was my fourth visit and I absolutely love DLP. The park in general has a unique magical feel to it and the rides are great. The castmembers are very friendly and always willing to help. During this trip me and my husband stayed in hotel Newport Bay and we loved it. Disneyland hotel residents can enter the park at 8 o' clock, which is a big advantage. There are free shuttle buses, that take you from the hotel to the parks every 12 minutes. Having said that, I also have some major points of criticism:1. The food is overpriced and it's far from haute cuisine. In my opinion following restaurants are to be avoided at all cost:   Planet Hollywood   they served the most repulsive lasagna I've ever eaten and my husband's pizza tasted like rubber   New York Style Sandwiches   serve overpriced sandwiches that are barely eatable  Cowboy cookout barbecue   the burgers here don't have any sauce, lettuce or tomatoes on them, it's just a dry burgerYou also shouldn't expect great food at La grange (all you can eat Tex Mex Buffet), although it is tolerable.It can be difficult finding a good meal in DLP, but I found Agrabah Caf   to be very good. They serve an all you can eat mediterranean buffet with a nice selection of cold and warm dishes including lamb tajine, couscous, moussaka, merguez, chicken, meatballs, warm and cold vegetables, chocolate pudding, pancakes, pies .... . For a good burger meal I can recommend restaurant en coulisse in the Disney Studios. 2. All of the merchandise is overpriced. 9,95 euro for one Christmas bauble is ridiculous!

I was in Disney land Paris this week. On Tues and wends the crowds were low, I never queued more than 10 mins for a ride attraction show, most of which I walked straight throught with not a single queue. You could easily walk around and see everything at a comfortable pace, even the queue for a character photo was no more than 20 mins. The weather I believe contributed to this fact   It was raining but with fewer crowds there no problem rushing in and out of each attraction and the parades still went ahead so you didn't miss any of the fun.Then on Thurs, there must of been a french holiday or something as the park completley packed out with thousands of French day trippers and the waiting time boards were all showing between 30 50 mins. After two days in comfort, I was so glad that I wasn't visting during a peak time, it was awful in the crowds. Luckily I was on a train home later that day!

If you measure DLP vs Orlando you will be continually disappointed but if you accept that it is a smaller, less organised and less varied than the US version thne its fine. 2 parks Disneyland and Disney Studios, instead of 5 (albeit the Park site has 4 or 5 different  areas    adventureland, frontierland, fantasy land, etc.) and therefore lessw alking to cover it all, but it's quicker to run out of things to do and you end up doing Space Mountain 2 or 3 times at the end of the day when queues are down to 5 mins.The Magic hours for disney hotel residents are pretty restricted with 2 hours from 8am and only 2 areas of the park open, and not all the rides in those areas.The Buffalo Bill show is worth doing (in the context of everything at Disney being extortionately expensive). The Car stunt show is worth doing (identical to the US one though, if you've already seen it). All the big rides are as good as in the US   there's just not as many of them. The fastpass system gets used up pretty quickly and Crush's Coaster is good but DO NOT queue 90mins for it! Oh yes   one other difference from US. At DLP if the queue time says 30 mins its 45   in US if it says 30 its actually 20.We did 3 &1 2 days at DLP including a daytrip into Paris to see Eiffell Tower (climded the stairs to level2) Notre Dame and The Louvre   nice day out. My kids (14,11,8) had had enough at the end (ie 2 & 1 2 days at DLP) which kind of sums it up: nice for a quick fix, but be realistic in your expectations.

With an adventure to Paris I thought it would be a good idea to reward the kids with something too. I made a great choice. The park has a whole lot in one. To me this Disney had a great layout. The attractions were much closer together so the kids spent more time riding rides rather than walking the park to get to the next ride. Even though we do not speak any french it was very easy to navigate through. Park maps are given in English or French and all host we came in contac with also spoke english. We went in November so the ride waits were 10 30minutes at the most. The kids smiled for hours upon our arrival. I surprised them with this because I didnt know if we would finish up with all the Paris city sight seeing in time and if they would be complaining about their feet hurt or if they were tired of walking ..etc..I never heard any complaints the entire stay.We took the RER A too the park. The ride was pleasant. Plenty of seats. Direct access to the park. You dont have to wait for a shuttle to ride you to the gates or anything (not that far.) I would suggest to buy the tickets online. I researched the prices before we left but since I didnt know if we were going to go for sure or not I didnt purchase them in advance. I wish I had because it would have saved 10euros pp and that could have been more spending money inside the park. I have no regrets. Would surely do it again . Check out their website specials ...they are awesome. I wish the Disney parks in the USA would run these type of promotions... We plan to come back in the future!

We've just returned from Euro Disney which was our 4th trip there over the past nine years. We bought four tickets for the Hallowe'en night party which were a complete waste of money as the queues for rides extended to two hours so we got on very few rides. The night was made worse by the behaviour of gangs of North Africans pushing in on rides that my daughter and her friend were queueing for. They also harrassed them by coming up to their face and learing, they have no idea how to behave. One spat during the Space Mountain ride which landed on my daughter's friends face. The youth got off bragging about it. There are no staff monitoring the queues so all this behaviour goes unchecked. The gangs also frequent the Village at night most noticeably at weekends and bank holidays. We have never experienced anything like it in the Florida parks. Normality resumed after the weekend and the park crowds thinned out and families could wander happily once more. We stayed at the Radisson Blu, the first time we have chosen to not stay in a Disney hotel in Paris. What an oasis of calm. Lovely hotel with a reliable shuttle every half hour and very pleasant staff. The last thing I'll comment on is the price of everything. Food and drink prices are shockingly high so be warned. A family of four would need   100   150 per day to cover lunch and dinner, and that's eating on a budget!

We paid circa   60 per person to visit Disneyland Paris. This make it a very expensive family day out, especially when food, drink and transport are factored in. Although the park is huge most of it is taken up by restaurants selling poor overpriced food and retail outlets selling overpriced Disney products. The few rides they had nearly all had huge queues and we had to wait around 50 60 minutes for every ride we went on. Althought the rides we went on were generally good unfortunately they weren't good enough to justify standing in line all day. I felt this was a wasted day on trip to Paris. Just far too many people and far too few rides.

We are BIG Disney park fans and really loved the Magic Kingdom Park. It is a bit smaller than Orlando's Magic Kingdom, but that made it easier to navigate. There is a Main Street USA with lots of shops and restaurants. Make sure you check out the two indoor walkway areas behind each streets shops. There are restrooms, back entrances to shops, displays and a great way to avoid the crowds of Main street. Frontier land has Big Thunder Railroad and the Haunted Mansion   both better than the Orlando versions. They don't have a Splash Mountain. Adventure Land has Pirates of the Caribbean, a cool Indiana Jones Roller Coaster (at Tokyo Sea, not in Orlando) and a fantastic Discovery Island area with a Pirate Ship, Caves, Swiss Family Robinson and the occasional Captain Jack Sparrow sighting. The Mediterranean buffet is expensive, but quite excellent and vegetarian friendly. The restaurant in the Pirates ride is also fantastic, but make sure you get reservations. Fantasy Land has a don't miss Alice in Wonderland Maze that I haven't seen at the other parks. DiscoveryLand has similar rides to the other parks: Space Mountain (much cooler than Orlando!), Star Tours, Buzz Lightyear, etc. Make sure you check out the walkthrough Jules Verne submarine near Space Mountain. We visited from Thursday Saturday and found Thursday and Friday to be nearly empty. Saturday was a mess, lots of people come into the parks just for the weekend. I definitely recommend going on a week day. Things I didn't like about the parks: We visited in October and found that many of the rides would close earlier in the day, for example the Indiana Jones Coaster closed at 5pm when the park didn't close until 8pm. Some of the restaurants were closed and some areas of the park were closed for the season (part of Fantasy Land). I'm not sure why they do this, but it was slightly irritating. The park isn't quite as clean as the other Disneys, there was some graffiti, some trash on the ground, etc. People were smoking in line for the rides as well   something that takes some getting used to. The staff didn't quite have the Disney personality that the others parks have, but that might be a cultural difference. We found a handful of staff to be rather rude (sweepers and shop staff). We did not enjoy WD Studios. We went on a Saturday and it was packed. The park is VERY small and the large crowds make it difficult to do anything. I do need to say that MGM is my least favorite park at WDW, so perhaps I am not the best judge. There is a Tower of Terror (always a great ride), Rock n Roller Coaster (outdated to say the least) and a very cool Crush's Coaster   an Indoor Roller Coaster (with a very long wait and no fast passes to be found). The Toy Story area had hour long waits for the rides. The Stitch show was cute   very similar to Crush Talk at Epcot. We really enjoyed the Cinemagique show as well. We only spent a few hours at this park and then reentered the Magic Kingdom park. If we go back, we won't visit WD Studios, just Magic Kingdom.

I've just returned from my first visit to Disneyland Paris. Having been to the Orlando Disney, I'm sorry to say I won't be returning for a few reasons. Generally, the experience just  wasn't Disney . For example:1. I found everything to be totally over priced. From the moment we arrived I got the impression it was all about how they could make the maximum amount of money out of us. For example, when you've spent   1400 on a 4 night stay, you don't expect to pay    7 for tea and coffee making facilities in your room. Come on, a   20 a night B&B in Blackpool puts them to shame on this one. Water over    2? A beer    4? A toffee apple    3? A hot dog, chips and soft drink    8? Good grief, at least Dick Turpin wore a mask!2. Considering France is the home of haute cuisine, the food on offer is appalling and over priced. Trying to eat healthily is well nigh impossible as it's chips with everything and God help you if you're a vegetarian.3. Why bother with a TV in your room if you're English? Every channel was in a foreign language, apart from the News and the info channel. Not at all child friendly for a supposedly child orientated resort.4. A member of staff was most rude and unhelpful. I simply asked for a carrier bag in The Disney Store as the one I had had ripped and was curtly told I couldn't have one unless I bought something. Considering the amount I spent to get there and was wearing a Disney Buffalo Bill Wild West Dinner Experience hat, that was pretty rich.5. My son was too small to go on the Space Mountain ride. The staff wouldn't even let him in the building to stand behind the barriers whilst I rode and insisted that he waited at the exit outside the building. In today's dangerous world, I found this reprehensibly unappreciative of child safety in the extreme.6. The Fast Pass ticket system needs a re think. Only being able to have one at any one time is illogical, really. For the same ride, that would make sense but not for different ones. Further, at one stage, the machines were issuing tickets for riding at 2145h at about 12 noon!7. Fast Passes aren't available on all popular rides. I couldn't get anywhere near the parachute and RC Rider rides, for example, without a 60 minute queue. Way too long, so I just didn't bother.8. Our hotel was in need of some TLC. Whilst not dirty, it just felt tired, in need of a lick of paint and general rejuvenation. (The Santa Fe).Overall, I am sorry to say that I was most disappointed with my visit. It certainly wasn't the quality Disney experience that one expects as a matter of course of anything bearing Walt's name.

we has an excellent trip. The journey from England to the the site was easy and we arrived mid afternoon at Davy Crockett lodge,. The lady at the checkin was friendly and extreamely helpful advising us that it was the last day to see the disney fireworks.Our cabin was fine, clean and we were given a free upgrade to a two bedroom cabin. the only negative point was that as it was under the trees it was dark even with the lights on. but what can you expect in a woodland setting! We stayed for 6 nights. The breakfast was very nice. we took our own cereal etc and ate the generous breakfast provided as a picnic for lunch each day. we went to the disney parks on four days and to paris on two days. We parked free at Disney and took the train into paris easy but expensive! The swimming pool on site was great   but cold as it was open in the evenings when we got back from Disneyland parks. The parks were very easy to find from davy Crockett lodge. The actual Disney parks were clean, well laid out and enough attrtactions to keep all the family happy. my seven year old loved the characters walkling about and having her photos taken with them . The older two enjoyed all the 'big' rides and we all loved the Stunt show in walt disney studio park. The parades are a must to see especially the torchlight and fire works last thing. I would reccommend taking food and drink in with you as all the resuarants and snack bars are very expensive and very busy. The shop on the camp site has a very limited choice and again is expensive but there is a supermarket very near in the nearby town. I was a bit concerned before we went because of the negative reviews but they all turned out to be unfounded. We had a great holiday. Do not go thinking it will be a cheap or perfect holiday ( it poured with rain on two of the days) because once you are 'in the magic' everthing will cost more but thanks to the Disney good organisation, cleanlyness and knowledgable and friendly staff you will find a bit of 'disney magic'

Just returned from Euro Disney 2 days ago. Kids had a great time and so did we. Went for 3 nights 4 days but with 2 young children ages 4 &2 found that the last day was really tiring would have been better if went for 2 nights 3 days. Also weather wasn't great on last day so would recommend that you save the indoor attractions(CINEMAGIC, ANIMAGIC, PLAYHOUSE DISNEY) until the very latest to avoid getting wet. If you going out soon wrap up warm!!!!!, Would recommend that you take plenty of snacks for the kids and drinks or bottles of water in advance. Biggest let down of the whole trip you cant help feeling being ripped off when it comes to eating and drinking. All restaurants are very expensive from less than average food. Expect to pay   20   euro for burger and chips for adults and   12  euros for the kids menu. average bill for meal for four is approx   80   100 euros!!!!!! we knew what to expect so weren't that shocked i would suggest you take a budget and try and stick to it otherwise can become very expensive. travelled by eurostar was great as direct train straight to resort would recommend you take advantage of disney express luggage service!!! kids got to meet all, the characters but you do have to fight through the crowds of europeans who have no idea on how to queue. alll in all a great experience buzz lightyear ride excellent, would visit again but leave it a couple of years

Here are the best amusement parks I've ever been in. It's really magical in Disneyland Paris and besides of everything being clean and neat, you will definitely feel you are somewhere else than you've ever been before. Everything's designed to make you feel you're in the Disney world and the objective is accomplished completely regardlessly of you're age or purposes of visiting the Resort. My main advice goes to those who are thinking of going and don't know where to... Take advantage of the offers on the Resort Hotels as that will make your experience more complete and trouble or fees free. Believe me you will appreciate much more all you stay if you stay within the resort that if you do it separately from visiting the parks.Finally this one... If going with kids take 4 Park Days, if not, 3 will be more than enough to visit every attraction and watch every show   even repeatedly! And we stayed there on low season with opening hours from 10am to 6pm. It's just amazing... You'll love it I'm sure ;)

Just back from 6 days in Euro disney, worth every penny!We got 4 days park tickets for the price of 3 prior to arriving. But struggled to find things to fill the full of fourth day, but this is still very good value for money.Positives:  Park offered attractions for all ages and none were disappointing.   The whole park was magical i.e. disney characters coming out for meet and greets, photos opportunities, daily parades, staff costumes, shops  As an adult I found plenty to do when i didn't want to go on the big rides (again)!  The majority of staff spoke english as a second language  Fast pass service reduced queues on big rides which allowed you more time to explore the park  Park location   directly outside train station  Courtesy Buses   ran every 10 15mins from disney hotels to park every day. We did not stay in a disney hotel but were able to use this bus free each day.Negatives:  Staff varied between being extremely happy and friendly to grumpy and uninterested  Food   within the park we only used the street stalls outside the park there is Disney Village which was a disgrace. The food was extortionate i.e Planet Hollywood   3 mains meals( pasta, burger and chicken), 2 soft drinks and 1 beer was 90 euro's. This would be ok if the food was good but the quality was awful, staff threw meals at you, decor was old and tired. The best eating place was.....McDonald's. Now i'am not usually a fan of McDonald's at home but in this instance you were guaranteed to get what you ordered and the standard is universal.POints of info:For any information outwith Disney the tourist information centre cited outside main park gates were fanastic. All staff speak English amongst other languages and were friendly and informative.Get a site map of both parks   Disneyland and Walt Disney Studio's and plan your day around parades, stunt shows, films, whatever the main attractions are when you go. This avoids missing some great shows. It does involve lots of organising but well worth it.You are not allowed your own food into the actual parks and your bags get searched. The security did remove things from other people's bags. Don't be put off by how a show can look on the outside, we thought this but still tried everything and really enjoyed everything.We took a 15yo male with us who loved every minute and was never bored.Take lots of cash, everything is expensive. 2.50 3 euros for a soft drink, 3 euros for ice cream etcWell worth it!

A very nice place to be and one day is not enough to have all the fun. Amazing rides especially the Hotel Hollywood and Aerosmith roller coster in the Disney studio while space odyssey in the Disney park. Since it was a Halloween day when I visited, it was slightly crowded and had to spend almost half hour waiting for every good ride.
Really enjoyed this trip   the kids thoroughly enjoyed themselves, but after 3 days was VERY ready to come home!!!  Would do it again though!

it's just wonderful! Aldo, quite expensive :P. But worth every penny. There is no right age for this attraction. You can enjoy it no matter what. I love Disney Studios, the feeling you get when you are there. Drags out the children inside you ;)!

My experience at Disneyland resort, Paris was fantastic; I cannot recommend it highly enough. However, I find it necessary to write this warning to ensure nobody else is ripped off by North Sud Transport aka NAVETTE AEROPORT DISNEYLAND SHUTTLE. I paid a return fare in advance and was picked up from the airport. Unfortunately they did not pick us up for the return journey. I could not contact them, neither could the helpful receptionist at Santa Fe Hotel and finally I had to take a regular taxi at a cost of 120euro, barely making it to the airport on time. I finally got hold of North Sud Transport a few days later and was told my money would be refunded within 10days....that was two months ago...despite numerous phone calls on my part and empty promises on theirs the money has not been refunded. Also I did not receive one word of apology.The last time I rang they hung up. I would hate anybody else to have their holiday ruined like us and I find it hard to believe that they can continue operating and ripping people off. Unfortunately, we did not notice the other posting on trip advisor warning people about this company.

The Hotel New York is great, the parks are diverse and immense fun. Studios have the edge for the adults and the traditional Disney park has the balance for the children. We had a great time in the parks and a fabulous time in the hotel, the weather is just that bit nicer than in the uk and we sunbathed in October. Val d'europe is close by and offers a shoppers paradise of cheap and cheerful to the most expensive outlets you can find. Its a great mix with a train ride to Paris if you get bored. The train is really the best option to get round and about, the buses take too long. VEA transport goes the long way round and the only other aspect we would comment on is that apart from breakfast, the hotel food is truly abysmal, eat out or buy in.Would we go back, yes for sure but we would choose to eat elsewhere and travel by car.Overall we had a great time and would recommend the Hotel New York and its staff.

If you book through Disney there are no hidden extras.We were staying for 6 nights at the santa fe and had passes for all our family for all 7 days.plenty rides for all age groups and with the use of extra magic hours and fast passes you can do all the rides in one day quite easily at this time of year as long as you avoid the weekends.During the week no queue topped longer than 30 mins and these are the rides that usually have fastpass. It is an incredibly easy system to use but I still continue to see people who havent a clue what to do.

I visited Disneyland Paris this week with my partner and Dad (Whos is 69 with health issues). We had an absolute blast, there is something for everyone no matter your age or ability.This park is alot smaller than the florida version but still has plenty to do and see. My only critisim I would have that Disney could control is that there where no fireworks and no tinkerbell coming down the zip wire.My favourite attractions where space mountain oh course for a thrill ride, buzz lightyear for fun and it's a small world for emotion. The queues where none exsitent we walked onto ever ride and attraction with very little waiting mainly loading and unloading time.The negitive side to disney is parents with children why should a child push in front of me to have their picture taken with tigger???? So what if I am 38 I paid my money to enter and have fun, so watch out parents I will stand my ground and not let your child take my turn!!!!!!!!This is not a cheap holiday but well worth the money especially if you can not afford Florida. There are plenty of eating options in both parks and the village which are resonable and value for money and pretty tasty.

advertised as kids under 7 stay and play for free, but the hidden expenses are you still have to buy a pass for the disney and universal studio for a child of 3 and over. Bus from the airport to disney hotels is 18 euro for adult and 15 euro for child ONE WAY. Stayed in Dream Castle Hotel and the restaurant only provided a buffet in the evening at 29 euro per adult and 10 euro for child over 3. Got reasonable meals over the next few days in the eating area entering universal studios.If your child has a serious medical condition you are supposed to present a doctors letter and you are given a pass to avoid the queues. My child has a serious medical condition, I presented the doctors letters and because my child looks normal, I was refused a special pass. The girl looked at my child and said  well what is wrong with her? My child is nearly 4 and now listens to everything   it was not the time or place for my child to find out that she had a life threatening illness. Thought the staff could have shown a bit more empathy.

1. Characters were amazing, so professional and absolutely lovely with the kids.2. Park it self is kept to an amazing standard.3. We went Oct 4th to 8th   Halloween time which was fab and out of school holiday time. Highly recommend it. Quiet and the weather is lovely. They do Halloween really well. Not scarey for little ones and great extra characters. Entertainment is superb and my kids loved it all. Look out for the fast pass to save queueing on rides!

I am just back from Disneyland Paris with my husband and our children aged 5 & 6. We had a magical time. I was never interested in going to Disneyland before and after reading the reviews wasn't really looking forward to it but I was mistaken. We arrived at 6pm at CDG as soon as we walked out of the baggage collection there was a lovely gentleman to guide us to our Disneyland bus which took us to our hotel   the Cheyenne. The check in was painless and we were directed to our rooms by the map supplied. The layout of the hotel as mentioned in other reviews is a wild west town. We found the rooms to be very clean and we had our towels changed, beds made and rooms tidied every day. We decided to take a the bus which goes every 10mins or so from the front of the main reception building to disney village for something to eat, a few minutes in the bus and we arrived at a bus depot   although you can't really see the entrance from here and us and some other newbies didn't know if we should get off or not but this is the stop for the parks and disney village. We had a walk round and decided on Annettes Diner, within 10 mins we were seated and singing and clapping along with the staff who were dancing in the aisles on their roller skates   my girls loved this, along with the frizzbe as a plate. The prices are steep compared to home but we were prepared for that. The childrens meals which included your normal chicken nuggets and chips etc came with a drink and dessert for    11 each, we ate from Annettes Classics which is    18 for large burger, chicken burgers etc with fries and drink and dessert. Next morning we headed for breakfast which we were more than happy with fresh bread, toast, ham, cheeses, cereal, juice, tea & coffee (saturday & sunday morning was abit crazy but it was fine) alot of people made up lunches from breakfast also. We arrived 8.30am at Fantasyland and it was wonderful, I would love to have the imagination of the people who created these rides, Peter Pan and It's a Small World are a must!! Also Thunder Mountain and Phantom Manor are fantastic!! We ate lunch in Main St which was again    11 per child and    15 per adult and over the next 2 days completed Disneyland Park. I had read reviews about Val D' Europe shopping mall and on our first main day there we decided late afternoon to take the bus to it   this is a MUST to keep to your budget, at the bus stops when getting off to go to the parks directly across the road at the other bus stops is a stop called Ligne 50 (Disney park to Val D' Europe) these are free buses for guests staying at disneyland hotels, it is a 5   10min journey (get off at Hotel Esyless and across the road is the shopping mall. We got beer (which we put in the sink with cold water ) 24 bottles for    11 (1 pint of beer in disney is    6), water 6 large bottles for    3 (1 small bottle of water in disney is    2.50), snacks (1 regular bag of Walkers in disney is    2.50) and even disney toys slightly less than disney prices. To return to Disney walk out of the same entrance to shopping mall and across the road from were you got off the bus is the return bus stop. In the evening we ate in Mickeys Cafe (we met, got autographs and photos with about 8 main disney characters, you should definately try here) which came to    90 this included 1 starter, 2 adults main courses, 2 childrens main courses, 3 desserts 4 bottles of water & 2 beers on the 3rd day we headed to Walt Disney Studios. Our girls had been allowed on all the rides in the Disneypark except Space Mountain and as some reviews had mentioned height restrictions I thought it must be the studios who had these. Both my girls are exactly 120cm and they were allowed on everything except Indiana Jonas they were even allowed on the Rockin Roller Coaster!! Please dont think your children have to be 120cm. There are only 3 rides in Walt Disney Studios the children wouldn't have been allowed on if they had been below 120cm so there is still plently of things for them to do under this height. Tower of Terror, Crashs Coasters & the tram ride are not to be missed. As this was Saturday and Sunday we decided to plan ahead and do the shows these days (no queuing for shows) and it worked prefectly (some of the main rides had 45   120 mins waiting time) First thing 10am we done some rides and when the queues started to form we headed to the shows (got fastpass for Tower of Terror on Saturday and Rockin Roller Coaster for Sunday for after the shows) CineMagique was excellent, the children loved Animagique and Stitch Live and we all enjoyed the Stunt show. We headed to Planet Holywood for tea which we had booked that morning so no waiting had a slightly better than McDonalds meal : ( 2 adult main courses, 2 childrens meals, 2 childrens desserts, 3 bottles of water & 1 beer    80 and then headed back to the parks as the queues had dropped and done Thunder Mountain and watched the Parade   all with no queuing. I had decided as we were on holiday to go to the wild west show as it got very good reviews    204 for the 4 of us. My husband and I got a bowl of chilli with corn chips for starter and we all got for main course a chicken leg, cumberland sausage, 1 4 of a corn on cob and a few boiled potatoes, dessert was apple crumble for adults and ice cream for children, beer and soft drink included. This is the only thing I didn't find fantastic, the food wasn't good at all, infact my girls wouldn't touch it and the show had us bored after 30mins but this is probably because it just wasn't our thing but I still don't think if we had enjoyed it that it was worth    204. On the Monday we packed our bags dropped them at the luggage store room just on your right as you come out of reception and were told to be back at 1.55pm to catch our bus to airport. We headed back again to both parks rode on all our favourite rides, done some shopping and headed back to catch our bus which was on time and dropped us at our departure terminal (no walking with bags). I have to say everything was extremely smooth   no hiccups with transfers what so ever. The staff at both the hotel and the parks were lovely and seemed to make more of an effort when our girls said please and thank you, hello and goodbye in French. Overall we had a really brilliant time, we have now booked for Florida next Nov. Can't wait

June 2010I'll be honest from the off, this isn't normally my cup of tea but with a five and six year old on a French holiday we bit the bullet and took them to Disneyland expecting the magic to materialise   it died after 10 minutes of stepping into the place.Fortunately we'd bought our tickets at the campsite we were stayng at as the queues were ridiculously long just to get in. That aside, we still had to queue to get our baggage checked and then queue at every ride. This day cost us over   200 for a family of four and we got on about five rides, each lasting less than 2 minutes. I've had better value for money at the travelling fairground that comes once a year to our local park. Judging by the car park, I'd say the place was only half full but the crowds were horrendous   you could hardly walk about.The Disney shops were full of over priced tat, tons of it. There was absolutely nothing that you'd have wanted to buy. My kids had been given   5 to spend by a neighbour and they struggled to fnd anything that cheap. In the end they got a small sweetie dispenser each. The part we were in was more just glorified play area, what few rides there were were just basic rubbish you had to queue for a minimum of 30 minutes each time. We eventually left at 5pm and even the kids were glad. For such young kids their patience was remarkable but they really were not bowled over at all. When I ask them about their favourite part of the holiday to France it was the swimming pool at the camp site, swimming in the river and the funny tunnels at the war bit (Somme Museum).A total rip off. Disney is just a money churning brand now   no magic left.

We were a party of 2 adults and 2 teenagers. lets start with the positives, place looks fantastic, everywhere you look you are pointing everything out, its just magical. the walk down mainstreet usa, with all the souvenier shops and food outlets is enough th get you excited, but then you look aheard to the castle, and you can't help but get excited.We stayed in a disney hotel, hotel cheyenne, and this enables you to get into the park early, and on some ride, or at least get into the front of the queue.there are 4 lands, and i will go throught them all. discovery land, has space mountain mission 2, star tours, buzz lightyear laser blast, autopia, nautilus, and was meant to have honey i shrunk the audience, but it was captian eo   michael jackson from th 80's with 3d effect. not my cup of tea, but was nice to have a sit down! the pick of the bunch here Buzz lightyear, star tours, which it a simulator type ride, and space mountain mission 2. Fantasyland was great, thought there were allot of rides closed for refurbishment. my fav was the peter pan ride, basically there are about 7 rides here, but its a very magical place, more aimed at families and younger kids, no thrill seeking rides here!Adventureland basically has 2 rides, and allot of outdoor play areas for kids up to the hieght of 1m40cm. the rides are indiana jones   great ride, and pirates of the carribean, very dark ride, but fun for all the family. Frontierland has 2 main rides, thunder mountain   which was great, and the phantom manor, as an adult i found it rubbish, but up to the ages of about 9 they will love it. The fast pass is something we didn't work out till the last day, but basically its free, just go to the ride you want to go on, swipe your ticket, a time will come up, and then come back for your ride, saving 75% wait time. Once this time has expired, you can use your ticket again for another fast pass and so on.The food. VERY EXPENSIVE, however you can do it on a buget if you look hard ebough. You can take a packed lunch. You can buy rolls for 6 euros each, and croc monsieurs, and you can fill up water bottles all around the park, fountains are everywhere. If you get a burger meal, you are looking at 12 euros each, for this you will get a large quarter style burger, large drink, large fries, and a pudding of yoghurt or ice cream. There are kids versions, and they are about 7 euros each. All drinks in the park are 2.5 euros, but like i say, if you take a water bottle in, you can drink for free all day. Hot dog meals are about 8 euros, but they are a rip off, not very big hot dogs and a drink. you want to go a bit more expensive, there are all you can eat menus, for about 23 euros per adult, and 15 for kids, not including drinks. but they can be as expensive as 34 euros per adult!What we did was go out of the park to the disney village, where there was a mcdonalds, which was the only place that wasn't overpriced, here all four of us got a large big mac meal for 25 euros total, half the price of the park. my advice, do the half board option, and you can then budget better. I took 230 euros for fri monday and came back with 10 euros. So not bad, i would like to go back, now i am wiser to the whole process. All in all a fab time spent, though i feel some lands do need a bit of updating, it was all i hoped it would be.

3rd visit to the park, first visit stayed in Sequoia Lodge, second Newport Bay, this time New York. If there was to be a fourth time, and there won't then it would be back to Newport Bay. I'll cover the hotel issues in another post.The park! Well it's Disney so the usual impressive Disney infrastructure always in evidence. We had a really heavy rainstorm on one morning and within minutes of the rain ending and the sun coming out there were people out sweeping the puddles away. The attention to detail always impresses, as does the general cleanliness of the place.However my main complaint is down to the number of attractions which were either closed, some for refurbishment others just closed, and others which just kept breaking down so you'd be turfed out after having queued. Too many to mention frankly.Now couple this with the balance seeming to have shifted unfavourably between the entertainment side and the retail  try and extract every last euro out of the visitor side  and then add in a healthy, or maybe should that be unhealthy dose of exchange rate misery, and it starts to leave a bit of a bad taste.Which nicely turns us to the food. Now Disney has never been particularly noted for fine dining, though Walt's always was, and indeed still is, the exception here. We had a first rate Sunday lunch on the half board plus menu and even the picky eaters in the family tried and supremely enjoyed everything, even things they thought they might not like. However away from Walt's, oh dear oh dear. You expect junk food, Casey's Corner is hot dogs for heaven's sake so nothing fancy. But soggy wet buns wrapped round ultra cheap dogs? Come on for that price I'd expect fine dogs not the rubbish that was served up on our visit, and way below what was served on previous stays.And so it went on, some places on the HB  list trying to be too fancy and just failing way way short. Others who have no pretensions to be fancy just being grim, eg Punta del Oro Tex Mex, found ouselves sticking to the floors and to the tables. YUK!Beaver Creek Tavern, fatty lamb, cold vegetables, dry and cold swordfish steak, desserts were good though.Parkside Diner, inedible main courses on the buffet, many adults were resorting to the childrens menu.Annettes Diner, another bright star and all three of us fully enjoyed our meal, they have been alongside Walt's as one of the more reliable places over the years.And then you try to go to places that you've visited before, eg Cowboy Cook out barbecue... closed, La Grange at Billy Bob's.... closed and so it went on. Les Cascadeurs... closed.Having paid for Half Board plus we were struggling to find suitable places to eat. We've found on previous visits that the best way to approach the parks is to take a sit down table service lunch early afternoon, that gives you a rest, and sets you up for the rest of the day. With what was on offer, assuming they were actually open, then this strategy was, for us a non starter.Of course it's not all a negative review, and some of the cast really do work hard to make people's visit enjoyable, but it seemed that they were struggling against a huge penny pinching strategy. For example first time ever with a long wait for It's a Small World. Why? Because only reduced number of staff on, and so those who were working refused to load every boat and were only loading alternate boats. I can however understand the logic why they were doing this, but it probably needed just one more cast member on duty. Yet the shops were packed with staff, extracting your money you see?So I'm sorry Disney Corporation, you charge a not inconsiderable sum for a visit, you've tipped over the edge from providing an attraction and turned it into a huge cash extraction process. Truth be known it was always that, but it is now just so blatant.I cannot recommend this venue until things change.I post very few reviews on here mainly due to time and only if I feel I have something to say, very often what I would say has already been said by others, so why take yp TS bandwidth.But DP needs a stinker of a review to get the act together.

The Newport Hotel is fantastic location, great decor, you feel like you are on a cruise ship, great staff and very helpful. Rooms very roomy, beds very comfortable, pillows were great for sleeping. Walk to Disney Village or get on the free shuttle bus. We bought the 1 2 board package and found this extremely good value, and spent a little extra to go to Wild Bill's dinner show was a fantastic night.

We lived in Germany for a few years and found that going to Disneyland Paris was a great way to get a touch of America. It helped cure some of homesickness. Although the parks are no where near the size as the one in Orlando there was plenty to do. We really didn't experience the lines like we did at the Disney parks in Orlando. The only downfall is you have to plan the trip well because if you don't you could miss somethings, like parades, shows, and maybe some rides.We stayed at a Disney resort for two of our trips and the Marriott Vacation Villa's for the next two trips. The Davy Crockett Lodge was nice but all in all it was a trailer. The benefit was it had a kitchen in it. We found that the Marriott Vacation Villa was a better choice for our stays. We got a great deal per night for a 2 bedroom, 2.5 bath, with full kitchen. There were many amenities at the resort however we really didn't take advantage of them due to the weather. My wife spent the good part of a morning in the spa which she loved. The Marriott did offer a shuttle service to the parks which is a lot better than paying about $15 to park.Besides the parks there are several other things to do. You can take the train into downtown Paris, go shopping at shops around the area, or take a trip over to the big cat park. We absolutely loved the atmosphere at Disneyland Paris. And would love to go back one day.

My daughter and I went to Disneyland Paris for 3 days during August, we had the most amazing magical time! I'm confused by the people who have written reviews stating there is nothing for young kids to do and no rides they can go on , we filled up 2 days of our stay and we didnt manage to do everything!! We stayed at the Davey Crockett Ranch where the staff were friendly and helpful, in the evening there was music and characters I'm not sure which my daughter loved more  the dancing on a stage or hugging minnie and mickey! The highlight of the whole trip had to be the parades in the evening...the fantillusion parade was Amazing!! and the fireworks(although very late for both of us) were truly something not to be missed!!The food is very expensive ... but then you would expect that in a theme park in this country so that's no surprise!!The stunt show is not to be missed   although my daughter wasnt keen on the ending we were about 3 rows from the front and the fire is huge at the end!My daughter loved the characters  who were found all around the park   she was terrified by Cruella, tickled by the chipmunks and hugged by every princess going, she was a bit dissapointed by not getting mary poppins' autograph , but maybe we'll get it next time.All in all we truly had a break to remember and I'm unsure which of us had the most fun!

New Generation  think Disney are missing out by dumping the old Charactors. The New Generation don't have the same magic as Cinderella, Mickey etc. Parades not as good and no fireworks display. Some rides closed and others being refurbished. Food needs looking at, not everybody likes fast food but at least you can now take a picnic in. Maybe spoilt after having gone to Florida.

Disney knows how to have fun! We were staying at the Davy Crockett Ranch, which work perfectly, we got entrance tickets as part of our stay in also meant parking was free  and we were allowed into the park earlier than the the crowds.From the moment we walked in, we loved it!! Its clean, friendly and has something for everyone. I havent been to Orlando  but i know it woud be bigger and better  however we had a great time. Some of the rides were fantastic  tower of terror was fab. I also LOVED stitch live, and my husband enjoyed the stunt show and The films special effects ride.i would commentent on the europeans queue jumping  yep its annoying, its as annoying when it happens at Alton Towers (it happens everywhere!!) But it really didint spoil the experience. The fire works and night parade... DO NOT MISS IT! brilliant, and bit of booing and hissing at the 'baddies' gives you some great photo opportunities.we really only ate in the park twice once for lunch  standard burger meal  with was average and then once for dinner at the roller resturant, whihc was expensive but was a nice restuarant and the service was good also.great place, will definately be returning

We found the food to be expensive and of poor quality. We went to the Blue Lagoon Restaurant near the Pirates of the Caribean ride and the food was cold when it arrived and the waiting on staff disappeared as soon as the plates hit the table.On a plus side we stayed at the hotel Santa Fe and the accomodation was reasonably priced very comfortable.

Just got back from a few days at disney staying at the hotel Cheyenne. Flew with easy jet & like many other people we found out at the last minute that our flight had been cancelled. However accomodation and new flights were arranged by the company immediately, so this really just provided us with a couple of extra days in Paris. We flew in to CDG & got the disney shuttle which goes from the airport to the disney hotels for    36 return (perhaps expensive for a 20 minute trip but considerably cheaper than a private taxi!)The hotel Cheyenne (although being one of the cheaper hotels) is comfortable enough (& it   s not like you   re going to be spending that much time in the rooms) Made up of many smaller buildings it   s set up like a wild west street, very atmospheric! Only a 10 minute walk from the disney village, you can also get the shuttle from the front of the hotel to the main disney park. Breakfast however can be somewhat chaotic, unlike the other hotels you have to fight it out for a table so if you   re not that worried about getting into the park for it opening wait until it gets a bit quieter!The disney parks are excellent for all ages. I went last year with my 4 year old cousin and this year with 2 other 21 year olds, think we enjoyed it more than the kids there! The main park is made up of main street and 4 different lands filled with rides, restuarants and shops all built in the style of that particular land. There are also a number of rides in the studio park as well as a new toy story play land. No matter what time of year you go you will have to queue to get on rides! We found September to be considerably quieter than previous trips made during the summer months but we still had to queue for 20 25 minutes, not all that bad considering normal queuing times. Even though queue times can be long, the parks are so atmospheric and there is so much detail in the rides and buildings that there is always something to look at! The main rides also have a fast pass system so you don   t have to wait in the longest queues. The parade is also defiantly worth watching.Go, get into the spirit of it and have a great time :)

Ive read some really poor reviews on here and really wonder if some people have visited theme parks before either in the school holidays or at the weekend   yes the parks are busy!!Weve just returned from spending 4 magical days at Disneyland it was amazing. One of our days included a saturday so we planned to do some of the show based attractions on this day as you dont wait for them you just need to turn up on time. We loved the stunt show, it was on 3 times on the saturday and holds over 5000 people each time, we also saw Cinemagique and Animagique, Stitch Live and grabbed fast passes for the Tower of Terror and the Rock and Roller coaster, we headed to the Disneyland Park and rode the big boat on the lake and watched the parade and the show. So although the parks were packed we still got loads done. During the week we loved the extra magic hours we had as we were staying in a Disney Hotel, you can get loads done in the 2 hours before the general public are allowed in. All the cast members we met were polite and we thought they did an amazing job considering how many languages they have to put up with. Americans may appear politer but they are only coping with one language. Whilst shopping I tried to put aside the rubbish exchange rate which isnt Disneys fault : ) and I worked out things at the cost of    1 to   1.50, which is what the rate was for a long time until sterling collapsed and i must say things seemed reasonably priced at that rate for a theme park . One note of caution is food is expensive so have a hearty breakfast and then travel to Val D'Europe in the evening its a lot cheaper. We had a pizza and drink and bread and olives for    9 per person in an italian restaurant in the shopping mall and we saw a nice all you can eat chinese buffet just outside the mall which didnt look expensive. We also shopped at the hypermarket to pick up some cokes and snacks for during the day which were loads cheaper than in the parks. We took the pink bus to the Elysee hotel which was free and the mall is opposite.Back to the parks   we didnt queue for more than 20 minutes for any ride during the week and we were glad we planned our trip. We got everything done in the 4 days we were there and rode many rides more than once.We booked the Lucky Nugget character birthday tea party at 5pm one day and I was a little hesitant and i had heard poor reviews of the normal meals there, but it was amazing, it cost    17 per person and there were unlimited amount of cakes, pastries, fruit and sweets and the waiters were always topping up the coke and sprite and fanta so our glasses were never empty. The live band were great and as it was one of our parties birthdays I ordered a cake at city hall (   24) and it was bought out and everyone was singing happy birthday ( in french but the tune is the same ) and we were lucky enough to have Mickey at our table who paid loads of attention to the birthday boy ( i say boy he was 31 but loved it )We also went to cafe Mickey one morning for breakfast which was    15 per person and again was great   loads of characters meets and no scrum ( unlike some of the time in the parks ) bacon, sausages, eggs, loads of meats, cheeses, bread, pastries, fruit, yoghurts were there , so lots of choice.I can see why this is Europes most popular tourist attraction and I can also see why some people would prefer america. But its in Europe and there are many more cultures and languages meaning that the experience is different but overall we had a magical time and cant wait to book and go again. Go to Disneyland Paris, but go mid week, and leave the world of Disney for your evening meals and most importantly plan so you get all the attractions and rides done. Disneyland Paris is just as good a Disneyworld Orlando. If you can not afford to go to Orlando then I would highly recommend Disneyland Paris as an alternative. Most of the rides are the same as what is out in Orlando. The only thing you do not get with Paris is obviosuly the weather. If you go to Disneyland Paris I highly recommend these rides Big Thunder Mountain, Buzz Lazer Blast, Nemo ride, Indiana Jones ride, Star Tours, Tower of Terror, Caption E0, Space Mountain, Small World, Aerosmith Rollercoaster ride, Pirates of the Caribean ride and the RC Racer. The shows are the same as in America as well ie the Stunt Show. I went to Disneyland California when I was 9 years old and had a great time. This time round, in my 30's, I still had a great time at Disneyland Paris!  Rides:There's something for everyone! We read online reviews to get a guide of what the rides were like. We didn't have enough time to go on all the rides, so prioritised.'Get there early if you are keen'   We arrived at the park around 9:30am as they let people go through security and the ticket gates early. They don't start the rides till 10am however we found that for some rides you can start queuing. We were lucky to be in the first groups to ride and completed at least 2   3 rides within the first hour of opening. 'Fastpass'   The fastpass ticket allowed us to wander around instead of standing in queue or we tried to go on rides in between, or sometimes we welcomed a rest.  'Expect queues'   There are signs at each ride telling you the approximate queuing time which is pretty realistic. Unfortunately you can't avoid queues. It was no different from my first experience of Disneyland 20 something years ago.I remember when I was 9 that I wasn't tall enough for some rides and was disappointed, but realise now that it would have been for my own safety.Highlights; Tower of Terror (if your stomach can handle it), Rock'n'Rollercoaster (if you like speed), Space Mountain (super fast!), Buzzlight Year (interactive, fun). Food:We brought our own snacks drinks along to the park.If you are looking for something different, we took the 'RER Line A' one stop from train station 'Marne la Vall  e Chessy' to 'Val d   Europe Serris Mont  vrain', ~3.30euro return (adult).If you turn right out of the station and walk to the end of the street you will find a 2 levelled indoor shopping mall called 'Val d'Europe', with supermarket and foodcourt. Would recommend the restaurants at the foodcourt as there were a variety of cuisines including; Chinese, Japanese, Italian, Korean restaurants.Bags:The lockers within the park were out of service, however there was a bag luggage storage facility situated at the ticket gates for a small fee. This was useful as we left our bags there instead of having to go back to the hotel. We found the service to be secure and good.

Our family of 4 (2 adults and 2 kids aged 11 and 9) really enjoyed ourselves there. We did a lot of research on the Euro Disney website and by reading other Trip Advisor reviews before we left NZ. Even though we arrived at am on a Friday morning, we had ridden on most of the big rides on the first day and then hit the balance over the next 2 days. 3 days long enough to do everything. Very clean grounds, very organised and staff very friendly. We were there over a weekend in the August holidays, so had to be prepared for crowds and long queues, but because we were already well advised, we knew what to do first and where to go etc. Take a lot of Euros and soak it up!

we just returned from our weekend at the Euro Disney Resort in Paris and we still are in shock about our experience there. We are great Disney fans and have traveled to parks worldwide and have already spent various vacations at the Resorts in Orlando and Anaheim. We have been very much excited to return to Paris, after been there in the opening week some years ago and the only thing we got in return was disappointment.We could not believe what was called Disney Village. We have never seen such a run down place before! It started with holes and giant cracks in the concrete everywhere, faded building facades, nothing to do for Kids, not even a playground was accessible. Entertainment was a not existent, even though they had announced a rock and roll party with car shows that day. Besides the Disney shops, little electric race cars which were not operated, a Balloon ride inside the resort lake for an additional 15 Euros per Person was available. We looked at some cars displayed and at 6pm a couple of kids started dancing on a little stage. To our disappointment, that was the entire party! We decided to have dinner at the rainforest cafe. No reservation required that evening so we got great seat but were also disappointed by the bad quality of food and the high prices. (For a starter plate and a fish course we paid 60 euros!) On our way out to the car we were held up by Souvenir sellers, trying to make us buy cheap metal Eifel towers. Next Morning we came back to enjoy the parks. We arrived there shortly before 10 am and the line in front of the security gates were so long, we decided to enter through the Walt Disney Studios. After a 20 minute wait and a baggage check that did not really include looking through bags, we were able to proceed through the ticket entrance into the Studio Park. The first ride we were heading to was the Crusher  s coaster. We arrived there at 10 Minutes after ten and were confronted with an 80 Minute wait. We thought this is because this attraction in new so we walked in to the RC Racer roller coaster. The line there appeared to be shorter so we got in. Right behind us a family was waiting and their child that got sick while standing in line. It took quite a while and lots of yelling until they got some help from the personnel working on this ride and were let out of the queue. The coaster was stopped during that episode because one of the operators had to assist the family. After a one Minute ride we attended a stunt show which was nice and around 11.30 we wondered back to the Disney Park  this was after we decided to proceed since the waiting time for all rides in the Studio Park were between 70 and 80 minutes, the Tower of terror had been closed due to technical problems and the crowd was getting exceptionally high. We entered the Disneyland Park and were literally shoved through Main Street. We were not able to walk freely so many people had been let in. We thought it was because it was lunch time and everybody had returned to main street  but we were proven wrong. Waiting time Big Thunder Mountain, was again 80 Minutes   and with fast pass option they asked you to return at 6.45 pm!!!. To make a long story short, after a lousy lunch, not being able to walk freely in the park due to the monstrous mount of people and incredible waiting times at every attraction (there was even an hour waiting time to hop onto the park train! Peter Pans Flight, had a waiting time over 120 minutes or, with fast pass, return at 9.30 pm   and it was noontime and so forth) we decided to go back to our hotel and to return in the evening when things were slowing down. We came back at 5 pm and encountered the same run of people, so we returned again at 7.30 pm. Discovery land was still overcrowded with waiting times at the attractions still over 80 minutes. So we went to see the Pirates of the Caribbean waiting time here, an acceptable 40 Minutes and it had just turned 8 pm. After a fun ride, we wanted to hop on to the Indianer Jones roller coaster, but with our arrival were informed that the ride had already been closed. After us asking why they close down the rides before they close down the Park at 10pm, the gentleman replied that he just does what he is told to and we should read the sings  and yes, there were signs that some attractions close before the park closes. Bad luck for us. We had payed full price ticket and all we got was a roller coaster ride, a stunt show, a unejoyable expensive lunch, a long afternoon at the hotel, 2 bus rides to return to the park and in the end a Pirates Ride and lot and lot and lots of people! One more thing we would like to mention at this point, the lighting at night was disastrous! All light came from little decoration lanterns but no lights in bushes, stairs or stronger street lights  I  m in my mid 30ies and I was not able to see the steps I had to go down properly! I can  t imagine what would have happened if your child would have run off or if it had gotten lost.  What really lifted this experience to something even more indescribable was the fact that we visited the Parks on September 11th and at this memorable date we had somehow expected a more elaborated precaution and security concept. We still cannot understand why so many people had been let in and if something would have happened we do not know how help could have been able to reach us. Thanks to this experience we did not return to the parks the next day, and will probably not return to Disney again. The sad thing, we met many other families also stating how disappointed they were and how their kids hated the Parks. We still don  t want to believe how disappointing this trip was, what a tourist trap Euro Disney is and how disrespectful we were treated!

Having read some of the horror stories that some unfortunate people had to endure, we were very apprehensive about our 3 day trip to Eurodisney. We were however relieved to find that with a little research, and following the helpful tips posted, we were able to enjoy a relatively stress free 3 days which the children loved.To reiterate the tips that made our stay much pleasanter:  Try to plan your days where possible  Book restaurants for lunch and dinner (the buffets are good options and provide good choices) and eat early or late to avoid the crowds  Take advantage of the early access to the park at 8am if you are staying at the Disney hotels (queues are 5 15 mins in the morning)  Buy water and snacks in the  Relay  store in the train station on your way into the villageWe stayed 2 nights (31 Aug 2 Sep) at the Hotel New York with 4 and 6 year old boys. The hotel was clean, staff friendly and helpful and perfectly located at a 10 min walk from the park. The hotel has an ice rink which was already open, and breakfast and dinner buffets at the Parkside Diner in the hotel were of good quality and provided a range of choices, even for children. I would liken the quality to a standard work conference buffet, so whilst not gourmet, it was perfectly adequate for a short stay, if a little overpriced (we paid 80 Euros for dinner for the 4 of us). Not a very  Disney  hotel which was a welcome relief for us, particularly as our boys are not particularly interested in the characters, but may be an issue if your little ones want access to Mickey & co.I would say that the main selling point of the hotel is its location, and as with all the Disney Hotels, the access to the park at 8am (2 hours before the general public) as we were able to go on all the rides with only a 5 15 min queue (Peter Pan, Buzz Lightyear, It's a Small World, Dumbo), which meant that by lunchtime, we had pretty much done all the rides that we wanted, and could relax over a nice lunch at Plaza Gardens (a good quality buffet in a relative oasis of calm for approx 75 euros for all of us). Having eaten at the Pizza Planet buffet where we paid just over 50 euros for the four of us (adequate choice of 3 pizzas: ham and olive, margherita or beef, pastas with a choice of 3 sauces ( bolognese, tomato or carbonara), with a salad bar (couscous, tomotoes, cucumber, sweetcorn etc) and dessert counter, if budget is not an issue, then I would recommend paying an extra 20 Euros to eat at Plaza Gardens for a good quality buffet with choices including mussels, salmon in white sauce, prawn and asparagus pasta, fillets of beef, pork, chicken, soups, good quality salad bar and dessert counter. In both cases, eating before or around midday meant that the restaurants were quiet. We booked a table at Plaza Gardens through the concierge at the hotel, and were the first to arrive at Pizza Planet at 11.45am.Regarding the park itself, I think the key is to have realistic expectations, to expect some queues and accept that Eurosdisney is all about sharing in the kids' excitement and having family time. We went mid week (Tues Thurs) after the August Bank Holiday, and whilst busy, we did not feel overwhelmed by crowds, anymore than you would at a theme park in the UK.The longest queue we experienced was 45 minutes for Thunder Mountain and the Autopia driving ride, both well worth the wait. Autopia displays its opening time on a plaque (sometimes 10am sometimes 11.30) so head towards it around 15 20 mins before to start queuing as it was very popular. The time passed quickly as we brought a couple of Toy Story card games that kept the boys occupied and engaged, and also loaded up our IPhones with 2 player games. Ice creams and snacks also made the queues less boring for the children. Also, getting on the rides early meant that we had the afternoons to wander around the less popular (and hence less crowded) Frontierland and Adventureland after lunch with an ice cream, and to pop over to the Studios park to see the Moteurs Action Stunt Show at 3.30pm. This show is worth seeing but if you have young children who are likely to be frightened by the shooting and explosions, then sit higher up the stadium as you can feel the heat from the explosions lower down! The Disney parade back in the main park is worth waiting for at the end of the day, before heading back to the hotel.All in all, we had a lovely break and were blessed with good weather, and even my cynic of a husband rediscovered his inner child!Whilst there is truth in some of the less flattering reviews (yes, in the 3 days, we saw a couple of people smoking, came across one queue jumper and some staff who at the end of the summer season probably could use a holiday themselves!) but none of which would prevent me from going and witnessing the happiness and excitement that Disney brings out in the children.Would I go back? Possibly in a couple of years once the boys are tall enough to experience the more exciting rides. I would probably give the US Disney a try first, but for the budget and proximity, Eurodisney proved to be an enjoyable pre school treat for a couple of days.

Have just returned from a 3 night break and the whole family had a great time. I had read the reviews before and was wondering if we had made a mistake looking forward to this holiday. We loved the parks, it was clean and the gardens were all well maintained. I can understand why it might not be so magical in August because of the long waits but for us the longest we waited for a ride was 45 mins, on our last day it had really got a lot quieter and waits were down to 15 mins for lots of rides. Fastpass worked well for the really popular rides. Had plenty chance to have photos taken with characters, had to queue (30 mins) for the official photos with Mickey etc We travelled by Eurostar and its so easy, straight out of the station onto shuttle buses and onto the Hotel. We stopped at Cheyenne and enjoyed the wild west theme. The room was fine, big enough for 3 nights and the food was nice too. Lots of choice, even my fussy eater enjoyed his breadkfast and dinner, good dessserts. It was better to eat early for both meals as it did get busy. It cost around 64 euros for a family of 4 and that included a drink each. You can eat at Mcdonalds for just a bit more than UK prices if you dont want to spend too much. Other reviews complained about staff in hotels and parks, but we found if you were polite and friendly so were they. Plan each day what you are going to do, be prepared to queue and watch out for queue jumpers, spread out in lines so no one can get passed you and for a few days forget your British politeness when waiting to go on rides and buses.

Thank God we weren't there as our main holiday   we would have been so disappointed. We're going to save our pennies and go back to Orlando for the authentic Disney experience!!

Visited DLP for the first time and I was apprehensive having read some of the reviews. I can now totally understand why some people can have an awful experience and some people just love it. We (2 adults, 2 children 6 and 8) stayed 2 nights at the Seqouia Lodge with tickets for 3 days in the park. We had an absolutely fantastic time. The harsh reality of this fantasy land is that you pay for what you get, and you can pay an awful lot. If you want to queue for thirty minutes to have your kids picture taken with Mickey, then you can, if you don't want to queue then book a meal in one of the restaurants that feature the characters, you won't queue, you'll get plenty of pictures, and you'll get decent but expensive food. the Auberge de Cendrillon is the top of the tree but at 60 Euros a head for adults and about 28 for the kids its not cheap, and thats the way it is. The queues for some of the rides are ridiculous, 90 minutes not uncommon, and the fastpass system is only of limited benefit when the place is busy, which is more or less all the time. The best time to go on those rides that you can't get on during the day is to go after dinner, 9.30pm onwards. If you travel by train for the day in the height of summer, and are on a budget then you could be forgiven for thinking that DLP is an unbearable waste of time. You need to plan, and if you can afford it then forget about the price and go for it. The rides are amazing, the motor stunt show spectacular, the atmosphere is awesome. I would definately visit again, there are ways to maximise the fun, but you need to think it through carefully.
Great Rides, great parade, good (halal) food. Great day with the lot.

Date of visit 25 August. I prepared for our visit with some trepidation having read many negative reviews but we (self and 9 year old) found it the most magical day out ever and certainly excellent value for money. We arrived at about 9.15 am and were able to park in the section closest to the entrance. Everything was clearly signposted and we only had to queue for a few minutes to exchange our vouchers at the ticket booth. Once inside all employees we came across were smiling, friendly and helpful. As for pushing and shoving, yes, there was some jostling from other visitors but no more than at attractions I have visited in the UK. My son was able to get close to nearly all the characters we came across and I had no difficulty taking his picture. I took a picnic lunch having read dire warnings about the cost and poor quality of the food and there were plenty of places to sit and eat it, though on the way out I did see a sign asking people not to take picnics into the park itself. Having said that, several employees passed us eating and nobody said anything. In the evening we had a meal at the Agrabah buffet restaurant in Adventureland which has a lovely setting (Aladin). We went straight after the first parade at about 8pm and being busy we had to queue for about 20 mins for a table. It was worth it, the food was excellent (North African), with a good selection to choose from. Three courses (eat as much as you want) and drinks came to 38 euros so not cheap but not extravagant either   you would struggle to get a good meal in London for that price. Snack wagons are available across the parc selling drinks 2,50 euros and popcorn 7 euros both cheaper than our local cinema in the UK especially as the popcorn comes in a re useable souvenir lidded container (my son instantly saw a home for his Toy Story soldiers). We saw the 'Animagique' show which we thoroughly enjoyed (singing along to the songs) and the 'Art of Animation' which is entertaining and informative. The parades were sumptuous and it really is worth sticking it out to the end for the Fantillusion parade where the floats and costumes are all lit up. I felt about 7 years old! We are not big fans of 'scary rides' so I can't comment on queues for those but the longest queue we had was 40 minutes which passed quickly chatting to other visitors but most were less. We stayed to the end and took a leisurely stroll back to the car park. There was no queue to exit the site and we were onto the motorway in no time. All in all, a fantastic day out and we can't wait to go again.

I'd like to point out iv never been during school holidays, so iv never had the joy of queuing for hours to get in the park and onto rides (I can see how this could dramatically alter the experience). Having just returned form our 10th visit to Disneyland Paris I regret to say that it feels like the Magic has finaly died. The Park itself could be a wonderful place, as it used to be, but it is now a run down shabby and poorly managed reflection of its former self. Our 6 day visit with a young child was beset by many problems which are summarised here. 1. People were smoking everywhere in the park except in the rides themselves. Although the restaurant areas are supposed to be non smoking, people were smoking in the seated areas around every restaurant we visited and around all the walkways and playgrounds. We never once witnessed any staff do anything about it. Are the Disneyland Paris Management unaware of the hazards of cigarette smoke or Disney's no smoking policy or do they simply not care? 2. The park is in a very poor state of repair with numerous holes and trip hazards in the walkways, bits of rides and decor missing or broken, rides breaking down and toilets in a disgraceful state with many blocked causing long waiting times. The riverboat was taken out of service while we were there and we had to wait 45 minutes while the Pirate ride was fixed after breaking down. Most of the rifles in the shooting gallery (costing 2 euros a go) had sights missing. Numerous faults and breakages in and around the haunted house. The pirate ship is presumably in such a state of disrepair that people are no longer allowed on it. The high rope bridge was covered in scaffolding. 3. There are now no shows on at the Chaparral Theatre, Fantasyland Stage and Castle stage and the only show on in the Hyperion is the African drummers who used to play outside of the Hakuna Matata restaurant. 4. Queue management now seems to be done to make it easy for the staff rather than fair for the visitors. We were at the front of the queue for attractions several times only to find ourselves not admitted first or directed to the back of the ride. 5. Opening times at some of the better value restaurants have been reduced and now close early in the evening. Most of the restaurants do not display their opening times so you can walk across the park for a meal only to find your chosen restaurant closed.

We went to Disney in December for my daughters 13th Birthday and had the most amazing time ever. We stayed at HOTEL CHEYENNE. The rides had small queues no more than 15min waiting time. The restuarants were OK but CAFE MICKEY was were we went on the night of her birthday all the characters were there and we got tons of photos. The parade was excellent and the characters christmas outfits were brill. I just wish I had taken my kids when they were younger (they were 13&11yrs) The only downside was the weather it was absolutely freezing and snowed on her birthday, the thermals and skiing trousers were a great item to pack as we had been warned about the cold before we went.

My fourteen year old daughter and I recently spent one of our six days in Paris at Disneyland. What a waste of a day. I guess we assumed that Disneyland Paris would offer an experience similar to what we have enjoyed a half dozen times in Orlando. Boy, were we wrong.First, we arrived from Paris by train right at opening time only to discover that there were just two people conducting security checks for all the people exiting the RER station. Seems to me that Disney customer service should be able to figure out that they might need more staff at busy times. So this was that start to our day: a thirty minute wait to have someone check my backpack.The staff that IS working at Disneyland Paris obviously does not benefit from the same training that their colleagues in America do. They were ornery, disheveled, inattentive, and     quite honestly   most appeared to be a bit daft. On several occasions, they even left their posts. Once while we were boarding    Rockin    Rollercoaster    and twice on    Space Mountain   , we were left to make our way to the trains and load ourselves in. This happened over and over so, consequently, we saw time and time again the rides leave the station with empty seats. More serious, perhaps, was that fact that on one of our turns on    Space Mountain   , no one ever checked to see if our harnesses were fastened. A major safety breech, I would imagine.The park itself was very    tired    looking, dirty, and in need of repair. The plaza in front of Disney Studios has holes in it where the concrete has worn away, buildings and rides need either a good scrubbing or a coat of paint, and the bathrooms were disgusting. I   ve always been so impressed with the attention to detail in Orlando. No such attention to detail is evident in Paris.And then there   s the smoke. Dear French People, have you not heard of lung cancer? You NEED to STOP smoking! And Dear Disneyland Paris, if you   re going to advertise the park as    Smoke Free   , it had better be. And if you   re going to have rules against smoking in line, you need to enforce them. The smoke was awful.On the up side,    Space Mountain    is (in my opinion) far better than the ride in Orlando.    Rockin    Rollercoaster    is just as good, although they don   t use the same recording studio setup for the ride, and    Tower of Terror    was fine.The one word I would use to describe our day at Disneyland Paris is disappointing. We were looking forward to enjoying a day like we have so many times at Walt Disney World and it just didn   t happen. If it tells you anything, I spent part of my day today looking for the address where I can write Disney CEO Robert Iger. The opening part of the letter to him will read:   Dear Mr. Iger, When was the last time you visited Disneyland Paris? From what I can tell, I   m pretty sure it has been a while. And I   m certain that when you do, you   ll be appalled.

This review will be most helpful to people who have visited WDW in Orlando and Disneyland in Anaheim many times (as we have), and are going to take time from their trip to Paris to go to Disneyland Paris as a novelty. The parks are not as good, but for the novelty aspect, it may not matter to you.My wife and I were here 20 years ago when it was new and had few rides. Now we came back with four kids ages 7 14.We went on a rainy Sunday in August. Got there at the time of opening, as we always do, by taking the RER from Paris itself (about 14e roundtrip). The Disneyland Park was open till 11, but we had gone on everything we wanted to and shopped at the Emporium on the way out, and still walked out by 9. (mind you, I have never left a Disney park before closing in the fifty times i have gone in the last 40 years). Our kids had a great time despite being soaked.
