We got the 2parkhopper (which is not available on the US site) by booking through a friend in the UK. You can also get it at the Park, but I would never want to have to wait on THAT line.We started with WD Studios, because it had a 7PM closing time. We skipped the Effects show, Stunt show and Backlot because we assumed the ones in Orlando were at least as good. Rock and Roller Coaster has a less interesting queue than in WDW and the ride is less loud and exciting. Tower of Terror is similar, but with a few extra bounces. Five min wait at that hour, no Fastpass needed. The Crush Coaster had a 70 min queue so we skipped it. Aladdin was same as FL. And the new kiddy area based on Toy Story was closed except to Season pass holders. So much for the Studios. On to Disneyland!A 5 min walk brought us to the entrance through the base of the Disneyland Hotel.The park is smaller but on the same scheme. Using the Fastpass system, we did most rides as usual.  Discoveryland  replaces  Tomorrowland  and is the same retro look of the new Tomorrowlands in the US. Buzz Lightyear similar, but the guns are hand held. Space Mountain is subtitled  Mission 2 . This version is a full length roller coaster car, and the ride is similar to Aerosmith. Nothing like FL or CA. But a fun ride. The head rest are hard and you get knocked around a bit, and there are inversions on this one too. Star Tours is in French, but the same. Autopia is same idea. Orbitron is same but entrance is on ground level so you aren't much higher than Dumbo or Aladdin. Fantasyland is spread out more but has a new, stand alone 'it's a small world  like the one in Anaheim. Teacups, Carrousel and Snow White are same. Pinocchio is like Anaheim. Peter Pan is same idea but jerkier as you fly around. No Pooh (oh Well).Adventureland has Pirates which is done well and is a nice update with extra scenes. Not much else there but an Adventure Isle similar to Tom Sawyer's. There is an Indiana Jones ride that is just another outdoor roller coaster (not like CA at all). The Thunder Mountain is essentially the same and excellent. Phantom Manor (not Haunted Mansion) looks like Psycho house and is an update of original ride with new scenes (and clearer if you know the backstory) and is well done. The Railroad is same. Main Street is same.The Castle is a 3rd version and is nice.That's it! Nothing else to do. Many fewer rides. (In case you were keeping score, there were only four rides on the entire left side of the Park!)For us, as a very expensive novelty, it was fun. But I can see why the European reviews are so poor.

Spent 2 days here with our children, 7 & 8. This park is HORRIBLE. First of all, the park allows guests to smoke virtually anywhere. One smoking area was designated RIGHT OUTSIDE A CHILDREN'S PLAYGROUND!!!! Not that it matters    no one seems to pay attention to the no smoking signs. Probably because no employees back this up. Which is the 2nd of all    employees are VERY hard to find in this park. Except where they are loading or unloading a line. Here, they are very friendly. But sssssllllllooooowwww    which is the 3rd of all. I don't know if it's the culture or just laziness, but employees seemed a little lost on loading and unloading. On a good note, just about every employee spoke some English. The biggest disappointment came when Toy Story 3 Playland wasn't open yet    when it had been advertised as being open in the US.  Invited guests  only. Tell that to a 7 year old who had spent the last month dreaming of seeing it. Guest relations was a joke and outright lied to us    swore there were no people in that closed area when you could see them with your own eyes. I would not recommend this park to ANYONE if they can get to or have been to DisneyWorld Fl.

Disneyland Paris is a dump. During the initiation rite (you can't join the gang without showing ability to tolerate long waits while suffering the noise and manners of the rudest people in the world) I jokingly said at the gate,  This won't be a patch on Gullivers World, Warrington. How we laughed, five hours later as my words turned out to be true. Desperate to find something for my children to enjoy, I cried,  OK so there's hardly any rides, and those we can go on have a one hour wait with fast pass, but look, let's go into Mickeys Emporium. Stupidly imaginging it was Mickey's house, how amused I was to discover it was ANOTHER SHOP!!!!!! I can't find the words, I can only say DON'T GO!!

A review below hits the nail squarly on the head. If your children are less than 1.4metres there is in fact little to do. Teacups, a car ride and a (Broken) carousel On all of these rides adults were pushing in front of children to get on!!!! If they are 1.2 meters they can get on the runaway train ride.The queues are ridiculous throughout and the 'attractions' are very widely spaced in order to give you the opportunity to pass (literally) hundreds of shops selling the same things. To be fair, the security warned us when we joined the 40 minute queue to get the bags searched  Keep smiling because you'll be queing all day . He was not wrong.The park was busy (as I expected) but I was astounded by the number of adults without kids in a theme park aimed at children. I was even more astounded when they were scrabbling to get on childrens rides and queue jumping past said children. Whether the Disney 'magic' prevents people observing civilised norms of behaviour i don't know. The adults pushing past children was not just limited to the rides, or the laughable attractions (For a laugh you have to see Pocahontus' garden, a couple of slides and seats   'weather permitting'!!!)Food is appalling. Pizza   7 Euro for kids and maybe three inches across. Thre are Panini's etc, but again very expensive (I think around12.50 euro) and again massive queues.This was the only place I have every been where there were people queue jumping to get out.

We have recently visited Disney Paris for the 3 time, and have been to the parks in USA a number of times. (we are Disney veterans having been approximately 10 times in all)With the possible exception of the food in the Blue Lagoon (which is fairly good) the parks do not compare well.Our most recent visit to Paris was spoiled by:Attractions breaking down; nearly all of the main attractions broke down on our visit  Pirates of the Caribbean, Buzz lightyear, big thunder mountain, back lot tour  some of them having regular problems on the day we were there. No apology from the staff  even when we were trapped in the Pirates ride for 30 minutes. Back lot tour proceeded with no commentary. The park has endemic queue jumping with no interest from the staff. We encountered rudeness  one of the characters hit out at a visitor who pulled on his coat to get attention for a photo when he clearly considered that his stint was finished! I have never seen such rude and arrogant staff as in Paris. My daughter was a little slow on one ride pulling down the restraint (Rock & Roller coaster) so a staff member did it and in doing so trapped her arm in the restraint which she did not notice. We have been to more theme parks and on more rides that I can count, and never had such bad treatment even at much lower prices or less esteemed organisations.We pre booked a character breakfast in the Village, at 24 Euro per adult, and were a little late (5 minutes) so my daughters rushed ahead while we stowed our luggage at the station  when they arrived at the restaurant with pre  booked ticket, they were not allowed to the table without payment for the meal! So they had to force their way to a table to wait  when I arrived 5 minutes later (still within the 15 minutes  grace  allowed) I heard about this and walked out to get breakfast elsewhere  moreover this is a buffet restaurant  no service at table, so the price is high for a shabby village outlet. We did look at the buffet and noted too that there were no pancakes and so it is a pretty standard breakfast at a very high price.We purchased tickets (high price of course) over the Internet from Disney  these you print off and take to the park. There was a long queue as usual for tickets so I showed the pre printed tickets to the staff and they pointed us back to the ticket queue to waste more time for 30 minutes  we then noticed the gate for pre printed tickets and used it  they simply did not know the procedure. The tickets are a pain, however as the scanner had difficulty with the bar code. My wife needed to take some food and medicine to the park, and for convenience we use a small carry  on bag with wheels, about the size of a small back pack but with wheels. We had no problem with this for most of the day, passing between both parks (we had  hopper  tickets) but then at about 6 pm the staff decided it was a  security risk  (having had it inspected at the bag check). So they demanded she book it into the storage at 6 Euros and we had to manage as best we could with medicine. The toilets in the best restaurant stink of sewage due to the old style of toilets or drainage. we had that before in April on our last visit so it is not a 0ne off. When i last visited the toilets were blocked and when i pointed it out to the restaurant manager he shrugged and said they are not his toilets!The  Skull  overlook over the lake stank of urine.Smoking is allowed in the park so often you will be eating or queuing next to someone smoking.Tables were being left uncleared of food in self service areas for long periods.Attendants made more effort to make sure they look good with their sun glasses than arrange for efficient filling of the cars, so that despite hour long queues for top rides, cars departed unfilled or part filled with plenty of space.Tips; well if you must go to Paris, don   t expect it to match the friendliness, care or quality of USA. The queues will be as long or longer (they lie about the time as we often timed the ourselves  40 minutes claimed on the big thunder mountain was close to 75 minutes in reality). The locals get better offers than you can easily find on the Disney site  pay one day get the second day free for example is widely advertised locally, but you cannot find any real discounts on the Disney site, other than a small discount of about 15% for booking on line.

We were just in Disneyland Paris on a Monday in August. The whole experience was a disappointment from beginning to end. To get into the park took at least 45 minutes, in three very disorganized queues first to go through security, then to get tickets, then to get into the park. The main problem with Disney is that it's far too crowded, at least in the summer. The park is much smaller that its Florida counterpart, so with so many people milling about it's hard just to maneuver the walkways. Obscenely long lines. And nearly every line had a line jumper! Park not as clean as in Florida, and the staff certainly not as friendly. Just before 6:00 p.m. my husband waited in line for fish and chips at Toad Hall restaurant. When he arrived at the counter, at 5:58, the manager literally closed the door in his face and said,  We're closed.  He was the last one in line and they could have easily closed the door after serving him. We had a crappy sandwich for dinner someplace else instead. Now the the good: the rides were all fun, especially It's a small World, the Fairy Tale boat ride, Pirates of the Caribbean. And the parade at 7:15 was great. But nearly all lines were 30 minutes or more; we averaged only one ride per hour. However, although I did not enjoy the day, my kids definitely did. They have good memories, so it wasn't a complete waste. I'll never go back to DPL. Stick to Disney in Florida or other locales.

For me Euro disney was an ordeal although my 5 year old loved it. It was so expensive and there really isnt that much to do for teenagers. Durign the summer, the lines are too long. The wiat time for a ride that was like 1 minute long, was at least 70 minutes.Was it worth the cost? I doubt it. Newport Bay Club is supposed to be 4 star. But the place is like a market, I tell you. The number of people at the check in, at the bus...The staff try their best I guess. I stood next to a lady who stayed at Santa Fe Hotel and she had previously stayed at Newport. She loved Santa Fe hotel and it was much cheaper and nearer the parc. It is also a lot smaller.If u want value for money try Hotel Santa Fe

Having jsut come back from DLP I was amazed that the scores of reviews I read on the web never told you what you really need to know if going to DLP with you children. We went over a weekend in early August, 2010, two adults and two children (3 and 5).Never go in the sumnmer hols and especiallly never at a weekend. The park is mobbed. They let in 10 times more people than the park can handle. We went on 3 rides in 2 days!!! The queues were that bad.Be aware that there is absolutely nothing there for toddlers. The crucial height restrictions are 1.2m and 1.4m. There really is nothing there for toddlers, a couple of pathetic rides (teacups!)for those up to 1m, a couple more pretty pathetic things for those above 1.2m but to get on 90% of the rides you have to be over 1.40m. Consequently, a visit is pointless with children under 1.40m (ie below about 7 years old).It is expensive, but that's no surprise.The park is massive but there is very little in it. Expect to walk for miles for very little return. Actual rides and attractions probably take up less than 2% of the entire surface area of the park. Disney's plan has cklearly been to fit as many people as possible into the park without any concern that there is nothing for the crowds to do once inside.The queues are truly horrendous. Expect to queue for between 1   2 hours for every ride. I had read this before I went and had assumed that the queus would be for the big thrill rides bit no one would queue for the sorts of things my 3 and 5 year old would want to go on. I was very wrong. As there is nothing for the young, the teacups and the carousel, the sort of basic rides you would find at any town fair in the UK, had queues of up to 2 hours!!! With hot, bored, tired children the scenes were horrendous. I canlt believe people put themselves through this and that no one onTrip Advisor or anyone else points out these horrors out.We were satying at the Sante Fe Hotel, which was very basic (just an accomodation block), but functional enough. We had tickets for 3 days but only stayed for 2 days as the experience was so awful. You simply can't have fun in those crowds, that heat, that much walking and so much queing for so little. For example, we queued for 1 hour to go on the carpets over Agra ride, a grand name for a simple toddlers fairground ride. I timed the ride. It lasted 1 minute 20 seconds. We had qeued for an hour!Make sure you bring a pushchair, you will need it. You can rent shopping trolley like pushchairs at the park for 9 euros per day but make sure you keep a hold of your receipt because people will nick your pushchair when it's parked! If you have your receipt you can at least go back and complain and get given another one (we had our pushchair nicked twice in 2 days!)Re food and drink, it's all junk food and coke. It is not possible to buy milk anywhere inside, outside or within miles of the park! If you do find some, it will be UHT milk.Bizarrely enough, children make up about 5% of the vistors to the park! The vast majority of visitors are adults from across Europe and lots of couples in theire 20's and 30's. Whether they were simple before they arrived , I don't know, but once there they seem to forget the normal structure and behaviour of adults in society. They visit all the rides. Whilst standing in line for small, basic funfair rides like the teacups and a carousel, suitable for those up to 5, I was amazed that 80% of the queue was made up of adults without children or adults with teenagers... to go on toddlers rides!!!!!!!!! This bizarre behaviour is repeated across the park.But queing is the name of the game there. You queue for everything, for hours. Before the parades start, people start queuubng and sitting down about 1 hour before! The park is not designed to enable you to see anything. Imagine a nor mal falt street with a parade on it, unless you are kerbside, you see nothing.The fantilusion parade is quite nice to watch but it starts at 10.30pm, ideal for toddlers   NOT! it lasts 30 minutes, then there ios a load of faffinf around and then the fireworks start at about 11.10pm. The fireworks are lovely, but what child can stay awake until that time. Our children are always up late, but with the heat, drudgery and qeueuing they were fast asleep and had been begging to be taken home hours before..All in all, I would strongly advise that you don't go to DLP. It's all hype. The actual experieince is tortorous at worst and deeply disappointing at best. There is absolutely nothing there for children under 1.40m, even if there were no queues and the park was empty, there still wouldn't be anything for young children to do. The three toddlers rides they have are teacups, a carousel and one other standard fairground ride. However, Disney have placed these rides in hard landscaping, given them a fancy name and tried to build some hype sround what are in fact utterly bog standard funfair rides that you will see in aat any county town fair in the UK, and whihc you can ride for 2 quid without qeueing.My children were so excited about going but when we got there, they were the first to want to leave. We had tickets for 3 days but left after 2 days deeply disappointed. In fact mad, because we then went on to Burgundy for the rest of our 7 day holiday. It was amazing, the beuaty and interet of the unspoilt hsitoric environment was incredible and served only to remind us how we had wasted 2 days of our lives at DLP.All in all, if you are simple, and an adult and like queuing, you may enjoy yourself.If you want your children to have fun, then take them to funfair in the UK and spoil them for a couple of hours. They will have much more fun and you will save hundreds of pounds. But whatever you do, don't believe the hype about DLP, it's all garbage. Incredibly, the place is utterly unsuited to children of pre teen age.

We were all so excited about going to disneyland, especially my 8 year old son. What a disappointment, firstly the place is so crowded, then it is full of food outlets and souvenir shops, if they concentrated as much on the rides and entertainment as they have on the shops it might be something worth visiting. Then there is the issue of height restrictions, if you are under 140cm you can't go on certain rides, but you still pay the same price as those who are 140cm and above. I fortunately bought our tickets from the train station which cost me 45 euro per person, which adds up to alot for a family of 5. Luckily we took food with us, but if we were to eat there, you could not get a decent meal for less than 10 euro per person, as it was on the way home we paid 6 euro for a crappy tasting hot dog in a squished roll.Worst thing of all is the long queues waiting for the rides, my kids waited 50 mins for a 2 mins ride, in all we were there from 11am till 8pm and between my three children they got to go on 6 rides.As for any other entertainment, there really isn't much and if you happen to see any characters in the streets, good luck even getting close, let along getting a photo with them.We are from Australia and if you have been to the theme parks at the Gold Coast you would know that disneyland does not even come close to the quality, value for money and entertainment.SERIOUSLY DON'T WASTE YOUR MONEY OR YOUR TIME, A DAY IN PARIS IS MORE WORTH IT

I was the biggest sceptic but I have been converted and now fully embrace the disney magic!Just lovely   great for my almost 4 year old   she had an amazing time.We stayed at Hotel New York which was fine and served its purpose and travelled on Eurostar   try and get the direct trains, changing is a hassle at Lille!Highlight was the expensive Auberge de Cendrillion and dining with the Princesses. Worth every penny   pure magic   a great food : ) Cafe Mickey was also great fun anf favourite area was Fantasy land. The parades were stunning...... altogether now....  It's just like we dreamed it, as far as I can see, it's just like we dreamed it, as good as good can be!

Went to Disneyland Paris two years ago and simply had to go back again this year!The queuing can be horrible at times, but the fast pass system is well functioning!I found the staff friendly, smiley and very helpful in general! People talking about litter and garbage must have come on a bad day, I think the park was very clean even though there were tons of people there. The parades are regular, and yes, there could have been more characters walking around in the park, but I think for the children and the characters safety it is a good idea to have a queue system and do it in orderly form.The eating options aren  t all that, everything is very expensive, and the food really isn  t all that, but for one day, I am willing to look away from that fact! Buy some breakfast before going and bring some fresh fruit in your backpack. Get your fastpass to Thunder Mountain and Buzz laser blaster first as they go FAST and I mean fast! We didn  t get to go on Thunder mountain and the waiting time was 1 hour and 45 minutes estimated and no fastpasses left. Have fun!

We went to Disneyland Paris in April 2010 and I can honestly say It was better than I could ever imagined.My Kids are 8,3 & 2 and watch the Disney Channel & Films all the time and watching their faces when Mickey, Woody & Co were standing there and getting pics taken was priceless.yes it's a bit pricey but who said The Best things in life are free??Go and do it and stay in the Davy Crocket Ranch Upgrade to a Premium Cabin & have the Holiday of a Lifetime!!!!!Disneyland Paris is a Dream Come True so Just do it!!!

I have just returned from 6 days at Disneyland Paris and I have to say it is not at all what I expected. I have previously been to the Disney parks in Florida 4 times and California once and was expecting something similar. How wrong was I! Although I have no complaints about the park itself, I found the majority of the other visitors (anyone that wasn't British) to be arrogant, ignorant, selfish and extremely rude. It seemed that only the British knew how to queue for the attractions and character greetings. My family and I were increasingly annoyed at the amount of times we were pushed or shoved out of the way. On one occasion, whilst waiting to meet one of the characters, we stood patiently waiting our turn only to be in the middle of a free for all whilst the Disney Cast Member stood by and did nothing! This is the third Disney Park I have visited and can honestly say that I will not be revisiting! The only other thing to mention is the cost of everything. We found everything to be expensive. In hindsight it would probably have been better to pay a little extra for the holiday and go back to Florida!

Beware of the Reviewer who writes  great place, loved it! . They obviously haven't lived! I actually feel sorry for the people who work at Disneyland Paris. Apparently, there have been major cutbacks which have affected not only the guests (us!), but the employees too in a big way. We have just returned and are so happy to be home in our clean, comfortable home again. Disneyland Paris is the most outstanding rip off of all times. They lure you in with 'extra' free days at the resort, only to trap you within their gates, offering you nothing but disgusting food (I've had better in hospitals), appalling service and dirty, run down hotel rooms. You are far better off flying to the U.S. and doing it all there   believe me! We couldn't even eat basic McDonald's type food (not that we wanted to) for less than 45 Euros for two adults and two children under 6! But at the end of the day, it's all about the children, isn't it? But where were the characters   I remember going to DL California back in the '70's. I have photos to prove this   on every corner there was either 'Grumpy' or 'Sleepy', Sleeping Beauty or Cinderella, Pooh Bear or Goofy. But no, not in Paris. Hardly a Disney character in sight, and when you did, you had to queue up for ages to have a photo taken with them! I know we all remember things to be so much better when we were kids, but this was such a disappointment   and what an expensive one too.

Visited Euro Disney yesterday. Be prepared to have your money ripped from you at every corner you turn  there are no end of food places, souvenir stands and all the American hype you ever dreamed off. The dreadful piped music is all over the park and is contniously pumped at you.DON'T go to Cafe Hyperion  le service est MERDE!!!!!! we waited over half an hour just to have our order taken. There were 4 very bored staff handing out ordErs but obviously the kitchen couldn't keep up with the demand and they wEre resting on the counter waiting to hand out orders. Would have been better employed in the kitchen. The servise was dreadful and they should spenD tIme at MCDonald's learning about efficiency.If you're claustrophobic, don't go near the Pirates of the Caribbean unless you like being in a ave for 45 minutes waiting in a slow moving queue.An experience I never wish to repeat again thanks very much.

Well, if you  ve never been to a Disneyland, it  s worth going, so to have seen it. I remembered alot of the sttractions from my visist in FLorida and Los Angeles decades ago. The Design is nice. But from what I remember, the other Disney places are cleaner, always staff takiong care of rubbish, with that special charming Disney atmosphere. Not so in Paris.. We had 2 children with us, most of the time they were scared by the rides ( Pirates and Buzz Laser) So I would recommend it not for children under 7 8 years. They really liked Small world. All major attractions were working and waiting times were reasonable. Shuttle bus service was frequent and we never had to wait.Sadly there were never any characters around, except for the times in the program in the main square. That was what my son had been so looking forward too. There is no other word for the food: horrible and extremely overpriced.If you don  t want to live on tastless fries , ice cream , undefinable meat in susages etc. you just have to bring your own fruit and sandwiches. Food is extremely expensive in side and outside the park.Luckily before our arrival we went to a large supermarket ( eg carrefour) and bought fresh bread and produce, cheese and coldcuts.We ate at the Steakhouse in Disney village. A kids menu around 12 Euro, with the chesseburger consisting of nothing but the bun and cheese and meat. No ketchup or salad or tomato. The chocolate pudding for dessert tasting burnt. I had a steak that reminded me more of the sole of a shoe, the side salad having about 3 drops of dressing. Service is slow, and not very personal.You just always have the feeling, all they want is your money with the least effort they can get bye.SO, I would recommend Disneyland to someone really wanting to go, with preparation to the things stated above. But I personally do not feel the urge to go again in the near future. There are so many other palces in Europe to see...

I paid in advance for return transport from CDG airport to the hotel at Eurodisney   waited 1 1 2 hours, they hung up on the phone, eventually had to pay another taxi to take us.They promised a refund   never saw it and they hang up the phone when contacted.North Sud Transport, also go by name of Trans Network and Navette Airoport. Dont touch them.Eurodisney was great for our 4 year old, Magic Castle Hotel was good, this was the only problem.

If you're going to Euro Disney please take note   the food inside the park is pretty bad and really expensive. BUT inside the train station (which you will walk past to get to the park) are a couple of cafes and a newsagents where you can buy sandwiches rolls drinks at a fraction of the price inside. We took a small cool bag loaded up and saved a fair bit of cash!!!Also in regard to the parks make sure you get FASTPASS tickets for popular rides, it's free and can save loads of time waiting in line.

On arriving at Disneyland Park Paris we decided to catch the train that circled the park. We queued for over half an hour, and were very disappointed. We thought the ride would orientate us to the park, but instead we just saw lots of trees. Lots and lots of people everywhere   long queues everywhere. Our children are aged 12 and 14   too old for the kiddy rides and too scared of the fast rides. There is a fast track pass that allows you to book a ride in advance, but we did not use this. However we did enjoy the  It's a small world  boat ride, and  Pirates of the Caribbean  ride. The Grand parade was enjoyable. In retrospect, we wished we had gone to the Disneyland studios.I would recommend this park for families with small children and thrill seekers   but be prepared to queue.

We were very excited to have an opportunity to visit Disney Paris, as my husband's family are Disney fans from way back. While the park is well layed out, and has all the attractions you'd expect, we were disappointed in the details. Our two boys (age 8 and 10) enjoyed themselves, but even they noticed the amount of garbage laying about, as well as the disgusting smoking that was permitted everywhere. When you are accustomed to the super tidy US Disney parks, this is definitely a letdown. Also, the legendary French appathy towards tourists is not much different in a park that is supposed to cater to everyone. While we met some cast members that seemed to enjoy meeting folks from all over, most were definitely less than friendly. All in all, not an experience we are likely to repeat.

My boyfriend and I have been visiting Disneyland Paris on a yearly basis for the past four years and we never tire of it! We usually buy the 2 park 1 day tickets online from the Disney website but I think you can get a slight discount buying online from FNAC and going to one of their stores to pick them up.The best days of the week to go are Tues Wed Thurs as we've found these to be quietest. Although it's always a bit of a gamble, sometimes we've literally had no queues at all and gone round and round on Space Mountain time and time again, and other times it's the usual 30mins  queues.My tips are to take water bottles to fill up from the fountains and a bag full of snacks, we   ve never had food or drink taken from us so it's no hassle to bring it. Wear comfy shoes as you will walk for miles! Pick up a map on your way into the Park so you can decide your plan of attack.All the rides are fab and there's a selection to appeal to everyone (I can't speak for the children's ride as we have no kids so avoid these!). Honestly there's not been any that disappoint and even ones which look a bit sedate like Star Wars prove good fun.Despite us not being the kind of people to enjoy dance shows, watching some of the Euro pop routines that are put on in the streets is entertaining.I think you need to go here with the right attitude of having fun. Disneyland Paris is unique and should be regarded as so. Go and have fun trying out different rides, glaring at the annoying Spanish kids, watching the Moteurs Action shows, feeling sick from too many loop the loops and then trudging back to the train station after 7 hours of crazy Disney muzak.

On our visit to the park, it was pretty much as expected. However, the weather was breezy, which kept us mostly cool. We went mainly for our two y.o. (others in our party were adults) and went on all the kiddie rides. Similar to Disneyland in California (the huanted manion was different and a little disappointing for me) but all in all, she enjoyed it, especially the character show in the at the end of Main Street in front of Sleeping Beauty's Castle. However, the fast pass system seemed to cater for those spending two days at the park (the passes were only available for the next day), which didn't help us at all. Also, as a regular visitor to the California park, the rides like small world are newer, and look it. The slightly shabby look of the ride in Calirfornia I find charming and nostalgic, which is missing a bit from Disney Paris.

I've been in Disneyland in summer. The park was extremely crowded and i think wasn't prepared to take so many people at one time. It was even nice in the morning, queues for the rides were short and there was not too many people, but after 12 o'clock the fun has started... I've been queueing for Space Mountain Mission 2 almost 2 hours... Moreover it's the only  extreme  rollercoaster there except of Indiana Jones. The rest of attractions are suitable for kids. I wanted to have a dinner there, but a waitress in a restaurant didn't know english and made some signs to get out.. I didn't try in other restaurants there and ate my sandwich. Builndings and surroundings are incredible. Even it this horrible crowd I could see the castle, street like in a western and a parade with mickey the mouse. I think I would have enjoyed it more during other seaoson, for example   autumn.

For those who as been to Disneyland California or World Disney in Orlando, please don't spend time going to the one in France.....not worth any penny compare to those in USAThe rides are bad...no light and you are always in the dark...waiting time too long even on week days.

we went over the may half term and had a great holiday. disney do do these sort of things really well and the kids loved it. my daughter were 5 and 2 and they had a great time. the park is aimed at young kids upto age 10, especially girls withe princess and minnie mouse themes seen a lot.its really well run and clean, and very safe so you know the kids wont fall into a pool accidently or etc. the main park is biiger and more like a treat ofr the kids. walt disney studios is all about their films and had a few things for older kids, but my kids prefered the main park.queues for the smaller rides are ok, but the big rides have long queues upto 45 minutes. you can get a fastpark ticket, where you prebook a timeslots later in the day, which is a good idea. food is ok and not too expensive   you can eat lunch for 7 8 euros.parking is very easy and plentyful and i would recommned driving if you have a car and a free parking pass.we will be going again and really enjoyed it. the kids especially loved the  its a small world  ride and the magic tea cups and carousel.i tried 2 rollercoasters   the mine train and indiana jones and both were good, but not massive compared to other parks.

My wife and I accompanied our son, his wife, and our two granddaughters (6 yrs and 4 yrs). Flying from Luton at 6am Monday to Paris (Charles de Gaulle) and returning Friday 10pm 5 days later. The flights with Easy Jet were on time and airport transfer was arranged separately with Tio Shuttle, booked via internet and paid in Euros on completion of each trip. I would certainly use them again and recommend them to others.We stayed at the Disney Santa Fe Hotel which lived up to its 2* status (a basic but comfortable base), had adjoining rooms and could pre book breakfast (included) either in the hotel restaurant or IN THE DISNEYLAND PARK.Also included was a 5 day pass for both the Disneyland Park and the Walt Disney Studios Park. Once inside there were rides and attractions for all ages and we made good use of the Fast Pass tickets to avoid queuing for the busier rides.Must see the daily Disney Parade at 4.30 each afternoon.In the evening we ate in the Disney Village   mainly fast food and a bit expensive. Annettes Diner was the most popular (waiters on roller skates!).A really different holiday which the kids (and adult kids !) loved and had us all wishing we had their energy.Wouldn't recommend for children under 4, they would miss out on so much.

if you have been to disney world florida or disneyland anaheim, you will be so disappointed here.over priced in all departments, only average customer service a pale iimitation of the real thing.3 days at the disneyland hotel, travelling from london on eurostar, for 4 adults and 3 small children cost close to   4000. my advice go for the real thing. the prime motivation here is to rip you off not entertain you. closing space mountain in half term week is a good example.

We stayed at Marriott's Village I'lle de France. Not a Disney hotel but only 5 minutes drive away. Well recommended. Go on line and look for the ticket bargains, we got 2 park tickets 4 days for the price of 3.There is an annual membership if you buy a full adult price one day 1 or 2 parks ticket plus 32 euros which gives you unlimited access for one year, though there are 65 blackout days (all the major holidays no doubt).If you have a young girl in the party and she would like a princess dress (there were lots of girls wearing them around the park) buy one in your local disney store before you leave. The park shops sell them at 2 3 times the cost.Make full use of the fastpass system, it will save you lots of queing time on the main rides. Generally waiting time with a fastpass ticket was 5 10 minutes. You are only allowed to register for one ride at a time.Disney studios was very dissappointing with a number of rides out of action long term, rides went unserviceable whilst we were there and none of the fastpass machines were working on the day we were there.My grandaughter was collecting the autographs of characters. Go to Woodey's Ranch in Disneyland. It was well organised and timed, though the queue was long. The characters in Disney Studios were very uncooperative and it was not at well organised. There lots of tears where children waited patiently only for the characters to be dragged off by their minders. Long queues every where. The tram ride ride was very dissappointing, particularly if you had the expectations of it being similar to Universal Studios. I hour wait for 10 minute ride. What we saw was good, but very short.Be prepared for the 8 euro hot dogs and similarly high prices on all other fast food outlets.Overall the 4 days worked well particularly in Disneyland. We got to do everything over that period. Disneyland scores 4 star but the studios are 2 star hence overall score of 3 stars.

I found the official brochure for Disneyland Paris very confusing, and needed the help of a local travel agent. However, once booked, the whole Disney organisation was pretty flawless. Of the nine Disney hotels, we opted for the Newport Bay, which we disco vered is the one furthest from the park, although it is only a ten minute walk and there is a shuttle train. No complaints about the hoterl, except that the pools are closed at lunchtime until 3 pm. When booking it is well worthwhile going for the character dining option whereby youjh meet the Disney characters while you eat. The other must is the Buffalo Bill wild west show. This is part of the pre booked package, and if you can, it is worth getting to the venue early and paying extra for the seats nearest the arena. The other big advantage of going for the package deal with Disney is that guests of the nine hotels have a pass enabling them to get into the park at 8 am rather than 10 am. You can then get onto the most popuar rides before the long queues start,.The half board option is the best as you get vouchers for dinner which can be used at any of the restaurants or for the Buffalo Bill show, which includes dinner. For lunch you can get filled baguettes or other snaks fauirly easily. We rate Planet Hiollywood as the worst value for money.

we traveled as a family to disneyland resort paris and stayed at the sequoia lodge hotel. we went at the start of the easter holidays and was plesantly surprised with the weather, the hotel is massive and set in the middle of two equally big hotels (newport bay and new york) which sit around the disney lake, these hotels are perfectly sited as it is only a 10 min walk to the disney village and the parks.on arrival we were greeted by the very friendly hotel staff who checked us in very quickly and showed us where our room was,the rooms are a decent size with two double beds and although very clean the decor was a bit dated and the lighting dull gloomy.the hotel has two big restaurants to choose from one slightly more expensive than the other but to be honest the food was just the same.for the three of us to eat a two course meal with one drink each averaged at   100 and this was the same if you ate at the disney village.we went to see buffalo bills wild west show with mickey and friends and would recommend this to all it was great fun.the disney village has lots of shops more or less selling the same over priced disney merchandise and about a dozen places to eat from mcdonalds to planet hollywood and steak house, we found the rainforrest cafe a nice place to eat.the disney parks speak for their selves with the new attractions very popular, as we went on the school holidays it was as expected very busy, i would recommend 2 days in each park to get round all the rides and shows.we enjoyed our stay at the sequoia lodge and were blessed with great weather for that time of year, the staff were very helpful always with a smile, but now that we have done the disney experiance probably would`nt go back.it was our first time in france and we took the rer train into the center of paris (the station is at the rear ot the disney village).paris is beautiful, we took the bus tour (les car rouge) which took us right around all the main tourist points and you could jump on or off at any point and have a wander around,it was an experiance i loved and for that would visit again.

We've been to DLP twice and are going again in JulyHad several different experiences which pretty much illustrate how important planning is.First time we went it was mid October and the place was nearly empty   we walked onto most of the rides and on several just stayed on the ride for repeat trips. Absolutely brilliant.Second time we (stupidly) went on a Saturday in September and it was heaving. We only got on a few rides and generally felt a bit frustrated. Totally our fault.We've done the trip via plane to CDG with the coach transfer which is fine but a bit slow. We've also done a day trip via train to Paris with the RER transfer (the direct train arrives too late in the day for a day trip) which was totally mad   too much travelling time, wouldn't recommend it.Next trip will be for several days and we're goind via eurostar direct to the park   should be nice and relaxing!On our October trip we stayed in the Disneyland Hotel which was wonderful and highly recommended if expensive! Literally across from the park entrance!The park staff were generally very polite (surprisingly) the only exception bizarrely were the characters who would walk off as a child approached!Food in the parks was pretty dire (at least where we tried). Annette's which is a diner just outside the park itself was brilliant however and well worth a visit. The Blue Lagoon was also quite interesting although it has a bad rep for service when busy. Walts was awful   terrible food, as was the Steakhouse which in France is a bit of a shock!The Buffalo Bill show was great fun   well worth the trip!Use Fastpasses properly, Plan the rides you really want to go on and go on those first thing while the queues are small (literally run to them!)   then you can relax and trail around at leisure later on.Whatever you do don't spend an hour queuing for the Dumbo ride which lasts 2 minutes and is pretty tame.Also   if you're going to the Studios, please don't miss the Rock and Roll Coaster as it's the best ride in either park by far   absolutely brilliant.If you turn up without a plan, mid morning during the school holidays then you're asking for a tiring, frustrating day. If you plan ahead and preferably go during the school term and mid week then you can have a great time   No it's not Florida, but it's not bad! I prefer it to Alton Towers which I find dirty, depressing and full of rowdy teenagers.

Myself, Husband and 2 1 2 yr old daughter went here for a 5 night break the week before half term (low season)   and had an absolute blast! Having read reviews on here, was a little worried as to if we would have a good time. We booked via Thomas Cook, at the Sequioa Lodge, with half board plus for me and hubby, tickets for the Wild West Show and Mickey Mouse Breakfast. Before we went I reserved a table at the Lucky Nugget for 3pm on the day we arrived (flew with Air France from Manchester, no problem going or coming back, although CDG airport was very pricey for food   so take a snack!!). We got the VEA shuttle which was a bit of a scramble at CDG but you just have to be organised, one sorts luggage other in queue to get on bus. There is alot of bustle but stay firm and we got seats etc. The other downside was the huge queue at check in at Sequioa. It was organised, but there were so many people arriving at the same time it seemed to take ages, but probably only 20 mins tops. All staff in hotel and on the Parks were helpful. If they didn't speak English they got someone who could. A smile can go a long way! Some of the other tourists were rude, we had a couple of run ins with parents trying to 'push' their kids under the roped off areas for meeting characters, but we found if we made a fuss they soon ended up at the back of the queue looking a little ashamed! We ate at Annettes Diner, Walts American Cafe, Cafe Mickey (breakfast and an evening meal), Lucky Nugget, all were fine. We tended to eat off the normal menu, as oppose to the half board menu. As long as you tell your waiter you have the vouchers, there was no problem. We didn't do this at the Lucky Nugget and it took them a while to sort out the computer bill! They were very pleasant about this though. Usually our bill would be around 30 euros extra, as we were drinking wine   beer which was usually around 6 euros a pint, or I think we paid 22 euros for a bottle of rose in Cafe Mickeys. The Wild West Show was great. Lots of hat waving and banging plates   all good fun for a 2yr old! The food was fine, we weren't ill! Got spare ribs, chilli, wedges, sweetcorn, bread and apple pie for afters. Also had a big bowl of tortillas. We also had a couple of glasses of beer which we didn't realise we got in the price   so all good! Breakfast at the Sequioa was fine. It was continental, but lots to choose from, and with a 2 yr old we always managed to find something she'd eat! The rooms at the Sequioa were fine too, We had two double beds in a ground floor location (2288). The highlight of the week was the Princess Lunch. Our daughter got to spend alot of time with Belle, Cinderella, Sleeping Beauty and Ariel. I would recommend you get a table near the fireplace, as Ariel and the Prince do a little dance, with Cinders mice. Our daughter was truly made up. We went at 230pm, by 4 ish the place was under half empty and sleeping beauty sat with our daughter for well over 10 minutes chatting from everything about her fairies, to dresses   it was magical. The meal itself was great, with free wine. We also got 6 pictures with cinderella taken within the price. With the half board plus vocuhers the bill was 60 euros, but we had such a good time we gave a decent tip. In the parks we queued for about 45 mins for a quick pic with Princess Tiara (we did this before the meal), so the value of having the princesses mulling around with no queuing etc was fab. The Sequioa lodge, I thought was similar style to a UK Center Parks (Penrith?). We called in a few of the other hotels, all have the same priced   variety of drinks   cocktails. The standards all looked about the same really. I think you pay more for how close you are to the park. We were about 10 15 min walk with a little legged person, so this was fine. We took our own pram which I was glad of as we would have had to walk to the parks then queue to get a pram hire. They also didnt have sun umberellas or rain covers which would have been an issue for the week we were there. It was also 6 euro 50 to hire for a day. Quite a few of the rides were closed which was a shame, however with a 2yr old there was plenty to do so it took off the stress of rushing around (many of the Buzz Lightyear ones, and dumbo). I would definetely have the Reservations Number in your phone for pre booking meals, also dont leave this to last minute, you need to book 1 2 days in advance if you want a particular time slot. We always ate breakfast early ish, between 730   830, never had an issue getting a table. I think we waited 5 minutes one morning, the other times we went straight in. We came home on the sat (29th May)   Bank Hol Weekend. There was a big difference in the amount of tourists in the parks. I would reccomend going out of season. We did notice the queuing time for Crushers Coaster was 75 minutes at 11am. The fast passes are great idea, so worth looking into these. We had a fab time, and wish I could go back   but will have to save some pennies first!

My girlfreind and i visited Disneyland in May and we were very disapointed.It took about an hour to get our entry tickets and like other reveiwers have pointed out the park is disorganized in some areas.Large crowds of children and there parents around the characters, jostling to take photo's.My girlfreind has been to florida and says member's of staff there greet the children and introduce them to the characters one at a time.They have a parade called star's and their car's  and staff were lining people along the street for about half an hour and how long did the parade last?...2 minutes 20 seconds!!Something happened to stall the  once upon a dream  parade which led to the deck of cards improvising for 5 minutes.I videoed this and you can hear the audience gradually going quite wondering what was going on.We thought it would be fun to go on the railway that travels around the park,but after an anoucement that there would be a 25 minute wait a train pulled up and only a few people got off which led to another long wait.When we finally got a seat there was nothing to see except trees and bushes untill you got to the next themed area.Be prepared for shocking prices,15 euros for a burger at one fast food joint,and as there is really only a choice between burgers,pizza and steak the cheapest option is mcdonalds.The stunt show was pretty good but at the end of the day its just another theme park,like alton towers,but with mickey's ears and you come away wishing there really was a Tinker Bell to magic the visa bill away!

I cannot stress enough that if you are going to Disneyland Paris in May do your homework! We were a family party of eight (two of whom were toddlers), staying at the Disney Hotel on the park. We were not told by Disney nor our travel agent that many attractions would be closed for renovation and that the park closed to everyone at 6pm. Whilst disappointed not to see the 9pm parade and the fireworks and not to experience rides such as the Studio Tour, Dumbo, etc. we did find that by 6pm the little ones had had enough. Be prepared for some shows to be narrated in French with no English translation shown.The one advantage of going at this time of year, before English schools holiday, is that the Park is very comfortable and little time is wasted in long tiring queues. The longest queue we experienced was Autopia at 40mins   a one off. My sister visited last August and for most rides they waited for well over an hour. We were able to see most of the attractions without delay and did not need to use our Fastpasses very often. Disney in our view, is not geared to healthy eating   fresh orange was the only drink without sugar and for vegetarians a cheese salad or pizza was the only choice. We did find a jacket potato stall in Frontierland but the cheese was indescribable! The park is spotlessly clean with litter patrols operating non stop. The toilets were not always as clean so take plenty of anti bacterial gel. Food and drink are expensive and not particularly good quality but one expects that on a captive site such as this. For a bottle of water expect to pay about   2.30 For a lunchtime snack 'deal'   pizza,salad,drink expect to pay   11 each.The staff on the park are friendly and very helpful. The medical centre cannot be praised highly enough. All in all a fantastic experience for the little ones with the parades and the Disney characters wandering around the park. For older thrill seekers some great rides very similar to Alton Towers but at twice the expense . If travelling by Eurostar with pushchairs expect one very slow lift and a long wait to get out of the station at Disney as the only other method of reaching ground level is by escalators which one cannot do with pushchairs and baggage. Compared to the child friendly walkway escalators at St Pancras the Eurostar station at Disney leaves a lot to be desired.

I recently went to Disney World in Florida for the third time (for my Birthday), and had the most amazing time. I couldn't have imagined a better trip when I left home. This summer (2010), I went to Paris, and didn't PLAN on going to Disneyland Paris, but had a free day, and thought it would be fun. WRONG!It was atrocious! First off, the park has much fewer attractions than in WDW or Disneyland, CA. But that wasn't the bad part. The bad part was atmosphere. It was DIRTY, and most of the fixtures and buildings were in disrepair!For anyone who has been in a US Disney Park, you know that Disney is spotless and amazing. Customer service is their number one goal, and they do an excellent job at it. Well, not here! The park is is total disgrace to the Disney name! And the cast members were unfriendly, and did not go out of their way to make your day magical in the way they do at home.The icing on the cake is that even though smoking is  not permitted  in the park (except for in designated smoking areas, the same as in WDW), people walk around smoking everywhere. In fact, it's hard to find a place to stand where you do NOT smell smoke. It's vile. I asked a cast member why they don't enforce this rule (as they do in WDW), and was told,  If you ask someone to stop smoking, they may punch you.  Nice. So I guess I have to suffer because the staff is afraid of being accosted by cigarette addicted lunatics.

I thoroughly enjoyed Disneyland, although it is THE most expensive land in ALL of the world (that I have visitied anyway!) Make sure to get your fastpass straight away (just pop your entry ticket into the machine near the attraction) and then go wait in the line (if it's 20 mins or less waiting time) as you'll be able to go on immediately after your first ride through the fast pass lane   we only worked this out on day two. If you stay at one of the Disney Hotels you get an extra two hours in the park but only on certain rides, certainly saves time though if you do these ones first and then go get your fastpass then wait in line then get your second ride straight away.Definitely glad we visited :)

We've been to the resort many times and planning to go there next month.Disneyland Paris is something special if you take your time to enjoy the excellent theming of the park,take time to rest and avoid Fantasyland at 'nap time'.Most castmembers are extremely helpfull and friendly. On crowded days however you'll find some are quite rude and not aware they work in one of the happiest places on earth and should play their role to make your visit unforgetable. Same goes for the visitors, some get so stessed and unpleasent because they only want to get on as many rides as possible and everyone else is in their way. On those kind of days it's better not to visit the popular rides but instead visit Adventure Isle, the Secrets of the Nautilus or enjoy the beauty of the arcades behind Mainstreet.The FastPass system can be very helpfull to plan your visit but we never actually plan a whole day, except for the parades and Enchanted fireworks, nothing beats the magic of seeing Sleeping Beauty's castle surrounded by Fireworks. It's DisneyMagic at it's best. (After the Fireworks the park closes but it's still possible to do some shopping in Mainstreet) Keep in mind that it's not possible to see all of the park or ride every ride in just one day. Get to the parkgates half an hour before opening, the French or not that strict and sometimes the gates open earlier, this gives you the chance to get on Big Thunder Mountain, Space Mountain or any other popular ride without having to stand in line too long. Make dinner reservations at City Hall so you can enjoy a good meal at one of the (child ) friendly restaurant instead of eating at an overcrowded fast foodrestaurant. The ' Once Upon a Dream' parade and 'Fantillusion'parade are somthing not to be missed, take your positions in time for a good view. One of the best places to see these parades is from the balcony of the railwaystation(bit crowded but great view) or just before the 'Bella Notte' restaurant. At Christmas time Mainstreet is the best location as it is snowing even on a cloudless day.

Ive been to Disney paris 3 times in last 2 years (and im 30 years old!) and i cant wait to go back.I have always travelled with eurostar and found the service to be outstanding, although i did prefer it when the terminal was at waterloo, as last time i went i had to drag all my luggage through monday morning rush hour on the tube not a pleasant experiance! I've stayed at the Cheyenne, the Newport bay and the Sequoia lodge. To be honest they are all similar really, but breakfast at the newport and sequoia is a much more civillised affair and you get the bonus of a swimming pool. Last time i stayed i was meant to be at the Cheyenne, but arrived back at my room after a day in the park, to find the firebrigade outside as there had been a water leak! The management were very helpful and got us a transfer to the Newport Bay that night, helped us pack up our things and then drove us to the Newport, where we then stayed for the remainder of our holiday (3 nights.) We also received 3 free one day park passes as a goodwill gesture, as it was nearly 3am before we finally got settled into our new room   dont think you can complain about this at all. I have visited in early June (perfect weather, parks quite quiet, but no fireworks etc) late september ( parks very quiet, all rides virtually walk on, but some things shut for refurb and short opening hours and mid July ( parks open 8am to 10pm, fireworks and nightime parades, but very very busy) and you do get a different experiance depending upon the time you visit.My personal favourite rides attractions are   big thunder mountain quite a tame ride, but fantastic with itthe stunt show in the studiosBuzz lightyears lasar questHaunted MansionRock and rollercoasterAnd im not so keen on   Crushes coaster   left me feeling quite sick, due to all the spinningSpace Mountain   far to jolty and again made me feel bit illHoney I shrunk the audiance   just boring, tho the odd special effect worth seeing Fast passes are a great idea and can save you lots of time, i wouldve had to queue for nearly 2 hours for some rides, but got on within 10mins with a fast pass. Disney food is pretty bad, although as a group of all adults what we done last time we went (last July) was to eat plenty at breakfast, then around lunch leave the parks (as at this time it gets crazy busy during peak times) grab a few snacks from the shop by the train station, eat them on the way back to the hotel and then go for a swim for a bit to relax before heading back to the parks. This is a definate advantage of going during the long summer opening hours. Then for dinner we either ate at the Plaza or in Disney Village   planet hollywood being my favourite. Everything is also expensive and i can imagine this is MUCH worse if you have children with you.The buses to and from the hotels are a nightmare (especially at busy times), and i always choose to walk rather than to feel like a sardine in a tin. The summer firework display and nightime lit up parade, was amazing and worth the extra summer crowds to see. But you have to be prepared to guard for space for some time before the parade starts if you want to get a good view, and as several other posters have mentioned you will get a lot of rude people trying to push in and actually push you out of the way. Overall i love the place and will be going back as soon as i can afford to. Its like being  allowed  to be a child for a few days as where else can adults wear mouse ears and not feel stupid!?

had a lovely day at disney, arrived at 10am the opening time and followed a disney train into the park as it opened, the train had all fave charecters on it and was so much fun. parades are spectacular the highlight of my day was the once upon a dream parade it was out of this world, the new genaration festival was brilliant set on a stage in front of sleeping beautys castle so makes for lovely photos as well as a magical day, something for everyone. All area themes are brilliant really enjoyed my day, princess castle had to be my highlight, also the opotunity to meet charecters was fab. Had the best hotdog of my life it did however cost 10euros for hot dogs and fries but they were so nice it was worth it, we ate on main street usa and as the first showing of the new generation festival was on it was a wonderful way to eat.

We just returned from Disneyland hotel in paris and the only thing i would complain about was the price of the food not so much for adults but for children the average price we saw was starting at    13.00 per head, now i have a 3 and 6 year old and that price for basic chichen nuggets and drink and dessert is too much, thats if they eat a dessert but the point is you dont have a choice take it or leave it.Now the positive the parks and hotel where brilliant the disney hotel have the characters in the lobby every morning and afternoon.The afternoon is a little show that the kids loved.The hotel gives you two hours head start of the queues in the morning and yes some rides are not open but some are so you go on them and start queueing for the other ones you like. The shows in the park are brilliant and even as a adult you cant help was admire the way the characters interact with all the children.I would go back and I would be a bit better prepared with food I would pack carrot sticks ,bread, snacks and drinks that sort of thing because like I said the food is far to expensive when you have kids with you.I would not use a travel agent next time but do it myself and the bus to the disneyland I would not use and didnt on my last trip I organise a car to pick us up and bring us back to the airport and it was about ten euro dearer than the bus ,saved us about 45 mins in waiting time.all in all ours time there was great just sort out the food issues and the place would be excellent.

We stayed at the Marriott village resort, and the place was perfect, 3 bedroom house and had all the amenities you would ask for when travelling with small children.Disneyland parks themselves were fab. My first time ever there and I would definately go back again. We went the end of March and the crowds were not bad, avg waiting time for the rides was half an hour, Dumbo the elephant was an hour. I found the gifts in the shops near the exits were pretty reasonable especially for disney. 8   10 euros for a t shirt, 7 euros for a mug, etc.The restaurants were expensive, went to Cafe Mickey the first night and for 2 adults and 2 children with just a main meal each and 2 beers was 90 euros. But you were paying for the children to see the Disney characters, and boy was it worth it to see the smiles on my kids faces. So I would definately go back again, and am now planning a trip to Disneyland Florida in the next 2 years.

With our young family we went to Disneyland Paris in July 2008 and thoroughly enjoyed it. So we decided to return 10 12 May 2010. Not as good. This time too crowded and you feel ripped off when they close whole sections without informing in advance or give discounts in return. Closed were in Disneyland the Fantasy Land   s northeast corner and train station and in Walt Disney Studios the Studio Land Tram Tour and the supposedly new attractions in the northeast corner. Also the Crush   s Coaster attraction seemed to have serious technical flaws on 12 May 2010 and was stopped several times.As a consequence the crowds were much larger for the big attractions that were open, with waiting up to an hour the standard. The annoying fast pass system should be abandoned, because it does not seem fair that you have to wait in line so long and then you see people entering in 5 minutes through the fast pass route, even when you can make use of this scheme yourself (one ticket at a time).Crush   s Coaster: although the Nemo movie theme and minimum height of 1.07m give you the impression that this attraction is suitable for small children, the reality is that even for adults this is quite a rough ride. My boy of 7 came out crying and I was very nauseous. Twilight Zone Tower of Terror: this is not for the faint of heart and stomach. The very rapid elevator movements and stops made my stomach ache for hours afterwards and my children of 5 and 7 crying, although a minimum height of 1.02m seem to indicate suitable for children.Food at the two parks: although you pay over the top prices, your only option is a very limited choice of standard fast food items. At least one healthier simple buffet style restaurant at each park should not be too much to ask. Until then I recommend a backpack with food and drinks.Disney hotels: A big plus is their location next to the parks and the 08:00 10:00 exclusive Disneyland only park opening for hotel guests. Especially when rates are discounted a recommendation. If full rates, though, an expensive option. Hotels are huge and crowded with for breakfast, dinner, and transport long lines. A suggestion is to seriously increase the eating & transport capacity. The bus frequency between the official Disney hotels and the park entrances is too low, resulting in pushing and shoving of crowds once the bus arrives. The alternative    train    ride from the back of the hotels charges you expensively in a classic tourist scam, something that should be hotel courtesy.We decided that visiting Disneyland Paris twice is enough and we will not go backa third time.TIP: If you go to Disneyland Paris, combine this with city trips to Paris and or London using the next door train station. For Paris buy a day pass for a 30 min train ride to Paris centre and then the metro to any of the sights and events you like. A 6 8 hour period will already make this Paris city trip worthwhile. For 2 or more days go to London with the Eurostar TGV train. From Disneyland Paris it only takes you 2.5 hours to arrive in the centre of London, King   s Cross   St. Pancras station. For logistic convenience I recommend Premier Inn Hotel King   s Cross St. Pancras, a 5 min walk.

First visit to DLP, helped by a friend who had made several trips and a fantastic guidebook   Brit Guide to DLP 2010 11. In my opinion if you turned up with young children (ours are 8 and 6) and you had not thought it through, you would have a good day but miss out on heaps. We went for 3 nights 4 days and as it turned out spent 2 days in each park. The best advice is to buy the half board premium meal plan which allows you to eat anywhere (but book in advance !) and more importantly take part in the character meals which absolutely made the experience for our children. We ate at Cafe Mickey on Day 1 which was BRILLIANT   lots of one to one interaction for photos and autographs which you will not get in the parks themselves as the characters are simply too busy and popular. We saw Mickey, Minnie, Pluto, Captain Hook, both chipmunks, Pinnochio, Goofy and Tigger. Day 2 we ate at Auberge de Cendrillon where all the Princesses are, and saw Cinderella, Aurora, Prince Phillip, Ariel and Belle, and Cinderella's 2 mice. Not to be forgotten, the food at both these places was AMAZING, top quality and the children both received a gift and at Cendrillon a free photo with Cinderella. Day 3 we went to the Buffalo Bill Wild West Show which was excellent too, a great experience for the kids and whilst more basic food, very plentiful. The meal plan worked out about   110 per day, and the meals above were for us all 120   230 euros per experience !! 4th Day we ate lunch at Restaurants des Stars which was good buffet food, but slightly disappointing in that we only saw Ratatouille but perhaps we had been spoilt up to then ! Glad we didn't use our meal vouchers for that.Use the Fast Pass system, lots of people seemed not to bother and then queue for up to 75 minutes for the most popular rides !?! Fast Pass is free ! Try and do the popular ones first or at the end of the day, or while the parades are on. Those who stay at Disney Hotels can get into the parks 2 hours before the general public   not all the rides are open but it does make a difference.See one parade in each park to take some good photos, and then enjoy the lull around the rest of the park during those days when it's on and you can find other things to do !It is expensive but take some carton drinks in your bag and a few snacks to eat discreetly (DLP officially don't allow picnics or food to be brought in to eat). My best tip is to go with the flow, try put the euros out of your mind and enjoy the experience ! We had a great time, our favourite family holiday so far, the kids can't stop talking about it and we all can't wait to book again to go back once we have saved up !

A spectacular day. Crystal blue skies. I've visited WDW more then 25 times so I consider myself a Disney expert. You have two parks to visit here. The main park is Disneyland itself and the second is The Disney Studios. Both are smaller then WDW, but Disneyland may be larger then its counterpart in CA. Rides are completely different then any Disney park I've been to. There's even a dragon under the castle. I had a fun filled day and the CMs there as well as the characters made me feel right at home.

Still a Disney fan   but upset by misleading meal packages at Disneyland Paris (DLP). I am in a long term dispute with DLP over their Disney Meal Packages. What they state on their web sites is not what the meal vouchers say.Last year we booked an  All Your Meals for Free  package (now replaced by  Half Board  packages). From the DLP web site it appeared that this offered a great deal for lunch and dinner at table service restaurant and saved us concerns about the poor   :    exchange rate.When we got the vouchers at Ashford Station (we travelled via Eurostar) we found that only one meal per day was table service or buffet and the other was only counter service (i.e. burger, chips,cola and a yogurt).As such the package deal was not a saving and in fact I think it cost about 40% than paying for the meals directly. It is good for Disney as it guarantees the revenue stream.DLP are saying that the meal restrictions were clearly shown on their web site but they have been deleted now. They are now refusing to discuss the matter further so I am escalating to their CEO.To save any problems, I suggest you print out all the booking details in advance and save any web pages on your PC just in case.

We stayed at Disneyland Paris on 31st January 2010 it was very disappointing.We arrived at our bedroom block (Sequoia Lodge) and thought we must be at the staff entrance as there were trolleys of dirty laundry strewn untidily all around the entrance.The door lock on bedroom took about 12 tries to open it. We only kept trying as it was such a long walk back to reception. I am quite used to electronic door keys, and the do require a bit of a    knack    sometimes to open them, but this one was faulty.We heard a member of staff in the corridor and told her the key wasn't working properly. She rudely asked how we had gotten into the room, then, shrugged her shoulders and walked away. I simply couldn   t believe it.The room was dirty     there was rubbish in the ice bucket and the bathroom floor was dirty.The window catch on one window was broken and a metal arm was hanging loose.Reception did not answer the phone when we tried to ring down.There were tiny towels in bathroom and not enough for 4 people as an adult would need two. It was like staying in a really cheap 'motel'.The shows were adequate, but certainly not spectacular. The    Winter Wonderland    party in Frontierland seemed to be more about cutting costs during the off season by having very few cast involved than providing a good show. And the cast could not skate well!     it looked like something put on by an amateur group.We had a nice dinner with the characters in Disney Village and enjoyed the rides, but In general, while the parks themselves have good rides, the staff do not smile nor seem that they are interested in children. There were a couple of good staff and I hate complaining, but really this was not a    magical    experience. We did our absolute best to enjoy the holiday, but we   ve had far, far better.Overall, Disneyland Paris was an expensive holiday, a poor experience andwe will not be returning.

Visited a few times over the last fews years and at different times of the year. Recommend both Christmas and Halloween, great decorations, extra parades and shows which give something a bit different. It snowed when we where there last time and that was really special, our son found this really magic!. Have visited both California and Florida and although the weather is a bit more hit and miss the Paris park is the best themed out of them all. There are still great attractions, they have the best Space Mountain ride! and it is as good as either of the Magic Kingdoms in america. My only gripe is that the character meet and greets are not as well organised as in the states and it can be a battle to get your pictures and autographs. Like others have mentioned some of the other visiting nations just push and shove their way through but that's not the parks fault, you just need to be aware of it and watch your kids. Food can be expensive, if you are staying on site book the half board deal it saved us a packet. If you want a quick exit on the night use the undercover passages walkways either side of Main Street they are not as crowded. Give your kids time to explore the Adventure Isle its like one big adventure playground, ours loves it. Parade route is never usually busy near Small World we have always managed to get a good view there and its nots as busy as main street. Staff have always been excellent, when our son fell over last time they arranged a taxi for us to go to hospital with one of their staff and bring us back   we never paid for anything and didn't have to claim on our travel insurance for his check up and treatment. Disneyland Paris is a great place to visit, it's well worth it!

We had a 5 day stay at the Sequoia Lodge ( see hotel review) travelling as an extended family of 4 adults and 7 and 3 year old children . Having been to the park in 1995 on a wet July day I was not really looking forward to it but it was great. Disney characters welcomed us at the hotel making the childrens day, the parks are great for all ages and the queues were not too bad if you used fast pass. (with 6 of us and some too small for the rides we could get passes for more than one ride at a time) The only ride with a bad queue was the crush coaster, and for some reason there is no FP for that!The biggest down side is the food, in the park and the village, poor quality and expensive we ate at Cafe Mickey for lunch, Annettes Diner and Planet Hollywood for Dinner in all of them the meals were over 20 euros each and were like supermarket ready meals, on top of that a pint of beer was 7 euros. Ice creams over 3 euros. The best meal we had there was at the Cowboy B B Q Cookout, nice food not too expensive.We bought the Disney Land Paris Brit Guide, full of great tips and a 20% off voucher for Planet Hollywood. We did a character breakfast and lunch at Cafe Mickey, breakfast was best but at both the children loved having Mickey and friends join them.Got home happy, tired and broke!

Just got back from a 3 night break with the family having taken our granddaughter for her fourth birthday. Lovely weather but that's about the only positive thing to report. We have been to Orlando several times and the original Disneyland in California but this one is a very poor offering in comparison. As other people have reported the parks are small and very crowded even at this time of year with waits of up to 100 minutes for some rides. Even the smaller rides were crazy. Having queued for an hour with a four year old for a three minute ride on the Dumbo roundabout you have to question the Disney 'magic'.However all this pales into insignificance when you consider (as many other reviewers have mentioned) the people. I have never been in such a rude, offensive ignorant crowd of people in my life   nor will again, given the choice. I won't stereotype and I am sure that there are some delightfully cultured, polite French people, but they certainly weren't in Disneyland Paris. We were shoved, jostled, barged out of the way as the locals pushed their way through. Not a word of apology   at best a hostile glare for having the temerity to be in their way. And not just the younger people. The charming disregard for any manners at all was embraced by all generations equally. The only apologies I heard in the parks were either in English or German  is there actually a word for 'sorry' or 'excuse me' in French? One has to wonder.And its not just the ignorant visitors that let the place down; the staff are a sorry bunch too. OK I accept that most of them are on minimum wages and probably have to work long hours but do they have to appear so miserable? Yes they were polite and many of them had considerable language skills but. with a few exceptions, there was no excitement or enthusiasm. They may just as well have been working in a supermarket. Those of you who have been to the American parks will know what I mean. There the 'cast' members really make an effort to embody and radiate the fun and excitement of the place and all of the ride crews interract with the visitors with a ready smile or some silly remarks or acting and it makes the whole experience something special. Here they don't bother   you're just a body to be moved onto or off of a ride like so many cattle. Great!We stayed at the Sequoia Lodge which was OK. The rooms were American in style with two big beds and a decent bathroom and it was clean. Unfortunately the attention to detail was poor with light bulbs missing, air conditioning which didn't work and, in our room, a bottle of pop left by the previous occupants behind the curtains and missed by the cleaners which started to fizz at 3 in the morning. Not so good.We ate in the hotel buffet the first night which was great   if you like bland luke warm overpriced food and surly staff. The total bill was in excess of 150 Euros for 4 adults and a child which I felt was outrageous as could have eaten twice as well for half the price in any restaurant chain in the UK.So good points....not many. Bad points.....Hmmm. Would I recommend it? Wholeheartedly   to anybody I really didn't like!
