I spent 4 days 3 nights here. It was awful, complete rip off. Don't go if you can help it.All shops are the same, lovely beautiful buildings and houses but nothingness in side. If you like the same merchandise being thrown at you in every building that resembles a house, then fair enough. Why couldnt they have Mickey and Donald having tea or doing a stooges act of some kind? Just shops shops shops. Overpriced crystal Mickeys etc too much branding, not enough fun.Freezing weather in February (biting cold), which is natural, but yet only food on the stands were coke and popcorn...where's the hot food? Tea, coffee? Jacket potatoes? I was in awe of their lack of common sense, the person running it is lacking something in their head. Plenty of clothes shops open. Plenty of Mickeys charging money for photos. The magic disappears as quick as your euros do.Every restaurant is like walking into McDonalds... awful. Food tastes horrible and there is little choice but burgers and hotdogs. The rides are seriously out of date, I'm 31, but my last visit was when I was 14yrs old, it was exactly the same. There is an extra park, but it reminded me of an industrial estate. The space simulator ride broke down halfway (after 45 minutes waiting in the cold), we got a brief apology by confused staff and led out the back door. Probably just as well because it had been boring as hell up to that moment.Most of the staff looked bored out of their head and it was like being in a gypsy fairground. The restaurants are quite obviously not large enough to cope with the number of tickets they sell, as you have to reserve. Staff sit everywhere with their hand gestures telling you not to do this, not to do that, don't sit here, get off the road, stop here, really started getting on my nerves after 2 days.Repetitive parades with annoying music (after 4 days you'll feel like throwing your coke at Mickey Mouse). The rides will have you waiting for an hour, but will last 3 minutes. We had a couple of good moments, the Rock n Roller coaster was good, the Little Mermaid show my 2 yr old loved, and the Cars ride. Thats all I can muster with positivity about the place. I was left looking at the hole in my bank account and feeling conned.

Eurostar is the most convenient from London to Marne la valee, where Disneyland park is located. The station is practically at the entrance to the park. We stayed at the Dream castle hotel which runs frequent shuttles to the park every 10 minutes. The hotel staff were very friendly and the bunk beds for my 2 kids were a smashing hit. We bought a 2 day pass and spent the first day at Disneypark and the second day at Walt disney studio. Highlights of the disney park were the disney characters parade,  Its a small world  cruise, sleeping beauty stage play although every attraction mesmerised our kids. At Walt disney studio which me and my wife liked more, the motor stunt, cinemagique and Aerosmith rollercoaster rides were our unforgettable memories. We thoroughly enjoyed it and it is a truly amazing unforgettable experience. We spent a morning on the day we were leaving at Val d'Europe and designer outlet shops which reminded me of Bicester near Oxford. Did a lot of window shopping there. Can't really think of anything to complain other the the fact that we were delayed due to a train strike on our way back but the friendly railway ticket staff at the Marne la Valee upgraded us to first class in Eurostar and it was a fitting finale to our holiday. Sad to leave this magical place.

We had been planning our 4day 3night trip to Disneyland Paris for months. We arrived by eurostar practically skipping into the disneyland park. I would really recommend the Disney Express service as they took care of the baggage for us until we were ready to collect it from our hotel. We stayed at the Santa Fe and had heard all of the horror stories but it was fantastic. Although it was a very tired concept, the room was clean and very close to the walking trail that leads to the Disney village. My only gripe about my stay was that we arrived for breakfast and the queue was practically out to the car park (via reception!!) so we quickly decided to avoid breakfast altogether and ended up paying for hot drinks on the way into the parks. This enabled us to take advantage of the extra 2hrs in the parks for the busiest areas of Fantasyland and Discoveryland. We booked Cafe Mickey for breakfast on our last day and this was fantastic, i have never seen bigger smiles on my son's face. I was truly sad to see our stay come to an end, but will definitely return again although will try another hotel purely because i would like to stay in them all eventually!

Just came back from a 5 day visit with my wife and 2 kids, during Easter. I already had been on the parks and I really like it's magic and attention to detail of all the attractions and the magic it includes.However, I really have to say   AVOID HIGH SEASONS. The queues for everything takes you to desperation! 75 minutes average time waiting (furthermore with little kids) for most attractions makes it impossible to enjoy! There's the FAST PASS option, but for major events they ran out too soon and you can only take one per each amount of time (I think before 3 hours you can not pick another one). So, I would really recommend Disney parks, but OFF SEASON! This way you'll spend more money, have opportunity to ride less attractions and won'st have the calm and peace of mind to enjoy it! Because the parks are really great, when you can enjoy them...

Not sure where people are going to find the rude staff they refer to in these reviews but I've just returned from yet another trip and loved it yet again! Went this time with my mother, brother, daugther (12), nephew (7) and neice (4). It was the two younger ones first time and they were mesmorised by it all. Coming from a rip off republic we didn't find the prices expensive but I would imagine once the English had finished complaining about everything else that they found the prices out of this world considering how cheap it is in the UK and with the exchange rate going against them. Average cost to east was    10 for an adult and    6 for a child (lunch or dinner). Food isn't the best but it's not the food you go for.Queues were suprisingly short for such a busy weekend (Easter) average 20   30 mins. We love it over there so much and the bottom line is if you're not up to a bit of hussle and bussle, higher than normal prices, over the top merchandise stores, screaming kids and moaning adults then it's not the place for you. Me   I just turn to tunnel vision and enjoy the buzz!!!

Just got back from Disneyland paris where we had the best time ever, I have never laughed so much in my life!!! I group of us went 6adults and 5 children ages ranging from 2 to 11. I don't even know where to begin,I was worried after reading some bad reviews but I shouldn't of been.The staff were fantastic making every effort to make the childrens dreams come true, my 9 year old didnt know where to look first.All the rides were in working order and we had a blast i don;t think we qued for longer then half an hour,but if thats to long for you, you can get fast track tickets, which gives you a time to go back and get at the front of the que.There are plenty of places to eat but its pretty much the same food, however again not a problem for the kids. You have to go on the hollywood tower ride its fantastic, and the staff really play the part.I cannot find a bad thing to say about this place, and i can't wait to go back next year, erm i mean my son can't wait to go back next year!!I would like to thank Tigger who went out of his way to make this little girls dream come true ( I am 30 but so what)

Loads of fun and amazing landscape, better to go there when is crowded cause you'll have everithing goind wild but than you'll have to wait about 30 45 minutes for many attractions like the space mountain or indiana jones rolercoaster.Animation is guaranteed but the food is realy poor and expensive besides being only crap food like fries and stuff like that. it seems that we are in USA and not in Europe.favourite attraction: Space Mountain

Rip off!! Rude people. What a PLAVA. Save a bit more and visit real one in USA. I ve never seen that many rude, ignorant and selfish people all together. Specially a few days in Paris, NEVER AGAIN. That was our worse holiday ever. I havent got any single nice things to say about Paris, Disney and People. If you still go ahead and visit Disney, make sure they tell you which attractions are not working before you book your trip. When we got there we find out that a few of their main attractions are not working,and rest of them are not very good anyway. STAY AWAY!!!!!!!!!

Took my 2 year old to Disneyland Paris this week   Tuesday til Friday. Flew with Easyjet from Liverpool   no problems at all. Flight just over an hour. DD had own seat as she's two, although more expensive much better! Had read a lot of reviews previous to going, some not very promising, so my expectations were lowered! I expected queues, expense and a poor hotel. We had booked a taxi shuttle with Opipare Travel   90 euros return for the 3 of us. A little more expensive than VEA   the recommended Disney one but we wanted direct. Took about 45 minutes.We were staying at the Newport Bay hotel and I had heard bad reviews and good. We arrived at around 11 am and Mickey Mouse was in the foyer for a phot opportunity! We joined the queue as my husband went to check in. The lobby was not too busy   and within 10 15 mins we had our photo and joined my husband at check in. Our room would be available at 2pm, not 4pm like some reviews had said   but it didn't seem too busy. We left our cases in the luggage area and made our way to the park.The park was faultless   our first day wasn't that busy to be fair and the rain at tea time got rid a lot   but not us! We had photos with ALL the characters, the queues werent too bad for the little rides althought it's a good idea to get to the park before the public at 10am and go back at about 7pm before the park shut at 8pm. On the first night there was a closing show where all the new charachter were putting on a show with Mickey and friends   this was not advertised and we got a good spot, we were on our way out!Aslo booked to go to the Auberge de Cendrillon   to have luch with the Princesses   our daughter loved it. Was very expensive, 60 euros each and 25 for her but we did get a three course fine dining experience with wine, canapes a gorgeous desert and a souvenir picture (with 9 photos, 1 big one) of our DD with Cinderella who greeted her on the way in. Ariel, Belle, Aurora and Prince Phillipe were there with Suzy and Perla the mice,and spent a lot of time talking and posing with our little girl! Well worth it but I was diappointed that Snow White wasn't there, as she is my DDs fave. Anyway   hotel was ok   a bit shabby, but very close to walk to park. Breakfast was excellent   we didnt have meal vouchers, just breakfast. It is only 3 star and I prefer 5   but you get used to it! You're not there long! TV was rubbish, couldnt access mini bar and travel cot was not the best. Bed was very comfy and bathroom was big. Mickey mouse toiletries weren't replaced daily though.Staff were hit and miss   some friendly, some miserable! Shop in hotel was great but stuff is expensive   60 euros for a Cinderella dress, 2,50 for bottle of coke, 7.50 for Mickey balloon, 10 for mickey mouse ears. But that's what you're there for. Unless you're going to stay in the Disney Hotel I don't think there's much difference, I've stayed in Santa Fe too   no difference, except in restaurants. Lift was not as much a problem as people made out either   there were 4 on each wing. Best advice   take rain clothes and a load of money and comfy shoes! Planet Hollywood and Rainforest Cafe   meal for 3 about 80 euros inc dessert and drinks   we really enjoyed it. But if you have a little girl go to the Auberge! Get to parades EARLY if you want a good spot and don't forget the studios   great for seeing minnie mouse too! Enjoy   its brilliant and I would go again but 2 days might be enough......?

went to disney parks on 25th march 2010, was so disappointed with both parks, be prepared to wait 75 mins for a ride as we had to on sunday. I expected the rides to be like the ones in Florida well they are not, there is no billed up to the ride like you get in florida, people push pass you with backpacks on, i came home bruised they are so rude. Some of the rides were closed big disappointment for us and the grandchildren. The rain spoils it too, so get a poncho before you go as 4 cost us 40 euros and they rip easy.Food well you just have to queue for up to 40 mins and thats just to buy fast food then find a table if you can good luck is what i say. Abit of advice save your money and go to florida

Just returned from a three night, four day stay at Disney Paris and felt compelled to write a review to balance out some of the VERY negative stuff that has been reported on this site, stuff which really bothered me PRIOR to our stay.Firstly we were blessed with a full three days of splendid March weather, sunny all day and warm, too warm for coats at times! Without doubt the weather helps create the Magic, on our fourth day we experienced heavy rain, lightning and rainbows, and to be fair I can imagine that four full days of that would have considerably reduced our smiles. So yes, I think to some extent as we all know the experience is weather dependant and March will always be unreliable, a risk, but a far more affordable risk!! We were blessed.The other MAJOR concern with this stay and based upon reviews is EXPENSE. But I was pleasantly surprised to be fair. The pound is poor, but thats not the fault of Disney Paris, the prices there are typical, even more inflated Theme park Prices. Food and Drink in particular are pricey, soft drinks hot drinks 2.50Euros, hotdogs 6.00Euros, muffins, brownies, popcorn candy floss etc etc all at least 2.50Euros. Merchandise and souvenirs are literally everywhere and prices here are also inflated, soft toys (medium size) 20 Euros, mugs 9.00Euros, fancy dress outfits 35 Euros. But to be fair the kids adore all this stuff and we spent many a minute milling through the same merchandise which is replicated a thousand times over in every store. And there are many many stores! So its pricey, but there is a mas of choice and the stores are an experience in themselves. They also provide welcome relief from the rain. We saved up and gave our daughter her own spending money for merchandise and snacks. To put it in perspective she took 130Euros and spent 95Euros and managed to buy realistically all the things she set her heart on.Mealtimes are probably the worst of the expense. We purchased pre paid Half Board Vouchers beforehand ( recommended to me) and I cannot emphasize how handy these are and the value for money they represent and the peace of mind they afford, knowing that you have paid up front and budgeted in advance. In effect they purchase your lunch or evening meal daily, they can be used at limited outlets, but always include your own hotel (Disney Hotels), and quite simply take all the stress out of finding somewhere to eat, because they limit your choice, meaning you only need to focus on a few choices instead of way too many!! To be fair we found that at the end of each evening we happily returned to our hotel to eat, it was by then nice to leave the Park, the rides, the shops, the queues behind, and believe me the need to sit down is strong! To put mealtimes in perspective, our Hotel Cheyenne (a cheaper Hotel) evening meal was rung up on the till nightly at 50Euros each for an EAT ALL YOU CAN BUFFET. That would be the cost without the prepaid Half Board Vouchers. And to eat ANYWHERE would be at least 50Euros per head, and considerably more in the likes of the more popular Rainforset Cafes and Planet Hollywoods. Add to this a pint of beer at 6.00Euros and a small glass of wine at 5.00Euros and soft drinks at 2.50Euros and you can quickly see how expensive mealtimes can become. My advice is purchase Half Board Vouchers for peace of mind in advance, eat at your Hotel in the evening to relax away from the Magic ( providing its decent) and purchase snacks in the parks during the day if required, but to be fair if you fill up with Hotel Breakfast instead, this won't cost too much.For lunchtime Snacks, Caseys Famous Hot dog stall shop, corner of Main Street is multi functional, providing reasonable hotdogs, provides a welcome place to sit and soak up the sun and the Magic, and importantly is ideally situated (from the slightly raised perimeter wall) to view the Main Street Parades and the Disney Showtime Spectacular at the Sleeping Beauty Castle in the distance. You can get closer but you really don't need to. If you go here order childrens meals even for ADULTS, you get a hotdog and an ice cream and a drink for 4.95Euros, as opposed to a single unaccompanied hotdog for 6Euros!! KEEP YOUR EYE ON THE CHILDRENS DEALS, they are often far better value for money. Macdonalds too in Disney Village, (love it or hate it) cost 15Euros for two medium burger meals and a happy meal, and is about as cheap as you will get for lunch dinner anywhere.We took 300Euros for the 4 days for snacks and merchandise etc (thats aside from our daughters 130 Euros.) I am glad to say we returned with 135Euro, she with 40Euros, so it can be done, and we are neither compulsive spenders nor meanies, we just bought what we wanted needed and we managed pretty well.The Parks are a joy, a delight for adults and children alike, and I defy anyone not to feel the magic of being a child again. I have some snaps of my daughter during this visit and the expression on her 6 year old face is priceless, expressions which to be fair I am not sure that I have seen before, and have certainly never captured. True enchantment. The money is probably money well spent for that alone (or am I just getting TOO caught up in the Magic??) You decide.Ride queues were not too unbearable, though as leg, back and feet ache sets in later in the day, they become increasingly daunting! Most typically ride times were 20 mins, the longest annoyingly but understandably are the small child rides, Dumbo in particular, which is slow, but compulsive for the little ones. Use your Magic Hours in Fantasyland if you have little ones and the Magic Hours apply here, most of the little rides are here, though only a selection were open each day for Magic Hours (8am 10am). You need to get on these before the public enter at 10am if you can. In Fantasyland  Its a Small world  is a joy and has short queues, and Peter Pans Flight is also worth a go.Interestingly the larger more adult rides had relatively short queues, often 10 minutes. So its a question of splitting the party up so you all get to go on as much as possible for your money, you won't fit enough in any other way. Big Thunder Mountain is a great mid level Family Ride, but was notoriously unreliable and broke down 3 times on 3 seperate days that we were in the queue. Nightmare!Disney Studio Park has some decent entertainment too (in fact we spent every afternoon here). Rock and Roller Coaster is a great ride and the queue never went above 5 mins. The Magic Carpets ride is a must for little ones (we spent more time on this than any other  and the queue was a manageable 15mins at most). Tower Of Terror is not for me but my other half raved about it. I also recommend the Moteurs Stunt show, Lilo and Stitch Interactive show and Tram Tours (this was closed during our visit but It has been recommended to me).In terms of Character Meet and Greets, we didn't experience the pushiness and arrogance described by other reviewers. In fact most adults were very considerate towards ALL children and prioritised their needs to meet the characters. Some kids were a little pushy there was a smallscale scrum for autographs, but to be fair I genuinely put that down to overexcitement rather than arrogance. Noticeably the characters have time slots, so once the time is up they leave, likewise if it starts to pour with rain, they leave. But I never saw them be rude. Firm but fair to me. I fail to see what is unreasonable about this, its all down to the luck of the draw, some characters you get to meet, some you miss, some you just miss because they need to move on. My daughter missed some one day, caught them the next, some she never got to see. Thats life, thats management of a theme park. I think to be fair too that maybe during March the scrumming is simply less because crowds are less, that said the stay was still very busy and crowded, but not unbearably so.We encountered absolutely delightful French Staff in all sections of the Park and Hotel. We found them to be helpful, charming, very child orientated, in fact they tried hard to contribute to the Magic. The Park is maintained spotlessly, you won't see litter, its maintenence is run with clockwork efficiency (except the daily parade always seemed to be ten mins late!!!) , yet the Magic is still there in the theming, the characters and the joy of the children.In summary and contrary to expectations (many based upon this site), we thoroughly enjoyed this experience from start to finish. I can only recommend those things we experienced, but I recommend them wholeheartedly. In summary and worth noting:Eurostar from Ashford International was easy and efficient (if expensive). Parking is   11.50 daily too! Premier Inn at Ashford was convienient, practical and very local, about ten mins from the Eurostar station for an overnight stay    57.00 per family room.Hotel Cheyenne was a joy, basic, a cheaper option than some but fit for its purpose, superbly themed and I wouldn't feel the need to upgrade having seen the other more expensive options. I would stay there again without a moments thought. And they have bunkbeds! Evening buffets are a little chaotic, but manageable, if you get there by 7pm at latest, and you will NEED to SIT DOWN for the day by then. Don't expect fine dining and candlelight, its cheap cheerful, mass produced, but edible and convienient, and for four days you can cope without moaning.Pre Purchase Half Board Vouchers for mealtimes. If you do nothing else I recommend, just do this.FantasyLand is a must see but EARLY see for little ones.Thoroughly recommend the Prebooked Character Breakfast at Cafe Mickey. Again expensive and food was adequate but not fab. But this was about meeting Mickey and Co, and you get to meet them close up and personal at your table, no scrums, no heads in the way on your pics, true personal time to share, the little ones loved it. ( And I did but don't tell).March was superb. A risky time to visit granted weather wise, but fewer crowds, better vantage points, less scrumming, more tolerant staff and PARENTS, better access to characters, shorter ride times......Happy Families. The best variety of charcaters were in Disney Studio Park, it was also easier to access these characters here since as a rule the park is less busy. Meet and Greets here were easier. Take some comfortable shoes. I'll leave that one with you, all will become apparent.Magical. Try it.

We were so looking forward to taking our family to Disney Paris. We have a 2 year old and a 4 year old. I am so disappointed, as was my husband. Please think twice before you make a decision to go here.Amongst everything else, if you are British now is a very bad time to be going over there, because of the    against the Euro. Once you get there, you are trapped. There is no local supermarket to stock up on soft drinks or snacks. There is nothing but Disney and it's merchandise for miles around. The whole thing is a very clever, expensive, well oiled machine. You HAVE to eat and drink there, and boy, do they nail you on prices. The food is ALL burgers, chips and pizza. Not bad for an odd day but any longer and feel like the man who made the film 'Supersize me'. Even the vile fast food is so disgusting. I was shocked as I thought the French even did fast food well. Not the case. For a simple cheeseburger, no drink or fries you are talking about   7. For 4 of you, even very little children who eat hardly anything, to eat in Rainforest Cafe, you are talking   80. Easily. My 2 year old has come home with 'French Belly'. It was dirty. You don't expect that in a Disney Resort anywhere. A nice reminder for the long trip home.  We stayed at the Hotel New York, not actually a bad hotel. But even their room service food was similar, with little choice. A tiny, burnt pizza here cost   20 to be delivered to your room. Because it is a Disney Hotel, British families, I am ashamed to say, were letting their kids run wild. They were screaming and running up and down the corridors at midnight and the same from 6.00 am. I felt like I was in Disney Hell.If you want to see the Disney Characters, which is what sets Disney about from other theme parks, you will have to get in line. And wait. It's as if they are rationed to the public, unlike the US versions (why??? Isn't this their USP?). Your kids will either have to queue up, for half an hour to meet them and have a picture taken, or you will have to fight with hundreds of French and Italian people, to get near them. It was awful. Grown adults were shoving little kids out of the way or trampling on them. I saw a British woman in tears with her baby in tears, and another British couple ending up in a row with a horrible Italian woman, who knocked their little girl for six. It was that bad. Not quite the magic I expected. My own daughter wept because she couldn't get near anyone. So disappointing.We were told to go mid week. Which honestly wasn't much better, than the Sunday when we arrived . If you like queuing for 45 mins per kiddie ride, be my guest. This is the place for you.Some of the areas needed a lick of paint. The staff around Disney, I have to say, were pretty nice. You'd expect that for 2 adults paying   70 per day. The French that are there, are in the main, so rude, queue jumping pushing and shoving their way to the front, it will make you wish you had stayed at home.We asked my 4 year old daughter what her favourite part of the trip was. She very innocently said,'swimming in the hotel pool with Daddy'. That tells you everything you need to know. I think that Disney in Florida would be a much better choice if you could afford it. But please, save yourself time and money and a lot of stress and don't bother with the Paris one. I wouldn't set foot in that place in a million years.
Great place though you need to stay there to enjoy it fully.

We had a great time midweek untill Friday my 3 year old daughter was stood with mum waiting for woody in the woodys roundup and was pushed and knocked down to the floor by french grown ups.When we asked the Disney guide with woody he said it was not his job, we even spoke to the compliants dept on site that day and they seemed to not want to know, shame we had done Disneyland Florida last year very good ropes are out to keep the grown ups back and que for the disney gang, Paris do not do this and is very disorganised as we and others found out, but i will end with the Hotel on site is very good and the staff very helpful, if only Disney sent the Paris staff to see and train with the U.S gang would this help, and Paris SMOKE in the park unlike the U.S ??.

I totally agree with Charlie1uk. We know the value of the pound is bad at the moment, but I object to have to pay at least DOUBLE just to be in Disney. What a complete RIP OFF! They have you there and they know it!POSITIVES: The kids enjoyed it   they would would'nt they! The charachters on the whole were very good. The pre booked dinners with the Characters were good especially Cafe Mickey, and the Prince Princesses at lunchtime (both pre booked as a package). Hotel OK  The Sequoia  rooms OK fairly comfortable, descent beds. Warm and air con good!NEGATIVES: Disneyland is a Massive Rip off! Everything you buy is over double the cost of in England and I thought that was bad enough!   70 to park at Ashford for 4nights 5days! Train station at Disneyland freezing and some staff are ignorant! Don't go in March as its just an icy cold concrete metal jungle! Freezing freezing cold! Have to pay for some public toilets! Fast food which we had to wait for for ages was cold, basic crap and double or more the cost of back home! Rather starve during the day than eat some of the cold nasty stuff they serve you up at the fast food outlets! We were late checking in and some staff seemed please they could  tell us off for being late ! and when you look around smiling at each other looking totally smug! Ignorant some of them! especially when your rushing with 3 kids and suitcases!! Sequoia Pool is terrible, freezing (thats the indoor pool) dangerous steps, dirty Jacuzzi with too many people and kids in   one unhygienic mess! and the staff just ignore you in general. Safety aspect terrible! The changing rooms are very small compared to the size of the place   just terrible. Looks good in the brochure : dont be fooled! Probably more negative stuff if I had the time. Hopefully my kids and grand kids won't temp me into going again just to see their smily happy faces when they meet the Characters! Hopefully someone might read this who will look into the rip off side of most things!

It is the Disney park with the highest detail of craftsmanship. It's a destination for 2 to 3 days, and then you can mix a bit of Paris in there at the same time! It does not get any better than that. People keep saying it's not the same as in the U.S. well it is not suppose to be. This Disneyland is different in every single way, but does not disappoint.

Travelled here with husband and 5 year old son. We had a blast! We were so lucky with weather, cold but blue skies and sunshine (layered clothing worked best). I am flabbergasted to read other reviews saying that park staff are snooty or otherwise. Without fault everyone we met was friendly and helpful (despite displays of arrogance and ignorance by visitors) and made our visit even better. French helps but all staff speak english and it's fine. You'll need at least two days there and comfortable shoes. Food generally falls into one of two categories   sugar or grease. Therefore plan. Agrabar cafe in adventureland looked great but was closed during our visit. Otherwise buffets (we ate in Restaurant des Stars in Walt Disney Studios) and hotel restaurants (book ahead) are a good option. Fast pass was great for the heavy hitters such as Big Thunder Mountain and Buzz, otherwise the two hours hotels guests enter for before the park opens are a godsend. We arrived on Sunday pm and got a lot done in Fantasyland (end even got to stay on certain rides for a second go) before the Park closed. It's also lovely to be there when it's lit up (the tea cups were gorgeous with japanese lanterns twinkling overhead). The weekdays were surprisingly busy with school tours etc. Didn't spend too much time in Walt Studios   it's more of an older child teenager location I think, although there are some rides for kiddies. One last thing..it's not readily advertised but it's easy peasy to get from Charles De Gaulle airport to the Parks by train. Go to terminal 2 via the circular shuttle train, buy your tickets for the TGV (or on tgv europe.com) and hop on. It takes NINE minutes!!! The buses take at least an hour and a half and it's a scrum. Stroll on the train, and be delivered to the door. You can get a bus from the park to all hotels (every 10 mins) or use Disney Express Upstairs in the train terminal building), collect your park tickets and have your luggage delivered to the Hotel. Head for the park, buy candy floss and prepare to be nine again!!

I went to Disneyland Paris this week with some friends from Uni.The park itself is very beautiful, everything it'd hoped. Sleeping beauty's palace was a fluffy pink concoction surrounded by trees cut into square shapes, adventureland would convince anyone that they were in the middle of a desert. The attention to detail in the design of the park was incredible.I very much enjoyed seeing a parade, waving to Minnie Mouse and blowing kisses to Buloo from the Jungle Book! The park is lovely and really reawakened the child in me.However, as an adrenaline junkie, I found Disneyland to be dissapointing as a theme park. The roller coasters were all in the dark, (which I find takes away any excitement) and, while all visually stunning, were pretty tame. The best ride is definitely The Twilight Zone   Hollywood Tower, in the Disney Studios. The ride is very well executed, set in a desterted, haunted hotel. The staff are all dressed up as 1920s bellboys and seem to really enjoy working on this attraction. When we got into the ride, we were sent into the  Library  to watch an introductory video. A member of staff was hiding behind the door, jumping out and scaring us with a loud  Bonjour!  When the lights went out to watch the film, he walked around the edge of the crowd, tapping people's shoulders. This really got everyone into a spooky mood and put the audience into the right frame of mind to enjoy the ride, a  sudden drop  in a pretend service lift.I read a lot of bad reviews about Disneyland before I left. I have to say, the staff were lovely, (if you approached them with a  Bonjour, pardon, I don't speak French    it's rude to launch into a sentence in English and that's why they can get snappy), and seemed very keen to help us. A useful phrase for me was  Cest mon anniversere!     It's my birthday!  which helped me to use an expired fast pass!I would say that if anyone was contemplating a trip to Disneyland, please bear in mind that it is for CHILDREN. The theme park rides are aimed at them and there aren't really any screamers. If you go to the park, enjoy the Disney aspects of it, the parades, Space Mountain, Alice's Maze etc. After all, this is what Disney does best, not roller coasters!

Yes it's expensive, yes it's cold, but YESS...it's Disney and therefore awesome! I was transformed into a 7 year old again, loved seeing the characters, loved the rides, loved the music and fun.It was very expensive, but we ate packed lunches and drank water all day.a few tips that helped us a lot:*drinking water fountains froze over because it was so cold   the ones in main street still worked*If you print your passes at home if you have a barcode, you do not need to queue, you can go straight to the turnstiles*If you have a fastpass, you can only have one at a time, but you are eligible to swipe again once your first fastpass is active   ie if the time is from 13.15   13.45, you can swipe for another at 13.15. Fastpass massively reduced our queuing times.*if you go and see the parade, stand near to the front (near it's a small world) as you can run to the busy rides straight away whilst everyone is still watching it.if you watch a show on the circular main street stage, stand closest to the castle as all the characters leave the stage at the back and you will get some great pics!*the little supermarket in the train station called Casino or something, was very cheap (in that area) for water, sandwiches and snacks*the deli in Disney Village is not good, very expensive for packet sandwiches* there was not huge amounts of difference between the two categories in buffallo bill show (in my opinion)*at the end of a season (parade season) some of the seasonal merchandise will be discounted, eg, we found some of the themed goods had 40% off   but an amazing reminder of the time season we visited!those who are children at heart will love this place   i did, and am dying to go back. What amazing escapism from the real world! loved it!

Not what I was expecting at all... The resort looked very  tired  and in need of an overhaul.... The piped  happy  music does grate after awhile and as for the restaurants, you would think that with all of the wonderful names and pretty exteriors, there would be decent food, however, it is all processed fast food with the exception of a few.... trying to find a vegetable or a piece of fruit is like finding a needle in a haystack... My son and I went in February which quite possible added to disappointment, but to go at any other time of year is far too expensive... I wouldn't spend 4 days at Chessington or Alton Towers, so wish I'd realised that it is JUST a theme park... 2 days would have been absolutely plenty of time to see both parks and enjoy the rides suitable for an 11yr old.I was expecting something Magical but didn't find it..... just a huge Visa Bill... thankfully I booked Full Board, because 6 euros for a ham sandwich is just a little bit excessive!!!

My husband and I travelled to Disneyland Paris without children just for the experience of it. We used our Paris Visite Pass for a 20% discount on the entry fee for the 2 parks 1 day ticket. We would suggest buying your tickets at a Visitor Centre in town, and avoid the ticket purchase line up at the park.We were very surprised how busy the park was in February. Most people wearing winter hats and mittens, small children wearing snow suits did not appear to stop their fun. The Main Street Parades were fun to watch, and the live Mickey Mouse Dance Show was enjoyed by all. The shops were plentiful, and had lots to offer every price range. The one ride we took was the  It's a Small World After All    it was colourful and fun. We ate at the Lion King theme resturant   it was typical theme park food   unremarkable, but a meal.We also visited the Disney Studio Park. We didn't find much there to amuse us, and we can't recommend it for the money paid.Overall, it was a fun place to visit   we enjoyed the day, without too much expectation.

I visited this destination with my six year old daughter for four days and three nights, and without having the luxury of taking her out of school during term time, it had to be mid half term holidays. I booked an all inclusive meals deal and stayed at the Sequio lodge. I thought I would review the whole expreience from this point of view.Upon arrival at Paris CDG it was decided to take the TGV train to the resort. Depending on what terminal you arrive at, the station is very easy to find and consists of either a short walk or a free shuttle train to terminal 2. You can pre book tickets online and collect them at the station from the many ticket machines (English translations) or like me pay at the ticket office. An adult and child ticket cost 23 euros which is about the same as the Disney bus, however we were at Marne la Valee in 10 minutes! Upon arrival there is a bus terminal directly outside which offers a free bus ride to your hotel, or you can choose to walk through Disney Village. In all it took about twenty minutes to walk to the hotel, and luckily the check in took no more than ten minutes, with staff speaking all European languages.HOTEL:  I could honestly see nothing wrong with it. It is enormous, but there are plenty of lifts and it is well sign posted. Our room was immaculate, with two king size beds and a TV. There are no tea coffee facilites, but I drink too much of that at home anyway. There is a swimming pool which does get busy and has minimal locker space so prepare to leave your belongings at the side of the pool. The bar area is quite spacious and a pint of lager cost six euros, but that is just the way it is at the moment with the current exchange rate. All meal times can be booked at check in or through the hotel consierge.FOOD:  Because of the time of year the hotel was busy so it is a good idea to reserve your meal times. Be aware that the park opens at 8am for hotel guests so if you can get an early breakfast time (7am onwards). Breakfast was a buffet, with cereals and pastries etc. You can  stock up  on pastries and fresh fruit to take with you, and believe me they do come in handy later in the day. This is not frowned upon and they are not taken from you at the park entrance. We were given lunch vouchers at check in and these were redeamed at numerous eateries in the park. The choice was limited pretty much to burger and chips in fairness, which is where the fruit comes in. You could purchase other foods with a pizza meal costing around 12 euros. Evening meals can go up to 10 o'clock and is again a buffet with a wide selection. It wasnt great but it was edible and to be honest we were both too tired anyway to care. THE PARKS:  I thought both parks were great and saw none of the miserable staff witnessed by other travellers. Again it was a busy time of year and we did queue on average about 40 minutes for each attraction. You can do the fast pass thing but to be honest that queue was almost as big anyway. In two and a half days in the parks we did everyting that could be done, and my daughter was ok with all the rides with the exception of Indianna Jones and Space Mountain which had height restrictions. Disneyland opens early for hotel guests but Walt Disney Studios did not open till 10am. The park seemed to have also got to grips with the disney character photo opportunites and a lot were not barriered off so people had to queue rather than stampede as of old.You can try and speak French if you like but in my experience the French seemed more offended that I was struggling with their language (A level) and everyone speaks English anyway!Ultimatley I could moan about a lot. It was freezing and it rained for two of the days but so what. Yes people are ignorant and try push in and let their kids run riot (at one stage two brothers were having a full scale fight in the queue and the parents were somewhat oblivious! I kid you not), but so what. Yes there are a lot of Disney shops that scream buy me to young children, but so what... you only live once and a trip is what you make it and my daughter loved it!!

Ive been to DisneyLand Paris with my parents and brother 3 4 times and we have LOVED every single visit. Theres something for everyone and, although the ques may be long during the school holidays, there is so much to look at the time goes by very quickly. Both parks are really clean and the staff really make your holiday. The only downside would be that some nationalities tend to push in more than other. unlike us brits who will just complain about ques others will simply try to slyly push past you. however this is not the fault of disneyland itself. There are plenty of places to eat from lower budget 'fast food' places to more expensive sit down buffetts and waiter service food venues. the food can be quite expensive (but hey you are in disneyland after all) there is a picnic area out side the park on the way from the carpark however if your in a group or travelling as a family it can be quite a walk for little ones, and personally i would save time and effort and but food. The rides are great, food is great, staff are friendly, the parades are definatley not to miss. Plently of photo oportunitiesOverall as four adults my brother and myself being 13 and 10 went we first went and 18 and 15 when we last went we have so much fun!DisneyLand Paris is certainly not just a kids holiday!!

If you enjoy getting ripped off then Disneyland Paris may just be for you.In addition we found the majority of the Parisians to be ignorant, arrogant and bad tempered   this included many of the Disney staff. We have 2 small children and you basically have to fight to get to see the attractions otherwise you get pushed to the back.It is not Euro Disney it is French Disney and they basically dont want anyone else there.If you want to experience Disney go to the states and let them look after you properly rather than put up with all the expense and hassle you get with Euro Disney.The kids did enjoy it but, boy, did we have to work that much harder here to make it enjoyable. Very dissapointed.

Just came back from Disneyland Paris. We stayed at the New York Hotel, Feb 12 15. The hotel itself is ok. I found the bed and pillows rather hard and we were unable to turn down the heat. However, opening the windows did help a little. The tub is very high and you need to be careful getting in and out. Breakfast is a joke. Runny power eggs, over salted bacon, and no orange juice. You will be ok if you like yogurt and rolls. The bar is overpriced, 10 euros for a cosmopolitain and 9 eurs for a single shot of whiskey. Both parks were very crowded and the staff couldn't keep up with it. We were turned away from using our Tower of Terror fastpass and told to stand in line. We are still unsure as to why because we arrived during our timeframe. All fastpasses were gone very early in the day. The average wait during our stay for rides was at least an hour. They also had several  technical difficulties  in both parks. We were stuck on Crushes Coaster for 15 mins and Rock N Rollarcoaster broke down for about 10 mins. The early morning hours are a waste. Peter Pan, the only ride open in Fantasyland, wasn't working. We had to go to Discoveryland and ride Space Mountain and Buzz Lightyear. We had dinner at Walt's in Disneyland Park and we feel that is very overated. The food is average, there isn't much choice, the steaks came out like leather and we felt very rushed. Overall, we will not return to Disneyland Paris. We feel that it is overpriced for what you get. The best part of the trip was Planet Hollywood in Disney Village but at 8.50 euros a drink, even that was too expensive.

After reading more than a few reviews on euro Disney, i really was not expecting great things, however our trip was one of a life time, of course as everyone says 'Its not like Disneyland USA' and its not, but it is also a fration of the price. We stayed at Davy Crockett Cabins which were abit of a drive from the parks but nothing to complain about, the cabins were spotless well heated and well equipped. The staff were amazing throughout the stay, and i found the services offered by the hotels and parks immpeccable. We had 5 inchs of snow and they still kept everything running, the parks were cleared of snow and puddles to make it easier for guests and free hot drinks were offered to help warm us up. I would definatly recommend Euro Disney as a short break and will definatly be going again!

After visiting Disneyland Resort Paris 20 times, i have always been satisfied with the service. After staying at the Disneyland Paris Castle Club, the customer care has been to a very high standard  the VIP Passes are a great advantage, cutting queing times greatly for all the best and busiest rides. The park has certainly changed since i visited it in 1992 but has changed for the better. All the employees are friendly and help wherever possible. People moan about the Park about prices, however you have to pay for quality. If you do not want to pay these high prices for the quality offered then don't visit Disneyland Resort Paris. I  3 Castle Club at the Disneyland Hotel

Our family, my wife and three children visited over New Year . It was our second visit, the first 8 years ago which was poor but either we had memoried like goldfish or hoped that it was a one off bad experience. It was not!There was one redeeming feature, the New Year dinner in our hotel was wonderful although very expensive. Other than that it was atrocious. The concierge was a joke, rude and unhelpful, my wife who was in a wheel chair was treated like a pariah, the attraction and in particular the rationed tickets for wheelchair users meant that a 30 minute queue for the public was a three hour queue for her because of the wheelchair. People rude, food poor, so poor that two of our family were sick after eating a    150 meal of disgusting filth in the pirates of the caribbean themed restaurant. Even the waiter sympathised, he was embarrassed.We have visited Disney Fl which is fantastic, this is as poor as it gets folks, don't bother, pay the airfare and go to FL

Just back from 4 days with my family including my son who is 7 and has Aspergers. Were told that Disney were great when t comes to looking after diabled guests and they were. Before arrving I telephoned and explained and they alocated us more suitable accommodation. When arriving at the park we went to City Hall with prrof of DLA benefit and were given a green pass for my son which allows you easy access to all the rides. Basically the person is allowed to access to the rides mainly via the exit and upon showing the pass will get onto the ride in about 5 mins. My son will not wait in queues and will become very aggressive so this was a godsend. You are allowed between 3 and 7 helpers with you. Because we are a family of 5 some rides myself or my husband had to sit out but mainly the staff just allowed us all on. Some rides, the most popular, you had to reserve a place so they could stagger disbaled guests but we never had to wait more than 30 mins (we just went somewhere else and came back at the right time) and that was at the weekend. The staff were all great and we had an excellent time.

Having heard from a number of people that DLP didn't have that 'magic touch' that Disneyworld in Florida has, I wasn't expecting a lot from it. However, I found majority of staff to be friendly and welcoming as well as in character. A number of rides I've been on in WDW and loved I actually preferred here at DLP, such as Pirates of the Caribbean, Space Mountain & Big Thunder Mountain.I also loved that you could go into the castle and the Sleeping Beauty story theme up there.

We returned from a trip to Disneyland, Paris after staying from 3rd to 5th January 2010. It is a great time to visit. It was very quiet and queues for the really popular rides were no more than 20 30minutes. You didn't even have to book to get into the restaurants and could wander in anytime. It was however extremely cold outside. We decided to vist Eurodisney after having been to Disney in Orlando 3 times. There really is no comparison. The magic is just not there. Everything is on a much smaller scale, especially Hollywood Studios. The staff do not seem to get into character at all. Working there seems to be just a job. They rarely smile or converse with you. Whereas in Florida all the staff seemed to love it. When a character appears, there are no queues formed to meet them by their assistants. There is just a mob of pushy people with no manners. The character stays for no more than 5 minutes and then disappears without letting you know if they are coming back.On a positive note there are however some good rides that Florida does not have like Crush Coaster and Cinemagic, both in Hollywood Studios. Their Big Thunder Mountain ride was better than the one in FloridaIt is a theme park but it is not Disney!!!

Stayed at hotel Cheyenne, good little hotel for the price. Done two visits now in two years staying at the same hotel. Did four nights, five day passes into the park. It is expensive so to keep the cost down booked half board & at breakfast made sandwiches for lunch, everybody does around you & no one is told off. Also flew with jet 2. Kids just love it & ask when can we go again.

I have visited Disney in Florida last year. A great experience, so the plan was made to visit Eurodisney. We also booked a stay in Hotel Cheyenne. To start with the hotel, it is poor value for money. The rooms are not very clean, the rooms (and beds) are small and the interior (the TV for example) are outdated. The breakfast is ultimate chaos. You receive a card where you see the time you are welcome for breakfast. The choice of food is not great. The price of the hotel is hugh, compare it with more expensive 4 or 5 star hotels. But the Cheyenne is a poor 2 star hotel if you ask me.I have different views abouth the stay in the park. We were there on a tuesday, friday and satyrday in November. The tuesday and friday were ok. Waiting times were not so long, from 5 minutes to max 20 30 minutes for the big attractions. Attractions are good. On saturday however, the lines were horrible. Up to 120 minutes. Luckily for us, we visited all the attractions and ran away from the parc. It was so crowded, i couldn't believe my eyes. What annoyed me most was the French element. The staff was arrogant, uninterested and not friendly at all. What a difference when i compare this to Disney World Orlando. There all the staffmembers are happy, helpfull and with their behaviour they add that magic to the Disney experience. Too bad that in France, such high standards are impossible. The prices in Eurodisney are also extremely high. A simple hot dog costs a fortune.Disney Village was a lot smaller then the village in Orlando. The restaurants in Disney Village are ok, but (ofcourse) quit expensive. Don't expect prime cuisine, but the burgers and steaks are ok. We eated in Planet Hollywood and Rainforest.My advice to Disney: improve the hotels, lower the prices and please fix the waiting lines. And maybe it is a good advice if Disney train there personell better. Learn them how to smile, be helpfull etcetera.

We are so, so disappointed. Before we left my husband and I were more excited about going than the children. We had such high hopes of having a fantastic 5 day trip there and had decided to go in December to add to the magic. Almost immediately our enthusiasm waned. We arrived at St Pancras to board the Eurostar and had expected some kind of friendly welcome but this wasn't to be. The only way we knew where we were boarding was by watching the monitors and by asking other passengers. My children helped themselves to the so called Disney Welcome Packs from the unmanned service desk. When we arrived at Marne Le Vallee, we headed straight to the Park while our luggage was sent directly to our hotel and had a nice afternoon looking round and watching the parades which I must admit were incredible. After a long day we waited 25 minutes for a bus to our hotel when we had been informed they ran every ten minutes. We finally arrived at the Hotel Santa Fe, why Disney would put their name to such a hovel I cant imagine.  Saturday and Sunday were absolutely awful, I expeced it to be very busy but I found the locals to be very rude and pushy. They dont seem to be able to grasp the concept of queuing like the rest of us. The Disneyland staff were at best civil and at worst completely arrogant, they would make short, sharp comments whether we were ordering in a restaurant or shopping in one of the stores, the only time I had a nice experience was in City Hall when a lovely member of staff went out of her way to find a screwdriver for me so I could put batteries in my son's camera, to her I am extremely grateful. We met another family there and they were as relieved to get on the train home as we were. Shame on you Disney :   (

Picture this...Buy tickets 110 minutes!Get yourself a 'Fastlane ticket': 40 minutes each!Space mountain, Starwars, Peter Pan, Small World etc.: Waiting lines vary from 60 minutes till 110 minutes!Get some food: 70 Minutes. after that no seats available!Fastlaneline: 40 minutes! Gecause this fastane line our other fastlane ticket was no longer valid!After one day we have only been in the Star Wars attraction. That was nice but it is also completly stupid to hear al this well known disney caracters speak French. Do yourself and your kids a favour and skip this parc. If Walt Disney was still alive he would wish he was dead when he lays his eyes on the French version of his dream.

We just finished a day at Disney. They said there were 50,000 visitors today 12 28. We waited one hour to buy the ticket to get in, then realized that all Fast Past tickets were gone (by 2pm) so they only option was to wait in line. The lines for all popular rides were all 110 minutes. By the end of the day, we had done 2 rides. Not a great return on investment. On peak days like today, they should advise you that lines are extremely long and you may at best get to go to two rides. Even the tame dumbo ride was 75 minutes. Go some where else in Paris, if you have a c hoice. The crowds are horible and there simply is not enough staff.

We have just come back from a 3 day stay at the park and our two toddlers ( 3 and 18 months) has a wonderful time   as did we. The rides were fantatstic, the parades awesome and the characters friendly and warm (which is just as well when it is cold and raining!). We smuggled in drinks and snacks, went back to the hotel for lunch (hotel New York was a lovely place to stay) and made full use of the early opening of the park for hotel guests and fast pass tickets. We had two buggies as there is a lot to get around. In short, plan your stay and you should enjoy your visit. We had a wonderful time and are already planning our next trip. Is it as good as America? Probably not but it's a hell of a lot cheaper to get there!

This park was what we expected. It is a smaller version of the original, the only difference was the language. It was in our travel itinerary because of our 10 year old daughter. There was a shuttle from the Marriott Resort where we were staying; one would have to obtain the shuttle tickets at least 24 hours in advance to secure a seat. Watch out for the last shuttle at night; if you miss it you'll have to take the local bus back to the hotel.Our daughter was very happy. The rest of the week we divided our time between Lourdes and downtown Paris. There are no words to describe the beauty of the city f Paris. The history and arts are soaked in the people's lifestyles. Most of the people we met were friendly; others were not any different than other large cities like NY City where I lived and worked many years. Make sure you have a comfortable pair of shoes to walk around with. If you opt for sneakers, get some black ones..the white ones look too touristy.

Everything in the Disneyland Park and Disney Village is HUGELY expensive and I don't believe we can purely blame the    Euro rate at the present time although it should be bourne in mind. Prices are really bumped up for the captive park users. We paid   5 for a small cup of hot chocolate and our cheapest meal for four during our four day stay in December was a McDonalds that came in at   34 (and included three  value  meals). We don't mind paying good money for a decent meal but there is little to offer in the resort that represents good value for money, acutally, NOTHING that represents good value for money.Also, is it just me, or is Planet Hollywood (located in the Disney Village) trapped in the early 1990's. My kids (7 and 13) wanted to go but with the likes of Mel Gibson, Danny Glover and the Lethal Weapon movies on the walls I felt that they wanted our money (18 Euros for a burger and a very small portion of fries) but they hadn't reinvested any of it in the resaturant for YEARS.......The furnishings are tired and dusty and twenty years out of date. Come on Planet Hollywood   get yourself into this century or we won't be going back.Disneyland Paris   great but an expensive holiday......having a  magical  time is very costly.....

I have brought my family to Disney's parks in California, Florida and Paris several times over the past 10 years. The US parks are fantastic, they really know how to create the MAGIC. However, Disneyland Paris is a disgraceful reflection of Disney   s customer service ethos. In general, I found their employees to be very rude, arrogant and disinterested in my experience of the parks. I have just returned from a 5 day trip and we have decided that we will never return to Paris for Disneyland. Its a shame because the attractions are actually quite good. The new Crush Coaster is excellent, as is the Tower of Terror, the live motorshow, Aerosmith Coaster, Haunted Mansion, Thunder Mountain, Space Mountain and a whole load of other attractions that most children can get on.It was  4C most of the time we were there, which was great as its really felt like Christmas with real snow on the ground.Disney, if you read these reports     send some of your heavy hitters to Paris to sort out this mess before you lose your investment.We will try PortAventura in Spain next time.

I know that I should not compare this park to the service and quality in the United States, but I must say that Disneyland Paris should invest in training their cast members to reflect the spirit and magic that Walt Disney would have imagined. Our family of four went to Disneyland Paris in November when there were no crowds due to the wet and cold weather. We had a nice experience eating lunch at the Auberge Cendrillon with the characters (it was 55 euros per person)   the food was great and the princesses were very attentive to the guests. On the other hand, wandering through the empty park, not a single cast member greeted us or even tried to smile. They all look miserable working there. The biggest disappointment?? An extremely rude cashier at the Aladdin boutique yelled at me for not being able to speak French (I asked him a question in English) and then he threatened to call security over a plastic bag (I asked for a bag because it was raining and I insisted on having a bag to put the pictures of Cinderella which came with no envelope, compliments of the restaurant, since it was raining). It was the worst experience at any Disney Park (I have been to Florida and I live in California). I have never been yelled at by a Disney employee. I will never go back and pay that type of money to be abused by their so called cast members. Disneyland Paris should realize that part of the magic of Disney is the attitude of the cast members.

Great time in a dreamland. yes it is expensive but the running costs are very high. My kids and I had a wonderful time at Disneyland paris. The staff godd do with a kick up the tail sometimes as they are not the happiest in the world.

I am very disappointed that i have to write this complaint, but we were very unsatisfied with our stay at Santa Fe Hotel, Disneyland Paris from 6th November '09 to 8th Novemever '09. We went especially for our child's first birthday as we wanted it to be a special, magical day for him.  There were numerous issus that arose over our weekend at Disneyland Paris, and feel that these should be reported and followed up. As a customer and mother I do not agree how these issues could of occured on our visit and am disgusted that Disneyland Paris allow such rude and unfriendly attitudes towards their paying customers. Firstly, when we arrived we were given a room on the first floor of which there was no lift for us to take the pram up even though on our booking we had noted that we had a baby with us. We had to go back to reception and ask for a room on the ground floor. The next room we were given was right next to the main entrance into the building. The main entrance door to the block would not shut so a draft was coming underneath our door. We stopped the draft by putting towels down by the door. We had a baby in a cot which is close to the floor, having to put towels by the door to stop the draft is really not good enough. When initially checking in, we were asked a time we would like to have breakfast. We asked if we had to chose a time as with a baby we are never on time and didnt want to rush. We were told that we had to chose a time, so we did. The next morning we frantically rushed to get ready for our allocated breakfast time, only to find ourselves waiting in a long queue. At first we thought the queue was for our table and waited patiently. As we had to rush to make it down on time, our baby was still in his night clothes. We then realised the majority of people in the queue did not have their ticket with an allocated time on, and the Disneyland Staff were just letting them in for breakfast with no priority for the people queuing with a ticket. When we finally found a table we found it to be dirty, the milk machine was out of milk, there were only broken bits of bread in the bread basket and there were no glasses to get juice. This is unacceptable. We are trying to get our child used to a feeding time. We had to break our schedule to fit in with the Santa Fe rules, only to find out nobody was sticking to the rules anyway.All this time was wasted which we could have spent in the park. Our friends then went back to the room to get a shower while we finished eating and feeding our baby. On return to the room, they found the new key they were given didn't work, so they had to go back to reception to fix this problem. Once again, more time that was lost that could have been spent in the park. They had to queue for a considerable amount of time to get to the reception desk, only to then speak to an incredibly rude and ignorant manager. Our friends explained the problem about the key to him, and expressed that they were disappointed about loosing time in the park as they also had to queue for breakfast when other people were allowed to push in etc. The manager replied that there were problems at Santa Fe with regards to the breakfast, but they had tried numerous other ways of doing it and the way they were currently using worked best. He then went on to add that he had been to many other hotels throughout the world and that they all have problems. Our friends said that they were also frequent travellers and had not seen breakfast in such shambles as that! The manager went on to argue with our friends that he had been to more countries and and stayed in more hotels than they had!! We find this to be completely unprofessional. The manager tried to resolve the problem by promising that he would come back to the room and fix the key. He never did. The rest of our 2 day stay we had to share the key which was completely unreasonable.  When we finally got to the park we were having a lovely time until.. We had booked the 'Birthday Meet and Great' in the Lucky Nugget for our son's first birthday. Again, we wanted his day to be extra special and one to remember for all of us. I phoned twice and both times when I reseved a place I was asked for his age and name. Once again, we had to wait a considerable amount of time to even be let into the Lucky Nugget, in which time other guests had started gathering outside. When the doors eventually opened, we found the other guests to push in and bombard other guests. With regards to Health and Safety, this is a very dangerous situation.  When we arrived we were seated at a table and then we went to change our son's nappy. When we came back, the staff were handing out the birthday cakes. We found the waiters to be very rude. They literally plonked the cake down in front of us. Nobody said happy birthday to him. A card was also placed on the table which was blank. It didn't even his name writen on it.  Goofy, Pluto, Tigger and Tac came round to meet our son, of which he loved. Then we spotted Mickey, but he was going round every table so we thought he would come to us last as we were situated near the end. When Mickey finally got to the tables near us, we assumed he would then come to us. To our dismay we relised he was about to leave, so my partner went over to him and kindly asked if he could you come over to say happy birthday to our son and sign his card. Mickey's helper then very rudely and abruptly replied  no, we are going he has no more time . We were so incredibly disappointed and upset by this. Our son has a Disneyland Paris autograph book with pictures of him with everyone except Mickey. Later, the staff then brought around the surprise for the the birthday boy girl and missed our table, so I went to the bar and asked if our son could have his surprise. A staff member called Aissa then went to get one and gave it to our son. We quickly realised the surprise was not suitable for under 3's, so we asked them if he could have a different surprise suitable for his age group. Aissa then went to find another product and once again came back with another surprise that was not suitable for under 3's. Aissa told us they didn't have anything for under 3's which I found funny as we were in Disney which is aimed at children, and we had seen things suitable for his age group around the park. We found the lady we spoke to very abbupt and her attitude towards us appalling. I was concerned my son would pick up on her negative approach as they pick things up so quickly at his age. I informed her that we had paid for him to have a birthday cake, meet the characters and receive a birthday surprise and that he had not recieved his surprise. She rudely replied 'You didn't pay for him'. We had to pay 19 euros a head for the adults. What right does she have to talk to paying customer like that? She then tried to get around the situation by telling us the surprise was not included in the price, and then told us that he could have the surprise that was not suitable for under 3's for him. Items have warnings printed on them for a reason. If our son had choked on the gift that Disneyland Paris gave him that was not suitable for his age group, imagine the public interest and what would be printed in the newspapers. Luckily we did notice, but if Disneyland Paris is going around giving presents to other children and the parents are not so alert to this, it's an accident waiting to happen. I told her that I would like to speak to a manager about these issues, only to be told there were no mangers on site. Once again, if something was to happen in the Lucky Nugget and there was no manager around to handle the situation, imagine the interest of the public and newspapers. Something else waiting to happen really!Finally a supervisor came and spoke to us. He was very pleasant and understanding of our issues raised to him. He also told us that we could complain near the entance of the park and explained that he could not do much more than which we found to be resonable. So, why couldn't Aissa who gave him the unsuitable toy, or the manager at Santa Fe handled it the same? Why did they have an abusive, threatening and uncaring attitude towards us? We're paying customers, wanting a fantastic birthday for our son. We found the staff to be unreasonable with us and make our time at Disneyland Paris uncomfortable and stressful. So much time was wasted going back and forth which could have been spent in the park. We're disgusted that Disneyland Paris employ people with such poor customer service and unacceptable approach to customers to work around children and deal with children and families everyday on their special occasions. The time for his birthday party was runined and we payed 19euros a head *4 to be argueing a fair point with a staff member that was so unreasonable and rude which i feel is totaly wrong. We paid   636 for 2 nights in a draughty room which was not suitable for a child to sleep in a cot low to the floor. When we complained at City Hall the staff were very helpful, understanding and friendly. They totaly understood our point that we could not give this toy to our son and kindly gave him teddy which was very kind. Why couldn't that have been done earlier at the Lucky Nugget? They were also very sympathetic about our troubles at Santa Fe. They informed us to write to Disneyland Paris as this is not acceptable behaviour for staff at Disney. We are so angry and upset to think we paid all that money for our son's birthday and ended up treated in such a poor manner. Disneyland Paris is meant to be a family park and we didn't expect such low standards, rudeness and aggressiveness.  So, that was his first birthday. It was meant to be incredibly special. Instead, it was an incredible let down.

Hi, just back from disneyland paris, we all loved it the atmosphere was amazing, hotel dead on, parades etc brilliatn couldn't fault it.But...did feel it was unbelievably commercialised the shops were wildly expensive ( though relatively empty) the food overpriced, though I know thats to be expected. My little girls are princess mad but the only way to get up close and personal with them was to take them to the princess lunch   well over 100 euros for myself, a 4 year old and a 2 year old when we asked were our favourite princess was   Belle  we were told she wasn't on that day which was a pity.While it is comforting to see security at times I found it nearly creepy to see all of this winter clad people talking into their walkie talkies at one stage when our 4 reached the top of the queue to meet goofy in his sleigh a little girl with learning difficulties jumped in with them to get her book signed, the security guy indicated to goofy not to sign and very firmly led the child to the bottom of the queue. I thought that was horrible he should have let her get her wee signature it was a easy mistke to make she was over excited and we certainly didn't mind.The security I felt were more to protect the characters then the visitors. Unfortunately my camera bag was lost  stolen, I think stolen, city hall were not particularly interested couldn't give me a receipt when I lodged what had happened with them. We were on our way home had to leave for the airport when I got home rang them back enquiring still no interest or any help finally got no. of local police department need to lodge a report with them even though I don't speak french and they don't speak english so that will be fun! Just felt Disney could have been a bit more proactive...anyway overall had a great time but wouldn't go every year ..

Went with easyjet got pre booked taxi from CDG Airport,stressfree way of doing it cost LESS than going on Disney bus for return journey with 2 kids 4 and 5 years old.Got to hotel SANTA FE in Disney Resort lunchtime on the Fri 25 Sept.Checked in charecters were in reception staff V friendly.Dumpped stuff and headed for park.Our park tickets and breakfast and evening meal included (booked prior to going).Jumpped on courtesy bus took about 4 mins to get there.Wow went into Disney park first through disney castle and hired big buggy for our kids makes life soo much easier cos you do a LOT of walking.7 euros for day hire we paid 20 euros for lunch for 4 of us not too bad.Some of the rides not suitable for kids under a certain height(not age) for safety and they do have parent swap ie one parent goes on the other waits with kids and then you change as you have already waited in an hour long Q.Unless you get the really horrible obstructive,ignorant member of female staff I came into contact with on tower of terror.We got there early and got Fast Pass tickets great waited in Q for 35 mins and one of our kids was too small so partner and oldest went on and a male member of staff Very helpfull advised when partner comes off give him smallest child and go to the barrier and be given access as we had passes and already queued.NO NO NO this girl advised me to go to end of queue.tried to explain what we had been advised but she was obviously in a rubbish mood she was having none of it.I have to admit I steam was coming out of my ears as we were advised of one thing but she just totally ignored it.If i could have found somewhere at that moment to have a complaint taken I would Have.Anyway kids loved it I loved it magical except for One member of staff everyone else is fantastic.Sata FE hotel basic,clean and staff and food great will go back

I have always dreamed of going to a Disney theme park. What a let down.The park was run down and dirty. The staff didn't have smiles on their faces. I was planning on going to America next and one of the main reasons was to visit the Disney parks   now Im not so sure.Shame. Magical it wasn't. Parade was great. Lines were ridiculous. Had a fast pass but couldn't figure out how to use it and no one would help us.I made the most of it though because it was always such a dream to go. But it was not worth the money.

Have just returned from a 3 night 4 day trip.Love Disney and have been fortunate enough to go to Florida and California. Disney Paris is not on the same scale as these parks but the European flavour helps to make this experience different. Language is not a barrier and all staff spoke english really well. The rides do part english part french and the shows have dedicated times in different languages. Yes its expensive  we returned today and paid around 13euros per adult for lunch and around 30euros for a 3 course dinner (not incl drinks). However there are ways to save  most restaurants have a fixed price menu (rainforest cafe had a main course and dessert for 19euro) Mcdonalds is a good place for lunch (just a short walk from the park entrance into disney village (around 5 7euro for a meal) and our 2 kids (aged 1 & 3) shared childrens meals. We found that in Disneyland & Disney studios we got a free hot drink in the afternoon with each reciept for drinks snacks in the morning so i would suggest buying drinks snacks seperately to take advantage of this offer  Also ask if you're not given the voucher straight away as I noticed one member of staff gave us only our purchase reciept and not the voucher which was placed at the side of the till!(may have been a mistake but worth checking).The christmas parade and illuminations parade are worth seeing (and still went ahead despite rain) and the park dressed for christmas was lovely. We took the kids to see santa and the queued for about half hour but we were allowed to stay with him as long as we wanted. The castle lighting ceremony is worth sticking around for and we certainly left with a christmassy feel.As we went midweek (and the weather was poor) ride times were avg 5mins and on some we walked straight on which was great as the weather didnt stop us doing anything.Ive given 4 5 due to the current exchange rate on the euro but although only there for a few days we feel like we've had a much longer holiday.Would definately go back.

We actually enjoy the parks alot. we bought 2 days pass. err dont have enough to cover the whole park.maybe we spent most of time on Q. however i abit dislike tat we have to fight to take photo with d disney character. err beside mickey, i think they should have a Q system for others. & worst of all, me & hb seem like very rude  fight  with all those kids! really embarrassing. so after few characters, hb abit fedup to take any more photos.

I will start with the same old statement that this was a wonderful fantasy trip of excitement splendour in a childish world of dreams and wishes sprinkled with fairy dust. Now that   s out of the way the truth of the matter is it is the biggest child manipulation for the purpose of adult extortion I have ever seen     The whole setup is geared to getting children to have a major I want fit at every corner throwing in the fact that a captive audience has no choice but pay through the nose,The good parts are few and far between but let me try to highlight them.1     That done now the bad points     food which is a no choice requirement will cost you   6 for a hot dog with tinned sausage or there is the toffee apples at   3 then there is a portion of chips at   3 which is half a Mc Donald   s portion ice creams come out at   3 for the smallest and a cup of coffee is   2.50 per dribble.
