We had one meal in the park which was a mixed grill consisting of a sausage, one 3 inch rib, a small burger and chips x 4 and 2 child meals of nuggets and chips with coffees and juices which came to   76.But you go for the spectacle and except the prices you say     Well to start it was raining so the travelators from the car park to Disneyland were not working so a walk of half a mile is you first jaunt followed by another 3 miles walking around getting fast passes to get on the rides followed by another 3 miles going on the rides and finding the fast passes are not so fast so you miss most of the rides you had fast passes for as you end up queuing anyway.Getting pictures of your nearest and dearest with Mickey or Pluto and the gang is a mad fight for the queue only to be the ones that just misses as Mickey had to go for a show and as we seen needed a fag break     Then there is the French element to the problem as they seem to think that queuing is a British requirement and they have a god given right to push in which caused at least 5 near punch ups with parents that I saw.     Be aware that if you are over 6 feet tall and stocky they will let you queue for 2 hours only to tell you you are to big for the ride when you get to the front and this is most prevalent on the Nemo ride.     We got a fast pass for Indiana Jones train at 2pm which got us in at 8pm just to give you an idea on how bad it is.There is an American grill just outside the gates called Annett   s Diner where we stopped to get some chips, you can see the cooking staff while you wait which caused us to cancel our order as they were handling raw chicken and cooked food without washing their hands as well as the normal itch scratching problems they seem to have and it looked like a scene from the Somali refugee cook houseBe sure as eggs are eggs the grandchildren will love it to bits and you will get some memorable photos but in the end as long as we accept this total rip off we deserve to be exploited by this money grabbing company that is so far removed from the great Walt Disney as to be unrecognisable.We spoke to an American working at the park that was on an exchange and she said it was terrible and nothing like the Florida Disney and she told us she would complain when she got back to the states.

Best fun ever!! It doesn't matter that you're all grown up because when you walk through the gates of Disney you become a child again. Our trip here was in November so the Christmas celebrations and decorations were underway which made it a little bit extra special. It's simple to get here from Paris city centre, about 40 minutes on the RER A train which you get on at any of the maion stations in the city. Trains are cheap and pretty frequent as well so that adds to the ease.

Hi,For my daughter 9th birthday, we went to Disneyland Paris. I booked from thursday till saturday. And just after the Halloween weekend.We booked by phone and I asked for a lower level hotel and they upgrade us directly to the Hotel New York (rated 4keys) for the price of a rated 3 keys hotel. I booked this period for different reasons but mostly because it was holiday where we live and not in France so less people and more english speaking visitors (more attractions, shows in english). Moreover they offered all meals. Last reason: it was the time between Halloween theme and the beginning of Christmas theme   so we enjoyed both.We arrived early the first day and our room was ready (normally check in 1500), we checked in around 1030.Because of the season, we had one rainy day. We rushed to the studio and did all the inside shows.Booked your restaurant in advance keeping in mind that if you maximize your time in the park, you will be tired in the evening (certainly the kids :) ).We had fun and no long waiting lines. Use the system fastpass, if the waiting was more than 15 min we chose the fastpass solution     scan your tickets to the fastpass and you get a ticket for a certain timeframe, that let you the time to go get a coffe or do another attraction without loosing time in line.Last but not least, good walking   comfortable shoes are mandatory.

We returned recently from our visit to 'Hallowe'en' Disneyland and it was just fantastic. We took my two children aged 11 and 8 yrs, and they both still had the 'wow' factor at it all, plus they were tall enough to enjoy all the rides except for possibly two which is a bonus when you're paying out so much for the tickets, that being said there are plenty of rides for the smaller ones to enjoy, Peter Pan and Small world being favourites. The best rides to aim for first thing in Disneyland are Buzz Lazer Blast, and the Phantom Manor and take a fast pass for Thunder Mountain and Star Tours as they queues are very long for these two. Also when we went the park was open til 10pm and rides which had horrendous queues in the daytime were practically non existent in the evening, down to something like ten mins so it's worth leaving the popular rides til late evening (check closing hours at the park tho). In Walt Disney Studios head straight for Crush's coaster which was brilliant, there's no fast pass on this so you have to get in early to beat the queues, definately worth a couple of rides on is the Aerosmith Rock'n rollercoaster which quietened the kids down for a bit! : ) We went for 3 nights and had two full days in the parks which was about right. We stayed at the Kyriad (an off site hotel with free shuttle) which still had a new fresh clean feel to it and a bar you could have a drink at later. The queues from hotels like the Santa Fe for the Shuttle bus where large, whereas we just were able to jump on the shuttle bus easily due to the hotel being nowhere near as huge and not having so many people to cater for. Disneyland at night is amazing with the pink castle all lit up and it will give you and your kids something to remember for a very long time. Food is expensive, walking around there are hot dog stands which come in at around 7Euros 50 for hot dog and drink or there abouts, so we ate well at breakfast, and then at 4.30 (to avoid food queues) treated ourselves at the Rainforest cafe in Disney Village well worth a visit, a quick turn around at the hotel, and then back into disney for some more action. We paid 20 euros per adult for main meal and a desert, and the kids menu for drink, main and desert was around 12 euros so with our drinks around 75 euros just to give you an idea. Definately worth going to, and for extra magic pick Hallowe'en or the Christmas festivities period.

I guess this just agrees with many other reviews   once the American parks have been experienced, this really is a poor second best. There really is no comparison of the general state and cleanliness of the parks, the friendliness of the staff and the quality of the rides. Eating in the park will just about bankrupt you and the food isn't up to much.To be honest, particularly given the present exchange rates, head for the USA if you want to  do Disney . In Europe, the Efteling park is much better.

We went to DLP on 21st Oct, staying at the Santa Fe Hotel. The hotel was lovely, no complaints! We were in the Disney Park for 8am which was worth it. The rides were good, the kids loved Buzz Lightyear. We took some snacks with us, which saved some money. We ate at Cafe Mickey, the food is discusting! lots of characters which was the only good thing. Rainforest cafe was better and the Lucky nugget saloon was ok but nothing great. Bad service in this one, waited 20mins to pay. They rush you then your left standing and waiting for ages. Buffalo Bills is worth it! Was great, we really got involved and was fun! The people are pushy and rude, pushing my 5 year old. I'd had enough after 2 days! Was a good time but we wouldnt go back there again!Everything expensive, but i knew what to expect. We travelled on eurostar which is great, Disney Express works very well too. The longest queue was about 30mins for Nemo and Peter Pan. but usually the queus go quite quick and we were usually only waiting for 5 10 mins. I wouldnt recommend going on a Saturday, it got extremely busy on this day. When it rains it rains! Head for the studios for more shelter! Stitch Live was worth seeing too. Be very careful, when its wet everywhere is very slippery, lots of people falling over! No one queues for anything, so in the end we stopped queueing too. They shove you in the lines, i ended up barging them back just to make them stop. Even with me being pregnant they do not care! Take rainjackets you WILL need them! If travelling on Eurostar you can take as much luggage as you want. We bought back lots of presents even a huge globe in a box and it was fine. there is an Esso garage outside near the Santa Fe but we didnt go there. The shuttle buses were fine for us, no pushing. Get breakfast before 8am, after this its really busy!

We arrived by Eurostar at 13.30, in the park by 14.00. Weather was lovely, sunny two days, chilly one day. Stayed at Sequia Lodge. Had 2 interconnecting rooms in Yellowstone Lodge, great for putting little ones to bed then adults could still chat in other room. We had the half board plan. Had dinner in Hunters Grill first night, standard buffet, nice food, kids found plenty to eat. The next night we ate in Disneyland Park, we opted for a buffet again because we had a baby with us and babies don't like waiting to be served! Went to Plaza Gardens   AVOID THIS AT ALL COSTS! We are not fussy eaters but most of the food was inedible, even the kids hated it. Long queues for the food. I think the crepes were about a week old, you couldn't even cut them   awful place. The ride queues were not too bad considering it was half term, about 40 minutes for the big rides except on Halloween when wait times shot up to nearly 2 hours by the afternoon. We have been to Florida many times and we love Disneyland Paris nearly as much as the Magic Kingdom, only downside is the prices, everything is so, so expensive. Our last day we ate at Rainforest Cafe, nice meal but for 4 adults and 3 kids it came to nearly 200 Euros just for a main course each and puddings for the kids.

We went to Disneyland on a grey Friday in the off season (early October) and had a great time. Apart from Autopia, we never queued more than 5 10 minutes, covered pretty much everything we wanted in a day (and did a few faves twice) and felt we got good value for money. The service was typically French ie unmotivated, slow but serviceable. One day was actually enough for us, although we didn't go the Studio. As plenty of people have noted the food is both expensive and awful (avoid the pizza burger at Pizza Planet   in fact avoid Pizza Planet, it is truly grim), and the merchandise is not cheap, but we gave the kids a budget to keep that under control.We also got the train from Paris, rather than stay at the hotels at Disney. Cheap and easy in both directions, with no parking hassles or getting lost.So my tip would be, if you can manage it, off season, weekday, a bit overcast   good time.

We visited on 22 26th October as a family of 5 (2 adults and 3 children, 14, 10, 3) via Eurostar from Ashford and stayed in the Newport Bay. See separate review for this.Tips for the two parks are as follows :1. WeekendsThe parks are absolutely rammed at the weekend, so if you can avoid Sat   Sun (plus the French school holidays) then you will have a much calmer time and more rides. Waiting times for the big rides were 90 minutes plus, with Fast Pass tickets running out by 2pm   when the park is open until 10pm ! The park was selling annual passes for 37 Euro so the locals were taking advantage.2. Magic HoursDue to the above, you must take advantage of the 8.00 start   I know you are on holiday but needs must ! There were only 7 rides open (4 in Fantasyland, 3 in Discoveryland) but you can get to ride on the slow loaders like Dumbo or popular rides like Buzz and Space Mountain without a queue. You need your hotel ID card to get into the park. It starts to get busier at 9.30 as non hotel people come in but they cannot access rides until 10.00   when the need for a clear plan becomes obvious !3. Fast Pass & PlanningYou need to have a clear plan (which may change at any moment) if you want to do big rides or get Fast Pass benefits and avoid long queues. First is to take advantage of the Magic Hours (above). Secondly is to plan your Fast Pass strategy. Your park ticket is your Fast Pass and you can get one at a time for one of the big rides. If your party do not all want to go on the rides (e.g. you have small children etc) then ensure you use their Fast Pass ticket ! You can also acquire extra Fast Pass tickets on a well known auction site ! I bought 10 extra FP's for   10 and they worked a treat and allowed us to really make the most of the benefit Fast Pass gives as we could have 15 tickets at a time !Just before 10.00, best bet is to go to the entrance of Frontierland where the rope gets dropped and you can RUN to be first on Big Thunder Mountain. When you come off, grab a Fast Pass or two for later and go to Indiana Jones and do the same. BTM is busy ALL DAY but Indiana is quiet in the first few hours.If you have Fast Passes, then Discoveryland is great as it has 3 rides close together.You can break up the day with trips on the train, steam boat etc and grab some lunch.Please note that some rides are only open Friday Monday in Fantasyland, and some do not open until 11.00 !! Examples are Alices Labrynth, the Petit Train and the Fairytale boat in Fantasy land and the Nautilus in Discoveryland. This means that at 10.00, Fantasyland becomes VERY busy !!!!4. Meal PlanningFood is VERY expensive if you do not plan. Fill up on breakfast at 7.30 and take bottles of water with you. Cheapest options in the park is to grab a Kids Happy Meal for 4.95 Euro for everyone at around noon to keep you going until dinner time. Sit down meals are expensive at around 30 Euro a head in Lucky Nugget.5. ParisA great option is to take a day out to Paris   we did it on a Saturday to avoid the crowds in the park. You can pre buy a ticket (Paris Visite) which gives unlimited travel for the day. We took in the Eiffel Tower to the 2nd floor (26 Euro for the 5 of us as u4 free), then a boat trip on the Seine (train ticket gave 25% off adults so cost 29Euro for all 5   u4 free again !). Saw Arc de Triomphe and then walked up Champs Elysee and dined out at McDonalds for 20 Euro !! it is about 200 yds from the Arc on the left. Took in Sacre Couer via the funicular railway (included in rail ticket). Was a really good day out and got back to hotel at about 7pm !!6. Studios ParkOpens at 10.00   but if you want to go on Crush's Coaster then you need to be at the front when rope drops at 9.45 as no Fast Pass but 2 hour queues. Lots of shows so planning essential to split up rides with shows. Note Stitch & Playhouse are in various languages so check on way in. Use your Fast Passes wisely for Tower and Aerosmith (around the shows).7. Parades & CharactersStudios parade was pathetic and not worth queing for   better to take advantage of quieter rides !Disney parade much better. If you go to Small World and watch from the elevated position is avoids the scrum at lower level   also allows you to get on the ride at the end of the parade too ! There was a Halloween parade at 4.45 and the main Disney one at 5.00. Don't be fooled into thinking the parade is over after the Halloween one ! There are lots of character interactions but they are not really organised and you need to adopt a locals attitude of push to the front otherwise you have no chance !8. When in Rome....Or Paris. You need to do as the locals do or just accept things and go with the flow otherwise you will get frustrated ! People push in. Families send Dad on to  save a place  in the queue. However, I found it most rewarding to speak a bit of my O level French and get a friendly response and a smile ! Overall we had a really good time because we had a plan for each day, based on feedback from this website, books and timetables. I would really suggest you plan, and be aware that you may need to change it at any time   especially where kids are involved !Let me know if you want me to answer any questions.

We booked this trip for my son's 5th birthday, we stayed in the Sequoia Lodge for 3 nights 4 days. On arrival check in was smooth and we went straight to our room to feed me one year old daughter, there was no kettle in the room which I was quite surprised about I called reseption 4 times and after an hour one eventually arrived!!! Not a good start! We proceded to the park which was a 10 15 min walk from the hotel. When we got there it was so busy the queues were too long. We managed to get on a few of the smaller rides and decided to brave the queues the following day. I have to say and I may be generalising but the French really don't seem to like Brits, it was quite apparent from both the french public and the staff especially at the hotel. Having been to Florida I have to question the positioning of this park as they didn't seem to have the same hospitality skills to deliver the  Disney Magic !!!!! Also no one seemed to know how to wait in line it was definatley evryone for themselves. I was surprised at how small the park was and the tour in the studios was poor. If I had to sum up the park and hotel I would say if is a very poor relation to Disney in the USA. One last comment, everyone seemed to be smoking in all areas and as it was so busy it felt very claustrophic and ash was flying everywhere and I was worried about me daughter who was in the pushchair!!! There were designated smoking areas but these weren't enforced and it was a free for all. Despite all this my son really enjoyed it which was the min point of the holiday but as for me its never again!!!

We were at the Santa Fe Hotel for 2 nights which were the worst experiance that we ever had. It felt like you were living in the Geto ! There was no heat , 1 2 roll of toilet paper in the bathroom every day. Furniture looked like is was bought at a 2nd hand shop. There is no Air condition which they do advertise in there adds, but no heat either . It also looked like it was old and shot. The key system did not work right and whenI went to get another key ,that did not work at all. When I took it back and was discusted the manager went back to my room with a master key and gave me 2 more new ones and said that they must update the hotel . The parks are very clean and fun , up to Disney standards. The hotel was lousey and dirty . Whe you pay about $ 200.00 a night to stay in a hotel you don't expect this kind of treatment . I have stayed at Disney in the states about 10 times and was always satisfied above my expectation. On a scale of 1 to 10 our experiance is 1. Stayed there 10 20 and 10 21 name is James Clements

We took our 4 year old Daughter for her Birthday 21 22 23 October. Caught train from Ashford and was very a simple and relaxed way to travel. Got off train at the park and got rid of luggage which was transferred straight to our Disney Hotel. Entered park about 2pm and It was raining when we got there so queues were at a mimimum and we managed to do quite a lot of rides in the 5 hours we had in the park. Tried to book an evening meal at City Hall but the computer system had gone down so we were told to do it at our hotel when we checked in. Checked in our hotel (Newport Bay) fairly quickly but were told that the earliest we could have a table for dinner was 8.45pm! We told them we needed to eat earlier as our Daughter was really tired and they found us a table at the Sequoia Lodge Hotel. We wish we hadn't bothered as the food was terrible and struggled to find anything we liked. We had the pre paid vouchers which I would recommend as they do save a lot of money but maybe avoid buffet restaurants and stick to table service. The second day which was my Daughter's Birthday was a lot more relaxed. We got to breakfast for 7.30am (any later and you would be waiting for ages). The breakfast was basic but you could get toast and cereals so not too bad. There were characters in the reception area which was great as everyone queued and waited their turn, unlike in the park. We got to the park for about 8.30pm and did quite a few rides with no queues, although a lot of rides don't open until 10am. We managed to do most rides in the morning and even meet a few characters. We then went to Rainforrest Cafe for a special lunch and the place was more or less empty at 12.30. Food was really good but pricey, a two course meal for 2 adults and 1 child with drinks was 60 Euros. We then went to the Studios which is a lot quieter than the main park and we did a few rides and shows. Stitch LIve and Playhouse Disney were brilliant and my Daughter loved them. We had pre booked a Birthday Party with the characters which was well worth the money. We turned up to Luckey Nugget Saloon at 5pm and were seated in the middle section and helped ouselves to a selection of cakes, buns and sweets. There was more then enough for everyone and the staff kept replenishing them. There were a lot of really good characters present and they came to everyone's table in turn. There were certain parents that couldn't wait their turn and kept taking their children to other peoples tables which was really annoying. We waited until the end when most people had left and my Daughter had the characters mostly to herself and even danced on stage with Mickey. We made the mistake to going to McDonalds at 7pm when the park closed and my husband queued to be served for nearly an hour. The meal cost 16 Euros so if you are on a budget this is a good place to eat, just not at 7pm!The final day was a Friday and a Halloween Special day when the park stayed open until midnight. We missed breakfast as we were so tired but still got to the park for 9am. When we walked in the park we knew it was going to be one of those days! It was much busier then the other two days and the queues for rides were massive already. Luckily there was only 3 rides we hadn't managed to do the other two days so we aimed to get them done. My Daughter wanted to go back on Pirates of the Caribean ride as that was one of her favourites, but when we got there were informed it had broken down. We went to the Snow White ride and queued for 30 minutes and then were told that was out of order. We also queued for Cassey Junior for 30 minutes and got to the front of queue when that also broke down. We wandered around a bit as all the queues were huge and decided to try and meet the Princess near the castle. We stood for 30 minutes waiting for her to get round to us but all the French and German people just pushed in which is one of the biggest complaints about the park. In the afternoon we went back to the studios and did a few more shows and chilled out for a bit, it was still a lot quieter than the main park.By 6pm I was really looking forward to coming home and the magic had definately gone for me, I would hate to be at the park in the summer holidays it must be chaos!Our hotel was basic and would have been a lovely hotel 15 years ago, it was mainly clean but looked like it hadn't changed since it had opened. It was convenient and functional but that was about all. The park was a lot smaller then I expected and and can't be compared to Florida. My Daughter loved meeting the characters, but rude foreign people spoiled it for her by pushing and shoving! The shows and parades were brilliant, but the food is mostly terrible and so overpriced. Go to the train station shop where everything is a lot cheaper and take a bottle of orange squash with you and fill up water bottles at the water fountains, it saved us such a lot of money! I am glad we went but would save the extra to go to Florida next time.

Just returned from 6 days 5 nights staying at the Hotel Cheyenne. Its the second time we've stayed there and this time took advantage of the Disney Dining Plan   as did a lot of other people who were seen clutching their vouchers.Hotel was just as good as the previous visit except husband got suspected food poisoning! He spent one whole day in bed and felt a bit fragile for the rest of the break. But he put on a brave face.As we were staying for so long we could take our time visiting the parks. Guests staying at the Disney hotels and selected hotels in the area are allowed into the main park 2 hours earlier   but not all the rides are open but it was great not having to queue.Fast pass tickets are a must especially if you are there on a Saturday. We attempted to go on Big Thunder Mountain just after the park had opened that day at 10 and the queuing time was already 70 minutes!!!The new rides in the Studio Park were enjoyed by my family. I hated Crush's Coaster (but then i hate rollercoasters) and had my eyes shut most of the time. Tower of Terror was also a favourite of my 11 year old.Everything is so expensive in the parks. A soft drink will set you back 2.50E and a child's dressing up costume 45E! We always made sure we had plenty of snacks and a bottle of water but did dine at Bella Notte (near Its a Small World), lovely pizzas and not as busy as some of the other restaurants and Restaurant en Coulisse in the Studios (that particular day it was freezing and i just wanted to go anywhere indoors that i could warm up in   food ok). Had planned on going into Paris to see the sights but due to husband feeling yuck, didn't bother. Did go to the Sea Life Centre (again) and Val d'Europe shopping centre. Hotel can organise a return shuttle service to the shopping centre for 5E adult and 2E child. I think we may just eat beans on toast for the next year and go to Florida next October. Want some warm weather for my hols.CheersLara

I have been visiting Disneyland Paris on a regular basis since it opened in 1992 as EuroDisney, and have written separate reviews of Disneyland Paris resort in general, The Studios Park, the Disney Village, Newport Bay Club hotel, and Sequoia Lodge hotel. This review is of the Magic Kingdom park only.I last visited in August 09, for 5 days, and noticed some changes. Disney are obviously feeling the pinch of the recession, as although the parks were very busy, the parades were shorter with fewer Cast Members  dancers between each float, and there seemed to be fewer CM's around the park in general. Also the fireworks were not as impressive as we have seen in the past, which is a shame. Shows had fewer performances, and some not every day. That said, we still had a great time, and will keep going back. The park is just a short walk from the railway station and shuttle bus stops, and the Disneyland Hotel is built over the entrance. You have to go through security first. Officially, food and drink is not to be brought into the parks, but they allow some drinks and snacks within reason. (Absolutely no alcohol) There are drinking water fountains in the park, usually near the restrooms. Smoking is permitted in designated areas only.You need to pick up 2 leaflets on your way in  the Park Guide, and the Programme, which gives information and times of shows and parades, and where to meet Disney Characters in the park. They are printed in several languages. You can also pick them up at City Hall inside the park. You pass under the Railroad Station to TOWN SQUARE, with the bandstand in the middle. The lockers under the station have not been in operation since they were closed for security reasons. Bags can be left at Guest Storage for a fee. Most of the services are in Town Square, and Characters arrive at certain times. Pushchair  stroller  wheelchair rental is to the right, and you can now pay a refundable deposit to take them out of the parks to walk to the hotels. The Railroad train goes around the perimeter of the park, stopping at each of the 4 lands.MAIN STREET leads straight from Town Square, to CENTRAL PLAZA and Sleeping Beauty's Castle. You can ride on a vintage vehicle down Main Street, past the shops, restaurants and cafes. A covered arcade runs down each side of Main Street, which is handy for avoiding the crowds. There is a Good Morning Main Street Parade at 10.15 each morning. Walt's restaurant is very good, and has good views of Main Street from the upstairs windows. Plaza Gardens Restaurant has buffet meals, and a Character Tea 3pm  5.30pm. Recommend booking in advance. In front of the castle is a circular stage where you can see a show with Mickey and friends at set times. From here, Frontierland and Adventureland are to the left, Discoveryland is to the right, and Fantasyland is behind the castle.FANTASYLAND is primarily for younger children, but anyone can go on the rides. You can get here by walking through the castle doorway, and out the other side. Inside the castle you can climb stairs to the gallery, where the story of Sleeping Beauty is told in tapestries and stained glass windows. Look for the cave under the castle, where you can see the dragon!This is the busiest Land. Many of the major rides in the park have a fastpass facility, and the machines are situated near the rides. You put your park tickets into the machine one by one, and get 1 ticket per person with a time slot to come back and ride later. Check the small print as it tells you when you can get another one  it may be before your ride time, so you can get FP's for another ride.PETER PAN ride is busy. Get a FP then go on DUMBO ride, as this does not have FP. SNOW WHITE, and PINOCCHIO are similar indoor rides where you sit in carts. They can be a bit scary for small children though. LANCELOTS CAROUSEL has 86 horses. MAD HATTERS TEACUPS  you turn a wheel to choose how fast you want to spin( or not).ALICE'S LABYRINTH  Alice in Wonderland maze, with jumping water drops and the Queen of Hearts castle. IT'S A SMALL WORLD  a boat ride with 281 costumed dolls of different countries,singing the Small World song, themed on the unity of mankind. The queue moves quite quickly and this ride is better than the one in Florida, IMO. LE PAYS DE CONTES DE FEES  canal boat ride, with miniature scenes from fairy tales. CASEY JUNIOR TRAIN  small coaster circus train from Dumbo, which goes around the canal boats.Auberge de Cendrillon is a restaurant in Fantasyland where you can meet the Disney Princes and Princesses. Quite expensive, booking essential.DISCOVERYLANDSPACE MOUNTAIN  This is a roller coaster in the dark, minimum height 1m40. Fastpass available.MYSTERIES OF NAUTILUS  Captain Nemo's submarine.HONEY I SHRUNK THE AUDIENCE  3D cinema theatre show.BUZZ LIGHTYEAR LASER BLAST  very popular, get a Fastpass for this ride. Sit in moving cars firing laser guns at martians to score points.STAR TOURS  simulator ride based on Star Wars film. Fastpass available.ORBITRON  like the Dumbo ride, but with spaceships. Quite high!AUTOPIA  drive cars on a track. Very popular, no fastpass available. People start queueing for this early. 2 persons per car, so adult can go with child.VIDEOPOLIS  large theatre with stage, and fast food restaurant. Have had shows here in the past, but in August 09 were only showing Disney cartoons on a giant screen. You can watch these while you eat.ADVENTURELANDPIRATES OF THE CARIBBEAN  no FP but the queue moves quite quickly, inside cave tunnels. Choose a quiet time if you are claustrophobic so you can walk straight through. Ride in a boat, with two small drops during the ride. Better than the one in Florida IMO. There is a restaurant inside the ride called the Blue Lagoon, where you can eat and watch the boats.ADVENTURE ISLE  rope suspension bridge over a waterfall, ( traditional bridge as well), caves, Swiss Family Robinson Tree House. Nice to do this at night when the lights are on, and not so busy.INDIANA JONES   TEMPLE OF PERIL  Runaway mine cart roller coaster based on the film. First 360 loop in Disney history. Went forwards when first built, then changed to backwards, now forwards again at present.There is a good buffet restaurant in Adventureland called Agrabah, with a North African  Aladdin theme.FRONTIERLANDBIG THUNDER MOUNTAIN  busiest ride here. FP available. Mine train that hurtles at high speed around and through a mountain. Pitch dark at times. Small children can go on this if they are brave enough! Better than the one in Florida IMO. Also good to ride this in the dark, and quieter when the parade is on. In August last ride entry was 11pm. We got on at the last minute with no queue. Get a FP then go toPHANTOM MANOR  haunted house with a difference. Sit in a 'doom buggy' to go round the house. May scare some small children. No FP but queue moves quite quickly.RIVERBOAT LANDING  Paddle steamers go round Thunder Mountain,and past Phantom Manor, playing peaceful music. POCAHONTAS INDIAN VILLAGE  Children's playground. Good view of Thunder Mountain from here.CHAPARRAL STAGE  shows vary from season to season. See Programme. This was 'Goofy's Summer Camp' in August, and is the theatre for Mickeys Winter Wonderland ice skating show during the Christmas celebrations.There used to be animals at Cottonwood Creek Ranch, but they were removed during the Foot and Mouth epidemic.The Lucky Nugget Saloon Character buffet lunch is very popular. Recommend booking in advance for this.PARADESCheck the Programme for times. In August the Once Upon A Dream parade was at 7.15pm and the Fantillusion Electrical parade was at 10.30pm , followed by the fireworks. Fantillusion and fireworks are not on all year round, so check before you book if this is important to you. People start to get their places an hour before, for the best views. Look at the parade route on the map, and try to be on an outer kerb so you see the floats coming towards and past you easily. We usually sit on the left side of Central Plaza, or at Town Square.There are special reserved areas for people in wheelchairs, so ask a CM to show you if this applies.DLP Fastpasses are sold on ebay, but you take a chance that they may be fakes.Useful sites are www.dlpfoodguide.com and www.dlrpmagic.comIf you have any questions, send me a message or ask on the Marne La Vallee Disney forum.

Our Trip to Disneyland Paris was truly a magical one. The Park is well done, the energy from the castmembers was great! The best new ride was the Crush Coaster! It's a blend of Space Mountain with Finding Nemo! The castles is beautiful and there's even a dragon under the castle! Thunder Mountain is cool, going underneath the River! Making memories there is easy!

if you haven't been to Orlando , then great, ignorance is bliss. Many people compare the two despite them not being a like for like setup.there are two parks adjacent to each other ( the train station in at the main entrance, and disney village is there too meaning that everything is within walking distance, for adults.As with other reviews, you are held to ransom with food, everything is overpriced and dont expect to pay anything less than 10 Euros for even a snack. If you are staying at a Disney Hotel and are family, be sure to opt for the Dining plan, during our visit kids ate free, which is a substantial savingWe visited off peak, and were better off for it ....bad weather, during school   no queues, good weather, holidays  Queues... appreciate that you cant have it both ways and you will be fine.This meant that even without extra magic hours the MAXIMUM we waited for ride was 5 10 minutes ( even without a Fastpass). As such although booked for 2 full days, we ended up completing both parks in one day, and re did the best bits on the second.

Didn't stay at the resort, just went for the day when on a 4 day Honeymoon in Paris. If you have a ParisVisite travel pass, you get 20% of the entrance fee for a 1 day 2 park pass, so cost us 50 euros each to get in. Went on pretty much all the rides (excluding the little kids stuff) and Space Mountain was the best (went on 3 times!). Tower of Terror is also very good, and Buzz Lightyear is good fun (even for a 28 year old!). Avoided eating there, by taking baguettes with us, and glad we did, menus in the park all looked expensive and not half as good as most little Parisian restaurants. Train from centre of Paris takes about 40 mins and literally takes you to the front door.Have been to Disney in Florida a couple of times, and it is far better, but this was still good fun.

Stayed in Disney for 5 nights from 23rd to 28th September. Stayed in the Cheyanne hotel.The hotel was great, themed around the 'west', the only thing missing was Clint Eastwood! Every thing about it was like a film set.The rooms were basic but clean and comfortable. As indicated in other reviews breakfast can be a bit of a battle, the need to find a table and make your way through the crowds to get your brekkie, but the brekkie was nice, the cereals were branded and the rolls and croissants were fresh.The parks were great and my two children absolutely loved it,( aged 4 and 8) along with myself and wife.Park staff were generally friendly and helpful, and there is plenty of things to keep you occupied. Getting photes and autographs from the characters is generally easy but on times it can be difficult as characters walk around the parks in the day but have limited time to spend with you.It is very expensive to eat and drink in the Disney parks. My top tip would be to take food from breakfast to have for lunch and if you can take drinks and snacks with you to supplement this. there were rumours that picnics would not be allowed, however all bags are searched on the way in and even with my rucksack overflowing with food this was not a problem.We drove down via Eurotunnel, so we had the car to carry this stuff. We took water, crisps, biscuits etc.In the evenings you need to eat in the Disney Village, unless you go out of the parks and find some where else, which in my reckoning would be quite a few miles away, because on my way in and out I could not see any where.Plenty of themed restaurants to eat in and all priced in line with one another. Main course start at apprx 14 euro rising to 25 euro, kids meals are approx 12 euro. If you like a lager with your meal expect to pay between 6.50 and 7.50 euro for 1 2 ltre.Would recommend the 'Rainforest cafe' this is themed as the name suggest around the rainforest with animals that come alive! and 'Mickeys cafe' where the characters visit and walk around the tables so that photos and autographs can be obtained.Over all the holiday was fab but very tiring. My top tip would be to stay away from the weekend as these get very busy and hence the cues are longer. We stayed from Wednesday to Monday, so we covered alot of the parks on Thursday and Friday meaning that come the weekend we could take a more leisurly pace to things.Back to the travelling, I had never drove in Europe before but the trip was reasonably striaght forward. Do not be put off by the trip, the Eurotunnel was straight forward, 35mins from Folkstone to Calais, then in France approx 3.5 to 4 hours drive depending on the number of stops you make. Most of the trip was on motorways so was straight forward and the motor way was reasonably quiet in both directions, but gets busier the closer you get to Paris, and it is then that you just need to take your time as you make your way through the motor way junctions. If you can obtain a Sat nav this will help, I borrowed one and to be honest it took us from door to door, if you cant and you go 'oldschool' you just need to plan your route. The route is straight forward though.Tolls were apprx 20 euro and you need to pay this in both directions. I travelled from Cardiff and the total round trip was 902 miles. Travelling down we stayed in Folkstone overnight prior to Eurotunnel, this broke the journey up, hoever coming back we did the trip in one, we left the hotel and midday and got home at 11 pm, this included 1hr delay at Eurotunnel.I hope this is useful to you.

We have just got back from a long weekend 3 nights, 4 days at Disneyland Paris (Fri Mon). We all had great fun and really enjoyed it. We have been to Disneyland in Florida before and whilst Florida is much bigger this is still great fun, well worth a visit and my 6 year old son had a ball!We stayed at the Disney New York Hotel which is a 4 star and great location right next to the Disney Village and both parks (5 10 min walk). It is not the cheapest but if you wait for the offers to be released we saved 550 GBP on our booking and our child went free.If you book a Disney hotel you get Extra Magic time (2 hours before the parks open). This is the best time to go on the rides which normally have large queues. We managed to get round both parks and all the rides in 3.5 days and we never stayed in either one any later than 5pm.I would highly recommend the Half Board Dining Packages that you buy in advance they are great value, you save lots of money and you can use the coupons in most of the restaurants in the parks and village.We travlled by Euro Tunnel, whilst the Euro tunnel is great and very quick trying to find Disneyland Paris once you disembark at Calais is a nightmare! The Map Disney provide is very basic and there was not one sign for Disney until 1 mile before the entrance! Thank god we had a sat nav even though she did seem to take us the longest route possible! We will def be booking for next year and this time Via Euro Star!

Once again I`m back from here as I have been going every year for 3 years. If I lived in London I`d be there weekly! I LOVE it.The park is CLEAN, BEAUTIFUL, ENCHANTING and has PLENTY of things to do! All the rides are fab especially Nemo but unfortunately this is the one ride that has queues lasting over an hour on peak seasons! but I didnt queue for more than 20 minutes long at any other ride and fastpass is there for busier days anyway! the parades were great but to be honest we only watched one on our last day because we were to busy!I am really sad and a little annoyed that there are no shows such as Tarzan and Lion King anymore its silly! however I actually did enjoy chilling and watching Mickey cartoons at the videopolis.The park is stunning at night whith all the lights and If you miss this then you have missed half the magic! The people moaning about the COSTS of food and drink here amongst other things should really do their homework before visiting this place! Paris in general is expensive so a main attraction within it is not going to be any cheaper! If you cant afford to spend 12 euro`s on just a hotdog then...DONT GO! I know the costs are atrocious but prepare for this way in advance! we took the half board premium option when staying over (this isnt Alton Towers so day trips I wouldnt reccommend unless you had good organizational skills) and saved hundreds!!

Having just returned from a 4 day stay here I feel the need to voice my concerns about the character meet and greets that are all around the park.We visited with our 3 and a half year old grandaughter who needless to say was very excited about meeting her favourite characters. Having waited patiently, or as patiently as a 3 year old can!  we were delighted when Donald, Minnie, Goofy and Chip n Dale all appeared after the Minnie parade and sttod in various places for the children to meet them. And this is where the mayhem started! Whilst each character had a 'minder' with them it was just a free for all and all the little ones, our grandaughter included, was shoved and pushed by older children and parents alike! There was no attempt by the 'minders' to stop this and resulted in many tears from the younger ones. The characters themselves made no attempt either to calm the situation and simply walked away after a few minutes leaving some very upset children and parents!We have been going to Disney both in Paris and Florida for many years and whilst I have never seen such disorganisation in Florida it has been more apparent in Paris on our last couple of visits. I feel it is such a shame that this is being allowed to happen as this is one of the main things children want to do, meet their favourite characters, but if it is going to be marred by scenes such as we saw then Disney need to address this and sooner rather than later. I could see things getting out of hand and if the so called 'minders' can't deal with it then they need to re think how they organise such meet and greets.

I have just come back from Disney and was not impressed. Although me and my boyfriend have both been to Disney in Florida  you cannot compare whatsoever to Disney in Paris. In Paris everything is smaller, and there are not enough rides for ages 18 25. For the younger ages it is perfect to see the characters, but for people our age (21) it is not worth going.Everything is aged, and it looks like some rides have not been touched since it opened. MGM Studios is tiny, and the two main rides are only Terror Tower and Aerosmith ride. And that is basically it there. We stayed at Hotel New York 2nd 5th sept. We got to the park at 4pm on Wednesday and I was pleasantly suprised that it was as busy as I'd expected it to be (managed to walk straight on to Phantom Manor   v.good ride). We all enjoyed the parades, didn't experience any pushing or shoving and mangaed to get a good view . We made use of the extra magic hours on Thursday & Friday and had little or no wait for most rides. Even upto lunchtime the longest we had to wait was 30 mins for Peter Pan (also v.good). BUT.... our train home wasn't til late on the Saturday, and so we quite a few hours to kill in between checking out of hotel and going to the train station, and the parks were absolutely crammed by 10am! Have to say that I found the crowds unbearable on that day, the minimum waiting time for most rides was 60 mins, which is not my idea of a fun day.... my sons favourite ride was Pirates of carribbean, so at 10am we made a mad dash and managed to get on with only a 5 min wait, but by the time we'd finished the ride the wait time was already at 15 mins. Luckily we then discovered Videpolis, which is a fantastic refuge away from the crowds. Kids loved watching the cartoons. Spent half a day at the studios, which I'm afraid I didn't rate at all. Animagique was enjoyable, Stunt show ok (although my 4yr old managed to sleep through it...), Tram tour terrible, and queue for Crush's coaster was 60 mins before it even opened!! We left park to eat in disney village. Loved Rainforest Cafe, v.expensive but good size portions, fantastic scenery and v.friendly staff. Also ate in annettes diner, again v.friendly staff but food was not good. Would visit again, but would make sure that the stay didn't include any weekend days. Staff in parks very friendly. Also agree with a lot of other reviews about the smoking in the parks (especially cigars!), there were lots of allocated smoking places but people just ignored this and walked around everywhere smoking. The only litter visible in the parks were ciggarette buts!! Think there were just too many for the cast members to clean away quickly enough.

HiI had been to Disneyland Paris about 10 years ago and also to other parks in the States and Japan even longer ago. We visited on a saturday in September and travelled by car.Getting there Car parkA few miles before the park there was lots of traffic and it took some time to get to the car park entrance. DisneyLand Park Paris has such a great atmosphere about it. We have been 4 times each time a 4 day and 3 nights holiday. The castle is obviously a top sight spot to see. We went on the Eurostar to DisneyLand and on our last time we stayed at Santa Fe. As you get off the train, we collected our luggage and got out of the station, we then got a shuttle bus when we stayed at Cheyenne and Santa Fe. When we stayed at Newport Bay Hotel we walked through Disney Village to get there but I think you can get a shuttle for there too. It was our first time so we didn't realise. You will see Disney Village straight away because there is a huge Las Vegas style sign with it written on. On our third time we stayed at the DisneyLand Hotel and with that, when you come out of the station turn right as if you are going into the park and there it is. It looks like a big pink palace. So when we put our luggage away we headed toward the park and at first you have to give your tickets to some staff and they will let you through. The first time we went it was September so there was no big occasion really. The second time was December so all the Christmas decorations were up... lovely. The third time it was just November and the fourth time it was Hallowe'en and there were pumpkins and orange spots on the floor. It was really fun. Then when they have checked your ticket you walk into Main Street USA. As you walk in you can see straight ahead of you the big pink castle. As you walk down Main Street USA there are lots of souvenir shops and cafes. There is one called Walt's where you can have character meals where when you have your meal, the characters come round and see you.... a good time for taking photos. We had a character breakfast and it was lovely but you have to book in advance. Then when you get to the corner on your left there is a diner style place where they do the best hot dogs... they are huge but gorgeous. Then opposite that there is a place where they do gorgeous cappucinos and there is also a Victorian style cafe where they also do character teas there. Next is the 4 themed areas of the park. First of all, there is Fantasy Land, good for little kids wanting to see princesses and most of the characters are round here. There are a few attractions such as Alice's Curious Labyrinth which is a giant maze, Blanche Neige et les Sept Nains which is a ride based on the story of Snow White, Casey Junior which is a little train   kind of a like a mini rollercoaster, Dumbo the Flying Elephant which are dodgems in th style of Dumbo, It's A Small World one of my favourite rides which is a water ride and as you are going round there are dolls from all different counties dressed in their style outfit, Sleeping Beauty's Gallery which is actually inside the castle which are just stained glass windows telling the story of Sleeping Beauty and there are also a few shops inside the castle, Dragon's Lair is round the back of the castle and is a giant model of the dragon with smoke and everything, then there is a carousel a Pinocchio ride, tea cups and peter pans flight which is a suspended ride where you sit in a seat the shape of a boat. In all four areas of the park there is also a little train which can take you from for example Fantasy Land to Frontier Land.Next are restaurants in Fantasy Land there is a Cinderellas restaurant where all the princesses come round and greet you and you get a 3 course meal and plenty more.Next is Frontier Land, my favourite area, my favourite ride is Big Thunder Mountain, this is set in like a runaway train in the middle of Rivers of America, beware though the lines can get long. Next is Phantom Manor, this is a haunted house where the movie Haunted Mansion came from this, it's not too scary, it's a slow moving car ride through the haunted house, where you're told the story of the bride and I won't say anymore. There are lots more things to do here too.Next is Adventure Land. This is kind of like a pirate themed area. There is Indiana Jones and The Temple of Peril rollercoaster.. never been on it but looks brilliant. Pirates of the Caribbean which comes from the movie. Lots more others.Next is Discovery Land. Buzz Lightyear Laser Blast is good for little boys even though I enjoyed it. You get a laser gun when you sit in a 2 seater carriage and have to shoot at targets and then try and beat the person sat next to you. Then there is the big scary ride of Space Mountain and that IS SCARY. Then there is a 4D cinema experience in Honey I Shrunk The Audience! That was good.Next is Walt Disney Studios.. I like this area too. Here is Animagique where it is all to do with Art and you can learn to draw Mickey Mouse by a professional. Also Crush's Coaster which is a not too scary ride my little sister went on it and she was 9. Cinemagique is amazing but I won't say loads because I will give it away. Rock 'n' Rollercoaster is good and a big and scary rollercoaster with lots of twists and turns.Then I will come to the hotels....First, DisneyLand Hotel, the most expensive but the most rewarding. First of all it has a view over the park. More of the characters come and see you. The lobby is amazing with a grand staircase and huge chandelier. The rooms are lovely and very clean as they are with most hotels at Disney actually.Then there is Disney's Hotel New York.. I have never stayed at this one but really want to. It is obviously a New York themed hotel and there is an ice rink outside it in winter.Then there is Newport Bay Hotel, which is a boat themed hotel and this is good but might be boring for children. There is a golf course behind it too.Then there is Disney's Sequoia Lodge which is a woodland style hotel.Then there is Cheyenne Hotel. This is cowboy themed we stayed in the block named Billy The Kid. My favourite hotel.Disney's Hotel Santa Fe is styled like America's South West. I didnt like this hotel at all. The rooms were OK but the food was awful but the breakfast was OK.Next Disney Village, Buffalo Bills Wild West Show is an all night cowboy show with a meal included and it is good. The little kids will enjoy it with stunts and tricks.Also, Hurricanes Nightclub is good for young adults and sometimes there is a hot air balloon you can have rides in. There are plenty of restaurants here such as Cafe Mickey, King Ludwigs Castle, Planet Hollywood and my personal two favourites Annette's Diner and Rainforest Cafe there is plenty more too. Obviously you can't enjoy the experience and really know what I am talking about until you' ve been and you can find out more at the website! PS Definitely take your camera...

Just returned from a 4 day break at DLP. Had previously visited Floria 9 years ago, so knew roughly what to expect, however slightly nervous after some reviews on this site. All i can say, is dont believe the negative comments. We are a family of 5 (3 children   6 year old twins and a 4 year old). We had a great time. Once you get in the park, you would think you were in America. Very clean, staff friendly (speak good english). I was expecting it to be very expensive, and although it wasnt cheap, we didnt find it too bad. There are meal deals everywhere, especially for the kids, noteably Pizzeria Bella Notte in Fantasyland where kids get drink, mickey mouse shaped pizza and an ice cream for under 5 euro. Drinks, pop corn etc are around 3 euro's. Not cheap as i say, but equilivent to cinema prices in the UK.The only negative aspect was for us is that the park closes at 19:00 now. We arrived at 18:00 expecting to stay late for fireworks etc, but found everyone coming out. We therefore planned our visit by arriving around 09:00 to take advantage of the early opening hours (you can get in at 08:00 if you stay at Disney Hotel). Note some sections of the park dont open until 10:00. However you can get on rides such as Peter Pan, Star Wars, Buzz etc early with no queues (5 mins max).Our trip was planned for the first week in September to avoid the French School hols (mid week too). It seemed to work as i was expecting it to be much busier. Most of the afternoons, the queues were 5 mins for Space Mountain, Star Wars, Rock n Roll Roller Coaster. Make use of the Fast Pass for Thunder Mountain (great ride) and Peter Pan (better for younger kids). Note, you can only have one fast pass ticket at a time. Our older twins, who turned 6 last week, got on every ride apart from Space Mountain, so i didnt think the height restriction caused an issue. The Studio park is also very good. The 'Crush' ride (based on Nemo) is good for the kids, although this is the only ride where 5 of us couldnt get in the same car. On the other rides 3 kids can squeeze into the seats. Note, there is no fast pass on crush, so as soon as you get into the Studio park, head straight for it.The kids got their photos will all of the characters. the longest we queued was 30 mins for Woody. Mickey and Minney turned up at various points, so had plenty of photo opportunities. Got a good view of the parade (17:00), no queuing for that. Just walked up at 16:55 and found a available space.We stayed in the Hotel L'Elysee which was ideal. Free bus every 15 mins and hotel had joining rooms which made it a straight choice between L'Elysee and Explorers. Huge Supermarket next to hotel so you can buy drinks, water, snacks and take them into the parks.Great trip overall. Would highly recommend it for anyone with young children. No 9 hr flight to the US to deal with. Travelled with Easy jet and hired a private taxi to hotel. Well worth it!

instead of keeping my online tickets on the 81 2 X 11 sheet with all my other stuff, i am cutting it out and putting it my wallet from now on. you guys should learn from my mistake and do this too! ok, well the disneyland park was not bad. we went to  it's a small world . the animatronics felt very cheap. and space mountain was very jerky and uncomfortable. then we went to walt disney studios, which was awesome! tower of terror was the best ride ever! the armagedden and stunt show spectacular were A  and i believe they are exclusive attractions to DLP as i have never seen them in cali or FL. the food was not as bad as everyone describes. the coke is 2.50 euros, which is cheap compared to the 4.50 euro drink at the effel tower. the disney meal was either a cheeseburger or chicken with fries and you got a dessert like chocolate cake or chocolate brioche and a drink for like 15 20 euros. can't remember exactly but you get a LOT of food. the workers were nice. i wasn't put off by anyone in particular. i didn't leave with any negative image of any of the workers. they were ok, nothing to complain about. bathroom were also ok. don't remember being totally grossed out. there was an attendant in there and also plenty of stalls to accommodate. the parades were ok too. quality is lower than orlando of course but still fun. the best part was sounvenier shopping. getting all the disneyland paris stuff with mickey and the effel tower. now here's the REAL reason why i came to DLP   lol!overall, it was one of the highlights of my trip to paris. a nice break from all the touristy sites of central paris. it was nice to visit once but i don't think i would go again. definitely go to orlando if you have the disney bug. i would recommend it if you are a disney fan and want to visit all the disneyland parks in the world.

Wonderful experience and I'm old and went alone. But the lttle kid in all of us wants to go to Disneyland and Paris is no disappointment. I bought a day pass for both Disneyland and the Disney Studios but didn't have time to do all of Disneyland in the 1 day, let alone go to the Studios. You'd need at least 2 days if not 3 to really see everything. It's very important to plan your trip ahead. Research which rides you want to go on and which Land they are in. All this is available on the internet BEFORE you go. Get there by, or before 9am to be at the front of the queue at the gates. Pre purchase your ticket. They open park gates a 9.30. Run to whichever Land you've decided you want to see first. You'll then be at the front of the queue when they open these at 10. Then run to whichever ride you want most. I did this and the wait for one of the most popular rides was only 10 minutes (kids run faster than me). An hour later it was 40 minutes, by early afternoon it was close to 90 minutes. Magic Mountain wait was 2 1 2 hours by 4pm. So be organised, be prepared, be quick or you'll spend the whole day in queues. Take rides early in day or evening after tour bus crowds have left. Even food, though readily available requires standing in a long queue. You can take food and drink into the park, suggest you do if only to save time. Do you want to queue for rides AND food. Be prepared to spend a lot on souvenirs, there are so many things you have to have. There is a spectacular Chistmas shop. You can buy photos of yourself on rides but you have to buy TWO copies, so if travelling alone, go to the photo booth with the person who sat next to you, that way you can each have a copy and split the 20 Euro cost. If buying t shirts or clothes, kids sizes are much cheaper. I'm told this is because childrens clothes incur no VAT (GST) in Europe. Don't know if this is right but they certainly were a lot cheaper than adult clothes. So if you are petit like me, you can buy a girls size 14 (XL) at half the price of equivalent size in Ladies. I did this all over Europe. Saved a fortune on T shirts, but you have to be slim. Toilets are scarce, and crowded (more queues) so again plan ahead! I found they were also bit  whiffy  (smelly) by early afternoon, but that's because people dump baby diapers and the toilets are not cleaned regularly. So spare a thought for others and take sealable bags if you have a baby. Smelly diapers are sickening especially after a few hours. Personally, and as a mother, I wouldn't take anyone under 3 years old to Disneyland. It's too long a day, too many crowds and they can't go on anything anyway. They'll also stop you from going on rides and enjoying your day, so if your hotel has a babysitting service, use it. But no matter how old you are, you'll have a ball at Disneyland Paris. It's a thrill even a 50.

I was allured by the invitation to have breakfast every morning with the Disney characters however there was no given number of how many Disney characters would appear at breakfast. My family, which included my brother, his wife and their 8month old daughter, myself and my 2 1 2 year old son arrived to the Disneyland Hotel (a four star rated hotel on the website) and we were perplexed as to where the valet service was. Directions for cars were not mark however when we figured out where to go we were pleasantly greeted by hotel staff both at the valet station and at reception. We allowed for the bell service to take our bags and were assured by the receptionist that our bags would be up to our room shortly. As we walked through the hotel filled with and overpowering scent of powder fresh, we made our way to the elevator that took us to the first floor which our room was located. The decor was beautiful, however upon inspection of the room, mold was noted to be in the corners of the bathtub, no refrigerator was available for people with infants who needed formula or stored breast milk. The  family room  that we booked, was supposed to be slightly larger and more suitable for, well, families was the same size as a regular room with two full size bed in a small room. Our baggage was missing for an hour before we finally called the front desk and reach someone who said they would bring our bags up. At that time we finally received our bags. We then made our way to dinner...this is when we noted a disclaimer. Dinner reservations are simply a requirement at the restaurants for dinner. The buffet at Inventions was mediocre. I've honestly had better at the Hilton in Austin, TX. We sat down to dinner and were excited to see Goofy who seemed to be making his way around each table. As he began to approach our table he turned his back towards the children and began to walk off to the restaurant kitchen leaving our children in the wind with no picture, autograph, not even a pat on the head. We began to get passed up by several of the characters through the night and we not only got heartbroken for the children, but frustrated as well. We asked the waiters if the characters appeared for breakfast in the same restaurant, as the website said you would enjoy your breakfasts every morning with Disney characters, the waiter said only two characters would be outside the restaurant for a certain amount of time. The price was not worth the food nor the experience. I paid 230 Euro dollars for 3 adults and 1 child to have a buffet dinner that you could get for 16 Dollars total on the Las Vegas strip. I really just wanted to make everyone eat until completely stuffed so we would get our money's worth.Breakfast in the morning was better than dinner. Although only one character would stand in front of the fireplace mantle at a time lines were formed so that people wouldn't get pushed back. The parks themselves are not comparable in size nor attractions to those of the parks in the US. We started our adventure on a rainy day and as such no Disney characters were in sight. We were given FastPass tickets that we could use for only one ride and were invalid at peak hours (from 1300 1600). Some workers looked as though they hated their job and treated guests at the park as though they hated their jobs. When my brother and I went to use our FastPass at 1610, the lady at the line said the tickets could not be used because it was past 1600. We were confused and mad. Walt Disney Studios was very small and this is actually were the children met the most characters. It only took approximately 3 4hours to walk around the park, see the attractions, and go on the rides that were worth going on. For lunch, we decided to make our way to Planet Hollywood since we needed some decent American food...yeah, that was not at all what we got. The spinach dip was disgustingly tasteless, the alfredo sauce had no taste or salt in it at all, the penne whatever my sister in law got was so awful she spit out her first bite and pawned it off on my poor brother. My fajitas were edible until I put quacamole on it. The quacamole tasted rotten. And the service...not only was our waiter rude to us in a sense that he always seemed like he had better things to do when he took our order he also failed to bring us water that we requested 3 times and almost forgot about the babies' food.Overall, my family and I were not impressed with the hotel, the parks, the staff, or the restaurants. This is not an experience I would recommend unless you really just have that much money to waste on over priced food and rude service and thoughtless, uncaring Disney characters.

We have just returned from a 4 night 5day break in Disneyland Paris ( 23rd Aug 09 to 27th Aug 09), Staying at the hotel New york New York.We traveled via Eurostar from St Pancras station which was fantastic with a 6 year old and a 3 month old baby, I was abit nervous about taking my 3 month old as I had e mailed the hotel many times regarding the facilities they had in the room but had no replys. So this is a review for those of you taking along a baby to Eurodisney.Eurostar: Was great, very convieniant. There are baby changing facilities onboard, very small cunbicle like an areoplane but serves its purpose. To warm a milk bottle I went to the carriage which served drinks and snacks and asked them for hot water to warm the milk up in, otherwise there is a microwave which you could ask them to warm the milk up in. . We stayed in Hotel New York New York because we had stayed there afew years ago and liked it. I had taken my mircowave sterliser with me, a bottle warmer and a travel kettle. HOWEVER do not do this because at reception they told me that they have there own strelisers, kettle and bottle warmers which they are happy for you to have a keep in your room throughout the duration of your stay!... Their sterliser worked great but I just used my own bottle warmer and kettle as I had brought them along with me anyway.It mey be worth taking your own bottle warmer as from memory I dont remember my bottles ( avent ones) fitting into their warmers but that was 3 4 years ago so it might be different now.In the park whenever we needed the milk warming we just went into any resturant and asked for hot water but most of them have a microwave. Changing nappies was done in the pushchair without any problems. There is a baby center in the magic kingdom park but i didnt feel the need to go there.Lastly make sure you take all nappies, wipes etc with you as it is very expensive to buy these things in the park and I used boiled Evian water ( low in sodium and recommended by health visitors when travelling abroad) to make the baby milk as you would do at home with boiling tap water.Hope this helps some of you, Please contact me should you need any further information. Many Thanks.

Just returned from a stay at the Newport Bay Hotel in the Disneyland Paris resort. Disney is wonderful, I love it. This was our second time in the Paris resort, we have also stayed at Florida a couple of years ago. There is no comparison really, Florida is bigger, better, more disney magic as the staff were all wonderfully friendly and over the top AAmerican which is great. Paris has a different atmosphere but still lovely. It is a lot smaller and the staff are not quite so friendly but the disney magic is still there for children and grown ups too. The Newport Bay Hotel is huge as they all are. Checking in and out was efficient enough, but the breakfast was crazy. The queues were massive even though you chose a certain time to be down there for. With the Disney Village only a 10 minute walk it seemed easier to walk there and call into Starbucks for a croissant and coffee. The room in the hotel was pretty basic but clean. The beds were comfortable and fresh, the only downside was the bathroom, it could have done with some new wallpaper and there was a little bit of mould in the tiles.All in all we had a lovely few days there. You really only need 3 or 4 maximum at the resort, whereas Florida you need a day for each different theme park, but it felt as though we'd had a break plus one hour flight time to me is better then nine hours in the air. One thing that I will say is that everything that you buy, whether it be food or gifts is incredibly expensive, we knew that it was expensive four years ago but this time we thought it was crazy expensive, but people still spend when you are there, it's part of the Disney fun. Would I reccommend it? Of course it's Disney!

The hotel we were staying in was average, although it was rated as a 4 star hotel. THe food was not good, thats why we decided to eat the second night out in a small town 20 km outside the parc. We should have done this the first evening as well.The rooms were ok, but what really bothered me was the fact that we had to pay for absolutely everything ; there was no minebar in the room and the price for water in the machines in the corridors was way too expensive. The little packages of coffee needed to be paid.But then again; you dont go to euro disney for the hotels of course.Restaurants in the park could work out expensive with long queues and all the food is fast food. SO if you are not a fan of fast food ; bring your own lunch,The rides themselves in the park although could have long queues at times their fairly well organised and move quickly, just a shame some rides are over with even quicker. There's something there for young and old and they do a family service too. There's small rides in boats like It's a small world, or rollercoasters like Space Mountain just depending on your likes and dislikes.There's plenty of shows to see at different times of the day but remember if you go in winter remember to wear your winter woollies to keep you warm as some of the shows are outside. At this time of year there's two parades one is of the Disney characters at about 4pm and the other at 7pm which is The light display where all the floats are lit up. The Disney Studios is the new addition to the park since last time I was here Make sure you don't miss the Studio Tour.

My fiancee and I just completed a trip to Disneyland Paris   we are big Disney fans and went to France for the sole purpose to visit this park and another local park. This was out first visit to this park and we were there from Wed. 8 19 through Sat. 8 22. I have been to the Florida, California and Tokyo Magic Kingdoms and this version was clearly the most beautiful of the bunch. The theming of this park is incredible and the Fantasyland in particular is magnificent. Although we were there in August, we did not find the queues to be too bad. We did have the VIP fastpass through the Castle Club at the Disneyland Hotel, but it seems that for the rides that did have long queues, fastpass could be utilized to it's potential with a wise strategy (getting there at opening, getting a fastpass for Big Thunder first thing, etc.). Even in the peak of the day, lines for Pirates of the Caribbean and Phantom Manor moved along nicely with times of 30 minutes or less. We loved the Disneyland Paris version of both of these rides, particularly Phantom Manor which takes on an entirely different storyline from the other versions. Everything seems to be done up a notch in this park   the Small World is beautiful and more colorful, the castle is amazing (complete with an awesome animatronic dragon living underneath of it), Big Thunder Mountain is built on an island so features a great underground tunnel at the starting and ending of the ride, etc., etc. I also loved the arcades built behind the stores on both sides of Main Street   what a great idea! This was a great route to utilize during parades, fireworks, etc. to avoid the mass of humanity on Main Street. We found that the cast members at this park were fantastic and just as friendly as other Disney parks. OK, now of course there are some negative remarks to be made for the park. Well, not necessarily negative but some things to be aware of: first, people are smoking everywhere in the park (queue lines, walkways, etc.). The park has designated smoking zones and I did see a cast member ask a guest to extinguish his cigarette on Main Street. However, so many people seem to smoke in Europe that trying to enforce the no smoking policy is like the police trying to enforce everyone going 55 mph on an interstate. It wasn't that big of a deal really, but annoying at times. Second, there is more line cutting that takes place in this park than in the US parks and they could do a better job of queue management. I can't say it is a French thing in particular, because we have seen plenty of line cutting at other parks and it is actually worse in the Spanish and Italian theme parks. I think Disney could help avoid the problem here by making some of the queue lines more narrow. Third, the fastpass system was very odd for the Indiana Jones rollercoaster (this thing is out of place here   it's like a NJ shore boardwalk rollercoaster dressed up with a little theming) as the fastpass line simply merged with the regular line with no attendant to control the merge point. This was also the case for Big Thunder at some times, but this might have been due to guests jumping over into the fastpass queue past the point where the FP ticket is checked. All of these things are minor annoyances considering the beauty and quality of attractions in this park. We had intended this trip for a one time visit so we could say 'been there done that', but we both agreed that we will definitely come back to visit this fine Disney park!

After all this years, Disneyland Paris has been stuck with a reputation of being Disney lite. Unloved by the French, frequented by the Brits but lacking the glamour and sheen of its American parents.This was our third visit to DLP. No visit to Paris is complete without a day trip to the park and our youngest had yet to visit. We have previously been to the original Disneyland in California as well as WDW in Orlando. DLP cannot rise to the heights of those parks despite the similar rides and in one or two cases having better rides such as Space Mountain.Its deficiencies are hard to overlook. The staff border on incompetence. There is no meeting and greeting, no Disney smiles (except one cast member who got into the spirit and realised that he works for the House of Mouse). The first ride we went to was Space Mountain, it had short waiting time. As we had a little one we did a parent swap which meant my wife stayed behind until I completed the ride. After I finished, did they let her on? No, every time my wife went up to them they kept shoving her away. We were in the parent swap segment and were just ignored as they let others on to the ride. This went on for 15 minutes. She would have been better of going to the normal line. It   s this kind of attitude that upsets visitors and gives the park a bad rep.Of course after all this years, its never going to get better because I am sure the management have knowledge of this but probably are not bothered to make improvements or correct these deficiencies.As we managed to make best use of Fast pass in Orlando, we tried the same trick here with mixed success. We waited for some rides, got on a few with a minimum of fuss, and went on several rides on FP but the FP wait times were rather long. Overall we did a good selection of attractions, enjoyed a fish and chips lunch although as expected it was expensive. Disappointingly the Haunted House broke as we waited to get on.We lined up for the daily parade. It was nice to see other adults realising that Disney is primarily for kids and making an effort that other children can get to the front or have a good vantage point. Also, the disabled section actually consisted of people who were entitled to be there in contrast with what I saw in Orlando last year. The parade itself was laughable. I already mentioned Disney staff failed to get in the spirit of things but the parade was so short. They filled in many of the characters strutting their stuff but it was just a few floats and it must have been Tigger   s day off as he was missing from the rest of the Pooh cast.Overall, its great for kids, good to go if you have never done Disney before but it could had been so much more, alas this park shall always be a lightweight and no amount of pixie dust will make a difference.
lots of walking..lots o ques..too many disney shops....over priced ...

Third visit this year and will probably be our last. Rides are showing signs of wear and tear and there was a distinct lack of characters compared to our last visit 5 years ago. They have added a couple of new attractions, hotel ride which we did think was very good and also Buzz lightyear which we considered to be very average. Did try several times to get on Crush but queuing time 2 hours so gave up on this one (no fast pass facilility). We felt rides needed updating and were overall disappointed with the park.

In general, with Disney, the brand is pretty consistent throughout the world. The same rides, similar food, clean cut staff and spotless facilities.Unfortunately, August 17, we were very disappointed to find the exception, Disneylad Paris. Even at 10 am, when the park had just opened, the bathrooms looked and smelled disgusting. It appeared that the bathrooms had not been cleaned since the day before. The condition persisted through the day, at other bathrooms. It wa so bad that we chose to use the train station bathrooms instead!Unacceptable.

Let's start by saying: you're better of avoiding a trip to this park in August. The queus are just too long (minimum 1 hour, up to 2 hours), the attractions break down regularly, the  fastpass  is a farce, because you can only use it twice on a day (given the times between the printing and use f the pass).The staff is friendly, but they have to obey so many bureaucratic rules, the organisation as a whole is very unfriendly. The Disneyland park scores  terrible  for me. It was the worst day for me of 2009 so far as I'm concerned.
