It's just a rip off.The second park (Disney Studios) is much better organised and has acceptable waiting times. This is mainly due to the high capacity of most shows   attractions. In this park you will enjoy your stay much better. You actually see a lot of things. The rollercoasters here are also much too crowded. The Nemo rollercoaster for instance had a 2 hour queue. Just skip it!This park scores  average .The combination of both parks scores poor for me. The management of Disney should work to improve this, this is not worthy of the Disney brand.

We (2 adults 2 kids) went Fri Sun in August, stayed in the Newport Bay Hotel. Hotel was OK family room a bit cramped. Basicaly a large  box  hotel with a fancy facade. The Park itself, well disappointing. Up to an hour and a half wair for some rides, fortunately hotel guests get in 2 hours early otherwise we wouldn't have bothered with most of them. Everything is very expensive to the point of rip off. You can't bring food drink in so you have to buy theirs. Example lunch   4 sandwiches, 4 bottles water 40 Euro.Two days is enough, during the last day the kids just wanted to go back to the hotel, boorish rude people pushing their way around the place I'd had enough too.My kids have been to Parc Asterix twice and would love to go back   they don't want to go back to Disney and that sort of says it all.

A great place for a short break! We booked our hotel nearby, in Marne la Vallee, only a 10 minutes drive away. Disneyland is very crowded during lunchtime. Large queues everywhere. Our tip: go as early als possible and make sure to plan the popular attractions with a fastpass. Lunch is cheaper outside Disney or bring your own lunch along and have a picnic in Disney. If you stay at a hotel outside Disney, and want to visit Disney more than 1 day, it is much cheaper to buy a annual passport. For 1 day, 1 ticket costs 62 euros. An annual passport costs 99 euros (expect parking ticket which costs 8 euros), with parking ticket included the annual passport costs 129 euros. We actually bought the annual passport and found out that we had also 10% off at all the restaurants in de park and shops!!We liked the attractions and fireworks in the end!!

Although we looked forward to spending 2 days at Disneyland, we were not completely satisfied at the end. Why? The big crowds in August obviously created long queues, mostly in the sun. Imagine spending 2 hrs in the queue, with minimum enthusiasm left when it's finally your turn to take a ride or see an attraction (unless there is a technical fault as has happened to us and we missed the climax of the attraction after spending 2 hrs in the queue!! And no one told us anything about the fault!!)

I went to Disney for a family break in AUGUST I think its best to put pro   s and con   s so pro   s first Great for kids Disney do things on a grand scale you can't argue that it was amazing visually lights, lights and more lights lots of friendly staff and very safe attractions.The rides were amazing and the shows were breathtaking (what else from Disney) The stunt show in the film park was just unbelievable and the haunted tower was the first ride ever to scare the hell out of me (and I like rides) the interactive rides were fast and fun and the whole thing was just so over the top it was great.The theme park next to it was just fantastic my kids spent most of the time completely speechless. ( no honestly) So how can there be consWell take a good set of walking boots it   s blooming huge the walk from the car park is 30 minutes and at the end of a 10 hour day that   s a long way. The lines on the rides are a pain so go for FAST PASS (this is only AM in the film studios) The foods prices are not even high they are on another planet, (completely not needed in my humble opinion) they make enough money on entry fees at 60 Euros a day average per person. I had three small pots of pasta and three drinks and a pizza you could get in ASDA for a pound and it cost the best part of 50 Euros (and that was a cheap one restaurant) We found a place in the Disney village doing chips (fries) for 3 Euros, a panines and chips for 8 Euros and water for 3 Euros, so you could eat for less (if you like chips and paninies) still 44 Euros for a meal for 4 that was better than an Asda pizza The Wild West show is over 250 Euros extra for a family of 4 Ice creams are between 2.50 and 4 Euros and water 4 Euros.Disney goods from any one of the tonnes of stores is like the food over priced.That   s it really for cons just the completely stupid food prices they feel they can rip you off .Disney ( at these prices) one of the richest companies in the world not really giving a damm about its customers in some respects. We took packed food in every day you are not meant to eat in the parks unless you have purchased it in the park but no one stops you. Just makes everythig a lot heavier to carry and you will walk you little legs off I assure you. But a good trip kids of all ages will love it best aimed at 6 plus though .

Father Christmas brought our boys (9 and 5 years) a 3 night trip to Disneyland Paris this year travelling by Eurostar in February. This is our second visit here but inbetween we have been to Disney World Flordia which is the real deal! Being from just outside London, the Eurostar was the obvious choice for travel and was quick and efficient arriving right at the gates of Disney. We left our luggage and headed straight for the parks. At this time of year we found that a few of the rides and many of restaurants were closed for general maintainance and it had lost its razzle after Christmas. As always theme parks are expensive to eat at but we had little choice when wanting a cuppa to warm us up. (about   7 for 2 bad vending type coffees!)After the day of travel and walking around the parks the boys were ready for an earlish night so we took the bus back to the hotel and collected our lugagge. On arrival at the Wild West we got stuck behind a coach party of kids checking in so it took a while, but this was just bad timing. We ate at the buffet restaurant at the Wild West which was okay (quantity rather than quantity) and priced as you would expect (About   65 for all of us including a soft drink each) and then went for an early night and another   6 for a pint. The rooms are fine for a family for 4 and comfortable. The bunks are high and not so suitable for very young. We took our own mini kettle and coffee making stuff so we could have a hot drink first thing. If you can be bothered to take a flask and make your own it will save you a bomb in the parks. On the first day we had the breakfast buffet which is generally continental but completely adequate. Having read about the hotel via trip advisor we also made up a packed lunch for the from the breakfast buffet, rolls and fruit etc. I know some may cringe at this, as I did a bit, but really everyones doing it and your saving a fourtune in the parks. My boys love the thrill rides but the little one couldnt go on a few because of the height restrictions, so maybe check how tall your kids are before you go. If they are over 1.2m they will get on most things. The second night we ate at the Santa Fe hotel buffet and this was similar although I liked the Wild West Hotel area better. The Santa Fe seemed busier and more crowded in general and a bit more impersonal and more of a work canteen theme! Having been back in 2003 staying in the Main Pink DisneyLand Hotel we promised ourselves that we would go back to Inventions which is the buffet in this hotel. In comparision its by far the best and has a great food selection   but expensive   150 for all of us including a bottle of over priced wine! You do get a couple of characters walking around who visit your table to see the kids, which is fun for them   so take your autograph books! If the fireworks are going at night its a nice place to watch them from as I remember from our last trip. Get into pin trading   my boys love it and its really addictive but keeps them entertained on the way round the parks. But again expensive. c. 6 euros a pin. But buy cheaper packs there or from ebay before you go with the intention to trade.All in all a fair trip but having been to DisneyWorld a bit of a let down   the characters and staff in general just dont have the razzamatazz   not rude but not fun. (Jaffar even made a child cry by chucking his autograph book across a wet floor   I know he's meant to be mean but the kid was only about 3 and was truly upset.)My top tips if your going:*Check around for a great price.*Walk along the canal from your hotel to the park   its not far and really nice.*Take Tea, Coffee & Flask making facilities, and make lunch from breakfast buffet   save yourself a bomb *Perhaps try the Mickey Cafe   they have characters at dinner too if this is for you.*Look into a dinner inclusive deal   you can eat at the disney hotels buffets. We didnt know about it but I think we would have saved money and it includes Cafe Mickey!*When we went in Feb its not busy and we jumped off and rides without much Q'ing.    days was enough and we were scratching around for things to do on the last day. * Play along with the characters you get more from it generally.In general go to experience it, but if we go back to Disney we will save our pennies and go for Disney World instead. Much more to see and do and you just cant compare the 2!

Not enough activities for adults and children and too much people with important waiting lines (sometimes more than 1h30..)Finally you do maybe 15 minutes of pure attraction for 6 full hours of waiting time...That's a poor ratio for fun and you finish the day more tired and stressed and happy to go home.It's maybe better out of summer, i don't know, but in summer, don't go !

We visited the park at the Easter weekend. As expected, the parks became increasingly busy, but good planning meant that the longest queue we waited in was 45 minutes   and that was due to incorrect signage at the entrance to the attraction. Otherwise, Extra Magic Hours meant that we managed to do the most important attractions early on   with Buzz Lightyear being a walk on.I was apprehensive, after reading reports on this site, but despite spending 5 days in the park saw no signs of pushy people. Everybody queued properly, even at the meets and greets. I didn't appreciate people smoking outside the smoking zones, but I didn't let it bother me too much. I had also read that the food was horrendously expension, and bad. Well, yes, the food is expensive, but as we live in a high cost country, the park was actually cheaper than home. I did feel sorry for people from other countries. I found water bottles purchased from the hotel shop to be the cheapest deal within Disney. The quality of the food in general was so so, but this is Disney, and was the case last time we visited Walt Disney World, so wasn't a surprise. The buffet at Innoventions was good, but not really worth the price. We found several of the same items on the menu at the Rendezvous des Stars buffet, which was a much better deal. Our meals at Cafe Mickey and Walt's were definitely high points. Except for at Innoventions and Annette's, I found the serving staff fairly indifferent, so that wasn't too great. We were on a half board plus dining plan, which wasn't good value for us, as our children are young and eat very little. I think we actually would have saved money by going a la carte, so I don't plan to go HB again until they're older.On whole, we found table service restaurants to be better value than counter service. The food was better, and the meals were more filling, which helped keep the kids in a good mood. I had heard there was only unhealthy food at the park, but didn't find it a problem to eat healthily.One regret was not getting a chance to ride on the railroad, but the lines were always huge.
it was a great place although it was really hot when we went and there was very little shade whilst we were queuing for rides.

I went to Disneyland Paris with my daughter and grandaughter (aged 5) 1st   4th Aug inc. We stayed at the Newport Bay Hotel which was beautiful, clean and friendly, but we did upgrade to the Admirals Floor on arrival. This meant our own reception desk (which by then was a bit of a waste as we had already checked in at the main reception) but most importantly, all you can eat breakfast in the Yacht Club restaurant which had no queues! This is a big plus as queues for the main restaurant were very long. We also opted for half board which meant we could eat one other meal per day (any time) at one of 14 different restaurants. This also proved to be a good idea and cheaper than buying it on the day. Only complaint about our hotel was that all the time we were there the outdoor pool wasn't open as they did not have enough lifeguards, so we all squashed in to the indoor pool. Such a shame as the weather was gorgeous. Be prepared for long queues on the main rides, our longest was 2 hours for Crush (the Nemo ride). I'd advise anyone to be organised and get your fast pass tickets to all the rides that have them early, there is no charge for these and it means you can go on without waiting. My advice   pace yourself! Try to get out of the parks mid day as this is the busiest and hottest time. There are lots of open spaces, lake etc to sit and have a picnic or just relax.

Great resort. Was surprised how quickly the queues moved. Longest wait was 1hr 40 mins for crushes coaster. Everything else wasnt too bad. More relaxing than i thought it would be. You forget all your worries and nothing exists but Disney. The kids (11 & 9 ) had a ball. Felt very safe environment despite the crowds. Parades fabulous and employees very friendly. Would suggest you go half board if possible as eating is expensive. Cant wait to go back. Am saving the pennies.

Going high season, school hols etc 2 adults and 2 young children 6&4, we were apprehensive to say the least about the crowds and queues. This was our first time and didn't know the park at all. We stayed at the Davy Crockett ranch which we easy to find and very welcoming. Our Log cabin(mobile home lookalike) was ready when we got there at 1200. It was very adequate for our needs. Clean and good provisions including a dishwasher! Don't expect a 5*. Kids loved it. Swimming Pool at the ranch is great. Getting to the park is 5 10 mins away by car and easy to park.On to the Park. We had 3 day pass tickets and hotel guests could go in from 0800 and take advantage of 2 hours before the main gates opened at 1000. Well recommend this as you can go on most of the fantasyland. Peter Pan ride was very good as was casey Jones for younger children. You can then get in early to the other areas and go on as many rides as possible with minimal queuing. Forget Autopia unless you get to the front. No Fastpass and minimum queue was about 30 mins. Not that good. Definitely take advantage of the fastpass system. Can save 30 45 mins on some rides. Food is expensive, but no more than London prices and it's all fast food. Good tip. You can buy large Sprite Coke for 2.50 Euro and get a another free later in the day. This is printed on your receipt. Considering the amount of people, it didn't really seem crowded. As everyone else says, queuing for the characters is a pain and queue jumping happens where you have wide queue line areas. If you get to the park after 1100, be prepared for a long wait for all rides. Overall it beat our expectations and the kids had a wonderful time and came away withsome lovely memories.

I have now been to Disneyland Paris three times (well, actually the first time it was still Euro Disney). The first time was OK   despite it still being built. The second time (three years ago) there was a strike on so no parades and hardly any characters. Disneyland Studios at the time was sad and gave the impression that it was closing down and the food was terrible. We stayed at the Sequoia Lodge which, at the time, was actually very nice. Strange how things can change in three years. We returned in April this year due to a massive family get together (so Disney would not have been my choice). What a huge disappointment. Lets start with the Sequoia were we stayed. Clean, but poor service throughout. The bath towels were the size of hand towels, one soap between the three of us sharing the room for the duration, the plug in the sink didn't work (i.e. you had to use a nail file to prise it out) and only half the lights in the room worked. I have since found out from friends associates who have also stayed at the Sequoia that they all experienced this as well      we can   t have all stayed in the same room!The main park at Disney, shows signs of being run down. The trams seem to have disappeared, as have the old cars. The toilets were dirty and the parades were, how can I put this, pathetic. If you want to see a decent parade go to Bridgwater Carnival in Somerset!The Studios fared slightly better in as much as it looks like it   s had a lick of paint, since our last visit. However, again, it is almost as if they are trying to save money big time. This was particularly obvious in Honey I shrunk the Kids. It was so worn that the film was fuzzy and half the audience couldn   t feel the mice. We had to explain to those of our party that had never been before what was supposed to happen. Disney Village, like the parks, seemed very sad. Sad staff, sad service, and (like the hotel) half the lights in the signs didn   t work. Very seedy.So, would I recommend Disneyland Paris? If you have children and have never been to Florida     yes. They will be happy as it   s Disney. If you are going with other adults     no. It   s a massive rip off. Over priced, shabby and tacky. Even the fast food     isn   t (expect to wait up to 20 minutes for a burger    and that   s AFTER they   ve taken your order!

My fourteen year old daughter (who has a distant memory of a trip to Orlando several years back) wanted to visit on a recent trip to Paris. It is a scaled down version of Orlando (or Anaheim for that matter) and is not worth the effort. Definitely overpriced for what is offered. I got none of the 'magic' that Disney has had in the past at Orlando. NOTE to Disney Park executives: Your food service needs serious help. I visited on June 29, and your restaurants were either closed, had serious personnel shortages, or had 'run out of food'!!! At 3pm I finally settled for some microwave hotdog and ridiculous chips. Really disappointed in the quality of this facility.

The 3 of us stayed in Disney's Cheyenne Hotel for 2 nights, which was a fairly pleasant Wild West Themed set of hotels. There was a bar in the hotel called The Red Garter which was 6 Euro for a pint of lager and 4 Euro for a diet coke. TIP! Keep your till receipts, because if you spend over a certain amount, your recepit will have a voucher at the bottom for a free glass of pop. We found breakfasts very bad indeed. Firstly it was like a rugby scrum of a morning (mostly with the other french guests) who dont queue like the english! just to get your hands on something to eat   and then there's a terrible 'continental' selection. Only croissants, 3 types of very sweet cereal, and cheese and ham to make up sandwich rolls from! Rubbish coffee, no Tea so all that was left that was ok, was orange or pineapple juice. So you leave the breakfast area still feeling hungry. We walked the 10 minutes along the man made river to the park entrance, as the shuttle busses are usually jam packed, and it is actually a very nice, quiet, easy walk. DONT EAT in the Disney Village Area (this is where most of the big eating establishments are before you actually get to the park gates). The food here is VERY expensive with a burger costing anything from 17 Euro to 30 Euro! We took our own stock of crisps, biscuits, pot noodles etc following advice we had had from other people that had visited, and it was a good job we did or else we would have been starving. At the end of the holiday though, we were longing for a proper meal of meat and vegetables, as only junk food seems to be on offer in the resort   unless your willing to pay through the nose! Unfortunately for us, the Disney Magic was seriously lacking as we expected to see Disney characters walking around the parks, but no. If you want to see one, let along have your photo took with them, then you have to queue up in a designated location for nearly an hour to do this. Again the park rides fill up very fast and before you know it there's at least a 70 minute wait for them, let alone the popular ones! We had a nice bbq chicken meal in the frontierland   which only cost 27 Euro   this was after we scoured the park for the best deals. As I say, for us it was a let down. Just seemed to be a glorified Theme Park, which was not as large as expected, souvenier shops at every turn with as high a price as the food establishments, no characters to 'coo' over and very rude europeans to battle with. All in all, a disappointment for an expectant 10 year old and 2 Disney loving adults!

I took the family to Disneyland Paris for the second year in a row. Definitely buy the annual pass if you plan for visit for more then 3 days and have 4 or 5 in the area. Much cheaper plus you might get lucky and come back as we did. Get one Fantasyland pass (the one up from the bottom) and you get 10% off food and store purchases plus free parking. Pays for itself in 3 days if you shop like my wife.Some tips: Fast Pass is great, get there first thing in the morning and go to your favorite rides to pick those up. Food isn't bad, we usually had lunch in the park and with a family of six, spent around 45 Euros. That is the  fast food  type of meals. We never tried the buffets and tried to go to one theme resteraunt   that was a disappointment. Gave us a table at the back and then ignored us for 10 minutes. Menu was bad for kids unless yours like odd seafood. We left and went to the Steakhouse just outside the park in Disney Village. A little pricey but well worth it.The Disney Studios park is not as good as Disneyland itself. Fewer rides and things to see but worth a visit. I can't figure out why the Crush Coaster has no fast passes and always a 2 hr lineup. My kids love it and say it is worth it. The car show at the back is worth a visit, lots of room so no need to wait in line, just get there 15 minutes before it starts. Don't bother trying to volunteer to participate when they ask, they always pick the pretty girl in the front! :)

First went to Eurodisney ( as it was then called) just after it opened. Stayed at the Newport Bay Club hotel for 5 days and had a great time, despite the bad press it was getting. Our sons were age 2 and 6. We returned every year for 5 or 7 days, although there was only the Magic Kingdom park then. We visited in July, so could spend time in the hotel pool as well. Disney Paris is a great introduction to Disney for young children especially,as you only need a few days, and you can Eurostar from the UK in under 3 hours. We took the boys to Disneyworld Florida for the first time when they were 9 and 13, as we felt they were now old enough to cope with 2 weeks of theme parks in the heat, plus the long flight. We have seen many miserable, hot, tired, screaming toddlers in the parks in Orlando. Not really what Walt had in mind!If you stay on site, there are 6 Disney hotels. The Disneyland Hotel is built over the entrance to the Magic Kingdom ( no outdoor pool). Hotels New York, Sequoia Lodge and Newport Bay are built on 3 sides of Lake Disney, just outside the Disney Village. (Have indoor and outdoor pools.) Regular bus shuttle to the parks or a 10 minute walk. Hotels Cheyenne and Santa Fe are further away, behind the New York, so not so convenient to walk to the parks. They do not have pools. You can only use the pool of the Disney Hotel you are staying in, as they give you a pass.There are other hotels further away, not Disney owned, but still provide the shuttle bus to the parks. We have stayed in the Explorers Hotel ( good for families with young children, Pirate theme. This hotel has a good connecting room facility. Indoor pool.)The Disney hotels are bed and breakfast, but you can now pay in advance for half board. This gives you a discount in the restaurants in the hotels and parks, for 1 meal per day, lunch or dinner. There are 3 price categories, which include a starter, main, dessert, and a soft drink. Adult price currently 16e for standard, 21e for plus, or 36e for premium per nt of your stay. There is a child price. You can read about the restaurants each category includes online, to help you choose the right one. They do not include the Rainforest Cafe, Planet Hollywood, or MacDonalds in the Disney Village.All restaurants can be booked in advance, either before you go, or in resort.We love the Blue Lagoon ( mainly fish) which in the Pirates Of the Carribbean ride!If you stay in a Disney hotel, you can go into the park 2 hrs ealier in the morning ( 8am) as Extra Magic Hours. You can book breakfast in Fantasy Land, instead of in the hotel if you wish. Advise booking early breakfast to avoid the queues in the hotel.( we book 7am). There are also Disney Characters in the hotels in reception, at breakfast( and sometimes at check in) time.The Disney Village ( used to be called Festival Disney) has restaurants,(including Rainforest Cafe and Planet Hollywood), cafes, bar pub, large Disney store, cinema, Buffalo Bills Wild West Show ( my boys loved this  seen it many times!) Nightclub, Billy Bobs Country and Western ( restaurant with line dancing etc). Also Cafe Mickey, where you can book a character breakfast or dinner.There are also restaurants in the Magic Kingdom park where you can book a character lunch, tea or dinner. They are a good way of getting photos, video and autographs of characters, as they come to your table. Saves queueing in the park ( sadly the French do not organise the queueing as well as in Orlando  there is some pushing and shoving). They will also organise birthday cakes etc for you, and sing Happy Birthday.Bags are searched before entering the Parks. As far as I am aware, there are NO lockers for hire. They had them originally near the entrance, but were closed during bomb scares some years ago, and I have not seen them in use again. Take a rucksack for jumpers  waterproofs etc. We refill plastic water bottles at the fountains to save having to buy drinks. Pushchairs  strollers can be hired for the day, but you cannot take them out of the park. Good idea to take some bright ribbon to tie on the handle, as they all look alike in the buggy parks! The Disney buses stop by the railway station. You can buy drinks and sandwiches here, cheaper than in the parks. It is only a short walk to the Studios and Magic Kingdom from here.We also take small battery fans with us in the summer great when you are in a queue in the heat.Adults can go on every ride in both parks. There is a height requirement for some rides, like Space Mountain and Rock n Roller Coaster.There are 4 lands in the Magic Kingdom, all leading from Main Street. Fantasy Land is usually the busiest, as rides are geared for small children. Discovery Land is to the right, and Frontierland and Adventureland to the left. Check the park map for showtimes and Parades. People will start queueing, or sitting by parade routes at least an hour before. Try to watch the Parades from an outer kerb, on a corner. You will get a good view of the floats coming towards and past you, without people leaning out to take photos video and blocking your view.The night electrical parade and fireworks are only at peak times, so check before you book. In the summer ( july Aug) they are every night. Also end Nov  Dec Jan for Christmas celebrations. The Parks will be quieter outside school holidays, but not as many shows  parades or fireworks.Use the Fastpass facility if busy. Put your park ticket into machine by ride. You will get a ticket giving you a timeslot to come back, and enter the fastpass entrance, to save a long queue. Check the small print to see what time you can get another fastpass ticket, as you can sometimes hold more than one at a time. Rides also have childswop, so parents can take it in turns to ride, without queueing twice, if children  babies are too young to ride.Food in the parks is expensive, but no different to all theme parks nowadays. Thorpe Park( in Surrey,) is extortionate  no drinking water fountains, and they have closed the fastpass machines. Now you have to BUY fastpass tickets to avoid a long queue. Hope Disney NEVER do this, it is a rip off. There are fast food outlets, and also more formal restaurants with waiter service. We like Blue Lagoon, Walts,Lucky Nugget Saloon( Character buffet)and Colonel Hathi's Pizza.The Studios are usually less busy than the Magic Kingdom, and close earlier. You can go to and fro both parks, but make sure you get your hand stamped, or you will have trouble getting back in, even with a hotel Disney Pass. They are very strict about this.Crush's Coaster is a very busy ride  head for this first. They have now opened Tower of Terror as well, a major ride. The Backlot Tram tour is good, showing movie special effects. Motors Action Stunt Show is very good ( same now in Orlando), check showtimes. The Studios has its own parade of film characters ( Mary Poppins etc). They also have film characters in the park for autographs  photos.If you want a day in Paris, the RER line A train goes from Marne La Vallee  Chessy station to Gare de Lyon frequently, and you can return late at night.I am going to Disney Paris again in August, with my eldest son, who is now 23, and in the Royal Navy. Staying at the Newport Bay for 5 days. You never outgrow Disney!If you have any questions, please send me a message, and I will do my best to answer it.

Be prepared to queue.Queue for breakfast, the bus in & out, security check, Tickets, entry, rides, characters, photos opportunity etc etc etc.The joy of our long awaited family holiday was dented by the hassled feeling of being pushed and shoved. Not to mention the queue jumpers.One staff member at  Guest Relations  named Julian deserves a special mention for his complete rudeness and utter unhelpfull attitude. Disney may have to do a bit more training if this is what us paying customers are to turn to when we need help and understanding.If only Tinkerbells Magic dust would work on this surly arrogant man.

I must first admit that I adore all things Disney so I approach this with some bias. This park was very easy to access and had well placed signage from the motorway and train. Park tickets were reasonably priced and truthfully, both parks could be seen in a day if needed. I have been to Disneyland in CA and visit Walt Disney World almost every weekend, so, I approach my visit as a well versed fan. The park attractions are very similar to the other parks with a few exceptions. Those that have been duplicated are much improved for the most part. Their Space Mountain: Mission 2, Phantom Manor (Haunted Mansion) and Crush's Coaster (at the Studios park) are not to be missed. Their baby switch option was fantastic and allowed attractions to be seen rather quickly. The park seems to turn a blind eye to outside food and drink and we brought quite a few items for a picnic. Inside merchandise and food drink was reasonably priced and even beat the WDW options even with the exchange rate! This is a must for fans and a great day trip for all others. The park was extremely busy when we visited (July) and had wait times for some attractions near 100 minutes. Efficiency is not a key trait and many long queue lines were a result of half full ride vehicles. Character meetings without a queue were often mob scenes and very aggressive. The parks are much smaller in scale than the rest and can easily be seen with strategic planning and the use of Fast Passes.

My friend and i were in disneyland paris from 28th june for 5 days, we had the time of our lives, we went on every ride and dont have a bad word to say about it.I guess people get angry because its expensiveand since they get upset about it, the write that is horrible.WE had the ost amazing time, we would do it again in a minute.The parks were clean , the attention to the detail was great.

I went with my wife and 2 year old daughter. First it cost THREE HUNDRED EUROS to get in. After I paid, they said they made a mistake and my 2 year old daughter did not have to be paid for. However, they could not refund us. You have to write in. Then they write back for  further information . Then they write again for copies of passports etc. They just don't want to give the money back. Once you are in, its just a total rip off; atrocious food; humungous queues. Rude french people pretending to be American. I felt ripped off and angry.

Maybe it's because I'm a big kid, but my partner and I looooooved Eurodisney! We only had one day there and it was a bit rushed to see everything but the rides were awsome as was the parade. It was just like being in a fairy tale! Would definatley go back and do it all again!

Disneyland Paris is like a giant shopping mall at extreme prices with a few attractions thrown in for good measure. To eat or drink, you probably need your grandmother's inheritance. If you are going for your little ones be aware that most of the more interesting attractions they won't be able to go on due to their height. The ones you can go on, you will likely queue for an hour and be disappointed. Bolshy crowds, extautionate prices and a great deal of walking is what is in store for you. The highlights as we experienced them were the parade at 4.15 pm where you actually get to see most of the princesses (otherwise you only get a quick view or take on the angry crowd for a photo or autograph) and the star wars attraction. Again for the star wars you need to be ready to queue in a hot tunnel for long periods of time. For boys over the age of 7 yet too short for the roller coasters this is the only attraction you can enjoy. Also beware, if you plan on staying at one of the hotels you are about an hour train ride from Paris.

Loved it here   all 3 of us, ranging in age from 11 to 74 : )So much to see and do. Get your map beforehand and try to plan what to see and when, especially if your time is limited.I've read that you're not allowed to take food and drinks into the park, but as long as you don't go overboard they don't seem to mind. There are fountains outside the park where you can refill water bottles, which will save you some money.Prices for food and drink are really high, also for souvenirs etc. The problem with the shops is that there are so many of them and you can't avoid them, so after a few days you get so used to seeing the same prices that they no longer seem to horrendously high   do your shopping on the first day or buy at home before you come.Plenty of opportunties for seeing the characters and getting photos and or autographs, so don't stress to get this done when you first arrive.Enjoy it   no matter what age you are!

Being American and a former Disney employee I have had many Disney experiences. We enjoyed our time at Disneyland Paris and the kids had a good time so just a few comments.The fast pass is awesome   use it wisely and you won't wait in a line all day. Immediately go to the ride you want that has a fast pass, if no line or a short line, get the fast pass and then stand in the short line   that way you get to go twice. Get there early, right when the park opens and then go on the busiest rides first (Crush's Coaster, Rock and Roll Roller Coaster and Tower of Terror at the studios). This way you can get them out of the way and enjoy them without a long line. From experience, you can usually do 2 3 rides in the first hour with very little wait. Also, as soon as you can get another fast pass go get it. At the US parks there are very clearly designated smoking areas   perhaps they have them in Disneyland Paris but no one smokes there. It was overwhelming. People holding their babies smoking, smoking in the queues, restaurants, bathrooms, everywhere... the staff did not direct people elsewhere to smoke. This was disappointing. I am appreciative of differences when we travel but people blowing smoke in your children's faces is not cool.

I have been to Disneyland Paris once, but plan to go back very shortly. I went on a school week and wasnt expecting any long queues. There werent but the main park was still  busy . I think this may of been as people come from all over the world, and their school holidays are probably different. Rides were fine, got to see most main characters and had a really fun time. Reccomend going on school holidays, I always say this in my reviews because it does make a difference. Going to Disneyland on a Saturday, what do you expect the park to be like? First night had a problem, had dinner at the Pirate fish place, I had pasta which was lovley, but my friend had swordfish, which came out cold. My other friend, had prawns, now in France, we had forgotten they like there heads....So when we asked them to cut them off, it didnt go to well. He eveuntually re orderd the pasta I had, wasting around 12 erous. Apart from this small upset, the rest of our trip was fantatstic. Dont worry about your French, at Disneyland Paris. Most staff will understand, though it is good to know some basics and key words (please, thank you, no, yes, thats fine) mabye even some food in French. People who give this holiday 1 or two stars, I feel are very harsh, and I would like to know why they do.

Just thought that you may be interested in our recent visit. We went with 5yr old little girl from Tuesday thru to Friday last week. We had excellent weather and really enjoyed ourselves. This was our first time to the parks so we were on a lot of learning curves. We booked through DLRP site, booking the hotel and half board vouchers.We went by car taking the early ferry to Calais and drove down to the hotel. This was an easy journey and we arrived in the resort about 3pm. Checked in, got our room and tickets and then headed into the resort. We were staying in the Santa Fe and got the shuttle to the resort which was very easy and not too full.We arrived in time for the Once Upon a Dream Parade with all the characters and floats. Great show but perhaps in retrospect a little too much for our initial visit as our DD was getting her head around the it all (especially as there's loud music accompanying everything.) Unfortunately Captain Hook accidentally scared her which meant that she took a while to take to the characters.As most people were leaving it was easy to get on many of the smaller rides so we went on the teacups, the merry go round and then just enjoyed walking around taking in the sites. We left around 630pm as we were quite tired by all our traveling and had an evening meal at Annettes Diner with our half board vouchers. The food here was ok, typical burger and fries with a little variation. Littley had pasta and a frisbee. We were there for the singing show which was quite a laugh and very 60s rock and roll. Our timing was great as we walked in and had a table straight away but when we left there was quite a queue. (This was about 1930). Back to the hotel for an early night   the shuttle was very busy and we decided to catch the larger one to Cheyenne and then walk through to our hotel which was really easy to do.The next day we had breakfast at 730am (have to pick a slot) and were in the parks by around 830 for the magic hours that you get for being in a disney hotel. These were really valuable as it meant we could get in a few rides n the morning, then head back to the hotel for lunch and a sleep before continuing later in the afternoon. Due to what was open we went to Discoveryland and did Buzz Lightyear (walked straight on) a great easy ride which although a bit scarey to start with (our DD is easily startled and this was her first experience of any of these sorts of rided) is great fun, especially when someone else is twirling the ride about! DD loved Orbitron which was lots of whirling round in planes and going up and down. We had a lot of runs at this over the time in the park and she loved every minute. We then headed to Adventure land and did the pirates of the Caribbean. Again, not a hard ride and not really too scary but DD wasn't sure of the dark and unexpected ups and downs. We chilled in Pocahontas play area for a while (still only 11am at this point) and then did the roundabout again before heading back to the hotel for lunch. Val D'europe shopping centre is about 10mins by car and has a huge hypermarket where we had brought cheese, tomatos and picnic stuff. Down by the river at the hotel there were some picnic tables and we sat and had a lovely quiet lunch before heading off for a snooze to recharge.Up again around 1530 to head into the studio park.We were trying to time it to see High School Musical routine which we did and DD loved it. They sing songs from all 3 films and also get the little ones involved in some of the dances. We then were in time for the Disney Play House party which was from the telly (I think,) it's a bit young for DD but she loved it as there were a lot of special effects. It's tricky cos you have to all sit on the floor and the characters are all puppets so sometimes they're hard to see. Still, it was a great show and one of her highlights. Still on the go we queued for the racing cars which were ok and then went on the Studio Tram which I loved but which DD found was very scarey. I'd be careful if you have a child who gets worried by the unexpected (even though we explained that is wasn't going to hurt us etc it was still very frightening for her.)That evening we headed to the Cheyenne to eat, had the buffet there on the half board and again got in early enough not to have to queue (although it was about 1930 this time.) We sat out by the bar area there which was really nice and DD played with lots of other children and just chilled, a great way to end the day and quite relaxing. Walked along the river to get back.Next day was pretty similar although we added in the Lilo and Stitch show which was really funny, did quite a bit of meet and greet and went on the Peter Pan ride which DD thought was the best one. We also watched a couple more shows   there's a dance one in Discoveryland which is very interactive and DD loved the dancing and taking part there. Also the big Mickeys Party one on the central stage. We ate that night in Disney Village at the Rainforest Cafe and had a lovely evening. Walked back to the hotel along the lake and river and it didn't seem to take long at all.All in all a great trip, timed about right (we did Friday in the park starting later and using the fastpass system which works well.) Wouldn't have stayed any longer as we'd done everything that was suitable. One thing that worked well for us was giving DD some made up vouchers which we said she could trade for various items (cuddly toy, t shirt etc) this meant she wasn't always asking for things and knew what to expect. The merchandising is strong out there and prices quite high. Food is expensive for things like sweets and bottles of water (3euros for a small bottle) but we took our own and also filled up at fountains. For meals the prices are probably no more than London prices.Hope this helps with any planning! All the best

My girlfriend and I have just spend two and a bit days at Disneyland Paris. I have to say it is a lot of fun and I really really enjoyed myself. The rides are great. Terror Towers, Crushes Coaster and the Aerosmith roller coaster are all brilliant. We stayed in the Santa Fe hotel, which I would recommend to anyone. It is one of the cheapest Disney hotels but it was clean and had everything we needed. The only down side is that it's about a 15 minute walk from the park, so it's time consuming to just pop back to your hotel room and pick up something you've forgotten. But it's no big deal really.I do have a few gripes though. Firstly food and drink prices are extortionate. Secondly I was sold meal vouchers over the phone. These allow you to eat at specified restaurants in the park, village and hotels. At about   20 per person per meal I was assured that I would save money. This is slightly misleading. If you eat at some of the posher restaurants you do save money. However the buffet meal at the Santa Fe hotel was about 20 Euros, so I didn't save any money on that particular meal. Also what I wasn't told is that the meal vouchers I ordered require you to choose from a limited menu in some restaurants. This I only found out when I sat down and looked at the menu. This leads me on to my major gripe. The Steakhouse restaurant was awful. It's fair to say it was my worst dining experience ever. We arrive at 9:00 with a reservation, but didn't sit down till about 9:20. My girl specifically asked whether the starter she ordered had cheese in it (she is allergic) and was assured that it didn't. After a very long wait the starter turned up, and guess what, it contained cheese. So the starter was replaced with very quickly with carrot and coriander soup. Unfortunately this was disgusting, it tasted like carrot juice and didn't contain any coriander. The main course and the pudding were similarly disappointing and slow to arrive. We eventually left the Steakhouse at 10:50, a full 1 hour 50 minutes after we arrived! I would like to say that none of the above ruined our experience. It was still a very enjoyable holiday and I would recommend it to anyone who could afford it

had a 4night break with my husband and 2kids staying at the santa fe. well it was brilliant the kids and both of us loved it the rides were great for all ages and the parades. over at the studio side of things was amazing so much amazing stuff to see and do and of course buy.only down side to the stay was the food not good choice at all. the hotel food was good just not the theme parks during the day. we had a character breakfast which served all sorts of food that was great the kids wanted that every morning definately worth the extra cost.

we were there on a saturday and the queues were just incredible   for most of the better attractions we had to wait between 30 and 60 minutesif it had not been for the small kid of our friends it would have been a rather disappointing visit   you should have seen his eyes when Mickey came ; )therefore for the ones young at heart I would recommend to visit it off peak

We had a good time in DLP last week, however there were a few disappointments with technical difficulties in the Studio Park, where at one point both the Rock and Roll Rollercoaster and the new Tower were closed. Whilst unfortunate I appreciate that these things happen so it was bad luck.What was noticable, however, was the attitude of many  cast members . A large number of the staff we saw particulary on the attractions, just looked fed up and certainly did not live up to the happy Disney spirit we have come to enjoy in 3 visits to the parks. At times we felt kind of felt like cattle being herded onto and off rides, and the staff added nothing to the experience. The exception to this was the new Tower ride where the staff were exceptional and never out of character.Whilst the quality of the rides cannot be faulted, they do suffer if the cast members operating them are less than enthusiastic.I also feel that there needs to be some attention to the fast pass system. In past visits this has been a means of fairly reducing queuing time, but there seems to have been a shift to fast pass holders actually getting preference in boarding rides at the expense of those who have opted to queue. This was most noticable in the Star Tours attraction where the standard queue was rudely ignored as Fast Pass holders turned up, resulting in an ever lengthening queue and actually standing at the final turnstile for nearly 10 minutes before being waved through. Fortunately the park wasn't overly busy so with the exception of Thunder Mountain (fantastic) and the new Finding Nemo roller coaster (jaw dropping) we didn't spend too long hanging around. Indiana Jones was literally  get off and get back on again , we walked straight onto Pirates, Haunted House and many more.Our only other gripe was queuing for and the quality of the food. Why have two lanes of queues being served by one service point? When you're paying top dollar for a pretty poor hamburger you shouldn't have to wait 20 minutes to order it, further more when you send fries back because they are cold, you don't expect the server to eat one from a new portion and pass the rest to you.As I say we did have a good time, but we did feel the Disney magic had lost a little bit of its shine.

Loved loved loved this trip, was one of the best holidays I have ever had (i'm still a big kid and love Disney). I would say that the park and surrounding attractions, including food and drink in the park and hotels are very pricey.That being said it was great, I met the stars and had lots of super pics!Enjoy! xxx

We were expecting this to be packed as it was English school half term, but no, arriving on a drizzly Tuesday 26th May, we found hardly any queues (Dumbo 5 mins, Pirates of the Caribbean, straight on, no waiting!!). Longest was Thunder Mountain at 20 mins. Returned on Thursday, it was a little busier but not that much.

Both parks were fantastic!We did both parks in two days, so one day for each park (this is my partner and myself).We bought most of our food from the train station as it was a LOT cheaper and the food was just as good.Stayed at Santa Fe which had a mexican buffet. If you are a mexican food lover do not go here. They had a burrito and cheeses and that was it that was mexican. Biggest waste of money, and we didn't even get a discount for staying there.

Me, My wife and my 14month old son went to Disney and Paris for 4 days over the late May Bank Holiday weekend. We spent time at both parks (Disneyland Resort and Walt Disney Studios). Given that our son is still young, we thought that this would be a perfect opportunity for all of us to have a good time in that we could do kiddie stuff whilst he was up and go on the adult rides whilst he had his naps. Here is our experience.    Baby Unfriendly   this park is not particularly baby friendly. Note that pushchairs are not allowed in any queues for rides or attractions and nor are they allowed inside for any of the shows. What this means is that if your baby is sleeping in his pushchair (and you don   t want to wake him up), you are stuck since you can   t join any queues. Disney have a clever concept called    Baby switch    whereby if you are parents with a baby it allows you to queue up and then take it in turns to go on the ride (with the other person looking after the baby). Nice idea if executed properly. What these buffoons at Disneyland Paris do is only allow one parent to queue whilst the other parent (with the baby) waits at the exit. Once the first parent has been on the ride (after queuing for say 1 2 hours on their own), then the other parent can go on the ride without queuing. Whichever genius thought of this didn   t realize that maybe if parents are on a    family    day out holiday, they probably don   t want to stay apart for the bulk of this period. Note: even if the baby is awake, you are not allowed to carry him in the queue.    Thrill Rides   As an adult, there is one decent ride that you could call a    thrill ride    and that is the Rock   N   Rollercoaster in Walt Disney Studios (which is excellent). The remainder of the rides were absolutely rubbish and I can say that none of them come even close to Nemesis, Air or Oblivion at Alton Towers. If you are an adrenalin junky     this is not the place.    Disney Characters     There is very little of the Disney    Magic    here     you can walk around for hours without seeing a single character, and the characters are mainly scheduled to be in certain places at certain times (e.g. parades). Would it be too difficult to have characters constantly walking around in the park     we are in Disneyland for gods    sake     I don   t think having characters actually around will demean the brand!    Staff     With few exceptions, the staff were rude and unhelpful. I asked a popcorn vendor for the location of the    Pirates of the Caribbean    ride (which is a big attraction and was actually about a 100 yards from where he was standing)     he just stared at me and said he didn   t know. We asked members of staff for the times of the English version of the Disney Play House show. After being fobbed off all day, at 5.30pm we were told that there were no shows that day in English due to technical reasons.    Although we were fortunate, we did bump into other people who said that they had been on 2 3 rides which had suffered from technical problems.    Smoking     they need to make this park a no smoking zone     it is pathetic to see smoke bellowing out everywhere, especially with children around.    Cleanliness     toilets were dirty, cutlery was not cleaned properly, generally untidy.    Queues     It is amazing how many people would jump queues (I am talking about teenagers   .and their parents!!)     try that in England and there will be fights!!Overall you don   t really get the feeling on any    Magic    here     the place is dirty, with unhelpful and unfriendly staff and is grossly overpriced. Although some of the shows are very good (e.g. the stunts show in Walt Disney Studios), overall it is not much of an experience. Maybe France isn   t the country that embodies the Disney culture and hence was always doomed to fail.I could go on   but I wont. My advice would be to go to Alton Towers, Gullivers Kingdom or Legoland in the UK (depending on what it is that you are after) and give this pathetic excuse of a Disney park a miss   OR save up for the real Disneyland which I have been informed by my wife is actually amazing.

I've been to Disneyland Paris many times since it opened. Here are a few tips which may have been of help to some of the recent contributors if they had known about them before their holiday.It is a total fantasy which can be wonderful. The reality is that it is exhausting and you cannot possibly see everything there is to see. Children can sometimes be overwhelmed by it all and a good escape can be the Pocahontas Playground or a lie down back at the hotel or an afternoon in nearby Sea Life. You need to plan your trip but be prepared to change and adopt your plans to take account of queues and tiredness. Don   t forget to eat. The McDonalds in the Festival Village is the cheapest place to eat. We snacked on Casey   s Corner hot dogs during the day and had our main meal away from the park in the evening.Over the years we have had various character meals. My favourite was my daughter   s birthday party last year at Caf   Mickey. The price was similar to other Disney restaurants of its class as a result it is popular and should be booked in advance if possible. Bring an autograph book and have the character meal at the start of your holiday because there can be crazy queues in the park and studio to meet Minnie, Mickey, Poo, Tigger etc. At Caf   Mickey they visit your table in turns all through the meal. We also did a character tea which was nice and another time we did the character birthday party which was hectic, noisy and a bit impersonal. Our party at the Disneyland Hotel was enjoyable but we more than paid for the view, name and location.Supermarket: There is a petrol station at the entrance to the Sante Fe Hotel. You can get the free hotel bus from the bus stop at the park (5 min). There is a public bus number 34 (   1.50 approx each way) from the Park also which takes you to Val d   Europe (10 min) where there is a huge supermarket (also restaurants) in the outlet centre. Also the RER (train) from Disneyland station will take you to Torcy (10 min) where there is another large supermarket. On our first visit in early 1993 I paid the equivalent of   3 for two small glasses of milk each morning and night at the hotel for my young niece   s bottle if only I knew where to shop! Tickets: As with everything else in Disney there can be queues for tickets so if you can buy them in advance or as part of a package you could save yourself time. We sometimes visit more than once in 12 months or visit the park for a week or more. In this case the annual tickets are far better value. There are three types of annual tickets one for residents of France, and for non residents you can buy the Fantasy or the Dream pass. All are valid for 12 months from the date of purchase. The Dream pass is valid for 365 days (costs around    170). There are some restricted dates on the Fantasy Pass such as 26th Dec to 1st Jan, Halloween etc (costs around    129). These passes give you discount in the shops, photographs, Buffalo Bills Wild West Show and restaurants. They also give you free parking in the Disneyland car park (usual price    8 for cars) I don   t think you get free parking in Festival Disney with the pass. You pay for the annual ticket at the usual ticket outlet under the Disneyland Hotel entrance to the park. You then go to the passport office where your photo is taken and the pass issued. Be warned if you are buying annual tickets for other children in your holiday group apart from your own children, you will need written permission from their parents for you to buy the pass and a photocopy of their parents    passport faxed to the Disney passport office. I don   t know why they make you go through such hoops to buy the ticket. We no longer stay in the Disneyland hotels. A very expensive Christmas holiday was spoiled three years ago by the intransigent attitude of Disney management and staff over a mix up over tickets. If you want to see the real    Magic    of Disney just make a mistake and see how you will be accommodated. With an hour to go before closing on our first day of our holiday, we brought the gala dinner tickets (similar to the entry tickets used since the park opened) instead of our entry tickets (which were different to all previous entry tickets) to get into the park. The Disney personnel wouldn   t ring the hotel to confirm we had a length of stay package, they wouldn   t agree a refund if we bought day tickets. They did nothing to help. On the night before Christmas Eve I missed the electrical parade and I got absolutely no satisfaction from my letters of complaint. I would never have returned but for my daughter   s birthday. Of course once we had the annual tickets anyway, we went on another trip for Christmas and have just returned home after celebrating my son   s birthday in Disney. We stayed in self catering houses called Hotel Citea Magny Le Hongre which were recommended on Trip Advisor. The three enjoyable holidays within the last 12 months cost less than the spoiled Christmas one.Other tips such as fastpass etc are covered by other contributors. Also covered by other contributors are the incredible prices charged in the shops. Here are my recent observations   A child   s High School Musical tee shirt was    8 dearer in Disney compared to our high street store. Because I had bought it at home for my daughter I couldn   t resist checking the price. The only difference was the label inside the shirt said    Disneyland Paris   . A Disney Princess stroller was    reduced    to    9 when the same one was    2.99 at home. In previous years there was a little shop open after you exited the park on the right hand side (under the Disneyland Hotel). It sold the end of lines at    reduced    prices.There seemed to be less people in the park and studio this holiday than any other since our first visit. If you are going to Disneyland Paris I hope you enjoy your stay.

We took the VEA Shuttle bus from the airport, we pre purchased our tickets but this doesnt mean you are guaranteed a seat   everyone is in the same scrum, sorry queue and you need to fight your way on. We stayed at the New York Hotel, which was great, couple of minor issues but would recommend the hotel overall. Those of us in the group who had been to Disneyworld in Orlando were disappointed with Disneyland Paris, the park just lacked the  Disney Charm  you get in Orlando. The worst thing was the smoking, there are designated smoking areas and supposedly a 68 euro fine for smoking outside of these but people are smoking everywhere regardless and with 2 small children and a pregnant member of the group it was quite unpleasant. The parks are not as clean and have to say the toilets were just disgusting. The staff varied some were just plain rude and unhelpful whilst others went out of their way to make sure the children were not stampeded by 40 year old woman who wanted their picture taken with a character first. The one thing we all hated was the total lack of manners displayed by a great number of visitors in the park. Europeans do not have the same level of manners as those in the USA and although it is not the fault of Disney there are things which could be done to improve matters.At the moment the exchange rate of GBP to Euro is very poor but the prices are crazy. To save money make up sandwiches from the breakfast buffet and take them in. They have a bag check at the front gate of the park but if you carry them wrapped in a jacket cardi they dont check and away you go. Disney Village has a good choice of places to eat but it is expensive. We ate in Planet Hollywood which was good quality and would say reasonable value for money. Annette's Diner was enjoyable but 4.80 for a pint of sprite with half a glass of ice spoiled it. Macdonalds is more expensive than home but still half the price of other places. It was however filthy and you were hit with a very unpleasant smell as you walked in the door. If you have been to Orlando dont expect the same at Disneyland Paris or you will be disappointed. But if you cant get to Orlando and want to give your kids a taste of Disney it is still worth it   no amount of money can buy the picture on their faces when they see Mickey Mouse etc right in front of them.

We took our 3 year old twins in May. We stayed at the New York, it didn't matter. The room was clean, it didn't matter. The room service menu was awful, it didn't matter. It was quite expensive, it didn't matter. What did matter was the awe struck look of incredulity when my twins saw the  real  Mary Poppins. The whole set up is super efficient, the parks are great and the  cast members  were all lovely to the kids. Thoroughly enjoyed our three days (it was long enough) and we will be going back (we didn't get to meet Tigger!)

I love it here! I literally could live there!Me and my partner had a day out and a half here and I have previously stayed a week there.Wonderful rides, even better with recent studio installments. Fab shopping for any Disney fan.A once in a lifetime experience I've had three times:)

I stayed here on 4th May 2009 with my husband and two sons (aged 4 and 2) for 3 nights. We stayed in the Jesse James block   (no lift?) The attention to detail was fantastic. It was a little tacky but we loved it and it was ideal for children. My son loved the top bunk. There was a long queue to check in but other than that the hotel was faultless. The sandpit kept the boys entertained in the evening.Having read other peoples advice we chose to go to breakfast at 7.30 every day. After 8am there were hardly any tables left. There was masses of food available and decent coffee juice etc. We booked a half board option although on the down side as the park closed at 7pm, and most restaurants closed by 6pm, we used the vouchers for lunch on 2 of the days we stayed. Annette's diner in the Disney village was good but service was very slow. Try to get there at least 15mins before the park closes. Agrabah cafe in the park served fabulous food and the setting was really pretty. We also ate at the Cafe to the Stars (Ratatouille cafe) in the Walt Disney Studios but it was no where near as good. We booked Eurodisney and Eurostar separately and found it to be cheaper than booking it directly despite the various offers of staying and playing for free   40% off etc We didn't book a seat for our 2 year old and found that there was lots of spare seats on the train.All the staff in the hotel and throughout the park were really helpful, friendly and all spoke English fluently.Drinks are currently 3.50 euros for a coke water fanta etc we bought a guide book which suggested buying lunch in the railway station (a couple of mins walk outside the park) A draught beer and glass of wine cost 12 euros at the hotel.We'd definitely stay here again.

Disneyland paris is an utter rip off.Last night we were charged 5 euros for 2 small glasses of milk for our granchildren.Meal at Sequioia lodge 137 eurosMeal at disneyland hotel 138 eurosYes there were characters but we had to pay ectra for drinks egpint of lager and galss of chardnnay 12.90eurosGift for my five year old grand daughter   little doll set   16,90 euros (same in pound shop in Scarborough   1)Lunchtime meal for 4 of us rather like a macdonalds 38 eurosthey charge for everything   towels for pool 2 eurosVery disappointedEven at this time of year massive queueswaiting time in park for rides and meals normally 20 mins   sometimes longerBe prepared Two baileys whiskies 20 euros

Here's the funny thing about my first experience to Disneyland (no, I haven't been to the allgedly superior American version) I enjoyed every second of it. Why is that funny? Well, for starters, I'm not a big disney fan ... or even a disney fan at all, not all that keen on themeparks either, but you can't help but be charmed by the place. Reading over some of the reviews, I found myself agreeing with all the criticisms; yes the food is expensive, but I anticipated that, yes, the queues are long, I anticipated that too, yes, the crowds (not necessarily all French just because the park is located in France) were rude and didn't have much 'queue strategy' but none of these things were really a fault of the park itself and more importantly, none of them came remotely close to ruining MY experience of the park ... and I'm generally a pretty cynical, introverted guy who isn't a big fan of people. For the 40 Euro entrance fee, I found the park to be an absolute delight from start to finish. We arrived at opening and didn't leave until we were practically thrown out at closing, exhausted but entirely satisfied. If you rush around you can pretty much cover everything in a day, including queuing for the rides. The Indiana Jones ride was exhilirating, the Small World waterboat ride was gorgeous, the castle was enchanting, the haunted house was silly but fun, the surroundings were lovely and always varied every couple of steps from the waterfalls of the Pirates of the Caribbean area in the Adventure section to the labyrinth in the Fantasy land section. I spent a good solid ten hours constantly going 'oooh! look at that!' ... 'oooooh! let's go on that' ... 'oooh! this is good!'. I think the park has a particularly difficult job catering for all needs but there is a little bit of something for everyone here. The criticisms I noted before are all valid, but I think the experience is what you make of it. I think you have to anticipate and accept things and not let them spoil your day. Of course their are going to be queues, its Disneyland for goodness sakes. Of course the food prices are a rip off, they always are at attractions like this, but right outside is a massive shopping complex and you can easily duck in and out of the park at your leisure. I find it a bit pointless complaining about the inevitable. My only critcism was that the fast pass ticket system was a bit of a shambles. You had to queue to get a fast pass ticket from a machine which gave you an allocated slot of when you can return to go on the ride. In between you couldn't get a ticket for any other ride until the one you already have a ticket for expired and even when you went back at the allocated time, there was still a lengthy queue from all the fast pass holders. After the first ride we gave up on the fast pass system altogether and simply joined the back of the queues which for the longest ride was about 30 minutes (Pirates of the Caribbean) and for many other rides was straight in with no waiting at all. Besides the rides there is plenty of other things to keep you entertained and occupied. I was just simply having too much damn fun to let the little niggles bother me.

Magical holiday for myself, my husband, my parents and my two daughters aged 6 and 9. We have never been to America so had nothing to compare it to but we all loved our time there. Everything about the park and hotel was spot on, we couldn't fault it. The hotel offered everything we needed and the park was just magical and we managed to see almost everything. The Terror of Tower is a must for adults, definitely not for children. It frightened the life out of me! We travelled from Spain with no problems apart from our transfer from the hotel to the airport on departure was too early and there were no transfer buses, so we had to make our own way to the airport by train, which was simple. It cost us 78 Euros which we claiming back from our travel agent here in Spain as we had already paid for transfer from the hotel to airport. Otherwise an A1 holiday, one which we will never forget.

We took our two boys (6 and 5 years) for a 5 day visit, lodged at the Explorer Hotel, and hope that our experience can help smooth the visit for others. First of all, we researched as much as possible before traveling, mostly from this site. Armed with this we set off. Arriving at Charled de Gaulle airport we discovered where our research was found wanting. We had booked a return shuttle with VEA but only found that the direct service to the Explorer Hotel is just 4 times a day after being dropped off at the main central bus stop in Disney for a (free) Parks Hotels shuttle, not a good idea with luggage and a full shuttle. The hotel had the direct service timetable and on the return shuttle to the airport we had the coach to ourselves, an excellent service worth investigating. The Explorers Hotel was clean and up to date (a kettle was provided so don't bring a travel one as we did) with a reasonable selection of TV channels. Breakfast was basic continental and a lot of people took an extra portion for lunch on the go in the parks. The swimming pool is very good with a large pirate ship play area although the intermittant cascade of water knocked our 6 year old off his feet with a few resulting scratches and bruises. There was a 2 Euro charge for towel use and friends were advised to bring their own towels. The bar had a huge drop down screen for the Champions League matches but I didn't buy a drink so can't help with the bar prices. Overall, a good hotel with a free, regular shuttle to the parks and an escape from Mickey after a day of Disney. We all enjoyed the Park and Studio although planning is essential. The Fastpass system is very good (and free for most ticket types) but queues are inevitable. We took i pods with TV programmes for kids (one i pod with a splitter for two sets of headphones would be an alternative) which were invaluable in 60 minute queues. Others brought gaming systems but we saw very few books in the queues (don't know why). The Park is large and needs at least 3 days to try out the rides and go back to the favorites, 5 days is better if the (smaller) Studios is included. The most popular rides for our boys were Pirates of he Carribean (don't bother videoing the ride as it is too dark for playback), Thunder Mountain (if the queue is back to the gate the wait time is 70 90 minutes, even if the display board says 20 minutes), It's a Small World (quick queues, especially after 7pm) and Autopia (the 5 year old was allowed to drive even though he was probably too small for the minimum hight, which wasn't checked). The marketing is almost as highly refined as the production and demands will be made on the wallet, although we bought a Buzz Lightyear outfit for   6 on e bay which was 40 Euros in the Park.  In Studios the best shows were Animagique (very Disney), Cinemagique (classic cinema but still entertaining for younger ones), Moteurs Action (stunt show   not sure if it would happen if wet) and Studio Tram tour (sit on the left hand side for the best view experience). The Tower of Terror was fun for a 39 year old but our 6 year old probably won't go on it again for several years and the adrenaline was heightened when I noticed halfway through that he was gripping the belt release buckle instead of the grabrail! We were lucky with the weather, only a shower over the 5 days, but a lot of queueing is exposed to the elements so plan accordingly (ponchos, suncream, etc). We had a large breakfast, a snack at lunchtime and a meal at 4 ish each day which was affordable overall. The Village, beside the Park, has better food (the German styled restaurant was particularly good) but prices range from moderate to expensive, with the exception of McDonalds (almost at the end on the right) which was cheaper and franchise quality. My credit card wasn't accepted on first try and buying something at the airport on the journey out may help advise the bank that your card is on holiday with you. On the return through Charles de Gaule airport it is worth eating before going through passport control as there are only two small cafes on the other side which are expensive and of average quality.Overall a good experience which can be made a lot moreenjoyable and affordable with preparation and planning.

Disneyland Paris   frustrating, inefficient, inept and a total waste of money. We travelled out to Marne la Vallais to be part of Mickey's Magical Party. We booked a day's ticket for the three of us   myself and my two children for   118   ouch. On the basis of the cost alone one would have expected something fairly special.With our 'home printed' tickets we arrived at around 10am opening time on the Tuesday following Easter. The admittance procedure was chaotic and stressful with massive surging crowds around the turnstiles with very little guidance, charm or direction from the Dsiney staff. When we finally were pushed and shoved to the front of the queue, the girl on the barier managing to swipe one of the tickets twice which meant that we had to submit to an exhaustive security check as they suggested that I was presenting forged tickets!Having cleared that up, we managed to get straight onto Space Mountain with a mximum 20 minute queue and that certainly lived up to its name. An awesome Roller Coaster in the dark that totally terrified but delighted the kids!Things from that point went downhill. What my 'cheap' deal for the days ticket didn't tell me was that it excluded Fast Pass so you couldn't apply for an alloted time with Fast Pass Scheme to go on one of the more popular rides   hence saving time and minimising the queueing. The queues were on average 50 mins with everyone obediently shuffling around the little taped off sections for their 5 minute experience that rarely lived up to the hype. We spent more time in queues than we did 'having fun'. There appeared to be total indiffernce from Disneyland 'Cast Members' about the lenght of the queues or any attempt to entertain people whilst they were waiting   merely a bored gallic shrug.There were also very few Disney character is evidence. Part of the fun for the kids was to collect as many autographs as you can   brilliant if any of the characters were in evidence. We scored Wendy and Peter Pan plus a couple of Chipmunks and that was it. Not sure where the rest went, perhaps they were in hiding as I hear Mickey gets routinely mobbed everytime he puts in an appearance.Lunch though was the total joke. The kids were on for Pizza so we headed for the Bella Notte; looked and sounded promising. The system for ordering food was so chaotic that I stood in line for almost an hour before being served with microwaved lasagne, limp Pizza and a salad that was a long way past its best. The cost   40 for food that your local suprmarket would be too proud to sell you.The day was partially salvaged by an impressive Parade and a the ride (again after a marathon queue) on the Tower of Terror next door in Disny Studios. Asdie from the last hour, I wished we'd stayed in Paris and saved our money. The kids were underwhelmed too which somehow defeated the whole object.I hate to be so critical however we did go to Eurodisney about 8 years ago when the kids were younger and had a wonderful time so had high expectations. To say we were disappointed was an understatement. Its interesting that having booked online that many leisure companies are concerned about hearing feedback but not Disney. They just send you an email to sell you more stuff and experiences. The Worl famous and renowned American service culture is completely unknown here.After the prices charged and the value given in exchange   we felt a lot poorer and just a tad ripped off.

We love Disneyworld, so it was really interesting to see how they tweaked things for European market. It is not as big as Magic Kingdom in Florida or California as far as rides, but there is plenty to fill a day. Many of the rides are better because they are new. It's a Small World was gorgeous, the dolls are new and costumes clean. Everyone smokes, so brace yourself for that. The train ride out is ok. The castle is cool, can go up on second floor where it tells story of Sleeping Beauty, and it has a dungeon with dragon. Color scheme is slightly different for castle and Main Street. They built more covered areas for rain. We loved it.

We've been to Eurodisney for the second time and even if we can't feel our legs and feet our heart is full.The Hotel Cheyenne is good enough for someone not caring to much about extras but just needs a place to dump things, take care of personnal hygene and sleep. The room is clean and the bathroom OK... be aware there is no fridge and no hairdryer. Kids have a bunk bed wich always makes them happy (if they can stay on top). The Hotel has is Disney shop, Disney characters appearences and thematic scenario (which is cowboys and indians) with ocasionaly horse rides and 4 wheel pedal cars (payable).The Disneyland resort is a childs dream not just for childs. There are packages made for someone staying at Disney Hotels and going to the resorts. You should take those (free bus always comming and going to the resorts and entrance for the days payed for both resorts, Disneyland and Studios   in and out as many times as you like in a day).The ambiance is great (even if crowded). For someone like us with a small child (4 y.o.) I suggest renting a stroller for 8    the first day and pay a caution (returnable) to keep it even to the hotel. It's just on a store to your right when you get in, just after you pass under the train station.Always plan what you're going to see depending on your child's age and personnal taste. Make good use of Fastpass (only some attractions have those   you can see it in the map and by getting next to the attraction there are some machines with a sign telling you to which hours you're reserving the right to enter in a smaller queue  you put your ticket in and a Fastpass ticket comes out).
