Go see other attractions with smaller queues and comeback at the time printed on the ticket.Take one day to see the parade and the other days to get in the attractions wich have no Fastpass but always have big queues (like Autopia).Respect the signs minimum height and red triangle. They know what they're doing and you don't!! Thinking your kid is tough might get you into trouble.Don't forget to take the train around the park, Indiana Jones (which always seems out of hand or the Chaparral Theather (for the same reason)Even if it seems strange to us, kids get completly dreamy with disney characters even if they know they're not real. It comes with the  out of a dream  ambiance. Queues are long if you dont plan. You can always pay for breakfast or lunch with Disney Characters.As for the second park (Studios) I think most of the attractions are made for grownups, even Nemo's ride is too much for some kids. Depending of the age (until 7 maybe):  Stitch Live  ,  Live on Stage ,  Cars Rallye  and  Flying Carpets . The rest is to noisy, to roller coaster or movie like to be really appreciated by smaller ones.The Village outside the parks (as you walk form the bus stops to the parks) is a good place to see for stores and food drinks. Beware of the prices, but dont miss going all the way to the ballon and back.One more thing. For around 12    per adult you can take the train near the bus stops to Paris and back, also ride the metro all around Paris. It's a easy and cheap extra, unavoidable by someone that doesnt know one of the most charismatic cities in Europe.

Myself and my boyfriend visited Disneyland Paris in March 09. We had previously visited Disney World Florida back in Sept 08. Disneyland Paris had NO magic from the moment we arrived till the moment we left!!! The parks were obviously a lot smaller hence meaning longer que's compared to Florida. Fast pass was hardly open even though there was about over an hour ques for each ride. I think if you have already been to Florida you will absolutely HATE it here. There was no magic, no exact times to what parades floats would be on show (e.g. High School Musical was not even scheduled to be on show whilst there but appeared 4 times in 2 days!) the staff were very unhelpful and cold, the public (French, Germans) were very very very rude and has put me off every wanting to go back there. They had no care what so ever and were pushing into ques where we had waited for over an hour, walking into you and just being generally pig ignorant. The price of food there was ridiculously expensive compared to Florida. You are looking at paying around 15 euros for a cold burger, cold chips and watery drink. RIP OFF!! I wouldn't ever go back there and am saving my money to go to Florida again where you get much more value for money and an awesome time!!

We decided to go to Euro Disney for the Easter weekend and we can honestly say that it is NOT worth the money at all. Maybe we were overly optimistic after going to Florida a couple of years ago, but Euro Disney is so small   there are very few rides, which means horrendous queue lengths on the more popular ones. This was our first (and last) time at Euro Disney. We've decided to save up and do the 'proper' Disney experience again in a couple of years and go to Florida   at least the Americans know how to do it properly.Also, we have never encountered such a rude bunch as the French. They push in the queues at any given opportunity and when you are queuing, they quite happily push you around. If you're looking for a good theme park, go to Alton Towers, avoid Euro Disney like the plague.

We   ve just got back from a 3 day trip to Disneyland Paris with our 6 year old son, and we had the time of our lives! I   ve read a few negative reviews about Disneyland Paris on here so was a little apprehensive as to what to expect. I needn   t have worried.We travelled from St. Pancras on Sunday 5th April, on arriving at St Pancras you get a Disney pack for children, it was a good start as my son loves colouring in and drawing so this was great, as was the 3 piece brass band that was playing Disney tunes at the station. Travelling time once you   ve got on the train is only about 2    hours and whilst on the train the Disney reps give you a tag for your luggage so when you get to the station in Disneyland you just hand your bags in and they get taken direct to your hotel and you can pick them up once you   ve checked in. This allows you to go straight into the park as soon as you get there and not have to bother sorting out your hotel check in until you   re ready to do so. The reps also give you a guide to the parks and your tickets as well. Once we   d dropped off our bags we went straight to the Disneyland Park, it   s a really well maintained and beautiful place. Clean and tidy and it really adds to the magic of Disney, we walked around a bit and saw the sights and went on a few rides but all three of us were quite tired so we decided to retire to the hotel (the Santa Fe     see separate review for details!) via the shuttle bus which runs every 12 mins.On our second day (6th April) we got to the park really early, well, 08:00 to take advantage of the magic hours, this really was a superb benefit of staying in a Disney hotel as we were able to get on rides like Space mountain with just 10 mins of queuing, the Buzz lightyear ride (which we went on twice!) was just 5 mins of queuing as was the excellent Star tours ride, the other rides which are more suitable for my 6 year old little lad, i.e. the teacups, the Dumbo ride, the carousel and rides like it   s a small world only took 15 to 20 mins to get on anyway. We also went on the train that takes you round the outside of the park, this was also an enjoyable experience, we hopped of it in frontier land and my son got his photo taken with Mickey, Minnie, Goofy, Pluto and Woody, he was thrilled to bits! He also got his photo taken with Donald Duck in our hotel lobby (another advantage of booking a Disney hotel).We then went for a quick bite to eat and yeah, it is expensive to eat in the park, we went to Casey   s hotdogs on Main Street which cost us 10 euros each for a hotdog with fries and a drink, but the hotdogs are massive so we didn   t mind too much to be honest!! And let   s face it, it   s not every day you get to go to Disney so I don   t mind paying these kind of prices once in a while, and there   s a McDonalds in the Disney village if you want to eat cheaply.We then went for another walk about and onto a few more rides and watched the parade which was excellent. We left the park about 20:30 and had really enjoyed our second day there. On the third (and unfortunately final) day 7th April we visited the Walt Disney studios, and were rewarded with another fun filled day, we started off with the spectacular stunt show, this is a must see if you visit, the skill of the riders and drivers has to be seen to be believed! We also went on the Armageddon special effects experience which although loud was superb. After that we went on the studio tram tour, this was thrilling as there were various special effects which were quite unexpected but very, very impressive. I.e. when the lorry bursts into flames and then thousands of gallons of water pour down to    put them out   . A favourite of my sons though was the    Cars    ride based on Disney   s film    Cars   ! If you think of the teacups ride in the Disney land park only with cars instead you   ll get what I mean! He loved them and we went on a couple of times because the queue was only about 10 15 mins! We also went on the flying carpet ride and quite a few others as well, in this park my son got his photo taken with buzz lightyear and Emile (Remys older brother from the film Ratatouille!!) which he absolutely loved especially as Emile seemed to be a little bit of a show off crowd pleaser in    real life        we then left the studios park and went over to the Disney village to have a look around and also get a bite to eat. After all this it was time to reluctantly go home, but it was a fantastic three days, with great weather and great memories that will truly last a lifetime for all 3 of us.We   ll definitely be going back again soon.

Just came back from a 5 day holiday at disneyland paris and i loved it! My 6 year old daughter loved every minute of it but her favourite atractions were Buzz lightyear(ride it 5 times) and the haunted mansion. I was a little afraid of riding space mountain after reading some bad reviews but ignore them and enjoy it, it's not that heavy as some say. I have to warn people that want to ride crush's coaster   It's not for small children at all. The twist and turns are sometimes heavier than space mountain, believe me i rided space mountain 3 times and wouldn't go again on crush's coaster at least with my daughter. Loved animagique, cinemagique and sticht live at the studios but tower of terror is just a one time ride.Believe me. The peter pan ride was quite a deception i was expecting a lot better. Great parade don't miss it and became a fan of big thunder mountain (ride it 5 times). We met several disney characters specialy at the studios in the morning. Just returned from four days in EuroDisney. Wow! The prices are AMAZING! 17.95 Euros for a burger (cold) and chips lunch per person after a long queue. Stayed at the Vienna Dream castle Hotel   great but a small beer was 6.96 Euros and tea or coffee in room an extra 6 Euros. Had a VERY Small lasagne in Rainforest cafe and it cost 21 Euros. What planet are they on?? Merchandise pricey too. 10 Euros for a mug! Kids loved it but then they didn't have to pay. Don't go unless you have loads of money and enjoy queing. WHAT A DISSAPOINTMENT!! This was our 5th trip here and we won't be going again.It has gone downhill for lots of reasons and we felt we did not get what we had paid for.We stayed in the Sequoia Lodge Hotel which was dreary and it had no tea coffee making facilities which one would expect, I gather none of the hotels here even the 5star one have this.The TV was as old as the hotel(15 years) and only had bbc news which was repetative after an hour, in english or back to back adverts for disney! Towels were thin and small, not bath size and we had to pay 2euros each in the pool (nonrefundable), for towels, ie 6 euros a day!!None of the usual shows were on and was a huge dissapointment to our grandaughter who looked forward to them.Only one Parade which was mid afternoon, no evening parade with lights.Forget going to the park early as most rides are not open untill the main opening time of 10am and even then you can walk right over to the back of the park and find the ride you want doesn't open til 11 or 11.30.The only shop you need to go in is the main Disney shop as all the others stock exactly the same items   boring or what?Well Disney you certainly will not be seeing us again, which is a shame as in previous years we had no complaints. I wonder if you have got too big for your Mickey Mouse boots!!

I was super excited to be going to Disneyland when I was backpacking through Europe   but unbeknown to me, the day I went was in fact a public holiday.The entire experience was awful   it took me an hour to get through the front doors and then I literally had to wait an hour for each of the rides I went on   the entire 9 hours I was there I only went on three rides. I queued for 90mins to get on the Big Mountain.All in all a mediocre and very costly day.

If you are coming to Paris don't waste your time here. A truly appalling experience and one that will see your wallet empty.We went yesterday at the insistence of our 3 kids. We are living in Paris so understand all about Paris prices. First off the cost: huge and you get little for it. Add in train fares from Paris a fast food lunch and the cost all up with admission for a family of 5 was about 460 euros or about US$630. For this you could fly from Paris to Dublin and back with the family for a whole weekend. Now this huge cost might not be so bad if you actually got something for your money. The queues are massive. The electronic signs at each ride showed lines of anything from 60 minutes to 120 minutes  for a 90 second ride. There is a 'Fastpass' system where you go to the ride and register for it later that day but the time lag between registering and riding was yesterday about 5 hours and you can only register for 2 rides. End result: you are wandering around the crowds getting frustrated and wondering why you are there. Ask yourself: do you have the stomach for a queue like this, running into hours with children in tow? Or even without them.Despite best efforts of our teenagers (who like all their generation seem to know how to work the system) my kids got on only 3 rides between arriving at 11:30am and leaving at 6:30pm. We visited in early Spring on a Saturday and out of European school holidays. The mind boggles as to what it would be like in Summer at peak time.How do you fill in the rest of your time? Well there are plenty of shops selling Disney themed things (did you come to ride or buy?) and places with long queues for fast food  a gastronomic crime in a country like France.So in summary: it's overpriced by a huge margin, particularly when you consider the many magnificent attractions Paris itself has to offer; you don't get what you paid for. At 60 Euros admission per person and 3 rides per person that's 20 Euros a ride. If there were modest queues (2 hours is not acceptable!) then you might feel you had received something for your money, but that is not the case by a huge margin.So my recommendation? Give it a wide berth and visit some of the fantastic things that Paris has on offer. Don't waste your Parisian holiday here.

Despite the cost and the lines and the relentless merchandizing, it is still a treat to see your child so excited about something.I'd say the ideal age to have brought my daughter would have been 4, one year ago. She was starting to figure things out. Too clever for her own good.  Daddy, why doesn't Mickey's mouth move? It moves in the cartoons! Daddy, I think his face is plastic! However, when we met the princesses at the restaurant Auberge de Cendrillon, the magic was complete.At the Disneyland Hotel, they offered a  Princess for a Day  package where they dress up a little girl in one of the Disney princess costumes and have a professional do her hair and make up. The princess gowns they have to offer are simply gorgeous. Some of them are even NOT made in China! (but close by) I could not resist getting one for my daughter. She did not take it off the whole time. She wore it through the park every day.Advice to people who have never been to Disneyland Paris.IT IS EXPENSIVE!The food is outrageously expensive. It is really sometimes a shock!The merchandizing is intense. Brace yourselves.Unless you have money to burn. Do not stay in the Disneyland Hotel. Sure you are only seconds from the park, but I'm sure you don't mind walking 5 10 minutes to save HUNDREDS of Euro's. Also, getting in is fast, but if you want to leave the park during the day and jet back to the hotel quickly, they still make you walk around the side!You do not need to be staying in the hotel to make reservations at INVENTIONS, the restaurant where the characters hang out at night.They keep the princesses under lock & key!They do not come to INVENTIONS for dinner or breakfast!We were in the park on 4 different days and they do not meander around the park like the rest of them. If your little girl(s) want to meet the princesses, you must make a lunch reservation at Auberge de Cendrillon. Other advice:If you are looking for really exciting rides, this is not the park for you. It's more about the magic of the characters for the kids.Use the Fast Pass system. If you are not good at waiting in lines and do not have some package where you can use it, then your experience will be ruined.Had I to do it over again, I would not stay in the Disneyland Hotel and would eat more dinners offsite.

In April 2008 (nearly a year ago as I write this) Me and three friends (who at the time were all 16 17) travelled to Disneyland Paris for 4 days and three nights via the eurostar from London St Pancreas. We stayed in the Hotel Santa Fe as it was the cheapest to accomidate our rather small student budget! We arrived in St Pancreas in pleanty of time to catch the eurostar and waited in the waiting lounge for around a hour or so...the Disney expirence started before we left the UK with a small old time brass band playing well known Disney songs in a alternative style...very entertaining!The eurostar took around three hours with nice veiws all round and was a nice way to travel even with small children making a racket, but being prepared for that is a must seeing as it is Disneyland afterall. We got off at the station within the resort and caught the first shuttle bus to our hotel where we waited to check in which once you reached the front of Q was a relitative well organised and fast process. the Santa Fe is a good budget hotel to stay in if you want to stay inside the park...there was pleanty of seating at breakfast, which was very nice in it's own right, lots of bread and juice. The rooms are all in theme with the saouth american feel...It's by no mean luxury but it will do someone who is planning to stay in the parks most of the time anyway. I have to give a specail mention to the breakfast greeter who seemed almost too happy and hyper for that time in the morning but it was better then her being rather grumpy insted. The Magic hours are well worth using as we got to ride big thunder mountin twice once at the front and at the back and space mountain front and back too!We loved it, then again we love Disney...It helps if your a fanOne tip...Always use the shuttle busses to get back to Santa fe as we tried walking back one night and ended up stranded in some bushes!

after reading lots of reviews on here and after having come back from Disney I found alot not to be true.People will say you only get fast food, thats not true, there are many restaurants that are not fast food i.e. Stakehouse, Walts just to name a few.Yes it may be busy, I found best time for it not to be busy is not during school holidays or the weekend, after all it is a massive theme park, what do you expect it not to be busy and no crowds?There maybe times you will find restaurants busy but what I would suggest, book them in advance!I stayed Sunday   Sunday and found monday   thursday is the best days to be in the park when its not the holidays as not as many people and far less waiting time for the rides!Disney has a large choice of restaurants to pick from and even has the Blue Lagoon for fish lovers, I would say that there are a couple of FastFood places but most of the places are not fast food

I was surprised at the number of visitors even during off season. In the middle of March, on a rainy Sunday you had to queue 45 minutes to get on the Peter Pan ride and the ride itself takes 5 minutes... And it's expensive! You have to calculate at least 50 Euro to get there from the Airport even if you take the shuttle bus. The most crowded restaurant is the McDonalds just outside the park in the Disney village. Why? Because it's the cheapest restaurant in the area. All the other places sell overpriced junk food and it doesn't even taste good. This is the second time we went there. The first time was about 5 years ago and then it was much better mainly because it wasn't as crowded at the time. So I think I'll try to avoid the place in the future. There's much better places like Legoland or Europapark. The only good thing I can say is that it's open all year round while the other parks are usually closed a couple of months during the winter season. Also some of the new rides are very nice but again queing takes the fun out of it. I also like the fact that the park is open until 10pm on weekends.

The first thing that happens when you arrive is that security ask you to throw any drinks or food you may have in the bin. You are then invited to buy their food and drink, starting with water for    2.50 for a small bottle.The only food available was  fast  food but you'll spend a lot of time queuing for it! If I didn't have young children I definitely wouldn't go here!

not being a disney fan, i took the family over to france on the disney express expecting hell but came home smiling after 4 days worth of laughter from my kids!we went early monday morning and although we were delayed in ashford for a hour it did not dampen our spirits! we arrived and with disneys baggage service our bags were wisked off to the hotel santa fe and we enjoyed the day in the park.the hotel was clean and tidy with our only worry being the windows being able to be fully opened by the kids..not very child friendly.the continental breakfast was busy every day but if you like that type of breakfast you will be in heaven, just dont sit under speakers blasting out the park is now open messages in 10 different languages every 5 mins!make full use of fastpasses and plan your day carefully!the best rides we enjoyed were the twightlight zone   tower of terror and the rock and roller coaster in the studios park.one hint is that outside the santa fe hotel is a garage which sells a menu of 2 sandwiches, drink, crisps and chocolate for about 5 euros which was far better value than disneys chicken nuggets and chips plus drink for 9.99 euros! food and drink is very expensive there.

Really rude people and really really expensive food. We had luch on the first day at pizza planet and spent   65 just on a salad 2 small pizzas and drinks. Dinner usually came to   100. This was my third disneyland (I'm gonna try and do them all), but my boyfriends first, so I'll give a bit of a review from both points of view.Food: We were expecting to be out of pocket by a lot but were pleasantly suprised at the price. Perhaps we are used to Paris prices but we shared a Texas Assiette from Frontier Land. It comes with two ribs and a quarter of chicken in sweet bbq marinade, and it also came with wedges and churros (or brownie) and a drink. This was 11 euro 55 and we were definitely full!! (An extra euro for beer) You could buy half a chicken for 7 euro, drinks were 2,50 euro and coffee 3 euro but a huge cup.Rides: Because this was built later than some of the other disneys, it means that the designers were given a chance to tinker with the rides. Space Mountain 2 was much faster and bigger than any other I had been on, it is also one of the rides with the smallest line. Most of the rides were also traditional, for example, Swiss Family Robinson tree instead of Tarzan, and Jack Sparrow was no where to be seen in The Pirates of the Carribean. The main problem we had was the lines (and it wasn't a busy day at all) most waits were about an hour. There also seemed to be a lot of periodic technical difficulties.Weather: This park has been designed for wet weather in mind, with a lot of area for eating is undercover and there are grand arcades on either side of main street. The only problem annoyance was that it was cold outside so you had to wear a thick jacket but once inside you were warm and had to take it off and if you didnt you would get cold when leaving the ride. This looked like a problem for mothers who seemed to have enough to juggle already and there are no nets on the seats in rides to put jackets or bags in to keep them secure.One other note, is that if you are tall (over 6 ft) you may feel a bit uncomfortable in some rides as they dont allow for much leg room. My boyfriend was not going to budge in some rides as he was literally crammed in! And they are very strict on the minimum height requirements, on Space Mountain we saw three check points and one boy got to the ride after two check points and still wasnt allowed on. But overall, the first timer had a magical time and so did I, and I would recommend this Disney to anyone!P.S. No fireworks at night, but the castle does light up

I have had a good read of the reviews before placing my own and I can only conclude that some of these people are staff of the Park or have been on a staff training day or when the MD has been visiting.The park is dirty. Take a ride on the steam boat and see the litter floating on the edge of the  river  at least two feet deep and I challenge anyone to say it is clean and sparkling. The concrete on the way in is all cracked with huge chunks missing and every few minutes one of us would trip on the uneven levels.On Thursday 19th (our last day) the following rides were broken: Armaggedon, Crush, RockN Roll Coaster and Indiana Jones. These are the majority of the larger rides and most were not available for an extended period. My children had queued on Indiana Jones for over an hour when it broke down   the staff advised me that everyone had been removed from the rides but after returning from a frantic 20 minute search I found them being led out   really frightening as a parent!As we were on a short break we ate at Disney or in Disney Village every evening. We were prepared for expensive but the reality was worse than that. As we had three children 12 14 they were eating adult portions but we stuck to one course and one drink to limit expense. No meal cost under 120 euros and the most expensive was 180 euros.Even lunch was bad. 50 euros for 5 hotdogs and bottles of water!Having been when Disneyland Paris had first opened I was looking forward to seeing the changes. It is like a tired old lady needing a major operation. More needs to be spent on the upkeep and maintenance of the place and with most queues being over two hours on a chilly February day, they need to look at speeding this up.With the current exchange rate I would recommend that people think carefully about going, or be prepared to spend a lot   whatever you consider expensive   at least double it!

If you can afford it, get yourself to Florida and you will have a far better experience in the US Disney parks. Although many of the rides are similar there seems so much more to do in Florida and they just do it so much better and but more effort into helping you enjoy the experience. It seems here the queues are very long and there isn't really much to do at all in the Disney Studios park at all, after about an hour we had seen all that had to offer.The fastpass system is good and I would get some extra fast passes on eBay so you can have a better chance of doing everything in a single day and avoid the amazingly long queues. You can sell these on again afterwards.Do take your own food with you if you don't have lots of money, the food inside the park as you might expect is very expensive. The train access from Paris is really good, only took about 25 mins to get from our hotel right into the middle of the complex.All in all, it's good if you are not planning on making the trip to Florida, but doesn't match up in terms of the amount to do and the amount of effort that is put in to make the experience a brilliant one.

We went for 4 days at the end of July, in fabulous weather (which helped!). Stayed at the New York, busy but good, and that gave us VIP Fastpasses which made all the difference. Skipped an awful lot of queuing. The reort is so clean it sparkles when you get off the train. It was consistent DIsney with all the rides although Space Mountain was a lot rougher than the Orlando version.What was disappointing was Fast Pass. On Space Mountain in dark tunnels people with other Fast Passes were actually pushing people over to get ahead of them with no concern for anyone's safety.

the place is great but if we compare to disney land USA florida and universal studios it is weak but it is not fair to put them in comparison For kids it is so muchFunGreat tip and preacious as well if you want to save money burchas the tickets online not at the park if you do you will save about 15 euro for the one day one park ticket and if you purchas the one day ticket 2 parks ticket you will save about 23 euro per person cause online you buy the tickets by GPB which due to exchange rate give you diffrent exchange rate and will save you moneyWe went yesterday using the one day 2 parks ticket and we got enough time visiting all the adults interest and some of the kids as well using the amazing fast pass which help in saving time and make easy to visit both parks in one dayIt was sooooo cold so wear cloth to warm you well january is not the best month to go to disney but in the other hand it wasnt crowded which was a great advantge, as mentioned before food is expensive there but actually food in paris is expensive as well

I can not think of one good reason to recommend Disneyland Paris for English people. With the current exchange rate the prices are just ridiculous   20 for a sub standard burger and chips or   17 for a kids meal. We enquired about the buffalo bill wild west show but at   240 for a family of 4 we decided against it!!!!The queueing system leaves a lot to be desired with people (locals) pushing in all over the place and the whole experience left us moping around in the hotel for 6 hours on our last day of 3 looking forward to going home.If you are thinking about going DONT DO IT.

went,the rooms were very tired looking and in need of redecorating and ours did smell too which i think was stale smoke and lack of fresh air.we also found the rooms to be very very hot but we had 2 rooms on the 3rd floor where as our other friends were on the 4th and ground floors and they said theres was freezing.All in all though we liked the hotel as the bar was close to the childrens play area if you fancied a drink you could still see the kids playing and the ice rink was great which our kids aged 5 10 absolutely loved,It also had a great location as it was so near to walk home from the disney village where the restaurants and shops were.We stayed from Jan 18th 21st and was so lucky with the weather as it wasn't really that cold.We took loads of thermals,hats scarves gloves etc but to be honest only needed them on our last day and it only rained once for a short sharp shower.on our first day the sunday we queued for thunder mountain for 40 minutes but from the next glad that we did because everything is just so expensive especially the way the euro has dropped.We used them in Annettes diner which has a great atmosphere at night but food only so so,cafe mickey which is absolutely fantastic,food great and loads of characters coming round to each table to have photo's taken and sign the kids autograph books(we thought we had to add cash to use vouchers here but didn't have to)and the characters;mickey pluto tigger captain hook and goofy would be up on chairs singing clapping and make everyone join in it was a great night,we also ate in The lucky nugget saloon which again has the characters coming round and must say it was the best food we ate whilst there.All in all we had a fabulous time and are definately gonna go back the same time next year,we A group of us booked last November to stay 3 nights at the New York New York. To be honest I had nothing but problems from the word go.I had 2 lots of payments taken from my card which I had a terrible time sorting out as accounts there could find no trace,my bank luckily was excellent and to cap it all I received a call to say an error had been made and I couldnt go on the Eurostar as fully booked,and would have to ring them direct to sort it out unless I was prepared to pay another   50.00 to upgrade!!!!! That was then sorted when they realised I had booked as the same time as friends and just used my own card as was advised to by the representative on the phone.I was quickly dispatched with vouchers as an apology.Anyway.back to the resort. My friend and I had booked connecting rooms so that of a nite we could plan the nxt day and still keep eye on the kids.That didn't materialise, my case also had a broken lock ,it had been fine when I lugged it from the Eurostar,and the hotel handyman had to be called to break my case open as the lock was completely smashed in.The hotel rooms are not spotless and had a whiff about them,but the staff were friendly,the breakfast was nice,the 2nd breakfast room is the best,not so hectic,and larger area.The bar is opposite a small playroom with tv and crayons etc,of a night we could have a drink and still keep an eye on the children.,and the staff do turn a blind eye when they get a little boisterous.Well we are there to have fun.If your first visit I would reccommend 3 nights as there is alot to see and do,the kids get overtired and it is not such a mad rush.,arrival day is knackering.We booked the half board plus vouchers as we were worrying about the strength of the pound,and I would strongly reccommend this,it saved us a fortune!!! And the themed restaurants are lovely,especially cafe mickey 30EURO ahead without wine,and lucky nugget which had a lovely buffet and lots of character.,also our friends booked the halfboard premium and that includes Buffalo Bills,which is a must. My kids had the time of their lives  even though our 2nd visit  January is bitter,but the kids can run and explore more as not so busy.Just pack your long johns and wear warm sensible shoes.I saw so many kids not dressed warm enough and shivering.And I spoke to a few people who were shocked at how expensive it is,so plan your budget and stick to it. An adult and two children to go on the ice rink was 30 euro,so plan your iteniary.We had a marvellous time and I will be staying at the same hotel,as super location and the staff were lovely.Check it out you'll love Disney Paris

Not going to go on and on but heres a few tips, hope it helps others.We visited Euro Disney in Jan 09.Freezing cold!!!! Colder than England, take hats, thermal gloves, scarfs warm waterproof trousers and warm waterproof shoes boots.Buy your park tickets in England, we thorght we would get a better deal buying at the park or at least when we were in france but beacause of how bad the euro is against the pound it cost us a fortune.Some of the attractions were closed in the park to refurbish, we know it has to be done and January is probably a good month but you dont get a discount on your tickets!!!As already mentioned on here, people push and shove in front of you, very rude but just stand your ground!Buffalo Bills is an excellent night out, but again try and buy your ticket in England.I think 3 full days is more than enough time between the two parks.If I can help any further just email me.Kim

I went to Disneyland for the first time, I have never been in a US attraction park before so I don't have a comparison. I went in the winter and while it was pretty cold (about 4 5 degrees celcius) it was bearable. It had the added advantage that there was not much waiting at the attractions. The price for the entrance is pretty high (50 EUR) but once you are in there is lots to do. You definitely get somethign for your money. I must say the staff were very friendly, only one or two incidents and they were minor. The majority of the staff were very friendly, smiling and helpfull. Once in the park one is truly in another world. One can hardly see anything outside the park and the worst part is the rude awakening when taking the metro home. Watch out for the metro tickets as they are more expensive than a normal ticket and we got fined when arriving in MArne la Valee as we thought our regular tickets would work there. i also suggest you buy the return ticket immediately since the queu was horrendous.I am not putting and  Excellent  comment due to the food. The service and food in the fastfood restaurants is just pathetic. Any McDonalds is better than what exists here. They are slow, badly organized and the food quality litterally sucks. The price for a burger, fries and a drink is minimally 10 EUR per menu which is double what McD charges and theirs are a lot better, plus they are organized for speed. My biggest disappointment was the food, even the doughnut I bought was dry and the coffee was really bad. Frankly this being Paris   a country known for good food and pastry it is not excusable for Disneyland to have such low standards at those prices. I am willing to pay their surcharged prices but they need to do something about organizing their speed of service and quality. This place should have a starbucks or maybe 5, a few REAL fastfood restaurants like McD or any other. They need to overhaul that sector because it kills the otherwise magical experience that Disneyland is. Overall I had a fantastic day   it was fun, it was cute, it was stunning and I will definitely return.

My sister & self stayed 5days 4 nights at Explorers Hotel B&B. Recommend eurostar (not the food!) but as there was no organised queueing system on return journey it meant a scrabble to get through customs in time for departure. Overall a good value holiday. Hotel was a little shabby in public areas & breakfast a bit mediocre but i could not fault the facilities. we took our own food, rolls, cup a soups etc & locked them away in suitcase.....food is really expensive with 2 burgers salad & coke at Annettes 47euros! 2 mcdonalds meals 14euros. Recommend if you have time take the RER to the supermarket at Val de europe. Also a trip into paris 29euros for 2 people to travel on trains all over   very good value. Some of the rides weren't worth the wait but it was so cold (no gritted paths so also very slippy), we just needed to get inside. best rides were thunder mountain & buzz lightyear. scariest was tower of terror & the one that hurt my head & back was space mountain! Organisation was poor in that some rides closed because of weather but didn't let people know until you got to the entrance which wasted quite a bit of time. They cancelled one of the evening parades with only 10mins notice. I think florida isn't much dearer & generally more space & things to see. I did find it all a bit limited. If you have the money, stay in the Disneyland hotel. I do not recommend the fight to get on buses when park closes although the Explorers was the first pick up & drop off   the other hotels seem to get a poorer service. Overall I would say don't bother if you don't like crowds, queueing, crying whiny children & spending lots of cash!

Iv just come back from spending new year at Disney Land Paris, staying at the Santa Fa hotel.Firstly I would just like to say how beautiful the castle looked, iv never seen anything like it and it defiantly made my day!Disney Village is a row of shops and restaurants between the parks and hotels. This is worth a visit for souvenirs and dinning out. Whilst there we went to the Wild West Buffalo Bills show, which i can not recommend enough. It was a fantastic show, the food was good and i can not praise the staff enough. A lot of thought has been put into it, and a trip to Disney land would be a waste without going to see this show. It does say that it   s not recommended for asthmatics, and being an asthmatic myself i did not have any problems. We choose to dine at King Ludwig   s castle which was value for money, apart from the size of the meal was on the small side and drinks were expensive. I was very pleased with my overall experience of the Disney park it   s self. It always seemed very clean; i don   t remember seeing one piece of litter (unlike our English amusement parks). They   ve put a lot of effort in the main street which consists of shops and food outlets. Whilst in the park I didn   t spend much time in queues compared to what i was expecting due to it being such a busy time of year. I would recommend using the fast pass service which is available for all Disney visitors; it cuts out so much time!Haunted Manor was a fairly good ride, not very scary but they have made an effort with it. My favourite part being the head statues that seem to talk and the holograms of ghosts and ghouls. Indiana Jones Temple of doom was very good but once again not very scary. Pireates of the Caribbean ride was very good, and liked all the detail they had put into the ride. Also got to meet Jack Sparrow just near this ride, who was a very good impersonator of the real one. Peter pan ride and Pinocchio ride were alright although a bit basic, but then these are rides for children. Its a small world ride was very good and impressed with all the different figures from around the world... really did get the sense that its a small world after all! Space Mountain mission 2 was very fast and defiantly liked all the lighting effects at the end, but found it bashed me about a bit to much, giving me a headache for the rest of the day. Star tours was very impressive. They have put a lot of effort into the different figures whilst you queue up such as C3P0 and R2D2. Honey I shrunk the audience was defiantly worth a visit and was amazed at the effects used with the cinema. Overall i was very pleased with my day in the Disney Park and would defiantly go back again.We also saw Cinderella and prince charming on our travels. We spent new year   s eve in the Blue Lagoon restaurant which is based next to the pirates of the Caribbean ride. We had an 8 course meal which was fantastic although it wouldnt have been to everyone   s taste. They had different types of entertainment to keep you amused to. Would recommend the fantaillsion parade, where all the loved Disney charters are on floats lighted up.I must say that i preferred the Walt Disney studios. I thought the stitch live was fantastic and was gob smacked when stitched started to talk to the people in the audience (it really is live). Both the Animagic and Cinemagic were very good and well worth a visit. I was amazed at the car stunt show, very impressed with all the stunts and once again recommend watching this! Was a bit disappointed with the Nemo ride, considering we queued for 2 hours.... they could have done a lot better i think. The Hollywood tower of terror was defiantly the scariest ride at Disney Land, and it doesn   t help being able to see over the park just before the lift drops you to the ground!Sorry for the long review, but really didn   t want to leave anything out. To conclude any person aged 1 to 99 will find some magic at Disney land and well worth a trip!!

We stayed at the recommended Disney Hotel the Dreamcastle Hotel from December 22nd to 29th and visited the parks for 6 days. As a family of four with a 5 and 2 year old we were going to Disney for the magic of the Disney Characters and the parades. We found these to be very good and my 5 year old daughter was enraptured when she got to cuddle Minnie, her favourite character. Fake snow down Main Street was lovely.Overall, however the park was very busy and hence the queues for most rides ridiculous. In Fantasyland we queued for 90 minutes for the Dumbo ride and instead of enjoying the ride the children were in tears by the time they got on. The Peter Pan ride was also a disappointment   no special effects and jerky movement. It's a Small World did not disappoint and we only queued for 20 minutes to get on this. We saw most of the shows our favourites being Cinemagic and the Stunt Show. The shows with the characters were good but confusing for our 5 year old as they were half in French, half in English even the songs. The Legend of the Lion King Show had specific shows for English or French which is a better idea. We found the rides in the Disney Studios to be good   esp the Aerosmith Rollercoaster, (don't even bother with Space Mountain   this one is much better and queues are less), and the Hollywood Tower. We also thought the Babyswitch system was excellent. This enabled my husband and daughter to queue to go on a ride and when they had been on it I could get on within 5 mins by going through the Fast pass entrance. People with little ones   use this service. We found the French people very friendly and there was not much shoving and if someone did step in front of you in a queue then we stepped straight back in front of them   livens up the wait anyway! I do think the park looks a little tired. It was a lot to pay for a bit of Disney magic at Christmas and this is all that was worth it really. Fast rides can be found at Alton Towers in the UK   no need to go all the way to France, especially seeing as most could do with updating. Finally the food costs as we expected were terrible. Also the quality of food, (which is mostly burgers and chips) is dreadful. My husband queued for 20 mins to get these for lunch in Disney Studios and when we took a bite the burgers were stone cold resulting in having to go and get replacements all round. Coffee and hot chocolate is 3 euros a cup. I would not return to Disneyland Paris in a hurry. Characters aside, it needs to be updated and the food outlets need improving. Florida here we come.

We took a tour bus to Paris Disney in October 2008. There was two parts. We did both parks very well and had time to spare.We were there when it open and left at 7:00 pm. The rides are very similar and were very disappointing to me. Over all because I have been to Disneyland and Disney world. I would rate this park for me a two out of five. The best ride was the tram tour.I love Cimagitic which should be a must do for all.

I've been to Disneyland several times and I've loved every single one... The first two times I was just a child and I went with my parents but now that I grew up I go to Paris at least once a year and Disneyland is a  must go  place everytime!Although I have read some bad reviews about it I honestly can't understand... I must say that Disney is a magical place for all ages (I loved it when I was 4, I love it now that I'm 20)... You have an excelent staff, very helpfull, amazing attractions (for all ages) and the Disney movie  gang  always near you (not only Mickey and Minnie but also Lilo & Stitch, Remy from Ratatuille, I name it). It's true that there are some periods of the year when the park is really crowded (especially during the Summer), but that is expected and if one want to avoid qeues go during the winter (February it's a nice month to go... It's cold but not to much and there aren't almost any qeues). Personally, I must recommend that you don't miss the second park (Disney Hollywood Studios) and, in this park go to Aerosmith Rock'nd'Roller Coaster, the Twilight Zone Hotel of Terror and Cinemagique (this last one is a show about the evolution of cinema... GO, you will love it). At Disneyland, don't miss Space Mountain, Indiana Jones, The Haunted Mansion, It's a small world and take a ride in the 1920's boat!Overall, I trully love Disney and I give it my highly recommendation! Trully, a place where Dreams come true!

We were offered a really good deal for an early December trip to Disney, Paris and decided to go. Then after reading on here wondered had we made a really big mistake?Nope, it was great!The weather was shockingly cold, but Disney turn on the Christmas magic and then you forget all about the weather.The good: The snow every hour on main street, how magical! We loved this.The parades, especially the fantalusion at night. Fabulous floats with lights and all our favourite characters. It  snows  then as well.The organised character meets. We found very little pushing and shoving and mostly well organised queues.The Christmas decorations were beautiful and the carols were really lovely.The park was very clean and constantly being swept by attendants.The pre entry for hotel guests was very good and only allowed on presentation of special pass from the hotel.The Father Christmas area was gorgeous, all snowy and Christmassy. Very nice. Especially since there was a hot drinks stand to get a cup of, very nice, hot chocolate from whilst queuing.Disney Studios is good fun too, especially the rock and roller coaster! My son loved the cars ride and would have stayed on all day.The Bad: The queuing for the Father Christmas visit! My God but this was awful. It turns out the Continental guests were letting their children see Santa have pictures, taking around 10 mintues for this and THEN the Parents were sitting on Santas knee as well! Astounding. It was taking between 10 20 mintues per family group and there is only one Santa for the park on duty at anyone time. Very frustrating, especially since just as you got near the front, the attendant would rush up and push you back out of the cabin! The Father Christmas was very good though, looked just like him.The park is in need of a few touch ups here and there but nothing major.The sheer ignorance of some of the other park guests was astounding! Not just the continentals either, but a few Brits as well. One of whom swore at me as I tried to move my son out of her photograph! That being said though the Continentals were far and away the worst at pushing, shoving and trying to queue jump. That is not Disney's fault though. I never had these problems at the California Park, but I think it is a cultural problem.Some of the staff can be a bit rude, but you just have to remember that although Disney is American the staff are not.If you are going to watch the parades, especially the last one I do recommend you sit on the rope half an hour before for the best views and hold your ground.Would we go back? Yes absolutely, we may even go next summer. Overall we had a really lovely time, much better than we expected.

We recently stayed in the disney hotel paris, we'd been to disney last year and stayed in the explorers hotel. Great hotel no complaints about it at all. However this year we decided we'd treat ourselves to the disney hotel. Got the VEA bus from the airport to the hotel we where the last people off the bus walked into the hotel reception straight away noticed we where missing a bag I had seen the bag on the bus when I was getting off my partner got off after me leaving his bag behind ran back to bus it was pulling away another bus was pulling in and this driving rang the driver of the bus we just got off to say the bag was on the bus he said he'd be right back. There was no one else on the bus except the driver we never got the bag back or expensive equipment inside. We reported this constantly to the hotel staff and repeated requested that the luggage room be checked. In fact we went 7 times about it and at no stage would anyone look in the luggage room for us. We knew ourselves it had already been stolen at this stage but would have been nice just to check for us.Upon request we met the manager of the disney hotel who was helpful organising a translator and transport for us to the Police station to report the theft. I will also add at this point that the items stolen are security marked.We where very disappointed with the response from disney and their hotel staff at no point did we get an apology or even upon checkout where we asked about or updated about the situation.We changed our room in the hotel 3 times and still ended up looking out into a bush which would you believe was the best of the 3 rooms . This wasn't even offered to be changed for us after our ordeal.  We where attending a birthday party in disney and had dinner in the hotel restaurant to celebrate this costing    75 each for buffet food not my idea of a good meal. We also had dinner with the princess in the park    55 each fantastic well worth the money and would recommend this. I will say in favour of the disney hotel great opportunities to meet the characters and great breakfast selection well organised. However we will not be back to this hotel and I would not recommend it to anyone else.Warning please be careful of your belongings on VEA buses

Well, it was last chance saloon with our son, who's nine going on 40   last chance for us to relish in his excitement over Mickey and more importantly this time..Father Christmas. Yep, he was there at Euro Disney and you know what   he was brilliant. Infact, despite the cold, harsh weather and the torrential rain, only Disney can make you forget all about it and enjoy yourself. The family stayed at New York, which is apparently the second best (I have my reservations about this   The Disney Hotel is definately the no.1, and the Newport Bay Club, no.2 in my book). Hotel SummaryNot as good as I would expect   It just didn't have the magic of the other 'big two'No Tea Coffee making facilities in roomMini Bar (as you'd expect) prices are extremely expensive. Big clean rooms.Great Ice rinkI haven't focused on the hotel   for us it was merely a base   for others it may be an integral part of the experience. I loved the fact that you could walk 10 minutes out of the hotel and be in the park. I loved that you could enter the park 2 hours before everyone else   a huge bonus for the up ahttps:  tonic.tripadvisor.com SavedPhotos g189258 i18801380,18801381 w1 Marne la Vallee Ile de France.html 18801380nd outers.The Park was brilliant   the staff extremely friendly. My parents used to live in Florida, so Disney world was a biannual experience for us   However, Paris does it better. I'm convinced of it   because it's smaller, it feels more intimate. The weather played a huge part with the crowds   so queueing times were never more that 15 minutes. (see photo)Of course, with every positive, must come a negative. The cost of food, beverage etc. is ASTRONOMICAL! Take lots of money. And then take some more.All in all, what a great experience  and thoroughly recommended.

This place has left me with amaizing memories. You approach the park and the first thing you see id Disney Hotel you walk under and you are at the enterance, Main Street USA and oldy world type street, American themed oldfashioned shops, at the top of Main Street USA is the Sleeping Beauty Castle, you can walk up which we did sometimes, only takes a few mins of for fun you can jump onto the transport which were old style police and fire vehicles, also an oldfashioned wagon. Through the castle is the beginning of the theme park, it is split into different lands, some are the great old classics like Snow White and Peter Pan, nice merry rides. There are all different rides throughout the park, Buzz Light Year was fun you ride around and have to shoot enemis for points!!!! Honey I shrunk the audience was a great experience, not a ride but a visual experience, u really feel like have been shrunk!!!! In adventure land there is like a fun park where you explore and walk over chain bridges and trough caves, also here is the Pirates Of the Caribbean ride we went on this, a nice ride, lots to see, we went on it loads as ques wernt too bad. We went on most rides and all were fun and memorable, all different. We saw plenty of characters and had lunch in The Lucky Nugget where there are lots of characters visiting your table. Parades were good, although people arrived in good time to ensure a great view, Im not one for standing around so always arrived a few mins before the parade and could see and hear fine!!! The atmosphere is buzzing all day and there something going on aroud every corner. On our second day the park had changed its theme to Christmas and it was amaizing, snow, trees, decos everywhere!!!! The castle was lit up pink (as always at night,) and had extra lights on which looked like it was drenched in Diamonds, it really took my breath away!!!! As we were leaving that night, we walked down Main street USA and it started to snow (artificial) and it really brought a tear to my eye, the thought that is put into this park is magical, it really makes a very memorable and magical trip!!!! Cant wait to go again....and again..... and again.............. WOW!!!!!

I love Disney, I mean who doesn't?I have had the opportuntity to go to Disneyland Paris 5 times this year with my 6th trip coming up in Janaury. We love it. My 3 year old daughter adores the place, seeing her little face light up when she sees mickey is worth the money.Yes the food is expensive, which is why it pays to get Half Board vouchers before you leave as you save up to 15% of what you would pay when you get there.I would recommend Cafe Mickey, this is a traditon and we always eat here. Celebrating a Birthday here is so much fun.Don't go expecting it to be like Disney World in Orlando because it isn't, Disneyland Paris is a thousand times better in my opinion. Walt Disney Studios is slowly becoming a great 2nd park, with new rides and attractions being added. This is the only place that I will take my little one on holiday and we are excited about going back in January...so excited that i have already booked up for 2009 aswell.

We went on an organized Social club trip to the Santa Fe hotel Disneyland Paris.Having never been to a Disney Resort before I had an open mind.When we arrived by coach at the Sant   Fe after a trip of over 12 hours we were all very tired and I was dreading queuing up to check in but as soon as we pulled up a man came to greet us with a pack with the key to are room in and details of the hotel and park tickets. So within 10 mins of arrival we were in our room. The room was clean and reminded me of a Travel inn Mexican style but it did us fine. We brought a travel kettle with us so we could make a hot drink.At 8.30 pm we just wanted a snack but were unable to get a bowl of chips in the Sant   Fe so we had to venture in to Disney village were we had a Panini and a drink. Very expensive. The next day we were in breakfast at 8.00am and after a sort queue was greeted by a charming lady who asked if we had been before and told us what to do.After reading reviews on this site we took the advice given and at breakfast made up some bread rolls with ham for our lunch. We had brought some crisps and snack bars with us. This saved us a lot of money and time as we were able to just sit and eat.After breakfast it was off to the Parks. No problem with the buses a sort wait and a 5 min ride took us to the park. We decided to go to the Disney Park first and got on an old bus that took us down Main Street towards the fairy tale castle. Park was fantastic. My thanks to all cast staff for making it a great day.In the evening we decided to eat at the Sant   Fe and try the all inclusive food menu for 23 Euros. There was plenty of choice and the food was plentiful and well presented but a have to say that my wife and I thought that it could have been warmer. After dinner we went to Disney village to watch the fireworks and bonfire.The next day it was time for Disney Studios fantastic. Again thanks to all the cast staff for a great day. I thought that the stunt car show should get a special mention because as the show was coming to a climax people started to walk out and not clap to show there appreciation of what was for me a brilliant show WELL DONE.The final thing we done on the Saturday night at 18.30 was the Wild West show and what a night. The food was good the Clown on our Texas team was great and as for the horse riding UNBELIEVABLE. After the show we went back to the park and watched the Xmas parade and to see the Xmas tree lights turned on. What a end.ConclusionsThe food and drink at Disney is not cheap but if your only there for a couple of days go for it.I have not been to America so this is my only experience of a Disney park and I have to say my family had the time of our lives. My thanks go to the staff. It only took a couple of days to recover.

Well Disney Land Park in Paris is one of the best amusement parks I have ever seen till date. My experience had been awesome. My friends were simply not wanting to go away from the park even after the park was about to close. Oh...yes..How can I forget to mention the guy dressed up as Disney. He was just awesome..!

Not up there with the Florida California versions, but enjoyable none the less, partly because we went for Halloween and it was fun with lots of pumpkins and Disney villains. The service wasn't up to the American standard, but was good. Of course, it rained!We stayed at the Disneyland Hotel and, although it was more expensive, I'm glad we did. It was so quick to exit the park and the get back into the hotel room. Service was good and having the characters around at breakfast completely made the stay for my 2 year old. However, the pool was a littel on the cool side and I wouldn't order room service under any circumstances   25 euros for a club sandwich! No water or tea making facilities in the room, but you could get a kettle from housekeeping.Overall, worth a visit but expect it to be expensive, rides good, characters good for younger visitors, not much at Disney Studios.

What   s so amazing about this place? OK, at the first glance, it gave us high expectations with the castle spires sticking up in the sky. But as getting closer, it was nothing but a theme park with boring constructions of what been picked out from the cartoon pictures. Too many people, too expensive (45     person), too boring and nothing impressed either me or the children. Queues on the high way to the park, queues to get a parking place, queues to buy the expensive entrance tickets, queues to be seated by a lunch table, 20 minutes only to be attended by the waiters, another 30 minutes to get what been ordered, queues to race attraction. The shortest time was 40 minutes to the attraction for the smallest children, the most popular attraction (Indiana Jones roller coaster) had a 120 minutes queue time! Is it too arrogant to expect the staff to at least know how to calculate when working as cash personnel? I know that we are in France and not to expect people to be able to speak English even though the Disney thing is an American concept. But do at least hire someone who can calculate what to give back on a 20 Euro bill when the customer is to pay 12 Euro   ? Or do I expect too much?Our children 9 and 11 years old hated the place and couldn   t see anything exciting about it. Relieving for us. We rather spend time in Liseberg in Gothenburg or Grona Lund in Stockholm next time, far more worth the money, time and much more amusement for our kids   and our selves. Sometimes it takes a disappointed experience like this to see that the grass is not greener on the other side   .Going back there, most likely not.

Just come back from fourth visit to Eurodisney.  First time went over a weekend and it was manic!!  Second time was just a day trip whilst on holiday elsewhere in France, at Christmas time and it had a magical atmosphere.  Third time was much better, we went by Eurostar and as the kids were older we just had normal luggage (humped around by hubby!) We went Mon to Thurs and it was quieter and we had a good time  Fourth time, again we went Mon to Thurs, it was Halloween theme which they did really well. Loved the parade, we were mainly in fantasyland as my kids don't like rollercoasters and we were with my 2year old niece. We managed to get on all rides within 20mins. The tea cups, we just went and got straight back on each time. It helped that my kids have two weeks half term so we could go the week most schools hadn't broken up yet. I would advise going during term time though, if you are allowed to.Good points: We got on everything we wanted. The atmosphere was generally charming. Didn't witness as much queue barging as I have done before. Kids loved it all.Bad points:   We were spoken to really rudely by a cast member. Did you know that you can't complain about anything to Disney? They've had so many lawsuits that now they ignore all complaints! Anyway, so I just have to let that one go and not let it spoil the holiday.   expense, with the euro so strong it was even more heavy on our pockets!Eurostar only:  getting from eurostar up to the way out. Our party consisted of me, my sister and my mum plus an 8 year old, 6 year old, 2 year old and 10 week old, so a pushchair, pram and four suitcases to contend with. There was absolutely no help whatsoever in getting off the train and getting up to the concourse., it was a nightmare!!  going through security and getting back down to platform, again a nightmare. There were no luggage trolleys so again we were struggling then we had to get everything through the xray machine, including pushchairs etc. one still had a balloon tied to it! Trying to hold a baby, stop kids run amock and get coats off, remove metal items and find it all the other side was ludicrous.Anyway, nothing you can do about it, just a warning to brace yourselves!!I have given three stars because of the cast member and the fact that no one will listen to you if you just want to say what happened. I'm not sure I will go again.

This is our third time to Disney in the past 15 years and i feel it getting better all the time, We travel by car and stayed at the Dream castle which was excellent, To enjoy Disney paris you must remember several things ! These are you are now in Europe so do push and shove it's what the Frence and Germans do, if not you wont't get anywhere ! Expect to pay higher prices this is Disney and you near Paris so cost will be higher, Also prepare for the wether to be chilliy, we went on the Ocotber 12th for 2 nights & 3 days and the park was wouderful in it's holloween season my 4 year old daughter loved it and remember it's a place you visit only a few time in your life, so take the pain of a folking out money and take a look of you kids faces you will see it's worth every penny,

We have visited Disney paris about 6 times and Disney Florida 3 times with adults and children so can compare both. We have not found the food over priced if you rember you are just outside of Paris. Ate a great buffet at Billy bobs in Disney village had a few great meals at Crystal palace resturant in the park.Prefered the Santa Fa atmosphere, Cheyenne was great for kids Sequia was more money and not very friendly rooms were no bigger than the cheaper hotels. Breakfast was fine but it is a mad house with everyone trying to eat at the same time. You are supposed to book a time but who wants to be stuck with a 30 min breakfast block on vacation. Also remember that at Diseys in USA breakfast is not included. Also there are characters in th hotel at breakfast which is lots better than waiting for an hour to see them in the parks. Yes the bus,s are crowded but the parks are all next to each other so you can walk to each. Where as in Disney world most of the time you have to bus hotel to park then park to hotel to catch a bus to a different park because the buses do not go from park to park and if you do not pay for a park hopper pass you can only go in one park per day.If you have any problem with the language Staff at Disney paris wear pins with flags of the languages they speak.Also please remember that Disney has been around way longer in USA than in Europe so the people there do get more excited and wil push crowd and shove to be in front we even saw 4 parent s fighting trying to get small children onto the Dumbo ride firstLiked the pirates ride and big thunder mountian more in Paris than in Florida.The worst thing with these places is you find out all the tips on your last day then you know where you should have gone first and what the best food places are. Most of all just remember you are on vacation Enjoy it

We went to Disneyland Paris last nov stayed in Sante Fe hotel. Christmas set up was fantastic , weather very cold , colder than uk would recommend staying in the park and if you can afford it Hotel NewYork which is excellent. Sante Fe is good basic, but a 20 min walk or 10 min on shuttle bus. would advise that you book your meals in advance as you save about 15% and would recommend treating your self and eating in the hotels in disney. Generally a set price 20 Euros for a three course and 12 euros for kids depending on which hotel, the new york will be a higher set price than Santa Fe if budget is tight the Sante Fe is a fine place to stay. Also the disney shops are fantastic and much better than those in the UK when we returned we wanted to buy some things we had seen in Paris but couldnt as they dont stock it in ukwe had the most wonderful time

We have been to disneyland paris for 5 years and each time has been as wonderful as the last.We always go at christmas time and we warned its cold, cold, cold, so wrap in lots of layers and comfortable shoes!!The parks first stop on entering is main street usa, my son and i always feel like we are in a disney cartoon at this point, the lanterns and music is very atmospheric indeed, and the old cars which drive up and down can be ridden in wait outside of the information centre at the top of main street and the vehicles will stop to collect you and drive you to the castle.the smells in main street are wonderful the scent of fresh bakery and hot chocolate fills the air.most people go into frontierand first so i would suggest doing things back to front and go to discovery first and fastpass space mountain to avoid queues, and wander around this land not forgetting its a small world which is great.Fantasyland is the land which the little ones love the most being home to dumbo, teacups etc, here at christmas there is oftain a christmas village which sells gingerbread and hot drinks etc, there is a stage show here near the railway station.the next world round is adventure which is home to pirates of the carribean so fast pass this one and step out of the cold this ride is always so so warm and you ride by the blue lagoon resturant, which is great for its seafood dishes.there is a great walk around the caves here although at this time of year can get icy so do be careful.frontierland is home to thundermountain use your fastpass here again to skip queues, and go to phantom manor which is wonderful might be a bit frightening for those little people!There is a train ride which goes round the whole park it stops at each land and is a great way of saving your feet.Get a guide for the parade times the christmas parade is a must and as it gets cold this is the time to buy a hot drink, and father christmas is on his sleigh during this parade.disneyland studios is a smaller park although it is always expanding with new rides crushers coaster and the towers hotel were new in 2007, the rides in this park are more older children and adult themed, rock and roller coaster, armegeddon, the towers hotel, etc. there is a parade here so check the times in the park when visiting, the backlot tour is great so dont miss it, so is the stunt show.the disney village is a walk from the park and have lots of resturants here, planet hollywood, annetts diner , mickeys, rainforest cafe and mac donalds, planet hollywood i would recommend they do a fixed price menu which is great and the ice cream is wonderful, rainforest cafe is on the more costly side but is a real experience.Buffallo bills wild west show is a must for any visit to disney we have been on Disneyland Paris is really a great place to stay for a short vacation or daytrip! A comparison with Disney World is very difficult to make. In Disneyland Paris all big rides are divided over 2 parks, in Disney World you'll need to visit 4 parks. That takes much more time and more money! A two day hopper pass for Disneyland Paris costs 108 euros (for 129 euros you have an annual pass). A two day hopper pass for Disney World costs 150 euros (an annual pass 350 euros).Some of the most popular rides from those 4 worlds of Disney World can be found in Disneyland Paris. Most of those rides are even improved. Space Mountain in Disneyland Paris is the best Space Mountain experience. The same can be said for Big Thunder Mountain. Buzz Lightyear Laser Blast with detachable laser canons is much more fun. In the Studios Park the cast members of The Tower of Terror still play their role as crazy bellhop for a complete experience. You will experience better parades in Disneyland Paris. Nice and big floats and good music everywhere along the parade route. It really gets you in the mood. Some people complain about the castmembers of Disneyland Paris. I think it depends on who you are dealing with. In Disneyworld it's much more easy for them to help because speaking English is sufficient. In Paris the visitors are much more diverse in their language. My experience with Disney World was that many of the cast members were elderly people who are kinda slow. Cast Members in Disneyland Paris are mostly in their 20's or 30's. I admit that visitors in European parks are more rude in their behaviour than in the U.S. That's got nothing to do with Disneyland Paris. Cutting in line seems to be a hobby for some Europeans. Food prices are much higher in Paris due to expensive euro or cheap dollar. Let's say they are normal for amusement parks. Disneyland Park Paris really is a nicely created park. It's compact but every ride has it's themed space. It's got the beautiful Disneyland hotel as entrance, the big Sleeping Beauty Castle (which looks very fairy tale like), the mysterious Haunted Mansion building, the Big Thunder Mountain that goes under the water, the impressive Space Mountain building with Jules Verne theme, the classic Walt's restaurant which looks over Main street. It's got two of the best park shows  The Legend of The Lion King  and  The Tarzan Encounter  and really nice parades. And it's got a real Christmas period with the winter cold and (sometimes) snow that makes the fairy tale complete. In the Studios Park next door you will find some unique attractions like Animagique, Cinemagique and Crush Coaster. Those together with the Tower of Terror are the best rides of the park. The Moteurs...action! Stunt show spectacular! was even brought to Disney World after it's succes in Paris.Other big rides in this park are Rock 'Roller coaster, Armageddon special effects, Studio Tram Tour and Stitch live. Playhouse Disney: Live on Stage! will be opening early 2009.Besides it all you have the most romantic city with it's rich cultural history next door; Paris!In Disney World you will get more rides, more (night)shows, more fireworks, more sun. But it wil cost you more time and money than Disneyland Paris. You wil get a whole other experience. Disneyland Paris is for a short stay with a lot of fun rides packed into 2 parks and some really nice themed hotels around it. Disney World is vacation on a complete Disney Resort isolated from the rest of the world with the Florida sun in the sky. Everything you want to know about Disneyland Paris can be found at this great fan site http:  www.dlrpmagic.com

My wife and I first went to Eurodisney within a few weeks of it opening in 1992, and with no experience of anything to compare it with we were impressed. The crowds weren't silly, the staff were friendly, the rides were geat (I still love Thunder Mountain!), Disney characters wandered around the park, and some of the restaurants rest areas had some great entertainment   I recall stopping for lunch somewhere and being entertained by a fantastic country band. Overall a good experience.Fast forward to 1996 and I went again as part of a corporate event and stayed in one of the Disney hotels. Again, the crowds weren't bad (though it was February), there was some fantastic entertainment around the park, and overall I enjoyed the trip.The next time I went was in 2002, with my 6 and 7 year old daughters. OK it was the summer holidays, but the crowds and queueing were beyond belief. Forget using the park railway, the queues for that were impossible so we walked, and walked, and walked. On top of the crowds I was disappointed that the Disney characters and entertainment I'd seen on previous trips had gone. The kids enjoyed some of the shows, but we struggled to get on more than 2 or 3 decent rides. Overall a disappointing day out.Our final (and we'll never do another one) trip to Disney was in 2006. We went at a different time of year thinking that keeping away from the summer holidays would keep the crowds down. Well, we paid the E180 or whatever it is to walk through the doors, and soon wished we hadn't. Crowds everywhere, 90 min queues for the popular rides, and E10 for a disgusting burger. Never never again, my kids were very upset by 3 4 pm as we'd only mangaged to get onto a handful of rides due to the overcrowding. We've no intention of ever going back again, the only way I'd go back is if Disney pay me and it would need to be a decent amount too! Also, be aware that if you're visiting the park by car you'll end up parking about 20 30 minutes walk from the park entrance. I've tried to balance the review as in the early days I enjoyed going there, but the park has lost a lot of the charm it had and seem to me to be overly greedy in exploiting families who feel that a trip to Disney is compulsory. Well it isn't!

If you've been to DisneyWorld, FL....you must remember   this park is in Europe, not the States. I still rate DisneyWorld as my favorite. However   realize this park is for Europeans, NOT Americans. But, Disney Paris does a great job with all the different visitors. First, this park is right off the RER A line, for those coming from the city of Paris. Its literally RIGHT off the train line. I was surprised by how close it was. It was 6.45 Euro per each ride on the RER from the city. Great for a day trip if you want a city break. Most of the Disney cast members do speak some English, so that was a break. The Disneyland Park, not the movie park next to it, is basically the same design as Magic Kingdom. Some things looks the same, but the Park is catering to a wide range of languages (English, French, German, Italian, etc..) so the two languages on the ride are French and English. Phantom Manor aka Haunted Mansion, has no narration in the ride cars, and has some notable difference. Space Mountain 2 was a hoot, worth the wait, and the Pirates of the Caribbean ride is not the updated ride that exists in DisneyWorld. Over all, I had a blast in the Disneyland Paris. For those who commented that the food prices are high   have you seen the high prices in the US parks???? Seriously, its expensive to eat in Paris itself, what's the surprise there? I was able to eat well on 20 Euro a day for all 3 meals, but I didn't do any sit down restaurants and took advantage of the water fountains dotted around. Highly recommend if your in the Paris area, or want a Disney fix if you live in Europe. For future trips, I now know the Eurostar goes straight to the Disney resort area and won't bother with a hotel in Paris and taking the train over.

I prefer this park to the Florida's park. It has better rides and feels like a nicer place to be. It can be done in a day but you may miss a few things out. Food was overpriced but its a theme park, there all expensive!The fireworks at the end of the day were a little disappointing, but I think that may be something to do with Disney and local residents complaining but dont quote me on that. This was the first theme park I ever went to back in 1995, my first rollercoaster ride was on the space mountain which is now even better and it got me hooked, you have to visit this park at least once, you will be hooked too.

We purchased tickets for Mickey's Not So Scary Halloween Party after being told by Disney Customer Service that it would be an amazing night of fun, with trick or treating and tons of candy for the kids.
