I'm 60, and with my wife, 2 adults, and their 4 children. went for 4 days, by EuroStar ( very good ). We paid for us two and one of the grandchildren, and the holiday cost us   1700. One meal for all of us, average quality and quantity, one evening was   150, and a burger bar lunch next day for me, my wife and one grandchild was nearly   50. What a shame, as it spoils what is in fact an enormously enjoyable time for all ages. We went on Space Mountain, Buzz LightYear, It's a Small World ( 4 times ! ), the teacups, magic carpet ride and other 'little children' rides, and many more, and I have to say, the quality and choice of entertainment is superb. We read loads of reviews so had a good idea what to expect both good and bad. We went for 4 days in August and expected it to be busy, it got manic towards end of week but was not too busy otherwise. Fastpass is the way forward for some of the rides, you must use this facility as its included with your guest pass if you stay on site. We stayed in the Sequoia Lodge and it was clean and pleasant and only 10 minute walk from the Park. Upon arrival check in was reasonably quick and as they couldnt get us into a good time slot in restaurant for breakfast we requested to have breakfast in the park , this turned out to be a great move. I dont think all the rides operate at this time but you can get on one or two and line yourself up before the rush begins.We ate once in the hotel, at the buffett in the evening, and it was great as it gave us all plenty to choose from, we all stuffed ourselves and felt it was reasonable value.We were disappointed with the Character breakfast as there were not that many characters compared to a friends visit earlier in the year.The night parade and fireworks were fab and worth staying up for. An indulgence for sure but worth it.

Have just returned from 3 days at the Parks and all I can say is   AMAZING! It is such a magical place and I did not want to leave. We're a US based, Disney loving family (Probably a dozen Disney World or Disneyland visits in the past 15 years). This was our 2nd Disneyland Paris trip   the first being just 2 years after opening...   with a 13 year gap in the middle...With good base of Disney knowledge, what I can say is this:The good: *Park is especially beautiful and well themed in spots   Frontierland, Fantasyland, for instance, may be the best of the bunch....   and the front plaza, before the Disneyland Hotel (at entrance) is really great looking... *The Phantom Manor is the best of the 3 Haunted Mansion variations we've been to... Same for  It's a Small World *Great to get a little Disney into a Euro vacation... A good day trip   but nothing more.The bad:* The Disney Studios theme park is Disney's biggest embarrasment ever... Instead of building a new, beautfiul park, they built it on the cheap and it shows   with nothing more than a handful of big buildings with recycled movies and shows from other parks   and a few shells of buildings outside to represent Hollywood (vs. a full fledged street of buildings at California Adventure and Disney Studios in Florida. Awful. *Pirates of the Caribbean is a great looking building and theme   outside   but the weakest of the 3 we've been to on the inside   with no Jack Sparrow added, as in the US.*The park is in a terrible state of disrepair in many areas   from peeling paints on rides and hotels, to mold and dirt on walls, to clumps of dust on rides, etc...   things that would NEVER be allowed to happen in Disney US parks. Attention to detail!*And   above all   the lack of rule enforcement was shocking. In the US parks, Disney is notorious strict on rules and guidelines... You wait your turn, you stand in line, you don't go in restricted areas, you don't smoke except in designated areas, etc... Park patrons cannot stand on chairs or climb flag poles or jump over fences, etc... to watch parades, etc..   or you will be shut down, in seconds, by park security... and or escorted away.... You just don't do it.... At Disneyland Paris   the crowds did whatever they wanted   from pulling chairs out of restaurants onto the sidewalks and standing on them to watch parades   to jumping over fences to get on a hill for a better view, to having a picnic or smoke (neither of which are allowed) when and where they wanted... The park workers did NOTHING to combat this... Nothing... . Very un Disneylike... I wonder if the park just gave up enforcing rules years ago   due to European tourists not being fond of following them?

We were slightly dreading taking our 6 and 3 year olds to Disneyland Paris this summer and indeed we even bottled a trip we were planning last Christmas because of the terrible reviews we'd read about the park and the hotels. Well, without wishing to sound smug, I think we've cracked it completely and discovered how to have an amazing time at Disneyland Paris. The snag? It'll cost you, but it's worth every penny.We rented an Empire State suite at the New York hotel, with another family, who had an adjoining room to ours. Our room was perfectly adequate for all of us; my husband and I had a huge kingsize bed and the children shared a perfectly good double sofa bed. We thus had a seating area during the day, whilst the childrens' bed was put away. The bathroom was immaculate and we had a great view. Lovely touches were that the children were given huge Mickey mouse mugs, filled with sweets on the first day, and also beautiful autograph books photo albums with gold pens, as part of our service.Down the hall came our first big win. A small private dining room, which was open all day and evening, where we had breakfast, accompanied only by a few other families who were also staying on our 'exclusive' floor. We had access to free soft drinks, hot drinks, cakes and newspapers throughout the day. Best of all was the breakfast buffet, which was superb. The real icing on the cake however was that we were visited during breakfast, by a host of different characters, including Mickey, Minnie, Pluto, Donald's Uncle and more. It was fabulous and a bit surreal to be joined at our table by Mickey. The children were overwhelmed and were able to spend lots of time with each character and we had ample photo opportunities. A far cry from the large queues we saw down in the lobby for the other guests to briefly meet the characters at set times during the day.As if this wasn't enough, our trump card was getting VIP fast passes included in the package. From 11am we were entitled to go to any ride with a fast pass (which is practically all of them) and to go straight through. We didn't have allocated fast pass times, like regular fast passes, which mean that you would normally queue to get the pass and then would only be able to cash in your pass during an allotted time and would only be allowed to hold one pass at a time. We simply walked straight onto rides whenever we wanted, that often had queues of up to an hour or more. It was absolutely brilliant and meant that not only did the children thoroughly enjoy themselves, but all the adults did too and therefore we got the very best possible holiday out of our four days.Compare this with a recent trip to Legoland I made with the children. Two hours to get there in the car and we made it onto two rides in the entire day, having queued for over 4 hours in total for those two rides. What a disaster!I went expecting all the negative things I'd heard about Disneyland Paris to be true, but I only came away with one complaint, which was the way the Princesses were so hidden away and impossible to meet without forking out an extortionate amount of money for a Princess dinner, or without queueing for over 2 hours. This disappointed my 3 year old girl, but she got over it quickly as she was having such a great time. The park was very clean and tidy, the attention to detail in every inch of the place was incredible (compare with Chessington, which oh so badly needs a facelift!) the staff we met were absolutely lovely and never rude and because we never had to queue, we never experienced the nightmare queue barging we'd heard so much about. We also stayed in a hotel about 2 minutes walk from the village, so never had to contend with shuttle buses either. it was all a hugely pleasant surprise.We bought the unofficial guide to Disneyland Paris from Amazon before we went and it was brilliant. We more than made up for the cost by using the 20% off voucher in the back for Planet Hollywood. We used the authors' advice about where to eat and thus avoided the revolting food and totally rip off prices experienced by so many guests at Disney (stick to Planet Hollywood, McDonalds and Cafe Mickey (book the latter) and you should be pleasantly surprised.) We went off brief for one meal and sorely regretted it...the Rainforest Cafe was a disaster and we ended up with a grovelling manager refunding us half the cost of the meal, it was so revolting late overpriced. The shops were brilliantly well stocked and yes they are expensive in comparison to the Disneystore back in the UK, but the merchandise is on the whole wonderful quality and hugely diverse.So, the crunch is the cost. We went during high season (the school summer holidays) and paid just under   1200 per family of four for 3 nights 4 days. We saved money by travelling from Dover to Calais on the ferry. Having paid not dissimilar prices in the past for Centerparcs, we felt the value for money this offered at Disneyland Paris was absolutely fantastic. Everyone I know who tried to do it on the cheap, including family, who couldn't believe we were going to go after they'd all gone on and on about how dreadful the whole experience can be, had a ghastly time. We had a brilliant time and are thoroughly looking forward to trying Florida in a few years time. It's a no brainer...save up the pennies and only go once instead of multiple times, but do it in style!

Have just returned from a 3 day trip to Paris, including 1 day at the Disney Parks. Disney itself was just as expected, a magical atmosphere and plenty of things to see and rides to experience.We had a few minor problems, though nothing that would completely spoil the day.Our first issue was the trip to Disney from central Paris. Having bought Zone 1 2 Metro tickets, we arrived at one of the link stations for the RER A line into Disney. We had not bought our ticket to Disney (in Zone 5) by then so looked around for a ticket office. As there was none to be seen, we boarded the next available train (which seem to run every 15 minutes). After arriving at the Marne la Vallee station 35 minutes later, we found that we were stuck on the wrong side of the gates! There were no staff on hand to help us and the only ticket machine was going to charge us 25Euro each for return tickets (when we knew they should have been no more than 13Euro). Luckily, the machine did not accept any of our credit cards as it was not working and we managed to pass through the gates behind a kind man with a pushchair! We then bought single tickets back to Paris for 6.45Euro. So be warned, BUY YOUR RAIL TICKET BEFORE YOU BOARD THE TRAIN IN CENTRAL PARIS! This wasted quite a bit of our time.We had bought our 1day hopper ticket on the internet before we left but when we got to the main entrance, there was a bit of confusion about where to redeem the printed voucher. Eventually we found it and got into the park to start our day.Having been to Disney in Anaheim twice and my friend having visited DisneyWorld Florida, we knew what kind of things to expect. The main park is smaller than the others but has really good rides and a great parade. Disney Studios also has great rides although the queues were a bit long for Crush Coaster (80minutes) so we did not manage to get on everything.All in all, we had a great day and would not hesitate to return. Although next time I think I will stay at one of the hotels in the resort to save train journey confusion!

Oh Disneyland Paris.......................ive been 13 times!I love this placethe first time i visited was in 1992 when the park opened! I was only 7 but i still love it as much as i did then!The last time i visited was in October 2007 for the 15th Birthday Celebrations and every time i go it gets better and better!Disneyland Park :This park is basically the usual Disney park, as you will find similar sister parks in California, Flordia, Hong Kong and Tokyo. By far this has the be the best 'Magic Kingdom' park out of them all!!Its the largest of all the 'Magic Kingdom Parks' Around the world and has a unique Castle like no other Disney ParkThe Rides here are really top notch and youll find old faveroutes of the American sister parks here such as Big Thunder Mountain and Space Mountain! But the difference here is the rides are much newer, therfore much more technolically advanced compared to the sister parks! For example Space Mountain, you get shot up a hugh Cannon into space at a G force speed unlike no other Disney Space Mountain! Youll hurtle around Meteors and planets and twist and turn in corkscrews all wondefully choreographed with music in the cars themselves! Big Thuner Mountain is also a lot better, being the only one of its kind actually disconnected from the main land being an island on its own having to travel under water in a tunnel to reach the mountain itself.Ride Ques can be quite long during summer so we always go when the kids are in school!!Notably my fave rides have to be Phantom Manor, Space Mountain, Thunder Mountain and Pirates of the Caribbean, all of which lie in different themed areas of the parkMain Street USA : The entrance to this Magical place, and sitting right at the end youll find the gorgeous Sleeping beauty Castle which is home to a living dragon under the Castle in a cave! Mains steet itself is lots of shops selling Disney Merchandise and also consists of food courts and places to buy cameras etc and any other item you may need for your vist here. Its also where the Daily Parades take place. notably from my visits the best restaurant here is Plaza Gardens overlooking the castle, which is also a hot spot for character dining! Discoveryland : Step into the future as Buzz Lightyear needs your help defeating the evil emperor Zurg, and you can catch a Space ship to the Star Wars worlds moon of Endor! Also home to Space Mountain this area of the park is fantasticly detailed around Jules Vernes Imagination of the world of discovery and tomorrow!Fantasyland : Where dreams come true, home to all the Disney Classics, this is home to peter Pans Flight, Snow Whites Scary Adventure, Pinocchios Adventure, Dumbo the Flying Elephant, Casy Jnr, Alice in Wonderlands Maze and its a Small World. Many of the rides here are for the younger guest, but for adults alike its still a magical part of the park. Peter Pans Flight being one of the most popular ride in the park with a magical flight over London and never Never Land!Adventureland : Home to the Pirates, Magic Carpets and Mysterious Temples. This is great! here you can jump on board Captain Hooks Ship, explore the Swiss Family Robinson Tree House, Pirates of the Caribbean and Indiana Jones' Temple of Peril Rollercoaster. I Must do!Frontierland: My fave, Western themed part of the park with big thunder mountain and scary Phantom Manor :p Lucky Nugget Saloon is a must do character dining experience. This part of the park also gets transformed during the halloween celebrations which is rather cool.So thats just a quick overview of the Disneyland ParkJust to let you know about the new Just like We Dreamed it Parade!!AMASING!! the floats all smell, for example Winnie the Pooh Float smelt of Hunny, and Minnie and Mickeys float smelt of Sweets and candyfloss with the Disney Princess float smelling of Sweets! I love this parade.....Food in the park isnt too expencive but as i mentioned Plaza Gardens id opt to go there, if you are not on Disneys Half Board Dining Plan its only 20 Euros for all you can eat buffet!!!Im sure you will love Disneyland Park, i think if someone goes and says it didnt touch their Heart in one way or another must be very strange indeed!Any questions feel free to msg me
First time at Disneyland. It was great!.  Busy but not overly so even at the peak time of mid July.    Saw both the 17:00 and 11:00 parades.  Both different & great.

oh dear, oh dear, oh dearhaving been to Disneyland paris afew times over the past 6 years, after visiting in July 08 i would never go again!!We arrived early, 9.25. Got our tickets and then walked in! this was meant to be the early opening for the hotel guests but the staff were far too busy talking and messing around to care and just let everyone in. At 10am the whole park opened, well the took the bits of string down so you could walk past the castle. this is were our hell started...... Being British, i can cope with que'ing! i was amazed the French have even got the knack of it too, but the Spanish! at one point myself and a french guy nearly killed a spanish family! i'll set the scene.... your queing for big thunder mountain (before it has its numerous breakdowns of the day) and you see some kids going under the barriers! next thing the parents of said children are pushing you out of the way! DLP a few years ago was a nice place, the staff would stop and talk to the children, swap pin's and generally be helpful, now i think we just get in their way.i was amazed to see que's of 2 hours for Crushes coaster, the hotellift ride(forgot its name), Big thunder mountain (but i think this is because it breaks down once an hour!) and Space mountain's que was a joke!by 2pm we had been on 2 rides, tried to get fastpasses but to be honest only the ones for spacemoutain and big thunder mountain work! so we gave up and went shopping!!!!!! and went back in at 7pm! thinking that as the park would be open until 23.00 we'd have plenty of time! WRONG!!! the park started shutting down at 22.00 and all the big rides where then out of bounds as they had to get ready for the fireworks!this park COULD be so much better! if...the staff were properly trained, they had 4 times the amount of staff, which would allow them to control the que's!they actually put all the cars for the rides out to help get rid of the que's and also filled every seat on each ride!!!i'm amazed that after 16years that the park is slipping back to its bad early days, but i s'pose that while most of our european friends have a lovely day by spoiling everyone elses day, DLP will still take everyones money!think i'll save my money and just enjoy the boxing days sale' que's instead!!

Having never been to a Disney Park before, we werent sure what to expect but nonetheless were pleasantly surprised. The staff were pleasant and the whole place was immaculately clean (rubbish never got a chance to hit the ground as  sweepers  fought to clear up litter.) Queues were long, but actually went quite quickly and fatspass scheme was a lifesaver! In the whole time we were there, we never even got close to any of the characters during their meet and greet sessions. They are scheduled to appear at specific places at specific times, although when you get there, you find a massive queue of kids waiting. As adults, we felt bad about pushing our way in to see the characters and as a result never got any pics with them. They move on at an exact time   sometimes leaving young children crying.The prices here are EXTORTIONATE!!! Its unbelievable how much they charge for food   especially in the Disney Village located between the 2 parks. Proces are disgusting and i feel sorry for anyone who went with children as its difficult to say no. All kids were dressed up in Princess Pirate fancy dress available from all the stores within the park   at a price of 60 Euros each!!!

Having been to Disneyland in the US three times, I did not go to Disneyland Paris last week with high expectations, expecting, as others have described on the internet, a smaller, tackier, and unfulfilling experience compared to the US versions.I am pleased to say that my experience of DP was quite the opposite and I absolutely loved the place. While it is true that the park does not have the quantity of rides available in Florida or California for example, the quality is arguably much better. For example, the roller coaster Space Mountain: Mission 2, is a significant improvement on the Florida version, and DP has some rides (e.g. Indianna Jones) that its Florida counterpart doesn't have at all!And comparing it to other parks in the area: Having been to Parc Asterix in the same holiday, I appreciate the slickness of the operation in getting in and out of the park, the longer opening times (10am 10pm), and if you use the fast passes well, and do the most popular rides first, the queues are not  too bad  (although Parc Asterix is superior in this department).I would recommend this park to all who love theme parks, and especially those who are looking for some convenient fun, which is located on their doorstep in Europe and urge people not to listen to those who say how inferior it is to the US versions, as I suspect this is mainly born out of snobbishness.

I have mixed feelings about Disneyland Paris.The bad: the lines were long and the fastpass system was down on almost all attractions. The mechanics did strike a couple of days so most rides were closed in the morning. There are not that many rides. It is a long way to walk from the car park to the parks.The good: the rides they have are nice. It is Disney so the theming is very good.The long lines was a problem for us on the first day. But the following days we got wiser and noticed that the line length varied a lot between the different attractions and time of day so with some planning luck the situation can improve a lot. Be sure to check the board which lists the waiting times which is located by the central plaza.We ended up eating lunch at the MacDonalds in Disneyland village a couple of days. It was cheaper and believe it or not less stressfu than eating in the parkl.IMHO the park it is inferior to WDW in Florida.Later during the same trip we visited the Europa Park in Germany which we found to be much better that DIsneyland Paris.

The Park itself was very Disney and we were all excited to get in. We arrived at 10am and thought we'd go into Disneyland first. When we bought our tickets from the campsite we were staying in, we were not told of opening and closing times. This being summer we expected a late night for both parks. Come to find out (after waiting in long queues all day) that both parks closed early during the week and when we realized this it was already almost closing time for the other park, Walt Disney Studios park. The Disney park itself closed at 8pm and this was after opening at 10am! We had paid for park hopper tickets and were unable to use the other park. While we should have checked on times ourselves, we assumed that the times would be later than that, especially for summer. As our day progressed, we decided to eat at a fast food eaterie in Fantasyland   with the exchange rate   our hot dog, chicken nugget (gross beyond comparison) and half a roast chicken came to $100. Ouch! And it gets better. After the lunch I was going to take my daughter to the restroom   gag! I could smell the stench of urine before I even got inside. We managed to walk to another land and found one that didn't stink. We found out the reason, or part of the reason   Disney Paris doesn't do air conditioning   not even on the rides! We chose to ride on Pirates of the Caribbean next. We were corralled into one huge mass of people going down underground to get to the ride   no air conditioning at all! I nearly passed out and almost went out it was so bad. We finally get down to the water (and boats) to find that the employees had air conditioning near their work stations. We found the same to be true on the Peter Pan ride as well. Hotter than heck inside the whole ride and a cool blast of air as we got off where all the employees were standing. For the amount of money we spent (with exchange rate it was almost the same as buying tickets at Disneyland in Anaheim) we expected a bit more Disney magic. There were no characters (cardboard cutouts were on Main Street for pictures) and just more. Extremely disappointed and wouldn't bother going again. What a shame.

Great Park. lots and lots to do and see.Kids had a good time. Park was clean, tidy. All that it promsed. Including high food prices though. But lots of effort went into it all, so worth the somewhat high entrance prices.station close for Eurostar. Pleanty hotel along that line (We styed at the Golden Tulip in Nerby Bussy St. George. Much cheaper I'm sure than the Disney hotel and great quiet town.Recommend any day!

I just ended a three week trip to Paris and Germany with my sister and 12 year old niece at Disneyland Paris. None of us had previously been to a Disney park and we loved it. It was a great way to end the trip. We stayed at the Disneyland Hotel which was very expensive, but a perfect choice. We arrived by TGV from Brussels and walked to the hotel. We stayed two nights and wish that we had another day. We arrived on Sunday afternoon about 2:00 and there were a lot of people. The crowds started to thin about 6:00 as people left to watch the final of the Europe Cup. Our timing was great. We loved the attention to detail all over the parks. Our favorite rides were the Phantom Mansion, Crush's Coaster (the only long wait we had), and Buzz Lightyear (we went three times). We had extra magic hours and an extra fastpass for staying in a resort hotel. These were great perks.Before the trip, my niece said that she was too old for character meals. We weren't the park for 10 minutes before she needed an autograph book for the characters' signatures. Since we were in Europe and most of the visitors didn't speak English, she didn't feel any peer pressure and could just experience the park as a child. At the Disneyland Hotel, we had characters at breakfast and we ended up having dinner with the princesses. We had dinner at Walt's and Auberge de Cendrillon. The food was very good at both. At the Auberge, there's a fixe prix menu, but there wasn't anything my niece wanted on it. There wasn't any problem with her ordering from the children's menu, although it's suppose to be for children 11 and under. A friend, who has been to both the Paris and Florida parks, didn't like the Paris park at all and much preferred WDW. I can't image how a trip to WDW could be as good as our experience in Disneyland Paris. We loved the parks, the hotel and the restaurants. The crowds were managable and the cast members were friendly and helpful.

Put simply, Disneyland Paris is an expensive vacation. That in itself would be fine, except for the fact that most staff members were rude, disinterested, and did not seem to want to help out guests of the park in the least. It seemed as though our spending our money to get into the park and purchase items was a type of 'privilege'!Also, after many great experiences in the US (especially at Disneyworld Florida, which we highly recommend!) with the Fast Pass system, it is almost non existant in Paris! Sure, they claim to use it. But most of the times we tried using it they were hard to find, we ended up in long lines anyway, or they would just shut them down altogether...even if the regular line was very long.While we would go back to Disneyworld Florida any time, we will not be returning to Disneyland Paris. Why spend money on a smaller park with higher prices...longer lines and confusing   inefficient Fast Pass systems....While the staff treats you in such a rude way? I tried ignoring the bad reviews I read on Tripadvisor before we left. However, sadly, now I know what it is like from first hand experience: Stay away! Go to Florida instead! There is no comparison.

I took a bunch of kids to Disneyland Paris as part of a school tour last August.They enjoyed it, but, it has to be acknowledged   it wasn't the highlight of their trip...The inward and outward bound journeys were an adventure for my kids so it began well. There weren't large queues when we arrived either so that was a major bonus.However, the situation with eating 'on the hoof' as it were, left a lot to be desired, in our opinion. If you were hungry, as we were, you either had to make do with a bare hot dog in a bare bun, for almost 5   , or you had to be seated in an eatery and wait a substantive amount of time for an over priced average burger joint meal... We went through the rhythms of the Eurodisney day, including the parade, the endlessly long queues for Space Mountain and the Peter Pan ride to name but two. Overall, we thought the boutiques over priced, and the eateries over estimated, but we still enjoyed it. To finish our trip we ate in Planet Hollywood at the parc. We were extremely dissatisfied with the value for money here. Nonetheless, as a once off, we wouldn't have missed it and would recommend it as such.

We went to Disneyland Paris in May 2008 with a two year old and a six month old!Flying was not the nightmare we expected, but when we got off the plane in France we had a bit of problem trying to get the buggy out of the hold as we had it in a buggy bag. If you are taking a buggy be warned that CDG airport is not exactly pram friendly!We had booked transfers and were dissapointed as they did not turn up in the Merc that we ordered nor with the two baby seats we requested. We found out later that the coach only took about 20 minutes to get to our hotel.We stayed in the Newport Bay Hotel in Disney. It was ok. Tatty and in need of a facelift (which seemed to have started). there was also a bit of damp mold round the windows etc. The bathroom was clean but again in need of a major facelift. Despite this the hotel staff were very nice and quite helpful. If you stay make sure to get down for breakfast before 7.45am. The queues after this are terrible. Also be warned   our 2 year old would not eat the breakfast at all   we had brought weetabix but the milk was UHT and the butter was not what we have at home so toast was a no go!Staying in Disney means getting into the park earlier than others   take advantage of this. The park was much busier than we expected for May. There were a lot of height restrictions on attractions   but not that were stuck to too much. There was quite a bit to do as a family and for our 2 year old   but trying to explain waiting in line to him was a challange. May was also quite hot too so again this can affect their tolerance!WARNING!! Most of the food in the parks is fast food and is vile. It is also very expensive! We ordered tomato soup for our 2 year old and were given what can only be described as a cup a soup! (for 10 euros!!!!) The Steakhouse in Disney village is a must! Beautiful food and great staff. Slightly more expensive (by about 30 euros) but it is a much better meal for that! The rainforest cafe is an experience with its mechanical animals. The noises can (and did) frighten younger kids though   food is ok, staff are awesome! Blue lagoon in the park is also another good place to eat. You can pay for breakfast at Mickey Cafe and eat with Characters there. Again toddlers run screaming! The breakfast is similar to that in the hotel although there are a few sausages and bits of bacon! (again not the best but ok)The shopping outlet nearby is not that cheap and there is also tax on top when you pay at the till which makes your cheap purchase more expensive than you expect. The shopping mall there is huge and the aquarium under it is worth a visit if your kids like fish. You are out of the park here though so make sure you practise your french!!Despite some of the reviews we read before we went, Disneyland Paris is well worth a visit. Our kids both loved it and so did we. We have been to Florida and it is a different experience than this, however it is still Disney, still magical and still brings out the big kid in all of us. Our 2 year old asks almost every day if we can go back   that can only be a good thing!?!

We where there for a 5 days 4 nights trip. It was our first visit, and we expect a lot. But, what we experienced, was magnificant and much above ours expectations.In brief, so much details of everything, so much tiny, nice things so much hospitality and organisation in this huge parks was amazing.It's very important to understand that there is two kind of people who visiting parks, people who live closely to parks (France, Benelux, England, Germany, Italy, Spain) and people from little bit far away countrys (rest of EU, East EU, Russia, Balcans, and rest of the world). This is very important to understand, because people from first group, can visit parks more often, so they don't need to force themselfs, because they can come again, and again, for 1 or 2 nights arragements.People from second gropup should plan their trip more carefully, if they like to experience everything, and to come after few years, again.Generaly, I would like to give few advices for people in the second group. 1. Take your time!Plan your trip very carefully, your itinerer should to be very detail, in minutes, if you like to see everything. Be free and write your itinerer in some usefull form (paper, mobile, PDA), based on time schedule of the parks attractions, which can be found in the web, BEFORE you come to the Paris. Every day parks visit 20.000   30.000 people, so you can imagine the crowds. Even more during the summer. So plan to stay at least 4 nights, if you plan to see everything now, and to come after few years, again.2. Stay in Disney hotels!That is the way to experinece parks much easier. In Disney hotels you can Meet'n'Greet with characters because interaction is better. Beside that you can use Extra Magic Hours, what is very important if you like to enjoy in Fantasyland without maddness and crowds. FASTPASS is very, very, very important priviledge of staying in Disney hotels.3. Book your dinners!Explore the web, READ a lot of reviews about restaurants, decide and then book your time, at least 30 days prior your first day. This is the way to save a lot of your money and nervs, and to enjoy your meals in the way you like the most.4. AttractionsYou should understand that there is a lot of people which don't know anything about some rides, and they can experience some very bad things. We saw a guy form Germany, around 50's which had a serious hart problems after Indiana Jones coaster. Also, my wife was in very bad nerve situation after Crush's Coaster and after Space Mountain: Missin 2 coaster. Hopefully, everything was OK in both situations, but you should be carefull.As a conclusion, DIsney Parks in Paris is fantastatic, amasing experinece, but if you like to enjoy in the best possible way, PLAN everything before you come for the first time.

Have just returned from my 2nd visit to Disneyland Paris, and again myself, husband and 4yr old daughter had a excellent time. We stayed at The Disneyland Hotel which made getting to both parks really convenient. We made use of the  extra magic hours  in the morning and went on all the rides that were open then several times without any wait. The queues this year for us didn't seem too bad, the longest one 50 mins for Crush's Coaster, which we all loved. The Tower of Terror was a real hit with all of, even my 4 year old liked it! Saw the parade every day   seen it a total of 10 times now, but is still lovely to watch. If I had one gripe it would be that there aren't enough characters wandering about, and the ones you do see are the same old ones time and again, there are plenty of different characters they could use, but don't seem to, anyway not worth worrying about, as I always try to make the best of my holidays with my family as they are precious, some people seem to like to find things to complain about, and if you look hard enough you will. I have already booked for next year, so I must be one satisfied customer! Enjoy your trip.

My husband and I love Disneyland, Anaheim and go at least once a year. While in London on a two week vacation, we decided to invest (yes it cost us that much) in a day trip to Disneyland Paris on the Eurostar. We only had 5hrs in the park. Luckily for us, it wasn   t a busy day and we didn   t have to wait in super long lines. I found that the Disney Experience was lacking. It felt like an amusement park and not the total immersion into the Happiest Place on Earth, I get in Anaheim. It might be attributed to the fact that we only had 5hrs and ran from ride to ride, trying to catch all the differences between the parks. One thing that really bothered us, was that all the indoor rides; Haunted House, Pirates, Space Mtn were hot and stuffy. They definitely needed to turn on the air conditioners! We were there May 7 2008.We are shoppers and love Disney merchandise and were surprised we had a hard time finding something to purchase as a souvenirs. When we go to Anaheim, we struggle picking which of several items to buy. You   d think you could find Mickey related Eiffel Tower   s, but that proved to be quite the chore. We may go back, one day, spend a few days at the resort to give it another chance. Besides, my new favorite rollercoaster is there   .Rock n Roller coaster featuring Aerosmith. Previously my favorite was California Screamin in Anaheim! I have to go back one day! IT WAS AWESOME!

Upon arriving on the Metropolitain, Paris' subway and rail system, we were informed that our rail passes didn't allow us an exit at the Disneyland station. We were required to pay 25 Euro each to get off of the platform and onto the Disney property. It was raining when we arrived but there is a gift shop that sells ponchos and umbrellas before you even enter the magic kingdom. Once inside, you get what you expect. Walt Disney's dream in action. The sign even says, 'Main Street U.S.A., Paris, France'. The ride lines were short because of the weather, we never waited more than about 15 minutes for a ride. Also, we were there on a Thursday, a weekday, and I would recommend that. We noticed the ropes that sometimes contain the lines. The potential to wait two hours for a ride is definitely there. I ended up spending three hundred USD before we walked in the park for passage and tickets to the Magic Kingdom and Disney studios. Most rides will translate to English after the French narration. It made for the most unique Disney trip I have ever been on. Prices inside the park are similarly inflated to other theme parks. Expect to spend some money, but expect to have a Disney style time. Be prepared, your inner child will find its way out once you enter the Magic Kingdom!

I went to Disney for a three day break with my partner. We opted for a one day disney hopper ticket for Saturday, and we made the right decision as by the end of the evening we were exhausted and felt we had seen enough for our money. It is cheaper to get your tickets on the internet before you go. The ticket prices in the hotels are the same as at the park (59 euros's for one day   2 parks) It saves queing if you buy them from the hotel.The Disney Studios park was better than the original park as it was less crowded, had better shows and was more suited to older people. The fast pass is a free service that allows you to go on some rides without ques, however this service wasn't offered on some of the rides which meant queing for approximatley 75 minutes for some rides. If your looking for a theme park specifically for the rides then Disneyland Paris isn't the right place.The two shows we saw in Disney Studios were great, first was a stunt show which made the whole day worthwhile, second was Animagique   a show with all the classic disney songs.If you have kids that want to see all the shows, all the characters and go on all the rides then you would deinitley need a couple of days, we happened to be in the right place at the right time to see the characters.All in all it was a great day at Disney, all once the parks close you can have a meal in one of the american style restaurants in Disney Village.

This place was such a rip off. I completely understand they need to make a buck or two, but this was beyond the pale. We went with 2x 8 year old boys and they were quite bored. The only decent rides that were there were a 40 minute wait. You have to be so patient as all the rides require a lengthy wait. They were too short for the main ride they wanted to go on. If you have deep pockets, this place is totally up your alley. Be totally prepared to keep putting your hand in your pocket all day long. The U.S. Disney theme parks are much better.

Went with my sister and three girls aged 9, nearly 7 and 4.Be prepared to queue. Even for rides like the tea cups we queued over 20 minutes. The bigger rides were over an hour. They have a fast pass system on certain rides which means you put your park ticket in a machine and get a ticket with an alloted time to go on the ride. Although they advertise that you can have five fast passes a day read the small print which says you can only have one fast pass at a time. So our idea of getting fast passes at the beginning of the day for 5 rides went badly wrong!Oh did I also mention that you have to queue to get a fast pass..grrrr.Our girls do not like scary rides so did not go on 'big thrill' rides. In Disney our favourites were Peter Pan..feels a bit like you are flying, Buzz Lightyear..you are in a carriage shooting aliens with guns..great fun, Its a Small World..a boat trip around countries (the girls loved this but I found it a bit spooky..don't like those dolls!).In Walt Disney Studios Park...Stitch Live was really impressive.If your kids don't like to be scared then watch out for the 3d honey I shrunk...it has realistic 3d snakes and other scaries. In the Studios Park the film tour bus ride special effects bit was impressive but it really scared the kids so be careful if they don't like fire and water! Don't want to post a spoiler but if you want to know more then email me. The Snow White ride was also full of witches and may be a bit scary for young kids.The 5pm parade was lovely, a really nice end to the day. Talking of characters if your kids want to do the autographs then try and catch the characters on walk about if you can...we queued for over an hour in 26 degree heat to get minnies photo and signature..worth it for the photo..they take a professional photo which you can buy and ours was a really nice momento but still a long time to wait. I would only do this for one character and only if they really want to. The queue did not seem that big but everyone in front had a signature and a photo so be warned as the queue did not move!High School Musical Parade is also on in Disney studio at the moment and the kids loved it (and me too if I am honest!).Didn't get chance to see the shows as the queues were just too big..come on Disney sort out advance booking for the shows as there was a huge queue an hour before the show doors even opened...too long to wait with young children.Anyway feel free to email with any questions, happy to help if I can!

My boyfriend and I went to Disneyland in May. May I say, it was great!! The adult rides, the scary ones and all, were sooo cool! This fantasy stuff like the Castle and the Parade and all, I can tell you, if you are still a little child inside, you're going to love it!! The parcs are very cool and very beautiful. Of course they sell stuff EVERYWHERE, and if you leave out the shops, half the park would dissapear, but still it was amazing!! I would reccommend though to make sure u have enough Fast Passes, cus the rides are extremely long waitingtimes, and if you have more than one fast apss, you can like get thez hours for 4 different rides and then just start with one and go one to the next, and the next and the next with like 15min of waitingtime MAX! The food sucks though, only junkfood, and in the end a hundred different names for different restaurants, but in the end they all sell junkfood. If you like junkfood , it was good though! : ) Overall, Disney is just sooo romantic i find!

I do not know why everybody thinks that Disneyland Park in Paris is smaller than its counterparts in the US. This is what Wikipedia says about Paris :  quote  Occupying 566,560 m   (140 acres), it is the largest Disney park based on the original in California. The park opened as Euro Disneyland on 12 April 1992.  unquote  True, if you count together the 4 main theme parks, the water parks and the total surface of the Resort, than Orlando is much bigger. But once more people, the Paris Magic Kingdom is the largest one in the world.More important to me, it is the prettiest one also. Maybe the French way of doing things is not always up to the American standards (especially customer service), but there is no Magic Kingdom so full of beautiful colors and details as Disneyland Park in Paris. I base myself on recent visits to Orlando and Hong Kong. Anaheim is on our schedule for next month.

We spent 3 days in eurodisney: 90% of the time in extra long cues: about 50 min. for each activity or meal; 10% remaining in short cues to pay about 3 euros for a 25 cl bottle of water!So: super tiring and expensive.Anyway, my son was enthusiastic, above all in meeting Disney star. For me was really stressing.Go in Eurodisney during week and not in the weekend!

We vistited 18 22 April 2008. Purpose of visit my granddaughter's 3rd Birthday. Travelling by Eurostar from St Pancras were Nanny, Grandad, Mummy, Stepdaddy and the special Girl. Uncle and friend, both 27, met us for the birthday and following day.Ok, here goes: Eurostar, slightly limited on seating space, especially when you have a tired little girl who has been woken early. All hotel, park and extras vouchers given on board. We were missing a breakfast voucher but the rep wouldn't couldn't help.Arrived in Paris, parks are 2 minute walk from station and if you are in a Disney hotel you can check your luggage in to be delivered to your hotel, so you are free to explore. After seeing the Tower of Terror looming we headed for the more gentle Disneyland Park. First greeting there was the famous Mickey shaped flower display of the Disneyland Hotel. Camera was out and stayed out. Entered the park and just in the square Mickey was out. Wow, these characters have so much time for the kids. Not only do they have photographers taking photos, but you can also take your own and plently. Each child gets their own special time. Only problem is that when the allotted photo shoot time is over you are not getting to see them. All times are clearly displayed in the programme though. Photos are available in park taken for two days. We checked out loads, felt no pressure to buy and only bought the ones we really wanted. One tip, the more you buy the cheaper each print, so save them up for as long as possible and buy in one go. You can view and come back later.I was back to being a kid, my granddaughter was overwhelmed. Characters also appear throughout the day for meet & greet. You can take photos, but this is a bit more chaotic. Some of the queues were long and not all had fast passes. Also you can only hold one fast pass at a time, but this does mean you can go on one ride while waiting for the next. Fast passes are for half hour slots though, so worth getting. Shortest and fastest queue was for Small Worls, did this and the Buzz Lightyear ride about 6 times each.We had the character breakfast in Cafe Mickey booked for the birthday and this was magical. PLENTY of choice, but the girls were too excited to eat. Mega fun had by all.Also had the birthday party booked in Plaza Gardens. Again this was fantastic, the characters had plenty of time for each group and the youngsters. Each child had a birthday cake and present. Only complaint is that the present was thrown unwrapped on to table by the waiting staff. (Picky, but it would have been nicer wrapped and given to child)We also booked dinner at Cafe Mickey. I had read that this was an upmarket McDonalds, do NOT believe this. Our food was excellent. Plenty of choice. A bit like a typical American diner in England. Characters in plenty again, with so much time for the kids. Our waiter was also excellent and very friendly. The staff also line up and dance at intervals. I would not have left so quickly but we wanted to see the night time show.We stayed in Dream Castle which is an associated hotel, but not a Disney hotel. To be honest, if you are getting the bus the distance and journey are no more difficult in these hotels and they are cheaper to book. I would stay at either the Disneyland Hotel or another associated hotel next time. Only difference I have heard is that you get characters in the Disney hotels.Disney Studios was a much older experience, but young ones could still have fun. It was more spread out and not as much there for young ones. We watched the Animagique show which was amazing. Also went on some of the rides, but some queues were just too long.My granddaughter managed to walk around for most if the first day, just a short carry here and there, but after that she was shattered, so either take or hire a buggy. Even big kids were in buggies, you do so much walking that it helps makes the day more enjoyable for you. Everybody also left bags on the buggies while going on the rides, they put your name on them and everything seemed very safe.The parades were great and we watched it in full for four of our five nights. I even caught my 28 year old son edging forward for a closer look, he does not get excited about anything other than football, so this was a big suprise. Arrive early though, at least an hour before for a good spot.A magical holiday had by all. Even my son wanted pictures with the characters. My best holiday ever. Five days later I am still tired and my feet are still sore, but just thinking of my experience makes me smile.I felt completely safe and would recommend this to single parents, as the journey also felt safe. Souvenir shops had some 'tat', but also had lots of high quality goods and not all of this was too expensive.Only downsides were the expense and choice of food inside the parks. Disney Village restaurants were also very expensive but lots more choice. My granddaughter lived on chicken nuggets and chips, which she never has at home, but in the restaurants there was always something happening to distract her from eating. There is a McDonalds in the Disney Village which is a very short walk from the parks, this can save a bit of money.

Just returned from an exhausting but great weekend. We caught the Eurostar on sat morning and arrived at lunchtime. After a quick sandwich for lunch we nipped on the RER train from Disneyland straight into Paris (about 1 hr travel and 2 trains) saw the Eiffel Tower and a few other landmarks. Back in time for tasty meal at the rainforest cafe, no q's at 7pm. Stayed 1 night at the Explorer's hotel, good value and shuttle bus. Arrived on Sun morning at 10am and went on about 6 rides before lunch. Longest Q was Peter Pan, about 25 mins. After lunch we popped next door to Universal Studios and headed straight to The Tower of Terror, and it was, wow!!!!!!!! If you like being waitless then this is for you, beware you leave your stomach at the top. My 7year old daughter loved it!! the Q was about 45mins for this one but worth it. A word of advice, Crush's coaster is quite a fast,spinning ride with lots of twists and turns, some of it backwards. my youngest daughter loved it but quite a few younger (4 7ish) children came off crying. A long Q too, 55 mins. We finished our day with a meal and caught the evening Eurostar home. A long weekend but if you don't mind being tired for a couple of days afterwards, well worth it.

I can't help but notice all the negative reviews. I've been to DLRP 8 times now. Just got back from a 5 day holiday there.It was brilliant. I had no problems with staff or attractions or queues. It was a hassle free holiday and everything went to plan!Although I must add, the first time I went was 13 years ago and I haven't been there for 5 years. A lot has changed in 5 years. They don't play the magical music in the lands anymore and the Disney atmosphere is certainly disappearing!I think the Disneyland Park certainly needs to get some serious PR treatment!!!

Although we frequently travel to Disney World Orlando from the UK we thought to pop across the channel to Disneyland Paris for a long weekend. Disney World it's not   but it is brilliant. We stayed at the Sequoia Lodge which was clean and comfortable with a good selection at the buffet breakfast (toast, pastry, fruit salad, yogurt and a variety of cheeses and meats   this can be quite busy earlier in the day so try and choose a slot for after 10am) as well as free kettles available from the Conserige. Both of the Parks as well as the train station and Disney Village are all within a 10 minute walk from the hotel which is a very nice feature. The Disney Park itself is fantastic   Space Mountain 2 is a more grown up version of the original with loops and corkscrews, Pirates of the Carribean is more atmospheric and the Haunted Mansion is set in a 'wild western' theme. Disney Studios is a smaller version of its American counterpart but the improved Tower of Terror and exclusive Crushes Coaster make up for its smaller size. The food in Disney Village is expensive and almost exclusively American with few vegetarian options so you may want to spend an evening or two in Paris (approximately 40 minutes on the Metro from Disney).

My experience of this attraction was unfortunately limited to the front gates. At every stage of the trip planning process, the Disney organization was incompetent and inflexible. When their online reservation service sent us the wrong tickets (for those of you who have purchased online, you know that this is a process nearly impossible to mess up   there are several stages and repeated validations before the purchase can be made), they refused to exchange them for another date, despite (a) there being no difference in price, and (b) it being THEIR mistake. Reconciling myself to traveling on the date they sent me tickets for, I called their reservation service to change the name of the person for the second ticket   with the new date, the first person could no longer accompany me. I was assured, repeatedly, that this was not necessary. Foolishly, it seems now, I accepted these assurances, only to be told by three levels of park officials once I turned up at the Park that there was no way they could let us in. To be standing at a park gate, with two valid tickets, both paid for by me, and to have been ensured by representatives that entry was not a problem, only to be told that my only way into the park was to buy a new, full price ticket for my companion, was appalling. As a corporation, and on the level of individual service, Disney acted callously and perhaps dishonestly. I cannot stress enough to potential visitors that they should be extremely careful in their dealings with the group, because if any errors occur, even their own, they have shown themselves absolutely unwilling to provide reasonable rectification of the matter. Very crass and disheartening.

Well being Irish we decided to celebrate St. Patricks Day in Disneyland Paris. I have to say thats its just as well my kids are disney fans because if the St. Patricks Day parade was anything to go by, they would have been so disappointed. The parade was actually a pre parade before the Disney Princess Parade and it was made up of 1 x Piper Band, 1 x Marching band and 1 x Irish Dancers and there was huge gaps in between these. I wasn't impressed. I was expecting something spectacular and amazing, its Disney afterall. The parade was a complete let down. There were some fireworks later that evening over the castle and it was all done to 'Riverdance' music. That now was great but as far as fireworks go it was over in about 3 minutes. Now in saying all of this, we love Disney so we didn't let it dampen our 5 days there. The kids weren't impressed with the parade either but everything else in Disneyland made up for it. They loved the autograph hunting and the rides. They are bigger and wiser now and it was more of a thrill for them. It has been 3 years since we were last there and my younger was 3 at the time. So in signing off that was our 3rd time to Disneyland Paris. We have no plans to go again and our next stop is Disneyland Florida Style. I can't wait !!!!
Bad food, very bad food, bad hotels but overall such ahit with the children that is worth making the trip

we have just got back from a week spent at eurodisney staying at the disneyland hotel in the park, with our 3 children aged 3, 5, and 7. i feel i have to write as before we went i searched trip advisor and found on the majority negative reports, so we were extremely worried about going. i must say how wrong the reports were, and our week was great. i admit some of the items on peoples reports were right, like the RUDE, RUDE french and spanish torists. The food was expensive but then what theme park isn't?. We loved the rainforest cafe, planet hollywood, auberge de'cendrillion, and the inventions restaurant in our hotel. The staff all over the park were really, really helpful and friendly, and the resort was extremely clean. i think you get what you pay for at eurodisney. We stayed castle club in our hotel where you get a few added bonuses which are well worth it   no queing on rides, free soft drinks and afternoon tea, disney characters strolling round the hotel at breakfast and most of the day. I can't believe a lot of people keep compaing eurodisney to florida   so unfair! this is after all only paris, and for children of our ages it was perfect and a taster of the real thing which we will go to when they are older but would be a waste of money now. Please don't be put off by all the miserable reports on here, see it for what it is, and don't forget you get what you pay for!!

For a disney park, there was a lack of disney magic for me, i had a 3night 4day break.Dont get me wrong we had a fab time and the parks where great, i just expected to see more of the disney caracters around, other than the 2hours they come out to pose for pic's(you are looking at atleast a 20min wait for this) and the disney parade's(not to be missed!!) it does not feel as though you are in disneyland.the disney park itself is lovely to walk around and the rides are fab, be warned if you are taking children there is a shop on every corner!!my sister has been to florida and said the caracter's are walking around and approaching you!! that would of been so much better here!!!the staff in the stores are not the most helpfull, a smile goes along way in my book!!i paid   84 for a 4day hooper ticket, not bad really, but you are looking at 9.95euro's for the cheapest meal in the park and that's fast food, very fast i might add ready in less than 2mins!!a simple coffee cost me 3.50euro's and i had to wait 5mins for it and it was cold!!if you are not good at waiting and queing this is not the place for you!!the park maps are a great help be sure to pick one up as they highlight the must see area's in each of the park's 5 'lands'.it's also worth getting a program so you have time's for the caracter meet and great's and the parade's.i hope this has been helpfull and you have a good trip!!!

Firstly our hotel (Holiday Inn) and flight (Easyjet) were great value but transport from the airport was a shocking 94 euros for a family of four, just one way in 2nd class. It took just 11 mins from CDG to Disney on the TVR high speed train so that works out around 8.5 euros per minute. What a disgrace! I will never complain about British Rail ever again! Taxi drivers ripped us off too, they either left the meter off and charged what they liked or whatever it said on the meter, they added on an extra couple of euros cos there were 'four of us'! We took taxis to the nearby Val D'Europe shopping center which was very good but avoid the outlet malls as they are very very expensive.Loved the theme parks but the whole experience is not a patch on the USA and Japanese versions. Don't get me wrong, we did enjoy our weekend and I'm not tight or miserable but I hate to be ripped off and that was what this trip was all about from start to finish. Disney studios is much smaller than the Disneyland Park so choose to do this one if you have less time in the day (or are tired!). The rides are great but not many with the fastpass facility. The shops are dear (as always) but my daughter bought the mickey ears at the Disney shop in Newcastle before we went for   3   the same in the park were 10 euros. DISNEY VILLAGEf you want to see premiership football while you're there, it will be on the screens at the sports bar in the Disney Village but you will pay 6.80 euros a pint. Between 7 9 euros a pint in the restaurants and hotels. 110 euros for a family meal for four in the Rainforest cafe   it was lovely but that was without any starters or desserts. All in all we had a good time but there's not a cat in hell's chance of me going back! I will stick with Florida thank you very much, especially as there are a lot less French people there.

Me, my wife and 2 kids aged 5 and 2 went from weds 12th march to saturday 15th march and we had a great time. The only drawback are the French visitors. I could swear but this website would probably remove this review. Numerous occasions you would queue up with your kids to get a photo with their favourite characters only for some french parent to push their kid in front. It did make me mad but didn't ruin my holiday as most of the rides were brilliant.Best thing to do is plan your day ahead. Head for the most popular rides early on as they get really busy later on. If you are staying in one of the parks hotels make use of the magic hours as they are a god send especially if you have young children as all the rides for little kids are open before everyone else gets in. We went on Buzz and all the rides in fantasy land in the magic hours slot which was great!! Like previous reviews have said the parades are a must and fantastic for the kids. But like I said before beware the french who always try to push you out the way for the best spots. Alot of the new rides are greatBest RidesTower of Terror (fantastic ride, highly recommended!!)Buzz Lightyear (great for all the family)Rock n Roller Coaster (Aerosmith in your ear all the way through is a real adrenaline rush)Best ShowsAnimagique (had to see it twice and you'll hum the song for weeks)Moteurs Stunt Show (great for all the family but very loud for small children who may get scared)Stitch Live (Got lucky on this one as the map says it's not open until 20th March but was told by a fellow Brit it was open. Fantastic for all the family)Cinemagique (great fun with Martin Short)Legend of the Lion King (great for all the family. The bongo playing at the beginning is great)Most overrated ridesStudio Tram Tour (boring seeing old film props. The only good bit was catastrophe canyon which lasted a couple of minutes. Was always breaking down when we were there. Best in view in the front 2 carraiges)Star Tours (huge dissapointment for me as I love Star Wars. Was like a simulator you find in a shopping centre)Alot of the restaurants and bars are really expensive but are great on entertainment and I found the food really nice. Be prepared though as if you like a pint like me you'll be forking out 6.80 euros (about 5 quid)!!Best restaurantsCafe Mickey (a real must. Disney characters come and play with the kids while eating. My son had his head licked by Pluto while he was eating his pasta. Was really funny)Annettes Diner (50's american diner. Burgers were great)

We (me, my hubby and 4 yr old daughter) have just come back from Disneyland Paris. We enjoyed it but it was expensive!!! We stayed at Hotel Cheyenne which was brilliant because it was like being in a Wild West town. All the accommodation was in different buildings so not too noisy and the rooms were very comfortable.I was unhappy with the price of food and drinks there especially as a lot of it wasn't very nice. Friends had told me that it was expensive but i was still shocked by what they charged there. Anyway here are some tips for having a good but cheaper time there. They are things that I was told before I went and proved to be useful. 1. Definitely go mid week   We went from Wed to Sat and we managed to do all the things we wanted to during the week. By Sat it was really, really busy. Tues is supposed to be the quietest day there. 2. Have your breakfast in the park rather than the hotel as you are nearer the rides etc and you get more varied food choices. You can get to go on some of the rides before the park opens at 10am.3. Take plenty of snacks and drinks with you. There are no supermarkets there so it is either eat their food or nothing. 4. Take disney clothes toys with you. Disney store in UK is much cheaper than the parks but then they do have more variety there.5. The Parades are a must   i think my daugher loved them the most. Our favourites were Cinemagique (walt disney studios) and Pirates of Caribbean ride.6. It is a good idea to get the map and schedule at the entrance to both sites and plan what you will be doing especially if you are limited for time.7. Try to avoid eating places at busy times e.g. after the parades   2pm (Walt Disney studios), 4.30pm and 7.15pm as they are really, really busy then. 8. Be prepared   there is lots of walking   so we used the hotel bus to get us to and from the park.Go and have lots of fun there and take plenty of cash with you!

We were there just for one day, but it was magnificent day. Even,one day there is too less to feel it as it deserves. Don't waste your time on eating,you have next to park willige to do that after closeing time. The only tip is don't go on weekends. It's too croweded. We was waiting over 60 minutes for some rides. Try to get fast pass. If you have any doubt as I had, GO THERE, you wan't regret.

I last went to Disney when I was 4 in 1992, this time took my younger cousin to Disney. It did not dissapoint and every ride was great fun, there was not one we did not like.The Best rides:   Thunder Mountain   Indian Jones    Pirates of the Carribean   Crush's Coaster   Rock 'n' Roll Coaster  Studio Tram tourWe didnt get on Tower of Terror, will do that next time!Disney is well worth a visit and can be for people of any age!

An excellent place to visit for all. Been to Disneyland Paris at least eight times now and had a great time every visit. Have stayed at nearly all the Disney hotels, don't bother staying in the more expensive ones. All rooms are very simular and have identical layouts. However,. the Newport Bay and New York are closer to the parks and breakfast isnt such a free for all!

Family of 2 adults and one 6year old stayed at the Santa Fe hotel in Disneyland Paris. Although this is the cheapest hotel , we couldn't fault it   it was big enough with 2 double beds and the bathroom was v. clean, cleaned every day and towels changed etc.. We went in Feb 08, it was freezing cold   what do you expect in Feb though? We walked along the canal each day through the Cheyenne village and past the other hotels, didn't take long and we liked the ducks! The food was very expensive, you can't eat cheaply here ! If you don't like buffets it's hard too. The breakfast was excellent , we went at 7.45 each day and didn't queue but after that there are HUGE queues.You soon get used to queueing! The day we arrived (Sat) was just nice but the Sunday was too busy. The next days were great though.Don't bother with Magic hours, you get into the park before everyone else but nothing's open to go on! There are barriers everywhere.We went by air and Charles de Gaulle airport was a nightmare! Once you get out , the bus stop was just outside.The rides were excellent and most OK for 6yr olds. We had autographs off a lot of the characters.The tram tour was worth the 20 min wait as was the boat ride with same wait.The only long wait we had was for the Peter Pan ride (90 mins ! ) but this was because it had broken and they fixed it ! We went on some things without waiting. 'Its a small world' is lovely and near there are a train ride Casey Jnr and a fairy tale boat ride which are nice for little ones. All in , we would go again !!

Having been to the Disney Resorts in orlando in 2006 and having had a brilliant time we were keen to go again but with a 8 month old now in tow as well as a 3 year old we went for the Disneyland Paris option instead and we were not disappointed at all. Just half an hour from Paris we stayed at the marriott village which is fantastic and very close to the park, shopping mall etc. The park itself is just as magical and well run as it's american brother. Hours of fun for the little ones as well as mums and dads. Going back again this year!!

We went to Euro Disney from 10th Feb 2008 to 14th Feb 2008. We knew it was half term, but thought that in February, that might not make it too busy. We were wrong! I don't know if this was it actually quiet, but if it was, I'd hate to see it in the summer! The weather was brilliant for February, which probably worked against us number of visitor wise, but we really did find it difficult to keep our 2 and 5 year olds entertained while we queued for half an hour to get on a ride (we ignored the ones which said the queue was longer than half an hour!).The first day was terrible, and we really wondered what we had got ourselves into, as our 5 year old was totally fed up, and we ended up going back to the hotel pool for a swim in the afternoon. On the subject, the Sequoia Lodge is built for about 3000 guests, but the swimming pool had 2 changing cubicles in each of the gents and ladies changing rooms. We went for breakfast the first morning but didn't bother after that!The 2nd day was better, as we went in with a plan, and found that by getting in as many rides as possible first thing in the morning, we could then take in a show in the afternoon (the excellent stunt show in Disney Studios Park). On the 3rd day we tried to take full advantage of the Fastpass system, but found that there were only 2 rides our kids were interested in with fastpass, so it didn't make a lot of difference. The 3rd day was just a morning in the park, so we went to Frontier Land, where it was actually possible to just walk onto the steam boat, then went to a show, which made our trip as our little girl got up on stage.Overall, we did enjoy the holiday, but it did have positives and negatives.The positives were :Easyjet   had never flown with them before, but was quite impressed. It is 'no frills', but you do get everything you would expect.Character Meal at Cafe MickeyThe rides   when you could get on. It's a Small World in particular was enjoyed by our kids, and although the queues are long, they are fast moving. The Steamboat was also another one that you could get on relatively quickly.Negatives:The queues   was expecting them, but not as much as this. Breakfast at the hotel was a write off, as was meeting Characters in the park without booking a character meal. On the last day, there was even a huge queue to get through the initial security gates, but what was more annoying was the number of people who thought they were too good to join the queue and just jumped it. To be fair, they guy I challenged about it told me, in English but he was obviously French, that he 'had a pass to get in at 8 o'clock'. Like the one I've got, I thought, but to be fair to the guy, he genuinely believed that he didn't have to queue because he had this pass, and he could have been correct, the point is that there were no Disney 'Cast Members' on hand to police the queue.Lunch with Disney Princess   Spent 150 Euros (about   120) to go to lunch with the Disney Princesses, and the food wasn't up my street atoll, and certainly not the kids! To be fair, it probably was top notch, but not what I was looking for. To top it all, our table was about the only one Cinderella didn't come to, so I took my we girl up to meet her as she was leaving, only to have a waiter tutting at me. I had paid 150 euro to meet her, I'm damned sure I was going to (and no, I didn't leave a tip!).Cresta   Didn't seem to want to know us once they had our money.On the whole, I'd give the holiday a pass mark, but I won't be rushing back.

Just got back from a MAGICAL 4 nights stay at Disney's Davy Crocket Ranch. I read some reviews before going and was dreadin the trip!We arrived at the chalets are they are basic but quite spacious and set in the woods which is a great peaceful hideaway after a day at the parks.Disney itself: Disneyland is magical especially when all lit up at night. We did have to queue but only for 15 30mins some rides didn't have any at all. Word of warning   if you want to do thunder mountain (which is nowhere near as good as space mountain) get to the Frontierland entrance at 9.40am and as soon as they move the rope   RUN! It was like a stampead and within 3 minutes there was a 45 minute waiting time.Space mountain, Buzz lightyear, Indiana Jones are the best rides in the park. Don't bother with Pinochio   cannot understand why anyone even queues for this, it was a joke.Food is NOT that pricey   half chicked, fries, drink and cake 11 euro.Be sure to watch the parades   they are well worth the wait. Sit on a bench and then when you hear it coming stand on it   best view in the park.Studios We found the studios a little dissapointing after disneyland   there is no magic here. The rides are excellent but the queues are much longer. Terror Towers is a must   get in the queue as soon as park opens otherwise you could wait upto an hour. Crush Coaster is also really good but usually 90 min queue. Rock n roll coaster really good and hardly ever queue. Special effects ride is not worth the wait   totally boring. The stunt show is a must   brilliant, don't get in the queue, just arrive 10 mins before show walk straight in and sit in the seats left at the back   best view.Watch out for the French   you queue for half an hour and they come round the outside and push straight in front.If you drive to Paris   be carefull. they drive like mad heads. My tomtom could not find the Eiffel tower so just follwo signs for Notre damn and its a big circle past all the biuldings to the tower.Oh one final thing   we took thermals, waterproofs, etc as most posts say hor terrible weather is in paris   It was beautiful, 15 degrees average, cold at night and first thing but all you need for the parks are a thick coat, hat , scarf & gloves. It was colder when we got home!Above all pretend you are a kid again and enjoy   once you've got the courage to do the first ride you'll be wanting more!!!!

This was my 3rd trip to disney since it opened in 1992. This is a great place for all, adults seem to love it just as much as the children. There really is so much to do. When planning a trip to disney, plan what you want to do ahead of time and work out how long you plan to stay. My last trip was with a friend in Nov 07 and we stayed 3 nightst 4 days. This was just the right amount of time in low season as the parks close earlier and being two adults we managed to get around the parks quite quickly and we had time to repeate are favourite rides big thunder mountain x 4 space mountain x 3. We travelled by eurostar which was nice, quick and hassle free. We stayed on site at the Disney sequoia lodge. (See separate review) This was just the right amount of time to explore the the parks, however we did not have time to do a day trip to paris or visit other attrations like the shopping complex near by. There is the 2 parks and the Disney Village. The disney park takes the most time it is split in to 4 lands, you enter on to main street which goes right up to the castle. There really is so much to do and in peak seasons and weekends queues can reach over an hour for the top attractions. Make use of fast pass on the rides that have them. The parades are great espcially fantillusion parade that they do over the summer and some evenings during Nov   Dec during the christmas season. some of the best rides in the Disney park are Big thunder mountain, Space mountaine, pirates of the caribbean. Advenureland has an area called adventure isles with caves and rope bridges which are great fun.Food can be expensive especially at the table service resturants try one of the fast food places like colonel hathi's pizza out post a box of pasta and bottle of water was about 9.00 euros. On the last day and had lunch at blue laggon which has a great atmosphere as it is at the start of pirates of the caribbean and really warm so nice in the winter lunch 1 main course (pasta) and water was about 20.00 euros Walt disney studios is a lot smaller than the disney park and takes a lot less time to get around but still has some great rides we spent less than a day in this park we got to the park just before 10 as it was low season and did not open till 10 we went straight to rock in roller coaster for my friend. I waited out side. We then done the stunt show, studio tram tour and crush. The stunt show is great even tho is was the same as what they had when I went in 2005. Crush is great we even went back to the studios on are last day just to go on crush for the last time it spins and goes a lot quicker than it looks and is one of my top 3 favourite rides out of both parks the only down side is there is no fast pass and we queued for just over an hour each time. Disney village. Quite a few places to eat and get a drink we had dinner here each night twice at rainforest cafe as we liked it so much. really good food, service and excellent cocktails. starter, main and cocktail was about 35.00 euros and then planet hollwood again good service and food very large portions and good cocktails. we also had lunch at cafe micky 1 day which was great fun full of characters and good food. if you have children this is a great place. Soup and a drink was about 13.00 euros.Night club was empy with the exception of a few locals this was on a friday night but it was low season.We had drinks in the sports bar which had a really nice atmosphere and service was good. Shops are every where there are so many diffrent types of soveiners some are expensive but things like the soft toys appeared no diffrent in price than what you would pay in a disney store. I have been to disney in the summer and over the bonfire chistmas season both are great. Summer benifits from longer opening hours and the additional night parade and fire works. Can get very hot. Winter the fire works were great for bonfire on the night we were there. The christmas decorations and atmosphere were excellant loved the hugh tree at the start of main street and the fake snow that kept falling evey now and then as you walked down main street. Just be prepared it was really cold when we went. If you like rides you may want to tryBig thunder mountain Space mountaincrush If you dont like rides or have young children you may want to tryPeter pans flightThe maze Adventure Isles Its a small worldA few tips for your visit.Prepare for the weather use fast past make a plan for things you want to do e.g. rides and restaurantsThings can get expensive so plan a budget Food Mainly fast food burgers, pizza, pasta and salads. The table service resturants offer more choice and some offer sides of vegetables. Have great time.
