We stayed at the park on 3 previous occasion and decided to treat the children (and ourselves) with another visit, especially since there was a special rate for children under 11. Last time we visited the park was in 2004 and in our opinion it is still the perfect place for kids and adults. No other park in Europe comes even close... There were some new rides which made it even more interesting. The Tower of Terror is an absolute hit. And we also loved the Crush'n Coaster based on Finding Nemo. We stayed at the Newport Bay in a room with lake view, which was an excellent choice. Breakfast was good but be early, as there was an enormous queue when we left. I read some posts about people complaining about the staff, but the staff members we met were very kind and helpful...Only one major comment; the horrendous prices for food. This is an outrage and steps should be taken to deal with this. It's unbelieve what they dare to ask for very mediocre food... We had dinner one night in the Rainforest Caf  , outside the park in Disney Village. It doesn't belong to Disneyland so we hoped that this would be a bit better and it was. Prices were still very high (   15 for a kids menu!), but at least our food was good and there was plenty for everyone (the salad my wife took was enormous...)All in all we had a wonderful time again and you can be sure that your kids will love it, but bring enough cash!

I have been to DisneyLand Resort Paris four times now and i have experienced different seasons. I have experienced summer there twice which was excellent there were fantastic shows and performances. I then went for Halloween which again was really good the park was covered in pumpkins. I then went xmas 2005 with my partner, it was really magical and i would defently recommend going, for people of all ages this is a wonderful experience. Out of all the times i have been i have stayed at the Disney's Hotel Santa Fe, this is only rated a 2 star hotel but i would defently give it at least a 3 star. It is good value for money, the rooms are very very clean and spacious, they have two double beds which are really really comfortable, and the hotel staff are always there to help and they are friendly. moving back to the park. There are rides for people of all ages from the tea cups to space mountain. If you haven't been before and are thinking about going i wouldn't hesitate. Best way to travel there is by the eurostar, it takes you direct to the park and there are free shuttle busses running to and from the disney hotels. Holiday overall 100 100

First went nearly 10 years ago, and this time round, it seemed more geared to taking your money off you than to delivering an experience not to forget.Actually, that's unfair, the unforgettable experience was provided by the prices. We were charged 27 euros for 2 sandwiches (nothing fancy, just regular sandwiches in a triangular box   like you'd get at lunchtime in the UK), 2 small coffees (vending machine size cups   not Starbucks buckets), 1 small fries (I counted them   24 fries to be precise) and a 500ml bottle of coke. The food prices are outrageous.I liked DLP the first time I went, and wanted to go back again. I wouldn't ever return.

I am an avid Disney world fan and have been to Florida many times, so having never been to DLP before I decided to treat my partner and I to a 2 day trip. We arrived on the Eurostar service from St Pancras, the journey was comfortable, fast and convenient.We arrived at the theme park approx 12.30pm and went straight to the Disneyland Park using a 2 day hopper pass. First opinion of the park was that it seemed filled to capacity with huge amounts of crowds. We headed towards Space Mountain 2 and I noticed the whole area smelled of horrid second hand smoke. This is in stark contrast to Florida, where everything is always clean, neat and tidy. I felt that people did not really repect the parks very much, throwing cigarette butts and litter all around.The parks are small in comparison to Florida, and while I wasn't expecting it to be similar, I felt the whole thing lacked the real 'disney magic' which I feel is so evident in Florida.Staff were not friendly, no 'good morning evening' when entering the parks, ride attendants were not pleasant, staff in restaurants seemed unhappy and hurried. Food was vastly overpriced. We were served cold fries, pizza etc for only 25 euros! Bargain, don't think so!.The parade in the afternoon was ok, but there were no fireworks in the evening and we were disappointed.Overall, it was an adequate trip, but wouldn't go back. We have already booked a 3 week trip to Orlando in September 2008 and are really looking forward to it.I would just like to say that it is such a wonderful experience to visit Disneyworld in Florida. The parks are wonderfully clean, staff are fabulous and make the whole experience so memorable. Also, having just been to DLP, I must express how fabulous the people of America are when visiting their country. Everytime I have visited Florida I have encountered the most hospitable people, both staff and tourists, and I think it is this element that keep us returning time after time. They take such good care of the parks and are so respectful. It is such a shame that DLP and the people who visit do not have the same mentality. Shame on you DLP!.

Getting there     Arriving at Terminal 2, at CDG, proceed all the way to the other side of the terminal to the rail station     you have to go downstairs after you see the large metal arches out the window. You can catch the TGV or the RER (A4) to the parks, but the TGV has room for luggage. This part isn   t too bad, you can also book a VEA shuttle online and you will be at the parks in about 40 minutes vs the 10 on the train. It takes all of about 20 minutes to get out of the arrivals area     depending on how fast your luggage gets out     as the customs seems to be as much a formality as anything else. If you find it cheaper, you can land in London and then transfer to the St. Pancras Rail station and then take the Eurostar in and make use of the Disney Express service. This should work like it does in WDW. If you took the train, be aware that you have to go through the Disney Village to get to the hotels area and the hotels all back onto the lake. You will as often as not have to hunt for the front desk. If you are staying at the Sequoia as I did, you have to go to the second floor for check in. The Hotel New York and Newport Bay both have ground level or at least more obvious front desk areas. If you are staying at the Disneyland Hotel, arriving by rail, you want to go the rightmost building before you enter the parks to get to their front desk. Hotel service and staff     decent, most staff will try to help if you don   t speak French and they don   t speak what you speak, but some don   t and these people will often seem crabby. The ones that speak more than one language are very helpful. Be prepared to get a mountain of paper for tickets, charge cards and meal coupons. Hotel rooms     I stayed at the Sequoia Lodge and found the room nice, a bit run down with random damage and some odd    artifacts    here and there (not unsanitary, but makes you wonder why it wasn   t cleaned however long ago). The room was spacious and being on a corner we were able to open windows to get a nice cross breeze for when the heat in the room was too high. We were on a non smoking floor, but as there were smoking floors in the hotel, you could smell smoke now and again and some rooms had people smoking     either as guests or when they visited from another floor hotel whatever. Characters     great, these people are great, play with and playing up the crowds regardless of size. I was especially floored by a Goofy who kept checking up on me during a dinner to make sure I was sitting up properly and the Robinson boys playing hide and go seek with me while I was trying t take their picture. One note     the characters won   t always stop to sign for the kids. This is a bit of a bummer, but often they are there to be part of the parks and if they are running, follow them and they might stop and sign when they get to a place where they can stop for a bit. Other times they don   t have the right gloves to hold a pen. There are however a great number of canned meet and greet locations.Dining   Great good was to be had just about everywhere. My wife and I enjoyed the breakfast in the hotel (Sequoia Lodge) more than the one breakfast that we took in the park. Special mention to Agrahba Cafe, Innoventions and Auberege de Cinderellion. Suggestions (Steve Jobs, are you listening    ? Apparently the Great Steve was there at the same time and being the majority owner of Disney, he can make changes just as he already has with the dropping of D2D sequels)     BAN SMOKING IN THE PARKS. Not only are the smokers rude with their smoking     though being from North America where smoking is increasingly taboo, I realize that the social taboos are not all shared, but I can   t imagine anyone enjoying second hand smoke being blown at them or their children. Smokers not only litter the parks with their buts, but this also leads to more garbage and a general lack of respect for the parks. If there were more garbages that might also help, they seemed to be conspicuously absent in this park as it seems that you can't turn around in the American parks without seeing one   or having one walk by.Overall (from a North American viewpoint): If you have been to the American parks and have the chance to come here, certainly make the trip to see what is different and enjoy the place (don't mind the people). If you are a Disney nut, then be sure to come here. If you have only one opportunity to ever see a Disney park and you can't make it to Orlando, this is still a great place to visit.

Whilst we were due to travel to Euro Disney for New Years Eve a massive and uncompensated muck up by Thomas Cook meant that we had to travel on New Years Day 2008 instead as Thomas Cook had booked us a room at the Newport Bay hotel that was not available. We were offered the Radisson SAS hotel by Thomas Cook and they considered this an upgrade despite the fact that it was off resort and the biggest specification we made at time of booking was that we stayed at a hotel in the resort. We therefore had to travel a day later to get the location we wanted and missed out on the new Years celebrations due to this mistake (which was only revealed to us over 3 weeks after the original booking was made!) Needless to say our one piece of advice is to book with any tour operator other than Thomas Cook as they did not seem to value our specifications at all and failed to provide the service they as a company exist to provide.Anyway, these gripes aside we travelled to Disney by the Eurostar which was absolutely hassle free and a far better option than flying in our opinion. The disney express luggage service is excellent and allowed us to go straight to the park and check in later. Despite the cold weather we managed to get around everything the 2 parks had to offer in 3 days, thoroughly enjoying The Legend of the Lion King show, the motor stunt show, Big Thunder Mountain and the aerosmith rollercoaster. The different shows and parades around did not disappoint and were all very well done. The queues died down in the evening although once again thanks to the fast pass service and availability of extra hours (which we would not have enjoyed if we had taken the hotel upgrade) we only queued for more than an hour about three times which considering we done everything was not bad at all.Having got to Disney we were impressed with the Newport Bay hotel as our room was very spacious and there was a disney charecter in the lobby each morning. We did not suffer the breakfast queues some people previously described as we went for the early option between 7am and 8am. We did however see some lengthy queues from half eight on. We went to Buffalo Bills Wild West Show and thoroughly enjoyed it. For a large show it is relatively well organised and something a bit different and whilst the food is not spectacular the cost of the ticket is good value for money. The only criticism we can really make of the trip (Thomas Cooks customer service aside) is that the meal we had at Planet Hollywood restaurant which was highly inedible and over priced. When you leave a restaurant to go to McDonalds you know there has to be something wrong!Overall a very enjoyable trip with a good variety of rides and shows meaning that there is something there for everyone.

Have been twice now to DLP, The most recent being New Years Eve just past. Yes it was very busy due to the time of year, but i was more than impressed with how well the park and the staff coped with it. Facilites were all kept clean and tidy throughout the day. The q's for rides were managed well and moved quickly enough considering the crowds. As it was NYE, the park stayed open until 1am with fantastic fireworks display. Truly something for everyone ay DLP

We travelled to disney paris on 30 12 2007 with coach company Buzzlines. The whole trip cost   595 (2 adults  1 child).Day 1   We departed from Dover (coach arrived bang on time) and travelled across on the ferry and down to our hotel (Novotel, Aulnay Sous Bois). The hotel was basic but filled our needs and was comfy. There was a steak house and an italian restaurant a stones throw away. The people on the coach were mainly young couples which surprised me as I thought it would be rammed with kids   there was one other family on board which meant my daughter had other children to play with.Day 2   Spent all day at Disney   Studios  Disneyland  Disney Village (10am to 12.30am!). The whole experience was totally fantastic. Thrill rides I recommend   Aerosmith rollercoaster, Terror Towers (only if you have a strong stomach!), Runaway train, Indiana Jones. Hint: Take full advantage of the fast pass system   it really does work and saves literally hours of queuing.As well as getting round the main rides it is essential to relax and take in the full atmosphere of the place (esp disneyland) and a ride on the steamer in Frontier land is a great way to do that. There is a fab balloon ride that we did not get on that takes off from Disney Village and rides right up into the air   the views must be amazing so if you can get to this then I would.It is impossible to do the whole of disney in one day (do able in two days) so if you are there for only one day don't try and rush round.We also watched the Animajique show which was very good, Armageddon ride was good too.As soon as we got to main street, disneyland it started to (fake) snow and was really magical. True disney magic.There are plenty of shops with lots of fantastic disney stuff so take plenty of dosh esp if going with kids   really top quality clothing and the trip is not complete without wearing a set of mickey  minnie mouse ears!The parades are wonderful. People start getting their positions about half an hour before the parade starts so if you want a seat on the kerb be prepared to wait some time. We were not prepared to wait as it was very cold (we watched the 9pm Fantasia parade on 31 12) but we still got a great view (and only waited around 5 mins) by standing on a grass bank   the parade was up high on floats so we probably had a better view than those at street level.You can greet and meet disney characters but the main ones get mobbed so be prepared to fight for your right to have a photo! As english we tended to try and queue but other nationalities had no such reserves so get in there!Other rides recommended by others on our coach were space mountain (thrill) and Buzz Lightyear (kiddies).We dined at Planet Hollywood in Disney Village which I can highly recommend. It was busy but we got seated within 10 minutes and the service was top notch. The french don't rush so whereas in england we would have been in and out within half an hour we enjoyed a good couple of hours having a full three course and a bottle of wine. After the last parade (near the magical fairy princess castle   which looks awesome at night) the street were filled with dance music and everyone was dancing and happy (helped by the plentiful stores set up selling glasses of champagne to celebrate the new year!).As you can tell i could go on for ages we enjoyed it so much. I haven't been to disney in Florida so I am not able to compare it to there although I have read other reviews and the US one seems to be even better   do not let this stop you from going to paris though.Only disadvantages   towards middnight the streets were rammed and queues in disney for refreshments were huge and cash machines were out of money. Suggestion: Take cash to last you a full day  Buy refreshments early on to last (bottles of water etc)  Take a ruck sack for purchases if you do not have a coach or car where you can leave them  Step outside Disney and seek refreshment in Disney Village which is less busy  Dress for the weather   you cannot enjoy it as much if you are cold  wet.Day 3   Our coach took us into Paris. We viewed the city via coach stopping off for photo opportunities. We saw the Arc de Triomphe, Champs Elyees, Musee D'Iarmee, Grand and Petit Palace, Opera Garnier, the Louvre, Notre Dame etc. We had a one hour boat trip along the Seine and ended up at the Eiffel Tower. The tower is huge when up close and a real breath taking experience. We did not have time to go up and the queues were very long ( I imagine this was due in part to it being evening and New years Day). Be aware of Algerian illegal immigrants trying to sell souvenirs and Algerian women offering you a piece of paper   Walk away they are trying to pick your pocket! Keep valuables and children close and enjoy the amazing sight of the tower. It is not expensive to go up the tower and we will definitely be returing to get up there. On the hour in the evening the tower lights up with millions of little lights   a proper spectacle.Day 4   returned home to England   again everything ran like clockwork   slightly longer on the way home due to passport control but we managed to fit in a visit to a beer warehouse!Biggest hint: Take a camera, memory card and batteries

I love Disneyland. To my shame we have been at least 20 times to Paris and a few times to Florida. I tell you that so you know I am a Disney lover and I think no one in the world does kids entertainment like Disney do.BUT.... Paris is starting to slip. The service when we were there last week was bad, the food in the parks was atrocious and ridiculously over priced (cold pizza, cold fries, and so on). The difference between the standards here and in Florida is huge. You're letting it slip DLP.

We (my husband and I) booked our tickets for PARCs Disneyland and Walt Disney Studios in advance via the Internet with Cityrama. We paid in advance too, so we had no queues in order to get in   but this wouldn't have been a problem as it turned out we were there early and there was a very small queue only. The ticket allowed access to the Village, Park and Studio, and we sampled all three within a day.I think I went on every ride possible, and the longest queue was for the best rides, say 15 minutes max.It was incredibly cold on 19th December and despite gloves and scarf, I soon found that I needed a hat   so if you don't want to buy, take one with you. It seems that the temperature was around   10degrees. The weather whilst extremely cold was not wet, and I'm sure this added to our experience   as did the  Snow  which fell from the skies (well, bubbles from the top of various buildings if we tell the truth) and it made a beautiful photo opportunity.We didn't stop at the photo opportunity places   as these had queues, and we weren't to bothered about not being with Nickey, Minnie   Goofy, but others were, so we left them queuing (probably around 15 mins before their turn came along).We walked the streets browsing in the shops, but soon discovered that one shop was very much the same as the next. We had coffee and cake in the morning and later a waffle   the restaurants were many, however we felt that the  nicer ones  (not the fast food type) were pretty expensive as expected in such a location   so we opted for a McDonald's later (after trying unsuccessfully to take a trip on the hot air balloon   but it had stopped because of high wind)   shame we hadn't gone earlier, as it was only around Euro8 I think!There were rides suitable for all ages, and the more frightening ones had a height limit   which was around 120cm   I'm not tall by any means, and having experienced these ones I can say it is a good safety measure.... I often left my seat, and found that my head banged on the top of the protection bars!All sites have a location map   which allows anyone to go around the different parks, and Walt Disney Studios was a memorable visit. We were a little disappointed that the Haunted House wasn't yet open to customers, and only accessible to those with special invitations.But, as a 40   45 years old couple   we would thoroughly recommend the trip   a day was enough to see all around, but it could prove to be expensive for families   who all seemed to make loads of purchases.

My Boyfriend and I went to Paris for the Easter Break and we had a fab trip. We spent a whole day at Disney Land from early morning to late at night and it was a fab day out. We really enjoyed all the rides aside from the long ques which is to be expected at that time of year. Disney land is on the expensive side but well worth the trip for the day that's in it. We found it hard to find nice food as we went to a steak house which was on site but it wasn't great and it was very expensive too.

The plan for our trip to Disneyland Paris was to travel to Beauvais Airport, take the bus to Porte Maillot and then the train out to Marne La Valley Chessy. This was definately the most reasonable option and the station is right beside the entrance to Disneyland. Unknown to us, however, the trains were on strike which left us stranded in the centre of Paris. We then had to take a private taxi which was 80   . The trains were still on strike for our return journey so we had to book a private shuttle. We booked this using Paris Shuttle Service. We were quoted 40    per person by phone and in an email confirmation but ended up having to pay 90    per person!I would never travel to Beauvais airport again as the transport links to Disneyland Paris are poor.

Had an absolutely fantastic time.  Loads to do and see and not enough hours in the day.  4 days just wasn't long enough though.  Great fun for all the family from little ones to grandmas and grandads.

This was our third time as a family to the park. We had a good time and got on many of the rides without queuing, very rare as we have queued for hours sometimes for certain rides.The park and the studios park is dated and really needs a good clean. We do enjoy going here but you have to realise that this is run mainly by the french and therefore the normal or expected 'Disney' customer service is missing. We went to Anaheim a couple of years ago and this was the first disney park to be opened, even after all that time the maintenance and the park look better than this one, and Disney Paris is only 15 years old!!!It is very expensive for what it is and meals accomodation is basic. Although, we did find a few buffet options this time in the park for around 22 euros per person. I would reccomend taking snacks and drinks into the park, when they search your bags at the entrance they do not mind that you take such items in. The shows are really good and the whole experience is a step out of reality.Most of the visitors there are very selfish and push jump the queues this can be very annoying. If you get stressed out by this and waiting in line with nothing to look at I would give this Disney a wide berth.Overall, go and expect a euro version of the disney. It cannot be compared to Orlando or any of the other disney this is in a league of its own. If anything just have fun looking at the miserable and unhappy staff compared to the 'All American Smile'!

Stayed at the Newport Bay for 4 nights. The room was nice but the hotel was pandemonium. I would imagine they are all the same. The foyer was constantly full of people queueing to check in. Breakfast was a free for all and you were ushered to your table by a head waiter whose main aim was to rush you through as quickly as possible. There were dirty plates and food piled up on tables all around the side of the breakfast room. The parks were too busy and at the weekends you had to queue for hours to get on one ride. On the Saturday, after one ride, we decided to call it a day and went back to the hotel for a swim. I didn't expect it to be like Florida, but it was such a disappointment. There was none of the magic we experienced there. The service and food were awful so we decided to eat at the Disney Hotel restaurant. What we had was nice but a main course for two adults, cheese board, coffee and wine, with a child's menu came to   126. I wouldn't mind but the portions were so small we left hungry. I can't think of anything positive to say about our trip and we certainly won't be returning.

I stayed at Disneyland for 4 nights, stayed at the Kyraid for 2 nights,Cheyanne for 1 night and the Holiday Inn at Bussy St George for 1 night, spent 2 days in the park, myself, wife and 11 year old son loved it, 80 year old father hated it, queued for a maximum of 30 mins for popular rides, some rides just walked straight on, food in the park was quite expensive so we made up packed lunches from our breakfast buffets and sneaked it in the park as you are not allowed to bring your own food. At night we ate in the Disneyland Village. Planet Hollywood, Annettes and most other resturants have deals so prices werent to bad, splashed out one night and went to Buffalo Bills Wild West Show, food, and drink as much beer or wine you want during the show,We also went to Val de Europe shopping centre 2 mins away by train and plenty of bargains to be had.Overall had a great time and will be back soon.

In short, we had a blast from beginning to end! We just loved Disneyland Paris. Staying at the Disney Newport Bay Hotel made everything easy, transport to and from is easy etc etcMy husband and I went with my family who had been to Disney World in Florida the year before. We had never been to any of the Disney theme parks so we came here with fresh eyes and thoroughly enjoyed ourselves seeing all these famous 'lands' that we'd heard about all our lives, as cliched as it will sound, it was just magical to us (in our mid 20's!). My younger brother (12 at the time) also had a fantastic time and loved every second of it. My parents however felt it paled in comparison to Disney World in Florida and didn't experience the amazement that we did. They did have a great time though and are planning to go back next year when they're in Europe, as are we and we can't wait!I think if you've been to some of the bigger parks then you need to be open to the fact that it's smaller (but still massive!!!) and appreciate it for what it is   a EUROPEAN version of Disneyland. It's not meant to rival Disney World or they would have just made another one and employed Americans there. I went in October in the lead up to halloween when Frontierland was decked out with pumpkins and looked brilliant. Disney definitely do things in style! The only thing I would change would be to spend four or five nights there instead of two, we felt we had to rush it all a bit. This time we're going for five nights so we can slow down a bit. If you can spare the time it's a good idea. If you're open, accept that the prices will be high, that they speak French, the queues will be long during peak times, souvenirs expensive and the food unhealthy and you'll have a brilliant holiday! Most people know what they're getting in for with a place like Disneyland, so get your moneys worth by enjoying yourselves! It's so easy to have fun there.

we went to Euro Disney from 1 10   5 10 and I have to say it was a rip off from the moment we got off the plane to the moment we got back on!! All they care about is money they cram too many people into every space possible and charge max price for it all! We did the parks in about 2 1 2 days and there was nothing really there for my 7 year old who likes faster rides, Thunder mountain was about it and he was not tall enough for the Space ride.All in all very disappointing and I would next time rather spend more and go Florida as its far better and overall much better value.

My family and I (me,hubby and 8 yr old son) stayed in the Sequioa Lodge Hotel. It was lovely and comfortable, and we used the pool every morning after breakfast, and evening (open til 10pm) Staff very friendly and helpful, and the restaurant was super for all you can eat meal. You can walk from the hotel to the parks within 5 mins around the lake....so nice.Recommended is Crush's coaster (very fast), Big thunder mountain (awesome) and Pirates of the Caribbean ride   loved it., also Buzz Lightyear ride was good too. We stayed from mon   thurs and it was barely busy. Hopped on the rides within 10 15 mins at the most. It is expensive, but if you budget and don't go mad buying everyone gifts, you should be ok.Will definately return. Had a great time.

The kids had a ball. Not as big as L.A but lots to do. Recommend 2 3 days stay as you have Walt Disney Studios next door to discover. They do accomodate english and french and the kids had a fantastic on their favourite ride Big Thunder Mountain. All the characters were there  Mickey, Minnie,Goofy, Donald and the gang. You will feel like a little kid all over again! Take the visa and dont currency convert too many times otherwise you wont enjoy!

We took our 17 year old to Eurodisney and she loved it but we hated it. Not the place to go if you don't like crowds or rude people. Eurodisney just seem to cram as many people as they can into the one place , regardless of how uncomfortable that is for people. The queues are horrendous and we stayed at the Sequoia lodge which was built around trees, which made it very dark and dismal. With dark and dismal furniture in the hotel too. The staff were generally nice, especially in the bar area but the Concierge were horrible, very unhelpful. We must have walked about 20 miles in the few days we were there as the Hotels are a good 10 to 15 minute walk each way to get to the parks. The food was very limited with fast food everywhere. What about having some proper french food as we were in France? Couldn't even escape for a day as we wanted to go to Paris but the queues out of the railway station were ridiculous. They should have organised buses to Paris but didn't . The only way you could have got to Paris otherwise was on a tour through the Hotel which again was just a money making farce, costing far too much. The only good part of the holiday was the Eurostar   if we could have stayed on that for the duration of the break we would have done! Never again.

Have been here on 5 occassions and 4 of those were for the halloween festival   and it cannot be beaten for fun and entertainment this time of year! Last year we went to Orlando in the mistaken idea that the Halloween festival would be bigger and better at it's American counterparts after all, the Americans make a bigger thing of halloween than us Europeans. How wrong ! Disneyworld's Halloween is not a patch on the Disneyland,Paris' Villans parade. The Paris park is highly decorated with pumpkins and pink witchesand autumnal scenes etc. In American park we were hard pressed to find a single pumpkin, in fact, Halloween is a seperate ticket event and expensive and nowhere near as decrorative as Disneyland, Paris! The American parade was tame compared to the 'darker' and grander European one. My choice would be Disneyland ,Paris. Honestly,don't miss it!

Just got back from disney, what a disapointment . Having been to disney in florida we had something to compare to and sadly it falls very short. The two parks can be done in a day and a half, and if it was'nt for kids go free it would of been a complete waste of money.The staff are ok but they just seem to be there for the job, There was also alot of spanish there, and what horrible people they are on holiday, lacking all manners. I even had to pull one man of the shuttle bus and make him say sorry to my 2 year old daughter for pushing her over in a rush to get on the bus. People told me the food was expensive. It is a RIP OFF!!!!!! 50euros for 2 adult hot dog, and 3 child hot dogs and chips. The hot dogs were over microwaved and the chips cold. The best bet is to take your own food or go to McDonalds. Im sad to say that McDonalds was the best food we had there. I could go on and on but I think you get the idea.

Visited the park in Dec 06, and thoroughly enjoyed every minute. We're not used to cold weather at home in Cairns, so this was very special for us to be able to enjoy the winter in France. No snow unfortunately, but the park put on fake snowfalls (with soap) to set everyone in the mood. The park is the same layout as all the others (this was only our 2nd Disneyland, but we've now done 4), and a little smaller, but very comfortable in comparison. Spotless condition, and very friendly staff. No problems with the language, as they all speak very good English, and tried very hard to keep a straight face when I attempted my high school French on them. Shuttlebuses to & from the Hotels (we stayed at the Holiday Inn..see separate review) run non stop, and the railway station just outside the park makes it all too easy to get around. My 7YO daughter could'nt get enough of this park, at that time of the year, as the parade s were failry constant, with some great music. ( Chante c'est Noel  still gets a regular blast on our CD player in the car in OZ..although it seems out of place during our summer here). I would have no hesitation in recommending this park above Tokyo & Anaheim IF you wanted cosy friendly and magical. Highly memorable.

Just spent 4 days at disneyland paris, and on the whole, had an awesome time. The rides are great if you don't mind having to queue a while, highly recommended are the rock'n'rollercoaster and Crush's Coaster (both in the studio's park next to disneyland)  the queues are shorter than the ones for space mountain and indiana Jones and the rides are just as good!The only problems we had while we were there were:1)   Being english, you wait your turn for the rides and that's that. The rest of the EU countries have a slightly different approach  you get pushed, shoved, elbowed  pretty much anything goes if it means they are a foot further than you in the queue!  It's an experience but after a few days, enough was enough!2)  if you want to eat there, you might need to save your pennies  it cost's a fair bit to buy food and drink in the park.It's definatly worth going and you can't help but get caught up in the magic of the place, the disney parade is just lovely, the rides are great and the staff seemed nice enough. We'd go back, but not for as long next time.

The theming of the park is excellent, but it was just so crowded that we could barely move. Queues for the bigger  thrill  rides were over an hour, and the fast track option was sometimes offering a time of 2.5 hours later which (baring in mind you can only have one fast track  open  at a time), is of little use. There were even significant queues to register for fast track, then you still had a queue for the ride anyway (although much shorter than the main queue). So, fast track was of little use. I suspect fast track was excellent when it was new and not many people had picked up on it, but now that everyone is using it, it has just lost its effectiveness. There were also queues for toilets, food, drinks   everything in fact. We even had to queue up to leave the park.I expected a certain amount of queuing and crowding, but these were at completely unbearable levels and spoilt any enjoyment.I also actually believe that other theme parks, such as Thorpe Park have a better range of rides for anyone over 10, although Disney wins on the theming.The food on offer was very poor, and again, all food outlets were crowded with long queues. I had a hot dog that was barely edible (and I am not fussy about food, so if I'm complaining it must have been bad!). I ate it because I couldn't face another queue to buy anything else and I was hungry.Really, really disappointing.

Our family LOVES Disneyworld so we couldn't wait to visit Disneyland Paris on our recent trip to Europe. We day tripped to Walt Disney Studios park from Paris. You can pick up combined train park tickets so you might want to skip buying the tickets at the Disney Store in Paris and buy the combined tickets at the train station (less than an hour train ride from downtown Paris). We got there 20 minutes after the park opened and were riding the Rockin Roller Coaster within 10 minutes. We had a blast since it was not very crowded July 4th. We saw lots of shows and rode every ride at the park except the Cars ride (its a spinny one and we don't like those). The new Crush's EAC Roller Coaster was FUN and had we been in Walt Disney World we would've waited for hours to ride the newest park ride (had just opened). My gals (14 and 7) LOVED that we got to do so much in only one day. We joked that the map was actually drawn to real scale since it was so manageable. If you are looking for thrills you might want to look elsewhere since the Tower of Terror wasn't open yet. But we all had a good time and enjoyed the different varieties of food offered too. We'll visit the other park next time.

Just got back from Disneyland Paris, was a little concerned by some of the reviews on this site but i'm very pleased to report I was very pleasantly surprised. Stayed at Holiday Inn, few complaints about this ie very long wait at check in   not enough staff, had to chase for replacement towels, fridge missing! HOWEVER, the shuttle bus was excellent   no problems getting on it in the morning at 10am or at 9am. The French people were absolutely lovely VERY hospitable; friendly and falling over themselves to help. Disneyland was absolutely lovely (and I have been to Orlando and Anaheim). Don't expect a duplication of what is in the US this is a resort in its own right and is different but lovely with it. Queues were quite long waited 40 mins for Big Thunder and never got on Crush as queue nearly two hours but it is a new attraction so it hey ho   saves us something new to do next time we visit. On the whole I was amazed at the good behaviour of the majority of the kids (and adults!). Contrary to other reviews we had no problem with generally with people in queues although the Spanish in particular don't seem to have grasped the concept at all! On the whole, absolutely great time would definately go again. My partner and I are in our thirties without any children.

Just had a fantastic day In disney land Paris. For the rides we only had to queue for about 25 mins for each ride, although we didn't get on 2 of the rides due to queue's of 90mins. Food and beverage costs where of average price for Paris. Our only complaint about the whole day was the toilets as the day went on they got worse, we tried many around the resort and they were all bad.

I stayed at disney for 3 days 2 nights with all my family and it was absoloutly amazing. We stayed in the hotel cheyenne which was fantastic. The rooms, buildings and everything was cowboy themed. It was as if you were really in a cowboy ranch. The parades were fantastic. We travelled on the eurostar which was nice. The rides were really fun and some were really fast like rock and rollercoaster and space mission. Some of the queus for rides are very long so it's worth getting a fast pass. The effects of attractions in wallt disney studios were truly magical. The fantilusion parade followed by wishes fireworks was defintly magical. It's defintly worth staying as it is great fun and amazing. Also there is so much to do.

I took a school party of 40 children to DisneyLand Paris on the final day of our holiday in France. I found the park clean and tidy and the kids definately loved it. It was also secure enough to let them walk around on their own. The only point which was a letdown was the pre paid for meal voucher which could be used in several restaurants. On locating these we found several to be closed. Bearing in mind these are spaced out around the park it was a bit of a hassle as we did not know in advance of their closure, apart from that it was excellent.

My partner and I visited Disneyland Paris for 2 days over the Bastille Day weekend in July 2007.To start with the positive, the rides and parades were excellent, the queues were short (apart from the new Nemo roller coaster) and the fastpass system worked flawlessly. We rode on all of the rides we wanted to and hardly queued at all (we calculated about 1 and  a half hours queuing over the 21 thrill rides we went on!).Unfortunately Disney customer service let the whole experience down. We chose to eat in the much touted (and fairly expensive) Blue Lagoon restaurant on the Saturday night of our stay, but a combination of poor service, undercooked or overcooked and cold food led us to send back our main courses, pay the bill and leave after our starters. Is it really that hard to prepare pasta and rice? On biting into my cold ostrich steak I felt pretty queasy.We decided to speak with the restaurant manager about the situation but he was very rude    oh, you don't want to pay for your meal?!    no, that wasn't what we were saying. He fobbed us off and told us to speak to Disney City Hall (basically the customer service office for the park) who were the only people able to deal with a problem of this magnitude. After spending 20 minutes talking to a Disney customer service representative who spent the most part treating me like I was an 2 years old with her bottom lip pushed out and head tilted to the side, We completed a complaints form and left. For us, the magic had most certainly left the magical kingdom.Perhaps it's to be expected, but it seems that Disney is fluffy and lovable when they're taking your money, but corporate and uncaring whenever anything goes wrong.

went to eurodisney for two days. queues a nightmare...quide time says 45 mins really means 1hour and a half!!!pirates of the carribean ride very disappointing as 1hr and a half wait for?????fast pass didnt exist in many of rides.....and 9 times out of ten there as none left.  queue jumping a big big problem. a lot of pushing and shuving. cleaniness a problem as bins never were emptied all day....littler everywhere  bugs     bad smells    . movie area was good especially the stunt show...however will not be returning. food expensive  . best advice go to the real mccoy in america!

I had read as many reviews as I could about Disneyland Paris before leaving for Paris and as many of the reviews were quite negative, quite frankly I wasn't particularly looking forward to my Disneyland experience. However having promised my two kids (10 and 8) that I'd take them, I knew I'd have to grin and bear it, if it wasn't a that great an experience. But you know the reality was, surprisingly, actually pretty good. I bought a two day park hopper ticket as we went on two separate occasions, having planned to do Walt Disney Studios the first time, and then Disneyland the second time. Walt Disney Studios (WDS) was a good choice for the first day we went because it was the Friday after a public holiday (May 18th) so it was really crowded at Disneyland as lots of French seemed to pull their kids out of school that day and go. We know Disneyland was crowded because WDS had to close for about an hour in the afternoon due to, we think, a bomb scare, so we walked over to Disneyland, which made Hong Kong look empty. Don't ever go to Disneyland on a Friday, Sat or sunday unless you love crowds and don't mind standing in line for rides. That said, the longest queue we saw that day was 70 minutes, which is nothing compared to 3 hours in some of the rides in LA when I was there.We liked WDS as I can say that it is fairly small and probably less stressful than Disneyland, but there's only really one rollercoaster  the Rock and Roller coaster (I'm not sure if that's the exact name) but it is a fantastic rollercoaster and we went on three times. The queues weren't long at all for that one. The studio tour had a long queue, so we kept going back there in the hope the queue would get shorter and sure enough it did, just around lunchtime, so we went on it. It was lots of fun and the kids thought it was great. Loud music, fast ride, but not quite long enough to be satisfying, so you have to do it more than once.Overall, I'd say WDS is a bit tame, if you are used to big rides and large attractions, but it was a pleasant and enjoyable day. The food is pretty pricey and it isn't marvellous, but it isn't bad either. And Disney village has lots of other options just outside the two parks too, if you don't like the theme park food options. Not hing was particularly cheap, but let's face it, nothing in France is. I knew it was going to be expensive to eat there, so the prices seemed to be what I expected. If you go there expecting cheap, good food, you will be bitterly disappointed. If you go expecting fairly pricey snack food, that does in fact taste quite good, you'll be fine. Take bottled water and snacks though with you (even though they say not to, they didn't stop us)   and you can refill your water bottles in the parks at the water dispensers just outside some of the toilets.Some days later (June 5th) we headed to Disneyland Park itself. After the mayhem of the day we walked in when we were at WDS, I was not looking forward to it, expecting huge crowds and massive queues. Wrong. It was much better this time. We went on a Tuesday, and got there at 9:45 am   ie 15 mins before it opened   and we walked straight in and onto a big thunder mountain roller coaster with only a 10 minute wait. On to space mountain   5 minute wait. At lunchtime, there was NOBODY queuing for Indiana Jones, so we went on three times as that, and Space Mountain are definitely the best rides in the park.the Lion KIng show is absolutely fantastic, and worth seeing so make sure you get an advance ticket on the day   they'll tell you where to queue up for it at the theatre.The haunted mansion was fun too.We had a very good all you can eat buffet lunch in the park   not cheap, but not ridiculously expensive either. The kids were a bit tired so it was good to sit down somewhere nice and have a decent meal   so sick of snack foods by that time. As I recall you pay for the kids based on their age. Lots of choices   however my daughter was amazed there were no french fries available! The medical centre was quite helpful when my daughter hurt her arm, and most of the staff were friendly and polite. Whist this park is quite bit smaller than its California or Florida counterparts, it is a pleasant park, providing it isn't too crowded. We found the park map a bit confusing at times, but as the park is reasonably small it's much harder to get lost in it than it was in the LA version!The parade at 4pm is fantastic, even if it is a bit over the top Disney glitz, but the younger kids will be blown away by it. Pick a spot carefully   we stood just where you come out of adventure land , just after the parade turns the corner into Main St, which was great   as we got a lot of  extra  entertainment by the cast members near there as there's extra room there for the cast to ham it up and have fun. My elder daughter was a bit over parades like this, but it was a real spectacle.So my advice is to get to the park you want to go to before it opens, and then go straight to the ride you want to go on. If there's a line, get a fast pass and come back. Then go to the next ride and queue for that one. Use the fast passes they're great.And don't go on the weekend.Overall, you should have fun.

We Spent a week in the Euro Disney resort which after USA was a HUGE letdown. But I dont think it was totally Disneys fault.. Anyway Buffalo Bills......... Not what it says on the tin!!!!I went there as a birthday treat with my 12 yr old daughter, The build up to the show was electric and I must say the promise of  Endless BEER  was a plus...(it was my birthday). The waiters seemed like they had seen 1 show to many and just wanted the end of the night to come.. We got split into 4 RANCHES and all each team got a captain who's job it was to get there section of the crowd all YEHARRRED up. My half pint glass was filled with a random beer(lager) which went down a treat and I managed to catch the waiter as he made his way back to the service area for a topup (2 x half pint glases). The light went down and the show started Then a lot of horses with riders holding flags going round and round the arena for 5 mins while we all claped to the music. My glass was empty but there was no sign of the waiters. Enter BUFFALO BILL.. spouted on about the wild west and how much he loved france.. (playing to the crowd I would think). Enter annie oakley (the best shot in     well eurodisney maybe.. As all the  SHOOTING DEMONSTRATIONS  were blanks and nifty electronics. And before you say.... NO im not stupid I wasn't expecting some special ops markswomen... During this time the waiter turned up!!!!! oh joy my glass was begining to get dry.. but NO he had a metal pot of chili and in true wild west fashion was SLOPPING it into our bowls Table Laps  as it was so dark You could not see what you were eating and most of the people sitting around me didn't touch it for this reason including me and daughter. Enter the grand SITTING BULL..(Who's name should really be   STANDING AROUND DOING NOTHING BULL) Who chanted a few phrases then went and stood on a makeshift mountain for 10 mins... YES 10 MINS... still chanting!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! I can only assume he need to fill a gap in the show. YEHAAAAAA   the waiter was back.. But only to clear the still full bowls of chili. This time I asked for a re fill of my drink!!!! A blank look later and he was gone. Another ten minuets past while Chief BULL'S gang were screaming and chasing half a dozen buffalo's around the arena. All of this stampeading in the dust didnt help our already very dry mouths. And still no sign of the waiter. Along came the main  TEXAS STYLE BARBECUE  meal of the night:  quoteSausage with herbs,Roasted ChickenRanch house smoked ribs, Texan vegetablesOld fashioned potatoesWarm apple cobbler with vanilla ice creamA Garlic sausage......A chicken leg with a dolop of barbecue sauceA rib (bone with fat)peas and sweatcornboiled pottatoeswarm apple (with all the bits) cobbler and ice cream.OH and a re fill.......... (3 x half pint glases).Soon this was all cleared away and again the suspect food was left on the plate by alot of people inc us. (why would you eat chicken thats been mass cooked, in the dark???)coffe cups were offered in replace for the glasses which I declined and again asked for a re fill. He went and returned with the words.....  NO MORE  and carried on to clear all the glasses away.. SHOCKED wasn't the word.Team games took place duing the clean up which was the highlight of the night and team pride became a must..(and it took your mind of the fact the glasses had gone forever) Alot of hat swinging and YEEEHAARRRRING later and it was Buffalo Bill's turn to say goodbye and to ask us all to clap yeehaaar etc, for the team of rough riders, Annie (use a real gun) Oakley and Chief (I want to wave my feathers around and chant) Bull. So in a nutshell: 59euro's, A Poor meal, A show that doesnt match the leaflet but not THAT bad, and NOT all the beer you want. You do get to keep your hat and the kids will prob love it. Go in a large group and I would guess you also would have a great time as long as the meal wasnt an issue.

2nd visit, more impressed this time than last, seemed to be less ignorance than before (i.e. queue jumping  it still happened, but less often than last time ) Was in the first 100 on the new rides in 'Toon Studio', the cars ride was pedestrian and small, but the younger kids loved it, Crush's Coaster was good too. Rock and Roll rollercoaster is still the best ride, but they didn't play any music on the ride itself, which I thought was kind of odd. As usual the cost of food was an issue, but i found that I did spend less than last time, but ALOT more on drinks.In the Village I was VERY dissapointed with the Rainforest Cafe, whose portion control was VERY tight for the price. Had a character lunch at Cafe Mickey, was very impressed, food was excellent and character time was good too! Am planning the next trip already!!!

I had been to WDW florida 3 times previous and decided to go to euro disney instead and have a couple of holidays in europe instead. What a mistake!Even though the parks were OK, the disorganisation in the parks, and the downright rude attitudes of europeans will ensure I never visit Paris again.. Don't get me wrong I am not against the French or europeans in general, I get on with anyone, but it was like the world was going to end as everyone was pushing and shoving, and people were so arrogant ignorant. When I stopped to let someone through they looked at me strange.Disney staff were helpful, but thought they could have done more. I did not try to compare with Florida, but it is clear somethings that are done in Florida would actually work in Paris and give everyone a chance to meet characters and enjoy the disney experience.A very disappointed Disney fan. Will be going to Florida next time...

Having been to Florida in October to disneyworld, we felt like a top up a bit closer to home so popped to disneyland Paris this May. We stayed at the Santa Fe (great hotel   see separate review).We were lucky with the weather which was mainly sunny and blue skies, which made the beautiful castle even prettier. We loved the park, the rides were fantastic, the parades were too, and we were blown away by the shows. We saw the Lion King show which was superb, the tarzan encounter which again was fantastic, and animagique which was my favourite because I loved the animals. The queues were not long at all, the longest one was 20 minutes for Autopia which takes longer to load, apart from that we got fast passes for all the popular rides and the rest of the rides load people so fast it doesn't take long at all.We had some fantatsic meals while we were here, yes you can just choose to go and eat at fast food joints, then don't be surprised if the food is fast food (referring to an earlier rather silly review)!! We ate at Walts, the Blue Lagoon, and Auberge de Cendrillon (and had personal visit by Cinderella and Snow White during our meal) and the food was fantastic, dressed crab, grilled steak with fresh veg, coconut tart, and fantastic wine and cocktails. We did loads of shopping too and bought some lovely things in the park, such as christmas decorations, mugs, I even bought a suede jacket in Frontierland.Our favourite rides were Peter Pan, Big Thunder Mountain, Buzz Lightyear, Autopia, Pirates of the Carribean, and we also loved Alices Maze and the littler rides like Pinnochio.We had such a great time, we did spend quite a lot but that was because we ate so much and shopped so much, but it was worth every penny.

We visited Disney Paris April 11 15 with our two little girls who are 3 and 5. We were a litte disappointed and so were our girls who really wanted to see the princesses. They were no where to be found. We saw every other character in the parades, character dinners etc.., but not a princess to be found until our last day we saw Snow White and Sleeping Beauty over by  Small World   ride. We had to wait in really long lines to see them both. I even asked at our hotel  The Disneyland Hotel  and they could not tell me where to find them. They just shook their head saying they have no idea what characters will be where. I could not believe my ears. Were we really at  Disney ???? I had to tell my kids that the princess were on a little vacation this week. It was heart breaking, truely. There was a castle and a whole  Princess Stage  area next to the castle, but no performances. I just could not believe it. I am sure my girls were not the only ones disappointed. Our weather was perfect during our entire stay which I think made the park even more busy than usual. The lines were unreasonably long for my two kids and so was the garbage everywhere. They bathrooms were even worse. I could not believe how many garbage cans were overflowing with garbage. And the bathrooms were so dirty and smelly I completely walked out of one and ran back to our hotel room just to use the toilet. I had a friend that visited in early March during a time the weather wasn't so nice and it was still very crowded and she also said the same thing that the garbage cans were overflowing every where and the bathrooms were just horrible.As for our hotel  The Disneyland Hotel, my husband and I were disappointed in the quality of the hotel. Yes, the location was perfect! The pool was not that great for young kids who are learning how to swim. Our room was really in need of updating ie...the bathroom, capet, linens. Personally we stayed at the Holiday Inn outside the park one night, and I thought it was nicer due to the updated bathroom etc... It was just newer all around. As for the food, well it was no doubt expensive. We enjoyed all of our dinner experiences at the hotel buffet  Inventions , Chef Mickey was outstanding food, but again all really expensive. I felt our lunchtie meals were more limited to  unhealty foods or fast foods . It would have been nice to have healthier selections. Our kids enjoyed the food as well.To be fair, I will say that we did enjoy our trip, but for the money we spent we expected much better quality  Disney Quality . We were at Walt Disney World last year around this same time and we had none of the same problems or experiences. We are not sure if we would recommend doing this trip if you have not been to  The Walt Disney World  nothing really compares to it. I would really like to return but can't see spending that kind of money for such poor quality of services.. Sorry Disneyland Paris.

Hey everyone!Got to visit Disneyland Paris at the end of April 2007...and I would def. recommend you go at this time as well! We got there about 15 mins after entry....and about 90% of the rides we didn't have to wait over 30 mins for...we got into the Indiana Jones roller coaster in 5 minutes and Space Mountain in 15!The weather was wonderful...and since it was the 15th Anniversary (That just started in April and goes to March next year) they had a train full of Disney characters go by every 30 minutes, too cute.Rides I would reccommend are Peter Pan's Flight...very cute, especially if you have children with you, Thunder Mountain, which was my favourite, It's a Small World (but thats a given!), Pirates of the Carribean, VERY COOL! Wanted to go on it again!.... and for a good laugh try out the Haunted Manor :)Food wasn't *ALL* that pricey... and they were in good portions...about 10 euro per person for a meal...could be worse! But the food was very good...try Casey's  famous  hot dogs! ;)Might be hard if you're wanting to get a photo taken with a character! Most of the lines to take photos with Mickey or Minnie were longer than those for an actual ride!!But other than that everything was perfect! I think we just got lucky with the month and weather! Have fun in Disneyland!!!!!

My two teenage daughters and I had a choice for our last day in Paris: Versailles or Disneyland. Our visit was during the April heatwave and it was well over 80F. I figured that the crowds would be massive on a beautiful Sunday at the palace so it didn't take much to convince me to go to Disney.The train ride from Gar d'Lyon was about 45 minutes. We put our luggage in storage at the station and went out on the RER A.The train literally drops you at the gates of Disney. I was very impressed. We had 6 hours at the park after which we needed to leave for the airport.It was just like being in Florida, heat and all. Despite the crowds we never waited more than 20 minutes. We got a fast pass for Indiana Jones and ate lunch while waiting. It was the best least expensive meal we had in Paris. My girls are vegetarians (one's a vegan) so finding food had been a chore. At Disney each eating place had a vegetarian option which was nice.My girls have always loved It's a Small World and we did it twice. We tried a few new rides and did old favorites as if they were still little kids. We did about a dozen rides altogether.The cost was a bit less than Florida and overall not a bad value. It was a great way to end our European adventure. I guess we were just a little homesick by then.

We arrived with our 7 year old and were lucky to have very good weather. The site is split between the Disneyland park and the adjacent MGM studios and you can buy passes to come in and out of both sites depending on queues and attractions of interest. Some of the more popular attractions offer Fastpasses , enabling to bypass the long queues , but you have to arrive at the attraction within the allocated time slot. of 30 minsI have to agree with other reviewers , that the staff and even some of the characters were miserable . There is a definite lack of staff on site . Food is very limited on site , unless all you want is fast food. Planet hollywood is Ok and service with a smile.If you checkout early at your hotel and spend the the day at Eurodisney , then suitcases can be left at the site entrance for 6.50 euros each. We british are a fair nation and queue politely , other are not so caring and just push in   this happens a lot !!!To make the most of your short stay, plan the rides you want to go on and get fastpasses to minimise the queuing time.

This was my first experience of Disney and have never ridden a rollercoaster, let alone the well themed rides that they operate at Disneyland Paris............but being with a partner who is Disney mad I didn't have a choice but to go to Disneyland Paris with her and her daughter..........plus the rest of her family (totalling 10)..........not that I regret it in any way. What a fantastic 4 days!!! We did everything from the carousel, Pirates of the Caribbean all the way to Rockin' Roller Coaster and Space Mountain. Having never experienced Disney at all I was apprehensive about some of the rides but WOW.............what else can I say......the theming is fantastic and any nerves soon disappeared and the adrenalin kicked in.......especially on the 2 roller coasters. I have never ridden a roller coaster in my 34 years (nor had my partners brother) and she subjected us both to them. Rockin' Roller Coaster was my first coaster ever and the ride was really smooth (a great first coaster for anyone who is not sure of whether to do one). The launch is quite powerful but was a BUZZ!! I can't say anything bad about Disneyland Paris and it's rides. Everything was great, it was clean, the service was great, the theming fantastic. I also started Pin Trading while I was there and the cast members were really helpful and approachable in giving advice and trading pins.........I think I'm addicted to trading as it gives you the opportunity to meet other people from all walks of life and different countries.If you're thinking of a family holiday I can recommend Disney to anyone...............whatever age..............whatever size of party. Our party ranged from 4 years to 64 years and we all had a great time.I'm waffling now because I could talk about my first experience of Disneyland Paris forever!!

hi just got back from disneyland paris went with mum who is in a wheelchair and my 4 yr old son. stayed at the sequioa lodge hotel as soon as we arrived we seen chip n dale an got there autographs and son got a photo with them. hotel room was lovely but the tv is in french only one english channel but we didnt really watch tv as we were out all day till half 10 at night. the village is great for shops which are open till 12 at night so leave that till after the parks. go on the balllon ride in the village the view from up above is fanntastic. we also had a character breakfast which was excellant seen a lot of characters and got photos. the parc was really good as we only had to que for twenty mins for the ridesthe parade was really good to for a good place go at the very beginning near its a small world ride or at the end were they go in. if you want charcters photos and autographs the best place to go is the studios as soon as you go though the gates there are characters every were and you dont have to que to see them either or go near the animaque ride and you will see a load there to. all the staff were very friendly and we had no problem with communicating with them and we dont even speak french if you say hello, please and thankyou you will be treated nicely. when eating would recommend the rainforest cafe, king ludwigs and cafe micky. may be a bit expensive but really nice food and you get a lot to. i took five hundread euros with me and still came back with a hundread euros. and thats with a 4 yr old that got every thing he wanted. overall it was a fantastic experience and would definatly go again in fact im already planning my next trip.

I have been to Disneyland Paris over 10 times in the last 12 years and i have never had a problem, it is a great place to stay and an amazing park. The food inside the park may be dodgy and overpriced but thats what you must expect from a theme park.Everyones complaining about the rides but there is over 50 rides and i would recomend 30 of them, especially thunder mountain, space mountain, pirates of the carribean and indiana jones.All of the hotel restaurants are excellant and so are the Disney village restaurants, (apart from McDonalds of course) The new studios park is very good but a bit too small i accept

Just got back from spending 4nights  5 days in Sequoia Lodge Hotel. i was feeling a bit worried going there as soom of the reviews were not exactly shining but I can honestly say it was a great holiday.We have a son 6 and daughter 8 and they simply loved it. I will not go on about Disneyland as other reviewers have summed it up better than I could but all i will say is enjoy the experience for what it is ! If you go looking for flaws and problems you WILL find them. If you go there to enjoy it with your family you WILL do so , believe me.One thing that i have nopt seen on here is advice on breakfast in the park. When you check in, ask to have breakfast in the park( not the village with the characters, as this costs extra). This gets you into the park at 9am , a full hour before everyone else, where you have a buffet breakfast in one of the lands. Brilliant. Get there early, run to the restaurant, grab a table, eat fast, get out on the rides before any que's! Excellent. We only did it for one morning as it was booked out, wish we could have done it every day !

Disneyland is not only for parents and kids, my boyfriend and I (21 years old) are just back and had the best time. There is plenty to see and do, especially now there are 2 parks as well as Disney Village. In the main Disney park i recommend Pirates of the Caribbean, Indiana Jones Temple of Doom and Big Thunder Mountain; Space Mountain and the Haunted Mansion are also worth a go. You should also watch the parade at least once while you are there. In the Walt Disney Studios park the parade is also great but you MUST ride the Rockin Rollercoaster (at the very least once) and the Backlot Tour. Disney Village is better than the parks for eating out, definately go the Steakhouse for the best steaks ive ever had, and Planet Hollywood had suprisingly good food and wasnt as expensive as i thought it would be. When eating in Disney you do need to spend more to get good food but it is undoubtably worth it; every restaurant will also do a deal e.g. starter and main course for 25 Euros. If you have children(or are a big kid yourself and can afford it) i think think the Newport Bay Club (more expensive) or the Hotel Cheyenne are the best hotels, the Disneyland Hotel looks fairytale like but i dont think its worth the money. If you dont have kids Hotel l'Elysee Val d'Europe is brillant, just one train stop away and is high quality.

Firstly i'd start by saying if you're reading this and thinking of going, book and go. As 2 adults who went without any children you can completely switch off and submerge yourself in the fantasy and the scale of the place. If you've been to Walt Disney World in Florida however DO NOT expect it to be as good   bear in mind the weather, it's not been open as long and need to cater for a multitude of languages.The 2 parks are really 1 and a half. Disneyland Park is as good as florida (except the heat) and will take a good 2 days to get through. Walt Disney studios is not that big although the shows are great and take up a large chunk of the day. Although everyone will have their opinion we've been a couple times and Sunday  Wednesday seems the quietest and Thursday to Saturday are growing numbers (partiularly locals). The difference between quiet and busy being 20mins versus an hours' wait on a single ride. The fastpass system though is helpful to cut qeues.In addition to the theme parks there's also Disney Village which is a mix of restaurants and shops. Fantastic place to go at night and only 2 min walk from the theme parks.The hotels are all within walking distance of the parks and disney village and would recommend the Sequioa or better, as well as slightly better location the breakfasts are much less stressful! Overall eating was fine, don't expect gourmet but there are a few nice places if you look hard enough (Manhatten & Walts being 2 i'd recommend.)The fact that its in France doesn't stop a non French speaker getting by (we've got by a few times) and although service isn't as good as Florida (how could anyone out do the americans at customer service!) it's certainly better than an average day in London.The last point to note is that if you get a chance to go on the eurostar direct take it. The feeling of being on a rollercoaster or shaking hands with Mickey Mouse 20mins after the train pulls in is incredible.Book it now, submerge yourself in Disney fantasy land and get ready for a holiday of a lifetime.

Since I'd never been to disney around xmas time and hadn't seen the studio's yet I thought I'd treat myself to a disney xms break last december!I arrived by thalys from brussels on a, which I liked. YOu arrive straight at the main train station. I then went to the ticket desk upstairs, they thought they wouldn't have my tickets there but they foudn them, this is good if you want to go straight into the park they can drop off your lugage at your hotel but since I wanted to check in first I headed over to the hotel new york. Had a wait a little since my room wans't yet ready but after about 15 min. I was able to check in, refresh a little and head on over to the main park.As soon as I arrived there where big lines for the parade so I went tot he trainstation and watched from there. Nice parade but not one I hadn't seen before.It was very busy but I had thought it might be, it was a sunday after all. So instead of trying to get into attractions I just walked around, soaked up the atmosphere and went into some shops. Was a tadbit dissapointed about the xmasdecorations, I had seen a few years before how they went all out for halloween and would have expected the same or even more for xmas, but I didn't see that... still lovely though and the castle at night took my breath away.Had dinner at Toad Hall, it was quite cold that day and there where no hot drinks or tomato soup left, but still ok dinner(fish and chips). To those complaining about expensive&bad food, why not check out (  ) before you go, they have the menu and prices for each restaurant and reviews by visitors. after dinner still more strolling, and going up robinson's tree, then I went back for fantissilusion. Saw a bench with an open space so stood there but then a guy next to me got mad so I left, and got a much beter place next to the road. Plus angry guy had been in the wrong position for the parade anyway ;o) it was great, if you go don't miss it! they even lighted the castle tot he theme of the parade.After parade much less busy so did a few attractions, LOVED buzz, and it was the end of my first disney day!next day breakfast and over to studio's, had read some bad reports but I loved it. Not busy at all, and really liked attractions as Cinemagique, Animagique and stunt show. Had also booked a guided tour for the afternoon, was by myself but it was great and very informative, only erm 10 euro's and it gives you great background information and points you to things that you don't really notice(did you spot Herbie in the store in studio 1?). I had also taken a tour in the main park on a previous trip that's great aswell.Had lunch at Rainforest cafe which I loved, coudn't even finish it(rasta pasta). Overall loved the studios, parade was nice aswell. After closing headed over to Anette's for takeout which I took to the hotel.The next day I went to the main park, not extremely busy most waiting time about 15 min, I didn't even have to use a fast pass did buzz several times, you really want to beat your previous score. Lion King was great, only attractions closed where peter pan, casey's and autopia. But if you check out the dlp offficial site beforehand it tells you all the closed attractions for your stay, and also when the parades shows are so you can plan your day around that. Had lunch at Bella Notte, againnice although could have added some cheese for hte pasta bolognese. Another take out at annettes and went back to home the next day.overall I loved it, would def. go again but would try to avoid weekends school holiday's. Also all the staff where very helpful throughout my visit, maybe that's also because having a smile on your face usually gets a much better response then a frown...

DON'T GO   especially in school holidays. (We're teachers, so have no choice, but thought Feb half term would be the best option)HUGE QUEUES   in 2 days got on 4 rides. Children could not cope with hour long queues   even the carousel had a queue of 25 minutes. Managed 1 queue for 45 minutes to meet a character. Missed half of the parade (couldn't see the dancers and characters) because didn't stake a pitch an hour before it started. Also queued to get in (despite having tickets), queued to get a buggy, queued for coffee, queued for toilets Etc.FEW CHARACTERS   saw 1 character with an hour queue on first day. Had expected to see them everywhere.CHARACTER LUNCH   expected 'cuddly' characters (as on adverts), also got Captain Hook and another pirate, who terrified the children so much I had to take them out before their birthday cake. This priviledge cost us 200 Euros!I knew it would be a 'rip off', but wasn't prepared for how bad.

My husband, daughter aged 10 and I have just returned from Disneyland Paris. We stayed at Hotel New York from 12 15th inclusive. Drive down from Calais not bad   this was our fourth visit. Checked in quickly at Hotel but disappointed to find no kettle in room and very surly cleaners on arrival at our room door. A great Disney welcome (not!). Unfortunately it was English half term and French school holidays and the park was very busy. Weather was attrocious and we had nowhere to get wet clothes dry easily. Queues to see the characters were long, we gave up half the time. Food was ridiculously expensive. We went to Planet Hollywood for Valentines Lunch and the in house photographer would not take no for an answer until I exploded. Went for coffee, and deli sandwiches one night cost 20 euros. Gave up after that and went to McDonalds. We found the French were given preferential treatment for everything. Queues everywhere all the time through security, for meals, characters. Having said that the new Buzz ride is great and the Stunt Show remains a favourite.However we will not return. Journey back home took 1 hour longer due to accident just on Paris outskirts. Save your money for Florida   we are going to and we are sure the food will be cheaper and the American people so much more warm and welcoming.

Having stayed at Disney Paris for 3 days this week it is so sad to see what Paris has to offer in comparisson to Florida and California. We have been to all 3 parks and Paris is certainly the  poor relation . Magic Kingdom was ok , but dont forget to take food and drink with you   how families cope i really dont know. Much too expensive. Although it was february and no school hols it was busy. Some attractions were not opened due to the weather. Highlight was Space Mountain and low light was deffinately the price and quality of food. I must say Disney has managed to improve customer care with all french staff attempting to speak english and smile   certainly better than a few years ago where we were treated apaulingly by staff who refused to try and understand us because our french was poor. The second day we went to Disney studios   WHAT A WASTE OF TIME AND MONEY ! The park was very small and attractions limited. The weather didnt help !!! We managed to get onto Aerosmith rollercoaster twice and to see the car show   thank goodness because we didnt find much else   ok Armagedon was ok but not really that special. There were technical problems with some rides that meant alot of people were just wandering around   and when we left after just 3 hours in the park we certainly weren't alone !!!!! People were leaving to go to Magic Kingdom or like us to go to find something to eat. We went to Disney Village and managed to be charged 20 euros for 2 sandwiches and coffee !!!!! All in all , save your money and fly to Orlando   a thousand times better !!!!!!!! I relly dont know what the answer is to the problems here.

This was our 2nd visit to Disneyland Paris. We took our 7 year old and 4 year old.We stayed at Newport Bay Club on a 4 nights for 3 offer. We had a fantastic time. I would always recommend staying at the onsite hotels, yes its a bit more money but really adds to the expereince and its not far to go home at the end of the day.Our suggestion would be to plan what you want to do each day   have breakfast early (not difficult with excited children in tow) and get to the park as soon as the gates open. Go on the most popular rides early and get a Fastpass as soon as you come off the ride.We had breakfast in the park one morning which was great as it means you get alot of rides done really quickly before queues start to form. Queueing wasn't too bad apart from the Buzz ride which was 30 mins.The shows are well worth going too. Arrive early as queues form very quickly. Parades in both parks are fantastic, again show up early so you can get a good spot.Baby switch works really well   although on space mountain the staff didn't seem to understand about it.Staff on the whole were very pleasant and helpful and both parks are spotlessly clean.We felt the selection of food was much better this time compared to our visit 3 years ago.
