The childrens menu had options for fresh food rather than just chips.Rainforest Cafe is great for the atmosphere   although pretty standard food.The Blue Lagoon   this resturant is our favorite   So beautiful and the food is really excellent. Remember to book ahead as it gets booked up very quickly.King Ludwig Castle was also very good   the staff are very friendly and its a fun expereince.The Auberge du Cendrillon has a excellent lunch buffet in a magical setting.We would really recommend pre booking a character lunch at the Lucky Nugget Salon   you get a very good buffet and the children get to meet the character without the pushing and shoving that goes on in the parks.Bufflo Bill wild west show is really good fun. Its a bit pricey (but what isn't at Disney) but the audience are involved all the way through, you get so involved you have to try and remember to eat your dinner!!The Sudio park has come in for alot of bad reviews however we had a great time. The Rock & Roller coaster is really good!! Its well worth reading a book such as  A Brits guide to Disneyland Resort Paris  before you go as it gives little tips for things to look out for that you may miss normally. i.e the the rain on the umberella, the massive fan and the the lighting switches. All the shows are well worth a visit the kids will love Amimagique and adults & kids will really enjoy Cinemagique its amazing. The stunt show is very good, but very noisy. There is alot of working going on in this park and its bound to keep on improving.Our final recommendation would be remember its Disney put a great big smile on your face as you walk through the gates and enjoy the magic. We cant wait to go back again

I've been to Disneyland Paris 3 times now and let me tell you its not just somewhere for the Kids,This year my fiancee and I went alone with no neices nephews brothers sisters etc and had a wonderful time. We went during the christmas season and it really was magical! The snow falls throughout the day were great and the fanatllusion parade was something else. We stayed in Hotel Santa Fe in Disney and although it says its a budget Hotel we found it to be ideal. We booked through the disney website and booked flights seperate and got a great deal, i would recommend this to people of all ages!!!

Went to Disneyland Paris just before the European students started their Christmas holidays, arriving in the afternoon of Mon 11th Dec for a three night stay. Had originally thought that that would be too long, but that was the minimum stay on our package deal. Stayed at Hotel Santa Fe. Found it good to be able to take the frequent, free, 5 minute bus ride to Disneyland Park. Midweek meant that crowds were bearable and waits for rides were short (max. 30 minutes), if at all. Would recommend winter and midweek, as the short waits really contributed to our enjoyment. Found all of the staff at Disneyland excellent, always friendly and helpful, and easily switching from language to language, according to the customer; all were friendly and amusing with the children, which kept the children in a happy mood for the whole time (no frayed tempers in sight).Used fast passes successfully also. Found the book,  The Unofficial Guide to Disneyland  very helpful to read before we arrived, even though it referred only to the american Disneyland sites. Much of the info was also applicable to Paris. It reviewed rides (many also at Dis. Paris) and gave much background info. that helped us to plan our visit well, thus saving both time and energy (important in order to be able to last the distance!). Favourite ride of my 16y.o and 8y.o daughters was Thunder Mountain, which they rode 5 times! Also used the  Baby Switch  option in order to go on rides that my 8y.o was too young for, viz Space Mountain (one parent rides first, the other is led to the end beginning of the ride by a staff member, waits for the 1st parent to finish the ride, then quickly hands over the  Baby  so that the 2nd parent can catch the ride immediately. All staff members really added to the enjoyment of the ride.Food was expensive, but we enjoyed a wonderful meal at Walts Restaurant on our last night; from our table by the window, we had a superb view of the evening parade and our waiter was a gem. Also enjoyed Rainforest Cafe, but never managed to get a table   only a seat at the bar (which was still an enjoyable experience for the 3 of us).Disneyland Studios was 2   3 hours only for us, but we thoughly enjoyed our tour of the site, because it gave one the opportunity to experience how some special effects are created, viz a flash flood through the  Canyon  that our bus train was driving through   complete with torrents of flood water. Was not expecting much of our Disneyland visit, not being a fan of theme parks and having read varying reviews, but can thoroughly recommend it. Loved the French influence, too.Checked out Thursday morning and took the train to Paris, arriving at our hotel with still plenty of time to begin our exploration of Paris (where we stayed until Sunday). The French people in both Disneyland and Paris were all incredibly friendly and helpful throughout our stay and communication was not a problem at all. A wonderful holiday for us all.

We (boyfriend and I) spent two days at Disney whilst visiting Paris and we loved it. We went while it was Xmas season.We bough a 2 day hopper ticket which allows you to go in and out of the parks as you wish.We spent the whole of day 1 in the main park. My advice would be to get there early as we noticed after midday the park was crammed full of people.Lots of photo opportunities if it wasnt for the rudeness of other people pushing in and shoving their kids under the characters noses. Not all countries are as polite and as reserved as Brits so if you dont want to get wound up, as we often did leave your manners at home(easier said than done!) Even father christmas took pity on us waiting in line patiently for a photo for about 5 mins while we apparently were invisible to everyone else.Must see the Lion King show which tickets were issued for but having pre read reviews on here i took the advice of getting food and eating in the Videopolis restaurant which saved us time and gave us a good viewing area. We got there half an hr before the show started which is just as well as the food service was slow. I think they have 3 english shows a day.We also enjoyed Disney Studios which I wasnt expecting to because of the bad reviews. There is nowhere near as much to do but this was good as it gave us a more relaxing day 2!Things I really loved:Space MountainLion KingChristmas ParadeMickey & Friends(xmas show)Aerosmith Rock & Rollercoaster(studios)Animagique(Studios)Motor Show (Studio)Studio Cinema ParadeWasn't too impressed with:The other people in the park!Fantaillusion maybe cos i expected fireworks that never cameArmageddonNever got the fake snow which I was really looking forward to.Disneyland Paris seems to get a bit of a bad press which I dont really understand. We had terrible weather while we there too but we couldnt fail to be happy with Mickey Minnie and Co all around us.I have been Florida which is obviously a lot bigger so that will always win when comparing but for the nearness of it and the cost, Disneyland Paris is well worth a trip  2 days if you want to make of all the shows and parades which in my opinion is what Disney is all about.Would definately go back there again and hopefully stay in a Disney hotel next time.

Just wanted to offer some tips if you are off to Disneyland Paris at Christmas (or possibly other times). We went 23 Dec   27 Dec 2006.We drove using the Euro Tunnel. When we got to the other side of the channel, after a while you pass a toll where you pick up a ticket and then further on down the motorway approx 2 hours later you pay 19.20 euros then drive another hour or so ......... however we got lost. All of a sudden you will see a little sign with Disneyland on and then nothing. We didn't know whether to stay on the motorway or turn off (we stayed on and I think we should have turned off) We ended up in the centre of Paris   passing the Stade de France. We tried to get off the motorway to get to a petrol station to ask someone directions, we may as well have been in the middle of India   it was like Wacky Races with cars coming from all directions!! Anyway someone put us on the right track. We arrived 6 hours after we got off the Euro Tunnel   3 more than usual. We stayed at the Santa Fe which was very adequate for a 2*   we figured we wouldn't be spending much time at the hotel anyway. We had a fab time and would definately go again, even staying in the Santa Fe. There is a bus outside reception that takes you straight to the park there and back so every 10 minutes or so. It's a bendy bus and don't bother to queue it is a free for all   be prepared to stand in busier times. I read on these pages that you need to get breakfast early as it is a mad rush. It is but there are plenty of tables. It is continental so basically croisants, small baguettes and cold meets. We took sandwich bags down to breakfast with us and took a few baguettes to eat later on. (Lots of people do).There isn't a kettle in the rooms but we took our own and took cup a soups and coffee etc. The parades are beautiful especially the Christmas ones   it is a really magical time. It was very cold but we took long johns to take the 'bite' off the top of our legs. It was amazingly clean, staff very friendly and attention to detail on the rides were spectacular. Be prepared to wait around 30 minutes on the rides but there are a lot of 'carriages' and the queues go down quite fast. (You can fast pass aswell). However   be warned the French don't queue. We English are too polite   after a couple of days   forget you are English and start using your elbows!! It was not uncommon where you were stood in a queue for half an hour and then this little kid will try and get past you saying pardon! pardon! to get to the front of the queue and then the parents will join him. Buy an autograph book and a chunky pen for the characters to sign. Sometimes you need to queue for the characters and sometimes, they walk around and you can approach them.Take some spare pennies for the souveniers which are reasonably priced. One more thing   we did hire a puchchair for 6.5 euros but you have to leave the pushchair outside the queues and twice ours went missing so you have to go back to the buggy park to get another one but take your receipt and you don't have to pay again. To summarise: Plan your route before you goTake Sandwich BagsWrap up WarmTake your own kettle One of the hotel staff printed off a route map to get back to the Euro Tunnel. Guess what. We got lost again, passing the Stade de France again when we didn't need to. It's best to plan the route before you go.We really did have a magical time and would definately go again.

We recently booked a surprise trip for our children  aged 11 & 14. Disneyland itself was lovely & magical however it was very over subscribed. We queued most of the day. The rides and experiences were good  however there are some major issues. The staff are rude and unhelpful. The cafe areas were unclean and we didnt once sit down to a table which had been cleared. There were no maps in English as they had run out. The food and merchandise is horrifically priced and for the food, of poor quality & a healthy option is nowhere to be seen. It snowed once for 2 minutes  its supposed to snow all the time & the characters are available for the kids on sparse occasions about 40 kids deep so a photo and cuddle is out of the question. All in all, a nice day but the magical experience can only be created by yourselves as the staff arent interested.Universal studios was dire  over priced and dull. It takes about 2 hours to do the whole park. We complained and asked if we could go in the other park again  of course...if you pay again!Again, rude staff, poor quality food, unclean and overpriced merchandise.The Disney Village  open to all with restaurants etc was ok. We had our New Years Eve meal here  it was   65 per head but the only meal worth eating whilst we were there. We were sold a wild west show  turned out to be salsa  and had to wait 30 minutes in the rain to get in & another 30 minutes on some back stairs waiting to be seated but food was nice.Overall  don't bother with Paris. We spent   2000 on the trip, taxis and food for 4 of us for 4 days...save your money & go to Florida & enjoy the magic.

We spend two days at Disney. You need to plan if you are going to see most of the attractions as lots of the good attractions overlap. Download a Disney programme from the Internet for times, this will help. On the website they do not mention if the shows are in English or French, you will get this information from the programme at the park.Studios You must go to see the Stunt show (Moteurs) Studio 6. They have three showings; this is very popular as it was packed. Animagique Studio 3     6 shows throughout the day, get there around 15 minutes before the start of the show, try and sit near the front. Last around 20 minutes Cineagique Studio 2     7 shows throughout the day, last for around 25 minutes. This was ok my 10 year old daughter really enjoyed it. The studio tram ride Studio 5     this was a bit of a let down nothing compared to Disneyworld. In the studios you can get some great photographs of the characters, it is not as busy as in the park. ParkThe one thing that you must go and see is The Legend of the Lion King point 39. They have two shows in English and two in French. You need to get your tickets from Discoveryland point 41 at 10.45am for the 2.30 showing, you need to get to point 39 around 2pm to get in line, so that you get a good sit. This was brilliant, just as good as the Lion King musical in London. It lasts for 30 minutes and you are allowed to take photos and video the performance. The Parades were also brilliant; you must take time out to see this. It is very expensive to eat & drink in Disney. They check your bags as you go into Disney, I do not know why they do this as they just take a quick look. Take in some food & drink of your own. We eat in Disney Village McDonalds for the two days; this was so much cheaper then within the park or studios. Soft drinks & water were around 3     4 Euros each.

My husband and I decided to visit Disneyland Paris after being to L.A in the summer.Our main aim was to see if it was a good as L.A and try to re live those dreams we had in L.A.On stepping into the park, it was like a dream.We were on the main street which is an exact replicar of Disney L.A   it was like dejavu.It was great looking round every corner and taking bets on what ride would be there.All the rides were great but we did have lots of queing some as long as an hour which was unlike L.A and not fun in bad weather.The castle was fantastic (especially at night) and would go as far to say it was better than the one in L.A   it even had a dragon in the dungeons!The food was very expensive but nothing out of the ordinary for Disney parks.The parade's were fantastic and we got the same buzz.At one stage we were walking along the main street and it started snowing which blew us away.It was amazing how they managed to have it snowing in the street, You would definitely be fooled into thinking it was real   as we did for a few seconds! It made our trip just that bit extra special.The only thing we were deeply disapointed in was Disney Stidios   what a WASTE OF MONEY AND TIME.I wish I hadn't wasted   60 and stayed in Disney instead for longer.For a start the studio tour was closed (which is the only thing worth doing) also the Areosmith coaster was shut down, and the parade they had on was something you would see in blackpool.It was a sham and would recomend paying to go in Disney another day instead of the studio's.I don't know how they can sell you tickets for a place that's not finished and had two rides to go on that are far from exciting????The Downtown Disney is just as bad   its seriously out of date and has no Disney feel to it at all. With very little choice of places to eat and no nightlife. Which is a shame seen as the one in L.A is like another Disney (so much to do, you could stay there all night as we did with live music in the street etc..) All in all Disney itself if Fantastic but the rest of it needs updating before the magic of Disney isn't something that happens in France.

We went to Disneyland Paris from 13th to 16th Dec and loved every minute. Our daughter is 3 years old and she loved every minute too. Especially meeting the princesses. I would definitely recommend visting out of season   we didn't have to queue for one ride!!! If we had older children (ie over 9 perhaps) i woud be a litlle concerned about the amount of things to do for them but the whole experience is magical so maybe that really wouldn't be a concern.The only thing negative I feel is the price and quality of the food inside the parks. It was very expensive ( about 20 for 3 x burger and chip meals) and not really of a McDonalds standard!!!! We tried to eat at our hotel (Cheyenne) which was much better. I would suggest trying to take some snack foods with you if possible.Having not visited the Disneyland in the USA I coudn't comment on the difference but we found almost every member of staff helpful and friendly. If anything we found other parents rude when it came to meeting the characters. They would just push their children to the front when everyone else was waiting patiently. All nationalities (including us Brits!) did this I hasten to add. We just found it quite amusing!!!In summary it was a magical experience, not only for our little girl but for myself and husband also.

Disneyland Paris   the train station at the entrance stinks of raw sewerage, the car park behind it has a stench of urine where people probably urinate. You are approached by Gypsies and beggars on the train to disney and all you see is graffiti. The staff there are very rude and impatient and unless you can have a car or afford the extortionate prices of their hotels don't even think about booking a hotel near by as there is no transport to them after 8.35pm. There is little night life which consists of a western bar of a few amateur line dancers and a night club of cheesy 80's music in which you cannot breathe because of the smoke (especially cigars) plus your clothes stink the next day.

I live in Brussels, so I go frequently to Disneyland Paris with my four year old. If you live nearby it pays to get an annual pass, and we have the top of the line pass which also gets us discounts at the stores and restaurants, a free stroller and free bag check at the entrance. The park is based on the LA Disneyland, but is newer (of course) and smaller. Almost everything is still in English and also in French. Main street is shorter and there are a few missing attractions from LA, but there are a lot more restaurants and a larger variety of food   all of it mediocre and expensive. Still, we love it and usually take the train in (which stops practically at the entrance) and stay a night in one of the hotels with a pool to get in a swim and our fill of the rides we like. If you go on a non holiday day in the dead of winter, you can actually stay on many of the rides as long as you like. If you are a homesick American in Europe, I recommend you check it out.

I have visited Disneyland Paris ten times over the last decade and still get excited at the prospect of a visit. I visited the park on my own, with my partner and with children and have never found a fault with it.The rides are excellent   Space Mountain (been on it 65 times), Rock 'n' Roller coaster, Big Thunder Mountain   they're all great.This is definatley not the place to go if you want to lose weight. Every street, every corner has a tempting treat waiting for you. I would recommend the coffee Grinder and Plaza Gardens Restaurant on Main Street; The Cowboy Cookout in Frontierland and Buzz Lighteryears Pizza Planet in Discoveryland.If you can afford it I would definately recommend staying in one of the hotels. I have stayed in the Santa Fe, Sequoia Lodge and the Newport Bay Club. They are so close to the park and add an extra bit of magic to your stay. To keep the cost down I would also recommend the Holiday Inn hotel that is on the Disney site. Holiday Inn have 'Disneyfied' themselves quite sucessfully.For nightlife you can either go to Buffalo Bill's Wild West show or visit one of the many restaurants in the Disney Village   Cafe Mickey is great for meeting the characters or go to the Rainforest Cafe if you fancy a break from everything Disney.I have also visited Walt Disney World Florida which is in its own league. But you can not fault DLP, it is fun, the staff are friendly and helpful, it is just a great escape from reality.

We went to the park twice within a month, the first in Sept 06, it was great, fantastic for the kids range 5 14years. A couple of rides were closed for renovation but not that we minded. The studios were also good thought probably more for the older children. We went two days and pretty much saw and rode nearly everything and were satisifed with our time there. The oinly complaint would be the food and drink prices though I think that would be standard for any major theme park, we bought in our own snacks and drinks, and noticed hundreds of the helium balloons escaping into the sky, so at about 7 euros I would recomend not buying them as they obviously fly away too easily. There wasnt too a long wait for rides, the kids never got inpatient. The only thing I would wnder about is people that bring their kids that are still in prams and strollers, they take up so much room and I really doubt anyone young enough to be pushed around would really benefit from Disneyland especially at the cost of bringing them in etc. The other thing is when we went on the 'Dumbo' type rides, mum or dad would go on with a child as expected but then the parent who isnt with the child would get on a 'dumbo' him or herself?? where you've got kids waiting to get on, I didnt understand why an adult would get on themselves, it's not too exiting ride to experience as an adult???The 2nd time we went after three weeks of our initial visit, we got the english school holidays, and the lines were full and the park was VERY busy, still it was ok, not as enjoyable as our initial visit.

Took my 5 year old and 1 year old to Disneyland. My 5 year old had a ball. She loved meeting the Princesses and visiting Fantasyland. A little girl's dream. Can really recommend The Pirates of The Caribean ride followed by lunch in The Blue Lagoon Restaurant. The whole family enjoyed this. Unfortunatley there is absoluteley nothing for the under threes so my poor 1 year old spent most of the time stuck in her pram. There were no play areas for a pair of little legs to run off steam and there was only one baby care facility in the entire park. There were no baby changing facilities in any of the restaurants. We stayed at the Santa Fe Hotel, one of Disney's own and was very impressed with the standard of accommodation despite it only having a two star rating. I've stayed in four star hotels that weren't as comfortable and the staff were exceptional. Food was buffet style and was more quantity than quality but you could eat as much as you like. Food in the park was reasonably priced but the merchandise was expensive.

What was nice is that there were a number of rides that the whole family (esp. younger members) could enjoy and less of the heartstopping rides. A few of the attractions were not operating on the day we went (there was a strike so only half the staff were running the place) but we still found enough to keep us occupied for the whole day. Highlights were the Buzz Lightyear ride, the Pirates of the Carribean ride, the Haunted Mansion, the Tarzan live show and the 3D movie, Honey I Shrank the Audience. My daughter of eleven and I were able to visit most of the attractions in the park on that one day. We packed a picnic with us so we didn't have to fuss about food and we visited all the Fast Pass ticket machines first so we didn't have to wait in a queue for hours. Re getting there, I visited the website, La Conciergerie and bought two combined RATP Disneyland Resort Paris tickets which included the roundtrip train ticket to Paris. It is, however, cheaper to buy the train Disney entry ticket at a Metro counter if your French is up to it.

Hey all me and my girlfriend have just got back from there and what a time we had!.The park is absolutely incredible with the attention to detail mind blowing even down to the way ropes were tied etc... yes! i was being really picky to try find something wrong.At present the park is celebrating halloween big time and i mean big!!!! PUMPKINS EVERYWHERE....ONLY.as a result the park is so busy at the weekends and i mean busy rammed but not to worry yes long queues but get to the park b4 10am and just fastpass every major ride to return later , you should not have to queue any longer than say 20 mins max on a fast pass ticket .We flew from london to Charles da gaul airport and then took trains to the park . It isnt as hard to find as some will have you believe..k here goesAt charles da gaul you simply board an rer train found at the end of terminal c ask for a paris visite ticket which is essentially a one day travel card at 16 euro or only 6 euro if under 25 yep thats right 25! found out too late on way home lol.anyway you want to be heading to chatelet station where you will change for an a4 train heading for marne le valle which is hey presto right outside eurodisney 4 mins to the gate.!also to note again found out too late there is a eurostar train from the airport at around 22 euro which takes ten minutes. If not the above journey is no more than 1 hour roughly 12 stops to chat the 8 to marne le valle.Leave the movie park till around 4 pm then there are no queues rock and roll coaster here we come !!! oh also eating out is very expensive lunch is 10 euro which is a mcdonalds type meal standard burger chips small drink and main meals are wayyy over the top , however there is a western diner called bobs and if you order from the snack bar menu upstairs , half roast chicken and chips only cost ya 12 euro cheapest we found!!!!!.try to get the big rides early in the morning or even better fast pass straight away coz you ainty gonna get on em otherwise especially space mountain and mine train 70 min queues after 11am.smokers be aware there are very few plces to buy ciggs in fact only the sports bars seemed to sell em bout 6 euro a pack.save money on drinks by keeping your plastic bottle and refilling at the drinking fountains which can be found inside movie park by the toilets.k thats all guys hope ive been of help to you all and have a great time me and my girlfriend did , in fact such was the magic i even proposed to her on the balcony of sleeping beauty castle * guys take note *enjoy Gary

My boyfriend and I went on the 24th 28th September, if you want a quieter time I suggest to go then, maximum time we had to queue was about 15 20 mins for Peter Pan (lovely little ride!).We stayed in the Sante Fe and after reading reviews I was a little nervous but we found ourselves pleasantly suprised. Check in was very quick although we had to walk quite far to our room (they are in blocks). Room was nice, beds are to die for they are so big and comfy!Shuttle buses run all the time but can get very packed as people are leaving to and from the park at peak times.Food is expensive and vegetarians be warned they do not cater much vegetarian choice! Ate in Rainforest Cafe, there was only one dish that was vegetarian, althought the rainforest cafe was spectacular. For lunch, try pop out to the disney village, its a lot less crowded and you can eat in various cafes which have more variety than the food in the disneyland park (burgers, pizza etc). Cafe Mickey is a must (in disney village), you get all the disney characters wandering around and sitting with you (good photo opportunities without the mass of queues!)If you are thinking disneyland is just for kids you are very wrong. We are in our early 20's and LOVED every second of it! Try get to the parades about 15 minutes before they start if you don't want to be pushed etc. Also, be warned, not sure why disneyland brings out the rudeness in people but you will get shoved into and pushed past quite a few times and the french don't seem to have any manners such as a polite excuse me.All the rides are worth a go, make sure you get on the Peter Pan ride its so lovely, and Buzz lightyear is also good. Honey I shrunk the audience is also good, but those who have young children may find it scary as there were at least 6 young children had to be taken out because they were scared.A good tip is if you can, hop on the shuttle bus to take you to Sante Fe, then pop over the road to the petrol station. You can find things much cheaper. To give you an idea, a small bottle of water is 2.90 euros in the park and the village. At the garage you can get a 2ltr bottle for 1.60. It is also good to stock up on snack foods also as they are far cheaper!All in all we loved every second of and and are now going back at Christmas!

Went with an open mind after reading reviews but must say we (2 adults, 2 kids age 6 and 2) had a fantastic time. Our 3 day passes were for a Wed,Thur and Fri at the start of October and not only did we not have to queue for any more than 5 minutes on ANY ride, but were often able to stay on for a second ride. I think queueing for an hour for what are very short rides would really spoil the experience. Take the kids out of school and enjoy at your leisure mid week. Favourite rides were Pirates of the Carribean and Star Tours (6 year old loved it) and Buzz Lightyear (both kids.) Space Mountain was fast, scary and, well, an experience. Animagique brilliant! Peter Pan (which we were able to stay on several times) was a bit of a disappointment. As reported by others, the food is poor and we brought our own with us from the Val d'Europe shopping mall as we stayed in the hotel there. Had two fantastic meals at night in the shopping mall at Val d'Europe and two poor meals at Planet Holywood (nothing special to look at) and Rainforest Cafe (great ambience   pity about the food) in the Disney Village. Three days is just about right. Will definately go back but no way would I go in high season.

What an absolute gem of a break we (my partner and kids, five and three) had a fantastic time. It has made me a legend in my own household. Learnt a few Disney lessons though which I wish to pass on to the first timers.Flew on BA into CDG and then went onwards on the RER to Disney. I wouldn't advise this with two small children and next time will pay the extra and Eurostar all the way direct from Waterloo. BA and the RER wasn't bad it is just the hassle and convenience factors that can be overlooked ie airport check in even with online facility and RER to Chatelet les Halles and change to go onwards to Disney. Took all day due to flight delay and caught in Parisian rush hour.....not good. The RER cost about    50 for a return journey for two adults and one child (5) under fours travel free.Stayed at the Radisson which was a very nice hotel but not that family focused and will probably stay in a Disney hotel next time (See separate review on hotel for further detail).Two parks are brilliant. Would recommend using fast pass to set your day up, concentrate on what you want to do and work round it. Catch the parades as they are emmense my little girl was beaming from ear to ear when she saw Stitch and got a sweet from Chip 'n' Dale. Get to the route about fifteen to twenty minutes before it starts and hold your ground otherwise you will find yourselves at the back of a big crowd.The meet and greets can be quite traumatic as some characters get swamped and the parents just push their kids into a melee whilst others have queuing systems but even then it is only the Brits who respect the queue.For Disneyland Park I would recommend the Buzz Lightyear Laser Blast and even Star Tours which my five year old boy and three year old girl (bit of a tom boy) loved. For the Studios definitely go to the Motor Stunt show which was fantastic and the Animagic show which I guarentee will have every child and adult singing and clapping along.Eating during the day can be quite expensive for what you get as the quality of the food is not great but the french seem quite wise to this and take their own food. Worth doing if planning to eat out in the evenings.Eating in the evening probably best to head for the Disney Village we were recommended to go to Cafe Mickey so the kids can get the full Disney treatment with the characters coming out whilst dinner is on but it had all been reserved so get in early before you leave to guarentee a place. We ate at the Rainforest cafe which was brilliant (full rainforest effects and decor   see it to believe it) and Planet Hollywood which is much of a muchness. Eat early about six o'clock to avoid queuing for a table. A meal for our family was about   50 60 tops.All in all if you want a top quality break for the family then please go. All ages will love it and the sheer magic of the place will win you over. The kids have already asked their grandparents to come next time.........

Arrived on the Disney Eurostar at 1330 on a Saturday for a four day stay. We went to our hotel and arrived at the park at about 1500. It was very busy. Queues were in the region of 1hr 30mins for the most popular rides and fast pass return times were for late in the evening, when we hoped the children would be in bed, so we didn't get on any rides. Sunday was quieter. Monday and Tuesday quieter still.The stunt car show in Disney Studios was excellent and Honey I Shrunk the Audience in Disneyland Park was very effective (but scared the children, 5yrs and 2yrs)   both of them are a must.After a disappointing start Disney worked it's magic and we can't wait to go again.

Do not go on a weekend. We went on a Thursday and it was pretty much quiet, and easy going. Our longest line up was 10 minutes. Compared to California Disney some of the rides were low budget ex: Indiana Jones, Nautilis... And some of the rides were missing entirely   Splash mountain. There was construction and a few rides were closed do to it.   Big Thunder Mountain. Over all we had a fun time, there were lots of characters running around and a parade. Space Mountain 2 was wild and so was the Aroesmith Roller Coaster. We saw super cool stunt show by Renault, and a crazy Tarzan show with great acrobatics.We had fun, but it didn't quite compare to Disney California.

Its lovel. and kids enjoy it but it is over priced. If you plan on going to the florida parks, go to Euro Disney first as there is no comparison between the two. In the states I was in awe of the sheer sizme of the place, never mind anything else. The french are ok and the park is good for a short break. Worth treating the kids to!

Well, just don't... while they are honestly trying, they are still who they are, e.g. if something goes wrong, it is never their fault. the park is good fun, the food overpriced and most restaurants grimy. but the kids love going there, and as guilt ridden caregivers, we oblige. we are even going back!

I just came back from a 3 days visit to Disneyland Resort Paris. The experience was a fairy tale. It was like I lived in another world of fantasy and forgot all the ugliness of the real world. I liked most Fantasyland, where the clasical disney stories were described. Most of the attractions are a magic experience but you have to spend much time to see them all. I think that 3 days is the minimum if you want to see the park and the studios without being on your feet 24 hours a day! My favourite attractions: The small world and the Pirates of the Caribbean. Don't miss them in any case!But although it was August it rained a lot most of the time. As I learned from other visitors it rains there about 9 months in a year!! I guess France (or another so rainy country) was not the proper choice to build such a park that people are walking outdoors all of the time. Of course there are many raincoats available for bying but in any case it is annoying to go around all day with the raincoats and the umbrellas. Queoues were usually long and we had to wait about 30   40 minutes for some attractions, but in some other ones 15 minutes was the maximum waiting time.One thing that I cannot understand is the reason that some people bring their infants at Disneyland Park. In my opinion this is not a place for so young kids. Infants are not familiar with disney characters and stories and make no difference for them. In addition they get tired very easily (to go around all the attractions is in any case tiring even for older kids), they cannot stand the rain (and the raincoats) and the cold, they have to eat and sleep at certain hours (soomething that cannot be possible in such a place) and many of the attractions can scare them a lot. Personally most of the infants I saw in the park were either sleeping or crying. I would suggest to parents to wait for their kids to become at least 5 years old (or even more) to visit the park with them. Food was average, although I chose the most expensive restaurants of the Park. Service was good, except at this French traditional cuisine restaurant Auberge de Cendrillon where people were standing in the queoue for ages and no waiter was bothered to informed us that we can enter the restaurant only if we had a reservation. In addition that restaurant closed every day at 4:00 pm and again when we went there after that time (we did not know it was closed, doors were open and much staff was inside) nobody was bothered again to informed us that we could not stay until we asked by ourselves after about 20 minutes of siting at the entrance!!! Walt's was a very nice decorated restaurant and with acceptable cuisine. Service was excellent, but the toilets were not in so good condition and the air conditioning was very strong although there was a lot of cold outside. Rainforest cafe was the most spectacular restaurant I have ever seen.... it was like I was eating inside a jungle with moving elephants beside me! The food was American style and the staff very polite and helpful. I ordered something outside the catatlogue because of a stomach problem but in any case they had any problem to prepare it.Blue Lagoon restaurant was situated in a spectacular place, the service was excellent and the food was above average.

If you have a baby toddler and are taking a pram buggy please invest in a bicycle lock and take it with you. We emerged from Buzz Lightyears Laser Blast to find our buggy had been taken from the buggy park. The staff didn't seem to take the problem seriously and said that someone had simply taken ours in error and we should keep checking the buggy park as it would be returned. They did lend us one of their strollers but only agreed reluctantly that we could take it out of the park to our on site hotel. Our buggy was never returned and in spite of being told to check at lost&found every day we were always made to feel like we were a nuisance. We were told by different staff members that this rarely happens, happens quite often, happens all the time and in one case is an 'organised' crime.Whatever the case we had to make a trip to the local hypermarket to buy a basic buggy and a cycle lock and although we had a fantastic time (hence the four star rating) this will forever be the holiday when the buggy got stolen.

My husband and I have just returned from a three day trip to Disneyland Paris and we had a fantastic time!! We spent two days in Disney and the new Disney Studios   which does have some great rides   Rock and Roller Coaster is fantastic for big kids! We stayed at the Dreamcastle Hotel which was fabulous very clean and comfortable. On arrival at CDG airport we decided to use the TGV service to Disney instead of the VEA bus, although it is slightly more expensive (about   29 for two adults) it only took 8 minutes which was fantastic, we did the same again on the return journey!In Disney I would recommend getting their for 8.30am to see Mickey open the park, although the attractions do not open until 9.00am you can get ahead of the queues.Definatley use the free fast pass system for the main attractions, particularly Buzz Lightyear as any age can ride.When watching the parade at night (10.30pm) head for the castle outdoor theatre, you get so close and get to sit on benches not on the pavement, we got seats about 45mins before the parade started. A word of warning, if you are going for the big rides, Big Thunder Mountain will be closed for maintenance from 21st August.This is the second time I have visited Disneyland Paris and I would definatley go again!

I've just been to DLRP for the fourth time, and we all had an amazing trip. The dates of our holiday were 25th June   1st July, which is high season (the queues were long). But with a whole week, we got everything done that we wanted to do, so my first tip is to make sure you allow yourself plenty of time to see everything.Secondly, the Fastpass system. You need to be pretty savvy to get the most out of this. Get to the park as early as you can (often its opened before the published time, especially during high season) and get all the Fastpasses you can immediately. Sometimes, it is possible to get multiple Fastpasses for the different attractions at over lapping times. Using this method, we did some of the busiest attractions (Big Thunder Mountain, Space Mountain, Buzz Lightyear's Lazer Blast, Star Tours) within a couple of hours. I stress again, be quick to get them  By 11am, the return time for Big Thunder Mountain was 18:00... and that often means you can't get another Fastpass until after that time!Eating out. Yes, its expensive, especially if you opt for table service restaurants. But some useful tips: the 'picnic' rule is not, in my experience, very well enforced. Most days on our holiday, we were literally taking in bags of food and nobody stopped us. Also, you do generally get what you pay for: for example, The Lucky Nugget in Frontierland costs 30Euros for adults, but you can eat all you want and the food is delicious, plus there are loads of characters and music while you eat. Book seats for all restaurants in advance to save having to wait for a table later on (you can do this in your Disney hotel or if you're staying off site at City Hall on Main Street).Finally, where to stay. My biggest tip for anybody thinking of going: stay in a Disney hotel. Its a little more expensive, but there are big benefits. Firstly, as the parks are very tiring its easy to walk back to your hotel for a freshen up before popping back (priceless in the summer when the main park is open until 11pm). You get free a shuttle service between your hotel and the parks, and the theming is brilliant. If you're on a budget, go to the Cheyenne and NOT the Santa Fe  Its only a few quid more but the rooms are bigger, the theming is fantastic and you get free Disney TV (you have to pay extra in Santa Fe!).I've been to Florida, and yes its an amazing place. I think many people are disappointed with Paris because they expect it to be the same thing  Its not. The Paris resort is not simply a small scale version of other DIsney resorts (when its finished, its going to be nearly as big as Florida anyway!); it has its own atmosphere and does things differently, but as long as you are prepared, make sure you've got plenty of time and read up on the resort as much as possible, I can't see how you could fail to have a fantastic time.

Before going to Paris and Disney we had been warned that it was expensive, but we thought we would treat ourselves.What I wasn't expecting was to have to pay to park before we had even paid to get into the park. Be warned if you have a campervan   it is TWENTY euros to park! We saw plenty of people turning around to find somewhere else. Surely if you are paying 43 euros per person (for one park) to get in, you shouldn't be expected to pay for parking.Despite this, the park was impressive and generally clean and well organised although it was phenomenally busy and hot with the French workmanship evident (potholes and cracks in the roads).Queues were already over an hour for the big rides by 12 o'clock, so we decided to use the fastpass system to allow us quicker access later. Generally this seems a good idea but be aware: this only seems to be operating up to about 1 o'clock   after this you will have a long wait (as we found with 70 minutes for thunder mountain).The rides were genuinely good, food ok although overpriced (but where isn't in a theme park) and the atmosphere was organised chaos. We didn't see any characters though and the parade was a madhouse.In general it was worth going, but to be honest I much preferred Florida Disney   it has the same rides but a far better atmosphere and is better value for money. My advice would be to save a little more and go to the US instead.

Just got back from 4 nights at Hotel New York at Disneyland Paris and had a wonderful time. We arrived on Monday 5th June which was a nightmare as it was a national holiday in Europe and the parks were very busy but during the rest of our stay the queues were short and fastmoving so I guess you have to be careful when you go   maybe opt for mid week in school holidays if you can.Our only gripe was the cost of everything   10EURO for a drink in the hotel bar and six of us ate in Cafe Mickey in Disney Village one night (two kids aged 4 and 7) and had a modest meal and it came to 190EURO. The attraction of this venue was that the characters come and greet you at your table and the look on our kids faces was really something   I hate the phrase you get what you pay for but .... The same with the Hotel New York, it is expensive but worth it as it is just 10 minutes walk from the park and there is no problem with overcrowding at breakfast etc. and the staff are wonderful with the kids.So.... should you go?... yesIs it relaxing?........ no but it is a lot of fun and your kids will love itIs Disney in America better and cheaper? ....... yes but I would only go there with kids older than seven or eight if your kids are younger give Paris a try, much shorter flight and easier on their little legs getting round the parksWhat was the best bit for us?........ Castle at Disney, Meeting the Characters, Buzz Lightyear Ride, The food in Disney Village which was fantastic without exception, Lion King Show, ParadesFinally don't listen to those guidebooks that tell you to plan your stay like a military operation, if you do you will just get stressed, take a look at your map now and again and go with the flow   you are on holiday!!!

The worst bit about it was that it is in France   where they are rude, obnoxious and French !!!!

Visited for four days end may 2006 and it was a most disappointing break. Weather was awful, hotel was chaos and dirty (newport bay club).Breakfast was so chaotic there were nearly fights in the queues for tables. The park itself was not prepared for the major uk holidays with many major attractions closed and hoardings up around many shops on main street.Fast pass only worked intermitantly and choas one day when the entry system failed and everyone had to get their entry passes stamped by hand.My young children were terribly disappointed and kept asking about when we could go to proper disney in florida.The studio park was waste of time and we were out within a couple of hoursWe could not believe how expensive it was either. I dont consider paying   60 plus for an average burger meal for 4 value for money.Only good point was eurostar train journey was excellent.Save your money and go to US as they do this sort of thing so well over there.

We visited Disneyland in Paris on the 4 June 2006 and was very disappointed. Paying to get in to the park was easy and there were plenty of cashiers to help you paying the fee for the park (no lines here)Once inside came the bitter truth of the magic, the place was packed with people and the favouirite attarcation pirates of the carribian was closed and no warning of this at the ticket office. But we could live with that, but then came the shock the fastest line to find was Peter Pan at 50 minutes. All the other main attractions were up to 100 minutes to wait for. So we were able to try 5 attractions including the boring Nautilus submarine so I should say we got to try 4 attractions for 121 Euros. I guess you can understand the disappontment our son showed (6 years).What did we do to try to improve our situation then!We tryed to get fast passes, all gone!We asked for advice on how to save the day and get some magic at the information, advice given was to skip the parade and go to Peter Pan instead, people will start getting home at 1700 to 1800 Hrs then it will get better, it did at 1930 Hrs and then the attractions was closed!The food in the park is overpriced to say the least, a hot dog is 4,7 Euros and picknick is forbidden.As the attractions are fantastic our recommendations must be1 Do not visit the park in high season as it is a rip off for what you get during this time2 Be french and try some civil resistance and have a picknick iniside the park and see the arrest of your family as an attraction as they are very difficult to try anyhow. I am sure the sight of Mickey stopping your family eating will aruse the french around you and thus helping you avoid the hot dogs for 4,7 Euros3 Try helping us in saying to Disneyland Paris that they should do as at the Eiffel tower does and that is to candidly state the waiting time to see the top before you pay as it is important to give children the right expectations!

Disneyland is one of those places everyone should visit at least once. I got my chance to go with some like minded friends and I had a really good time.  Read the travelogue at...  http:  myweb.tiscali.co.uk afleming holidays disneyland paris.html  Cheers  Alex

I want to share my experiences with all other parents who are planing to go to Disneyland Paris (DLP) with their children. I just returned from a 8 day trip with my 8 year old boy (15 22. April) of which 2 days were spent in DLP. After extensive research on the net about how to experience DLP in the most efficient and enjoyable way I would like to give you a summary of the most valuable tips:As for a trip to Paris in general I have come to the conclusion that don  t bother going with small children (0 6 yrs). It will be tiering, expensive and wont yet leave a lasting impression on them! Disneyland Paris is probably not yet worth the money at this age. Whatever your kids will enjoy doing in DLP you can offer them for a fraction of the price in your home town! So, wait until they are a bit older to really enjoy the experience. Our friends with 3 kids (8,6,4) had a 1 day horror experience. The 8 year old enjoyed herself, the 6 year old was sleeping in the 4 year olds buggy while the 4 year old had one fit after the other. When the DLP closed even the parents picked a fight. Arrive EARLY before opening time. Although the opening was scheduled at 10 am, they let you through to Main Street USA at 9.30 am: entry to the lands at 10 am sharp.  If you arrive with luggage do not waist time checking into your hotel. You can store your stuff at the entrance to the complex for     2,5.  for the day  buy your entrance ticktes, take a map of DLP and enter the Park on foot     do not take the train     it is awfuly slow!!!!!!  get fast pass tickets for all the main rides (6) see list below: don  t start going for apparently 5 min rides     fastpasses will be out by 11.00 !!!! This means you will spend half a day getting your fastpasses and running through all the lands and then going on your fastpass rides. List of Fastpass attractions:Frontierland1.Big Thunder Mountain (mild roller coaster   great fun)Fantasyland2.Peter Pan's Flight (quite boring)Discoveryland3.Buzz Lightyear Laser Blast (my 8 year old liked it)4.Star Tours (good)5.Space Mountain: Mission 2 132 cm (didn  t do)Adventureland6. Indiana Jones and the Temple of Peril 140 cm (didn  t do)   If you particularly enjoy any of the fastpass attraction get another fastpass ticket as soon as you come out of that attraction.    perhaps fastpasses will stil be available for a second ride in the afternoon! Using this method we went on Buzz Lightyear twice.  If you want to watch the The Lion King show without queuing go to the Hyperion Caf   at the Videopolis Theatre (in Discoveryland) and buy yourself a meal half an hour before the show starts. The show is in the same building! Get your food, get a seat and watch the show while you eat!!!! People who didn  t know about that were queuing for the show for hours!  At 16.00 the parade begins, so time your rides to ensure that you are already waiting on the edge of the parade route 30 45 minutes before it starts. Pick a good spot near the start of the parade route The parade enters the Parade Route from next to  it's a small world . A good spot is opposite the Pizzeria Bella Notte or gelateria Fatansia. Usually far less crowded than the rest of the route. Remembered to sit down near the barrier early this time to get good view.  If you watch where the parade starts you can then head back to the rides while everyone else is still watching. Tried this trick on two consecutive days and was able to go on 4 almost empty rides until the masses came back from watching the parade.   Get on your last rides just before the park closes  You will be in the park after everyone else has left, and all the shops on Main Street are still open. (this way we went on thounder mountain 4 times!!!!)  We stayed at the M  wenpick (a 4 Star much cheaper non Disney hotel), which can be reached easily by the purple PEP BUSES. Why pay more for a 2 star Disney hotel? You only go there to sleep anyway.  Take sandwiches from your hotel breakfast buffet for a snack in the park..  Carry a zipable bag and a bottle of water around.   Keep valuables on you. Not in your bag!  There is no pharamacy around.  Both shows Lion King and The Tarzan show are to be recommended  Buffallo Bill Dinner Show at night has to be purchased separetly   can be recommended.What would I do differently?  I would try and book a breakfast with the disney characters on the day of my arrival at DLP for 8 to 9 am. This way the kids get their autograph for sure. It means no queuing to see them in the park and the possibility to walk around the park before masses arrive.  Take more time to enjoy the Disneyland illusion (I know it  s hard to enjoy while running after fastpass tickets, trying to orient yourself in this huge complex)What did my 8 year old enjoy most1.Big Thunder Mountain (mild roller coaster   great fun) in Frontierland fastpass2.Pirates of the carabean Adventureland no fastpass (best time to do right after you have watched the parade at the beginin of the parade route, whlie others are stil watching it)3.Buzz Lightyear Laser Blast and Star Tours in Discoveryland fastpass4.In Fantasyland he enjoyed it  a s small world. He didn  t enjoy Peter Pan's Flight (fastpass) that much and I agree (quite boring).5.Buffallo Bill Dinner Show. It was a wonderfull way to end the Disney experience.So, plan ahead, be well prepared and equiped and most of all enjoy the experience yourself. Your child will notice the difference.

The 4 day trip was excellent though tiring. You have got to love walking! The Sequoia Lodge Hotel was fine, though we had asked for adjoining rooms and were given rooms opposite. Thank goodness there were plenty of toilets so that a group of 5 didnt have to trudge miles   HOWEVER, WOMEN BEWARE   THERE ARE NO SANITARY MACHINES OR CHEMISTS ANYWARE. WHY? I cannot seem to access a customer complaints site or telephone number for Disneyland Paris either to get an answer to this.

We did Eurodisney for the UK half term break in Feb. The weather was bleak and cold, and rather drizzly, but better than in the UK where it was bleaker and colder. This was my second stay at the Sequoia. We chose the S because it is the 'lowest grade' Disney hotel with an indoor pool, which is great (though you have to brave the cold to reach the pool house! Towels cost, so either bring your own or nick the room's!). Poolhas a slide and a jacuzzi   both very pouplar.Hotel itself is not a problem, but it cost   600 Monday Friday for a room sleeping four (two double beds). It was OK, but nothing palatial. No room service, NO kettle tea coffee making facilities   obviously they want you to spend the money downstairs.The food is the big problem, as it is throughout Disney, where the food   even in the US Disney   is outrageously awful. So bad that I can't believe Americans put up with it. Monumentally bad. Stupendously bad. Outrageously bad. Appalling. (etc) Just bad, bad, bad   ruins the entire stay.The food in the Sequoia was less awful than in the park, but still nothign to write home about. Breakfast is Ok if you like cheese  boring jams, butter, but the croissants and rolls are fresh and very good. Juice tastes 'tinned'. Worst of all is the coffee. Disney sold its soul to Nescafe, and that's all you get. Everywhere. The whole park. Every hotel. Rubbish, rubbish nescafe. One tip   inside the MCdonalds in the nightmarish Disney village (though at least you can eat at the Rainbow Cafe and Planet Hollywood, which is marginally better than the Disney garbage food) is a little stall that actually sells Kenco coffee (or somethign similar). It actually tastes not bad. But, of course, this is SUPPOSED to be France. How and why teh French put up with the atrocious food at Disney and utterly undrinkable coffee I don;t know   I assume they just wash their hands of the whole place. I think they should insist on decent food there   it's a disgrace to France.We ate once at the Sequoia, the posh Hunter's Buffet   that was actually very good considering   BUT HORRENDOUSLY EXENSIVE. I mean, out of all possible reason a rip off price. I'll try and check what we paid, but it was somethign like   20 a head   and, of course, once the children are 12 it's adult price.If you want decent food get to the shopping mall at Marne la Vallee. oh, the relief!!! Decent french food.I agree with the rave review of Aerosmith   our 12 year olds loved it   much better than Space Mountain they said which bashed the heads unmercifully. The Thunder Mountain here is better than in the States, and Space Mountain is a loop ride here, which it isn't in the US. Those, togetther with Indiana Jones and the T of Doom, are the only real thrill rides here   which is not a complaint, as obviously Disney caters for younger children. Next year it's Universal and the Hulk!!! Conclusion   Disney is very expensive. Stay at My Travel Explorers hotel if you can get in   we keep trying to book and it's full. Does big rooms for six with kids in a bunkbed room inside   very appealing sounding. Also has an indoor pool. And a shuttle.But the best is to get a flat at Marne la Vallee, and then you have a civilised place to escape to, and DECENT RESTAURANTS! Staff at the Sequoia very good   polite and efficient.Oh, Buffalo Bill show   very, very expensive   good fun, food poor (as usual) but a fair amount of it.The Paris trip is also very expensive, but it's a great way to see all the 'main bits' in one day, very easily. You get a Bateau Mouche trip   good, but only get an hour for lunch by Notre Dame which isn't enough for both lunch AND cathedral, and you don't have time to do the towers which children would love. BUT you do get the Eifel tour, which is great   no queing as the tickets are prebooked! But if you are more adventurous take the RER to Le Chatelet and then zoom around wherever you want .AND EAT SOME DECENT FOOD!!!!!

Have just returned from a 4 day break staying at the Hotel Cheyenne with my husband and 2 kids aged 9 and 10.The whole experience was just brilliant. The kids thoroughly enjoyed themselves and so did we. Disneyland Park itself was immaculate and every toilet we visited was exceptionally clean and pleasant smelling and they were all being continually cleaned! All the staff we met, both in the park and shops were all extremely friendly and helpful.We found that this 4 day, 3 night break was just long enough to cover both Disneyland Park and the Studios. We were slightly disappointed by the Studios and managed to cover it in half a day but the rides in the Park more than managed to make up for it. Yes, the food in Disney Village and Disneyland Park was extremely expensive but if you go catered for this and expect it you will be fine. After all this was our main holiday and we ate what we wanted, bought what we wanted and still managed to come home with some money!A top tip is to have a character breakfast. Ours was in Cafe Mickey and the food was delicious and plus the opportunity to have your photo taken with the assorted characters was plentiful without having to stand in a queue.We ate in Rainforest Cafe, Cafe Mickey and King Ludwigs Cafe. All food more or less the same in each restaurant.Make sure that if you go at this time of year that you wear waterproof clothing, hats, scarves, gloves and very comfy walking shoes as you are on your feet a very long time!I would definitely go back but maybe at Christmas time or Halloween but I definitely wouldn't go in the summer. The queues were virtually non existent and the most time we spent in a queue was 10 minutes for Big Thunder Mountain which was well worth it. The Fastpass system is a godsend and recommended.We stayed at the Hotel Cheyenne which was excellent   please see Hotel review for it.The people that have written negative reviews about DLRP must have been to a totally different place to where we have just been!!!!

I just got back from a great time with my sister at Disneyland Paris where we stayed at Hotel New York. We went to Florida when we were little, so this was a chance to indulge in some nostalgia.When planning how much time you need if you're an adult without children, two full days should cover it. Best order is to do Disney Studios in the middle, to clear the Disney from your system before you go back to the Park. It took about 5 hours, including meal breaks and a hobbling sister with blisters from new shoes, to cover two lands. To get the adrenalin pumping, go on a rollercoaster first thing in the morning. If you have a hotel Fastpass, you just hand it to the Fastpass entrance attendant and don't queue with non residents. Oh, and you take your bags on all the rides, including 360 degree rollercoasters, so maybe best to keep them small and zippable.Fantasyland was my favourite: Peter Pan, Snow White, Pinnochio and It's a Small World were pure Disney magic. Be warned that you wander round the Alice in Wonderland labyrinth for quite a while! There's a good view from the top of the little castle though. Check out the themed weathervanes on the rooftops. Also make sure you go downstairs through the glass shop in the main castle to see the sleeping dragon.The Parade: We nearly didn't bother, but actually it was a great injection of Disney magic and 20 minutes of really good fun.   Dancing   and singing   ... A Disney Hol iii day! Discoveryland: The overall theme is the future as visualised by Jules Verne which is very odd as it's kind of wrought iron with computers. The Star Wars flight simulation was so fantastic I went twice! Honey I Shrunk the Audience had a very long preamble and boring Kodak advert which took the shine off the cool 3D effects. Also you have to clamp the headphones to your ears to hear the English translation. The much hyped Space Mountain 2 was OK, but quite clunky and we collected a few bruises after being thrown around. A new Buzz Lightyear ride is being built and the ad for it on the hotel channel looks brilliant, kind of like It's a Small World but where you cruise through shooting targets with laser guns. Frontierland: Phantom Manor had the most comfy seats of any ride so was quite a relaxing break and the ghosts were groovy. Big Thunder Mountain runaway train was pretty tame, but still fun. Unfortunately the Wild West in overcast March skies looks a bit too brown and wooden for an effective theme.Adventureland: Beware getting lost on Adventure Island if you're in a hurry! Swiss Family Robinson treehouse was OK, but sadly the view from the top was non existent as it was covered with leaves. The Indiana Jones rollercoaster was a real screamer although again quite clunky. My favourite was Pirates of the Caribbean   most of the queue is inside in the warm so a good spot to head to if it's raining   but my sister got soaked. They're re doing it in April to take into account the film so maybe you get to be stranded with Jack Sparrow on a desert island?!Disney Studios: We went on the third day and it was quite a let down. They haven't really sorted out the queuing so there was alot of hanging about. The Behind the Scenes Tram ride was pretty boring, with only two active bits   sit on the right to avoid being drenched  and a few flame throwers. The Armageddon ride had a huge preamble and wasn't that exciting. I'd recommend heading straight for the awesome Aerosmith rollercoaster and just keep going round! It's so smooth, there are 360 degree loops and G force and different music blasts out every time. The other highlight was the Moteurs Spectaculeur show, which is an amazing stunt show of cars and motorbikes.As for eating at Disney, diets, budgeting and healthy eating are out. No wonder the kids are running up and down corridors at 11pm having consumed enough additives to preserve Fungus the Bogeyman! The cheapest adult meal in the park itself is around 10E for burger and chips and a fizzy drink. The water fountains were turned off, and it was 3E just for a drink.Best food: Art Deco restaurant in Studios near Aerosmith rollercoaster where we had a lovely beef stew and tomato and mozzarella salad with drink for 18E. I momentarily considered paying 4E for a plate of raw grated vegetables, I was craving fresh food that much!Worst value food: Cafe Mickey in Disney Village. We paid 20E each for awful fish and chips   soggy batter and the chips had obviously been standing around a while. Because the Disney characters come round every hour to your table, there are loads of photo opportunities and hugging so it is worth the effort. However you're probably better off ordering a starter and then heading to MacDonalds afterwards.Top tip: You can get to the real world if you go to the railway station between the Park and Disney Village. There's a coffee and sandwich shop and a tabac selling snacks at cheaper prices than the hotel shop.In Disneyland, there are souvenir shops everywhere and cunningly each is slightly different. If you're after a particular T shirt or item, do make a note of where you saw it as the ranges on offer vary. If you're staying at a Disney hotel, say *at the beginning of the transaction* before you hand over anything as there's some paper work, that you'd like it sent to your hotel. This saves you taking bags on the rides and you can pick up the bags at your hotel shop after 8pm.

I have been fortunate to have now experienced all three Disney theme parks, California, Orlando and now Paris. First of all I am an adult, but then the theory has it you can become a kid again when you enter into Disneyland...I just became a mean adult!Disneyland in California was the first and in my opinion is the best, you experience what Walt Disney really had in mind for all of us. Orlando is pretty much the same but much, much bigger with all the added attractions, EPCOT, water parks, etc. and those in themselves are really separate parks. Then there is Euro Disneyland just outside of Paris, about a 35 45 minute Metro ride. What a huge disappointment it was! It did not have the  magical  feel of the other two parks in the least!!!!It was certainly not maintained to the high standard that we have come to expect from the other two parks, garbage on the ground, buildings in disrepair   chipped paint, worn. Even the costumes worn by the staff were not sharp looking. Staff were sloppy and lacked  smiles and enthusiasm ... Parisiennes are not warm, fuzzy, smiling folks anyway. A lot of Europeans smoke, and it is allowed in the park and yes, it the line ups too   try standing in close quarters with someone blowing smoke in your direction and on your kids!!!!The service was poor and extremely slow, they ran out of food, they ran out of change and getting onto the rides was the worst! Six of us went and it wasn't cheap   12 years and up are considered adults   the kids only made it onto 4 rides as most line ups took at least 45 minutes to one hour! We went on Friday, Feb. 24, 2006   it was also bloody cold!We heard that Disneyland did not  take off  in Europe and we could certainly understand why. My suggestion is to save your  Euros  and pass on the park as it was a huge let down! You get far more of a thrill from the Eiffel Tower!

We (2 adults, 4 year old child) visited only Disney Land Park (not Studios) on quiet day, but there were 20 40min. queues everywhere, which was frustrating. Food was also bad and expensive. It was quite weird, that the same food (especially bad coffee and lame bakings) was offered everywhere in park though the cafees and restaurants were so different and well set up. Indeed I came to suspect, that e.g. Nestle and Buttoni (frozen pizzas) are paying to Disney corp. for serve their products as promotional purposes. I gave 3 5 despite of too long queues and bad food, because me and my family really liked the park's atmosphere and attractions. For us there was indeed too much to do in single park in one day because of the small child. Next time have to leave her to hotel : )

Visited February half term with a ten and twelve year old. As a seasoned theme park visitor in USA and Europe I was pleasantly surprised with Disneyland Paris. Queues were minimal. The odd ride with a more than 10 minute queue had a fastpass option so that you could come back later and not queue as long.If you have breakfast in the park (at no extra charge if you stay at a Disney hotel) you can ride several rides before the park opens to the public. We did this two successive days and had no wait at all. Get to breakfast earlier to get best advantage.The attractions aren't quite as numerous as in Florida but judge it on its own and it is still an excellent place to visit.Prices to stay at hotels in the off season are cheap and include free park entry.

We have just got back from Disneyland Paris, and WOW what a place!Our whole family have never had a better holiday   it was amazing. The parks are outstanding, the rides are much newer and better than the American versions especially Pirates of the Caribbean, It's a Small World, Space Mountain and Big Thunder Mountain   we've been to Walt Disney World 3 times and the original Disneyland in California twice. The parades are excellent in both parks, and we've never seen as many characters in the US as we saw in our 3 days in Paris. My daughter filled 2 autograph books, about 60 characters   and you just seem to bump into them much more randomly and magically than in the States.The themeing in the Disneyland is so fantastic too, the American parks   though nice, are a total mess when you have been to Disneyland Paris. The way the park is laid out is a masterpiece, the planting, fountains, waterfalls and buildings are all so beautiful. It really makes Walt Disney World look like a rough, dated and nasty cheap fun fair.The staff are so nice too, all can speak good English and nothing was too much trouble.Food is quite expensive but it's worth it, most of it was beautiful.We are going back in the summer to see the new ride Buzz Lightyear's Lazer Blast. And after talking to a cast member we learned that next year there will be 2 new day time parades for the parks and also a new  land  in the studios called  Toon Studios  with 3 new rides. And then in November 2007 the only thing which is currently missing in my opinion the TOWER OF TERROR is opening in the Studios.We live in the UK and can safely say we will never again visit Walt Disney World. What is the point?All the Disney Magic we could ever need is waiting just 1 hour away at Disneyland Paris.Anna

Disneyland Paris was quite lame. In fact, it bordered on being a waste of not only money, but time.The number of attractions is quite limited and pales miserably to either of the parks in the United States. I guess this is what happens when a corporation (Disney) builds a park instead of a singularly talented, visionary man (Walt).Disneyland Paris has about one third of the attractions and way less fun than the parks in the States. Two of the marquee rides, Space Mountain and Big Thunder Mountain, were  closed  for no apparent reason   on a SATURDAY. French labor laws? Poor management? I don't know the answer but the result was plain: the park was a big disappointment.Save your Euros, Pounds, or Rupees for a trip to the States and the real deal!

Stayed at the sequioa lodge at disneyland paris.This is our fifth visit to this hotel (three times at christmas)We arrived on the 15 of December with our party of seven.As always our hotel was excellent and every where was very festive.We found the first two days very quiet in both parks with no wait for rides.It was very different by the weekend when it seemed most of Paris was in the parks(two hour wait for thunder mountain and peter pan ride)I must recommend the  Grease  show in the disney village and the Lion King show in Disneyland Park. We ate at the Rainforest Cafe on the first night good meal and service but toilets were out of order and had to que over at Cafe Mickeys to use theirs.We received a voucher for King Ludwigs (20% off),so went their on the second night.we have eaten here before and it is still excellent better than the other restaurants in the disney village.We didn't realise that children ate free before 7pm so this meal was very cheap(we couldn't use the voucher as well so went back on our last night and used)Would definately go back at Christmas atmosphere magic, shows good but would go on week days avoid weekends.Recommend traveling by eurostar excellent!Disneyland Paris is the place to be at Christmas have been to Florida Disney World and it's not as Christmassey apart from the Christmas parade being longer.

This my partner and I stayed in the New York Hotel for the first time and were very impressed; amazing view over the lake, Newport Bay hotel, ice skating rink and Panoramagique balloon. We were greeted with the usual great hospitality, and also received a surprise room upgrade.As usual we had a near perfect Disney holiday. All cast members in the hotel and both parks were extremely friendly. I'm glad the rudeness I see from some miserable, ignorant guests hasn't rubbed off on them.We managed to go on all rides as many times as we liked. The longest wait time was around 20 minutes, but we were also given 3 VIP fastpasses each and so spoilt for choice : )Although physically very similar, I'm always fascinated by the cultural differences within all the different parks, and it's not surprising to see how French culture permeates in this park. Everything has a distinctive French slant on it, from the way you are served in the restaurants, to the organisation of crowds and queues. Having also been to the US parks and the Tokyo parks this year, I love DLP for it's own unique cultural take on the Disney franchise. My only criticism here would be the occasionally negligable attitude towards crowd control and queing   however this is just about beyond the control of the cast members themselves. We witnessed people climbing over railings and trampling flower beds which I find EXTREMELY out of order (ONLY in DLP), skipping pre shows by forcing the automatic doors open (ONLY in DLP) and people generally queue jumping and going to places they shouldn't be (ONLY in DLP) One particular example is when a french couple climbed over a railing and walked on to the out of bounds beach area in adventureland, with the ship wreck. Do these people even realise they shouldn't be there!? They left footprints through the display and this is a great shame. They MUST put up more signs and regulate this boisterous behaviour before it's too late. Rant over : )The only other negative is the maintenance that needs to be done around the resort, but then again this is only thanks to the previous mentioned yobbos that don't know how to respect the place.Overall, a fantastic Disney break. DLP probably ranks last out of all my favourite disney resorts, but still well worth every penny. : )

I have visited Disney World Florida many times over the past 14 years and enjoyed myself each time. Therefore I was looking forward to taking my Grandchildren of 4 and 8 to Disneyland Paris to enjoy the same delights. Boy was I mistaken. All the staff in each park(with the expection of a young lady called Sarah on the Backlot Tour) need a personality transplant, at times they were possitively arrogant with little or no linguistic knowledge. If you do not speak French, Spanish or German some of the tours can be boring, animations like honey I shrunk the audience become a challenge. I wear glasses so I had those on, a pair of three D glasses and earphones to translate the commentary into english   NOT comfortable.The atmoshere is frosty, there is no light heartedness as I love when in Florida, and it is VERY EXPENSIVE.We stayed in the Santa Fe which was a good hotel, the Charectors walked around and greated people then went for photo opportunities. the food was ok. the bar staff pleasant. the rooms clean and adequte but slightly small.We stayed to see the princess' show at 6 oclock and I had to stand in front of the buggy to stop people knocking my 4 year old grand daughter in doing so I was called names in languages I did not understand but could guess the inference; I was even hit in the back of the knees on one occassion by a man pushing his way through at any cost and I am not a small woman but he got the better of me. I dread to think what the park is like in the summer when the weather will bring more people out. The term head down and elbows out should be the motto of this park.Not a good experience, however my grandchildren loved it so in the end it was worth the battering from the ignorant few. We only had one day which is not enough I will go again but when all the adults are in work becuase the children were much better behaved.

I just returned from a 4 day vacation at Disneyland Paris. Like other reviews I am surprised to see some of the negative reviews. I thought the park was very clean and well run. This is my second time to Disneyland Paris. The weather was a bit cold but I didn't mind because it kept the lines short. The castle looked nice with all of the lights on it. Disney Studios is small but it looks like they are adding Tower of Terror, which will be a nice addition. Also the Stunt show was great. Downtown Disney looked a little old looking but I think they were working on fixing it up while I was there.My only complaint is the price and quality of food.
