I've been to Disneyworld in Florida many times and never complained once about the food or the price. You are going to expect to pay a little more for eating in the park. But the cost of food in DLP is crazy. 10 euro (12 USD) for a hamburger, fries and drink. The food wasn't very good quality either. Also many restaurants were closed so the selection was limited. I ate at Rainforest Cafe, Planet Hollywood, and Billy Bobs for dinner. Both Rainforest Cafe and Planet Hollywood were disappointments. Over 30 euro a person and poor quality. Billy Bobs was the best meal we had in Disney. It was 25 euro for all you can barbeque. The quality was pretty good, although my standards of good food dropped over the course of 4 days. Overall I had a good time. The staff was friendly and helpful. Main Street was lit up for Christmas time. The end of November was not a bad time to go because of the short lines and Christmas decorations. I will be back in June!

We have been to Disney a few times and have stayed at the Hotel New York, Newport Bay and Davy Crockett. All times I have booked with Barbara at Phone and fly as she offers a good service and great low prices.I would recommend the New York if you could afford it particularly in winter as it is only a few minutes walk to the park.The room had 2 double beds and private bathroom which was very clean. To be honest we spent most of our time in the park as we had unlimited tickets.Local shops are a bit pricey as you are a captive audience but we were expecting that.If you go in winter take plenty of warm clothing as it was a bit of a shock for us the first time when the temperature was about 10 degrees lower that here in the uk.Other than that we had a great time and would recommend it to famiilies with young children up to about 10yrs.

I found several reviews appear to avoid the nitty gritty side of DLP:In some ways, I could justifiably call Disney land the persistence of the rat race on holiday, but then again that's often the way with Theme parks. One thing it was not   a relaxing family outing. I'd challenge anyone who suggests otherwise. If you enjoy organising your time, objectives, goals, memory within minutes of precision then disneyland is for you and perhaps your family. A touch of assertiveness and agression helps, just try not to be agressive to other people. I watched one parent hound a disney character and chase him until the guy gave in, but there was no anger. The French might be known to be arrogant but the only road rage I experienced was from a fellow Brit who simply could not give up his cutting you up habit whilst on holiday. You just need to speak to them with fair respect and do not expect them to automatically respond to your demands in English. After all I don't know many British people who would take well to Foreigners making continual demands in their native language. Just be fair. I lost my ticket for the photo of daughter and myself with Pooh; the woman in front was aggressively insisting that the photos shown were not of her daughter and despite the saleslady being polite and going through all the photos for over 15 minutes, the woman just walked off. How obnoxious. I asked politely and was treated very well and got my overpriced photo. Whatever happened to at least a little politeness and decorum?If you've been to Disneyland Paris before, you'll already know the rules, how to get around and what toexpect. If it's your first time, you are most likely to write off your first day and your children just may burst into tears unless you've brought them up to deal with theme parks and to be pushy and assertive from the outset. Having a pregnant wife and toddler in tow did not work for me, by the time we got anywhere the queues were unfeasibly unfeasible. Even walking up the Robinson Crusoe tree was a continual stream rather like london underground   seriously! you could not go back part way down, or pretend to be on a deserted island.If having a relaxing afternoon to sip tea, take in the view of a pleasant park and give the children free roam to play all all sorts of various paraphenalia, then visit the large gardens east or west ofParis; on a sunny day these are wonderful places to get away from the madness of modern day life, although you'll have to engage is some of that wonderful Parisien city driving and fight to find a parking space on popular days and weekends.This summer we found a place called 'Parc De Loisirs' in Normandie. It only cost us E30 for the whole family all day and it was a wonderfully semi relaxed warm summer's day family outing, hardly any queues and not overcrowded, included a brilliant water play area as well as fun for older children over many acres. It's not for teenagers but a complete contrast to Disneyland Paris which I would summarise as stressful mayhem. You can enjoy it but you must be willing to join in a 'fight for your right to party'; sit down and you'll miss your slot, just like the Stock Exchange.There's no doubt, its true that you can complete a fuller tour of Disneyland in one day, or two depending on energy levels and strict military precision.Take advantage over those who are making their first visit decide to arrive late, think that Disneyland is a place for a pleasant fun family outing, or simply are trying to get to grips with the layoutof the park and the various rides and activitesHence, if you have children of different ages and are more than one parent, family day it is not. Success lies in separation, unless you're all bursting with energy.Fastpass: concept is good and mathematically fair but as human nature appears to seek to milk every opportunity, rather like aggressive overtaking or undertaking at a roundabout, or queue jumping, manyolder kids can be seen hogging the fastpass machine a taking out anything up to 10 tickets at a time, on the same entrance ticket. This ought to be policed.Getting to see Pooh bear. The problem with Pooh is that most parents want their younger children to have a magical cuddle, or young children want to visit, or the odd female adult wishes to fulfilla dream of giving stinky Pooh a big hug. So Pooh is popular. The characters are only available between 10am until 12:30. If you are late in the queue, expect to wait over an hour while your littletoddler starts to get fed up after patently waiting for 45 minutes. And quite right they are too. So to avoid a long wait, go see pooh immediately you get in the park; after all your younger childwill not need fastpass tickets because they cannot go on those rides anyway   get into the queue as soon as you get into the park.As for children that are old enough to go on the main rides... head immediately out to get fast pass tickets for all the main rides (5). Then, before the queues develop, get on the rides that do not need fast pass tickets. Beware the temptation to go on a ride that just says 5 minutes waiting time, for once you have completed the ride, the fast passes are already set for the afternoon... Then if you want to have a tea with the disney characters, book it now by going all the way back to the entrance info desk, that is to get there before everyone else does. Try to book a time that slots in between or after your fastpass tickets.(The Peter Pan ride appeared to be for much younger children, for older kids and adults it's well... short. Lots of LED lights poking out of a miniature London skyline.)Now purchase an autograph book and pen from one of the kiosks.Beware, if you want to see the Lion King show   you must queue well before the time alloted to the distribution of tickets. For us, the time was 11 am, so expect to be at the distrbution point at thevery latest at 10:30 am   earlier, the better. Oh yes, you will queue until the tickets are distributed and then the queue will evaporate very quickly. But at least you'll have the tickets and you'll see allthose people who arrived at 11 am getting upset, even their children crying, or arguing with a member of staff.... watch out. Your only alternative is to buy a snack at the Videopolis and make your way to the sit down area inside where you can still see the show   as long as a seat or space is available, but it's not ideal. And by the way, do not pick your nose before the show starts as a camera zooms in on the crowd and displays the image on the two screens either side of the stage; amusing and embarrassing if you do get caught out (no, not me)!Ditto for the parade of disney characters, you must time your rides to ensure that you are already waiting on the edge of the parage route 30 45 minutes before it starts. Otherwise you will miss out. You could of course time your picnic to coincide and multitask, just like work, so as to not waste precious time sitting on a bench...Hopefully you now have visited several non fastpass rides without too much waiting and seen the lion king show. Meet up with the rest of your family for a packed lunch. Of course Disney states that you must leave the park to have a picnic, but at their exorbitant prices, its a complete rip off. And believe me, the food from Auchan is much better, that is if you are into french cheeses, brioche, authentic French patisserie and chocolate milk drinks   (do the same under the Eiffel Tower with a bottle of red wine).Try and catch some disney characters but note that they will wonder off after a few minutes either to relocate or take a toilet break.Spend the rest of the day going through all the 'walk through' adventures like the skull island, crusoe's tree or captain Nemo's.We received advice that rides would be easy to get on in the last half hour (19:30). Not true. However, cue up that one last time for about 45 minutes for your last ride, painful waste of time perhaps, but you'll get one last ride. An employee will ensure that the queue is terminated.In all of this madness, I never observed any drunken louts, spitting, or queue jumping as I have done in Thorpe park or Chessington.My family had an awful time on our first day. My toddler spent more time crying than having fun, decided to give up on waiting for Pooh and my 9 year old missed out on just about everything but a few rides that were not so popular. There was no magic, and quite frankly it was a total waste of money and time. I laughted at the queue for the haunted house   it was a labyrinth 'baaaah'. Being a sheep isn't for me, so I set this aside in my precision schedule for day two...Second day, I just went in with my 9 year old and put on my 'City Of London' driving attitude. My daughter was utterly tired at the end, but with my precision and timing we did the lot. Well almost, because we ended up wasting time when the Peter Pan ride broke down but still got on the ride in the end.It was partly my fault as I had not realised that the half terms for English and French school children overlapped completely, presumably at quieter times, life could be easier. However, I can only take my children out at school holiday times and I have now been told that DLP is crowded most of the time anyway.What I find amazing is that to take your family to Disneyland Paris on school holidays includes the usual UK price hike. Just before I went, I saw offers for   165 per person per night and that was 3* within the park; but there's no way I would want to stay within the park for more than two nights. Instead I hired a self catering gite (a lodge), 15 minutes from DLP for   250 including all the white goodsand heating costs (heating is a separate charge which is generally not levied in summer). Paris was only E27.50 and 30 minutes away, so we had 7 nights in the region of Paris, including the Eiffel tower, Montmatre, jardins de Luxembourg and Bois de Vincennes. With a few luxiuries, 7 days in Paris cost me under   800 including a relaxing break sitting in front of 'Le Consulat' in Montmatre, with two full days in DLP.Some interesting points:  the same pack of sweets as DLP was E2.90; in Auchan it was E1.13  Three hot chocolate drinks set me back E7.90, for the same price you can purchase a whole tin of luxury hot chocolate drink in Carrefour, which in the UK would be at least 4 times the price...  Pack lunch for the whole family, with treats, sweets and drinks cost me less than E10 each day, only a little more with a bottle of wine or Cremant  You must pay an additional E8 to park your car  My daughter's highlight was the Lion King show. Then Thunder mountain.  My highlight was the maze of tunnels and walkways inside and under Skull mountain, I stayed for ages.To summarise:If I believed in an afterlife, this would not be it.It was certinaly not the magical visit I had anticiapted for my 9 year old daughter, but it was fun once you acceptedthe crowds and the queuingThe potential for DLP was for us certinaly marred by the crowding and the struggle for resources and the price hiking  but still demand outstripped supplySome people can afford to spend   2k  for a week at DLP, but i'd rather take my family to the Belarics or Greece ona relaxing beach holiday. For us, holidays are supposed to be a least a little relaxing, not continual mayhem. Wethought that 2 days at DLP and 3 days milling around Paris was a good deal for under   800.Good luck on your visit if you go.

Disappointed to see so many negative reviews for Disneyland Paris. We have been 10 times,stayed in every hotel and cant get enough. In june we spent a week in the Disneyland hotel and found the staff couldnt do enough for you.As with anything you get what you pay for so the more money you spend the better your quality of hotel,but depending on how much time you'll actually spend in your hotel decides if its worth upgrading to a hotel with more facilities.We splashed out on the castle club floor and found it to be well worth every penny(or Euro). The characters in the park are out at set times,as are the ones doing meet and greet in the hotels(the hotel m g's are done in line order to give your child a chance to get autographs photo's without being pushed by others.You also get the chance to purchase photos of your child against a themed backdrop). 7 or 8 assorted characters come out hourly along main street and although you might have to join a queue for Mickey,most others will be milling about for 20  minutes.The princesses take up their places at the base of the castle roughly every hour. Although rides are shut at certain times,there is still plenty to amuse and entertain. Although I only speak a little French Ive not had a problem with the language barrier. The best value for meals is probably to be had at the Lucky Nugget,eat as much as you can buffet with character interaction.

We were in Paris the first week in November. Weather was great. We asked several people the best way to get to the park, and they all suggested the underground. It took only 40 minutes from the center of Paris. The train was clean and safe. You literally get off the train at the last stop take an escalator up and arrive at the main gate. It's that easy! There are three major sections: The Disneyland Park aka  The Magic Kingdom,  a second park,  The Walt Disney Studios  (smaller, yet similar to both the Disney MGM studios in Florida; and Disney's California Adventure), and  Downtown Disney.  We must have picked the perfect day (November 9), because the park was virtually empty and there were practically no queues. The DLP is smaller than Disneyland USA or The Magic Kingdom in Walt Disney World, but it is absolutely charming nonetheless. Fantasyland rides like Snow White, Pinocchio or Peter Pan are in French, but are exactly like their US Counterparts otherwise. Tomorrowland has  Space Mountain   Mission 2  Much faster and scary (yes, it loops!) than the one in the US. The parades and shows were charming. For those who complained about the food, we were baffled, because we ate lunch in the Plaza Gardens Restaurant, which was buffet style and delicious. The staff couldn't have been kinder or more helpful.The Walt Disney Studios Park still needs a little extra before it can compare to The California Adventure or to the MGM Studios, but it was still great fun riding the Aerosmith Rock N' Roller Coaster (multiple times, I told you there was no queue), and watching the touching Art Of Disney Animation.Downtown Disney is great for shopping and restaruants, but we had one day and preferred to stay in the parks. We recommend it as a great day trip to break up Paris sightseeing. If the queues are short, you can do it all in a day, if longer, two days tops, the parks aren't that big. But we highly recommend doing this, particularly if you love Disney.Also, there were more characters throughout the parks than you can ever find in the USA. Some have organized queues (Chicken Little, Minnie Mouse, Daisey Duck, The Incredibles, Winnie The Pooh), and others wandered the parks (Pluto, Mickey Mouse, Lilo & Stitch, Chip & Dale, Baloo Bear and more). The children all appeared to be very happy and so were we. Great fun for kids and grown up kids of all ages.

Just had a 5 day break at Disneyland Resort Paris. I have real mixed feelings about this place.Disney are so obviously the masters at doing this kind of thing   and at taking money out of your wallet. My main issues are I suppose with the European culture, and the problems my young son had with trying to get signatures from the characters. If you are not prepared to push, you don't get anywhere. even when we paid for a character breakfast he struggled   perhaps because we are English!! The atmosphere in California was much better from this perspective.Apart from that a good time was had, Halloween was in full swing, but we had clearly lost parts of the park in preparation for the Christmas season. There is also a lot of construction work which due to closures of walkways almost lead to people being crushed on a number of occassions at the bottleneck points.As with everyone else   food is poor and expensive.Overall:Is it a fun place to go   yesDoes it have big queues   yesIs it a break from reality   yesWould I go back   only when my son is old enough not to want to be bothered with the characters

I visited DLP with 3 boys aged 8, 10 and 12. They had a really great time. They particularly enjoyed all of the  big thrills  rides ( 8 year old was too short for Indiana Jones), also the car stunt show, Armageddon and Pirates of the Caribbean. Several of the Studio attractions had prohibitively long queues, even though we arrived well before opening time.It is definitely worth getting a fast pass for Big Thunder Mountain which is a very popular ride with a height restriction of 102cm and a very low age limit  meaning everyone can go on it!! It is no fun queueing in fairly cramped conditions for 50 mins . Peter Pan (which my sons thought was rubbish!) also has very long queues so fast pass essential.Food inside DLP was awful and overpriced. I recommend taking a picnic from your hotel breakfast and eating in the lovely picnic area ( sheltered areas provided), or buying a nice baguette from the RER station.My biggest moan would be that the attractions dont feature recent or even recognisable Disney characters  even I havent seen Alice in Wonderland  my boys had no idea what it was!! Where was Buzz Lightyear, Woody, anyone from Monsters inc, Atlantis, etc etc.? No good having a parade of baddies if children dont know who they are!Quite a few attractions were seasonally closed, but Hallowe'en was in full swing. Entry prices are actually quite reasonable compared to say Blackpool Pleasure Beach, or Alton Towers in the UK. Two or three days is long enough to comprehensively do both studios and park. Disney Village had queues to rival the park!!

This was may familys 4th visit to Disneyland paris and we still love the place the magic is still there both parks are very clean and well kept, ok there were a few rides closed and some of Tomrrowland was boarded off but if that was what it takes to update the park then so be it, we did know this before we went as it was on the DLP website. But this happens in all the Disneyland parks I have never riden Big Thunder Mountian in California as on the 3 visits it has allways been shut the same in Florida.1 thing i wish is that people would stop compairing it to Florida as it is not it is in France Where they speak Speak French and English and yes it is quite expensive but thats Disney for you ! I love this park and all the others plus it is only a 2 1 2 hour drive from Calias just go and enjoy it and let the big kid come out !

Stayed at the fantastic Movenpick Hotel, superb for every facility and great value fo rmoney (  358.00 2adults and 1 child for 3 days)TIP: Buy the 3 day Fantasy Pass  it lasts for a year and is cheaper than the 3 day pass. Plus you get lots of discounts in shops and restaurants. Shame about Disneyland. Some rides were closed, food venues were also closed with no note of apology. The signage was also in short supply, we had to hunt around for ages for toilets   why don't they put up maps in the park with 'you are here signs'.Some of the French employees should also undertake extra Customer Service courses as many were rude and abrupt, even at the EuroStar enquiry desk in the train station.My party, and some others, felt that the introductions to some of the rides should have been in English and not in French as many other nationalilties also understood English but not French. Many children got bored during this introduciton.And for renaming the Seven Dwarf with French names.......Perhaps they should revamp and Americanise   afterall it is what visitors expect.

We had heard that eating inside Eurodisney (or Disney Village) was a bit expensive comparing quality price.Well, we found a good place to eat well and at a good price: There is a restaurant like MacDonald's (but it's not McD.) just beside the Space Mountain 2. The menu is 9   : big hamburger chips coke50cl.You can also eat hot dogs for 4   ; 8    with beverage. But you should eat a lot of them to make your stomach to be aware of food.

Me and my young family think that Disneyland in Paris is fabulous! We   ve visited it twice now (Easter 2004 and August 2005) and we   ve had a trip to Disney World in Florida in between (Christmas New Year) and I couldn   t honestly say which is better. Sure, Disney World is bigger and it   s all in English but it   s so far away! In my experience both have their positives and negatives.People also say that the weather in Florida is better. Well, it certainly doesn   t get cold in Florida but it can get unbearably hot which can make the Disney experience miserable. I   d much rather have mild warm weather (like you get in Paris in the summer) than soaring temperatures when you   re trying to navigate round a busy theme park. The heat saps everyone   s energy and makes everyone irritable.People also say that Disneyland Paris is expensive but I   d say that   s true about Disney in whichever country you go to. Whether you   re talking about the cost of accommodation, food, snacks or gifts, Disney isn   t cheap but then the experience is second to none and nobody does a theme park like Disney!One thing really going for Orlando is that there is so much to do there (maybe too much?!) and each one of the 4 Disney Parks is fabulous. However, when it comes to Paris there is a major imbalance between the Disneyland Park and the Disney Studios. We struggle to find things to do at the Studios in Paris and if it wasn   t for the Stunt Car Show then it wouldn   t really be worth the visit. This is a massive disappointment because the Disney MGM Studios in Florida is fantastic and needs two days set aside to see everything.When you compare the Magic Kingdom in Florida against Disneyland in Paris then the obvious differences are the size and the language. But then the use of space in Disneyland is phenomenal with so much packed in and they also do try and cater for all languages (English, German, Spanish and French). You do have to remember that you are in Europe. We found that most of the signs were in French with English underneath; most of the staff speak pretty good English (much better than my French!) and that they make a good effort during the shows too. When we went to see the Legend of The Lion King it was entirely in English with French and German shows scheduled for other times during the day. The Winnie The Pooh show was in a mix of French & English and for Honey, I Shrunk The Audience you get a pair of headphones to put on and you can choose your language.Ok, enough of the comparisons because it   s fair to say that its    swings and roundabouts    when you try to compare the two side by side.Each time we   ve been to Disneyland in Paris we   ve stayed there for 4 nights and stayed at the fabulous Disneyland Hotel which sits pride of place right over the entrance to the Disneyland Park which means that you can be in Fantasyland one minute and back in your room 5 minutes later. I   ve written a separate review for the Disneyland Hotel in the appropriate section but I will stress that staying here has made our visits so much more enjoyable.The first thing that strikes you about any Disney Park is how clean it is. Then you might notice the fabulous attention to detail. There really is so much to gaze and marvel at and the flowerbeds, trees and grass are always pristine. Disney really does go out of its way to make the surroundings pleasant and safe.One word of advice (and this applies to everything Disney whether it   s meal times, retiring to bed or getting into the Parks)    THE EARLIER THE BETTER! The best time to be in the Disneyland Park is between opening time (usually 9:00am) and 11:00am, during this time you more or less have the park to yourself and can walk up to any ride and get on pretty much straight away. After 11:00am it does start to get busy. When it gets to noon you should be thinking about lunch because by 12:30 1:00pm everywhere will be packed.We managed to spend the equivalent of 2 full days in the Disneyland Park and we enjoyed everything that we did whether it was Star Tours, Big Thunder Mountain, Pirates of The Caribbean, Honey I Shrunk The Audience, Peter Pans Flight, It   s A Small World, Casey Jr     Dumbo   s Circus Train, Mad Hatters Tea Cups, Carousel, Adventure Island, Dumbo The Flying Elephant, Autopia (speedway), Alice   s Curios Labyrinth and the Pirates Beach.Yes you have to queue sometimes, annoying as it is, but if you do get in early then you can get so much more done before the hoards arrive. I think that every queue that we did encounter stayed moving and we never really became frustrated or fed up.Both of the parades were wonderful but then I   ve yet to see a duff Disney Parade! This Fantalusion Parade which was on at 10:30pm was especially good. Each float is wonderfully lit and this is enhanced by all the lights in the park being switched off as the parade starts. This parade was then followed by the Wishes Firework Display which was nothing short of spectacular and really does fill the sky.Our two kids are aged 7 and 2 and there is much to do here no matter what age you are. There is certainly as much for the little kids as there is for the big kids. Our 2 year old daughter had a whale of a time and still talks animatedly about what she did and saw at    The Disneyland   . We didn   t take our own buggy this time and instead we hired one which is easy to do and costs    6.50 a day. When you take it back you can ask for a receipt so that if you also visit the Studios on the same day (or vice versa) then you can get a stroller without having to pay twice. The buggies also have a useful foot plate on the back for slightly bigger kids to stand on.As I said earlier the Studios Park feels a bit empty when compared to the Disneyland Park. However, the redeeming features are the Stunt Car Show which is awesome (even if there is a bit too much talking in between the stunts), Aladdin   s Flying Carpets and the Studio Tram Tour (complete with Disaster Canyon). I think there   ll be more for us to do here when our kids are a bit older.All in all I cannot fault a trip to Disneyland in Paris especially if you stay at a Disney Hotel (I would definitely recommend the Disneyland Hotel!). There   s always something to do and marvel at, it   s clean and it   s safe. You will find yourself being swept away with it all because it   s truly magical, totally unique, utterly charming and your kids will love you for it!

This was our first trip to a Disney park and as a sceptic I thought there wouldn't be much for adults to do. However, after this trip I can thoroughly reccommend a trip there for the whole family. We stayed close by in the Pierre   Vacances ( see separate review) appartments. Having done a bit of research in a specific DLP book we had some good tips for our visit. However, we didn't do too well in getting there early, about 1015 each day, so the first day was spent waiting 20 30 minutes to buy tickets. Spookily enough we bought our next tickets in the hotel ( or RER station disney store tourist office) so we didn't have to queue. One bad point is that the ticket staff try to sell you the two park ticket, which is advertised a lot more prominentaly, with the cheaper ticket appearing in very small print by the ticket booths. Having asked for the 1 park ticket, the price was a lot more than I was expecting so I challenged this in french, at which point I was given the sales patter in english about the great Studio parks. Again after some more sales chat I got the tickets I wanted, but how many people realise , or are to timid to challenge this attitude?Having entered the park we took the train around it to discovery land. The guide recommended using the fast pass system which we did throughout, the most annoying thing being many of these ticket machines were unserviceable leaving maybe 1 in 3 or 4 working and eventually a cast member would hand out the tickets manually. I was amazed how many people didn't use these tickets and muttered when your short queue joined the normal long queues for rides! I felt sorry for the cast members at the fast pass entrances as some people would show up early for their pass times and then argue sometimes aggressively with the cast trying to get in early, luckily they stood their ground and told them to wait! Using the passes for the rides at the end of Day1 we had pretty much done all the big rides in the park. We'd missed the tickets for the first Lion king performance, but at that time it rained heavily so we stood in the theatre to keep dry. Again the cast were good as there were a few spare seats left and they allowed children to sit down whilst we stood behind the barrier.The rides I enjoyed with my eldest son 7 years were space mountain (managed to sneak him on twice   technically a bit too short), Thunder mountain, Pirates of the caribbean, haunted house and indianna jones ( the books say you loop backwards not so). The kids enjoyed the rockets in discovery ride, star wars and the car driving. One of the frontier land rides ie the boats various was not working in August at all.The shows were good although the boys didn't really enjoy tarzan, but the Honey I shrank the audience made a lot of people jump and squirm. On the second day we saw all the evening parades fireworks which were very impressive  we saw the fireworks from our hotel every night which at a distance are under whelming.I think 2 days is enough for DLP, we had been on every ride, seen all the shows and contary to the book's advice had managed to bring in a packed lunch   drinks each day. The drinks ice creams are comparable to UK theme park london prices. A lot of forumites complained of cigarette smoke, I don't like smoke, but found only a tiny amount of people smoked in queues etc so it was no great bother. We visited on a monday and wednesday in the august school holidays and it wasn't too bad for queues especially as the rides stay open late.So go visit and enjoy!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Just got back from Disneyland Paris, and we had a really great time.We stayed outside the park at Pierre et Vacances and had a two day pass to enjoy the park and then spent some time in Paris itself.I noticed that I had saved about   1600 by booking my own flights (Flybe) accomodation via Expedia and by buying my tickets direct from Disney on the internet. I don't know how happy I'd be to spend so much on a Disneyland hotel,especially as eating in the park was expensive.The best rides were Big Thunder Mountain, Rock and Roll Rollercoaster and Pirates of the Carribean.Don't miss Honey I shrunk the audience and the Stunt show spectacular, both were really amazing experiences!We ate at the Blue Lagoon one evening but the food was disappointing for the cost. Save your money and eat in Paris in the Latin Quarter one evening Much better.We used a really good guide called  A Brits guide to Disneyland Resort Paris  which was really good.Other tips I'd give are Wear comfortable shoes, and don't go on Saturday or Sunday because Parisiens do fill the place up at weekends.Go and have fun, and don't forget the romantic city itself!

Disneyland Paris is a great holiday for the whole family! But there is one thing to remember   it is in FRANCE, not the US. By this I mean that you can not go there thinking that you will have the same experience in France as you would in the US. You won't. And you will probably end up as disappointed as some of the other reviewers seemed to be.Here are the differences: 1) People smoke there. People still smoke in France (and then some), so there will be people smoking at Disney.2) The characters are often (but not always) not as warm and cuddly. French people are not as warm and cuddly...3) Customer service is not as good. No country in Europe has customer service as good as in the US. I am an American living in Europe, this is a fact that I have come to accept.The only truly bad aspect to Disney Paris is the food. It is extremely expensive, which is also the case in the US, but it is AWFUL. Really bad.All's said, Disney Paris is STILL a great place to take the family, just don't forget that it is not Disney Orlando or Cali. It's French with all the 'charm' that goes with their culture.

Not what I had expected having visited the 2 American theme parks. Found Disney Village to be smelly (greasy cooking smells) dirty and very expensive.Walt Disney Studios and the Park were passable. There were very few members of staff visible   no characters unless you went to allocated place and queued to see them. Very few sign posts  and map not that reliable.Several of the restuarants were closed as were drink stalls. Goods in shop were expensive   a small bottle of water 2 euros (so take it in with you.)Some of the rides were closed   no information as to when they were to be reopened. The only thing they got right was the free shuttle bus service to and from hotels.If you need to go 1 day will suffice and 2 at the most.

We have just returned from 2 wonderful days at DLP. Admittedly one of our party was in a wheelchair so this meant that we did not have to queue for some of the attractions but the park was not as busy as we had expected so the queues were not too bad. We arrived at the park at 9am and at this time there were very few people there so we were able to get straight on the rides we wanted to do without waiting at all!Aerosmith's Rock and Roller Coaster and Space Mountain are both fantastic and some of our party could have happily spent the entire 2 days just riding them!! Space Mountain has been improved with Mission 2.The cast members varied in how helpful they were, we had to speak to them on most rides because of the wheelchair, and while some of them were lovely, others were real 'jobsworths'. The rule seems to be that a person in a wheelchair can take up to 3 members of their party with them even though there were 9 of us so we had to split up and this usually meant sending a half empty carriage through the attraction. Some of them would let an extra child fill up the empty space and some wouldn't.When we hired the wheelchair we were not told that we needed a blue card to go with it so having got to the rides, we then had to shlep all the way back to City Hall to get one. Here we were told that the card would be fine for visiting the other park the following day, but when we tried to use it in the Disney Studios we were told that no, we needed a green card!We ate at Cafe Mickey with the characters and I don't think I have ever laughed so much! I thought they would just sign autographs and pose for pictures but watch out for Balloo and co   nothing so sedate!! They were fantastic and rounded off our visit with a big smile.If you have a disabled person with you, tell them as you pay for the car park as you need the code to get in and yes, they are sending you into the car park of the hotel that backs onto the entrance, we drove round thinking no, they can't mean in there!

Okay, it isn't Disneyworld. My husband and I were on our honeymoon in paris for 10 days. We had an extra day and decieded to go to Disney. It was a blast, it felt like a vacation from our vacation. Don't get me wrong we loved paris, but this was fun. Granted there were about 8 main rides, it was small and manageble. We went in on a Sunday in October and the crowds were moderate 40 minute waits for most major rides. BEWARE...we had the metro tickets for the week in paris, however you can't travel to the zone that disney is in without a different ticket. On a sunday the metro tix booths are closed the only way you can purchase tickets is from a machine that is all in french. So we took our chances and rode the train planning on paying the person on the other end of the line(i think it was an extra 5 euro a person) However, there was a police waiting at the exit of the metro and without a valid ticket we got ticketed 50 euro!! This was the tourist price more if you are a paris citizen. A total trap they didn't care that we couldn't purchase tickets, but they ran our credit card and charged us.

People asked if my fiance and I were going to DLP with children   'no' we said, looking astonished, 'why would we?' We had a fabulous time   even cynical ol' us were excited by having our photo taken with Minnie Mouse...! Disney sort of sweeps you up in its exuberance.The Park is amazing   what impressed us most was the incredible use of space. You can actually walk from one end of the Park to the other in about 10 minutes (although not in a straight line!) but they have crammed so many rideas and attractions into the space it feels a lot bigger. There is judicious use of flower beds and trees, and it feels a lot less 'plasticky' than I expected. The gardeners are to be congratulated   the flowers were all blooming and the topiary was amazing. Apparently 5million flowers are planted every year!RidesWell, we found as two 29 year olds that the park is clearly divided into Children and Adult rides. The rollercoasters mostly fall into the latter category, with Space Mountain, Indiana Jones and Thunder Mountain being the best (although we both felt our heads were knocked around a lot on Space Mountain and I wondered briefly about whiplash   definitely not one to go on if you have EVER had a neck injury! Indiana Jones gives the same buzz without the headache, although to our disappointment it does not go backwards as claimed in our guidebook!) The kiddie rides are imaginative but less appealing for adults, although we particularly enojyed Pirates of the Caribbean, Le Pays de Contes de Fees (a cruise around miniature storybook scenes), Casey Junior (all right, it's a little train for kids but we liked it!) and actually Peter Pan's Flight was rather sweet, although too jerky to give you the impression that you really are flying!The other rides are enjoyable but you have to remember the park is aimed at kids and not expect too much in the way of trickery thrills. It's a Small World is puke inducing in its pink frillyness but certainly a masterpiece of engineering! Star Tours feels strangely dated. Honey I shrunk the Audience is fun. We also went on the train that goes all the way round the park   if you're hoping to be able to see the whole park you'll be disappointed; they've even concealed the park from the train! Very clever but slightly frustrating.We were well aware that we were going to the Parks in peak season and so were prepared for long queues. However, following advice on tripadvisor we got to the park every morning at 9am when it opened   and it was brilliant. For about 2 hours you can literally walk onto the rides   even in August   and it's really very bearable. After that it gets very very busy (but we tended to go back to the hotel in the afternoon and then return in the evening) and other people and their children become very irritating! Fastpass is a fantastic invention and you really should make use of it if you want to do the big rides. Most of the rollowercoasters have at least two 'trains' going round so the queues do move, but we did pass signs for 70 or 80 minutes wait during the lunchtime period. Strangely, Peter Pan seemed to be the one with the longest queues!ParadesWe saw all three on one day. 'The Wonderful World of Disney' was at 7pm and included some huge floats of the Disney characters. Very impressive and a lot of fun but we did have to stand several rows back as we weren't prepared to sit on the kerb for an hour beforehand to reserve a place! Our favourite was definitely the Fantillusion Parade at 10.30pm   really beautiful use of lights synchronised with music. The Wishes display at 11.15pm was amazing for the use of projection onto the castle and the use of lasers   very clever. The fireworks were okay but nothing particularly special.ShowsWe only saw one   the Lion King show. Great fun and a potted version of the story with all the main songs. Strange mix of Disney type furry costumes and the more sophisticated costume design of the West End Broadway show. Performers were obviously giving it their all though, and the singing was excellent.If you want to see a show, beware. You have to queue at certain times of the day at the Videopolis in Discoveryland, and the queues get VERY long in a short space of time (they close the Discoveryland station at this time). The tickets go quickly and people are often turned away disappointed. After missing the evening 'slot' for tickets (the sign at Main Street said 'sold out' even before they were supposed to have given the tickets out   apparently they count people in the queue!) the next day my fiance queued for an hour for tickets. However, there are ways round it. There is a fast food restaurant in Videopolis, and if you order your meal cannily you can catch the show from the top part of the auditorium. Wish we'd thought of that!Studio ParksWe really enjoyed the buzz at this park. Obviously, it's smaller and less famous, but the Rock n Roller Coaster with music by Aerosmith was so good we went on it twice in a row (two rides on that by 9.15am   see, it pays to get there early!) We also enjoyed Armageddon, which is suitably silly and requires audience participation (those staff work HARD, I tell you!) and the Studio Tram Tour, although we didn't feel that it was worth the hour long queue. The bit in Catastrophe Canyon was good though   fire and water rushing towards you! We also heartily recommend the Moteur Action show   the audience stand holds thousands of people and it's a great show, full of stunt driving and effects. What really makes it is the use of cameras during the show, projecting the shots onto a big screen. Plus, they also show you how the stunts are done, which we found fascinating. We also enjoyed the Animagique show, which involves Donald Duck (speaking in English) and Mickey Mouse (speaking in French) and an adventure into various Disney films all in UV light   very attractive.OverallLots of fun   we had a three day hopper and it's definitely value for money. The variety of attractions is huge and there's always something to look at. Most of the rides give you information in three languages, and all the staff have a smattering of three languages. We think we saw the best of the Parks by structuring our day as we did   going very early and then taking the afternoon off is definitely recommended.One ride nobody tells you about is actually not in the Parks at all. The Panoramagique balloon is at the other end of Disney Village (we don't really recommend Planet Hollywood   had better burgers from our local butcher...but they do good cocktails!) and costs 12 euros for a 10 minute or so ride. The balloon is tethered permanently to the ground and rises up above the Park. It's then that you see the real genius of Disney   the layout of the car parks (completely hidden from ground view) and the hotels take up at least three times as much ground area as the Parks themselves. It's also illuminating to see the main park from the air   the roofs look terribly concrete and modern compared with the magic in the detail below! We were really pleased we managed to do this one, although of course it depends entirely on weather conditions and when we arrived in the morning we were told to come back later.What else? The thing that most impressed us about the whole experience was the attention to detail. Everything is done to make people feel as confortable as possible. The arcades that line Main Street are stunning. There is plenty of space, although of course that is used to maximum capacity during busy times. Around every corner there is something new. And you can even have your purchases delivered to your hotel so you don't have to carry them around with you all day. We didn't eat in the Park as we figured it would be very busy, but we didn't think it was that expensive really. The prices in the shops were only what you would pay for the same items in a shop in England. There are some very good quality fridge magnets, pens, keyrings etc for about   2.50 so there is plenty for pocket money purchase. The big seller seems to be the princess dresses   we saw many, many small girls dressed as Belle, or Snow White etc. And the dresses are not cheap so gird your wallet when taking small girls with you! But on the whole we didn't see what the fuss was about. You wouldn't expect to pay less than   15 for an all you can eat restaurant at a Theme Park in England   why should you in Disney? The only reason the trip is expensive is because you have to buy every meal rather than whipping up a bowl of pasta at home. Plus you are paying for the Disney experience   which, let's face it, is expensive to run. The number of staff employed in the Parks is staggering   and that includes gardeners, painters, engineers, firemen...along with the performers themselves.I think it's well worth the money, and in our three days we really felt we had seen everything we wanted and done everything we wanted. Highly recommended. We shall come back when we have children!We stayed at the Moevenpick Dream Castle Hotel   review under appropriate section.

My friend and I took our combined five teenagers here (12years to 15years). We moaned before we got there and then had double the fun that they did ! If you don't need to go on the scary rollercoaster 8 times, you can manage to do everything in the same day. We enjoyed Disneyland on the first day and then the studios on the second, finishing the evening at Disneyland again. The motor stunt show was worth 50 euros itself ! We missed out on one show in Disney Studios because we never read the times properly, but if you are there from 10am you should have no problems. We didn't enjoy the crowds for the parade, but the up side was that we got on the rides which are busy during the day. We found good value food and some of us ate salads ! The two park two day tickets were 50euros each, which we did not see advertised anywhere, and there were minimal queues for admission (or anything). We never queued longer than 15mins and used fastpass once. The children went seperately from us in Disneyland and felt safe, despite having had a few scares in Paris itself. Brilliant !

Just returned from DLP. Compared with 2003 visit, hardly any characters to be seen. Parade seemed much shorter and lacking in 'pizzazz'. General atmosphere seems to have taken a downturn. There seemed to be far fewer staff around in their various capacities   due to European working hours directive or general economies because Disneyland is in financial bother? The rides themselves were as good as ever but in 2003, we left feeling  The Magic , in 2005   not.

Just returned from a disappointing trip to DisneyParis. We have visited 3 times before and always enjoyed ourselves, but this time it was a different story. On entering the car park there was not a single Disney representative to guide people to the parking bays. Finding where the correct place to leave the car was took us a considerable amount of time as there was simply no one about to ask.Once inside the Disneyland park we noticed alot of areas looking shabby and in need of paint and maintenance. A typical example was the Alice in Wonderland maze. There were huge gaps in the maze walls, cracked, worn paintwork, rubbish left all over the floor and thrown in the bushes and loads of stinging nettles growing up the maze bushes. Not ideal when you've got kids running round the place!Alot of the staff we very miserable and unhelpful. We approached 3 staff members to find out why the Indiana Jones ride had come to a halt and we had obvioulsly inconveniently interrupted their conversation. As we walked up the them one of them was carrying out a rude gesture with her breasts, the other two laughing and joking at her, which we found to be very inappropriate   considering the kids were with us and that Disney is meant to be all about good wholesome family entertainment.The impression we got from the studios was that it has been flung together quickly in order to rake in more money. There is very little there and all the attractions are on top of one another. It doesn't have a good pleasant feel to it. It looks cheap and is absolutley no comparison to the Florida one.

My husband and I recently returned from a long weekend in Paris. Since we were ahead of schedule, we thought we would catch some Euro Disney Magic! What we caught was very long lines, Fast Pass booths closed, several attractions closed, too many restaurants cafes and too few attractions. The staff was terrible at loading attraction cars   normally, you line up and they try to fill all the seats, right? 20% of the cars that went by were empty. Also, in six hours, we did not see ONE charachter! It was unbelievable considering that it was so busy. At best, it was lousy. If you are an American, you will most likely hate it. Another poster said the entrance was beautiful, but it went downhill FAST after that. I agree. Also, be careful if you take the RER out to Disney from Paris. Be sure your fare is correct before you arrive as you insert your RER ticket for entry into the Park. If your fare is short, you are locked out and you have to buy a  violators ticket  for 25 Euro. Europa Park in Germany is 10 X better.

With two small kids in tow, my husband and I now see why Disneyland is so popular with parents. They (and the hotels that surround the park), have 'kid friendly' all figured out. We just got back from a week vacation in northern France, beginning with Disneyland Paris and ending with the Loire Valley and were very pleased with our experience at Disneyland Paris. Yes, it's expensive. Yes, you need to do a little advance planning to avoid the lines. But anyone who's been to any of the other parks (we're from So. California) knows this already and can make adjustments as necessary. The park was beautiful (would you really expect less from Disney?), the staff was pleasant and friendly, we avoided lines by buying our tickets in advance and arriving early and the overall experience was heaven for our three year old. Have a plan for hitting the highlight rides, use fastpass, and you'll be fine. One concern we had was that even some of the tame rides (i.e. Snow White) were a little dark and 'scary' for very young children. We had to be careful and scope out the rides first to avoid having the kids cover their eyes for the whole ride.

We got back from Disneyland Paris yesterday and had a fantastic time. We went for the DLP Classic Package that entailed two nights accommodation and three day's passes to the two Disney parks. A very good deal. I went with my wife and one year old.We stayed at the Newport Bay Club and found the staff friendly and helpful and the rooms spacious, neat and clean. Newport is only a 10 minute walk from the two parks but one can take the yellow bus or the Mickey mouse tram from the hotel to the various facilities at DLP. The downside of Newport Bay Club was the fairly chaotic reception area and check in and the completely chaotic breakfasts! TIP: Take your breakfast at 7am or 7:30am at the latest   anytime after that you will be queing for ages. If those times are too early for you then rather grab a breakfast bite in the Disney parks. Also, we found there was no kettle and tea coffee facilities in the room. This would not normally be a problem but it certainly is if you need boiled water for a baby. The main Disneyland park was fantastic. I went to Disneyland Anaheim nearly 10 years ago and I believe the range of activities, facilities and the aesthetic appeal of DLP is easily comparable with the Anaheim park. We spent a full day and a half in the main park and could have stayed for longer. I was worried that there would not be much to do with my one year old there but my worries were unfounded. He had a ball! There certainly is something for kids of all ages (and adults too, of course!)No place can escape without some criticism and DLP is no exception, however the negatives of the place are small and mostly easily avoidable. I would agree with comments on this site regarding queing and smoking in the park. Tolerance of smoking is very different in Europe than in the UK and USA and it is unbelievable how many people smoke at DLP (teenage kids in the park seem to have a cigarette permanently in their hands!) I too found all the smoke to be a major irritation, especially in the queues for rides. Hopefully this is something that DLP changes soon.The queus were not bad at all. Maybe we chose a good time of year (end April) and a good time of the week (arrived Thursday and departed on Saturday). The only ride that had huge queues and an unbelievably long wait was Space Mountain 2. However, your big thrill seeking rides like Space Mountain, Thunder Mountain & Indiana Jones are always going to have longer queues than others. If you want a rollercoaster ride then I suggest you get on them as soon as possible after the park opens at 9am. All other queues we tried did not take long at all   15 minutes at the most we waited. The one ride you have to go on with small kids is  Its a Small World    absolutely charming and no queues too! Our little one enjoyed it so much that we went twice in a row!Another TIP: The daily parade at 4pm is EXCELLENT and you want to pick a good spot on Main Street from around 3:30pm so that you can have an excellent view.After spending the Thursday and Friday at the main park we decided to avoid the mass crowds on a Saturday and opted for the Walt Disney Studios for this day. It was a wise choice as the crowds were far less than the main park and we hardly ever had to queue to get into any of the attractions. Walt Disney Studios is enjoyable but far more suited to older kids (6 ). It does not have anywhere near the range of attractions & activities that the main Disney park has but it is still well worth the visit. I would suggest spending a good half day at the Studios. Highlights at the Studios are the backlot tram tour, the two daily parades, the Aerosmith roller coaster (on a par with Space Mountain) and the thoroughly entertaining Cinemagic show. A word on the staff at DLP: Some people on this forum have been critical of them with comments such as that they have been unfriendly, unhelpful etc. On the whole we found the staff to be extremely friendly, cheerful and accommodating. I did experience one surly character in a shop in the Studios but he was very much the major exception to the rule. I would give the staff 10 10 during our visit. One final word of advice is beware of the strange departure system at the Disneyland train station: they only communicate the platform of your departing train 10 minutes before departure and the Info Centre there are either unable or unwilling to give you this information and just tell you to keep watching the notice boards. This system caused quite a bit of anxiety amongst passengers when we were there. 10 minutes might seem like an adequate amount of time to get to your train but one is never too confident of this if you have a lot of luggage, parcels, strollers, kids etc. to get to the train in less than 10 minutes!!!All in all, it was a great visit and I hope my comments above will assist you in preparing for a visit. We will definately go back to Disneyland Paris before the end of this year!

Just back from 4 days in DLP   it was our 3rd trip in 5 years and probably the worst   simply because of the queues. THere was the offer of kids go free so this is probably why it was so busy as well as being Easter Hols. We queued for almost an hour and a half for the Peter Pan ride, which lasts about 2 mins. All fastpass tickets were gone by 11am for all the fastpass attractions. That was the only thing that put us off, queueing with 2 kids aged 7 and 4 is not easy, especially when they need the toilet etc.. after 1 2 an hour. It was also a pain when one person in front of us queued then suddenly as they got near the ride, about 6 of their friends joined them, I can tell you I had words on more than one occasion. Some of the rides were closed for maintenance (my sons favourite,  Casey Junior )so that was disappointing and also there was lots of easter activities on. We didnt do the easter egg hunt in the maze but by all accounts it wasnt worht the queue. We stayed at the Newport Bay Hotel, having previously stayed at the Santa Fe and Hotel Cheyanne and even though you pay more for this hotel it is worth it. If you are booking it, I would recommend paying   20 extra per person and book the Admiral's floor, its quicker to check in and check out (no queues!!), you can get room service, which we did one morning for breakfast, it cost 10E to have it delivered but worth it, the room has a mini bar, which was actually not expensive. The pool was a bonus as we had one day of rain so headed back early and spent a couple of hours there. It did get busy but lots of shooting water and a jacuzzi to keep us amused. The character dinner at Cafe Mickey in the village is worth a visit, the food is good, (not cheap, but what is there) but lots of characters for the kids to meet and dance with. All in all a good holiday but if we go back it wont be when there is an offer like Kids for Free again, it wasnt worth the hassle.

I was very disappointed with Disneyland Paris. Upon entering the park, the entrance area is very nicely done but after that things go downhill. Much of my disappointmnet is because I was comparing it to Disneyworld, Orlando Florida. In Paris, I thought the attention to detail was missing. Lines for greeting characters were chaotic and there was no control to insure all guests could greet the characters. The  magic  of Disney just seems to be missing.

We have just returned from a 2 night trip to Disneyland Paris via Eurostar. Eurostar direct to DP was on time but shabby and toilets were terrible on outward and return journeys. Do they give the families the worst trains for this trip I wonder? Better facilities on South West trains!Really appreciated the luggage service with Eurostar to Disney hotels. Worth going for as you can go straight to the park when you arrive at 1.30pm.Disneyland Paris was as I expected, from reading the previous reviews. It only rained on 2 of our 3 days, so we were lucky. Beware of puddles everywhere   my only pair of shoes got soaked on the first day. Better take more than one pair of shoes with you.There are too many smokers around the park   even in the open air I could smell smoke everywhere, and it should be banned while queuing   most of the queues are partly inside and it's dreadful to have all that smoke in a closed atmosphere and you can't escape! I will be writing to DP requesting that smoking be banned in queues and ideally throughout the park with designated outside areas marked for smokers.Food expensive. Tea dreadful   got cup of hot milk and water, with a tea bag to put in. Had to throw it away. Suggest you drink coffee instead.But me and my family with 2 children of 7 and 8 really enjoyed our stay. You can only do rides easily for the first and last hours. In between lots of queues, but we can only go at peak times as my husband is a teacher.The parade was excellent. Remembered to sit down near the barrier early this time to get good view.The fact that the park is small is a plus in my view. We still didn't see and do everything in 2.5 days and it is less tiring going from one thing to another. I wouldn't have wanted the park to be any bigger.Stayed at Hotel Cheyenne   excellent   have written a review on the Hotel Cheyenne section of this website.We enjoyed it, but I do wish that smoking was banned in the park. I have never experienced so much smoke in an open air place.

Just back from 4 day trip staying in Sequioa Lodge with 2 five year olds.Had a really fab time and enjoyed the European flavour of Disney! We found the staff lovely and full of enthusiasm.The queues were a bit irksome at first but we were amazed how used we got to them! TIP:think of a few games to play in queues and go armed with little sweetie treats!!Hotel was good and staff once again very keen to help. Swimming pool bit of a disappointment cos very small and overcrowded.Didn't mind though cos we had no time to swim too busy in the parks!!!!TIP: go to breakfast at 7.00 sounds early but its worth it when you see the HUGE queue at 7.45!!!Plus you finish breakfast just in time to be first in the line to meet the Disney character at 8.00!!!!!!All in all had a surprisingly good time! Take good walking shoes,a kagool,lots of snacks and drinks,a chunky pen for characters to be able to hold and your camera. But most of all bring your imagination and a sense of humour!!!You'll need it!P.S Bet you won't be able to get the 'small world' tune out of your head for a few months either!!!!!! ENJOY!!!

We have just returned from a five day holiday at DisneyLand Paris.The Sequoia Lodge hotel was clean & friendly breakfast was good only ten minutes walk to Disney Parks.The parks were excellent, clean, shows excellent, food reasonable, parades excellent.THE DOWN SIDESome of the characters were not very friendly with the children when asking for photos or autographs. The Macdonald restaurant and take away in the holiday village was dirty tables, floor, bins and TOILETS weren't cleaned.

An otherwise forgettable first visit to Disneyland Paris was salvaged by a trip on the fantastic Aerosmith Rock'n Roll Rollercoster tucked away in the Walt Disney Studio Park. The ride is fully enclosed in a hanger, so on arrival you have no idea what to expect. We queued for only 10 minutes (compared to up to 50 minutes for other, inferior  attractions ) and only once inside we were able to see the cars being launched at what appeared to be an incredible speed. After take off I can say that the acceleration was like nothing else I have ever experienced. The ride was utterly terrifying, with loop the loop and worse, all at very fast speed. The initial acceleration from take off will remain in my memory for ever. As for the rest of Dinseyland Paris   ruined by the queues and totally forgettable. Terra Mitica at Benidorm beats it hands down.

Yeah it's expensive, (hotels, food, etc...) guess what so is Disney in the States. Once you come to the realization that you are going to pay quadruple price for everything you should have a great time. The park is very clean and in great condition. The staff is friendly and spoke English very well. You can do the whole park in one day with no problem even with small children. Mass transportation throughout the Disney area is very good. There is a RER train station directly in front of the Disney Village so you can catch a train that links directly to the Paris Metro. Nice four day weekend trip. If you have small kids they will love it.

The Disney experience is undoubtedly great, my 2 girls were in heaven the whole of the week just gone we were there. But what put a downer on the experience for me was the outragious prices, 6 euros for a pint of lager, the exchange rate was 1.27 euros to a pound in the santafe hotel, so that is nearly   5 a pint, Coke was over   1 for a can and   2 for a small bottle. What was worse was getting the feeling I was trapped in the disney high price scheme and I was. With no other choice as we did not bring the car we had to eat disney. We were staying at the Santa Fe hotel, for such a high cost I was surprised that there was no coffee machine in the room? Then I discovered why they were selling tea bags at the reception. Rooms were good with nice beds. Food was again      expensive, ignorant french and spanish people everywhere, they seem to have no qualms about pushing to the front of any queues, barging kids out of the way as if they were furniture, without a muttering of  pardon . Overall very tiring, but good, the food although expensive was very good, except the steakhouse in the disney village,  steak  house should read old boot. Annettes & King Ludwigs were the best restaurants very nice food.A lot of rides were closed, but there were plenty of carnivals and the Disney Studios was excellent.

We have just returned from our first trip to EuroDisney with our two boys (7 & 8). Feb 28th to March 3rd. We stayed at the Cheyenne and had a ball. I was a bit worried going after reading the moaners about  only nescafe  etc. But from the start everything went great, the coach transfers are all on time, bus driver was very pleasant, hotel reception was very well organised. We were checked in and at our room in record time   no messing around. Dropped our bags and headed straight for the parks. Its totally geared for children which was brilliant as thats the reason we went to give them the trip of a lifetime and memories for ever. We went to the Rainforest Cafe for dinner the first night and the staff couldn't have been more helpful. Its great to be able to eat out with children and not have to be constantly telling them to sit down and be quiet as nobody takes any notice of them   well, maybe the non nescafe drinkers! We fell into bed that night and up early the next day. The breakfast was great the kids totally enjoyed being able to top up their milk and orange juice for themselves. But the waste of food is incredible   it might be an idea if the hotels made up pre packed lunches for guests as people couldnt get enough on to their trays and most of it was left on the tables. Got the parks done in about a day and a half. Ate at the Blue Lagoon on the second night which was nicer again as the Pirates ride comes through the restaurant. Went to the Silver Spur on the last evening and the waiter came straight to our table with colouring sheets and pencils for the boys which kept them entertained while we waited for our food. Good time of the year to go as the longest queues were about 15 minutes on average. The snow in the last day and half made it for my boys as we would never get that volume of snow at home   made snowmen etc., I wouldnt go in the summer as it wouldnt be fair on children with the queueing. Please parents bring warm clothes for the children invest in waterproof boots shoes etc., as some kids going around miserable with no gloves, hats etc., and belly tops aagh! with blue midriffs. I will definately go back.

Our family and my sister's family have just returned from a very cold ( 5c) holiday ay Disneyland. Most of the children loved it. All the adults did not. On the negative side the food was not good and, worst of all, the coffee seemed to be Nescafe most of the time. It seems Nescafe did a deal with Disney and its the only coffee you can get there!The queues were long and in some cases Fastpass was closed so if you are planning to pay the extra for Castle Club and VIP passes check out the reality of Fastpass because even if it is open you still queue. Comparisons would be Fastpass 15 20mins versus 45 mins in the normal queue.We stayed in the Disneyland Hotel which is right at the gates and very convenient. It is so close to the railway station that you may as well take your own bags to the hotel rather than rely on the, admittedly excellent, Disney service to transport your bags from station to your room. The rooms were good, except the bathrooms were a little cold for us, but we do like tropical temperaures even in the depths of a French winter.We stayed for 4 days which is the absolute maximum.In the winter to get warm the place to go is the Pirates of the Caribbean. It is underground and the queues are minimal most of the time.We are unlikely to go back.Our daughter (aged 9) who has been many times to Blackpool Pleasure Beach, because we have family near by, said she preferred BPB!The whole parc is still losing money, I believe, and it does feel a bit like it.Most staff were pleasant but some offhand. It definately lacks that American service ethic that you get in Florida

i've just come back from my first trip to euro disney and went with my wife and two children aged 6 and 5.i thought i would share some of my experiences with you and give some tips to people whom are going or thinking of going to eurodisney. Firstly if you're travelling by air into charles de gaulle airport then getting to disney is going to be one of your first concerns.i would highly recommend silvershuttle it is a one man private hire service who will take you to eurodisney from the airport for 12 euros for adults and 8 euros for children. he meets you at the airport outside the terminal with a sign with your name on.we also arranged for him to pick us up from the disney hotel on the day of our departure.his name is michael and i can't speak highly enough of him.cheaper than the shuttle and the taxi. we stayed at the newport bay hotel which was ok.staff were professional, helpful.however, and i'm sure the other disney hotels will be the same,the hotel was crowded all the time. i believe that there are over 600 rooms so don't expect a leisurely stroll without bumping into loads of other tourists. breakfast was typical continental fare with staggered sitting times which you are asked what time you want when you arrive.we arrived at the hotel at 1130 and were not allowed to check into our room until after 3pm.there is a facility where you can leave your luggage for free.one minor gripe. there are no coffee tea making facilities ie cups and coffee tea bags and kettle in the room.my wife asked at reception and was told that it would cost us 8 euros for the privilege of that.,and that was each time we wanted coffee tea.the newport bay is about ten minutes walk to the parks.it was absolutely freezing when we went which was 15th feb for three days.and it snowed when we were there.it does put you off queuing when it is so cold and i would recommend to anyone thinking of going to eurodisney to go after april,to benefit from warmer weather and lighter nights as it does make a difference. there aren't that many rides in the disneyland parks.i have not been to florida so i'm glad i went to paris first.people i spoke to in the queues, and there are lots of them,said that florida was a hundred times better than paris.the general opinion of everybody was that the people working in disney paris were not that friendly and it was just a job,whereas the staff in florida enjoyed their work.i didn't see a smiling french face the whole time i was there and i'm not exaggerating.lots of the shows etc are in french with a smidging of pidgeon english.this is after a straw poll revealed that over 90per cent of the audience were british.one example was a ride called armageddon based on the film starring bruce willis.we were ushered into a small room where the french host asked where everyone was from.there were no french there,95 per cent british and four germans, and yet the host told us that she would talk in french.it involved audience participation so you can only guess what sort of response she had.they don't tend to cater for the majority of their audience.the rides are good though,thunder mountain was my favourite.my daughter loved the characters. i would also recommend booking a character breakfast before you go as they get booked up very quickly.we ended booking a breakfast at cafe mickey at 17 euros for adults and 12 euros for children.food was ok and
